[DR186] AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES Doctoral Course (D.M.226/2021) English Italian
INFO General information related to the current academic year Duration
3 years Order
2024
status Open Language English Italian Type Doctoral programs Regulation D.M. 226/2021
Interuniversity Course No Programmed Access Location SASSARI Department AGRARIA
[ TSS ]
Higher School Degree Optional qualifications (choose from the following)
[ TSS+L1-IPO ]
Bachelor's degree
[ TSS+LM-IPO ]
Master's degree
[ TSS+LS-IPO ]
Specialist degree
[ TSS+TS-IPO ]
Foreign degree Program, texts and objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Doctoral students receive specific training for conducting scientific and technological research activities in public and private research institutions. Through specific pathways linked to industries and companies, doctoral students can acquire high-level professional skills, develop and apply research results, and initiate business and technology transfer activities.
Expected professional opportunities include research careers in universities, public institutions, or private research structures, in the fields of territorial planning, environmental monitoring of resources, innovative technologies and processes related to the agri-food industry, where specific competencies are required, as well as agrometeorological services and environmental agencies. Establishment of research spin-offs for technology transfer to companies. Scientific qualification of professional activities for access to the school (agronomist and forester, veterinarian, engineer, architect, biologist, naturalist, chemist, etc.). They may exercise free profession with specialization in the fields of studies and research or enhance their entrepreneurial skills in agricultural, agroforestry and animal husbandry, agri-food and territorial governance, scientific dissemination and technology transfer of innovation. Employment opportunities are also considered in primary production and food processing industries, and in consulting and services in relevant sectors.
Specific training objectives.
The course aims to train highly qualified doctoral students capable of meeting the demand for research and development in the following fields:
i) agrometeorology and plant eco-physiology;
ii) agricultural crop productivity;
iii) management and protection of agricultural and forest production systems; conservation, protection and valorization of natural resources;
iv) biotechnology tailored to regional, national and international production needs;
v) breeding and reproduction techniques, nutrition and feeding, applied genetics and selection of animal species using molecular biology techniques, quality and safety of animal-derived food products.
vi) Study of soil degradation forms, understood as loss of soil productivity or utility, actual or potential, due to natural or anthropogenic factors affecting food production and safety, livelihoods, production and supply of other ecosystem goods and services.
vii) Factors and forces leading to soil degradation and desertification.
Over three years, doctoral students acquire the scientific method and necessary skills for designing experimental projects, conducting experimental plans and laboratory activities, mathematical-statistical data processing, evaluating statistical-experimental inferences, and disseminating research results.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH

Professional activities in the Military Veterinary Corps of the Army Professional activities in Ministries Characteristics of final exam.
The final exam aims to develop the student's ability for independent work and to assess and highlight their organizational and presentation skills. To be admitted to the final exam, the student must have passed all exams required by the study program. According to Law of November 8, 2021, No. 163 and the Interministerial Decree of July 7, 2022, No. 652, the final exam is preceded by a practical assessment test. The final exam confers the professional qualification.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine, the student must hold a secondary school diploma or another equivalent title obtained abroad.
Access to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine is regulated, for each location and academic year, by numerical quotas for students (EU and non-EU) through a Ministerial Decree by the Ministry of University and Research (MUR).
To access the course, the candidate must have adequate initial preparation; specifically, they must have good text comprehension skills and knowledge of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and logical reasoning. These knowledge areas are verified in the admission test, the TOLC - VET, consisting of 50 questions to be completed in 90 minutes.
Candidates ranked within the number fixed by MUR for the course are enrolled, unless they explicitly withdraw in writing. Vacant places are filled by moving down the ranking until the programmed number is reached, for both EU and non-EU students, for the study program.
The student's academic debt, reflecting the lack of specific knowledge required for access to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine, identified during the admission test, is remedied in the first year of the course through recovery methods, verification, and elimination following the assignment of specific additional training obligations according to the Department's teaching regulations.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in VETERINARY MEDICINE Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Veterinarian in independent practice;
Specialist activities within the National Health Service: ASL and IZS;
Professional activities in agro-zootechnical, pharmaceutical, feed, and animal-derived food production and processing industries;
Professional activities in Local Authorities: Municipalities, Provinces, Regions;
Professional activities in cooperation agencies Professional activities within the European Union context: EFSA, DG SANCO, etc.;
Professional activities in Universities and Research Institutions: CNR, INRCA, etc.;
Professional activities in the Military Veterinary Corps of the Army Professional activities in Ministries Communication skills.
The graduate in Veterinary Medicine must be able to communicate effectively with clients, non-experts, colleagues, and Authorities on medical-veterinary topics, basic and specialized, and be able to listen and respond using appropriate language according to the context and interlocutor. They must also be able to communicate, both in writing and orally, on basic and specialized medical-veterinary topics. In addition to Italian, they must be able to communicate efficiently in English, using specific medical and contextual terminology. Communication skills are verified and assessed through case discussions and methodologies in the context of exercises, orientation, internships, exams, and the final exam.

SECTION: AUTONOMY OF JUDGMENT
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10359

Autonomy of Judgment.
The master's graduate in veterinary medicine must be able to act, in daily practice, with full autonomy of judgment in the exercise of the profession, supported by their own knowledge, skills, and abilities, to improve the quality of care, animal well-being, and public health. In awareness of their ethical responsibilities towards individual animals or groups of animals, clients, and the community, the veterinarian operates with the understanding that their professional decisions may have decisive impacts on the environment and society.
The acquisition of the ability to exercise autonomy of judgment is achieved during the study course, through practical exercises and simulations, and is verified during the final examination for each discipline.
Learning Ability.
The veterinary medicine graduate must possess adequate experience in independent study and the organization of their own continuous education, and have the ability to independently conduct a bibliographic search in databases and professional update websites. Must be capable of critically reading scientific articles, even in English, which allows them to understand international literature and stay updated.
At the end of the study path, they will have acquired a cultural background that will allow them to proceed to the third cycle of university studies: Research Doctorate, Specialization Schools, University Master's Degree of the second level.
Learning assessments are conducted through passing exams and conclude with the evaluation of the final test.
Knowledge and Understanding.
BASIC SUBJECTS Knowledge and Understanding The knowledge acquired in the field of basic subjects should be considered introductory, for a better understanding of the fundamental subjects of veterinary culture. Preparation in the fields of physical, chemical, biochemical, and biological (animal and plant) sciences should therefore be viewed in the context of understanding the basic concepts underlying knowledge of anatomy, physiology, pharmacology and toxicology, and animal pathology.
At the end of the training activity, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
 The main stages of morphogenesis, from fertilization to embryonic development; the morphology of embryonic appendages; the structural and ultrastructural organization of the animal cell (cytology), particularly the composition of the cytoplasm, nucleus, and morphology of various cellular organelles; the morphological characteristics of various animal tissues; the morphological characteristics of bones of various animal species, major joints, and muscles.
 The macroscopic and microscopic characteristics of the various body systems of mammals of veterinary interest.
 The general zootechnical business context. This is to be evaluated with respect to its technical and economic characteristics.
 Knowledge of the main browsers available, specific search methods with major search engines; ability to create a document with specific instructions on structure and content type; ability to create and use a spreadsheet with the application of formulas and graphs; create a presentation focused on a specific topic.
 Knowledge of the nervous mechanisms regulating physiological activities of the organism; knowledge of muscle metabolism and movement control; understanding the importance of metabolism regulation for thermoregulatory and productive purposes; knowledge of mechanisms regulating milk synthesis and secretion; knowledge of hormone secretion methods and how they regulate organic homeostasis; knowledge of mechanisms of digestion of carbohydrates, lipids, and protein and non-protein nitrogen; the fate of digestion products in relation to animal health/well-being and production; ability to perform a ruminal fluid sample and its chemical-physical and microbiological analysis.
 Isolation and recognition of the main types of veterinary interest microorganisms, in understanding their organization, and interpreting their variability and evolution; the different types of immune response, the main diagnostic (direct and indirect) and preventive (vaccines) methods used for controlling infectious diseases; immunopathology.
 Basic molecular knowledge necessary for understanding biological systems; the role and function of macromolecules and their interactions in cellular metabolism and information transmission; all competencies necessary to learn the physiological mechanisms required for maintaining homeostasis under physiological and pathological conditions and the action of drugs.
 Adequate knowledge of the main invertebrate and vertebrate taxa and plant species of veterinary interest, being able to describe their characteristics with appropriate scientific terminology; understanding the role of these taxa for the veterinary profession, as well as the role of ecological conditions in the evolution of studied species.
ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS AND ZOOTECHNICAL SCIENCES The veterinary medicine student, within the zootechnical field and animal productions, must know and understand:
 Knowledge of nutrition and animal feeding for the main species of veterinary and zootechnical interest in different life and production stages; develop strongly characteristic competencies for the veterinary profession in an increasingly globalized context, aimed at satisfying numerous aspects of correct nutrition and feeding of animals, considering and respecting current regulations, ethics, circularity and sustainability, protection and environmental impact in a preventive, animal health and well-being, food chain safety, and One Health perspective; the main aspects of animal nutrition and feeding and the main characteristics, evaluation, and utilization of common animal feeds.
 Characteristics of different breeds of domestic species raised (for profit and companionship) with particular attention to morphological differences resulting from different selective pressures in main breeds; their characteristics and peculiarities and their distribution on national and international territory; the molecular basis of genetic information, heritability of traits, main qualitative genes involved in the expression of phenotypic traits, and main quantitative genes involved in different production performances.
 On production chains and breeding systems for broiler chickens, laying hens, breeder chickens, and meat rabbits. For different avian and rabbit production categories, housing methods, management of reproductive and production phases, and feeding techniques are presented with attention to animal well-being, product quality, and environmental respect.
 Information for a correct and autonomous morphofunctional evaluation of domestic animals, effective management of breeding hygiene, and knowledge of autonomous research of sources for animal feeds.
 The physiological needs and well-being of animals and managerial and profitability needs of operators; modern techniques for breeding.
PRE-CLINICAL DISCIPLINES AND ANIMAL HEALTH The knowledge acquired in basic and pre-clinical subjects is fundamental for understanding organ and system pathologies in the medical, surgical, and obstetric sectors.
The student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
 Classification of lesions by organ, system, or body system related to etiology; species-specific pathologies and pathognomonic lesion patterns with various differences between animal species; etiopathogenesis, evolutionary stages, and diagnostic-orientative significance in reversible and irreversible disease forms; main pathologies of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, cardiovascular, skin, and lymphatic systems; importance of certain pathologies due to their zoonotic nature or their international spread; classification systems (histological and cytological) of lesions; criteria allowing differentiation between inflammatory and neoplastic lesions; main malignancy criteria to distinguish between benign and malignant neoplastic lesions.
 The main pathogenic mechanisms, their classification, and which morphological alterations (macroscopic, histological) are responsible; knowledge of the main morphological alterations; knowledge of some zoonotic pathologies; knowledge of the stages of necropsy and the correct drafting of the necropsy report.
 Knowledge of the fundamentals of using the main classes of clinically useful veterinary drugs, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic uses, side effects, and toxic effects; knowledge of the fundamentals of Toxicology, toxicokinetics, and toxicodynamics of the main xenobiotics responsible for poisoning in animals.
 Competencies on Infectious Diseases affecting domestic animals, with particular reference to pathologies affecting companion animals and the equine species, and integrating, at the conclusion of the two Infectious Diseases courses, fundamental aspects of veterinary public health.
 Demonstrate knowledge of etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, prevention, and therapy of the main parasitic diseases of animals; ability to perform: fecal smears; copromicroscopic examinations, parasitological examinations on organs and viscera; issue clinical diagnoses, perform antiparasitic treatments.
 Knowledge and understanding of avian anatomy, the functioning of the systems, and the main pathologies of birds, particularly the etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnosis, and direct and indirect prevention of avian diseases.
 Physiopathological mechanisms responsible for the main alterations of the organism's homeostatic systems and the causes and mechanisms leading to damage, the organism's response, and the repair strategies.
CLINICAL DISCIPLINES The knowledge acquired in basic and pre-clinical subjects is fundamental for understanding organ and system pathologies in the medical, surgical, and obstetric sectors.
The student must acquire the following Knowledge and Understanding abilities:
 Knowledge of the methods for conducting clinical examinations, both direct and using instruments, on small and large domestic animals affected by surgical pathology, to be able to issue diagnosis and prognosis and propose therapy including anesthesia and analgesia; b) rational approach to scientific and clinical reasoning, considering their respective strengths and limitations.
 Acquire a logical-practical method of clinical reasoning applied to the clinic of companion and production animals, to formulate diagnosis in life of diseases, issue prognosis, and choose appropriate therapy.
 On etiopathogenesis and the correct conduct of the clinical examination in various species of domestic animals, on the interpretative methodology of symptoms and clinical signs aimed at diagnosing the most common surgical conditions.
INSPECTION AREA The disciplines of the inspection area provide the student with knowledge and competence regarding the production chain of animal-origin foods and to evaluate the hygiene and safety of animal productions, and the processing and transformation processes of the final product, integrating technological, national and international regulatory, and health insights.
The student, at the end of the course, must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the following themes:
 The production chains of fresh meat and meat-based products, fish products, eggs and egg products, honey, and hive products (1.8). In particular, must demonstrate having acquired the ability to monitor and evaluate the correct application of hygienic-sanitary regulations aimed at maintaining consumer health and food safety, and knowledge of the system for evaluating, managing, and communicating risk within the various food production chains.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
BASIC SUBJECTS The basic scientific notions are indispensable for understanding the disciplines characterizing the veterinary medicine degree course.
Knowledge of these subjects is matured and developed throughout the curriculum and, in particular, refined through practical activities (biochemistry and molecular biology laboratory, microscope room, computer room, dissection room, guided visits to companies) and orientation activities.
The student must acquire the ability to work in a group and, starting from the first year, practical skills in handling veterinary interest animals.
All practical activities are recorded in the Log-book.
The student must be able to apply knowledge:
 On the morphology of the cell and tissues to the study of organs and systems of Domestic Animal Anatomy.
 Recognize within the various systems each individual organ. Moreover, the study of the microscopic characteristics of various organs will serve for understanding and studying pathological organs and structures.
 Of the general zootechnical business context in applied form, regarding the relationship between veterinary service and the business objectives of the entrepreneur. In particular, with regard to achieving break-even points and positive revenue-cost balance of production, as well as quality management control systems and to produce a final product adhering to the given specifications.
 To solve problems related to the physiology of organs and systems in the program and to provide a physiopathological interpretation of signs and symptoms of pathology; evaluate the functioning of systems, hormonal and nervous control of different physiological processes in order to assess the good functioning of the organism; establish a correlation between food intake and the animal's health/well-being status and the quantity/quality of productions; correctly perform ruminal fluid sampling, evaluate causes modifying nervous and hormonal mechanisms regulating physiological processes in relation to the animal's productive and health status; evaluate causes and mechanisms of alimentary nature leading to reduced growth, lower productions, and metabolic dysfunctions such as ruminal acidosis, meteorism, and non-protein nitrogen intoxication.
 Critically examine and evaluate literature and presentations; collect, preserve, and transport samples, choose appropriate diagnostic tests, interpret and understand the limitations of test results; on the principles of disease prevention and promotion of health and well-being.
 Work safely in a chemical/biochemical laboratory and apply the logical approaches of the experimental method to experimental and clinical reasoning.
 Regarding the scientific approach and correct scientific terminology; in the zoological and botanical field, demonstrate the ability to consider an overall view of environmental characteristics influencing such species; demonstrate having assimilated the importance of the synergy of different scientific competencies, in order to allow the veterinarian to implement a correct scientific research and knowledge approach, as well as to interact with colleagues of different scientific training.
ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS AND ZOOTECHNICAL SCIENCES The learning of knowledge in this area will allow the veterinary medicine graduate to:
 Possess knowledge and understanding abilities that allow the development and/or application of original ideas in the context of animal nutrition and feeding.
 Demonstrate knowledge of the characteristics of each breed based on its breed and production purpose; The student must demonstrate possession of knowledge and understanding abilities of the subject to make logical connections that allow answering questions posed during exams; to highlight morphological differences resulting from selection for a specific use and understand the final (evolutionary) meaning of a particular character; to know exactly the methods of control and evaluation of breeders in order to improve the population.
 Analysis of the poultry and rabbit production chains with reference to breeding and feeding techniques, improvement of animal well-being and environmental management, evaluation of product quality. They must also demonstrate having acquired.
 Autonomously evaluate the morphofunctional characteristics of domestic animals; be able to apply knowledge to animal breeding techniques; have acquired autonomy in searching for sources and studying.
PRE-CLINICAL DISCIPLINES AND ANIMAL HEALTH The learning of knowledge in this area will allow the veterinary medicine graduate to demonstrate possession of knowledge and concepts useful for:
 Establish correlations between certain pathologies and lesions, also referring to possible associated cytological and histological patterns. Must also demonstrate the ability to perform a cytological report and a histological diagnosis aimed at developing a conclusive diagnostic judgment.
 Demonstrate possession and application of knowledge and concepts useful for establishing correlations between the development of certain lesions and their possible consequences on the function of organs/tissues/cells; ability to perform a necropsy and correct histological sampling, compile a final report with one or more morphological diagnoses aimed at determining the cause of death of the animal.
 Apply acquired knowledge for the correct choice and use of drugs in clinical practice, e.g., choice of administration route, emergency therapy, maintenance therapy, species-specific differences, legislation on veterinary drugs; apply acquired knowledge to recognize and treat acute and chronic intoxications in animals.
 Apply and integrate knowledge to solve problems related to infectious pathologies affecting domestic animals.
 Demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge to correlate etiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and control of parasitic diseases with a correct diagnostic process.
 Apply avian anatomy, the functioning of the systems, and the main pathologies of birds, particularly the etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnosis, and direct and indirect prevention of avian diseases, and integrate these knowledge to solve problems related to anatomical, physiological, and pathological characteristics.
 Correlate and understand the relationships between cause, mechanisms triggered by noxae, and the physiopathological state of the animal organism in response to such stimuli.
CLINICAL DISCIPLINES The learning of knowledge in this area will allow the veterinary medicine graduate to acquire the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
 Ability to perform basic surgical techniques during a surgical procedure on soft tissues such as excision, removal, hemostasis, and suturing; ability to choose, dose, and administer the appropriate anesthetic and analgesic agent for specific surgical procedures as well as monitoring during anesthesia.
 The student must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge to clinical practice, managing a clinical case with critical ability and autonomy, according to POA, or evaluating a forensic report.
 To complete the clinical examination in various species of domestic animals and demonstrate ability in the clinical decision-making process; study autonomy, promoting the use of assimilated knowledge, preparatory to the application of clinical examination and fundamental surgical techniques, for the development of a correct diagnostic and therapeutic process in the evaluation of various clinical cases; manage animal patients safely and respectfully; develop the ability to apply these knowledge and solve problems related to new or unfamiliar topics; communicate clearly and unambiguously to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors; understand the ethical and professional responsibilities of the veterinarian in relation to animals under their care, the environment, clients, policies, and society.
INSPECTION AREA The learning of knowledge in this area will allow the veterinary medicine graduate to acquire the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
 On food hygiene and safety, particularly the existence of internationally important diseases that represent a national and international risk for biosafety and trade; The student must demonstrate knowledge of legislation regarding the movement of raw materials and diseases with mandatory notification of related veterinary public health, zoonosis, and food hygiene and technology issues, and possess concepts useful for conducting control activities and formulating an inspection judgment.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Veterinarian To adequately perform their professional functions, the veterinary medicine graduate must acquire competencies that allow them to operate in the various fields of the profession.
To perform their function in the clinical field, they must be able to detect and evaluate the health and well-being status of a single animal or a group of animals and develop appropriate treatment plans in the interest of patients, taking available resources into account.
For this purpose, they must possess the following competencies: provide advice to the owner regarding breeding, feeding, administered drugs, and vaccinations to maintain the animal in good health; collect information for a correct anamnesis; identify the animal's pathological state; develop a therapeutic program appropriate to the identified pathology, species, and age of the animal; plan a verification plan to evaluate the disease progression and therapy effectiveness, adapting it to the circumstances that arise.
To correctly operate in the field of zootechnical productions, they must be able to evaluate the physical condition, well-being, and nutritional status of an animal or a group of animals and advise the client on breeding and feeding principles.
For this purpose, they must possess the following competencies: analyze the need expressed by the breeder; use biotechnology, feeding plans, and breeding techniques to improve animal condition and zootechnical production, respecting animal well-being and the environment; provide the breeder with indications on preventive measures to avoid the spread of possible pathologies within the breeding facilities (e.g., separating animals based on age and physical condition, etc.); monitor the animal's health status from a reproductive aspect, regularly subjecting them to examinations and controls to improve fertility; apply assisted reproduction techniques (induction and synchronization of ovulation, artificial insemination, etc.).
To exercise in the field of animal health, the veterinary medicine graduate must be able to develop and advise on prevention and prophylaxis programs for individual animal species in line with accepted standards of animal health and well-being and public health, recognize suspicious symptoms of possible reportable and zoonotic diseases, and take appropriate actions, including notification to competent authorities.
For this purpose, they must possess the following competencies: construct and update animal health registries; plan and carry out controls, prophylaxis, and periodic clinical visits as required by law; prepare intervention measures as required by law in case of a public health threat; carry out extraordinary interventions (non-specialist emergency clinical activities, wildlife population control, etc.) following reports from private individuals, law enforcement, and public bodies.
To operate in the field of inspection of animal-origin foods, the veterinary medicine graduate must be able to critically detect and evaluate the state of salubrity, hygiene, and quality of animal-origin foods.
For this purpose, they must possess the following competencies: verify the hygienic state of vehicles used for transporting animal-origin food products; verify compliance with hygienic-sanitary regulations regarding cleaning and maintenance of premises, equipment, and facilities; verify the hygienic quality of raw materials, semi-finished products, and final products, submitting samples for appropriate laboratory tests; verify self-control systems (HACCP); create and manage the quality control system in the agri-food production sector; develop the company's hygienic-sanitary self-control plan based on HACCP certification or plans for compliance with requirements of mandatory and non-mandatory certifications; evaluate the conformity of business processes with the developed plan; prepare corrective actions to address any non-conformities found; provide technical and practical indications for continuous system improvement.
Also, they must ensure the correct management of the slaughter phase through the execution of pre-slaughter examination on animals to verify correct identification, absence of diseases transmissible to humans or animals, as well as symptoms of diseases/disorders that may render the meat unfit for consumption; perform post-mortem examination of the carcass (heart, lungs, liver) of the slaughtered animal, supervise the sanitary scalding of the meat, and perform blood sampling for hygienic and sanitary checks on refrigerated carcasses.
Function in the Workplace Context.
Veterinarian The veterinarian carries out their professional activity in service to the community and to protect the health of animals and humans.
As specified in Article 1 of the code of ethics, the Veterinarian is dedicated:
to the protection of humans and animals from dangers and damages resulting from the environment, animal diseases, and consumption of provisions or other animal-origin products;
to the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of animal diseases and the protection of their well-being;
to the conservation and functional development of the zootechnical heritage;
to the conservation and safeguarding of the environment and faunal heritage, inspired by the principles of protecting biological diversity and compatible coexistence with humans;
to activities related to the life of companion, sport competition, and exotic animals;
to promoting respect for animals and their well-being as sentient beings;
to promoting hygiene-sanitary prevention campaigns and education for a correct relationship between humans, animals, and the environment;
to activities related to food production, their correct management, and evaluation of risks connected to food safety management.
To carry out these professional activities, the Veterinarian can work as an employee, as a collaborator on individual and specific projects, or as a self-employed professional; in this case, registration with the veterinary order of the competent province is required. The veterinarian must also possess good communication skills and be able to effectively interface with their clients-users.
Description of Specific Training Objectives.
The Master's degree course in Veterinary Medicine is a single-cycle course with programmed access and mandatory attendance, aiming to train graduates with technical-professional and ethical competencies that allow them to perform their functions in the care and prevention of diseases in production, companion, and non-conventional species, in the protection of animal well-being and the correct technical and sanitary management of production, nutrition, and reproduction of farmed species, in the sanitary surveillance of animals raised within the national health service, particularly in the prevention of zoonotic disease spread with potential economic-productive repercussions, in the control of animal-origin foods and specific production technologies.
The objective of the degree course is therefore to provide graduates with the fundamental knowledge and abilities for the exercise of the Veterinary Doctor profession, following the guidelines of the European Association of Establishment for Veterinary Education (EAEVE) and national guidelines.
The quality of veterinary medical training is achieved through a detailed training process, within a five-year study course, organized in 2 semesters/year for a total of 10 semesters. The student must gradually acquire specific knowledge and competencies to independently address professional choices in the diagnostic-therapeutic field and in the care, control, and eradication of diseases.
In the first and second years, the basic science subjects (physics, chemistry, biology, computer science, and biostatistics) and part of the basic veterinary science subjects necessary for knowledge of the healthy animal (biochemistry, anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, zootechnics and genetic improvement, including the management of production and companion animal breeding, general pathology, and microbiology) are covered. In the third, fourth, and fifth years, the characteristic activities focused on preventive and health aspects (pathological anatomy, epidemiology, infectious and parasitic diseases including zoonotic ones, veterinary public health, pharmacology and toxicology), inspection (hygiene, quality, and safety of animal-origin foods), clinical (clinical medicine and propaedeutics for small animals, horses, and production animals, medical, surgical, and obstetric pathology, anesthesiology and intensive care, imaging diagnostics), and integrative (client communication, bioethics, and economic management of breeding and veterinary facilities) are covered, paying attention to the peculiarities related to animal species.
Parallelly, from the first year, the student carries out practical activities within various subjects both at Department facilities (University Veterinary Teaching Hospital, Teaching Paddocks, Teaching Laboratories and Research) and at public and/or private entities and foreign universities, contracted.
In the first and second years, students will acquire the practical skills necessary to interact safely in various breeding contexts with ruminants, pigs, horses, and companion animals, respecting their specific ethological characteristics.
In the third year, they will learn the competencies related to the productive and sanitary management of production animal breeding and the management of animals housed at the department and teaching hospital.
In the fourth year, they will carry out activities in the territory at companion animal shelters (e.g., municipal kennels), contracted production breeding facilities, and wildlife recovery facilities to acquire the competencies necessary for the sanitary, productive, and clinical approach in various fields.
In the fifth year, students will carry out internship activities at University and contracted national or foreign entities, aimed at acquiring professional competencies and skills in the various sectors where the veterinary medical profession is exercised, in accordance with the 'Day one competences' established by the European Association of Establishments for Veterinary Education and European regulations.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law November 8, 2021, No. 163, the final exam for the completion of the single-cycle Master's degree in veterinary medicine (class LM-42) enables the exercise of the veterinary medical profession. For this purpose, the final exam includes the performance of a practical assessment of the professional competencies acquired through the internship within the study courses, aimed at verifying the candidate's level of preparation for the professional qualification that precedes the defense of the thesis.
In particular, the student acquires practical-professional competencies in the following sectors: companion animal, horse, and exotic animal clinic; veterinary public health and food safety; animal productions and medicine of production animals.
The skills and competencies acquired in practical exercises and the internship are documented in a specific document (LogBook).
Throughout the entire course, attention is paid to the student's acquisition of 'Day one competences' (DOCs), a list of fundamental knowledge and competencies that the new graduate must possess from their first day after graduation.
These abilities are detailed in a document drafted by the European Coordinating Committee on Veterinary Training and adopted by EAEVE and specified for each subject.
The objective is to monitor the compliance of the minimum standards set for the veterinary training study program, established by the European Union Directive 2005/36, and to evaluate, promote, and further improve the quality standards of the structures that train the Veterinarian.

Dentists and Oral Surgeons Graduates in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis have employment opportunities in the field of Independent Dental Practice.
They can carry out, according to current regulations, managerial activities of I and II level within the National Health System.
Characteristics of the final exam.
To be admitted to take the graduation exam, the student must have attended all courses and passed the relevant exams.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, No. 163, the final exam for the completion of the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis - Class LM-46 enables the exercise of the profession of dentist. For this purpose, the aforementioned final exam includes the performance of a Practical Assessment (PPV) of professional skills acquired through a Practical Assessment Internship (TPV) within the study courses, aimed at verifying the candidate's practical preparation level for professional qualification, which precedes the defense of the thesis. The PPV is organized through the student's discussion of 3 multidisciplinary clinical cases treated as the primary operator during the TPV, involving multidisciplinary treatment plans with services related to the majority of disciplines covered by the TPV, according to the procedures established by the protocol drawn up by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis Degree Courses, in agreement with the National Dental Register Commission. To pass the PPV, students receive a suitability assessment, after which they proceed to the defense of the thesis.
Therefore, for the completion of the Master's Degree, the submission of an original thesis developed by the student under the guidance of a supervisor is required. The entire graduation committee acts as co-supervisor during the defense, otherwise a correlating lecturer may be appointed. The determination of the grade occurs according to the procedures established by the Academic Body in line with the regulations set by the University.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis (CLMOPD), one must possess a Diploma from a five-year secondary school or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable under current regulations.
The Single Cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is subject to numerical limitation in accordance with Article 1 of Law 264/99.
The didactic organization of CLMOPD requires that students admitted to the first year possess adequate knowledge of the Italian language and initial preparation, obtained from previous studies, covering knowledge in logic, general culture, biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics.
The verification of the student's initial knowledge is considered completed upon passing the admission test.
Students admitted to the course who show initial gaps will be assigned an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA) to be fulfilled during the first year of the course based on criteria defined in the Study Course Didactic Regulation.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in DENTISTRY AND DENTAL PROSTHESIS Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Dentists and Oral Surgeons As the degree program is highly professionalizing, graduates find immediate employment opportunities after graduation; both in independent dental practice, in public health employment, and also in university teaching.

Judgment Autonomy.
The graduate: - Possesses the ability to independently set up and implement therapeutic programs aimed at the care and rehabilitation of the stomatognathic system - Is able to recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy - Is able to independently manage the dental treatment of the patient - Is able to evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment plan, the interventions carried out, and the results achieved. Judgment autonomy is cultivated in the student through reading scientific articles. Specifically dedicated to the acquisition of judgment autonomy is the development of a project, which can be a thesis project or a scientific project, culminating in an independent work with a bibliography.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific methodology, linguistic, and computer skills.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- Fundamental principles of the operation of computer systems with reference to the main implications in the biomedical field; methods and technologies for information management;
- Principles of descriptive medical statistics, the statistical terminology adopted in the scientific field for describing populations and samples, an adequate knowledge of the basic probabilistic and inferential foundations, and the methodological elements useful for interpreting the design of a scientific study;
- Basic principles of mechanics applied to the structural behavior of biomechanical systems composed of biological structures interfaced with artificial ones such as implants and prostheses; basic elements of mechanics applied to the observation of the structural behavior of the human skeleton;
- General principles of psychology as indispensable references in the relationship with the patient;
- Fundamental notions of pedagogy applied, in particular, to health education, understood as the implementation of processes of awareness and responsibility in the exercise of the profession;
- The English language directed, in particular, to the basic knowledge of medical and dental terminology and the understanding of scientific texts;
Such foundational knowledge is acquired through mandatory attendance of courses that include frontal lectures and, if necessary, practical exercises. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Basic Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- Main concepts of mechanical physics, thermodynamics, and electromagnetism, elements of biomechanics and fluid physics. Basic concepts of nuclear physics and radioactivity applicable in dental practice.
- Biological cellular and molecular mechanisms of living organisms, regarding structure, function, biomolecule turnover, and information flow from genome to proteome; cell structure, cellular compartmentalization, and processes of cell division and communication. From molecular biology to evolved biological systems.
- Principles of general and organic chemistry; chemical nomenclature and representation of molecular structure, balancing of chemical reactions. Nomenclature, structure, and properties of various classes of organic compounds. Basic knowledge of molecules of biological interest such as sugars, lipids, proteins, and heterocyclic compounds.
- Structure and function of common biochemically relevant molecules and biochemical mechanisms of metabolic activities and the main qualitative and quantitative laboratory methods;
- Structural and ultrastructural organization of cells and tissues, modes of tissue renewal and their implications for regenerative medicine, methods and tools of morphological investigation, with particular reference to oral-facial structures.
- Fundamental notions of macro and microscopic anatomy of various organs and systems that constitute the human body, with particular reference to the knowledge of the macroscopic and microscopic morphology of all components of the stomatognathic system, considering their topographical relationships and individual functional roles.
- Mechanisms and modes of operation and interaction of organs and systems, with particular reference to the knowledge and understanding of the functioning of the stomatognathic system and its functional relationships with the systems and organs of the entire organism.
- Complexity of pathological phenomena developing in the human body. Etiological factors and molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying pathological processes that govern the response to tissue damage and its repair; fundamental biological defenses activated as a response to pathogens. Morphological alterations caused by pathogens in cells and tissues and their systemic and functional consequences for the organism. Biological bases of transformation and neoplastic disease. Physiopathological mechanisms of cardiovascular and hematological pathologies.
- Basic principles of microbiology and host-parasite relationship. With particular reference to microbiology and pathogenic microorganisms of interest to dentistry.
- Morphological bases of the most frequent pathological processes of various organs and systems, with particular reference to the head and neck region, and specifically to oral cavity pathologies; methods for performing histological or cytological examinations, including the correct application of methodologies in use.
- Laboratory diagnostic investigations according to the main stages: pre-analytical, analytical, post-analytical; issues concerning patient preparation, sample collection, and storage;
- Fundamental knowledge for the critical evaluation and interpretation of the results of the main laboratory diagnostic investigations, in addition to knowledge of the main laboratory diagnostic techniques.
Such foundational knowledge is acquired through mandatory attendance of courses that include frontal lectures and, if necessary, practical exercises. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Dental Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- Rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare professionals;
- Structure of a scientific article and methodology for researching bibliographic sources on the WEB;
- The specific language of specialized disciplines;
- Physical, chemical, biological, and mechanical characteristics of dental materials, their potential and limitations;
- Clinical methodology and diagnostic procedures for the objective examination of the oral cavity; semiological terminology;
- Oral ecosystem, natural history, and epidemiology of the most socially impactful dental pathologies (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer, dental erosions, oral-dental trauma, dental malocclusions);
- Tools and materials for home oral hygiene, potential and limitations of systems for detecting oral mucosa and the main laboratory investigations used in odontostomatology, with particular reference to technological-applicative aspects;
- Procedures and correct use of materials available for evaluating devices produced by the dental laboratory;
- Normal and pathological aspects of soft and hard tissues of the oral cavity, from a clinical perspective, and the most frequent pathologies of the jaw bones;
- Fundamental clinical diagnostic procedures;
- Dental malocclusions and related joint problems; anatomical, etiopathogenetic, instrumental, and operational aspects for diagnosis, planning, and implementing treatment plans;
- Potential and limitations of the main instrumental investigations used for diagnostic purposes in oral surgery; surgical instrumentation; surgical techniques and protocols; prevention of physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of surgical activities;
- Epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and causal therapy of plaque-induced periodontal pathologies; pre-clinical knowledge for planning and performing causal periodontal therapy; instruments, techniques, purposes, indications, and contraindications of surgical periodontal treatment; clinical and instrumental diagnostic methods necessary for the correct planning of surgical therapy for periodontal diseases;
- Theoretical and pre-clinical information in the field of prosthetic rehabilitation of partial edentulism using fixed, framework, or total prostheses through the production of total prosthetic devices;
- Anatomical-topographical limitations of the maxillofacial region and knowledge of oral and maxillofacial semiology; pathologies of interest to maxillofacial and otolaryngological fields such as neoplasms, trauma, congenital and acquired malformations, inflammations, cysts, salivary gland pathologies; clinical and instrumental otolaryngological semiology;
- Basic notions of pediatrics and pediatric pathologies with oral manifestations; pathologies of interest to dentistry in pediatric age and the decision-making process leading to diagnosis and planning of treatment in developing subjects; acquisition of prevention strategies based on individual risk profiles through personalized treatments;
- Indications and contraindications for implant-prosthetic rehabilitation treatment, and risk assessment in patients eligible for such treatment, characteristics of implant devices, physiological mechanisms, morphofunctional characteristics, and factors influencing the osseointegration process; techniques and prognosis of crest augmentation and maxillary sinus lift procedures;
- Theoretical, practical techniques, and clinical criteria in the field of conservative dentistry for designing and implementing a functional and aesthetic structural restoration of the tooth; correct use of adhesive materials, coronal reconstruction in relation to dental tissue destruction, endodontic recovery of root canals;
The knowledge regarding dental specialized disciplines is acquired through mandatory attendance of courses that include frontal lectures and, through regular participation in professional clinical internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Medical and Surgical Sciences of Interest to Dentistry
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- Pathology of the human organism in its complexity through the study of clinical medical and surgical sciences;
- Pathogenetic mechanisms, general foundations of clinical, laboratory, and instrumental semiology, therapeutic perspectives within the main systemic diseases of interest to internal medicine. Interferences that pharmacological therapy for systemic diseases may determine on dental and stomatological pathologies and therapies;
- Main semiotic-clinical issues and systematic approach to the most frequent surgical diseases; clinical presentations of oncological pathologies requiring surgical treatment; conditions requiring urgent surgical treatment;
- Areas of intervention of reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgery, biology of skin, flap, and microsurgical flaps. Main oral-facial malformations requiring multidisciplinary treatment, including the involvement of the dentist;
- Notions on radiation physics, principles of radiological image formation, radiological equipment technology, and clinical information contained in radiological reports and images. Additionally, applications of imaging techniques in dentistry and maxillofacial fields;
- Anatomy, physiology, and functions of the skin and mucosa for maintaining health and pathologies most frequently encountered; systematic approach to the most relevant dermatological and infectious pathologies, functional and instrumental semiology aspects, and specific clinical methodology;
- Physiopathological bases, clinical-nosographic framework, and diagnostic process within neuropsychiatric disciplines. With particular attention to neurological syndromes, especially pathologies involving the oral-facial region. Psychiatric disorders in patients with dental and stomatological pathology;
- Classes of drugs directly and indirectly related to dental practice, with particular attention to molecular mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics, therapeutic uses, and appropriateness of use for each drug class. Adverse reactions that may occur during dental pharmacological therapy, related to the drug in use, patient genetic and physiopathological characteristics, and potential interactions with other drugs the patient is taking for non-dental conditions;
- Main notions regarding dental pathology in pediatric patients, with particular attention to the treatment of patients with special needs;
- Fundamental knowledge on the administration of anesthesia and specialized drugs and the management of emergencies that may occur during dental and stomatological care and therapy;
- Notions on legislative, organizational, operational, and planning aspects of healthcare systems as a whole and the entities operating within them, operational mechanisms, and management tools used in healthcare companies to ensure a constant link between resources used and results;
The knowledge related to medical and surgical sciences is acquired through mandatory attendance of courses that include frontal lectures and clinical and laboratory internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Prevention and Dental Health Services Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- Theoretical-practical aspects, clinical criteria in the field of community dentistry; methods for relating to oral cavity diseases from a preventive perspective; designing and implementing a prevention project; notions in the field of health sociology and methodology of organizing health services; demographic and epidemiological aspects of oral cavity pathologies;
- Useful information for evaluating one's professional activity from a regulatory-ethical perspective with specific reference to criminal, civil, and insurance-social implications and recognizing the main forensic pathology scenarios;
The knowledge related to prevention and dental health services disciplines is acquired through mandatory attendance of courses that include frontal lectures and clinical and laboratory internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific methodology, linguistic, and computer skills.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- Utilize technology associated with information technology as a proper support for diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices and for health-level surveillance and monitoring. Develop and manage a personal dental practice archive;
- Design clinical studies, applying statistical-epidemiological data processing techniques, to independently perform statistical analyses and interpret their results;
- Apply foundational knowledge and terminology to easily consult and understand scientific literature regarding the structural biomechanics of prostheses and implants;
- Apply psychological knowledge as indispensable references in the relationship with the patient;
- Apply pedagogical knowledge to plan health education interventions for groups and communities and to transmit basic dental knowledge;
- Utilize linguistic skills necessary to understand and draft specialist documents and communicate in English on dental topics for continuous professional updating through direct consultation of authoritative textbooks and international scientific literature.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the above activities is an intensive laboratory/practical exercise activity.
Basic Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- Apply the knowledge of basic disciplines, such as the structure and function of the human organism in homeostatic conditions at molecular, cellular, and organ-system levels, for maintaining health conditions and for the correct application of translational scientific research;
- Apply the knowledge tools of disease etiopathogenesis, innate and specific organism defense systems, cellular and tissue damage repair processes, and neoplastic transformation mechanisms for performing any activity related to health protection;
- Apply their knowledge with full understanding of the main themes of dental microbiology;
- Decide, based on methodological and cultural foundations and experience, on the opportunity for specialized examinations or analyses and access to clinical biochemical data as a diagnostic tool;
- Apply a technical base of data to address issues arising during the clinical examination, which constitute an essential part of the data related to patients in dental and stomatological practices and dental pathology;
- Formulate a request for a histological examination and interpret a histopathological report, with particular attention to oral cavity pathologies.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the above activities is an intensive laboratory/practical exercise activity.
Dental Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- Effectively and safely use the dental work environment; describe the oral ecosystem, the natural history, and the epidemiology of the most socially impactful dental pathologies (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer, dental erosions, oral-dental trauma);
- Utilize the specific language of specialized disciplines;
- Perform diagnoses, plan and implement treatment plans, apply prevention protocols, perform conservative therapy plans for hard tissue pathologies of the tooth aimed at morphological, functional, and aesthetic restoration while respecting the health of periodontal tissues and the functionality of the stomatognathic system;
- Perform the clinical examination of the oral cavity, identifying normal anatomical structures and detecting main epidemiological indices; correctly and appropriately use semiological terminology to communicate effectively with the patient and properly interact within the dental healthcare team; organize adequate health promotion interventions; organize effective dental and stomatological prevention interventions for individuals and communities; identify and use tools and materials for home oral hygiene; identify potential and limitations of systems for detecting oral mucosa and the main laboratory investigations used in odontostomatology;
- Critically read a scientific article; consult databases to acquire scientific documentation, applying research results to therapies reliably; identify the potential and limitations of the main instrumental investigations used for diagnostic purposes;
- Perform primary and secondary prevention and diagnosis of prevalent oral mucosa and jaw bone pathologies; perform early diagnosis of potentially neoplastic and neoplastic lesions of the oral cavity;
- Perform the objective examination of the oral-maxillofacial region, identifying and diagnosing surgical pathologies;
- Adopt protocols and behaviors to prevent physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of surgical activities; treat simple cases of oral surgery; identify treatment priorities and collaborate with other specialists in planning interventions for patient recovery; evaluate the effectiveness of surgical interventions and results achieved; recognize and correctly use surgical instrumentation;
- Develop a multidisciplinary clinical case approach and coordinate a surgical team, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare professionals; detect and motivate informed consent for surgical therapy;
- Obtain adequate photographic documentation of the oral cavity; evaluate the use of the most suitable prosthetic materials and techniques in relation to different clinical conditions;
- Apply causal therapy protocols for endodontic and periradicular pathologies of endodontic origin adaptable to individual patients; implement endodontic therapy plans even in high-risk patients, with the aim of morphologically and functionally restoring the affected dental elements;
- Evaluate the severity of issues related to orthognathic diagnosis and the diagnosis and treatment of temporomandibular joint dysfunctions; apply available orthodontic techniques for treating the same in developing age and adulthood; identify the type of approach for planning prosthetic rehabilitation therapy;
- Apply theoretical and pre-clinical knowledge for formulating diagnosis and treatment plans, performing causal periodontal therapy, and correctly using periodontal instrumentation; understand the nature, advantages, and limitations of periodontal surgery; formulate diagnosis and treatment plans for complex periodontal cases requiring surgical treatment;
- Apply theoretical knowledge and pre-clinical skills for formulating a plan for prosthetic rehabilitation of partial edentulism, taking impressions for fixed prostheses, and producing plaster models; formulate diagnosis, treatment plan, and prognosis for prosthetic rehabilitation with PPR; design and implement all phases of PPR prosthetic production, from clinical examination to delivery;
- Perform a specific evaluation of maxillofacial and otolaryngological pathologies; perform anamnesis, clinical examination, and treatment of oral cavity pathologies in pediatric patients; implement preventive strategies for the main dental and stomatological pathologies of pediatric age; diagnose infectious, surgical, and mechanical complications of implant-prosthetic rehabilitation treatment; plan and implement maintenance of implant health; treat infectious, surgical, and mechanical complications of rehabilitation treatment.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of specialized dental activities are intensive laboratory activities on manikins, clinical internships with patients, and the discussion, re-elaboration, and presentation of clinical cases.
Medical and Surgical Sciences of Interest to Dentistry
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- Understand and apply the specific language of these disciplines; interpret the main pathological presentations and diagnose their connections with dental pathology;
- Recognize common internal medicine clinical presentations and evaluate the clinical/dental implications of systemic pathology; critically evaluate and correlate clinical symptoms, physical signs, interpreting their pathogenetic mechanisms and deepening their clinical significance; adequate clinical reasoning ability to analyze common and relevant clinical problems; correct approach to the treatment of oral pathologies associated with systemic diseases of interest to internal medicine;
- Conduct a correct clinical approach to patients with surgical problems: prepare the patient for surgery and prevent, then address, potential complications. Adequate interaction with the surgical team;
- Resolve issues concerning the application of imaging techniques in dentistry and maxillofacial fields, and the clinical contextualization of information contained in radiological reports and images.
- Quantify and manage perioperative anxiety in dentistry for pediatric, elderly, and disabled patients.
- Apply neurological knowledge in the diagnosis and treatment of headaches and facial and head neuralgias of dental and stomatological origin; understand potential implications of pharmacological therapy for neuropsychiatric conditions on dental and stomatological pathologies and therapies;
- Identify the appropriate anesthetic and correct administration technique for each patient based on their systemic condition, recognize complications, and apply initial resuscitation maneuvers;
- Design and organize a dental clinic in compliance with legal requirements, with a correct doctor-patient relationship from a legislative and contractual perspective;
- Develop a clinical approach based on modern evidence-based methodology for the correct diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up management.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of these activities are intensive laboratory activities and clinical internships with patients, along with the discussion, re-elaboration, and presentation of clinical cases.
Prevention and Dental Health Services Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- Correctly complete the clinical record and identify areas where it is mandatory to forward the report or report a crime to judicial authorities; acquire valid informed consent in dental contexts; establish a correct relationship with the patient; maintain confidentiality and information obligations; recognize common occupational diseases and areas of medical-legal interest related to dentistry; guide professional conduct in accordance with current Italian legal obligations;
- Apply knowledge in the field of general and applied hygiene and manage knowledge of health determinants and main risk factors in the interaction between humans, their physical-social environment, and the microbial world.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of these disciplines are intensive laboratory activities and clinical internships.

Function in the Workplace Context.
Dentists and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons The graduates will be able to:
know the full range of general dentistry within the context of comprehensive patient treatment without producing additional risks to the patient or the environment;
identify treatment priorities in line with needs, participating with other professions in planning interventions aimed at reducing oral diseases in the community based on knowledge of the principles and practice of community dentistry;
learn the fundamentals of human pathology, integrating physiopathological and pathological study with clinical methodology and diagnostic procedures that allow the evaluation of major disease conditions; learn the main correlational frameworks and complementary medical and surgical therapeutic procedures to the dental profession, as well as being introduced to basic knowledge of care and assistance according to pedagogical, psychological, sociological, and ethical principles;
know drugs directly and indirectly related to dentistry practice and understand the implications of pharmacological therapy for systemic diseases regarding dental therapies;
know the science of biomaterials as it pertains to dentistry practice;
control cross-infection to prevent physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in professional practice;
know the full range of anxiety and pain control techniques related to dental treatments (within the limits permitted to the dentist);
analyze scientific literature and apply research results to therapy reliably; know the epidemiological aspects, prevention, and treatment of oral and dental diseases;
develop a multidisciplinary clinical case approach, especially in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare professionals;
deepen topics related to the general organization of work, its dynamics, bioethics, patient relationship and education, as well as community dentistry topics, through monographic courses and interdisciplinary seminars;
communicate with the patient and educate the patient on appropriate and effective oral hygiene techniques;
provide the patient with adequate information, based on scientifically accepted knowledge, to obtain informed consent for therapy;
correctly interpret the legislation concerning the practice of dentistry in the European Union country where the dentist practices and provide assistance in compliance with medical-legal and ethical standards in the country where they practice;
recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy;
organize and guide the dental healthcare team using the full range of available dental auxiliary personnel;
deepen their knowledge regarding the development of a multicultural society, with specific reference to the variety and diversification of value and cultural aspects, also from a humanistic perspective.
possess written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian;
The graduate: - Possesses the ability to independently set up and implement therapeutic programs aimed at the care and rehabilitation of the stomatognathic system - Is able to recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy - Is able to independently manage the dental treatment of the patient - Is able to evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment plan, the interventions carried out, and the results achieved. Judgment autonomy is cultivated through reading scientific articles, participation in conferences, and congresses.

Description of specific training objectives.
The general objectives and the structure of the study plan described below refer to the contents of the new Ministerial Decree on New Degree Classes - Regulation for Master's Degree Courses, which defines Master's Degree courses in compliance with European Union directives and the University of Sassari's Academic Regulations. The study plan provides 360 University Credit Units (CFU) over 6 years and 60 CFU per year. The distribution of the 360 CFUs is determined in compliance with the conditions specified in the decree attachments, which establish the credits to be assigned to disciplinary areas including training activities 'essential' for the training of a dentist.
For the University Credit Unit (CFU), corresponding to an average of 25 hours of student effort, a value of at least 8 CFU per lecture or theoretical/practical session and at least 12 hours/CFU for professional internship activities are proposed, in harmony with the University of Sassari's Academic Regulations. The remaining portion of the credit is available to the student for personal study.
The holders of professional training courses are responsible for the internship related to the course. For each individual internship, an interim evaluation must be conducted, which the instructor will consider for the final exam grade. The physiological and clinical knowledge of general medicine and odontostomatology acquired through the training activities included in the study plan and clinical practical activities determine and define the professional profile of the dentist operating in European Union countries. Upon completion of six years, the graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics has acquired the knowledge and technical skills to enter the dental profession in both private and public sectors.
The study program is characterized by a two-year period focused on basic training activities aimed at familiarizing students with the structural organization and vital functions of the human body, including courses addressing issues related to understanding the principles underlying the scientific methodology.
The subsequent three-year period involves the study of medical, surgical, and specialist disciplines with particular reference to clinical issues related to odontostomatology pathologies. These training activities take place concurrently with the study of dental disciplines and professional clinical internships.
Theoretical courses and clinical internships in oral pathology, restorative dentistry, oral surgery, periodontology, orthodontics, pediatric dentistry, and prosthetics, while developing different skills, pursue the common goal of acquiring abilities and experiences to address and solve oral health problems from a preventive, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective, also respecting the medical-legal and ethical standards in EU countries. In the fifth year, a course in maxillofacial pathology and therapy and a course in implantology are introduced, which, like the previous ones, are given a specific theoretical-practical and comprehensive approach to treatment. The sixth year involves a purely professional clinical internship activity aimed at synthesizing the diagnostic-therapeutic knowledge acquired in previous years for the treatment of patients with odontostomatology issues.
Students may propose study plans corresponding to an individual curriculum, provided they respect the distribution between SSD as regulated by the attachments to the Academic Regulations. The deadlines for submitting individual study plans are determined by the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery's Academic Calendar. Study plans are examined and approved by the Council. The Course Committee, on the proposal of the Teachers, organizes teaching activities in which the student exercises their personal choice, up to the acquisition of a total of 8 CFU. Student-selected teaching constitutes official teaching by the Teachers. Among the student-selected activities are monographic courses consisting of lectures, interactive and seminar-style monographic courses, conferences, internships conducted in research laboratories or clinical departments, and other activities deemed compatible with the Degree Course objectives by the Course Committee. Rules for submission and approval of student-selected training activities. Eight credits are available for student choice, which will be recognized upon passing the verification exam. Each student communicates to the Degree Course Council the chosen training activities for the following academic year among those available and recognized within the framework of autonomous choice activities. The choice must be approved by the Degree Course Council, after consulting the Parity Teaching Committee, which assesses its consistency with the training objectives.

University researcher in public and private research institutions Final exam characteristics.
The student has access to 10 CFU dedicated to preparing the Master's thesis. To be admitted to the graduation exam, the student must have completed all courses, passed the related exams, and acquired the 350 CFU preceding the Licensing Degree.
The graduation exam focuses on the discussion of an original thesis prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor; a co-supervisor may be appointed.
The graduation grade (expressed out of 110) is determined by the following parameters, as clearly stated in the CdLM Council minutes (March 2017):
1) Weighted average of grades converted to out of 110;
2) Points awarded by the Graduation Committee during the thesis discussion, based on the quality of the work and presentation, completion of the degree within 6 years of enrollment, honors obtained in exams, and participation in international exchange programs.
3) The points in point 2 are added to the weighted average of grades already converted to out of 110.
4) Honors may be awarded with unanimous committee decision to candidates who achieve a weighted average of exam grades equal to or greater than 102/110. Mention may be awarded with unanimous committee decision to candidates who achieve a weighted average of exam grades equal to or greater than 105/110.
Required knowledge for admission.
The requirements and admission procedures for the Single-cycle Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery are governed by national laws and regulations.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery, one must hold a High School Diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, and pass the admission test.

Communication Skills (COMMUNICATION SKILLS)
Graduates must be able to communicate clearly and unambiguously their conclusions, knowledge, and the reasoning behind them to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, as well as, using the methods required by the circumstances, to their patients. To this end, graduates:
1) will be able to listen carefully to extract and synthesize relevant information on all issues, understanding their content, and exercising communication skills to facilitate understanding with patients and their relatives, enabling them to share decisions as equal partners.
2) will communicate effectively with colleagues, the community, other sectors, and the media, and will know how to interact with other professional figures involved in patient care through efficient teamwork.
3) will demonstrate good sensitivity towards cultural and personal factors that enhance interactions with patients and the community.
4) will be able to handle critical communication situations, such as communicating serious diagnoses, discussing sensitive topics regarding sexual and reproductive life, and end-of-life decisions.
