UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1215] MEDICINE AND SURGERY
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Single Cycle 6 Years
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10384

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates must have the ability to integrate knowledge and manage complexity, as well as formulate judgments based on limited or incomplete information, including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
To this end, graduates:
1) Will be able to demonstrate, in the course of professional activities, a critical approach, constructive skepticism, and a creative attitude oriented toward research. They will be able to consider the importance and limitations of scientific thinking based on information obtained from various sources to establish the cause, treatment, and prevention of diseases.
2) Will be able to formulate personal judgments to solve analytical and complex problems and independently seek scientific information without waiting for it to be provided, using the foundations of scientific evidence.
3) Will be able to formulate hypotheses, collect, and critically evaluate data to solve problems, being aware of the role of complexity, uncertainty, and probability in medical decision-making. They will be able to effectively plan and efficiently manage their time and activities to address uncertain conditions and exercise the ability to adapt to changes.
4) Will be able to exercise personal responsibility in caring for individual patients, respecting the deontological code of the medical profession.
5) Will be able to exercise reflective thinking on their professional activities regarding the relationship with patients and other operators, the methods used, the results achieved, and their personal and emotional experiences.
Learning Skills.
Learning Skills (LEARNING SKILLS)
Graduates must have developed the learning abilities that allow them to continue studying mostly in an independent and self-directed manner.
To this end, graduates:
1) Will be able to collect, organize, and critically interpret new scientific knowledge and health/biomedical information from various resources and databases.
2) Will be able to obtain specific patient information from clinical data management systems, using information and communication technology as a valid support for diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices and for health monitoring, understanding its application and also the limitations of information technology.
3) Will be able to manage a good archive of their medical practice for subsequent analysis and improvement.
4) Will be able to identify their own training needs, even starting from audits of their practice, and design self-training paths.
Preclinical Area The graduate will be able to:
- Correlate the structure and functionality of the normal organism as a complex of biological systems in continuous adaptation, interpreting morpho-functional anomalies observed in various diseases;
- Describe the fundamental molecular, cellular, biochemical, and physiological mechanisms that maintain the organism's homeostasis, knowing how to describe the life cycle of the human being and the effects of growth, development, and aging on the individual, family, and community, with attention to gender differences;
- Recognize the fundamental biological defense mechanisms and pathological mechanisms of the immune system;
- Describe the relationship between microorganisms and host in human infections;
- Recognize the concept and function of genes, the different principles of inheritance of traits, and the concept of genetic variability;
- Correlate the principles of drug action with their indications, paying particular attention to differences in sex, gender, and population;
- Illustrate the origin and natural history of acute and chronic diseases, having essential knowledge related to physiology, pathology, and epidemiology;
- Express themselves appropriately in scientific English in doctor-patient relationships and among colleagues.
Clinical Area The graduate will be able to:
- Recognize the pathophysiological and anatomopathological aspects of diseases, both in medical and surgical fields;
- Evaluate the specific symptoms of various pathologies and correctly frame them within differential diagnostic processes;
- Identify diagnostic investigations, both biological and instrumental, including innovative ones, to propose them appropriately within the diagnostic pathway for individual patients, evaluating the correct cost-benefit ratio;
- Correctly interpret the results obtained from diagnostic investigations;
- Identify the most appropriate therapies, including innovative ones, evaluating the risk-benefit and cost-effectiveness ratios;
- Know and appropriately apply the issues related to pain therapy and end-of-life care;
- Apply all their knowledge while considering issues related to gender and ethnic differences as well as the cultural context of the patient;
- Interpret and approach various pathologies within the context of developmental age, adult patients, complex patients, and chronic patients with multimorbidity;
- Know and apply the principles of evidence-based medicine;
- Recognize emergency and urgent clinical scenarios to identify necessary actions for initial intervention and patient safety.
Public Health and Services Area The graduate:
- Will be able to illustrate the origin and natural history of acute and chronic diseases, with particular reference to epidemiology, health economics, and the principles of health management;
- Will have a good understanding of the mechanisms determining equity in access to healthcare, the effectiveness, and quality of care itself, also in relation to gender and cultural differences;
- Will be able to list and discuss the main determinants of health and disease, such as lifestyle, genetic, demographic, environmental, socio-economic, psychological, and cultural factors in the population as a whole, correlating them to the state of international health and the impact of globalization;
- Will know the rules and practices aimed at maintaining and promoting health in the workplace, identifying situations requiring specialist competence;
- Will know the main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization, principles, and applications of preventive medicine in different contexts;
- Will have adequate knowledge of gender medicine, family, and territory, acquired also through practical field training experiences;
- Will be able to discuss the essential elements of professionalism, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities underlying the profession; will know deontological norms and those underlying high professional responsibility;
- Will have knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing team work.
Applying Knowledge and Understanding.
Preclinical Area The graduate will be able to:
- Apply knowledge of fundamental genomic, biochemical, cellular, and physiological mechanisms maintaining the organism's homeostasis;
- Know the morphological aspects enabling the recognition of various human tissues, allowing organ diagnosis;
- Interpret morpho-functional anomalies of the organism observed in various diseases, both acute and chronic;
- Know the potential and limitations of the main techniques of cell and molecular biology; know the fundamental elements of a gene and a DNA sequence; be able to consult major online molecular genetics databases;
- Evaluate the diagnostic relevance and clinical implications of microbiological analyses;
- Identify normal and abnormal human behavior, also in the context of development;
- Clarify the etiology and natural history of acute and chronic diseases;
- Illustrate the mechanism of action of drugs and their application field, with particular reference to response variability related to gender, ethnic, and pathophysiological factors;
- Know the main pharmacological interactions and contraindications of individual drugs as well as the principles for their correct use within complex therapeutic schemes;
- Apply basic knowledge for approaching biomedical problems;
- Relate appropriately with patients and colleagues from other nationalities.
The objectives will be acquired through the student's participation in frontal lectures and small group activities within integrated courses and laboratory activities, and verified through written and/or oral exams.
Clinical Area The graduate will be able to:
- Correctly collect the clinical history, including family and personal aspects, as well as social elements;
- Perform a general and specific objective examination of individual organs and systems;
- Evaluate the patient's mental state, behavior, and experience;
- Apply the principles of clinical reasoning, diagnostic procedures, and basic techniques, analyzing and interpreting their results to correctly define the nature of a problem, applying appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies;
- Set up the therapeutic pathway, both medical and surgical, ensuring the most appropriate path for each individual, safeguarding life strictly according to the principle of evidence-based medicine;
- Recognize the complex, chronic, multimorbid patient, and tailor a personalized diagnostic-therapeutic pathway;
- Care for diseases and patients effectively, efficiently, and ethically, promoting health and preventing disease, fulfilling the moral obligation to provide medical care in the terminal phases of life, including palliative symptom therapy, with particular reference to pain;
- Correctly and autonomously manage common medical emergencies.
The acquisition of the above objectives will occur through integrated courses of clinical and basic subjects and through professional internship activities starting from the third year of the course. The achievement of the objectives will be verified during the exams of each integrated course and the evaluation by tutors of internship activities.
Public Health and Services Area The graduate will be able to:
- Undertake appropriate preventive and protective actions against diseases, maintaining and promoting the health of the individual, family, and community, correctly using all available resources (diagnostic, therapeutic, organizational, preventive);
- Apply the principles of privacy to demographic and epidemiological data available at local, regional, and national levels, using them correctly in decisions regarding individual and public health;
- Establish diagnostic-therapeutic pathways based on the essential principles of health economics, with specific attention to the cost/benefit ratio, continuity of care between hospital and territory, and organizational appropriateness;
- Respect professional values including excellence, altruism, responsibility, compassion, empathy, reliability, honesty, and integrity, committing to follow scientific methods and continuously update; maintain good relationships with the patient and their family, safeguarding well-being, cultural diversity, and patient autonomy;
- Correctly apply the principles of moral reasoning and make appropriate decisions regarding possible conflicts in ethical, legal, and professional values, including those emerging from ethnic or gender differences, economic hardship, commercialization of healthcare, and new scientific discoveries;
- Respect colleagues and other health professionals, demonstrating the ability to establish collaborative relationships, appropriately valuing each individual involved; will be able to set up a correct multidisciplinary approach for fragile patients with multimorbidity.
The acquisition of these objectives will occur through integrated courses of clinical and basic subjects, as well as through professional internship activities starting from the third year of the course. The achievement of the objectives will be verified during the exams of each integrated course and the evaluation by tutors of internship activities.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Associated Competencies.
General Practitioner Exercise of independent practice,
Exercise of general practitioner Access to Specialization Schools Access to Research Doctorate Employment in University and Research Institutions Role in Work Context.
General Practitioner
- Good human communication skills;
- Ability for self-learning and self-assessment (continuing education);
- Ability to analyze and independently solve problems related to clinical practice by applying the principles of evidence-based medicine;
- Ability to continuously update knowledge and skills, possessing the methodological and cultural foundations for autonomous acquisition and critical evaluation of new knowledge and skills (continuing professional development);
- Ability to interact effectively with other professional figures (interprofessional education);
- Application of the necessary methodological foundations for a correct approach to scientific research in medicine, together with autonomous use of information technology.
Specific Training Objectives Description.
Qualifying Training Objectives of the Class: LM-41 Medicine and Surgery Graduates in Master's Degree programs in Medicine and Surgery must possess:
- The scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation necessary according to Directive 75/363/EEC for the exercise of the medical profession and the methodology and culture necessary for lifelong training, as well as a level of professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy derived from a training path characterized by a holistic approach to health problems of healthy or sick individuals in relation to the chemical-physical, biological, and social environment surrounding them. For this purpose, the Master's Degree program provides a total of 360 CFU, structured over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired in training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills;
- Essential theoretical knowledge derived from basic sciences, in the perspective of their subsequent professional application; the ability to critically detect and evaluate, from a clinical perspective and in a unified vision extending to sociocultural and gender dimensions, data related to the health and disease status of the individual, interpreting them in light of basic scientific knowledge, pathophysiology, and organ and system pathologies; skills and experience, combined with self-assessment ability, to responsibly address and solve priority health problems from a preventive, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective; knowledge of the historical, epistemological, and ethical dimensions of medicine; the ability to communicate clearly and humanely with the patient and family; the ability to collaborate with different professional figures in various group healthcare activities; the ability to apply, in medical decisions, also the principles of health economics; the ability to recognize community health problems and intervene competently.
The professional profile of Master's graduates must include knowledge of:
- Behaviors and attitudes of the medical knowledge being;
- Fundamental notions and methodology of physics and statistics useful for identifying, understanding, and interpreting biomedical phenomena;
- Fundamental biological organization and basic biochemical and cellular processes of living organisms;
- Basic processes of individual and group behavior;
- Mechanisms of transmission and expression of genetic information at the cellular and molecular level;
- Structural organization of the human body, with its main anatomoclinical applications, from macroscopic to microscopic levels, including ultrastructural aspects and the mechanisms through which this organization is realized during embryonic development and differentiation;
- Essential morphological characteristics of systems, organs, tissues, cells, and subcellular structures of the human body, as well as their main morpho-functional correlations;
- Biochemical, molecular, and cellular mechanisms underlying pathophysiological processes;
- Foundations of the main laboratory methodologies applicable to the qualitative and quantitative study of pathogenic determinants and significant biological processes in medicine;
- Modes of operation of the various organs of the human body, their dynamic integration into systems, and general control mechanisms in normal conditions;
- Main functional findings in healthy humans; foundations of the main imaging diagnostic methodologies and the use of radiation, principles of biomedical technology applications in medicine.
Master's graduates must also:
- Have acquired and deepened the interrelationships between the content of basic sciences and clinical sciences, within the complexity inherent to the health status of a healthy or sick person, with particular attention to the interdisciplinary nature of medicine;
- Have developed and matured a strongly integrated approach to the patient, critically evaluating not only all clinical aspects but also dedicating particular attention to relational, educational, social, and ethical aspects involved in prevention, diagnosis, treatment of disease, as well as rehabilitation and recovery of the highest possible psychophysical well-being.
Graduates in Master's Degree programs in Medicine and Surgery will carry out medical-surgical activities in various roles and professional fields in clinical, healthcare, and biomedical contexts.
For the purposes indicated, graduates of the class must have acquired:
- Knowledge of the organization, structure, and normal functioning of the human body, for the maintenance of health in healthy individuals and understanding of pathological modifications; knowledge of the causes of diseases in humans, interpreting their fundamental molecular, cellular, and pathophysiological mechanisms;
- Knowledge of the fundamental biological defense mechanisms and pathological mechanisms of the immune system, as well as the relationship between microorganisms and host in human infections, including related defense mechanisms;
- The ability to correctly apply methodologies to detect clinical, functional, and laboratory findings, critically interpreting them also from a pathophysiological perspective for diagnosis and prognosis, and the ability to evaluate cost-benefit ratios in choosing diagnostic procedures, paying attention to both correct clinical methodology and evidence-based medicine principles;
- A systematic understanding of the most relevant diseases of various systems from a nosological, etiopathogenetic, pathophysiological, and clinical perspective, within a unified and global view of human pathology, and the ability to critically evaluate and correlate clinical symptoms, physical signs, functional alterations observed in humans with anatomopathological lesions, interpreting their production mechanisms and deepening their clinical significance;
- The ability to apply appropriate clinical reasoning to analyze and solve common and relevant clinical problems in both medical and surgical fields, and the ability to evaluate epidemiological data and know their use for promoting health and preventing diseases in individuals and communities;
- Knowledge of the principles underlying the analysis of human behavior and adequate experience gained through in-depth and continuous interactive teaching experiences in the field of doctor-patient relationship and communication, regarding the importance, quality, and appropriateness of communication with the patient and family, as well as with other healthcare operators, being aware of their own and others' values, and the ability to appropriately use methodologies oriented toward information, education, and health instruction, as well as the ability to recognize major behavioral and subjective experience alterations, indicating preventive and rehabilitative therapeutic directions;
- Knowledge of anatomopathological findings as well as cellular, tissue, and organ lesions and their evolution in relation to the most relevant diseases of various systems, and knowledge acquired also through participation in anatomoclinical conferences of the anatomopathologist's contribution to the clinical decision-making process, referring to the use of histopathological and cytological diagnostics (including smear and oncocytopathology) with molecular techniques, in the diagnosis, prevention, prognosis, and therapy of diseases in individual patients, as well as the ability to interpret anatomopathological reports;
- The ability to correctly propose various imaging diagnostic procedures, evaluating risks, costs, and benefits, and the ability to interpret imaging diagnostic reports, as well as knowledge of indications and methodologies for the use of radioactive tracers, and the ability to correctly propose therapeutic use of radiation, evaluating risks and benefits, and knowledge of radioprotection principles;
- Knowledge of the main and most up-to-date laboratory diagnostic methodologies in clinical, cellular, and molecular pathology, as well as the ability to correctly propose various laboratory diagnostic procedures, evaluating costs and benefits, and the ability to rationally interpret laboratory data;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, anatomopathological, preventive, and clinical issues regarding the broncho-pulmonary, cardiovascular, gastroenterological, hematopoietic, endocrine-metabolic, immunological, and uro-renal systems, providing etiopathogenetic interpretation and indicating diagnostic and therapeutic directions, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist in the aforementioned fields;
- The ability to recognize the most frequent otorhinolaryngological, odontostomatology, oral cavity, locomotor system, and visual apparatus diseases, as well as skin and venereal diseases, indicating main preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic directions, and the ability to identify conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist in the aforementioned fields;
- The ability to recognize, through pathophysiological, anatomopathological, and clinical study, the main alterations of the nervous system and psychiatric and social context diseases, providing etiopathogenetic interpretation and indicating diagnostic and therapeutic directions;
- The ability and sensitivity to integrate specialized issues into a broader view of the overall health status of the person and their general well-being needs, and the ability to integrate into a global and unified assessment of the overall health status of the individual the symptoms, signs, and structural and functional alterations of individual organs and systems, aggregating them from a preventive, diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective;
- Knowledge of physiological changes in aging and issues related to disease status in the elderly, and the ability to plan medical and healthcare interventions for geriatric patients;
- The ability to analyze and solve clinical problems of internal medicine, surgery, and specialty fields, evaluating the relationship between benefits, risks, and costs in light of evidence-based medicine principles and diagnostic-therapeutic appropriateness;
- The ability to analyze and solve clinical problems of oncological nature, addressing the diagnostic-therapeutic process in light of evidence-based medicine principles, as well as knowledge of pain therapy and palliative care;
- The skill and sensitivity to apply essential health economics principles in medical decisions, with specific attention to the cost-benefit ratio of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, continuity of care between hospital and territory, and organizational appropriateness;
- Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of the humanities regarding the historical evolution of medical values, including epistemological and ethical aspects; the skill and sensitivity to critically evaluate medical acts within the healthcare team;
- Knowledge of the different drug classes, molecular and cellular mechanisms of their action, fundamental principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, and knowledge of therapeutic uses of drugs, response variability related to gender, genetic, and pathophysiological factors, pharmacological interactions, and criteria for defining therapeutic schemes, as well as knowledge of the principles and methods of clinical pharmacology, including pharmacovigilance and pharmacoepidemiology, side effects, and drug toxicity and abuse;
- Knowledge, from a preventive, diagnostic, and rehabilitative perspective, of issues related to health and disease status in neonatal, childhood, and adolescent age, within the competence of the non-specialist doctor, and the ability to identify conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist and to plan essential medical interventions for the main health problems, by frequency and risk, related to pediatric specialty pathology;
- Knowledge of pathophysiological, psychological, and clinical issues regarding female fertility and sexual dysfunction from a medical sexological perspective, natural and assisted procreation from an endocrine-gynecological perspective, pregnancy, prenatal morbidity, and childbirth, and the ability to recognize the most frequent gynecological pathologies, indicating fundamental preventive and therapeutic measures, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist;
- Knowledge of pathophysiological, psychological, and clinical issues regarding male fertility and evaluation of male gametes, male sexuality and its dysfunctions from a medical sexological perspective, natural and assisted procreation from an endocrine-andrological perspective, and the ability to recognize the most frequent andrological pathologies, indicating fundamental preventive and therapeutic measures, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist;
- The ability to recognize, in the immediacy of the event, clinical scenarios of emergency and urgency, taking necessary initial actions to ensure survival and the best possible care, and knowledge of intervention methods in disaster situations;
- Knowledge of the fundamental norms for maintaining and promoting the health of individuals and communities, and knowledge of norms and practices aimed at maintaining and promoting health in the workplace, identifying situations requiring specialist competence, as well as knowledge of the main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization and the ability to indicate principles and applications of preventive medicine in various and complex communities;
- Knowledge of deontological norms and those related to high professional responsibility, critically evaluating the ethical principles underlying different possible professional choices, and the ability to develop an interdisciplinary and transcultural mental approach, especially in collaboration with other healthcare team members, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing team work, as well as adequate experience in the general organization of work, connected to sensitivity to its characteristics, bioethics, history, and epistemology of medicine, the relationship with the patient, as well as towards community medicine themes, acquired also through direct field experiences; knowledge of the characteristics of multicultural society, with specific reference to the variety and diversification of value and cultural aspects;
- A deep knowledge of the technological and biotechnological development of modern biomedical science, including knowledge of the principles of scientific research in the biomedical field and clinical-specialist areas, the ability to search, read, and interpret international literature for planning research on specific topics, and developing a critical interpretation mindset of scientific data;
- Adequate experience in independent study and organization of their lifelong training, and the ability to conduct bibliographic research and update, the ability to critically read scientific articles derived from knowledge of scientific English, enabling them to understand international literature and update; written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian; useful computer skills for managing information systems of services and their self-training; adequate knowledge of family and territorial medicine, acquired also through practical field training experiences.
In particular, specific professional skills in the fields of internal medicine, general surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, as well as medical and surgical specialties, acquired through professional training activities for a duration of at least 60 CFU, carried out in an integrated manner with other training activities of the course at university healthcare facilities.
The duration of the course for the acquisition of the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is 6 years.
Regarding the definition of curricula prepared for the execution of activities provided by Directive 75/363/EEC, the university didactic regulations comply with the provisions of the present decree and Article 6, paragraph 3, of Ministerial Decree No. 270/04.
Finally, in accordance with Ministerial Decree No. 8 of April 2, 2020, amending the didactic organization of Class LM41 - Medicine and Surgery as per Ministerial Decree of March 16, 2007, the professional training internship is a qualifying part of the professional training. Within the 60 CFU to be acquired throughout the training path, destined for the aforementioned professional training activity, 15 CFU must be dedicated to the completion of the quarterly practical-evaluative internship within the study course, as per Article 3 of the Ministerial Decree of May 9, 2018, No. 58 and amendments, aimed at obtaining professional qualification. This internship is carried out for a number of hours corresponding to at least 5 CFU per month and is structured in the following periods, not necessarily consecutive: one month in Surgical Area; one month in Medical Area; one month, to be carried out not before the sixth year of the course, in the specific field of General Medicine.
The Master's Degree Program in Medicine and Surgery at the University of Sassari aims to train a doctor capable of addressing, after graduation, any type of specialist training in both medical and surgical fields, as well as organizational roles in healthcare systems and their professional updating.
The specific learning objectives are defined in line with both general and specific indications provided by the European Qualifications Framework (Dublin descriptors), integrating them with those proposed by the Institute for International Medical Education (IIME), Task Force for Assessment, and "The TUNING Project (Medicine) – Learning Outcomes/Competences for Undergraduate Medical Education in Europe": the objectives are finally consistent with those indicated by the "Core Curriculum for the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery" proposed by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Italian LM41 Degree Programs.
The Course, for the achievement of didactic objectives, provides a total of 360 CFU, structured over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired in practical training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (professionalizing CFU). The 12 semesters of the Course, including 36 integrated courses, provide for the attribution of CFU in accordance with the table of indispensable training activities. Each CFU corresponds to a student workload of 25 hours, of which no more than 12 hours are frontal lectures in basic, characteristic, and related disciplinary fields, or theoretical-practical teaching (seminar, laboratory, exercise), or 25 hours of guided study within the teaching structure.
Each professionalizing CFU (training and orientation internships) corresponds to 25 hours of student work, also including small group teaching activities, as well as each CFU for student-selected activities and the final exam.
The specific mission of the Master's Degree Program in Medicine and Surgery is biomedical-psychosocial and aimed at the real development of "professional competence" and "professional values." It is based on the importance of integrating the biomedical paradigm of "curing the disease" with the psychosocial paradigm of "caring for the human being" within the meta-paradigm of "complexity of care." This specific mission is therefore aimed at training a doctor, at an initial professional level, who possesses:
- A multidisciplinary, interprofessional, and integrated vision of common health and disease problems;
- Education oriented toward disease prevention and health promotion within the community and territory;
- A deep knowledge of new care and health needs, focused not only on the disease but especially on the sick person, considered in their entirety of body and mind and inserted in a specific social context.
The teaching method adopted, useful for achieving the expected qualifying characteristics, provides for the horizontal and vertical integration of knowledge, a teaching method based on a solid cultural and methodological foundation acquired through the study of pre-clinical disciplines and subsequently predominantly focused on problem-solving and decision-making, early contact with the patient, and the acquisition of good clinical and interpersonal skills with the patient.
In the didactic project of the Master's Degree Program, the right balance of vertical and transversal integration is proposed between:
a) Basic sciences, which must be broad and include knowledge of evolutionary biology, molecular biology, and genetics, as well as biological complexity, aimed at understanding the structure and function of the human body in normal conditions, for maintaining health conditions and correctly applying translational scientific research;
b) Knowledge of pathological processes and the mechanisms causing them, also to set up prevention, diagnosis, and therapy;
c) Clinical medical practice and methodology, which must be particularly solid, through extensive use of tutorial teaching, capable of transforming theoretical knowledge into personal experience to build one's own value scale and interests, and to acquire professional skills useful for managing the complexity of medicine;
d) Humanities, which must constitute a useful background to reach awareness of the medical being and the deep values of medical professionalism;
e) Acquisition of scientific, medical, clinical, and professional methodology directed at health problems of the individual and community.

The final exam aims to develop the student's ability for independent work and to measure and highlight their organizational and presentation skills. To be admitted to the final exam, the student must have passed all exams required by the study program. According to Law 8 November 2021, n.163 and Interministerial Decree 7 July 2022, n. 652, the final exam is preceded by a practical assessment test. The final exam makes the degree qualifying.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine, the student must hold a secondary school diploma or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad.
Access to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine is regulated, for each location and each academic year, by numerical quota programming of student contingents (EU and non-EU) with a Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of University and Research (M.U.R.).
To access the course, the candidate must have acquired adequate initial preparation; specifically, they must have good reading comprehension skills and knowledge of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and logical reasoning. Such knowledge is verified in the admission test, called TOLC - VET, consisting of 50 questions to be completed in 90 minutes.
Candidates ranked within the number fixed for the course by M.U.R. are enrolled, unless they explicitly withdraw in writing. Vacant places are filled by moving down the ranking until the programmed number is reached, for both EU and non-EU students, for the study program.
The student's academic debt, indicating the lack of specific knowledge required for access to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine, detected in the admission test, is remedied in the first year of the course through recovery methods, verification, and elimination following the assignment of specific additional educational obligations according to the Department's teaching regulations.

The graduate in Veterinary Medicine must be able to communicate effectively with clients, non-experts, colleagues, and Authorities on medical-veterinary, basic, and specialist topics, and must be able to listen and respond using appropriate language according to the context and interlocutor. They must also be able to communicate, both in writing and orally, about basic and specialist medical-veterinary topics. In addition to Italian, they must be able to conduct efficient communication in English, using specific medical and contextual terminology. Communication skills are verified and assessed through case discussions and methodologies in the context of exercises, orientation, internships, exams, and the final exam.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The master's graduate in veterinary medicine must be able to act, in daily practice, with full autonomy of judgment in the exercise of the profession, supported by their own knowledge, skills, and abilities, to improve the quality of care, animal well-being, and public health. Being aware of their ethical responsibilities towards individual animals or groups of animals, the client, and the community, the veterinarian operates with the understanding that their professional decisions can have decisive repercussions on the environment and society.
The acquisition of the capacity for autonomy of judgment is achieved during the study course, through practical exercises and simulations, and is verified during the final examination for each discipline.

Learning Ability.
The veterinary medicine graduate must possess adequate experience in independent study and the organization of their ongoing education, and have the ability to independently conduct bibliographic research in databases and professional update websites. Must be capable of critically reading scientific articles, even in English, which allows them to understand international literature and stay updated.
At the end of the study program, they will have acquired a cultural background that will allow them to proceed to the third cycle of university studies: Research Doctorate, Specialization Schools, Second-Level University Master's Degree.
Learning assessments are conducted through final exams and conclude with the evaluation of the final project.

Knowledge and Understanding.
BASIC SUBJECTS Knowledge and Understanding
The knowledge acquired in the basic subjects should be considered introductory, for a better understanding of the fundamental subjects of veterinary culture. Preparation in the fields of physical, chemical, biochemical, and biological (animal and plant) sciences should be viewed in the context of understanding the basic concepts underlying anatomy, physiology, pharmacology and toxicology, and animal pathology.
At the end of the training activity, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
 The main stages of morphogenesis, from fertilization to embryonic development; the morphology of embryonic appendages; the structural and ultrastructural organization of the animal cell (cytology), particularly the composition of the cytoplasm, nucleus, and morphology of various cellular organelles; the morphological characteristics of various animal tissues; the morphological characteristics of bones in various animal species, major joints, and muscles.
 The macroscopic and microscopic characteristics of the various organ systems of veterinary interest mammals.
 The general context of animal husbandry enterprises. This is to be evaluated with respect to its technical and economic characteristics.
 Knowledge of the main web browsers available, specific search methods using major search engines; ability to create a document with specific instructions on structure and content type; ability to create and use a spreadsheet with formula application and graphs; create a presentation focused on a specific topic.
 Knowledge of the nervous mechanisms regulating physiological activities of the organism; knowledge of muscle metabolism and movement control; understanding the importance of metabolic regulation for thermoregulatory and productive purposes; knowledge of mechanisms regulating milk synthesis and secretion; knowledge of hormone secretion methods and how they regulate organic homeostasis; knowledge of mechanisms of digestion of carbohydrates, lipids, and protein and non-protein nitrogen; the fate of digestion products in relation to animal health/well-being and production; ability to perform rumen fluid sampling and its chemical-physical and microbiological analysis.
 Isolation and recognition of the main types of veterinary interest microorganisms, understanding their organization, and interpreting their variability and evolution; different types of immune response, main diagnostic (direct and indirect) and preventive (vaccines) methods used for controlling infectious diseases; immunopathology.
 Basic molecular knowledge necessary for understanding biological systems; the role and function of macromolecules and their interactions in cellular metabolism and information transmission; all competencies necessary to learn the physiological mechanisms required for maintaining homeostasis under physiological and pathological conditions and the action of drugs.
 Adequate knowledge of the main invertebrate and vertebrate taxa and plant species of veterinary interest, being able to describe their characteristics using appropriate scientific terminology; understanding the role of these taxa for the veterinary profession, as well as the role of ecological conditions in the evolution of the studied species.

ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS AND ANIMAL HUSBANDRY SCIENCES
The veterinary medicine student, within the context of animal husbandry and animal productions, must know and understand:
 Knowledge on animal nutrition and feeding of the main species of veterinary and animal husbandry interest in different life and/or production stages; developing strongly characteristic competencies for the veterinary profession in an increasingly globalized context, aimed at satisfying numerous aspects of correct animal nutrition and feeding in consideration of and respect for current regulations, ethics, circularity and sustainability, environmental protection and impact, prevention, animal health and well-being, food chain safety, and One Health; the main aspects of animal nutrition and feeding and the main characteristics, evaluation, and utilization of common animal feeds.
 The characteristics of different breeds of domestic species raised (for profit and companionship) with particular attention to morphological differences resulting from different selective pressures in main breeds; their characteristics and peculiarities and their distribution across national and international territories; the molecular basis of genetic information, heritability of traits, main qualitative genes involved in the expression of phenotypic traits, and main quantitative genes involved in different production performances.
 On the production chains and breeding systems of broiler chickens, laying hens, breeder chickens, and meat rabbits. For different productive categories of poultry and rabbits, the methods of housing, management of reproductive and productive phases, and feeding techniques are presented with attention to animal well-being, product quality, and environmental respect.
 Information for a correct and autonomous morpho-functional evaluation of domestic animals, effective management of farm hygiene, and knowledge related to autonomous research of correct traditional and digital sources related to animal breeding.
 Animal husbandry technologies for the main species of interest aimed at improving farm profitability and production quality while respecting the environment and animal well-being.

PRE-CLINICAL DISCIPLINES AND ANIMAL HEALTH
The courses in the pre-clinical and veterinary public health areas constitute one of the foundations of the veterinary profession and include disciplines preparatory to clinical and inspection activities. The student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
 Classification of lesions by organ, system, or body system related to etiology; species-specific pathologies and pathognomonic lesion patterns with various differences between animal species; etiopathogenesis, evolutionary stages, and diagnostic-orientative significance in reversible and irreversible disease forms; main pathologies of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, cardiovascular, skin, and lymphatic systems; importance of certain pathologies due to their zoonotic nature or international spread; classification systems (histological and cytological) of lesions; criteria for differentiating inflammatory from neoplastic lesions; main criteria for malignancy to distinguish between benign and malignant neoplastic lesions.
 Main pathogenic mechanisms, their classification, and the morphological alterations (macroscopic, histological) they cause; knowledge of main morphological alterations; knowledge of some zoonotic pathologies; knowledge of necropsy phases and correct preparation of the necropsy report.
 Knowledge of the fundamentals of using main classes of clinically useful veterinary drugs, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic uses, side effects, and toxicities; knowledge of the fundamentals of Toxicology, toxicokinetics, and toxicodynamics of main xenobiotics responsible for animal poisoning.
 Competencies on Infectious Diseases affecting domestic animals with particular reference to pathologies affecting companion animals and equine species, integrating, at the end of the two Infectious Diseases courses, fundamental aspects of veterinary public health.
 Demonstrate knowledge of etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, prevention, and therapy of main parasitic diseases of animals; ability to perform: fecal smears; copromicroscopic examinations; parasitological examinations on organs and viscera; issue clinical diagnoses, perform antiparasitic treatments.
 Knowledge and understanding of avian anatomy, functioning of organ systems, and main pathologies of birds, particularly etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnosis, and direct and indirect prevention of poultry diseases.
 Physio-pathological mechanisms responsible for main alterations of organism homeostatic systems and causes and mechanisms leading to damage, organism response, and repair strategies.

CLINICAL DISCIPLINES
Knowledge acquired in basic and pre-clinical subjects is fundamental for understanding organ and system pathologies in the medical, surgical, and obstetric fields. In all these fields, practical and analytical abilities, along with autonomy of judgment, are required and assessed, considered essential in clinical professional training.
The student must acquire the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
 Knowledge of the methods for conducting clinical examinations on small and large domestic animals affected by surgical pathology, both directly and using instruments, to issue diagnosis, prognosis, and propose therapy including anesthesia and analgesia; b) rational approach to scientific and clinical reasoning, considering respective strengths and limitations.
 Acquire a logical-practical method of clinical reasoning applied to the clinical care of companion and production animals to formulate diagnosis in life of diseases, issue prognosis, and choose appropriate therapy.
 On etiopathogenesis and correct conduct of clinical examination in various domestic animal species, on the interpretative methodology of symptoms and clinical signs for the diagnosis of common surgical affections. The course aims to provide the basis for performing and interpreting the main diagnostic methods to be used in a correct diagnostic process.
 On etiology, pathophysiology, clinical signs, and diagnosis of main internal medicine pathologies of domestic animals; performance of general and specific physical examinations of individual systems and interpretation of anamnestic data, reports, symptoms, clinical findings, and laboratory results; autonomy of judgment in assessing an animal's health status; communication skills and correct use of medical terminology; ability to learn within the context of veterinary medical and pathological semiotics and ability for independent study.

INSPECTION AREA
The disciplines of the inspection area provide the student with knowledge and competence regarding the animal food production chain and to evaluate the hygiene and safety of animal productions, as well as the processing and transformation of the final product, integrating technological, national and international regulatory, and sanitary insights. Theoretical and practical knowledge acquired through the study of animal productions, pathological anatomy, infectious and parasitic diseases, and public health are necessary for understanding the teachings provided within the inspection area.
At the end of the course, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the following topics:
 The fresh meat and meat-based product supply chains, fish products, eggs and egg products, honey and hive products (1.8). In particular, they must demonstrate the ability to monitor and evaluate the correct application of hygiene and sanitary regulations aimed at maintaining consumer health and food safety, and to know the risk assessment, management, and communication system within different food supply chains. The ability to connect different aspects and topics covered in the integrated course and the acquisition of tools to develop critical analysis of concrete cases will be valued.
The disciplines of the inspection area provide the student with knowledge and competence regarding the animal food production chain and to evaluate the hygiene and safety of animal productions, as well as the processing and transformation of the final product, integrating technological, national and international regulatory, and sanitary insights. Theoretical and practical knowledge acquired through the study of animal productions, pathological anatomy, infectious and parasitic diseases, and public health are necessary for understanding the teachings provided within the inspection area.
These competencies will be acquired and refined through practical activities carried out in small groups, orientation activities, and inspection sector internships (7 CFU for a total of 175 hours) where the student is actively engaged in practical activities under the supervision of the course instructor and/or veterinary personnel from SSN structures (ASL, zooprophylactic institutes) or authorized agri-food sector companies.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
BASIC SUBJECTS
Basic scientific knowledge is essential for understanding the disciplines characterizing the veterinary medicine degree course. Knowledge of these subjects is developed throughout the curriculum, particularly refined through practical activities (biochemistry and molecular biology lab, microscope room, computer room, dissection room, guided visits to companies) and orientation activities. The student must acquire the ability to work in groups and, from the first year, practical skills in handling veterinary interest animals. All practical activities are recorded in the Log-book.
The student must be able to apply knowledge:
 On cell and tissue morphology for the study of organs and systems of Domestic Animal Anatomy.
 Recognize each organ within the various systems. Additionally, the study of the microscopic characteristics of various organs will aid in understanding and studying pathological organs and structures.
 In the applied context of the general animal husbandry enterprise, with respect to the relationship between veterinary services and the entrepreneur's business objectives. In particular, with regard to achieving break-even points and positive revenue-cost balance, as well as quality control systems for production management to produce a final product aligned with given specifications.
 To solve problems related to organ and system physiology and provide a pathophysiological interpretation of disease signs and symptoms; evaluate organ system function, hormonal and nervous control of different physiological processes to assess organism functionality; establish a correlation between animal feed intake and health/well-being status and production quantity/quality; correctly perform rumen fluid sampling, evaluate causes modifying nervous and hormonal mechanisms regulating physiological processes based on animal production and health status; evaluate causes and mechanisms of nutritional origin leading to reduced growth, lower production, and metabolic dysfunctions such as ruminal acidosis, meteorism, and non-protein nitrogen intoxication.
 Critically examine and evaluate literature and presentations; collect, preserve, and transport samples, choose appropriate diagnostic tests, interpret and understand test result limitations; on principles of disease prevention and promotion of health and well-being.
 Work safely in a chemical/biochemical laboratory and apply logical approaches of the experimental method to experimental and clinical reasoning.
 Related to the scientific approach and correct scientific terminology; in zoological and botanical contexts, demonstrate the ability to consider an overall view of environmental characteristics influencing these species; demonstrate assimilation of the importance of synergy between different scientific competencies, enabling the veterinarian to implement a correct scientific research and knowledge approach, as well as interact with colleagues of different scientific backgrounds.

ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS AND ANIMAL HUSBANDRY SCIENCES
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to:
 Possess knowledge and understanding abilities to develop and/or apply original ideas in the context of animal nutrition and feeding.
 Demonstrate knowledge of the characteristics of each breed based on breed origin and production purpose; the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the subject to establish logical connections to answer examination questions; highlight morphological differences resulting from selection for specific use and understand the final (evolutionary) significance of a particular trait; know exactly the methods of control and evaluation of breeders to improve population.
 Analysis of poultry and rabbit supply chains with reference to breeding and feeding techniques, improvement of animal well-being and environmental management, and quality product evaluation. They must also demonstrate acquisition of.
 Independently evaluate the morpho-functional characteristics of domestic animals; apply knowledge to animal breeding techniques; acquire autonomy in research and study.
 Physiological and well-being needs of animals and managerial and profitability needs of operators; modern techniques for animal husbandry.

PRE-CLINICAL DISCIPLINES AND ANIMAL HEALTH
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to demonstrate knowledge and concepts useful for:
 Establishing correlations between certain pathologies and lesions, referring also to possible associated cytological and histological patterns. They must also demonstrate the ability to perform a cytological report and a histological diagnosis aimed at formulating a conclusive diagnostic judgment.
 Demonstrate possession and application of knowledge and concepts useful to establish correlations between the development of certain lesions and possible consequences on organ/tissue/cell function; ability to perform a necropsy and correct histological sampling, compile a final report with one or more morphological diagnoses aimed at determining the cause of animal death.
 Apply acquired knowledge for correct drug selection and use in clinical practice, e.g., choice of administration route, emergency therapy, maintenance therapy, species-specific differences, veterinary drug legislation; apply knowledge to recognize and treat acute and chronic intoxications in animals.
 Apply and integrate knowledge to solve problems related to infectious diseases affecting domestic animals.
 Demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge to correlate etiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and control of parasitic diseases with a correct diagnostic process.
 Apply avian anatomy, organ system functioning, and main pathologies of birds, particularly etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnosis, and direct and indirect prevention of poultry diseases, and integrate these knowledge to solve problems related to anatomical, physiological, and pathological characteristics.

CLINICAL DISCIPLINES
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to acquire the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
 Ability to perform basic surgical techniques during a soft tissue surgery, such as excision, removal, hemostasis, and suturing; ability to choose, dose, and administer the appropriate anesthetic and analgesic agent for specific surgical procedures, as well as monitor anesthesia.
 The student must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge to clinical practice, managing a clinical case with critical and autonomous capacity, according to POA, or evaluating a forensic report.
 To complete the clinical examination in various domestic animal species and demonstrate ability in clinical decision-making; autonomy of study, promoting the use of acquired knowledge, propaedeutic to the application of clinical examination and basic surgical techniques, for the development of a correct diagnostic and therapeutic process in the evaluation of various clinical cases; manage animal patients safely and respectfully; develop the ability to apply these knowledge and solve problems related to new or unfamiliar topics; communicate clearly and unambiguously to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors; understand the ethical and professional responsibilities of the veterinarian in relation to animals under their care, the environment, clients, policies, and society.

INSPECTION AREA
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to acquire the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
 On food hygiene and safety, particularly the existence of internationally important diseases representing a national and international risk for biosafety and trade; the student must demonstrate knowledge of legislation regarding the movement of raw materials and diseases with mandatory notification of public health veterinary issues, zoonoses, and food hygiene and technology, and possess concepts useful for conducting control activities and formulating an inspection judgment.

Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN

Competencies associated with the function.
Veterinarian
To adequately perform their professional functions, the veterinary medicine graduate must acquire competencies enabling them to operate in various fields of the profession.
1. To perform their function in the clinical field, they must be able to assess and evaluate the health and well-being status of a single animal or group of animals and develop appropriate treatment plans in the interest of patients, considering available resources. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: provide advice to the owner on breeding, feeding, administered drugs, and vaccinations to maintain animal health; collect information for a correct anamnesis; identify the pathological state of the animal; develop an appropriate therapeutic program based on the identified pathology, species, and age of the animal; plan a verification program to assess disease progression and therapy effectiveness, adapting to new conditions.
2. To operate correctly in the animal husbandry production field, they must be able to assess the physical condition, well-being, and nutritional status of an animal or group of animals and advise the client on breeding and feeding principles. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: analyze the needs expressed by the breeder; use biotechnology, feeding plans, and breeding techniques to improve animal condition and production, respecting animal well-being and the environment; provide breeders with preventive measures to avoid disease spread within farms (e.g., separating animals by age and physical condition, etc.); monitor animal health status in reproductive aspects, regularly conducting exams and checks to improve fertility; apply assisted reproduction techniques (induction and synchronization of ovulation, artificial insemination, etc.).
3. To exercise in the animal health field, the veterinary medicine graduate must be able to develop and advise on prevention and prophylaxis programs for individual animal species in line with accepted health and well-being standards and public health, recognize suspicious symptoms of reportable and zoonotic diseases, and take appropriate actions, including notification to competent authorities. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: build and update animal health registries; plan and carry out required controls, prophylaxis, and periodic clinical examinations; prepare intervention measures as required by law in case of public health threats; carry out extraordinary interventions (non-specialist emergency clinical activities, wildlife population control, etc.) following reports from private individuals, law enforcement, and public bodies.
4. To operate in the field of animal food inspection, the veterinary medicine graduate must be able to assess and critically evaluate the salubrity, hygiene, and quality of animal food products. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: verify the hygiene of vehicles used for transporting animal food products; verify compliance with hygiene regulations regarding cleaning and maintenance of premises, equipment, and facilities; verify the hygienic quality of raw materials, semi-finished products, and final products by submitting samples for laboratory testing; verify self-control systems (HACCP); create and manage quality control systems in the agri-food production sector; develop the hygienic-sanitary self-control plan based on HACCP certification or compliance with mandatory certification requirements; evaluate compliance of business processes with the developed plan; implement corrective actions for identified non-conformities; provide technical and practical guidance for continuous system improvement. Additionally, they must oversee the correct management of the slaughter phase through pre-slaughter inspection of animals to verify correct identification, absence of diseases transmissible to humans or animals, and symptoms of diseases/turbances that may render meat unfit for consumption; perform post-mortem inspection of the heart, lungs, and liver of the slaughtered animal; supervise the sanitary boiling of meat; perform blood sampling for hygienic and sanitary checks on refrigerated carcasses.

Work Context Function.
Veterinarian
The veterinarian performs their professional activity in service to the community and to protect animal and human health. As specified in Article 1 of the code of ethics, the veterinarian is dedicated to:
- Protecting humans and animals from dangers and damages arising from the environment, animal diseases, and consumption of food or other animal-derived products;
- Preventing, diagnosing, and treating animal diseases and safeguarding their well-being;
- Conserving and developing the livestock heritage;
- Conserving and safeguarding the environment and wildlife heritage, inspired by the principles of biodiversity protection and compatible coexistence with humans;
- Engaging in activities related to companion, sport competition, and exotic animals;
- Promoting respect for animals and their well-being as sentient beings;
- Promoting hygiene and health prevention campaigns and education for a correct human-animal-environment relationship;
- Engaging in activities related to food production, their correct management, and evaluation of risks related to food safety management.
To perform these professional activities, the veterinarian can work as an employee, collaborator on specific projects, or as a self-employed professional; in the latter case, registration with the veterinary order of the competent province is required. The veterinarian must also possess good communication skills and be able to effectively interface with their clients/users.

Specific Training Objectives Description.
The master's degree course in Veterinary Medicine is a single-cycle program with limited access and mandatory attendance, aiming to train graduates with technical-professional and ethical competencies enabling them to perform their functions in the care and prevention of diseases in livestock, companion, and non-conventional species, in the protection of animal well-being, and in the correct technical and sanitary management of production, nutrition, and reproduction of farmed species, in the sanitary surveillance of animals raised within the national health service, particularly in the prevention of zoonotic disease spread and potential economic impacts, in the control of animal food products and specific production technologies. The objective of the master's degree course is to provide graduates with the fundamental knowledge and abilities for the practice of veterinary medicine, following the guidelines of the European Association of Establishment for Veterinary Education (EAEVE) and national guidelines.
The quality of veterinary medicine training is achieved through an articulated training process within a five-year study program, organized in 2 semesters/year for a total of 10 semesters. The student must gradually acquire specific knowledge and competencies to independently make professional choices in diagnostic-therapeutic fields and in the care, control, and eradication of diseases.
In the first and second years, basic science subjects (physics, chemistry, biology, informatics, and biostatistics) and part of the basic veterinary science subjects necessary for understanding the healthy animal (biochemistry, anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, animal husbandry and genetic improvement, including management of livestock and companion animal farms, general pathology, and microbiology) are covered. In the third, fourth, and fifth years, characteristic activities focused on preventive and sanitary aspects (pathological anatomy, epidemiology, infectious and parasitic diseases including zoonotic ones, veterinary public health, pharmacology and toxicology), inspection (hygiene, quality, and safety of animal food products), clinical (clinical and propaedeutic for small animals, horses, and livestock, medical, surgical, and obstetric pathology, anesthesiology and intensive therapy, imaging diagnostics), and integrative (client communication, bioethics, and economic management of livestock and veterinary facilities) are covered, paying attention to species-specific peculiarities. Parallelly, from the first year, students carry out practical activities within various courses, both at department facilities (University Veterinary Teaching Hospital, teaching paddocks, teaching labs and research labs) and at public or private entities and foreign universities with agreements. In the first and second years, students acquire the practical competencies necessary to interact safely in various livestock contexts with ruminants, swine, equines, and companion animals, respecting their specific ethological characteristics. In the third year, they learn competencies related to the productive and sanitary management of livestock farms and the management of animals housed at the department and teaching hospital. In the fourth year, they carry out activities on the territory in facilities for companion animal care (e.g., municipal kennels), contracted livestock farms, and wildlife recovery facilities to acquire necessary competencies for sanitary, productive, and clinical approaches in different fields. In the fifth year, students carry out internship activities at university facilities and at national or foreign agreed entities, focused on acquiring professional competencies and skills in the various sectors of veterinary medicine practice, in accordance with the "Day One Competences" established by the European Association of Establishments for Veterinary Education and European regulations. According to Articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, No. 163, the final exam for the single-cycle master's degree in veterinary medicine (class LM-42) authorizes the exercise of the veterinary medicine profession. For this purpose, the final exam includes the performance of a practical assessment of professional competencies acquired during the internship, aimed at verifying the candidate's preparation level for professional authorization before the thesis defense. In particular, students acquire practical-professional competencies in the following sectors: companion animal, horse, and exotic animal clinical care; veterinary public health and food safety; animal productions and livestock medicine. The skills and competencies acquired in practical exercises and internships are documented in a specific document (LogBook). Throughout the program, attention is paid to the acquisition by the student of 'Day One Competences' (DOCs), a list of fundamental knowledge and competencies that the new graduate must possess from their first day after graduation. These competencies are detailed in a document drafted by the European Coordinating Committee on Veterinary Training and adopted by EAEVE and specified for each course. The objective is to monitor the compliance of the minimum standards set for the veterinary training program, established by the European Union Directive 2005/36, and to evaluate, promote, and further improve the quality standards of the structures training veterinarians.

The final exam aims to develop the student's ability for independent work and to measure and highlight their organizational and presentation skills. To be admitted to the final exam, the student must have passed all exams required by the study program. According to Law 8 November 2021, n.163 and the Interministerial Decree of 7 July 2022, n. 652, the final exam is preceded by a practical assessment. The final exam makes the degree qualifying.
Required Knowledge for Admission.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine, the student must hold a secondary school diploma or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad.
Access to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine is regulated, for each location and academic year, by numerical programming of student quotas (EU and non-EU) with a Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of University and Research (MUR).
To access the course, the candidate must have adequate initial preparation; specifically, they must have good reading comprehension skills and knowledge of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and Logical Reasoning. Such knowledge is verified in the admission test, called TOLC-VET, consisting of 50 questions to be completed in 90 minutes.
Candidates ranked within the number fixed by MUR for the course are enrolled, unless they explicitly withdraw in writing. Vacant places are filled by moving down the ranking until the programmed number is reached, for both EU and non-EU students, for the study program.
The student's academic debt, indicating the lack of specific knowledge required for admission to the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine, identified during the admission test, is remedied in the first year of the course through recovery, verification, and elimination methods, following specific additional educational obligations as per the Department's teaching regulations.
Degree Awarded.

Veterinarian in independent practice;
Specialist activities within the National Health Service: ASL and IZS;
Professional activities in the agro-zootechnical, pharmaceutical, feed, and production/transformation of animal-derived food industries;
Professional activities in Local Authorities: Municipalities, Provinces, Regions;
Professional activities in Cooperation Agencies professional activities within the European Union context: EFSA, DG SANCO, etc.;
Professional activities in Universities and Research Institutions: CNR, INRCA, etc.;
Professional activities in the Military Veterinary Corps of the Army professional activities in Ministries Communication Skills.
The graduate in Veterinary Medicine must be able to communicate effectively with clients, non-experts, colleagues, and Authorities on medical-veterinary topics, basic and specialized, and be able to listen and respond using appropriate language according to the context and interlocutor. They must also be able to communicate, both in writing and orally, about basic and specialized medical-veterinary topics. In addition to Italian, they must be able to communicate efficiently in English, using specific medical and contextual terminology. Communication skills are verified and assessed through case discussions and methodologies in the context of exercises, orientation, internships, exams, and the final exam.
