Autonomy of Judgment.
The master's degree graduate in veterinary medicine must be able to act, in daily practice, with full autonomy of judgment in the exercise of the profession, supported by their own knowledge, skills, and abilities, to improve the quality of care, animal well-being, and public health. Being aware of their ethical responsibilities towards individual animals or groups of animals, clients, and the community, the veterinarian operates with the understanding that their professional decisions may have decisive impacts on the environment and society.
The acquisition of the ability to exercise autonomy of judgment is achieved during the course of study, through practical exercises and simulations, and is verified during the final examination for each discipline.
Learning Ability.
The veterinary medicine graduate must possess adequate experience in independent study and the organization of their ongoing education, and have the ability to independently conduct bibliographic research in databases and professional update websites. They must be capable of critically reading scientific articles, even in English, to understand international literature and stay updated.
At the end of the study path, they will have acquired a cultural background enabling them to pursue the third cycle of university studies: PhD, specialized schools, or second-level university master's programs.
Learning assessments are conducted through passing exams and conclude with the evaluation of the final test.
Knowledge and Understanding.
BASIC SUBJECTS Knowledge and Understanding
The knowledge acquired in the field of basic subjects should be considered introductory for a better understanding of the fundamental subjects of veterinary culture. Preparation in the fields of physical, chemical, biochemical, and biological (animal and plant) sciences should be viewed in the context of understanding the basic concepts underlying knowledge of anatomy, physiology, pharmacology and toxicology, and animal pathology.
At the end of the training activity, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
 The main stages of morphogenesis, from fertilization to embryonic development; the morphology of embryonic appendages; the structural and ultrastructural organization of the animal cell (cytology), particularly the composition of the cytoplasm, nucleus, and morphology of various cellular organelles; the morphological characteristics of various animal tissues; the morphological characteristics of bones in different animal species, major joints, and muscles.
 The macroscopic and microscopic characteristics of the various organ systems of veterinary interest mammals.
 The general context of the zootechnical enterprise. This should be evaluated in terms of its technical and economic characteristics.
 Knowledge of the main browsers available, specific search methods using major search engines; ability to create a document with specific structural and content guidelines; ability to create and use a spreadsheet with formulas and graphs; create a presentation focused on a specific topic.
 Knowledge of the nervous mechanisms regulating physiological activities of the organism; knowledge of muscle metabolism and movement control; understanding the importance of metabolic regulation for thermoregulatory and productive purposes; knowledge of mechanisms regulating lactation synthesis and secretion; knowledge of hormone secretion mechanisms and how they regulate organic homeostasis; knowledge of mechanisms for digesting carbohydrates, lipids, and non-protein nitrogen; the fate of digestion products in relation to animal health/well-being and production; ability to collect rumen fluid and perform its chemical-physical and microbiological analysis.
 Isolation and identification of the main types of veterinary interest microorganisms, understanding their organization, and interpreting their variability and evolution; different types of immune response; main diagnostic (direct and indirect) and preventive (vaccines) methods used for controlling infectious diseases; immunopathology.
 Basic molecular knowledge necessary for understanding biological systems; the role and function of macromolecules and their interactions in cellular metabolism and information transmission; all competencies necessary to learn physiological mechanisms required for maintaining homeostasis under physiological and pathological conditions and the action of drugs.
 Adequate knowledge of the main taxa of invertebrates and vertebrates and plant species of veterinary interest, being able to describe their characteristics using appropriate scientific terminology; understanding the role of these taxa for the veterinary profession, as well as the role of ecological conditions in the evolution of studied species.
ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS AND ZOOTECHNICAL SCIENCES
The veterinary medicine student, within the zootechnical and animal production context, must know and understand:
 Knowledge on animal nutrition and feeding for the main species of veterinary and zootechnical interest in different life and production stages; developing strongly characteristic competencies for the veterinary profession in an increasingly globalized context, aimed at meeting numerous aspects of correct animal nutrition and feeding in consideration of current regulations, ethics, circularity, sustainability, environmental protection, and prevention, animal health and well-being, food chain safety, and One Health; main aspects of animal nutrition and feeding and the main characteristics, evaluation, and utilization of common animal feeds.
 Characteristics of different breeds of domestic species raised (for profit and companionship) with particular attention to morphological differences resulting from different selective pressures in major breeds; their characteristics and peculiarities and their distribution nationally and internationally; molecular foundations of genetic information, heritability of traits, main qualitative genes involved in the expression of phenotypic traits, and main quantitative genes involved in different production performances.
 On production chains and breeding systems for broiler chickens, laying hens, breeder chickens, and meat rabbits. For different productive categories of poultry and rabbits, housing methods, management of reproductive and productive phases, and feeding techniques are presented with attention to animal well-being, product quality, and environmental respect.
 Information for a correct and autonomous morpho-functional evaluation of domestic animals, effective management of farm hygiene, and knowledge of autonomous research of appropriate traditional and digital sources related to animal breeding.
 Breeding technologies for the main species of zootechnical interest aimed at improving farm profitability and production quality while respecting the environment and animal well-being.
PRE-CLINICAL DISCIPLINES AND ANIMAL HEALTH
The courses in the pre-clinical area and veterinary public health constitute one of the foundations of the veterinary profession and include disciplines preparatory for clinical and inspection activities. The student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
 Classification of lesions by organ, system, or apparatus related to etiology; species-specific pathologies and characteristic lesion patterns with differences between animal species; etiopathogenesis, evolutionary phases, and diagnostic-orientative significance in reversible and irreversible disease forms; main pathologies of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, cardiovascular, skin, and lymphatic systems; importance of certain pathologies due to their zoonotic nature or international spread; classification systems (histological and cytological) of lesions; criteria for differentiating inflammatory from neoplastic lesions; main criteria for malignancy to distinguish between benign and malignant neoplastic lesions.
 Main pathogenic mechanisms, their classification, and the morphological alterations (macroscopic, histological) they cause; knowledge of main morphological alterations; knowledge of some zoonotic pathologies; knowledge of necropsy phases and correct preparation of the necropsy report.
 Knowledge of the fundamentals of using main classes of clinically useful veterinary drugs, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic uses, side effects, and toxicities; knowledge of the fundamentals of Toxicology, toxicokinetics, and toxicodynamics of main xenobiotics responsible for animal poisoning.
 Competencies on Infectious Diseases affecting domestic animals, with particular reference to pathologies affecting companion animals and equine species, integrating fundamental aspects of veterinary public health at the end of the two Infectious Diseases courses.
 Demonstrate knowledge of etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, prevention, and therapy of main parasitic diseases of animals; ability to perform: fecal smears; copromicroscopic examinations; parasitological examinations of organs and viscera; issue clinical diagnoses and administer anti-parasitic treatments.
 Knowledge and understanding of avian anatomy, functioning of organ systems, and main pathologies of birds, particularly etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnosis, and direct and indirect prevention of poultry diseases.
 Physio-pathological mechanisms responsible for main alterations of organism homeostatic systems and causes and mechanisms leading to damage, organism response, and repair strategies.
CLINICAL DISCIPLINES
Knowledge acquired in basic and pre-clinical subjects is fundamental for understanding organ and system pathologies in medical, surgical, and obstetric fields. In all these areas, practical and analytical understanding abilities, along with autonomy of judgment, are required and assessed, considered essential for professional training in clinical settings.
The student must acquire the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
 Knowledge of methods for conducting clinical examinations on small and large domestic animals affected by surgical pathology, both directly and using instruments, to issue diagnosis, prognosis, and propose therapy including anesthesia and analgesia; b) rational approach to scientific and clinical reasoning, considering respective strengths and limitations.
 Acquire a logical-practical method of clinical reasoning applied to companion and profit animal clinics to formulate diagnosis in life of diseases, issue prognosis, and choose appropriate therapy.
 On etiopathogenesis and correct conduct of clinical examinations in various domestic animal species, on the interpretative methodology of symptoms and clinical signs for diagnosing common surgical concerns. The course aims to provide the basis for performing and interpreting main diagnostic methods used in a correct diagnostic process.
 On etiology, pathophysiology, clinical signs, and diagnosis of main internal medicine pathologies of domestic animals; performance of general and specific organ system examinations and interpretation of anamnestic data, reports, symptoms, clinical findings, and laboratory results; autonomy of judgment in assessing animal health status; communication skills and correct use of medical terminology; ability to learn within veterinary medical semiotics and pathology; and ability for independent study.
INSPECTION AREA
The disciplines of the inspection area provide students with knowledge and competencies related to the production chain of animal-derived food products and to evaluate the hygiene and safety of animal productions and the processing and transformation of the final product, integrating technological, national and international regulatory, and health aspects. Theoretical and practical knowledge acquired through the study of animal productions, pathological anatomy, infectious and parasitic diseases, and public health are necessary for understanding the teachings delivered within the inspection area.
At the end of the course, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the following topics:
 Fresh meat and meat-based product supply chains, fish products, eggs and egg products, honey and hive products (1.8). In particular, they must demonstrate the ability to monitor and evaluate the correct application of hygiene and health regulations to maintain consumer health and food safety, and to know the risk assessment, management, and communication system within different food supply chains. The ability to connect different aspects and topics covered in the integrated course and the acquisition of tools to develop critical analysis of concrete cases will be valued.
The disciplines of the inspection area provide students with knowledge and competencies related to the production chain of animal-derived food products and to evaluate the hygiene and safety of animal productions and the processing and transformation of the final product, integrating technological, national and international regulatory, and health aspects. Theoretical and practical knowledge acquired through the study of animal productions, pathological anatomy, infectious and parasitic diseases, and public health are necessary for understanding the teachings delivered within the inspection area.
These competencies will be acquired and refined through practical activities in small groups, orientation activities, and inspection sector internships (7 CFU for a total of 175 hours), during which the student actively participates in practical activities under the supervision of the course instructor and/or veterinary personnel from SSN structures (ASL, zooprophylactic institutes) or authorized agri-food sector companies.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
BASIC SUBJECTS
Basic scientific knowledge is essential for understanding the disciplines characterizing the veterinary medicine degree course. Knowledge of these subjects is developed throughout the curriculum, particularly refined through practical activities (biochemistry and molecular biology lab, microscope room, computer lab, dissection room, guided visits to companies) and orientation activities. The student must acquire the ability to work in groups and, starting from the first year, practical skills in handling veterinary interest animals. All practical activities are recorded in the Log-book.
The student must be able to apply knowledge:
 On cell and tissue morphology to the study of organs and systems of Domestic Animal Anatomy.
 Recognize each organ within various organ systems. Additionally, the study of microscopic characteristics of various organs will aid in understanding and studying pathological organs and structures.
 On the general context of the zootechnical enterprise in applied form, regarding the relationship between veterinary services and the entrepreneur's business objectives. In particular, with regard to achieving break-even points and positive revenue-cost balance, as well as quality control systems for producing a final product aligned with given specifications.
 To solve problems related to organ and system physiology and provide a pathophysiological interpretation of disease signs and symptoms; evaluate organ system function, hormonal and nervous control of different physiological processes to assess overall organism function; establish a correlation between animal feed intake and health/well-being status and production quantity/quality; correctly collect rumen fluid samples, evaluate causes modifying nervous and hormonal mechanisms regulating physiological processes based on animal production and health status; evaluate causes and mechanisms of nutritional origin leading to reduced growth, lower production, and metabolic dysfunctions such as ruminal acidosis, meteorism, and non-protein nitrogen intoxication.
 Critically examine and evaluate literature and presentations; collect, preserve, and transport samples, choose appropriate diagnostic tests, interpret and understand test result limitations; on principles of disease prevention and promotion of health and well-being.
 Work safely in a chemical/biochemical laboratory and apply logical approaches of the experimental method to experimental and clinical reasoning.
 Related to the scientific approach and correct scientific terminology; in zoological and botanical contexts, demonstrate the ability to consider the overall environmental characteristics influencing these species; demonstrate assimilation of the importance of synergizing different scientific competencies to enable the veterinarian to implement a correct scientific research and knowledge approach, as well as interact with colleagues of different scientific backgrounds.
ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS AND ZOOTECHNICAL SCIENCES
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to:
 Possess knowledge and understanding abilities to develop and/or apply original ideas in the context of animal nutrition and feeding.
 Demonstrate knowledge of breed characteristics based on breed and production purpose; the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the subject to establish logical connections to answer examination questions; highlight morphological differences resulting from selection for specific use and understand the final (evolutionary) meaning of a particular trait; accurately know the methods for controlling and evaluating breeders to improve population.
 Analysis of poultry and rabbit supply chains with reference to breeding and feeding techniques, improving animal well-being and environmental management, and quality assessment of products. They must also demonstrate acquisition of.
 Independently evaluate the morpho-functional characteristics of domestic animals; apply knowledge to animal breeding techniques; acquire autonomy in researching sources and studying.
 Physiological and well-being needs of animals and managerial and profitability needs of operators; modern techniques for breeding.
PRE-CLINICAL DISCIPLINES AND ANIMAL HEALTH
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to demonstrate knowledge and concepts useful for:
 Establishing correlations between certain pathologies and lesions, also considering possible associated cytological and histological patterns. They must also demonstrate the ability to prepare a cytological report and a histological diagnosis aimed at reaching a final diagnostic judgment.
 Demonstrate possession and application of knowledge and concepts to establish correlations between lesion development and possible consequences on organ/tissue/cell function; ability to perform a necropsy and correct histological sampling, compile a final report with one or more morphological diagnoses to determine the cause of animal death.
 Apply acquired knowledge for correct drug selection and use in clinical practice, e.g., choice of administration route, emergency therapy, maintenance therapy, species-specific differences, veterinary drug legislation; apply knowledge to recognize and treat acute and chronic intoxications in animals.
 Apply and integrate knowledge to solve problems related to infectious diseases affecting domestic animals.
 Demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge to correlate etiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and control of parasitic diseases with a correct diagnostic process.
 Apply avian anatomy, organ system functioning, and main pathologies of birds, particularly etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnosis, and direct and indirect prevention of poultry diseases, and integrate these knowledge to solve problems related to anatomical, physiological, and pathological characteristics.
 Correlate and understand the relationships between cause, mechanisms triggered by noxae, and the organism's pathophysiological state in response to such stimuli.
CLINICAL DISCIPLINES
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to acquire the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
 Ability to perform basic surgical techniques during soft tissue surgery, such as excision, removal, hemostasis, and suturing; ability to choose, dose, and administer the appropriate anesthetic and analgesic agent for specific surgical procedures, as well as monitor anesthesia.
 The student must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge to clinical practice, managing a clinical case with critical and autonomous capacity, according to POA, or evaluating a forensic report.
 To complete clinical examinations in various domestic animal species and demonstrate decision-making clinical process ability; autonomy of study, promoting the use of assimilated knowledge, preparatory for applying clinical examinations and fundamental surgical techniques for developing a correct diagnostic and therapeutic process in evaluating various clinical cases; safely and respectfully manage animal patients; develop the ability to apply these knowledge and solve problems related to new or unfamiliar topics; communicate clearly and unambiguously to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors; understand the ethical and professional responsibilities of the veterinarian in relation to animals under their care, the environment, clients, policies, and society.
INSPECTION AREA
Learning knowledge in this area will enable the veterinary medicine graduate to acquire the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
 On food hygiene and safety, particularly the existence of internationally important diseases representing national and international risks to biosafety and trade; the student must demonstrate knowledge of legislation regarding movement of raw materials and diseases with mandatory reporting of public health veterinary issues, zoonoses, and food hygiene and technology, and possess concepts useful for conducting control activities and issuing inspection judgments.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Associated Competencies.
Veterinarian
To adequately perform their professional functions, the veterinary medicine graduate must acquire competencies enabling them to operate in various areas of the profession.
1. To perform their function in clinical settings, they must be able to assess and evaluate the health and well-being status of an individual animal or group of animals and develop appropriate treatment plans in the interest of patients, considering available resources. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: provide advice to owners on breeding, feeding, medications to administer, and vaccinations to maintain animal health; collect information for a correct anamnesis; identify the pathological state of the animal; develop a therapeutic program appropriate to the identified pathology, species, and age of the animal; plan a verification program to assess disease progression and therapy effectiveness, adapting to new conditions.
2. To operate correctly in the context of zootechnical productions, they must be able to assess the physical condition, well-being, and nutritional status of an animal or group of animals and advise clients on breeding and feeding principles. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: analyze the needs expressed by the breeder; use biotechnology, feeding plans, and breeding techniques to improve animal condition and zootechnical production, respecting animal well-being and the environment; provide breeders with preventive measures to avoid disease spread within farms (e.g., separating animals by age and physical condition, etc.); monitor animal health status in reproductive aspects, regularly subjecting them to examinations and checks to improve fertility; apply assisted reproduction techniques (induction and synchronization of ovulation, artificial insemination, etc.).
3. To exercise in the field of animal health, the veterinary medicine graduate must be able to develop and advise on prevention and prophylaxis programs for individual animal species in line with accepted standards of animal health and public health, recognize suspicious symptoms of reportable and zoonotic diseases, and take appropriate actions, including notification to competent authorities. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: construct and update animal health registers; plan and carry out required controls, prophylaxis, and periodic clinical examinations; prepare intervention measures as required by law in case of public health threats; carry out extraordinary interventions (non-specialist emergency clinical activities, wildlife population control, etc.) following reports from private individuals, law enforcement, or public bodies.
4. To operate in the field of inspection of animal-derived food products, the veterinary medicine graduate must be able to assess and critically evaluate the salubrity, hygiene, and quality of animal-derived food products. To this end, they must possess the following competencies: verify the hygiene of vehicles used for transporting animal food products; verify compliance with hygiene regulations regarding cleaning and maintenance of premises, equipment, and facilities; verify the hygienic quality of raw materials, semi-finished products, and final products by submitting samples for laboratory testing; verify self-control systems (HACCP); create and manage quality control systems in the agri-food production sector; develop the hygienic-sanitary self-control plan based on HACCP certification or compliance with mandatory certification requirements; evaluate compliance of business processes with the developed plan; prepare corrective actions for any non-conformities found; provide technical and practical guidance for continuous system improvement. Additionally, they must oversee the correct management of the slaughter phase through pre-slaughter inspection of animals to verify correct identification, absence of diseases transmissible to humans or animals, and symptoms of diseases that may render meat unfit for consumption; perform post-mortem inspection of the carcass (heart, lungs, liver) of the slaughtered animal; supervise meat sanitization; collect blood samples for hygienic and sanitary verification on refrigerated carcasses.
Work Context Function.
Veterinarian
The veterinarian performs their professional activity in service to the community and to protect animal and human health. As specified in Article 1 of the code of ethics, the Veterinarian is dedicated to:
- Protecting humans and animals from dangers and damages arising from the environment, animal diseases, and consumption of food or other animal-derived products;
- Preventing, diagnosing, and treating animal diseases and safeguarding their well-being;
- Conserving and developing the zootechnical heritage;
- Conserving and safeguarding the environment and wildlife heritage, guided by principles of biodiversity protection and compatible coexistence with humans;
- Engaging in activities related to companion, sport competition, and exotic animals;
- Promoting respect for animals and their well-being as sentient beings;
- Promoting hygiene and health prevention campaigns and education for a correct human-animal-environment relationship;
- Engaging in activities related to food production, their correct management, and evaluation of risks related to food safety management.
To perform these professional activities, the Veterinarian can work as an employee, collaborator on specific projects, or as a self-employed professional; in the latter case, registration with the veterinary order of the competent province is required. The veterinarian must also possess good communication skills and be able to effectively interface with their clients/users.
Description of Specific Training Objectives.
The master's degree course in Veterinary Medicine is a single-cycle program with limited access and mandatory attendance, aiming to train graduates with technical-professional and ethical competencies enabling them to perform their functions in the care and prevention of diseases in profit, companion, and non-conventional species, in animal well-being protection, and in the correct technical and sanitary management of production, nutrition, and reproduction of farmed species, in the sanitary surveillance of animals raised within the national health service, particularly in the prevention of zoonotic disease spread and its potential economic impacts, in the control of animal-derived food products and specific production technologies. The objective of the master's degree course is to provide graduates with the fundamental knowledge and abilities for the practice of the Veterinary Medicine profession, following the guidelines of the European Association of Establishment for Veterinary Education (EAEVE) and national guidelines.
The quality of veterinary medicine training is achieved through a structured educational process within a five-year study program, organized in two semesters per year for a total of ten semesters. The student must gradually acquire specific knowledge and competencies to independently make professional choices in diagnostic-therapeutic contexts and in the care, control, and eradication of diseases.
In the first and second years, basic science subjects (physics, chemistry, biology, informatics, and biostatistics) and part of the basic veterinary science subjects necessary for understanding the healthy animal (biochemistry, anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, zootechnics and genetic improvement, including management of profit and companion animal farms, general pathology, and microbiology) are covered. In the third, fourth, and fifth years, characteristic activities focusing on preventive and health aspects (pathological anatomy, epidemiology, infectious and parasitic diseases including zoonotic ones, veterinary public health, pharmacology and toxicology), inspection (hygiene, quality, and safety of animal-derived food products), clinical (small animal, equine, and profit animal clinical practice and propaedeutics, medical, surgical, and obstetric pathology, anesthesiology and intensive therapy, imaging diagnostics), and integrative (client communication, bioethics, and economic management of farms and veterinary facilities) subjects are addressed, paying attention to species-specific peculiarities. Parallel to this, from the first year, students engage in practical activities within various courses, both at department facilities (University Veterinary Teaching Hospital, teaching paddocks, teaching labs and research labs) and at public or private entities and foreign universities with agreements. In the first and second years, students acquire practical competencies necessary for safe interaction in various breeding contexts with ruminants, swine, equines, and companion animals, respecting their specific ethological characteristics. In the third year, they learn competencies related to the productive and health management of profit animal farms and the management of animals housed at the department and teaching hospital. In the fourth year, they carry out activities in the territory at companion animal shelters (e.g., municipal kennels), profit animal farms, and wildlife recovery facilities to acquire necessary competencies for sanitary, productive, and clinical approaches in different contexts. In the fifth year, students carry out internship activities at university and national or foreign partner institutions to acquire professional competencies in the various sectors of veterinary medicine practice, in accordance with the "Day one competences" established by the European Association of Establishments for Veterinary Education and European regulations. According to Articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, No. 163, the final examination for the single-cycle master's degree in veterinary medicine (class LM-42) authorizes the exercise of the veterinary medicine profession. For this purpose, the final examination includes a practical assessment of professional competencies acquired during the internship, aimed at verifying the candidate's preparation level for professional authorization before the thesis defense. In particular, students acquire practical-professional competencies in the following sectors: companion animal, equine, and exotic animal clinical practice; veterinary public health and food safety; animal productions and veterinary medicine for profit animals. Practical and internship competencies are documented in a specific document (LogBook). Throughout the program, attention is paid to the acquisition by students of 'Day one competences' (DOCs), a list of fundamental knowledge and competencies that the new graduate must possess from their first day after graduation. These competencies are detailed in a document drafted by the European Coordinating Committee on Veterinary Training and adopted by EAEVE, specified for each course. The objective is to monitor the alignment of minimum standards set for the veterinary education program, established by the European Union Directive 2005/36, and to evaluate, promote, and further improve the quality standards of the structures training the Veterinarian.

High school diploma Fees and contributions Regulations - Fees Roles Student representative for the course of study ROSALBA TEDDE Chair LUIGI NONNE, GIOVANNA MARIA ANTONIETTA FODDAI Program, texts and objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Lawyer, Judge, Notary, Legal expert in companies and public administrations The Master's degree guarantees access to all high-level legal professional activities: law, judiciary, notary; managerial roles within banks, insurance companies, companies, independent authorities, public administrations, European and international institutions.
Regarding access to legal professions, graduates must follow different procedures depending on the profession they aim for. For law and notary, the degree is accompanied by a period of legal or notarial practice of varying duration, depending on whether it begins during the final phase of the study path or is taken concurrently with the specialization school for legal professions. For the judiciary, additional qualifications are required beyond the Master's degree, including the specialization school for legal professions, which is directly managed by universities. Competitions for other highly specialized professions involve internal procedures or external access, always requiring the possession of a degree in Jurisprudence.
Final exam characteristics.
The degree is obtained through the completion of a final work (thesis) that has the characteristics of an original product, developed under the guidance of a supervisor and subsequently presented to the graduation committee for final discussion.
Required knowledge for access.
To enroll in the Master's degree in Jurisprudence, it is necessary to hold a high school diploma. The law does not impose any numerical limit on enrollments. At the beginning of the academic year, all enrolled students must take a test to verify initial knowledge - concerning general culture - which consists of a non-selective access test to assess students' preparation, preceded by an introductory course to legal studies.
Degree awarded.
Master's degree in GIURISPRUDENZA Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Lawyer, Judge, Notary, Legal expert in companies and public administrations The Master's degree guarantees access to all high-level legal professional activities: law, judiciary, notary; managerial roles within banks, insurance companies, companies, independent authorities, public administrations, European and international institutions.
Regarding access to legal professions, graduates must follow different procedures depending on the profession they aim for. For law and notary, the degree is accompanied by a period of legal or notarial practice of varying duration, depending on whether it begins during the final phase of the study path or is taken concurrently with the specialization school for legal professions. For the judiciary, additional qualifications are required beyond the Master's degree, including the specialization school for legal professions, which is directly managed by universities. Competitions for other highly specialized professions involve internal procedures or external access, always requiring the possession of a degree in Jurisprudence.

Communication Skills.
Graduates must be able to clearly and articulately communicate normative data and related principles. They must also be able to identify problems and provide solutions, adapting communication methods to different interlocutors. To this end, the degree course is also oriented towards acquiring an appropriate and rigorous legal language, as well as the ability to process written texts.
Learning Abilities.
Graduates must possess in-depth interpretative, case analysis, legal qualification (relating facts to legal facts), comprehension, representation, evaluation, and awareness capabilities to address interpretative and application problems of law.
They must also possess the basic tools for updating their own competencies.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1158] LAW
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: 5-year Single Cycle
SECTION: Judgment autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10431

Judgment autonomy.
Graduates of the degree course must be able to identify, collect, and critically analyze normative data, correlating them with concrete problems that may arise, also through the study of doctrine and jurisprudence.
Graduates must also have the ability to formulate autonomous judgments and to contextualize problems in an interdisciplinary manner.
Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Graduates of the degree course must:
- have acquired elements of in-depth knowledge of basic national and European legal culture, also using case-based techniques and methodologies, in relation to themes useful for understanding and evaluating principles or institutions of positive law
- have acquired in-depth historical knowledge that allows for the evaluation of institutions of positive law also from the perspective of their historical evolution
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Graduates of the degree course must:
- possess the ability to produce clear, relevant, and effective legal texts (normative and/or contractual and/or procedural) in relation to the employment contexts, well-argued, also using computer tools
The teaching methods and tools through which learning outcomes are achieved include:
- lectures
- exercises
- seminars
- legal laboratories
- individual meetings, particularly with the thesis supervisor during the thesis preparation.
Relevant are also the internships carried out by the student, which constitute useful tools for applying acquired knowledge.
Regarding the teaching tools for assessment:
- regarding seminar activities: written or oral reports;
- final exams in individual courses, possibly preceded by intermediate tests;
- outcome of internships certified by host organizations.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Associated competencies for the role.
Lawyer, Judge, Notary, Legal expert in companies and public administrations
The Master's Degree ensures the necessary competencies for performing typical legal professions of the same degree: namely, judiciary, notary, and legal practice.
It also enables operation in sectors requiring in-depth legal preparation in various fields of law: for example, managerial roles in state administration, local authorities, and all other public and private bodies, or in non-governmental organizations of the so-called third sector; independent practice as labor consultants or tax specialists.
The in-depth study of international law subjects enables access as officials in international organizations such as the European Union, Council of Europe, United Nations, FAO, UNESCO.
The presence in the study plan of economic subjects provides the competencies suitable for performing the role of administrator in entities or private companies and completes preparation for public professions.
Function in work context.
Lawyer, Judge, Notary, Legal expert in companies and public administrations
Graduates of the degree course, in addition to directing themselves towards legal professions and the judiciary, may carry out activities and be employed in functions characterized by high responsibility in various fields of social, socio-economic, and political activity or in institutions, public administrations, private companies, trade unions, in the field of information technology law, in the field of comparative, international, and community law (European lawyer), as well as in international organizations where the jurist's analytical, evaluative, and decision-making skills prove fruitful even beyond sector-specific content knowledge.
Description of specific learning objectives.
Graduates of the degree course must:
- have acquired elements of in-depth knowledge of basic national and European legal culture, also using case-based techniques and methodologies, in relation to themes useful for understanding and evaluating principles or institutions of positive law;
- have acquired a comprehensive body of historical knowledge that allows for the evaluation of institutions of positive law also from the perspective of their historical evolution;
- possess the ability to produce - also using computer tools - clear, relevant, and effective legal texts (normative and/or contractual and/or procedural) in relation to employment contexts and well-argued;
- possess in-depth interpretative, case-based analytical, legal qualification (relating concrete facts to abstract scenarios by studying their jurisprudential application), understanding, representation, and evaluation skills necessary to address interpretative and application problems of law;
- possess in-depth basic tools for updating their own competencies.
Graduates of the degree course, in addition to directing themselves towards legal professions and the judiciary, may carry out activities and be employed in functions characterized by high responsibility in various fields of social, socio-economic, and political activity or in institutions, public administrations, private companies, trade unions, in the field of information technology law, in the field of comparative, international, and community law (European lawyer), as well as in international organizations where the jurist's analytical, evaluative, and decision-making skills prove fruitful even beyond sector-specific content knowledge.

Master's Degree Class LM-46 - Class of Master's Degrees in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis Interuniversity Course No Programmed Access Location SASSARI Department MEDICINE, SURGERY AND PHARMACY Website https://sdr.medicinachirurgia.uniss.it/it/didattica/odontoiatria-e-protesi-dentaria  Fees and contributions Regulation for Careers - Fees Roles President AUREA MARIA IMMACOLATA LUMBAU Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Dentists and Oral Surgeons Graduates in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis have employment opportunities in the field of Private Practice as a Dentist.
They can carry out, according to current regulations, managerial activities of I and II level within the National Health Service.
Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to take the graduation exam, the student must have attended all courses and passed the respective exams.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, No. 163, the final exam for the completion of the single-cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis - Class LM-46 enables the exercise of the profession of dentist. For this purpose, the aforementioned final exam includes the performance of a Practical Assessment Test (PAT) of professional skills acquired through an Internal Practical-Valuation Internship (PVI), aimed at verifying the candidate's practical preparation level for professional qualification, which precedes the defense of the thesis. The PAT is organized through the student's discussion of 3 multidisciplinary clinical cases treated as the primary operator during the PVI, involving multidisciplinary treatment plans with services related to the majority of disciplines covered by the PVI, according to the procedures established by the protocol drawn up by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis Degree Courses, in agreement with the National Dental Register Commission. To pass the PAT, students receive an assessment of suitability, after which they proceed to the defense of the thesis.
Therefore, for the completion of the Master's Degree, the submission of an original thesis developed by the student under the guidance of a supervisor is required. The entire graduation committee acts as co-supervisor during the defense, otherwise a correlating lecturer may be appointed. The determination of the grade occurs according to the procedures established by the Academic Body in line with the regulations set by the University.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis (CLMOPD), one must possess a Diploma from a five-year secondary school or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable under current regulations.
The single-cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is subject to numerical limitation in accordance with Article 1 of Law 264/99.
The didactic organization of CLMOPD requires that students admitted to the first year possess adequate knowledge of the Italian language and initial preparation, obtained from previous studies, covering logic, general culture, biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics.
The verification of the student's initial knowledge is considered completed upon passing the admission test.
Students admitted to the course who show initial gaps will be assigned an Additional Educational Obligation (AEO) to be fulfilled during the first year of the course according to criteria defined in the Course Didactic Regulations.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in DENTISTRY AND DENTAL PROSTHESIS Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Dentists and Oral Surgeons Since the degree program is highly professionalizing, graduates find immediate employment opportunities after graduation; both in private practice, in public health employment, and also in university teaching.

Communication skills.
The graduate: - Possesses intermediate English language knowledge necessary for consulting scientific texts and journals
- Is able to communicate effectively with the patient and educate them on maintaining oral health. Is able to provide appropriate information based on protocols and knowledge accepted by the scientific community. - Knows how to develop an interdisciplinary clinical case approach, especially in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the work of the healthcare team. Learning ability.
The graduate: - Possesses the ability to consult databases to acquire scientific documentation and analyze scientific literature, applying research results to therapy reliably - Is able to correctly interpret legislation concerning the practice of dentistry in the European Union country where the dentist practices and to provide assistance in compliance with current medical-legal and ethical standards. Learning ability is assessed through continuous verification methods during training activities, integrating knowledge acquired during specific activities with knowledge gained through personal study, evaluating the critical contribution demonstrated during practical, seminar, and clinical internship activities, as well as through verification of the self-learning ability developed during the final project activity.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1201] DENTISTRY AND DENTAL PROSTHESIS

SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment

Autonomy of Judgment.
The graduate: - Possesses the ability to independently design and implement therapeutic programs aimed at the care and rehabilitation of the stomatognathic system - Is able to recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy - Is able to independently manage the dental treatment of the patient - Is able to evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment plan, the interventions carried out, and the results achieved. Autonomy of judgment is cultivated in the student through reading scientific articles. Specifically dedicated to the acquisition of autonomy of judgment is the development of a project, which can be a thesis project or a scientific project, culminating in an independent document with bibliography.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific methodology, linguistic and IT skills.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- fundamental principles of the functioning of information systems with reference to their main implications in the biomedical field; methods and technologies for information management;
- fundamental principles of descriptive medical statistics, the statistical terminology adopted in the scientific field for describing populations and samples, an adequate knowledge of probabilistic and inferential foundations, and the methodological elements useful for interpreting the design of a scientific study;
- basic mechanics concepts applied to the structural behavior of biomechanical systems composed of biological structures interfaced with artificial ones such as implants and prostheses; basic mechanics elements applied to the observation of the structural behavior of the human skeleton;
- general principles of psychology as indispensable references in the relationship with the patient;
- fundamental notions of pedagogy applied, in particular, to health education, understood as the implementation of awareness and responsibility processes in the exercise of the profession;
- the English language directed, in particular, to the basic knowledge of medical and dental terminology and the understanding of scientific texts;
Such foundational knowledge is acquired through mandatory attendance at courses that include frontal lectures and, if necessary, practical exercises. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Basic Disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- main concepts of mechanical, thermodynamic, and electromagnetic physics, elements of biomechanics and fluid physics. Basic concepts of nuclear physics and radioactivity applicable in dental practice.
- biological cellular and molecular mechanisms of living organisms, regarding structure, function, biomolecule turnover, and information flow from genome to proteome; cell structure, cellular compartmentalization, and processes of cell division and communication. From molecular biology to evolved biological systems.
- principles of general and organic chemistry; chemical nomenclature and representation of molecular structure, balancing of chemical reactions. Nomenclature, structure, and properties of various classes of organic compounds. Basic knowledge of biologically relevant molecules such as sugars, lipids, proteins, and heterocyclic compounds.
- structure and function of common biochemically relevant molecules and biochemical mechanisms of metabolic activities and the main qualitative and quantitative laboratory techniques;
- structural and ultrastructural organization of cells and tissues, modes of tissue renewal and their implications for regenerative medicine, methods and tools of morphological investigation, with particular reference to orofacial structures.
- fundamental knowledge of macroscopic and microscopic anatomy of various organs and systems that constitute the human body, with particular reference to the macroscopic and microscopic morphology of all components of the stomatognathic system, considering their topographical relationships and individual functional roles.
- mechanisms and modes of operation and interaction of organs and systems, with particular reference to the knowledge and understanding of the functioning of the stomatognathic system and its functional relationships with the systems and organs of the entire organism.
- complexity of pathological phenomena developing in the human body. Etiological factors and molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying pathological processes that govern tissue damage responses and their repair; fundamental biological defenses activated as a response to pathogens. Morphological alterations caused by pathogens in cells and tissues and their systemic and functional consequences for the organism. Biological bases of transformation and neoplastic disease. Pathophysiological mechanisms of cardiovascular and hematological pathologies.
- basic principles of microbiology and host-parasite relationships. With particular reference to microbiology and pathogenic microorganisms of interest in dentistry.
- morphological bases of the most frequent pathological processes in various organs and systems, with particular reference to the head and neck region, and specifically to oral cavity pathologies; modes of performing histological or cytological examinations, including the correct application of current methodologies.
- laboratory diagnostic investigations according to the main phases: pre-analytical, analytical, post-analytical; issues concerning patient preparation, sample collection, and storage;
- fundamental knowledge for the critical evaluation and interpretation of the results of the main laboratory diagnostic investigations, in addition to knowledge of the main laboratory diagnostic techniques.
Such foundational knowledge is acquired through mandatory attendance at courses that include frontal lectures and, if necessary, practical exercises. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Dental Disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare professionals;
- structure of a scientific article and methodology for researching bibliographic sources on the WEB;
- specific language of specialized disciplines;
- physical, chemical, biological, and mechanical characteristics of dental materials, their potential and limitations;
- clinical methodology and diagnostic procedures for the objective examination of the oral cavity; semiological terminology;
- oral ecosystem, natural history, and epidemiology of the most socially impactful dental pathologies (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer, dental erosions, orodental trauma, dental malocclusions);
- tools and materials for home oral hygiene, potential and limitations of systems for detecting oral mucosa and the main laboratory investigations used in odontostomatology, with particular reference to technological and applied aspects;
- procedures and correct use of materials available for evaluating dental laboratory products;
- normal and pathological aspects of soft and hard tissues of the oral cavity, from a clinical perspective, and the most frequent pathologies of the jaw bones;
- fundamental clinical diagnostic procedures;
- dental malocclusions and related joint issues; anatomical, etiopathogenetic, instrumental, and operational aspects for diagnosis, planning, and implementing therapy plans;
- potential and limitations of the main instrumental investigations used for diagnostic purposes in oral surgery; surgical instrumentation; surgical techniques and protocols; prevention of physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of surgical activities;
- epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and causal therapy of plaque-induced periodontal pathologies; pre-clinical knowledge for planning and performing causal periodontal therapy; instruments, techniques, purposes, indications, and contraindications of periodontal surgical treatment; clinical and instrumental diagnostic methods necessary for the correct planning of periodontal surgical therapy;
- theoretical and pre-clinical information in the field of prosthetic rehabilitation of partial edentulism using fixed, skeletal, or total prostheses through the production of total prosthetic devices;
- anatomical-topographical limitations of the maxillofacial region and knowledge of oral and maxillofacial semiotics; pathologies of interest in maxillofacial and otolaryngological fields such as neoplasms, trauma, congenital and acquired malformations, inflammations, cysts, salivary gland pathologies; clinical and instrumental otolaryngological semiotics;
- basic knowledge of pediatrics and pediatric pathologies with oral manifestations; pathologies of interest in pediatric dentistry and the decision-making process leading to diagnosis and planning of treatment in developing-age patients; acquisition of prevention strategies based on individual risk profiles through personalized treatments;
- indications and contraindications for implant-prosthetic rehabilitation treatment, and risk assessment in patients eligible for such treatment, characteristics of implant devices, physiological mechanisms, morphofunctional characteristics, and factors influencing the osseointegration process; techniques and prognosis of ridge augmentation and maxillary sinus lift procedures;
- theoretical, practical, and clinical criteria in the field of conservative dentistry for designing and implementing a functional and aesthetic structural restoration project for teeth; correct use of adhesive materials, coronal reconstruction in relation to dental tissue destruction, endodontic recovery of root canals;
The knowledge regarding specialized dental disciplines is acquired through mandatory attendance at courses that include frontal lectures and, through consistent participation in professional clinical internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Medical and Surgical Sciences of Interest to Dentistry The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- the pathology of the human organism in its complexity through the study of clinical medical and surgical sciences;
- pathogenetic mechanisms, general foundations of clinical, laboratory, and instrumental semiotics, therapeutic perspectives within the main systemic diseases of interest in internal medicine. Interferences that pharmacological therapy for systemic diseases may determine on dental and stomatological pathologies and therapies;
- main clinical and semiotic issues and systematic approach to the most frequent surgical diseases; clinical presentations of oncological pathologies relevant to surgery; conditions requiring emergency surgical treatment;
- areas of intervention for reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgery, biology of skin, flap, and microsurgical flaps. Main orofacial malformations requiring multidisciplinary treatment, including the dentist's intervention;
- knowledge of radiation physics, principles of radiological image formation, radiological equipment technology, and clinical information contained in reports and radiological images. Additionally, applications of imaging diagnostic techniques in the field of odontostomatology and maxillofacial;
- anatomy, physiology, and functions of the skin and mucosa for maintaining health and pathologies most frequently encountered; systematic approach to the most relevant dermatological and infectious pathologies, functional and instrumental semiotics aspects, and specific clinical methodology;
- pathophysiological bases, clinical-nosographic framework, and diagnostic process within the fields of neuropsychiatric disciplines. With particular attention to neurological syndromes, especially pathology involving the orofacial region. Psychiatric disorders in patients with odontostomatology pathology;
- classes of drugs directly and indirectly related to dental practice, with particular attention to molecular mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics, therapeutic uses, and appropriateness of use for each drug class. Adverse reactions that may occur during dental pharmacological therapy, related to the drug in use, the patient's genetic and pathophysiological characteristics, and potential interactions with other drugs the patient is taking for non-dental conditions;
- main knowledge regarding dental pathology in pediatric patients, with particular attention to the treatment of patients with special needs;
- fundamental knowledge on the modes of administration of anesthesia and specialized drugs and the management of emergencies that may occur during dental and stomatological care and therapy;
- knowledge of legislative, organizational, operational, and planning aspects of healthcare systems as a whole and the entities operating within them, operational mechanisms, and management tools used in healthcare companies to ensure a constant link between resources used and results;
The knowledge related to medical and surgical sciences is acquired through mandatory attendance at courses that include frontal lectures and clinical and laboratory internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Prevention and Dental Health Services Disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis knows and understands:
- theoretical-practical aspects, clinical criteria in the field of community dentistry; methods for relating to oral cavity diseases from a preventive perspective; designing and implementing a prevention project; knowledge in the field of health sociology and methodology of organizing health services; demographic and epidemiological aspects of oral cavity pathologies;
- useful information for evaluating one's professional activity from a normative-legal and ethical perspective with specific reference to criminal, civil, and insurance-social implications and recognizing the main forensic pathology frameworks;
The knowledge related to prevention and dental health services disciplines is acquired through mandatory attendance at courses that include frontal lectures and clinical and laboratory internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific methodology, linguistic and IT skills.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- use technology associated with information technology as a proper support for diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices and for health-level surveillance and monitoring. Develop and manage a database of their dental practice;
- design clinical studies, applying statistical-epidemiological data processing techniques, to independently perform statistical analyses and interpret their results;
- apply knowledge and basic terminology to easily consult and understand scientific literature regarding the structural biomechanics of jaws rehabilitated with prostheses and implants.
- apply knowledge of psychology as indispensable references in the relationship with the patient;
- apply pedagogical knowledge to plan health education interventions for groups and communities and to transmit basic knowledge in the field of dentistry;
- use linguistic skills necessary to understand and draft specialized documents and communicate in English on dental topics for continuous professional updating through direct consultation of authoritative textbooks and international scientific literature.
Among the teaching tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the above activities is an intensive laboratory/practical activity.
Basic Disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- apply the knowledge of basic disciplines, such as the structure and function of the human organism in homeostatic conditions at molecular, cellular, and organ/system levels, for maintaining health conditions and for the correct application of translational scientific research;
- apply the knowledge tools of etiopathogenesis of diseases, innate and specific organism defense systems, cellular and tissue damage repair processes, and neoplastic transformation mechanisms for performing any activity related to health protection.
- apply their knowledge with full understanding of the main themes of dental microbiology;
- decide, based on methodological and cultural foundations and experience, on the opportunity for specialized examinations or analyses and access to clinical biochemical data as a diagnostic tool.
- apply a technical database to address issues arising during the clinical examination, which constitute an essential part of the data related to patients in dental and stomatological practices and dental pathology.
- formulate a request for a histological examination and interpret a histopathological report, with particular reference to oral cavity pathologies.
Among the teaching tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the above activities is an intensive laboratory/practical activity.
Dental Disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- effectively and safely use the dental work environment; describe the oral ecosystem, the natural history, and the epidemiology of the most socially impactful dental pathologies (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer, dental erosions, orodental trauma);
- use the specific language of specialized disciplines;
- perform diagnosis, plan and implement treatment plans, apply prevention protocols, perform conservative therapy plans for hard dental tissue pathologies aimed at restoring morphological, functional, and aesthetic aspects while respecting the health of periodontal tissues and the functionality of the stomatognathic system;
- perform the clinical examination of the oral cavity, identifying normal anatomical structures and detecting main epidemiological indices; correctly and appropriately use semiological terminology to communicate effectively with the patient and properly interact within the dental healthcare team; organize adequate oral health promotion interventions; organize effective dental and stomatological prevention interventions for individuals and communities; identify and use tools and materials for home oral hygiene; identify potential and limitations of systems for detecting oral mucosa and the main laboratory investigations used in odontostomatology;
- critically read a scientific article; consult databases to acquire scientific documentation, applying research results to therapies reliably; identify the potential and limitations of the main instrumental investigations used for diagnostic purposes;
- perform primary and secondary prevention and diagnosis of prevalent oral mucosa and jaw bone pathologies; detect early diagnosis of potentially neoplastic and neoplastic lesions of the oral cavity;
- perform the objective examination of the oromaxillofacial district, identifying and diagnosing surgical pathologies;
- adopt protocols and behaviors to prevent physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of surgical activities; treat simple cases of oral surgery; identify treatment priorities and collaborate with other specialists in planning interventions aimed at patient recovery; evaluate the effectiveness of surgical interventions and the results achieved; recognize and correctly use surgical instrumentation;
- develop a multidisciplinary clinical case approach and coordinate a surgical team, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare professionals; detect and motivate informed consent for surgical therapy;
- obtain adequate photographic documentation of the oral cavity; evaluate the use of appropriate prosthetic materials and techniques in relation to different clinical conditions;
- apply causal therapy protocols for endodontic and periradicular pathologies of endodontic origin adaptable to individual patients; implement endodontic therapy plans even in high-risk patients, with the aim of morphologically and functionally restoring the affected dental elements;
- assess the severity of issues related to orthognathic diagnosis and the diagnosis and treatment of temporomandibular joint dysfunctions; apply available orthodontic techniques for treating the same in developing age and adults; identify the type of approach for planning gnatological rehabilitation treatment;
- apply theoretical and pre-clinical knowledge for diagnosis and treatment planning, for performing causal periodontal therapy, and for the correct use of periodontal instrumentation; understand the nature, advantages, and limitations of periodontal surgery; formulate diagnosis and treatment plans for complex periodontal cases requiring surgical treatment;
- apply theoretical knowledge and pre-clinical skills for formulating a diagnosis and treatment plan for partial edentulism rehabilitation using fixed prostheses, for taking impressions in fixed prosthesis, and for creating stone models; formulate diagnosis, treatment plan, and prognosis for prosthetic rehabilitation with PPR; design and implement all phases of PPR prosthetic production, from clinical examination to delivery;
- perform a specific evaluation of maxillofacial and otolaryngological pathologies of interest; perform anamnesis, clinical examination, and treatment of oral cavity pathologies in pediatric patients; implement preventive strategies for the main pediatric odontostomatology pathologies; diagnose infectious, surgical, and mechanical complications of implant-prosthetic rehabilitation treatment; plan and implement maintenance of implant health; treat infectious, surgical, and mechanical complications of rehabilitation treatment.
Among the teaching tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of specialized dental activities are intensive laboratory activities on manikins and clinical internships with patients, in addition to the discussion, re-elaboration, and presentation of clinical cases.
Medical and Surgical Sciences of Interest to Dentistry The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- understand and apply the specific language of these disciplines; interpret the main pathological presentations and diagnose their connections with dental pathology;
- recognize the most common internal medicine clinical presentations and evaluate the clinical/dental implications of systemic pathology; critically evaluate and correlate clinical symptoms, physical signs, interpreting their pathogenetic mechanisms and deepening their clinical significance; adequate clinical reasoning ability to analyze common and relevant clinical problems; correct approach to the treatment of oral pathologies associated with systemic diseases of interest in internal medicine;
- conduct a correct clinical approach to patients with surgical problems: prepare the patient for surgery and prevent, then address, potential surgical complications. Adequate interaction with the surgical team;
- resolve issues concerning the application of imaging diagnostic techniques in the field of odontostomatology and maxillofacial; ability to clinically contextualize information contained in reports and radiological images.
- quantify and manage perioperative anxiety in dentistry for pediatric, elderly, and disabled patients.
- apply neurological knowledge in the diagnosis and treatment of headaches and facial and head neuralgia of odontostomatology origin; understand potential implications of pharmacological therapy for neuropsychiatric conditions on dental and stomatological pathologies and therapies;
- identify the appropriate anesthetic and correct administration technique for each patient based on their systemic condition, recognize complications, and apply initial resuscitation maneuvers;
- design and organize a dental clinic in compliance with legal requirements, with a correct doctor/patient relationship from a legal and contractual perspective;
- develop a clinical approach based on modern evidence-based methodology for correct diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up management.
Among the teaching tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of these activities are intensive laboratory activities and clinical internships with patients, in addition to the discussion, re-elaboration, and presentation of clinical cases.
Prevention and Dental Health Services Disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis is able to:
- correctly complete the clinical record and identify the areas of intervention where it is mandatory to forward the report or report a crime to the judicial authority; acquire valid informed consent in the dental field; establish a correct relationship with the patient; maintain confidentiality and information obligations; recognize common occupational diseases and areas of medical-legal interest in dentistry; guide professional conduct in accordance with current Italian legal obligations.
- apply knowledge in the field of general and applied hygiene and manage knowledge of health determinants and main risk factors in the interaction between humans, their physical-social environment, and the microbial world.
Among the teaching tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of these disciplines are intensive laboratory activities and internships.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Function.
Dentists and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
Self-employment,
Public Health Employment,
University Employment.
Function in Work Context.
Dentists and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons Graduates will be able to:
- know the full range of general dentistry within the context of global patient treatment without producing additional risks for the patient and the environment;
- identify treatment priorities in line with needs, participating with other professionals in planning interventions aimed at reducing oral diseases in the community based on knowledge of the principles and practice of community dentistry;
- learn the fundamentals of human pathology, integrating physiological and pathological study with clinical methodology and diagnostic procedures that allow the evaluation of major disease patterns; learn the main correlational patterns and complementary medical and surgical therapeutic procedures to the dental profession, as well as being introduced to basic knowledge of care and assistance according to pedagogical, psychological, sociological, and ethical principles;
- know drugs directly and indirectly related to dentistry practice and understand the implications of pharmacological therapy for systemic diseases regarding dental therapies;
- know the science of biomaterials as it pertains to dentistry practice;
- control cross-infection to prevent physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of the profession;
- know the full range of anxiety and pain control techniques related to dental treatments (within the limits permitted to the dentist);
- analyze scientific literature and apply research results to therapy reliably; know the epidemiological aspects, prevention, and treatment of oral and dental diseases;
- develop a multidisciplinary clinical case approach, especially in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare professionals;
- deepen topics related to the general organization of work, its dynamics, bioethics, patient relationship and education, as well as community dentistry topics, through monographic courses and interdisciplinary seminars;
- communicate with the patient and educate the patient on appropriate and effective oral hygiene techniques;
- provide the patient with adequate information, based on scientifically accepted knowledge, to obtain informed consent for therapy;
- correctly interpret the legislation concerning the practice of dentistry in the European Union country where the dentist practices and provide assistance in compliance with the medical-legal and ethical standards of the country where they practice;
- recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy;
- organize and lead the dental healthcare team using the full range of available auxiliary dental personnel;
- deepen their knowledge regarding the development of a multicultural society, with specific reference to the variety and diversification of value and cultural aspects, also from a humanistic perspective.
- possess written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian;
The graduate: - Possesses the ability to independently design and implement therapeutic programs aimed at the care and rehabilitation of the stomatognathic system - Is able to recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy - Is able to independently manage the dental treatment of the patient - Is able to evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment plan, the interventions carried out, and the results achieved. Autonomy of judgment is cultivated through reading scientific articles, participation in conferences, and congresses.
