Communication Skills The graduate: - Possesses an intermediate level knowledge of English necessary for consulting scientific texts and journals
- Is able to communicate effectively with patients and sensitize them towards achieving and maintaining oral health, providing adequate information based on knowledge and protocols accepted by the scientific community,
- Can develop an interdisciplinary approach to clinical cases, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the work of healthcare teams.
Learning Abilities The graduate: - Possesses the ability to consult databases for acquiring scientific documentation and analyze literature, applying research results to diagnosis and therapy reliably
- Is able to correctly interpret legislation concerning the practice of dentistry in the European Union country where they practice and provide assistance in compliance with the medical-legal and ethical standards of that country.
Description of specific training objectives.
The general objectives and the structure of the study plan described below are based on the contents of the new Ministerial Decree on New Degree Classes - Regulation of Master's Degree Courses, which defines Master's Degree courses in compliance with European Union directives and the University of Sassari's Academic Regulations. The study plan provides 360 University Credit Units (CFU) over 6 years and 60 CFU per year. The distribution of the 360 credit units is determined in compliance with the conditions specified in the decree attachments, which establish the credits to be assigned to disciplinary areas including training activities 'essential' for the training of a dentist.
For the University Credit Unit (CFU), corresponding to an average of 25 hours of student effort, a value of at least 8 CFU per lecture or theoretical/practical session and at least 12 hours/CFU for professional internship activities are proposed, in harmony with the University of Sassari's Academic Regulations. The remaining credit quota is available to the student for personal study.
The holders of professional training courses are responsible for the internship related to the course. For each individual internship, an ongoing assessment must be carried out, which the instructor will consider for the final exam grade. The physiological and clinical knowledge of general medicine and odontostomatology acquired through the training activities included in the study plan and clinical practical activities determine and define the professional profile of the dentist operating in European Union countries. Upon completion of six years, the graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthesis has acquired the knowledge and technical skills to enter the professional field of dentistry, both private and public.
The study program is characterized by a two-year period focused on basic training activities aimed at acquainting students with the structural organization and vital functions of the human body, including courses addressing issues related to understanding the principles underlying the scientific methodology.
The subsequent three-year period involves the study of medical, surgical, and specialist disciplines with particular reference to clinical issues related to odontostomatology pathologies. These training activities take place concurrently with the study of dental disciplines and professional clinical internships.
Theoretical courses and clinical internships in oral pathology, restorative dentistry, oral surgery, periodontology, orthodontics, pediatric dentistry, and prosthesis, while developing different skills, pursue the common goal of acquiring abilities and experiences to address and solve oral health problems from a preventive, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective, also respecting the medical-legal and ethical standards in force in EU countries. In the fifth year, a course in maxillofacial pathology and therapy and a course in implantology are introduced, which, like the previous ones, are given a specific theoretical-practical and comprehensive approach to treatment. The sixth year provides a clinical internship exclusively for professional training, aimed at synthesizing the diagnostic-therapeutic knowledge acquired in previous years for the treatment of patients with odontostomatology issues.
Students may propose study plans corresponding to an individual curriculum, provided they respect the distribution between SSD as regulated by the attachments to the Academic Regulations. The deadlines for submitting individual study plans are determined by the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery's Academic Calendar. Study plans are examined and approved by the Council. The Course Committee, on the proposal of the Teachers, organizes teaching activities in which the student exercises their personal choice, up to the acquisition of a total of 8 CFU. The student's elective teaching constitutes official teaching by the Teachers. Among the student's elective activities are monographic courses consisting of lectures, interactive and seminar-style monographic courses, conferences, internships carried out in research laboratories or clinical departments, and other activities deemed compatible with the objectives of the Degree Course by the Course Committee. Rules for submission and approval of student-selected training activities. Eight credits are available for student choice, which will be recognized upon passing the verification exam. Each student communicates to the Degree Course Council the selected training activities for the following academic year among those available and recognized within the framework of autonomous elective activities. The choice must be approved by the Degree Course Council, after consulting the Parity Teaching Committee, which assesses its consistency with the training objectives.

Dentists and Oral Surgeons Graduates in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics have employment opportunities in the field of Private Practice as a Dentist.
They can carry out, according to current regulations, managerial activities of I and II level within the National Health System.
Characteristics of the final exam.
To be admitted to take the graduation exam, the student must have attended all courses and passed the relevant exams.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, No. 163, the final exam for the completion of the single-cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics - Class LM-46 enables the exercise of the profession of dentist. For this purpose, the aforementioned final exam includes the performance of a Practical Assessment Test (PAT) of the professional skills acquired through a Practical Assessment Internship (PAI) within the study courses, aimed at verifying the candidate's practical preparation level for the professional qualification, which precedes the discussion of the thesis. The PAT is organized through the student's discussion of 3 multidisciplinary clinical cases treated as the primary operator during the PAI, involving multidisciplinary treatment plans with services related to the majority of disciplines covered by the PAI, according to the procedures established by the protocol drawn up by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics Degree Courses, in agreement with the National Dental Register Commission. For the purpose of passing the PAT, students receive a suitability assessment, after which they proceed to the discussion of the graduation thesis.
Therefore, for the completion of the Master's Degree, the submission of an original thesis prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor is required. The entire graduation committee acts as co-supervisor during the discussion, otherwise a correlating lecturer may be appointed. The determination of the grade occurs according to the procedures established by the Academic Body in line with the regulations set by the University.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics (CLMOPD), one must possess a Diploma from a five-year secondary school or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable under current regulations.
The single-cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics is subject to numerical limitation in accordance with Article 1 of Law 264/99.
The didactic organization of CLMOPD provides that students admitted to the first year must possess adequate knowledge of the Italian language and initial preparation, obtained from previous studies, covering knowledge in logic, general culture, biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics.
The verification of the student's initial knowledge is considered completed upon passing the admission test.
Students admitted to the course who show initial gaps will be assigned an additional training obligation (OFA) to be fulfilled during the first year of study based on criteria defined in the Course Didactic Regulations.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in DENTISTRY AND DENTAL PROSTHETICS Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Dentists and Oral Surgeons Since the degree program is highly professionalizing, graduates find immediate employment opportunities after graduation; both in Private Practice as a Dentist, in public health employment, and also in university teaching.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The graduate: - Possesses the ability to independently design and implement therapeutic programs aimed at the care and rehabilitation of the stomatognathic system - Is able to recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy - Is able to independently manage the dental treatment of the patient - Is able to evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment plan, the interventions carried out, and the results achieved. Autonomy of Judgment is cultivated in the student through reading scientific articles. Specifically dedicated to acquiring Autonomy of Judgment is the development of a project, which can be a thesis project or a scientific project, culminating in an independent work with a bibliography.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific methodology, linguistic and IT skills.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics knows and understands:
- Fundamental principles of the functioning of information systems with reference to the main implications in the biomedical field; methods and technologies for information management;
- Principles of descriptive medical statistics, the statistical terminology adopted in the scientific field for describing populations and samples, adequate knowledge of probabilistic and inferential bases, and methodological elements useful for interpreting the design of a scientific study;
- Basic mechanics concepts applied to the structural behavior of biomechanical systems composed of biological structures interfaced with artificial ones such as implants and prostheses; basic mechanics elements applied to observing the structural behavior of the human skeleton;
- General principles of psychology as indispensable references in patient interaction;
- Fundamental notions of pedagogy applied, in particular, to health education, understood as the implementation of awareness and responsibility processes in the exercise of the profession;
- English language focused, in particular, on the basic knowledge of medical and dental terminology and the understanding of scientific texts;
Such foundational knowledge is acquired through mandatory course attendance, which includes frontal lectures and, if necessary, practical exercises. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Basic Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics knows and understands:
- Main concepts of mechanical, thermodynamic, and electromagnetic physics, elements of biomechanics and fluid physics. Basic concepts of nuclear physics and radioactivity applicable in dental practice.
- Biological cellular and molecular mechanisms of living organisms, regarding structure, function, biomolecule turnover, and information flow from genome to proteome; cell structure, cellular compartmentalization, and processes of cell division and communication. From molecular biology to evolved biological systems.
- Principles of general and organic chemistry; chemical nomenclature and representation of molecular structure, balancing of chemical reactions. Nomenclature, structure, and properties of various classes of organic compounds. Basic knowledge of biologically relevant molecules such as sugars, lipids, proteins, and heterocyclic compounds.
- Structure and function of common biochemically relevant molecules and biochemical mechanisms of metabolic activities and main qualitative and quantitative laboratory methodologies;
- Structural and ultrastructural organization of cells and tissues, modes of tissue renewal and their implications for regenerative medicine, methods and tools of morphological investigation, with particular reference to oral-facial structures.
- Fundamental notions of macroscopic and microscopic anatomy of various organs and systems that constitute the human body, with particular reference to the knowledge of macroscopic and microscopic morphology of all components of the stomatognathic system, considering their topographical relationships and individual functional roles.
- Mechanisms and modes of operation and interaction of organs and systems, with particular reference to the knowledge and understanding of the functioning of the stomatognathic system and its functional relationships with the systems and organs of the entire organism.
- Complexity of pathological phenomena developing in the human body. Etiological factors and molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying pathological processes that govern tissue damage responses and their repair; fundamental biological defenses activated as a response to pathogens. Morphological alterations caused by pathogens in cells and tissues and their systemic and functional consequences for the organism. Biological bases of transformation and neoplastic disease. Pathophysiological mechanisms of cardiovascular and hematological pathologies.
- Basic principles of microbiology and host-parasite relationship. With particular reference to microbiology and pathogenic microorganisms of interest in dentistry.
- Morphological bases of the most frequent pathological processes of various organs and systems, with particular reference to the head and neck district, and specifically to oral cavity pathologies; modes of performing a histological or cytological examination, including the correct application of methodologies in use.
- Laboratory diagnostic investigations, according to the main phases: pre-analytical, analytical, post-analytical; issues concerning patient preparation, sample collection, and storage;
- Fundamental knowledge for the critical evaluation and interpretation of the results of the main laboratory diagnostic investigations, in addition to knowledge of the main laboratory diagnostic techniques.
Such foundational knowledge is acquired through mandatory course attendance, which includes frontal lectures and, if necessary, practical exercises. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Dental Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics knows and understands:
- Rules and dynamics characterizing the teamwork of healthcare operators;
- Structure of a scientific article and methodology for researching bibliographic sources on the WEB;
- Specific language of specialized disciplines;
- Physical, chemical, biological, and mechanical characteristics of dental materials, their potential and limitations;
- Clinical methodology and diagnostic procedures for the objective examination of the oral cavity; semiological terminology;
- Oral ecosystem, natural history, and epidemiology of the most socially impactful dental pathologies (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer, dental erosions, oral trauma, dental malocclusions);
- Tools and materials for home oral hygiene, potential and limitations of systems for detecting oral mucosa and main laboratory investigations used in dental and oral medicine, with particular reference to technological-applicative aspects;
- Procedures and correct use of materials available for evaluating dental laboratory products;
- Normal and pathological aspects of soft and hard tissues of the oral cavity, from a clinical perspective, and the most frequent pathologies of the jaw bones;
- Fundamental clinical diagnostic procedures;
- Dental malocclusions and related joint problems; anatomical, etiopathogenetic, instrumental, and operational aspects for diagnosis, planning, and implementing treatment plans;
- Potential and limitations of the main instrumental investigations used for diagnostic purposes in oral surgery; surgical instruments; surgical techniques and protocols; prevention of physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of surgical activities;
- Epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and causal therapy of plaque-induced periodontal diseases; pre-clinical knowledge for planning and performing causal periodontal therapy; instruments, techniques, purposes, indications, and contraindications of surgical periodontal treatment; diagnostic clinical and instrumental methods necessary for correctly planning surgical therapy for periodontal diseases;
- Theoretical and pre-clinical information in the field of prosthetic rehabilitation of partial edentulism using fixed, framework, or total prostheses through the production of total prosthetic devices;
- Anatomical-topographical limitations of the maxillofacial region and knowledge of oral and maxillofacial semiotics; pathologies of interest in maxillofacial and otolaryngological fields such as neoplasms, trauma, congenital and acquired malformations, inflammations, cysts, salivary gland pathologies; clinical and instrumental otolaryngological semiotics;
- Basic notions of pediatrics and pediatric pathologies with oral manifestations; pathologies of interest in pediatric dentistry and the decision-making process leading to diagnosis and planning of treatment in developing subjects; acquisition of prevention strategies based on individual risk profiles through personalized treatments;
- Indications and contraindications for implant-prosthetic rehabilitation treatment, and risk assessment in patients candidates for such treatment, characteristics of implant devices, physiological mechanisms, morpho-functional characteristics, and factors influencing the osseointegration process; techniques and prognosis of ridge augmentation and maxillary sinus lift procedures;
- Theoretical, practical, and clinical criteria in the field of conservative dentistry for designing and carrying out a structural restoration project of the tooth on functional and aesthetic grounds; correct use of adhesive materials, coronal reconstruction in relation to dental tissue destruction, endodontic recovery of root canals;
The knowledge regarding specialized dental disciplines is acquired through mandatory course attendance, which includes frontal lectures and, through regular participation in professional clinical internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.
Medical and Surgical Sciences of Interest to Dentistry
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics knows and understands:
- Human pathology in its complexity through the study of clinical medical and surgical sciences;
- Pathogenetic mechanisms, general bases of clinical, laboratory, and instrumental semiotics, therapeutic perspectives within the main systemic diseases of interest in internal medicine. Interferences that pharmacological therapy for systemic diseases may determine on dental and oral medicine pathologies and therapies;
- Main semiotic-clinical issues and systematic approach to the most frequent surgical diseases; clinical presentations of oncological pathologies relevant to surgery; conditions requiring urgent surgical treatment;
- Areas of intervention of reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgery, biology of skin, flap, and microsurgical flap transplants. Main oral-facial malformations requiring multidisciplinary treatment, including the involvement of the dentist;
- Notions on radiation physics, principles of radiological image formation, radiological equipment technology, and clinical information contained in reports and radiological images. Additionally, applications of imaging diagnostic techniques in dental and oral medicine and maxillofacial fields;
- Anatomy, physiology, and functions of the skin and mucosa for maintaining health and pathologies most frequently encountered; systematic approach to the most relevant dermatological and infectious pathologies, functional and instrumental semiotics aspects, and specific clinical methodology;
- Physiopathological bases, clinical-nosographic framework, and diagnostic process within neuropsychiatric disciplines. With particular attention to neurological syndromes, especially pathology involving the oral-facial area. Psychiatric disorders in patients with dental and oral medicine pathology;
- Drug classes directly and indirectly related to dental practice, with particular attention to molecular mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics, therapeutic uses, and appropriate use of each drug class. Adverse reactions that may manifest during dental pharmacological therapy, related to the drug in use, patient genetic and physiopathological characteristics, and potential interactions with other drugs the patient is taking for non-dental conditions;
- Main notions regarding dental pathology in pediatric patients, with particular attention to the treatment of patients with special needs;
- Fundamental knowledge on the administration of anesthesia and specialist drugs and the management of emergencies that may occur during dental and oral medicine care and therapy;
- Notions on legislative, organizational, operational, and planning characteristics of health systems as a whole and the entities operating within them, on operational mechanisms and management tools of greater relevance used in healthcare companies to ensure a constant link between resources used and results;
The knowledge related to medical and surgical sciences is acquired through mandatory course attendance, which includes frontal lectures and clinical and laboratory internships. Verification methods are the classic oral interview and/or written report.

The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics knows and understands:

- Useful information for evaluating one's professional activity from a regulatory-legal and ethical perspective, with specific reference to implications in criminal, civil, and insurance-social fields, and recognizing the main forensic pathology scenarios;

Basic Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics is able to:
- Apply knowledge from basic disciplines, such as the structure and function of the human organism in homeostatic conditions at molecular, cellular, and organ-system levels, for maintaining health conditions and for the correct application of translational scientific research;
- Apply knowledge tools of etiopathogenesis of diseases, innate and specific defense systems of the organism, cellular and tissue damage repair processes, and neoplastic transformation mechanisms for performing any activity related to health protection;
- Apply their knowledge with full understanding of the main themes of dental microbiology;
- Decide, based on methodological and cultural foundations and experience, on the opportunity for specialized examinations or analyses and access to clinical biochemical data as a diagnostic tool;
- Apply a technical basis of data to address problems arising during clinical examination, which constitute an essential part of the data referring to patients in dental and oral medicine practices and dental pathology;
- Formulate a request for a histological examination and interpret a histopathological report, with particular regard to oral cavity pathologies.

Dental Disciplines
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics is able to:
- Effectively and safely use the dental work environment; describe the oral ecosystem, natural history, and epidemiology of the most socially impactful dental pathologies (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer, dental erosions, oral trauma);
- Use the specific language of specialized disciplines;
- Perform diagnosis, plan and implement treatment plans, apply prevention protocols, perform conservative therapy plans for hard dental tissue pathologies aimed at restoring morphological, functional, and aesthetic aspects while respecting periodontal tissue health and stomatognathic system functionality, both in normal and high-risk patients;
- Perform clinical examination of the oral cavity, identifying normal anatomical structures and detecting main epidemiological indices; correctly and appropriately use semiological terminology to communicate effectively with the patient and interact correctly within the dental healthcare team; organize adequate health promotion interventions; organize effective dental and oral medicine prevention interventions for individuals and communities; identify and use tools and materials for home oral hygiene; identify potential and limitations of systems for detecting oral mucosa and main laboratory investigations used in dental and oral medicine;
- Critically read a scientific article; consult databases to acquire scientific documentation, applying research results to therapies reliably; identify potential and limitations of the main instrumental investigations used for diagnostic purposes;
- Perform primary and secondary prevention and diagnosis of prevalent oral mucosa and jaw bone pathologies; perform early diagnosis of potentially neoplastic and neoplastic lesions of the oral cavity;
- Perform objective examination of the oral-maxillofacial district, identifying and diagnosing surgical pathologies;
- Adopt protocols and behaviors to prevent physical, chemical, and microbiological contamination in the performance of surgical activities; treat simple cases of oral surgery; identify treatment priorities and collaborate with other specialists in planning interventions for patient recovery; evaluate the effectiveness of surgical interventions and results achieved; recognize and correctly use surgical instruments;
- Develop a multidisciplinary clinical case approach and coordinate a surgical team, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing the work of healthcare operator teams; detect and motivate informed consent for surgical therapy;
- Obtain adequate photographic documentation of the oral cavity; evaluate the use of appropriate prosthetic materials and techniques in relation to different clinical conditions;
- Apply therapeutic protocols for prevention of endodontic and periradicular pathologies of endodontic origin adaptable to individual patients; perform endodontic therapy plans even in high-risk patients, with the aim of restoring morphologically and functionally the dental elements affected by pathology;
- Evaluate the severity of issues related to orthognathic diagnosis and the diagnosis and treatment of temporomandibular joint dysfunctions; apply available orthodontic techniques for treatment in developing age and adulthood; identify the type of approach for planning prosthetic rehabilitation therapy;
- Apply theoretical and pre-clinical knowledge for diagnosis and treatment planning, for performing causal periodontal therapy, and for correctly using periodontal instrumentation; understand the nature, advantages, and limitations of periodontal surgery; formulate diagnosis and treatment plans for complex periodontal cases requiring surgical treatment;
- Apply theoretical knowledge and pre-clinical skills for formulating a diagnosis and treatment plan, for performing prosthetic rehabilitation of partial edentulism, for taking impressions for fixed prostheses, and for creating plaster models; formulate diagnosis, treatment plan, and prognosis for prosthetic rehabilitation with PPR; design and implement all phases of PPR prosthetic production, from clinical examination to delivery;
- Perform specific evaluation of pathologies of interest in maxillofacial and otolaryngological fields; perform anamnesis, clinical examination, and treatment of oral cavity pathologies in pediatric patients; implement preventive strategies for the main dental and oral medicine pathologies of the developing age; diagnose infectious, surgical, and mechanical complications of implant-prosthetic rehabilitation treatment; plan and implement maintenance of implant health; treat infectious, surgical, and mechanical complications of rehabilitation treatment.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of specialized dental activities are intensive laboratory exercises on manikins, clinical internships with patients, and discussion, re-elaboration, and presentation of clinical cases.
Medical and Surgical Sciences of Interest to Dentistry
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics is able to:

- Conduct a correct clinical approach to patients with surgical problems: prepare the patient for surgery and prevent and, if necessary, address surgical complications. Adequate interaction with the surgical team;
- Solve problems concerning the application of imaging diagnostic techniques in dental and oral medicine and maxillofacial fields, and the clinical contextualization of information contained in reports and radiological images.
- Quantify and manage perioperative anxiety in dentistry for pediatric, elderly, and disabled patients.
- Apply neurological knowledge in the diagnosis and treatment of headaches and facial and head neuralgia of dental and oral medicine origin; understand potential implications of pharmacological therapy for neuropsychiatric pathologies on dental and oral medicine pathologies and therapies;
- Identify the appropriate anesthetic and correct administration technique for each patient based on their systemic condition, recognize complications, and apply initial resuscitation maneuvers;
- Design and organize a dental clinic in compliance with legal requirements, with a correct doctor-patient relationship from a legislative and contractual perspective;
- Develop a clinical approach based on modern evidence-based methodology for correct diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up management.

Prevention and Dental Health Services Disciplines

- Apply knowledge in the field of general and applied hygiene and manage knowledge of health determinants and main risk factors in the interaction between humans, their physical-social environment, and the microbial world.
Among the didactic tools used to achieve the ability to apply knowledge in the context of these disciplines are intensive laboratory activities and internships.

recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for medical therapy;
organize and lead the dental team using the full range of available auxiliary dental personnel;
deepen knowledge in the context of a multicultural society, with specific reference to the variety and diversification of value and cultural aspects, also from a humanistic perspective.
possess written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian;

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The general objectives and the structure of the study plan described below refer to the contents of the new Ministerial Decree schema "New Classes of Degrees - Regulation of Master's Degree Courses," which defines Master's Degree courses in compliance with European Union directives and to the University Academic Regulations of the University of Sassari. The teaching plan provides 360 Credits (CFU) over 6 years and 60 CFU per year. The distribution of the 360 credits is determined in accordance with the conditions specified in the decree's attachments, which establish the credits to be assigned to disciplinary areas including 'essential' training activities for the formation of the dentist.
For the University Credit Unit (CFU), which corresponds to an average of 25 hours of student effort, a value of at least 8 CFU is proposed for frontal or theoretical/practical lectures and at least 12 hours/CFU for professional training internship activities, in harmony with the University Academic Regulations of the University of Sassari. The remaining credit quota is available to the student for personal study.
The holders of professional training courses are responsible for the internship related to the course. For each individual internship, an interim evaluation must be conducted, which the instructor will consider for the final exam grade. The acquired physiological and clinical knowledge of general medicine and odontostomatology through the training activities included in the teaching plan and clinical practical activities determine and define the professional profile of the dentist operating in European Union countries. Upon completion of six years, the graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics has acquired the knowledge and technical skills to professionally enter the dental field, both private and public.
The CdS is characterized by a two-year period focused on basic training activities aimed at familiarizing the student with the structural organization and vital functions of the human body, including courses addressing issues related to understanding the principles underlying the scientific methodology.
The subsequent three-year period involves the study of medical, surgical, and specialized disciplines with particular reference to clinical issues related to odontostomatology pathologies. These training activities are conducted concurrently with the study of dental disciplines and professional clinical internships.
Theoretical courses and clinical internships in oral pathology, restorative dentistry, oral surgery, periodontology, orthodontics, pediatric dentistry, and prosthetics, while developing different skills, pursue the common goal of acquiring abilities and experiences to address and solve oral health problems from a preventive, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective, while respecting the medical-legal and ethical standards in force in EU countries. In the fifth year, a course in maxillofacial pathology and therapy and a course in implantology are introduced, which, like the previous ones, are given a specific theoretical-practical and comprehensive approach to treatment. The sixth year provides a clinical internship activity exclusively for professional training, aimed at synthesizing the diagnostic and therapeutic knowledge acquired in previous years for the treatment of patients with odontostomatology issues.
Students may present study plans corresponding to an individual curriculum, provided they respect the distribution among SSD as regulated by the attachments to the RDA. The deadlines for submitting individual study plans are determined by the Academic Calendar of the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery. Study plans are reviewed and approved by the Council. The CCL, upon proposal by the Teachers, organizes teaching activities from which the student exercises their personal choice, up to a total of 8 CFU. Student-selected teaching constitutes official activities of the Teachers. Among the student-selected activities are monographic courses consisting of lectures, interactive and seminar-style monographic courses, conferences, internships conducted in research laboratories or clinical departments, and other activities that the CCL deems compatible with the objectives of the Degree Course.
Rules for the submission and approval of student-selected training activities. Eight credits are available for student selection, which will be recognized upon passing the verification exam. Each student communicates to the Degree Course Council the selected training activities for the following academic year among those available and recognized within the scope of autonomous student-selected activities. The choice must be approved by the Degree Course Council, after hearing the opinion of the Parity Teaching Commission, which assesses its consistency with the educational objectives.

The student has access to 10 CFU dedicated to preparing the Master's thesis. To be admitted to the graduation exam, the student must have attended all courses, passed the related exams, and acquired the 350 CFU preceding the Qualifying Degree.
The graduation exam focuses on discussing a thesis developed originally by the student under the guidance of a supervisor; a co-supervisor may be appointed.
The graduation grade (expressed out of 110) is determined by the following parameters, as clearly stated in the Council of the Master's Degree Board minutes (March 2017):
1) Weighted average of grades converted to out of 110;
2) Points awarded by the Graduation Committee during the thesis discussion based on the quality of the work and presentation, completion of the degree within 6 years of enrollment, honors obtained in exams, participation in international exchange programs.
3) The points from point 2 are added to the weighted average already converted to out of 110.
4) Honors may be awarded unanimously by the Committee to candidates who achieve a weighted average of exam grades equal to or greater than 102/110. Mention may be awarded unanimously by the Committee to candidates who achieve a weighted average of exam grades equal to or greater than 105/110.

Communication Skills (COMMUNICATION SKILLS)
Graduates must be able to communicate clearly and unambiguously their conclusions, knowledge, and underlying rationale to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, as well as, using the appropriate methods for the circumstances, to their patients. To this end, graduates:
1) will be able to listen attentively to extract and synthesize relevant information on all issues, understanding their content, and exercising communication skills to facilitate understanding with patients and their relatives, enabling them to share decisions as equal partners.
2) will effectively communicate with colleagues, the community, other sectors, and the media, and will know how to interact with other professional figures involved in patient care through efficient teamwork.
3) will demonstrate good sensitivity towards cultural and personal factors that enhance interactions with patients and the community.
4) will be able to address critical communication situations, such as communicating serious diagnoses, discussing sensitive topics related to sexual and reproductive life, and end-of-life decisions.

SECTION: Judgment Autonomy

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates must have the ability to integrate knowledge and manage complexity, as well as formulate judgments based on limited or incomplete information, including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities related to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
To this end, graduates:
1) Will be able to demonstrate, in the course of professional activities, a critical approach, constructive skepticism, and a creative attitude oriented towards research. They will know how to consider the importance and limitations of scientific thinking based on information obtained from various sources to establish the cause, treatment, and prevention of diseases.
2) Will be able to formulate personal judgments to solve analytical and complex problems and to independently seek scientific information, without waiting for it to be provided, using the foundations of scientific evidence.
3) Will be able to formulate hypotheses, collect, and critically evaluate data to solve problems, being aware of the role of complexity, uncertainty, and probability in medical decision-making. They will be able to effectively plan and efficiently manage their time and activities to address conditions of uncertainty, and exercise the ability to adapt to changes.
4) Will be able to exercise personal responsibility in caring for individual patients, respecting the medical profession's code of ethics.
5) Will be able to exercise reflective thinking on their professional activities regarding the relationship with patients and other operators, the methods used, the results obtained, and their personal and emotional experiences.

Learning Skills.
Learning Skills (LEARNING SKILLS)
Graduates must have developed the learning abilities that allow them to continue studying mostly in an autonomous and self-directed manner.
To this end, graduates:
1) Will be able to collect, organize, and critically interpret new scientific knowledge and health/biomedical information from various resources and databases.
2) Will be able to obtain specific patient information from clinical data management systems, using information and communication technology as a valid support for diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices and for health monitoring, understanding its application and also the limitations of information technology.
3) Will be able to manage a good archive of their medical practice for subsequent analysis and improvement.
4) Will be able to identify their own training needs, even starting from audits of their practice, and design self-training paths.

Preclinical Area
The graduate will know:
- To correlate the structure and functionality of the normal organism as a complex of biological systems in continuous adaptation, interpreting morpho-functional anomalies found in various diseases;
- To describe the fundamental molecular, cellular, biochemical, and physiological mechanisms that maintain the organism's homeostasis, knowing how to describe the life cycle of the human being and the effects of growth, development, and aging on the individual, family, and community, paying attention to gender differences;
- To recognize the fundamental biological defense mechanisms and pathological mechanisms of the immune system;
- To describe the relationship between microorganisms and host in human infections;
- To recognize the concept and function of genes, the different principles of inheritance of traits, and the concept of genetic variability;
- To correlate the principles of drug action with their indications, paying particular attention to differences in sex, gender, and population;
- To illustrate the origin and natural history of acute and chronic diseases, having essential knowledge related to physiology, pathology, and epidemiology;
- To express themselves appropriately in scientific English in doctor-patient relationships and among colleagues.

Clinical Area
The graduate will know:
- To recognize the pathophysiological and anatomopathological aspects of diseases, both in medical and surgical fields;
- To evaluate the specific symptoms of various pathologies and correctly frame them in differential diagnostic processes;
- To identify diagnostic investigations, both biological and instrumental, including innovative ones, to propose them appropriately within the patient's diagnostic pathway, knowing how to evaluate the correct cost-benefit ratio;
- To correctly interpret the results obtained from diagnostic investigations;
- To identify the most appropriate therapies, including innovative ones, evaluating the risk-benefit ratio and cost-effectiveness;
- To know and appropriately apply the issues related to pain therapy and end-of-life care;
- To apply all their knowledge while taking into account issues related to gender and ethnic differences as well as the patient's cultural context;
- To interpret and approach various pathologies within the context of developmental age, adult patient, complex patient, and chronic patient with multimorbidity;
- To know and apply the principles of evidence-based medicine;
- To recognize clinical emergencies and urgencies, in order to identify the necessary actions for initial intervention and patient health safety.

Public Health and Services Area
The graduate:
- Will be able to illustrate the origin and natural history of acute and chronic diseases, with particular reference to epidemiology, health economics, and the principles of health management;
- Will have a good knowledge of the mechanisms that determine equity in access to healthcare, the effectiveness and quality of care itself, also in relation to gender and cultural differences;
- Will be able to list and discuss the main determinants of health and disease, such as lifestyle, genetic, demographic, environmental, socio-economic, psychological, and cultural factors in the population as a whole, correlating them to the state of international health and the impact of globalization on it;
- Will know the norms and practices aimed at maintaining and promoting health in the workplace, identifying situations requiring specialist competence;
- Will know the main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization, the principles and applications of preventive medicine in different realities;
- Will have adequate knowledge of gender medicine, family, and territory, acquired also through practical training experiences;
- Will be able to discuss the essential elements of professionalism, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities that form the basis of the profession; will know the deontological norms and those underlying high professional responsibility;
- Will have knowledge of the rules and dynamics that characterize team work.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Preclinical Area
The graduate will be able to:
- Apply knowledge of fundamental genomic, biochemical, cellular, and physiological mechanisms that maintain the organism's homeostasis;
- Know the morphological aspects that allow the recognition of various human tissues, enabling organ diagnosis;
- Interpret morpho-functional anomalies of the organism found in various diseases, both acute and chronic;
- Know the potential and limitations of the main techniques of cell and molecular biology; know the fundamental elements of a gene and a DNA sequence; be able to consult the main online genetic databases;
- Evaluate the diagnostic relevance and clinical implications of microbiological analyses;
- Identify normal and abnormal human behavior, also in the context of development;
- Clarify the etiology and natural history of acute and chronic diseases;
- Illustrate the mechanism of action of drugs and their application field, with particular reference to response variability in relation to gender, ethnic, and pathophysiological factors;
- Know the main pharmacological interactions and contraindications of individual drugs as well as the principles for their correct use within complex therapeutic schemes;
- Apply basic knowledge for approaching biomedical problems;
- Relate appropriately with patients and colleagues from other nationalities.
The objectives will be acquired through the student's participation in frontal lectures and small group activities within integrated courses and laboratory activities, and verified through written and/or oral exams.

Clinical Area
The graduate will be able to:
- Correctly collect the family and personal medical history, complete with social aspects;
- Perform a general and specific objective examination of individual organs and systems;
- Evaluate the patient's mental state, behavior, and experience;
- Apply the principles of clinical reasoning, diagnostic procedures, and basic techniques, analyzing and interpreting their results, in order to correctly define the nature of a problem, applying appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies;
- Set up the therapeutic pathway, both medical and surgical, ensuring the most appropriate path for each individual, safeguarding life strictly according to the principle of evidence-based medicine;
- Recognize the complex, chronic, multimorbid patient, and tailor a personalized diagnostic-therapeutic pathway;
- Care for diseases and patients effectively, efficiently, and ethically, promoting health and preventing disease, fulfilling the moral obligation to provide medical care in the terminal phases of life, including palliative symptom therapy, with particular reference to pain;
- Correctly and autonomously manage common medical emergencies.
The acquisition of the above objectives will occur through integrated courses of clinical and basic subjects and through professional training activities starting from the third year of the course. The achievement of the objectives will be verified during the exams of each integrated course and the evaluation by the tutors of the training activities.

Public Health and Services Area
The graduate will be able to:
- Undertake appropriate preventive and protective actions against diseases, maintaining and promoting the health of the individual, family, and community, knowing how to correctly use all available resources (diagnostic, therapeutic, organizational, preventive);
- Apply the principles of privacy to demographic and epidemiological data available at local, regional, and national levels, using them correctly in decisions regarding individual and public health;
- Establish diagnostic-therapeutic pathways based on the essential principles of health economics, with specific attention to the cost/benefit ratio, continuity of care between hospital and territory, and organizational appropriateness;
- Respect professional values including excellence, altruism, responsibility, compassion, empathy, reliability, honesty, and integrity, committing to follow scientific methods and maintain constant updates; maintain good relationships with the patient and their family, safeguarding well-being, cultural diversity, and patient autonomy;
- Correctly apply the principles of moral reasoning and adopt the right decisions regarding possible conflicts in ethical, legal, and professional values, including those that may arise from ethnic or gender differences, economic hardship, commercialization of healthcare, and new scientific discoveries;
- Respect colleagues and other health professionals, demonstrating the ability to establish collaborative relationships with them, appropriately valuing the individual roles involved; will be able to establish a correct multidisciplinary approach in fragile patients and those with multimorbidity.
The acquisition of these objectives will occur through integrated courses of clinical and basic subjects, as well as through professional training activities starting from the third year of the course. The achievement of the objectives will be verified during the exams of each integrated course and the evaluation by the tutors of the training activities.

Specific Training Objectives Description.
Qualifying Training Objectives of the Class: LM-41 Medicine and Surgery
Graduates in Master's Degree programs in Medicine and Surgery must be equipped with:
- The scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation necessary according to Directive 75/363/EEC for the practice of the medical profession and the methodology and culture necessary for lifelong training, as well as a level of professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy derived from a training path characterized by a holistic approach to health problems of healthy or sick individuals in relation to the chemical-physical, biological, and social environment surrounding them. For this purpose, the Master's Degree program provides a total of 360 CFU, spread over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired in training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills;
- Essential theoretical knowledge derived from basic sciences, in the perspective of their subsequent professional application; the ability to detect and critically evaluate, from a clinical perspective, and in a unified vision extending to the sociocultural and gender dimension, data related to the health and disease status of the individual, interpreting them in the light of basic scientific knowledge, pathophysiology, and organ and system pathologies; the skills and experience, combined with the ability for self-assessment, to responsibly address and solve priority health problems from a preventive, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective; knowledge of the historical, epistemological, and ethical dimensions of medicine; the ability to communicate clearly and humanely with the patient and family; the ability to collaborate with different professional figures in various group health activities; the ability to apply, in medical decisions, also the principles of health economics; the ability to recognize community health problems and intervene competently.

The professional profile of Master's graduates must include knowledge of:
- Behaviors and behavioral attitudes of the medical being;
- Fundamental notions and methodology of physics and statistics useful for identifying, understanding, and interpreting biomedical phenomena;
- Fundamental biological organization and basic biochemical and cellular processes of living organisms;
- Basic processes of individual and group behavior;
- Mechanisms of transmission and expression of genetic information at the cellular and molecular level;
- Structural organization of the human body, with its main anatomical-clinical applications, from the macroscopic to the microscopic level, including ultrastructural aspects, and the mechanisms through which this organization is realized during embryonic development and differentiation;
- Essential morphological characteristics of systems, organs, tissues, cells, and subcellular structures of the human body, as well as their main morpho-functional correlations;
- Biochemical, molecular, and cellular mechanisms underlying pathophysiological processes;
- Fundamentals of the main laboratory methods applicable to the qualitative and quantitative study of pathogenic determinants and significant biological processes in medicine;
- Modes of operation of the various organs of the human body, their dynamic integration into systems, and the general control mechanisms in normal conditions;
- Main functional findings in healthy humans; fundamentals of the main imaging diagnostic methods and the use of radiation, principles of biomedical technology applications in medicine.

Master's graduates must also:
- Have acquired and deepened the interrelationships between the content of basic sciences and clinical sciences, in the dimension of complexity inherent to the health status of a healthy or sick person, with particular attention to the interdisciplinary nature of medicine;
- Have developed and matured a strongly integrated approach to the patient, critically evaluating not only all clinical aspects but also dedicating particular attention to relational, educational, social, and ethical aspects involved in prevention, diagnosis, treatment of disease, as well as rehabilitation and recovery of the highest possible psychophysical well-being.

Master's graduates in Medicine and Surgery will carry out medical-surgical activities in various roles and professional clinical, health, and bio-medical contexts.

For the purposes indicated, graduates of the class must have acquired:
- Knowledge of the organization, structure, and normal functioning of the human body, for the maintenance of the health status of a healthy person and the understanding of pathological modifications; knowledge of the causes of diseases in humans, interpreting their fundamental molecular, cellular, and pathophysiological mechanisms;
- Knowledge of the fundamental biological defense mechanisms and pathological mechanisms of the immune system and knowledge of the relationship between microorganisms and host in human infections, as well as the related defense mechanisms;
- The ability to correctly apply methodologies to detect clinical, functional, and laboratory findings, critically interpreting them also from a pathophysiological perspective, for diagnosis and prognosis, and the ability to evaluate cost/benefit ratios in choosing diagnostic procedures, paying attention to both the correct clinical methodology and the principles of evidence-based medicine;
- A systematic knowledge of the most relevant diseases of various systems, from a nosological, etiopathogenetic, pathophysiological, and clinical perspective, within a unified and global view of human pathology, and the ability to critically evaluate and correlate clinical symptoms, physical signs, functional alterations detected in humans with anatomopathological lesions, interpreting their production mechanisms and deepening their clinical significance;
- The ability to apply clinical reasoning to analyze and solve common and relevant clinical problems in both medical and surgical fields, and the ability to evaluate epidemiological data and know their use for promoting health and preventing diseases in individuals and communities;
- Knowledge of the principles underlying the analysis of human behavior and adequate experience, gained through in-depth and continuous interactive teaching experiences in the field of doctor-patient relationship and communication, on the importance, quality, and appropriateness of communication with the patient and family, as well as with other health operators, being aware of their own and others' values, and the ability to appropriately use methodologies oriented towards information, education, and health education, and the ability to recognize the main alterations in behavior and subjective experiences, indicating preventive and rehabilitative therapeutic directions;
- Knowledge of anatomopathological findings as well as cellular, tissue, and organ lesions and their evolution in relation to the most relevant diseases of various systems, and knowledge, acquired also through participation in anatomoclinical conferences, of the contribution of the anatomopathologist to the clinical decision-making process, with reference to the use of histopathological and cytological diagnostics (including smear and oncocytopathology) also with biomolecular techniques, in the diagnosis, prevention, prognosis, and therapy of diseases in individual patients, as well as the ability to interpret anatomopathological reports;
- The ability to correctly propose various imaging diagnostic procedures, evaluating risks, costs, and benefits, and the ability to interpret imaging diagnostic reports, as well as knowledge of the indications and methodologies for the use of radioactive tracers, and the ability to correctly propose the therapeutic use of radiation, evaluating risks and benefits, and knowledge of the principles of radioprotection;
- Knowledge of the main and most up-to-date laboratory diagnostic methods in clinical, cellular, and molecular pathology, as well as the ability to correctly propose various laboratory diagnostic procedures, evaluating costs and benefits, and the ability to rationally interpret laboratory data;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, anatomopathological, preventive, and clinical issues regarding the broncho-pulmonary, cardiovascular, gastroenterological, hematopoietic, endocrine-metabolic, immunological, and uro-nephrological systems, providing their etiopathogenetic interpretation and indicating diagnostic and therapeutic directions, and identifying conditions that require the professional contribution of the specialist in the aforementioned areas;
- The ability to recognize the most frequent otorhinolaryngological, dental-stomatology, oral cavity, locomotor system, and visual apparatus diseases, as well as skin and venereal diseases, indicating their main preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic directions, and the ability to identify conditions that require the professional contribution of the specialist in the aforementioned areas;
- The ability to recognize, through pathophysiological, anatomopathological, and clinical study, the main alterations of the nervous system and psychiatric and social context diseases, providing their etiopathogenetic interpretation and indicating diagnostic and therapeutic directions;
- The ability and sensitivity to insert specialized issues into a broader view of the overall health status of the person and their general well-being needs, and the ability to integrate into a global and unified evaluation of the overall health status of the individual the symptoms, signs, and structural and functional alterations of individual organs and systems, aggregating them under preventive, diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative aspects;
- Knowledge of the physiological changes of aging and the issues of disease status in the elderly, and the ability to plan medical and healthcare interventions in geriatric patients;
- The ability to analyze and solve clinical problems of internal medicine, surgery, and specialist nature, evaluating the relationship between benefits, risks, and costs in the light of evidence-based medicine principles and diagnostic-therapeutic appropriateness;
- The ability to analyze and solve clinical problems of oncological nature, addressing the diagnostic-therapeutic process in the light of evidence-based medicine principles, as well as knowledge of pain therapy and palliative care;
- The skill and sensitivity to apply the essential principles of health economics in medical decisions, with specific attention to the cost/benefit ratio of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, continuity of care between hospital and territory, and organizational appropriateness;
- Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of the humanities regarding the historical evolution of medical values, including epistemological and ethical aspects; the skill and sensitivity to critically evaluate medical acts within the health team;
- Knowledge of the different drug classes, molecular and cellular mechanisms of their action, fundamental principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, and knowledge of therapeutic uses of drugs, response variability in relation to gender, genetic, and pathophysiological factors, pharmacological interactions, and criteria for defining therapeutic schemes, as well as knowledge of the principles and methods of clinical pharmacology, including pharmacovigilance and pharmacoepidemiology, side effects, and drug toxicity and abuse;
- Knowledge, from a preventive, diagnostic, and rehabilitative perspective, of issues related to health and disease status in neonatal, childhood, and adolescent age, for the non-specialist doctor, and the ability to identify conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist and to plan essential medical interventions for the main health problems, by frequency and risk, related to pediatric specialty pathology;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, psychological, and clinical issues regarding female fertility and sexual dysfunction from a medical sexological perspective, natural and assisted procreation from an endocrine-gynecological perspective, pregnancy, prenatal morbidity, and childbirth, and the ability to recognize the most frequent gynecological pathologies, indicating fundamental preventive and therapeutic measures, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, psychological, and clinical issues regarding male fertility and assessment of male gametes, male sexuality and its dysfunctions from a medical sexological perspective, natural and assisted procreation from an endocrine-andrological perspective, and the ability to recognize the most frequent andrological pathologies, indicating fundamental preventive and therapeutic measures, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist;
- The ability to recognize, in the immediacy of the event, clinical situations of emergency and urgency, taking the necessary initial actions to ensure survival and the best possible care, and knowledge of intervention methods in disaster situations;
- Knowledge of the fundamental norms to maintain and promote the health of the individual and communities, and knowledge of the norms and practices aimed at maintaining and promoting health in the workplace, identifying situations requiring specialist competence, as well as knowledge of the main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization and the ability to indicate the principles and applications of preventive medicine in various and complex communities;
- Knowledge of deontological norms and those related to high professional responsibility, critically evaluating the ethical principles underlying different possible professional choices, and the ability to develop an interdisciplinary and transcultural mental approach, especially in collaboration with other health team figures, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing team work, as well as adequate experience in the general organization of work, connected to sensitivity to its characteristics, bioethics, history, and epistemology of medicine, the relationship with the patient, as well as towards community medicine themes, acquired also through direct field experiences; knowledge of the characteristics of multicultural society, with specific reference to the variety and diversification of value and cultural aspects;
- A deep knowledge of the technological and biotechnological development of modern bio-medicine, including knowledge of the principles of scientific research in the biomedical field and clinical-specialistic areas, the ability to search, read, and interpret international literature for planning research on specific topics and developing a critical interpretation mindset of scientific data;
- Adequate experience in independent study and organization of their lifelong training, and the ability to conduct bibliographic research and update, the ability to critically read scientific articles derived from knowledge of scientific English, enabling them to understand international literature and update; written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian; computer skills useful for managing information systems of services and their self-training; adequate knowledge of family and territorial medicine, acquired also through practical training experiences on-site.

In particular, specific professional skills in the field of internal medicine, general surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, as well as medical-surgical specialties, acquired by carrying out professional training activities for a duration of at least 60 CFU, to be carried out in an integrated manner with other training activities of the course at university healthcare structures.

The duration of the course for the acquisition of the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is 6 years.

Regarding the definition of curricula prepared for the execution of activities provided by Directive 75/363/EEC, the university didactic regulations comply with the provisions of the present decree and Article 6, paragraph 3, of Ministerial Decree No. 270/04.

Finally, in accordance with Ministerial Decree No. 8 of April 2, 2020, which adapts the didactic organization of the LM41 - Medicine and Surgery class as per Ministerial Decree of March 16, 2007, the professional training internship is a qualifying part of the professional training. Within the 60 CFU to be acquired throughout the training path, destined for the aforementioned professional training activity, 15 CFU must be dedicated to the completion of the quarterly practical-evaluative internship within the course, as per Article 3 of the Ministerial Decree of May 9, 2018, No. 58 and amendments, aimed at obtaining professional qualification. This internship is carried out for a number of hours corresponding to at least 5 CFU per month and is structured in the following periods, not necessarily consecutive: one month in Surgical Area; one month in Medical Area; one month, to be carried out not before the sixth year of the course, in the specific field of General Medicine.

The Master's Degree Course in Medicine and Surgery of the University of Sassari aims to train a physician capable of addressing, after the degree, any type of specialist training in both medical and surgical fields, as well as organizational roles in healthcare systems and their professional updating.

The specific learning objectives are outlined in a manner consistent with both general and specific indications represented within the European Qualifications Framework (Dublin descriptors), integrating them with what proposed by the Institute for International Medical Education (IIME), Task Force for Assessment, and by "The TUNING Project (Medicine) – Learning Outcomes/Competences for Undergraduate Medical Education in Europe": the objectives are finally consistent with what indicated by the "Core curriculum for the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery" proposed by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Italian LM41 Degree Programs.

The Course, for the achievement of didactic objectives, provides a total of 360 CFU, spread over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired in practical training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (professionalizing CFU). The 12 semesters of the Course, which include 36 integrated courses, provide for the attribution of CFU in compliance with the table of indispensable training activities. Each CFU corresponds to a student workload of 25 hours, of which not more than 12 hours of frontal lectures in basic, characterizing, and related disciplinary fields, or theoretical-practical teaching (seminar, laboratory, exercise), or 25 hours of assisted study within the teaching structure.

Each professionalizing CFU (training and orientation internships) corresponds to 25 hours of work for the student, also structured in small group teaching activities, as well as each CFU for student-selected activities and the final exam.

The specific mission of the Master's Degree Course in Medicine and Surgery is biomedical-psychosocial and aimed at the real development of "professional competence" and "professional values." It is based on the importance of integrating the biomedical paradigm of "curing the disease" with the psychosocial paradigm of "caring for the human being" in the meta-paradigm of "complexity of care." This specific mission is therefore aimed at training a physician, at an initial professional level, who possesses:
- A multidisciplinary, interprofessional, and integrated vision of common health and disease problems;
- Education oriented towards disease prevention and health promotion within the community and territory;
- A deep knowledge of new care and health needs, focused not only on the disease but especially on the sick person, considered in their entirety of body and mind and inserted in a specific social context.

The teaching method adopted, useful for achieving the expected qualifying characteristics, provides for the horizontal and vertical integration of knowledge, a teaching method based on a solid cultural and methodological foundation acquired through the study of pre-clinical disciplines and subsequently mainly focused on the ability to solve problems and make decisions, early contact with the patient, and the acquisition of good clinical and human relationship skills.

In the didactic project of the Master's Degree Course, the right balance of vertical and transversal integration is proposed between:
a) Basic sciences, which must be broad and include knowledge of evolutionary biology, molecular biology, and genetics, and biological complexity aimed at understanding the structure and function of the human body in normal conditions, for maintaining health conditions and correctly applying translational scientific research;
b) Knowledge of pathological processes and the mechanisms that cause them, also to set up prevention, diagnosis, and therapy;
c) Clinical and methodological medical practice, which must be particularly solid, through extensive use of tutorial teaching, capable of transforming theoretical knowledge into personal experience in order to build one's own scale of values and interests, and to acquire the professional skills necessary to manage the complexity of medicine;
d) Humanities, which must constitute a useful background to reach awareness of the medical being and the deep values of medical professionalism;
e) Acquisition of scientific, medical, clinical, and professional methodology directed at health problems of the individual and community.

The student has access to 10 CFU dedicated to preparing the Master's thesis. To be admitted to the graduation exam, the student must have completed all courses, passed the related exams, and acquired the 350 CFU preceding the Enabling Degree.
The graduation exam focuses on discussing a thesis developed originally by the student under the guidance of a supervisor; a co-supervisor may be appointed.
The graduation grade (expressed out of 110) is determined by the following parameters, as clearly stated in the Council of the Master's Degree Board minutes (March 2017):
1) Weighted average of grades converted to out of 110;
2) Points awarded by the Graduation Committee during the thesis discussion based on the quality of the work and presentation, completion of the degree within 6 years of enrollment, honors obtained in exams, participation in international exchange programs.
3) The points in point 2 are added to the weighted average of grades already converted to out of 110.
4) Honors may be awarded with unanimous committee decision to candidates achieving a weighted average of exam grades equal to or greater than 102/110. Mention may be awarded with unanimous committee decision to candidates achieving a weighted average of exam grades equal to or greater than 105/110.

The requirements and admission procedures for the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery are regulated by national laws and ministerial regulations.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery, one must hold a High School Diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, and pass the admission test.

Communication Skills (COMMUNICATION SKILLS)
Graduates must be able to communicate clearly and unambiguously their conclusions, knowledge, and underlying rationale to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, as well as to their patients in the manner required by the circumstances. To this end, graduates:
1) will be able to listen attentively to extract and synthesize relevant information on all issues, understanding their content, and exercising communication skills to facilitate understanding with patients and their relatives, enabling them to share decisions as equal partners.
2) will effectively communicate with colleagues, the community, other sectors, and the media, and will know how to interact with other professional figures involved in patient care through efficient teamwork.
3) will demonstrate good sensitivity towards cultural and personal factors that enhance interactions with patients and the community.
4) will be able to address critical communication situations, such as communicating serious diagnoses, conversations on sensitive topics related to sexual and reproductive life, and end-of-life decisions.
