SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10384?annoOrdinamento=2018

Autonomy of Judgment.
Graduates must have the ability to integrate knowledge and manage complexity, as well as formulate judgments based on limited or incomplete information, including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
To this end, graduates:
1) Will be able to demonstrate, in the course of professional activities, a critical approach, constructive skepticism, and a creative attitude oriented towards research. They will be able to consider the importance and limitations of scientific thinking based on information obtained from various sources to establish the cause, treatment, and prevention of diseases.
2) Will be able to formulate personal judgments to solve analytical and complex problems and to independently seek scientific information, without waiting for it to be provided, using the foundations of scientific evidence.
3) Will be able to formulate hypotheses, collect and critically evaluate data to solve problems, being aware of the role of complexity, uncertainty, and probability in medical decision-making. They will be able to effectively plan and efficiently manage their time and activities to address uncertain conditions, and exercise the ability to adapt to changes.
4) Will be able to exercise personal responsibility in caring for individual patients, respecting the medical profession's code of ethics;
5) Will be able to exercise reflective thinking on their professional activities regarding the relationship with patients and other operators, the methods used, the results obtained, and personal and emotional experiences.

Learning Skills.
Graduates must have developed the learning abilities that allow them to continue studying mostly in an autonomous and self-directed manner.
To this end, graduates:
1) Will be able to collect, organize, and critically interpret new scientific knowledge and health/biomedical information from various resources and databases.
2) Will be able to obtain specific patient information from clinical data management systems, using information and communication technology as a valid support for diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices and for health monitoring, understanding its application and also the limitations of information technology.
3) Will be able to manage a good archive of their medical practice for subsequent analysis and improvement.
4) Will be able to identify their own training needs, even starting from audits of their practice, and design self-training paths.

Preclinical Area. Graduates will be able to:
- Correlate the structure and functionality of the normal organism as a complex of biological systems in continuous adaptation, interpreting morpho-functional anomalies found in various diseases;
- Describe the fundamental molecular, cellular, biochemical, and physiological mechanisms that maintain the organism's homeostasis, knowing how to describe the life cycle of the human being and the effects of growth, development, and aging on the individual, family, and community, paying attention to gender differences;
- Recognize the fundamental biological defense mechanisms and pathological mechanisms of the immune system;
- Describe the relationship between microorganisms and host in human infections;
- Recognize the concept and function of genes, the different principles of inheritance, and the concept of genetic variability;
- Correlate the principles of drug action with their indications, paying particular attention to differences in sex, gender, and population;
- Illustrate the origin and natural history of acute and chronic diseases, having essential knowledge related to physiology, pathology, and epidemiology;
- Express themselves appropriately in scientific English in doctor-patient relationships and among colleagues.

Clinical Area. Graduates will be able to:
- Recognize the pathophysiological and anatomopathological aspects of diseases, both in medical and surgical fields;
- Evaluate the specific symptoms of various pathologies and correctly frame them in differential diagnostic processes;
- Identify diagnostic investigations, both biological and instrumental, including innovative ones, to propose them appropriately within the patient's diagnostic pathway, evaluating the correct cost-benefit ratio;
- Correctly interpret the results obtained from diagnostic investigations;
- Identify the most appropriate therapies, including innovative ones, evaluating the risk-benefit and cost-effectiveness ratios;
- Know and appropriately apply the issues related to pain therapy and end-of-life care;
- Apply all their knowledge while taking into account issues related to gender and ethnic differences as well as the patient's cultural context;
- Interpret and approach different pathologies within the context of developmental age, adult patients, complex patients, and chronic patients with multimorbidity;
- Know and apply the principles of evidence-based medicine;
- Recognize clinical emergencies and urgencies to identify necessary actions for initial intervention and patient safety.

Public Health and Services Area. Graduates will be able to:
- Illustrate the origin and natural history of acute and chronic diseases, with particular reference to epidemiology, health economics, and the principles of health management;
- Have a good understanding of the mechanisms determining equity in access to healthcare, the effectiveness and quality of care itself, also in relation to gender and cultural differences;
- List and discuss the main determinants of health and disease, such as lifestyle, genetic, demographic, environmental, socio-economic, psychological, and cultural factors in the population as a whole, correlating them to the state of international health and the impact of globalization on it;
- Know the norms and practices aimed at maintaining and promoting health in the workplace, identifying situations requiring specialist competence;
- Know the main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization, principles, and applications of preventive medicine in different realities;
- Have adequate knowledge of gender medicine, family, and territory, acquired also through practical training experiences;
- Discuss the essential elements of professionalism, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities underlying the profession; know the deontological norms and those underlying high professional responsibility;
- Have knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing team work.

Applying Knowledge and Understanding.
Preclinical Area. Graduates will be able to:
- Apply knowledge of fundamental genomic, biochemical, cellular, and physiological mechanisms that maintain the organism's homeostasis;
- Know the morphological aspects that allow the recognition of various human tissues, enabling organ diagnosis;
- Interpret morpho-functional anomalies of the organism found in various diseases, both acute and chronic;
- Know the potential and limitations of the main techniques of cell and molecular biology; know the fundamental elements of a gene and a DNA sequence; be able to consult major online genetic databases;
- Evaluate the diagnostic relevance and clinical implications of microbiological analyses;
- Identify normal and abnormal human behavior, also in the context of development;
- Clarify the etiology and natural history of acute and chronic diseases;
- Illustrate the mechanism of action of drugs and their application field, with particular reference to response variability related to gender, ethnic, and pathophysiological factors;
- Know the main pharmacological interactions and contraindications of individual drugs as well as the principles for their correct use within complex therapeutic schemes;
- Apply basic knowledge for approaching biomedical problems;
- Relate appropriately with patients and colleagues from other nationalities.

Objectives will be acquired through student participation in frontal lectures and small group activities within integrated courses and laboratory activities, and verified through written and/or oral exams.

Clinical Area. Graduates will be able to:
- Correctly collect the family and personal medical history, complete with social aspects;
- Perform a general and specific objective examination of individual organs and systems;
- Evaluate the patient's mental state, behavior, and experience;
- Apply the principles of clinical reasoning, diagnostic procedures, and basic techniques, analyzing and interpreting their results to correctly define the nature of a problem, applying appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies;
- Set up the therapeutic pathway, both medical and surgical, ensuring the most appropriate path for each individual, safeguarding life strictly according to the principle of evidence-based medicine;
- Recognize the complex, chronic, multimorbid patient, and tailor a personalized diagnostic-therapeutic pathway;
- Care for diseases and patients effectively, efficiently, and ethically, promoting health and preventing disease, fulfilling the moral obligation to provide medical care in the terminal phases of life, including palliative symptom therapy, with particular reference to pain;
- Correctly and autonomously manage common medical emergencies.

Acquisition of the above objectives will occur through integrated courses of clinical and basic subjects and through professional training activities starting from the third year of the course. Achievement of the objectives will be verified during the exams of each integrated course and the evaluation by tutors of the training activities.

Public Health and Services Area. Graduates will be able to:
- Undertake appropriate preventive and protective actions against diseases, maintaining and promoting the health of the individual, family, and community, correctly using all available resources (diagnostic, therapeutic, organizational, preventive);
- Apply the principles of privacy to demographic and epidemiological data available at local, regional, and national levels, using them correctly in decisions regarding individual and public health;
- Establish diagnostic-therapeutic pathways based on the essential principles of health economics, with specific attention to the cost/benefit ratio, continuity of care between hospital and territory, and organizational appropriateness;
- Respect professional values including excellence, altruism, responsibility, compassion, empathy, reliability, honesty, and integrity, committing to follow scientific methods and continuously update; maintain good relationships with the patient and their family, safeguarding well-being, cultural diversity, and patient autonomy;
- Correctly apply the principles of moral reasoning and adopt appropriate decisions regarding possible conflicts in ethical, legal, and professional values, including those emerging from ethnic or gender differences, economic hardship, commercialization of healthcare, and new scientific discoveries;
- Respect colleagues and other health professionals, demonstrating the ability to establish collaborative relationships with them, appropriately valuing the individual roles involved; know how to set up a correct multidisciplinary approach in fragile patients and those with multimorbidity.

Acquisition of these objectives will occur through integrated courses of clinical and basic subjects, as well as through professional training activities starting from the third year of the course. Achievement of the objectives will be verified during the exams of each integrated course and the evaluation by tutors of the training activities.

Specific training objectives description.
Qualifying objectives of the class: LM-41 Medicine and Surgery
Graduates in Master's Degree courses in Medicine and Surgery must possess:
- The scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation necessary according to Directive 75/363/EEC for the practice of the medical profession and the methodology and culture necessary for lifelong training, as well as a level of professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy derived from a training path characterized by a holistic approach to health problems of healthy or sick individuals in relation to the chemical-physical, biological, and social environment surrounding them. For this purpose, the Master's Degree course provides a total of 360 CFU, spread over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired in training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills;
- Essential theoretical knowledge derived from basic sciences, in the perspective of their subsequent professional application; the ability to detect and critically evaluate from a clinical perspective, in an integrated view extending to the sociocultural and gender dimension, data related to the health and disease status of the individual, interpreting them in light of basic scientific knowledge, pathophysiology, and organ and system pathologies; skills and experience, combined with self-assessment ability, to responsibly address and solve priority health problems from a preventive, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative perspective; knowledge of the historical, epistemological, and ethical dimensions of medicine; the ability to communicate clearly and humanely with the patient and family; the ability to collaborate with different professional figures in various group health activities; the ability to apply, in medical decisions, also the principles of health economics; the ability to recognize community health problems and intervene competently.

The professional profile of Master's graduates must include knowledge of:
- Behaviors and behavioral attitudes of the medical being;
- Fundamental notions and methodology of physics and statistics useful for identifying, understanding, and interpreting biomedical phenomena;
- Fundamental biological organization and basic biochemical and cellular processes of living organisms;
- Basic processes of individual and group behavior;
- Mechanisms of transmission and expression of genetic information at the cellular and molecular level;
- Structural organization of the human body, with its main anatomical-clinical applications, from the macroscopic to the microscopic level, up to the main ultrastructural aspects and the mechanisms through which this organization is realized during embryonic development and differentiation;
- Essential morphological characteristics of systems, organs, tissues, cells, and subcellular structures of the human body, as well as their main morpho-functional correlations;
- Biochemical, molecular, and cellular mechanisms underlying pathophysiological processes;
- Fundamentals of the main laboratory methods applicable to the qualitative and quantitative study of pathogenic determinants and significant biological processes in medicine;
- Modes of operation of the different organs of the human body, their dynamic integration into systems, and general control mechanisms in normal conditions;
- Main functional findings in healthy humans; fundamentals of the main imaging diagnostic methods and the use of radiation, principles of biomedical technology applications in medicine.

Master's graduates must also:
- Have acquired and deepened the interrelationships between the content of basic sciences and clinical sciences, in the dimension of complexity inherent to the health status of a healthy or sick person, with particular attention to the interdisciplinary nature of medicine;
- Have developed and matured a strongly integrated approach to the patient, critically evaluating not only all clinical aspects but also dedicating particular attention to relational, educational, social, and ethical aspects involved in prevention, diagnosis, treatment of disease, as well as rehabilitation and recovery of the highest possible psychophysical well-being.

Graduates in Master's Degree courses in Medicine and Surgery will carry out the activity of physician-surgeon in various roles and professional clinical, health, and bio-medical contexts.

For the purposes indicated, graduates of the class must have acquired:
- Knowledge of the organization, structure, and normal functioning of the human body, for the maintenance of the health status of a healthy person and understanding of pathological modifications; knowledge of the causes of diseases in humans, interpreting their fundamental molecular, cellular, and pathophysiological mechanisms;
- Knowledge of the fundamental biological defense mechanisms and pathological mechanisms of the immune system, as well as the knowledge of the relationship between microorganisms and host in human infections, and the related defense mechanisms;
- The ability to correctly apply methodologies to detect clinical, functional, and laboratory findings, critically interpreting them also from a pathophysiological perspective, for diagnosis and prognosis, and the ability to evaluate cost/benefit ratios in choosing diagnostic procedures, paying attention to both the correct clinical methodology and the principles of evidence-based medicine;
- A systematic knowledge of the most relevant diseases of various systems, from a nosological, etiopathogenetic, pathophysiological, and clinical perspective, within a unified and global view of human pathology, and the ability to critically evaluate and correlate clinical symptoms, physical signs, functional alterations detected in humans with anatomopathological lesions, interpreting their production mechanisms and deepening their clinical significance;
- The ability to apply appropriate clinical reasoning to analyze and solve common and relevant clinical problems, both medical and surgical, and the ability to evaluate epidemiological data and know their use for promoting health and preventing diseases in individuals and communities;
- Knowledge of the principles underlying the analysis of human behavior and adequate experience, gained through in-depth and continuous interactive teaching experiences in the field of doctor-patient relationship and communication, on the importance, quality, and appropriateness of communication with the patient and family, as well as with other health operators, being aware of their own and others' values, and the ability to appropriately use methodologies oriented towards information, education, and health education, as well as the ability to recognize major behavioral and subjective experience alterations, indicating preventive and rehabilitative therapeutic directions;
- Knowledge of anatomopathological findings as well as cellular, tissue, and organ lesions and their evolution in relation to the most relevant diseases of various systems, and knowledge, acquired also through participation in anatomoclinical conferences, of the anatomopathologist's contribution to the clinical decision-making process, with reference to the use of histopathological and cytological diagnostics (including smear and oncocytopathology) with biomolecular techniques, in the diagnosis, prevention, prognosis, and therapy of the individual patient's diseases, as well as the ability to interpret anatomopathological reports;
- The ability to correctly propose various imaging diagnostic procedures, evaluating risks, costs, and benefits, and the ability to interpret imaging diagnostic reports, as well as knowledge of the indications and methodologies for the use of radioactive tracers, and the ability to correctly propose the therapeutic use of radiation, evaluating risks and benefits, and knowledge of the principles of radioprotection;
- Knowledge of the main and most up-to-date laboratory diagnostic methods in clinical pathology, cellular, and molecular pathology, as well as the ability to correctly propose various laboratory diagnostic procedures, evaluating costs and benefits, and the ability to rationally interpret the laboratory data;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, anatomopathological, preventive, and clinical issues regarding the broncho-pulmonary, cardiovascular, gastroenterological, hematopoietic, endocrine-metabolic, immunological, and uro-nephrological systems, providing etiopathogenetic interpretation and indicating diagnostic and therapeutic directions, and identifying conditions that require the professional contribution of the specialist in the aforementioned areas;
- The ability to recognize the most frequent otorhinolaryngological, dental-stomatology, oral cavity, locomotor system, and visual apparatus diseases, as well as skin and venereal diseases, indicating the main preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic directions, and the ability to identify conditions that require the professional contribution of the specialist in the aforementioned areas;
- The ability to recognize, through pathophysiological, anatomopathological, and clinical study, the main alterations of the nervous system and psychiatric and social context diseases, providing etiopathogenetic interpretation and indicating diagnostic and therapeutic directions;
- The ability and sensitivity to insert specialized issues into a broader view of the general health status of the person and their general well-being needs, and the ability to integrate into a global and unified evaluation of the overall health status of the individual the symptoms, signs, and structural and functional alterations of individual organs and systems, aggregating them under preventive, diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative aspects;
- Knowledge of the physiological changes of aging and the issues of disease status in the elderly, and the ability to plan medical and health care interventions in geriatric patients;
- The ability to analyze and solve clinical problems of internal medicine, surgery, and specialist order, evaluating the relationship between benefits, risks, and costs in light of evidence-based medicine principles and diagnostic-therapeutic appropriateness;
- The ability to analyze and solve clinical problems of oncological order, addressing the diagnostic-therapeutic process in light of evidence-based medicine principles, as well as knowledge of pain therapy and palliative care;
- The skill and sensitivity to apply the essential principles of health economics in medical decisions, with specific attention to the cost/benefit ratio of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, continuity of care between hospital and territory, and organizational appropriateness;
- Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of human sciences regarding the historical evolution of medical values, including epistemological and ethical aspects; the skill and sensitivity to critically evaluate medical acts within the health team;
- Knowledge of the different drug classes, molecular and cellular mechanisms of their action, fundamental principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, and knowledge of therapeutic uses of drugs, response variability related to gender, genetic, and pathophysiological factors, pharmacological interactions, and criteria for defining therapeutic schemes, as well as knowledge of the principles and methods of clinical pharmacology, including pharmacovigilance and pharmacoepidemiology, side effects, and drug toxicity and abuse;
- Knowledge, from a preventive, diagnostic, and rehabilitative perspective, of issues related to health and disease status in neonatal, pediatric, and adolescent age, for the non-specialist physician, and the ability to identify conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist and to plan essential medical interventions for the main health problems, by frequency and risk, related to pediatric specialist pathology;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, psychological, and clinical issues regarding female fertility and sexual dysfunction from a medical sexological perspective, natural and assisted procreation from an endocrine-gynecological perspective, pregnancy, prenatal morbidity, and childbirth, and the ability to recognize the most frequent gynecological pathologies, indicating fundamental preventive and therapeutic measures, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist;
- Knowledge of the pathophysiological, psychological, and clinical issues regarding male fertility and evaluation of male gametes, male sexuality and its dysfunctions from a medical sexological perspective, natural and assisted procreation from an endocrine-andrological perspective, and the ability to recognize the most frequent andrological pathologies, indicating fundamental preventive and therapeutic measures, and identifying conditions requiring the professional contribution of the specialist;
- The ability to recognize, in the immediacy of the event, clinical situations of emergency and urgency, taking the necessary initial actions to ensure survival and the best possible assistance, and knowledge of intervention modalities in disaster situations;
- Knowledge of the fundamental norms to maintain and promote the health of the individual and communities, and knowledge of the norms and practices to maintain and promote health in the workplace, identifying situations requiring specialist competence, as well as knowledge of the main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization and the ability to indicate principles and applications of preventive medicine in various and complex communities;
- Knowledge of deontological norms and those related to high professional responsibility, critically evaluating the ethical principles underlying different possible professional choices, and the ability to develop an interdisciplinary and transcultural mental approach, especially in collaboration with other health team figures, deepening knowledge of the rules and dynamics characterizing team work, as well as adequate experience in the general organization of work, connected to sensitivity to its characteristics, bioethics, history, and epistemology of medicine, the relationship with the patient, as well as towards community medicine themes, acquired also through direct field experiences; knowledge of the aspects characterizing multicultural society, with specific reference to the variety and diversification of value and cultural aspects;
- A deep knowledge of the technological and biotechnological development of modern bio-medicine, including knowledge of the principles of scientific research in the biomedical field and clinical-specialist areas, the ability to search, read, and interpret international literature for planning research on specific topics and developing a critical interpretation mindset of scientific data;
- Adequate experience in independent study and organization of their lifelong training, and the ability to conduct bibliographic research and update, the ability to critically read scientific articles derived from knowledge of scientific English that allows them to understand international literature and update; written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian; computer skills useful for managing information systems of services and their self-training; adequate knowledge of family and territorial medicine, acquired also through practical training experiences.

In particular, specific professional skills in the fields of internal medicine, general surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, as well as medical and surgical specialties, acquired by carrying out professional training activities for a duration of at least 60 CFU, to be carried out in an integrated manner with other training activities of the course at university healthcare facilities.

The duration of the course for the attainment of the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is 6 years.

Regarding the definition of curricula prepared for the execution of activities provided by Directive 75/363/EEC, the university didactic regulations comply with the provisions of the present decree and Article 6, paragraph 3, of Ministerial Decree No. 270/04.

Finally, in accordance with Ministerial Decree No. 8 of April 2, 2020, which adapts the didactic organization of class LM41 - Medicine and Surgery as per Ministerial Decree of March 16, 2007, the professional training internship is a qualifying part of professional training. Within the 60 CFU to be acquired throughout the training path, destined for the aforementioned professional training activity, 15 CFU must be dedicated to the completion of the quarterly practical-evaluative internship within the study course, as per Article 3 of the Ministerial Decree of May 9, 2018, No. 58 and amendments, aimed at obtaining professional qualification. This internship is carried out for a number of hours corresponding to at least 5 CFU per month and is structured in the following periods, not necessarily consecutive: one month in Surgical Area; one month in Medical Area; one month, to be carried out not before the sixth year of the course, in the specific field of General Medicine.

The Master's Degree Course in Medicine and Surgery of the University of Sassari aims to train a physician capable of addressing, after the degree, any type of specialist training in both medical and surgical fields, as well as organizational roles in healthcare systems and their professional updating.

The specific learning objectives are outlined in a manner consistent with both general and specific indications represented in the European Descriptors of Qualifications (Dublin descriptors), integrating them with what proposed by the Institute for International Medical Education (IIME), Task Force for Assessment, and by "The TUNING Project (Medicine) – Learning Outcomes/Competences for Undergraduate Medical Education in Europe": the objectives are finally consistent with what indicated by the "Core curriculum for the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery" proposed by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Italian LM41 Degree Courses.

The Course, for the achievement of didactic objectives, provides a total of 360 CFU, spread over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired in practical training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (professionalizing CFU). The 12 semesters of the Course, which include 36 integrated courses, provide for the attribution of CFU in compliance with the table of essential training activities. Each CFU corresponds to a student workload of 25 hours, of which not more than 12 hours of frontal lectures in basic, characterizing, and related disciplinary fields, or theoretical-practical teaching (seminar, laboratory, exercise), or 25 hours of guided study within the teaching structure.

Each professionalizing CFU (training internships and orientation) corresponds to 25 hours of student work, also including small group teaching activities, as well as each CFU for student-selected activities and the final exam.

The specific mission of the Master's Degree Course in Medicine and Surgery is biomedical-psychosocial and aimed at the real development of "professional competence" and "professional values." It is based on the importance of integrating the biomedical paradigm of "curing the disease" with the psychosocial paradigm of "caring for the human being" in the meta-paradigm of "complexity of care." This specific mission is therefore aimed at training a physician, at an initial professional level, who possesses:
- A multidisciplinary, interprofessional, and integrated vision of common health and disease problems;
- Education oriented towards disease prevention and health promotion within the community and territory;
- A deep knowledge of new care and health needs, focused not only on the disease but especially on the sick person, considered in their entirety of body and mind and inserted in a specific social context.

The teaching method adopted, useful for achieving the expected qualifying characteristics, provides for the horizontal and vertical integration of knowledge, a teaching method based on a solid cultural and methodological foundation acquired through the study of pre-clinical disciplines and subsequently mainly focused on the ability to solve problems and make decisions, early contact with the patient, and the acquisition of good clinical and interpersonal skills with the patient.

In the didactic project of the Master's Degree Course, the right balance of vertical and transversal integration is proposed between:
a) Basic sciences, which must be broad and include knowledge of evolutionary biology, molecular biology, and genetics, and biological complexity aimed at understanding the structure and function of the human body in normal conditions, for maintaining health conditions and correctly applying translational scientific research;
b) Knowledge of pathological processes and mechanisms that cause them, also to set up prevention, diagnosis, and therapy;
c) Clinical and methodological medical practice, which must be particularly solid, through extensive use of tutorial teaching, capable of transforming theoretical knowledge into personal experience to build one's own scale of values and interests, and to acquire professional skills useful for managing the complexity of medicine;
d) Human sciences, which must constitute a useful background to reach awareness of being a physician and the deep values of medical professionalism;
e) Acquisition of scientific, medical, clinical, and professional methodology directed at health problems of the individual and community.

[ TSS ]
High School Diploma Professional roles President ELISABETTA GAVINI Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Pharmacist The main career opportunities for graduates in Pharmacy Master's Degree are:
- Community pharmacist;
-Hospital pharmacist and Pharmacist in the context of the Territorial Pharmaceutical Service, following Specialization in Hospital Pharmacy;
- Scientific-technical drug information officer.
Graduates may also consider other professional activities carried out in the European Union in the field of drugs.
Therefore, graduates in Pharmacy find career opportunities, for example, in the following fields:
● procurement, preparation, control, storage, distribution and dispensing of quality medicines;
● formulation, production, packaging, quality and stability control and toxicological evaluation of cosmetic products;
● dissemination of information and advice on medicines and medical devices, including their correct use, and personalized patient support for self-medication;
● advice in the field of cosmetic, dietary and nutritional products, as well as herbal products for maintaining and safeguarding health;
● participation in institutional public health campaigns.
Final exam characteristics.
The Master's Degree in Pharmacy belongs to class LM-13, which has become qualifying (Law 8 November 2022, n.163, Interministerial Decree n.651 of 5 July 2022). The final exam for the Master's Degree in Pharmacy includes the completion of a practical assessment of professional skills acquired through the internship within the Study Course; this assessment precedes the thesis discussion and aims to verify the candidate's technical preparation level for professional qualification. The thesis (final exam) is developed by the student under the guidance and supervision of a supervisor; the thesis must be the result of an experimental research activity on an original mono- or multi-disciplinary topic or a critical collection and processing of bibliographic material or other data related to the cultural and professional content of the Study Course, demonstrating the student's ability to work independently, the acquisition of the necessary skills for project development, and mastery of the topics discussed. The thesis discussion will take place before the final exam assessment committee, which is supplemented by pharmacists designated by the professional order.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Pharmacy Single Cycle, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable.
An individual admission test is mandatory, also online, with modalities defined by the Didactic Regulations of the Course Council. Through the test, which includes multiple-choice questions divided by specific subjects to be completed within a specified time, basic knowledge from the secondary school curriculum in physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology, logic and English is verified. If the test does not meet the minimum requirements defined by the Course Council, an additional mandatory training obligation (OFA) will be assigned, to be fulfilled according to the modalities established by the Didactic Regulations of the Course Council.
Planned career opportunities and professional roles for graduates.

Communication Skills.
The Master's graduate in Pharmacy develops skills:
- as a consultant in the healthcare field, listening to, informing, and advising patients on medicines, medical devices, herbal products, food supplements, and foods intended for special diets;
- appropriate relationship and communication skills with patients/clients of all ages and with other healthcare professionals;
- organization and management skills for pharmacies.
The developed skills enable the Pharmacy graduate to operate as a drug expert in the preparation, control, dispensing, and monitoring of medicines, medical devices, and other health products such as cosmetics, food supplements, herbal products, and foods intended for special diets, including the compounding of medicines for personalized therapies, and in pharmacoeconomic evaluations, therapy adherence assessments, and prescription appropriateness evaluations, also in a hospital setting.
These objectives will be achieved through professionalizing thematic seminars and a practical assessment internship in a public pharmacy or a hospital pharmacy. Completing part of the internship in a pharmacy abroad contributes to acquiring language skills. Assessment methods include written and/or oral exams. Professional skills acquisition is evaluated through a practical assessment. Acquisition and evaluation of scientific-communication skills are also provided through the writing and discussion of the final thesis.
Learning Ability.
The Master's graduate in Pharmacy possesses relational and interaction skills with the public and healthcare operators, with whom they develop synergies. They are prepared for continuous updating to align their knowledge with developments in drug sciences and technologies and health products, and to enhance their cultural foundations and professional competencies through Advanced Training pathways (Research Doctorate, Master's Degree, Specialization Schools). They possess independent judgment.
These abilities develop throughout the training path through active attendance at theoretical-practical lessons, thematic seminars, practical assessment internship, and thesis writing, and are verified through written and/or oral exams, including intermediate assessments, practical assessment, and thesis discussion.
