Judgment Autonomy.
The judgment autonomy of the Master's graduate in Pharmacy must be exercisable whenever they find themselves in a situation requiring decision-making that necessitates the acquired knowledge. During their training path, the student acquires multidisciplinary knowledge that they are capable of applying during the TPV. At the end of the university course, the Master's graduate in Pharmacy is able to manage the pharmaceutical service in various work contexts, develop synergies with other healthcare professions within public and private structures and entities, interact effectively with the public by providing information and advice, and act as a liaison between the physician, patient, and healthcare service structures. Judgment autonomy is developed through specific training activities and didactic tools such as lectures, laboratory exercises, even individual, videos, procedure demonstrations, thematic seminars, and is completed with the TPV and the thesis, which lead the pharmacy student to progressively assume autonomy and responsibility. The acquisition of judgment autonomy is verified through written and oral exams, in-course assessments, laboratory activities, and reports prepared during these training activities, as well as the thesis discussion, while the practical assessment verifies the acquisition of competencies and professional autonomy.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area: SYNTHESIS Knowledge and Understanding The graduates must have demonstrated possession of the knowledge that constitutes the basis for personal and professional growth, as well as for undertaking further studies, particularly in research doctorates, Master's programs, and Specialization Schools. The Study Course will be organized into semester-long courses where knowledge of basic, pharmaceutical-chemical, nutraceutical, technological, cosmetic, biological, and pharmacological subjects will be acquired through lectures and laboratory exercises under the guidance of the instructor. Verification of the achievement of expected outcomes will occur through oral interviews and/or written assignments. In-course assessments will allow periodic verification of the learning status of the taught concepts and, if necessary, activate recovery courses for students lagging in preparation.

Each activity will be assured through the use of the Microsoft Teams online platform or according to any directives from the Academic Bodies.

BASIC DISCIPLINES The main objective of basic disciplines is to provide the foundation so that subsequent courses related to the synthesis, development, and control of drugs and health products can be received and applied on a solid knowledge base.

Within basic disciplines, the educational offer is structured as follows:

MATHEMATICS AND ELEMENTS OF MEDICAL STATISTICS Knowledge and understanding of set and function concepts, properties of elementary and quasi-elementary functions, limits, and differential calculus with its main applications, and an introduction to ordinary differential equations.

Specific objectives: to provide a solid understanding of real number, function, graph, limit, derivative concepts; brief introduction to differential equations; the ability to represent a phenomenon using a mathematical model.

PHYSICS Knowledge and understanding of the scientific method, units of measurement, and dimensions of physical quantities; kinematics, dynamics, brief introduction to mechanics, work and energy, conservation laws, fluids and gases, brief introduction to thermodynamics, brief introduction to electromagnetism and ionizing radiation.

Specific objectives: to provide the basic skills of physics to address issues in subsequent courses. The topics covered will lead the student to acquire the correct methodology for analysis by applying the scientific method.

GENERAL AND INORGANIC CHEMISTRY WITH LABORATORY Knowledge and understanding of atoms and molecules, the mole and chemical reactions, atomic structure and periodic properties of elements, chemical bonds, molecular geometry, chemical nomenclature, intermolecular forces, gaseous, liquid, and solid states, solutions and their properties, preparation and dilution of a solution, chemical equilibrium, brief introduction to solubility, kinetics, introduction to acids and bases and pH, electrochemistry.

Specific objectives: to provide the fundamental principles of general and inorganic chemistry to enable the student to understand and describe phenomena and transformations involving atoms and molecules. In the laboratory, the student will see the practical application of some of the topics covered theoretically.

PRINCIPLES OF ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY Content: The course includes the study and calculations of solution concentrations and conversion between units of measurement, applied study of chemical equilibrium in general and particularly acid-base, hydrolysis, buffer solutions, solubility, redox, and coordination equilibria.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with basic skills regarding aqueous solutions in terms of concentration measurement and equilibrium reactions.

HUMAN ANATOMY WITH ELEMENTS OF ANIMAL BIOLOGY Knowledge and understanding of the interpretation of metabolic processes at the cellular level, tissue organization and their morpho-functional correlations with microscopic anatomy. Basic anatomical knowledge of different systems and organs, with in-depth study of the microscopic characteristics of organs composing the human body for understanding structural and functional relationships.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with basic skills regarding the structural organization of eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells; the structure and function of various cell types and tissues of the human body. Ability to know and use anatomical language, possess adequate knowledge of the morphological organization of the human body, describe the macro and microscopic constitution of the organs composing it; acquire the ability to recognize and describe macroscopically and microscopically, also using images, the various parts of the body.

PHARMACEUTICAL BOTANY AND ELEMENTS OF PLANT BIOLOGY Knowledge and understanding of general characteristics of plant cytology, histology, and organography, knowledge of plant systematics, morphological characterization and recognition of the main plant species of pharmaceutical interest.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with basic skills for the macroscopic recognition of the main plant species of medicinal interest and their use in pharmaceutical, herbal, and food fields.

ORGANIC CHEMISTRY Knowledge and understanding of chemical bonds according to atomic orbital theory, hybrid and molecular orbitals. General principles of thermodynamics and chemical kinetics. Acid-base equilibria in organic chemistry. Nomenclature, physical properties, preparation methods, and reactivity of common classes of organic compounds. Basic elements of stereochemistry. Basic elements of heterocyclic chemistry.

Specific objectives: to provide the basic skills to recognize organic functional groups, their physical properties, preparation methods, and reactivity. Knowledge of the nomenclature of various classes of compounds.

GENERAL PATHOLOGY (WITH ELEMENTS OF MEDICAL TERMINOLOGY) Knowledge and understanding of cellular, molecular, and functional mechanisms underlying the general etiology and pathogenesis of diseases. Cellular adaptations, damage mechanisms, aging, cell death and repair, inflammation, immunobiology and immunopathology, and oncology.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with information on the main aspects of General Pathology, enabling them to use the acquired knowledge to understand the etiology and pathogenesis of diseases and their treatment. The course also aims to provide technical-linguistic tools for effective and appropriate communication with the public.

GENERAL PHYSIOLOGY Content: The course, through a multidisciplinary and systematic approach by organ systems, will address the processes and mechanisms underlying the functions of different organs and organ systems of the human body, the mechanisms used by the main regulatory physiological systems to allow different organs and systems to work in a coordinated and integrated manner to maintain homeostasis and, therefore, health (physiological condition).

Specific objectives: to provide the student with fundamental knowledge on the main mechanisms regulating homeostasis and physiological functions of the organism, with particular attention to their interactions with drugs and other biologically active agents.

MICROBIOLOGY Knowledge and understanding of biological, physiological, and molecular relationships between the host and microorganisms, with particular interest in the etiological agents responsible for old and new diseases. Action of main antimicrobials, related resistance mechanisms, and host defenses. Different isolation and identification techniques for new and old generations, with awareness that all topics are continuously evolving.

Specific objectives: to provide adequate knowledge of the structural, biological, and physiological properties of pathogenic microorganisms and the mechanisms through which these microorganisms exert their pathogenic action. Acquire the basics for understanding host/parasite interaction and analyze diagnostic/clinical aspects useful for understanding therapy.

HYGIENE AND HEALTH EDUCATION Knowledge and understanding of the concepts of health, disease, causal factors, and risk factors. Primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention. Epidemiological methodology. General and applied epidemiology for the study of infectious and non-infectious diseases. Prevention of infectious diseases with particular attention to immunoprophylaxis and chemioprophylaxis. Health education interventions: from theory to practice.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with skills to recognize conditions that damage or promote health, evaluate attitudes and behaviors favorable to promoting well-being, and collaborate in health education programs.

PHARMACEUTICAL- AND FOOD-RELATED, TECHNOLOGICAL, REGULATORY, BIOLOGICAL, AND PHARMACOLOGICAL DISCIPLINES The main objective of pharmaceutical-chemical, nutraceutical, technological, regulatory, biological, and pharmacological disciplines is the learning of the design, synthesis, development, use, and control of drugs of synthetic, semi-synthetic, and natural origin and their medicinal products, nutraceuticals, food supplements, cosmetics, medical devices, and health products. Knowledge and understanding of drug regulations and ethics form the correct professional execution of the pharmaceutical service within the National Health Service and national and European regulations, interaction with other healthcare professions, and communication with non-specialist interlocutors. Galenic knowledge provides the ability to address personalized therapies.

The objective of the bio-pharmacological area disciplines is to provide solid knowledge and understanding of the general strategies underlying physiological processes through the study of the structure of major biomolecules and their receptors, as well as signal transduction and their functions, in order to understand their clinical use, side effects, adverse reactions, and drug doses in the main organ and system pathologies.

For some learning areas, in addition to lectures, practical laboratory sessions, thematic professionalizing seminars, and meetings with experts or professionals in the field are provided.

In this context, the educational offer is structured as follows:

CELLULAR AND METABOLIC BIOCHEMISTRY Content: Biomolecules. Structure and function of proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids. Principles of enzyme kinetics. Structure of biomembranes. Solute diffusion through pores and channels, mediated transport. Glucidic, lipidic, aminoacidic, and nucleotide metabolism. Principles of Bioenergetics and energy utilization: Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Structure of nucleic acids. DNA replication. Transcription and regulation of gene expression. Genetic code and protein synthesis.

Specific objectives: to provide the basis of the physical, chemical, and biological context in which molecules, reactions, and metabolic pathways are framed. Knowledge of the relationships between structure and function of major macromolecules, framing enzymatic catalysis, thermodynamics, and metabolism at the molecular and cellular level, highlighting their connections. Develop specific scientific skills such as thinking, writing, and critical evaluation.

APPLIED MEDICAL BIOCHEMISTRY Content: Methods and models in biochemical research. Safety in biological laboratories. Analytical and preparative separations. Methods of separation of classes of biomolecules. Purpose, general principles, instrumentation, and applications of the following techniques in biomedical fields: spectrophotometry and spectrofluorimetry, ultracentrifugation, chromatography, electrophoresis and isoelectric focusing, immunochromatographic techniques, and proteomic analysis techniques.

Specific objectives: to acquaint the student with principles and purposes of the most used methodologies in biochemical research for isolation and structural and functional analysis of biomolecules. The student will be able to use logical procedures and experimental methodology, indicate and describe the main biomedical applications of biomolecular technologies covered in the course.

GENERAL AND MOLECULAR PHARMACOLOGY Content: Aspects of pharmacodynamics (specific and non-specific drug effects, interactions with receptor and non-receptor structures, signal transduction systems) and pharmacokinetics (routes of drug administration and their absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion), mechanisms of variability in response, including elements of pharmacogenetics and pharmacogenomics, and new technological approaches to therapy (pharmacogenetics, pharmacogenomics, biological drugs, and gene therapy).

Specific objectives: to provide knowledge regarding the mechanisms of drug interactions with different biological targets of the human body, with attention also to new technological approaches (pharmacogenetics, pharmacogenomics, biological drugs, and gene therapy).

PHARMACOLOGY AND PHARMACOTHERAPY Content: General principles of pharmacology, pharmacotherapy, and pharmacognosy. Neuropharmacology. Pharmacotherapy of mood disorders. Pharmacology of neurodegenerative diseases. Cardiovascular pharmacology. Drugs for renal function. Inflammation, fever, and pain therapy. Gastrointestinal drugs. Lipid metabolism drugs. Respiratory drugs. Principles of antimicrobial and antineoplastic chemotherapy. Hormones and antagonists. Doping.

Specific objectives: to provide basic skills in pharmacology and pharmacotherapy (drug-receptor interaction, mechanism of action, signal transduction, evaluation of therapeutic efficacy and safety, adverse reactions, and side effects. Drug interactions.

TOXICOLOGY AND PHARMACOVIGILANCE Content: Definitions of toxicology. Kinetics of toxins (routes of administration, absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion). Dynamics of toxins (receptors, ion channels, enzymes, transcription factors). Neurotoxicological investigation methods. Agonism, antagonism, inverse agonism, partial agonism, Kd. Toxic dependencies: definitions and neurobiology. Opioids, Psychostimulants, Alcohol, Cannabinoids, Nicotine, Designer drugs. Pharmacovigilance.

Specific objectives: to inform students about the toxic effects of drugs and the pathologies resulting from their use, abuse, or misuse. Principles of pharmacovigilance.

MORPHOLOGY AND DIAGNOSTICS OF DRUGS Content: Main drugs of therapeutic, toxicological, and abuse interest. Study of main extraction methods for active principles of natural origin, and basic knowledge of manipulation of plant, animal, and mineral drugs.

Specific objectives: to provide concepts and basic knowledge for the identification and knowledge of derivatives of natural origin, particularly plant, mineral, and animal. Lead the student to knowledge of the biological activity of drugs (pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic aspects) and toxicological aspects of their active constituents, thus evaluating their therapeutic use.

PHYTOCHEMISTRY AND HERBAL PREPARATIONS Content: Study of active principles, phyto-complexes, and main metabolic pathways. Preparation of plant extracts, their identification and purification to produce extracts usable in herbal preparations.

Specific objectives: (Phytomedicine module) to provide the student with knowledge of the most important plant-derived drugs, active principles contained therein, biogenesis of main metabolic pathways, and potential use in phytotherapy. Provides the basis for understanding the quality and safety of plant drugs, analyzing adverse effects and possible drug-toxicological interactions. Provide the student with the basis for the correct and safe use of medicinal plants and their derivatives.

(Preparations module) Lead the student to address the main extraction and analysis methods of phyto-complexes. Prepare for the laboratory preparation of main plant extracts to be included in finished herbal preparations.

PHARMACEUTICAL AND TOXICOLOGICAL CHEMISTRY Content: Pharmacokinetic aspects: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion. Pharmacodynamic aspects: drug-target interaction. Influence of steric factors. Bioisosterism. Enzyme inhibition. Toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic aspects of xenobiotic agents.

Specific objectives: to provide knowledge of molecular mechanisms underlying the action and toxicity at molecular, cellular, tissue, and systemic levels of major drug classes and xenobiotic agents.

PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY 1 Content: Chemotherapy against bacteria and mycobacteria, antiprotozoal, anthelmintic, antifungal, antiviral, and conventional and targeted antitumor therapy (with elements of immunooncology). Endocrine therapy, pituitary hormones, steroid hormones, insulin and oral hypoglycemics, thyroid hormones. Drugs for the gastrointestinal system (constipation and laxatives, diarrhea and antidiarrheals, dyspeptic diseases).

Specific objectives: to provide the educational and informative criteria regarding chemical-physical properties, indications, and mechanisms of action, SAR studies (with relative molecular activity maps) of drug classes (BNF 82) related to the course.

PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY 2 Content: Chemical-physical properties, molecular mechanism of action, structure-activity relationships, and therapeutic use of the main classes of drugs for the central nervous system, cardiovascular, respiratory, and gastrointestinal systems.

Specific objectives: to provide knowledge useful for therapeutic applications, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of the main classes of drugs acting centrally and peripherally.

ANALYSIS OF MEDICAMENTS Content: Theoretical principles of quantitative and qualitative analysis of some organic and metal-organic substances listed in the European Pharmacopoeia with individual laboratory exercises related to their determination and identification using chemical and instrumental methods.

Specific objectives: to provide a systematic approach, knowledge, and methodologies useful for the quantitative and qualitative recognition of pharmaceutical substances listed in the Official European Pharmacopoeia.

PHARMACEUTICAL TECHNOLOGY AND GALENIC PREPARATIONS Content: Principles of formulation and routes of administration. Basic formulation operations and conventional pharmaceutical forms (composition, preparation methods, and tests according to FUXII). Preservation and primary packaging. Stability and stabilization of a medicinal product. Preparations from plant drugs (Cannabis). Preparation, control, packaging, and pricing of galenic, magistral, and officinal preparations.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with a complete understanding of conventional pharmaceutical forms from both theoretical and practical perspectives. At the end of the course, the student will be able to formulate, prepare, package, and perform quality controls of officinal and magistral galenic medicines, as well as apply the national pricing of medicinal products.

INNOVATIVE PHARMACEUTICAL FORMS Content: Innovative drug delivery systems to improve bio pharmaceutical characteristics (stability, solubility, bioavailability). Controlled and targeted drug release formulations. Delivery of biological/biotechnological drugs. Formulation aspects of vaccines.

Specific objectives: to complete the student's knowledge on available pharmaceutical forms in the market with modified-release medicines. Provide the student with theoretical knowledge regarding recent formulation aspects of biological and biotechnological drugs and vaccine delivery.

PHARMACEUTICAL LEGISLATION AND ETHICS Content: Main ethical aspects related to the exercise of the pharmacist profession. Regulations for authorization to market, distribution, and dispensing of medicinal products (Legislative Decree No. 219/2006). Veterinary Medicines. Pharmacy inspections. Integrated assistance, off-label prescription of medicinal products. Equivalent and Biosimilar Medicines. Service Pharmacy. Classification of diagnostic products and other products for maintaining health and well-being, including herbal preparations, cosmetics, medical devices, and in vitro diagnostic medical-surgical devices and biocides.

Specific objectives: to acquire the basic theoretical principles related to the marketing and dispensing of drugs, the Italian healthcare system, the SSN, the pharmaceutical market, and its socioeconomic impact. The knowledge acquired during the course constitutes essential elements for the exercise of the pharmacist profession.

TECHNOLOGY AND LEGISLATION OF COSMETIC PRODUCTS AND MEDICAL DEVICES Content: European Regulation 1223/2009. Structure of the skin and hair. Main cosmetic ingredients (lipids, surfactants, conditioners, rheology modifiers, colorants, preservatives, antioxidants, humectants, film formers). Cosmetic forms. Antiperspirants and deodorants. Sun protection products. Cleansing products for skin and hair. Main classes of medical devices and regulatory aspects.

Specific objectives: to illustrate the European Regulation on cosmetics to the student, provide basic knowledge of the main raw materials used in cosmetic formulation, and describe in detail the formulation and mechanism of action of some important cosmetic types. Provide basic knowledge on types and regulations of medical devices.

FOOD AND DIETARY PRODUCTS Content: Foods between nutrition and well-being, metabolism, and energy needs. Principles of food legislation, supplements, vitamin-fortified foods, and other substances, special medical foods. Chemical, dietary, and toxicological aspects of the main nutrient categories: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, vitamins, minerals, and water. Chemical, dietary, and toxicological aspects of the main food and dietary product categories.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with basic skills regarding knowledge and understanding of the main nutrient categories, and provide indispensable knowledge to give nutritional advice or on dietary products.

COMPLEMENTARY AND INTEGRATIVE ACTIVITIES The main objective of medical disciplines is to provide knowledge and skills in the field of first-level analysis to enable the Pharmacy graduate to effectively communicate and develop synergies with other healthcare professions, participate in health education programs, perform first-level analytical procedures and first aid interventions, and use instrumental devices for second-level services provided in pharmacy.

Economic-management disciplines aim to introduce elements of business management to provide knowledge on the dynamics of operational management in pharmacy, while statistical disciplines are useful for understanding statistical-epidemiological health data.

ELEMENTS OF MEDICAL STATISTICS Content: Evidence-based medicine. Experiment and observation. Design of a scientific study. Analysis of a scientific article. Statistical terminology. Types of variables. Concepts of univariate, bivariate, and multivariate statistics. Frequency distributions. Tabular and graphical representations. Measures of central tendency. Measures of variability. Axioms and rules of probability. Bayes' theorem. Diagnostic test indicators. Gaussian probability distribution. Population and sample. Sampling. Hypothesis testing. Correlation and regression.

Specific objectives: to familiarize with the principles of descriptive medical statistics and know the statistical terminology used in scientific contexts for describing populations and samples. Adequate knowledge of basic probabilistic and inferential principles, knowledge of methodological elements useful for interpreting the design of a scientific study. Acquisition of medical statistics elements useful for correctly understanding the results of a scientific study.

CLINICAL ANALYSIS AND INSTRUMENTAL DIAGNOSTICS:
CLINICAL ANALYSIS Content: Introduction and role of clinical biochemistry, biological samples of interest and reports, analytical and biological variability, quality control, diagnostic logic in laboratory medicine, predictive values. Laboratory data: EBLM.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with the necessary skills to interpret the results of a laboratory analysis. In particular, understand the role of biological and biochemical parameters at different levels of structural organization, from single cells to the entire human organism. Possess the necessary knowledge for studying molecular alterations underlying genetic and acquired diseases; the necessary knowledge for evaluating laboratory data.

INSTRUMENTAL DIAGNOSTICS Content: Devices for non-invasive measurement of: arterial pressure and oxygen saturation percentage. Devices for non-invasive monitoring of arterial pressure and cardiac activity in functional connection with accredited cardiology centers. Devices for performing electrocardiograms with telecardiology modalities to be conducted in connection with accredited cardiology centers, defibrillators. Basic concepts of the measured parameter, normal and pathological values, and useful information for interpreting the report will be provided.

Specific objectives: to provide technical indications regarding the use of instrumental devices for second-level services provided in pharmacy within the scope of services provided by Service Pharmacy.

PHARMACY MANAGEMENT Content: Systemic theory of the company; institutional structure; asset structure. The system of operational management and dynamics of values; analysis of operations related to financing, acquisition of productive factors, production, and sales; monetary, financial, and economic aspects of management; concepts of cost, revenue, income; different notions of capital. Conditions of business equilibrium: economic, monetary, and financial equilibrium. Financial problem: quantification of financial needs; internal and external sources of financing; self-financing. Applications.

Specific objectives: to provide a synthetic interpretative framework of the characteristics, principles, and fundamental management issues of business systems. Also provides knowledge on the dynamics of operational management and tools for accounting representation of equilibrium conditions in the income statement.

MANAGEMENT OF MINOR DISEASES:
SKIN AND VENEREAL DISEASES Content: Different forms of dermatitis, common skin infections (bacterial, viral, and fungal), parasitic dermatitis, differential diagnosis of onychopathies, most frequent trichological manifestations, and general characteristics of cutaneous neoplastic lesions.

Specific objectives: to provide the student with basic skills regarding the knowledge of dermatological diseases of high frequency affecting the skin, hair, nails, and mucous membranes for correct clinical assessment.

MINOR DISEASES Content: Pain, edema, diarrhea or pseudo, constipation, fatigue, cough, fever, dizziness, abdominal swelling, dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux, sleep disorders, anxiety, cystitis, and intimate mycoses. Each symptom will be related to issues, "red flags," questions to ask the customer, diagnostic analyses, therapeutic and educational approach.

Specific objectives: to provide students with some basic knowledge, fundamental for assessing minor diseases for which patients frequently consult the pharmacist, and to provide the elements of evaluation useful to understand the need for medical intervention or the opportunity to intervene with therapeutic (pharmacological and non-pharmacological) and educational approaches.

OTHER FORMATIVE ACTIVITIES These activities, which deepen and complement the basic, characteristic, and related knowledge already acquired by students, concern ENGLISH LANGUAGE
- Knowledge of grammar and text elaboration, as well as their comprehension (European Level B2)

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area: SYNTHESIS Graduates of the Pharmacy Study Course must have demonstrated the ability to apply, in the performance of their profession, knowledge of a) pharmaceutical chemistry for performing and describing quantitative (drug dosage) and qualitative (drug recognition and purity tests) analyses of drugs; b) practical techniques for preparing galenic preparations and performing technological controls of pharmaceutical forms according to the Italian Official Pharmacopoeia and the European Pharmacopoeia; c) pharmaceutical legislation.

In particular, graduates must be able to apply knowledge useful for the professional execution of the pharmaceutical service within the National Health Service, and interact clearly with other healthcare professions and non-specialist interlocutors.

The didactic tools used to achieve these objectives include both classroom lectures and laboratory activities under the guidance of the instructor. Verification methods include written and oral exams, and laboratory tests.

Knowledge and skills are acquired and verified through basic disciplines, pharmaceutical-chemical and technological disciplines, and biological and pharmacological disciplines.

Each activity will be assured through the use of the Microsoft Teams online platform or according to any directives from the Academic Bodies.

BASIC DISCIPLINES MATHEMATICS AND ELEMENTS OF MEDICAL STATISTICS); PHYSICS
- Ability to correctly apply mathematical knowledge.
- Ability to correctly apply the tools of the scientific method and operational skills related to the principles of classical physics.

GENERAL AND INORGANIC CHEMISTRY WITH LABORATORY; PRINCIPLES OF ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY; ORGANIC CHEMISTRY
- Ability to apply, describe, and apply the properties of electronic configurations for characterizing chemical bonds, molecular geometry, and performing calculations necessary for studying chemical reactions and equilibrium systems.
- Ability to apply the basic aspects of analytical chemistry in the context of drug analysis.
- Ability to apply the fundamental knowledge of organic chemistry aimed at learning pharmaceutical, chemical, and biological disciplines.

PHARMACEUTICAL BOTANY AND ELEMENTS OF PLANT BIOLOGY; GENERAL PHYSIOLOGY; HUMAN ANATOMY WITH ELEMENTS OF ANIMAL BIOLOGY; GENERAL PATHOLOGY (WITH ELEMENTS OF MEDICAL TERMINOLOGY); MICROBIOLOGY; HYGIENE AND HEALTH EDUCATION
- Ability to apply basic knowledge of Botany and the most common plant species used in official and traditional medicine.
- Ability to apply knowledge of organ functions, particularly the human body as a whole, to distinguish different pathologies.
- Ability to use anatomical language, acquire adequate knowledge of the morphological organization of the human body, describe the macro and microscopic constitution of the organs composing it, and acquire the ability to recognize and describe macroscopically and microscopically, also using images, the various parts of the body.
- Ability to interpret fundamental pathogenetic and pathophysiological mechanisms, from the cell to organs and systems. Ability to correctly address the main diagnostic techniques through a correct clinical approach.
- Ability to apply knowledge of the structural, biological, and physiological properties of pathogenic microorganisms and the mechanisms through which these microorganisms exert their pathogenic action. Acquire the basics for understanding host/parasite interaction and analyze diagnostic/clinical aspects useful for understanding therapy.
- Ability to apply knowledge useful for the professional training of the pharmacist as a National Health Service operator in the management and prevention of diseases and promotion of health.

PHARMACEUTICAL- AND FOOD-RELATED, TECHNOLOGICAL, REGULATORY, BIOLOGICAL, AND PHARMACOLOGICAL DISCIPLINES ANALYSIS OF MEDICAMENTS
- Ability to recognize, through a systematic approach, pharmaceutical substances listed in the Official European Pharmacopoeia.
- To have acquired mastery of the theoretical principles and experimental methodologies necessary for a correct quantitative analysis of pharmaceutical substances.

PHARMACEUTICAL AND TOXICOLOGICAL CHEMISTRY; PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY 1 AND 2
- Ability to describe synthetic processes for obtaining the main heterocyclic systems, basic components of many pharmacologically active compounds.
- Ability to describe the chemical, biological, and therapeutic-applicative aspects of antimicrobial, antiviral, and antitumor chemotherapeutic drugs.
- Ability to identify therapeutic applications, synthesis, structure-activity relationships, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of the main classes of drugs for the Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems, and for cardiovascular, pulmonary, and gastro-enteric pathologies.
- Ability to recognize the chemical mechanisms underlying possible toxicity at molecular, cellular, tissue, and systemic levels of major xenobiotic classes, including chemical and biological weapons.

FOOD AND DIETARY PRODUCTS
- Ability to identify the main chemical components of foods, agents responsible for food deterioration, and the nutritional value of foods in relation to preservation methods. To have acquired mastery of diets in different pathologies.

PHARMACEUTICAL TECHNOLOGY AND GALENIC PREPARATIONS; INNOVATIVE PHARMACEUTICAL FORMS; PHARMACEUTICAL LEGISLATION AND ETHICS
- Ability to apply the production technologies of conventional liquid, semisolid, and solid pharmaceutical forms and control of raw materials and medicinal products.
- Ability to recognize various pharmaceutical forms and medical devices dispensed in pharmacy.
- Ability to apply legislative norms regarding the production, trade, stability, and safety of medicinal products, medical devices, and health products, as well as manage the pharmacoeconomic aspects of the pharmacist's professional activities in public and private sectors and professional ethics.

TECHNOLOGY AND LEGISLATION OF COSMETIC PRODUCTS AND MEDICAL DEVICES
- Ability to apply regulations regarding cosmetics, and recognize the main raw materials of interest in cosmetics and their role in cosmetic formulations.
- Carry out information and orientation actions on hygiene and cosmetics.
- Ability to know the types of medical devices and apply the relevant regulations.

CELLULAR AND METABOLIC BIOCHEMISTRY; APPLIED MEDICAL BIOCHEMISTRY
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge on biological processes at the molecular level, with particular attention to the structural organization and functions of biological macromolecules and the ways living organisms use energy contained in nutrients.
- Ability to apply biochemical knowledge and methodologies in biomedical fields.

GENERAL AND MOLECULAR PHARMACOLOGY; PHARMACOLOGY AND PHARMACOTHERAPY; TOXICOLOGY AND PHARMACOVIGILANCE
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge on molecular mechanisms underlying the action of endogenous molecules.
- Ability to recognize therapeutic effects following drug-organism interactions.
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge on the interaction of toxins with the organism at molecular, cellular, and systemic levels, with particular attention to substances of abuse and the human pathology related to their self-administration.

MORPHOLOGY AND DIAGNOSTICS OF DRUGS; PHYTOCHEMISTRY AND HERBAL PREPARATIONS
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge on plant drugs, with particular regard to composition and preparation of main herbal preparations, identification methods, quality control, drug-toxicological effects, common extraction methods, and current regulations for production, marketing, and monitoring of adverse reactions.

COMPLEMENTARY AND INTEGRATIVE ACTIVITIES ELEMENTS OF MEDICAL STATISTICS
- To be familiar with the principles of descriptive medical statistics;
- Ability to evaluate scientific data concerning drugs, understand statistical-epidemiological health data, and actively participate in institutional public health campaigns.

PHARMACY MANAGEMENT
- To understand the dynamics of operational management in pharmacy.

CLINICAL ANALYSIS AND INSTRUMENTAL DIAGNOSTICS; MANAGEMENT OF MINOR DISEASES
- Ability to communicate with other healthcare professions;
- Ability to perform first-level analytical procedures and first aid interventions;
- Ability to use instrumental devices for second-level services provided in pharmacy;
- To understand the results of analyses performed.

OTHER FORMATIVE ACTIVITIES
- Ability to apply linguistic and grammatical knowledge and experience to understand the reading of written texts in English on general and scientific topics.

Official languages of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN Competencies associated with the function.
Pharmacist The Pharmacy degree, belonging to class LM-13, is a qualifying degree and therefore confers to the graduate the competencies and training necessary to practice the pharmacist profession in both public and private structures. The Pharmacy graduate, based on the knowledge, skills, and competencies acquired during the study course, can primarily operate in the preparation and dispensing of medicines, even in personalized form, thanks to knowledge of pharmaceutical technology, pharmacology, and drug regulations, as well as quality control of medicines prepared based on chemical-pharmaceutical and analytical competencies. The pharmacist contributes to patient care to promote adherence to therapy and advise on the correct use of medicines, including biological ones, based on pharmacological, toxicological, and biomedical competencies implemented under DM 1147 of 10/10/2022. New disciplines complete the medical and diagnostic knowledge useful for the application of Service Pharmacy, while economic disciplines prepare for business management in pharmacy. The teachings of pharmacognosy, nutraceuticals, and cosmetics enrich the pharmacist's preparation as a health professional. The multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary knowledge and skills acquired during the study course also allow the Pharmacy graduate to take on the role of a qualified person in the various actors of the drug supply chain (industry, distributors, and wholesalers) as well as a technical-scientific information provider.

Function in the workplace context.
Pharmacist Within the context of healthcare service distribution in the territory and achieving the objectives defined by the National Health Service (SSN), the pharmacist is a professional capable of connecting the patient, physician, and public and private healthcare structures. Thanks to their multidisciplinary competencies, they are able to operate for the purposes of public health, including through monitoring of medicines and other health products, personalized patient follow-up, including chronic patients, for adherence to pharmacological therapies, and counseling for healthy individuals for disease prevention.

Description of specific educational objectives.
Pharmacy graduates have a theoretical and practical preparation to exercise the profession of Pharmacist as a drug expert in the preparation, control, dispensing, and monitoring of medicines, medical devices, and other health products such as cosmetics, food supplements, herbal preparations, and foods for special diets. The Pharmacy Study Course will provide the Pharmacist with multidisciplinary competencies that will enable them to provide services for the prevention and protection of health on the territory, responding to the continuous and changing demands of society in the health field. In this way, the Pharmacist contributes to achieving the objectives set by the National Health Service. The Study Course, considering also European regulations, provides a complete understanding of the medicine from its composition (active ingredients and excipients), preparation, packaging, and quality control, as well as pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the active ingredient useful for understanding and advising on the correct use and reporting of adverse reactions. The Pharmacist's training is completed by the theoretical-practical study of current regulations in health matters and the exercise of pharmaceutical activities and pharmacy business management.

The health professional has a training path that refines their basic mathematical, physical, chemical, and biological knowledge aimed at understanding and learning medical, biochemical, pharmacological, pharmaceutical, and technological disciplines specifically characterizing the Pharmacist profession. The training path is enriched by teachings aimed at integrating linguistic and computer knowledge, training the Pharmacist for the provision of new services provided by Service Pharmacy, and differentiating the cultural and professional profile of the Pharmacy graduate from that of the CTF graduate.

By ensuring the essential disciplinary content defined by DM 1147 of 10/10/2022, the Bachelor's Degree provides knowledge and competencies in:
• Basic mathematics, physics, informatics, English, and statistics;
• Fundamental principles of general, inorganic, organic, and analytical chemistry;
• Animal cell biology and plant structures;
• Human anatomy and physiology;
• Pathology, microbiology, and public and environmental hygiene;
• General, applied, and clinical biochemistry;
• Pharmaceutical chemistry and analysis of medicines;
• Preparation and formulation of various pharmaceutical forms and medical devices;
• Methodological and regulatory principles related to quality control of medicines and other health and well-being products;
• Legislative and ethical norms necessary for the exercise of professional activity;
• Pharmacology, pharmacotherapy, and toxicology;
• Pharmacognosy of medicinal plants and their pharmacologically active principles;
• Advanced knowledge of pharmaceutical technology, also related to the preparation of personalized therapies in pharmacy;
• Composition and nutritional properties of foods, dietary products, supplements, and foods for special diets;
• Diagnostic products and other products for maintaining health and well-being, including herbal preparations, cosmetics, medical devices, and in vitro diagnostic medical-surgical devices and biocides;
• Principles of pharmacoeconomics and health economics, health communication, and business management;
• Multidisciplinary activities useful for implementing health education programs, performing first-level analytical procedures and first aid interventions, and using instrumental devices for second-level services provided in pharmacy.

High School Diploma Fees and contributions Regulations for Careers - Fees Roles Responsible for approving study plans GABRIELE MURINEDDU Chair ELISABETTA GAVINI Program, textbooks and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Pharmacist The main professional opportunities for graduates in Pharmacy are:
- Pharmacist
- Hospital Pharmacist
- Pharmacist in the ASL (Territorial Pharmaceutical Services)
- Drug Scientific Information Specialist The training path may also consider other professional activities carried out in the European Union by holders of the aforementioned degree to enable equal professional opportunities in the European (community) context.
Characteristics of the final exam.
The final exam consists of the discussion of a written work related to:
1) collection and critical processing of bibliographic material or other data relevant to the cultural and professional content of the study program (compilative thesis);
2) experimental activity on an original mono or multidisciplinary topic, carried out in a research laboratory where a Department or Study Program lecturer works, or in other public or private structures, under the supervision, as supervisor, of a Department or Study Program lecturer (experimental thesis).
Guidelines for thesis preparation contain information regarding scoring, supervisor, internship, etc.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the single-cycle Master's degree in Pharmacy, one must hold a secondary school diploma, as provided for in Article 6, paragraph 3, of Ministerial Decree 22 October 2004, No. 270.
An admission test with multiple-choice questions is mandatory, verifying basic knowledge from the secondary school curriculum, related to physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology, logic, and general culture. Additionally, a training debt may be assigned in relation to answers concerning mathematics and physics topics. This debt may be recovered by passing the mathematics course exam.
Specific educational objectives.
The single-cycle Master's degree in Pharmacy has a duration of five years for a total of 300 credits and provides the necessary theoretical and practical preparation for the exercise of the profession of Pharmacist, once the relevant professional qualification is obtained. A mandatory 30 credits (equal to 900 hours) are reserved for the professional internship, to be carried out in a public pharmacy, in a hospital under the supervision of the pharmaceutical service, or in municipal pharmacies, for a minimum of six months.
In addition to the essential preparation for practicing the profession of pharmacist, Pharmacy graduates possess advanced scientific preparation in the health field, aimed at forming an expert in drugs and their therapeutic use, capable of constituting a fundamental connection between patient, doctor, and public health structures, collaborating in drug monitoring on the territory, implementing therapy in both territorial and hospital settings, and providing patients and doctors with essential information for the correct use of drugs. It identifies as a "drug professional," i.e., a consultant willing to listen and dialogue with the patient, providing information, instructions, warnings, advice, and checks before and after drug use, and more generally on various topics related to strengthening health status. The professional profile of the pharmacist also includes that of a healthcare operator who, within the scope of their scientific and technological competencies, contributes to achieving the objectives of the national healthcare service, participating in health education initiatives, pharmacovigilance, and prevention campaigns.
The Pharmacy study program complies with the CEE Directive 85/432 and authorizes the exercise of professional activities such as quality control of medicinal products, storage, preservation, and distribution of the same in wholesale trade and in public and hospital pharmacies.
The specific educational objectives of the study program will be achieved through:
a) basic activities useful for developing scientific preparation necessary for understanding and deepening the characteristic disciplines;
b) characteristic activities necessary to acquire mastery of the chemical-physical characteristics of active principles, pharmaceutical forms, pharmacology and pharmacotherapy, toxicology, and pharmacovigilance;
c) training activities aimed at knowing the legislative and ethical norms useful for exercising professional activity;
d) related and integrated chemical, biological, and medical activities to adequately complete professional preparation.
Graduates in the Pharmacy study program must have acquired: fundamental multidisciplinary knowledge for the use of drugs, their structure, and activity in relation to their interaction with biomolecules at the cellular and systemic level; chemical and biological knowledge, integrated with pharmacoeconomics and knowledge regarding national and community laws regulating various activities in the sector; safety, quality, and efficacy requirements as specified by WHO regulations and national and European directives for medicinal products and health products; knowledge useful for performing the pharmaceutical service within the national healthcare system; the ability to interact with other healthcare professions; knowledge of the methodology of scientific research applied particularly to sector themes.
The graduate must also possess the knowledge and learning abilities necessary to undertake specialization schools, particularly in Hospital Pharmacy, as well as Research Doctorates. The Pharmacy graduate must also be able to use at least the English language, both in writing and speaking, with a level enabling autonomous operation in international communication, and possess adequate knowledge to use the main computer tools. The Study Program has activated a monitoring system for student careers that, through annual analysis of passed exams, allows the Course Council to identify and correct potential issues to prevent dropouts and facilitate obtaining the degree within the scheduled time.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in PHARMACY Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Generic Area The acquired knowledge constitutes a basic element for personal growth, for undertaking further studies, particularly in research doctorates, specialization schools, teaching, and professional work contexts. The study program will develop through semester-long courses. Knowledge will be acquired through frontal lectures and exercises. Verification of achieving expected outcomes will occur through oral exams and in-course assessments. This methodology allows for periodic verification of learning status and, if necessary, activation of recovery courses for students lagging in preparation.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Generic Area Graduates in the Pharmacy study program must demonstrate the ability to apply, in professional practice, knowledge of a) pharmaceutical chemistry for performing and describing quantitative (drug dosage) and qualitative analyses of drugs (drug recognition and purity tests); b) practical techniques for preparing galenic formulations and performing technological controls of pharmaceutical forms according to the Italian Official Pharmacopoeia and the European Pharmacopoeia; c) pharmaceutical legislation.
In particular, graduates must be able to apply knowledge useful for performing the pharmaceutical service within the national healthcare system, as well as knowledge necessary to interact with other healthcare professions. Didactic tools used to achieve these objectives include both classroom lectures and laboratory activities under the guidance of the lecturer. Verification methods include exams with oral discussion and/or written work and laboratory tests.
III - Judgment autonomy Judgment autonomy must be exercised whenever the Pharmacy graduate or pharmacist faces the need to make decisions requiring the knowledge outlined in the previous points.
Verification methods and didactic tools for achieving expected outcomes include in-course oral or written assessments, division of exams into multiple parts, monthly exam sessions, and, at the student's request, examinations on the completed program. The tutor, in agreement with the subject lecturer, follows students in exam preparation through written exercises, explanations, and oral examinations. Many courses include official or theoretical exercises that generally prepare students in various disciplines leading (in a propaedeutic manner) to multidisciplinary knowledge of drugs.
In general, all lecturers act as tutors for students in the Pharmacy study program.
IV - Communication skills This aspect is particularly important due to the extreme heterogeneity of the interlocutor in social and cultural terms and the increasingly diverse origin of pharmacy customers from EU and non-EU countries. The Master's graduate must be able to provide health-related consultation according to the classical principles of health education, listening to and advising patients on therapy, pharmacology, and, more generally, on health and well-being topics, thus playing a connecting role between patient, doctor, and health structures, as well as possessing relational and organizational skills in pharmacy management. These objectives will be achieved through professional seminars and the professional internship in a public pharmacy or hospital pharmacy. Verification methods include oral interviews, while the internship activity will be evaluated by a professional order committee.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN V - Learning ability In the healthcare field, continuous updating is fundamental due to the constant introduction of new or revised drugs and health products based on new international scientific findings. This updating can be partially acquired through public initiatives, especially university ones, and partially through individual initiatives, thanks to the information possibilities offered by media and the internet. Achieving these objectives also involves autonomous activities in the training path or the completion of the thesis, whether compilative or experimental.
Students are often involved in seminars, courses, and conferences. Each year, visiting professors, highly qualified scientists from abroad, are invited to collaborate with our university's teaching and research structures. They not only conduct traditional teaching but often deliver more technical lectures, experimental lectures on many new findings and issues in the chemical-pharmaceutical, pharmacotherapeutic, and technical-pharmaceutical fields. The thesis internship period, especially for the experimental thesis (minimum one calendar year), is an important training moment that focuses the theoretical-practical skills acquired by the student during the study period towards a research activity on often internationally significant themes. It is important to note that there is a growing student demand to carry out part of the experimental thesis research abroad, at academic sites, research institutes, and industries, using international student mobility programs.
The introduction of 4-CFU elective courses, complementary to the Pharmacy study program, allows for improving students' preparation for the profession of pharmacist or, more generally, for the role of drug technician.
Expected outcomes are verified through the successful completion of written and/or oral exams, practical or theoretical exercises during and at the end of each course.
Competencies associated with the role.
Pharmacist Upon obtaining the Master's degree in Pharmacy and the relevant professional qualification, graduates exercise the profession of Pharmacist in accordance with CEE Directive 85/432 and are authorized at least to carry out the following professional activities:
- Preparation of pharmaceutical forms of medicinal products;
- Manufacturing and control of medicinal products;
- Control of medicinal products in the laboratory;
- Storage, preservation, and distribution of medicinal products in the wholesale phase;
- Preparation, control, storage, and distribution of medicinal products in public pharmacies;
- Preparation, control, storage, and distribution of medicinal products in hospitals (hospital pharmacies);
- Dissemination of information and advice in the medicinal products sector.
- Control, storage, and distribution of self-medication drugs in parapharmacies.
Role in work context.
Pharmacist A professional figure capable of constituting a fundamental connection between patient, doctor, and public health structures, collaborating in drug monitoring on the territory, implementing therapy in both territorial and hospital settings, and providing patients and doctors with essential information for the correct use of drugs.

High School Diploma Roles President PAOLO GIUNCHEDI, PAOLA MOLICOTTI Program, texts, and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Master's Degree in Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Technology (CTF)
Master's graduates in CTF possess theoretical and practical preparation to become pharmaceutical professionals and professionals in health products (cosmetic products, diagnostic products, herbal products, medical-surgical devices, foods for special medical purposes and special diets, etc.). Their preparation is primarily directed towards the industrial sector. Additionally, since class LM-13 is enabling, and includes a highly qualified professional internship path (TPV), they can also practice the profession of pharmacist.
Specifically, and as examples, the CTF degree prepares for multiple professional activities, for example in the fields of:
• preparation of pharmaceutical forms of medicinal products;
• production and quality control of medicinal products, medical devices, and medical-surgical devices;
• analysis and control of medicinal products;
• preformulation studies;
• bio pharmaceutical studies of the pharmaceutical form of medicinal products;
• dissemination of information and advice on medicinal products, including their correct use;
• formulation, production, packaging, quality control, stability, and toxicological evaluation of cosmetic products;
• production of phytopharmaceuticals, antiparasitics, and health devices;
• analysis and control of the physico-chemical and hygienic characteristics of mineral waters;
• analysis and quality control of products destined for food, including those for special diets and dietary products;
• transformation, mixing, concentration, and fractionation of plant parts and their derivatives, for therapeutic or herbal use.
Final Exam Characteristics.
The Master's degree CTF requires an obligatory experimental thesis accounting for 26 ECTS, distributed as follows: research and preparatory studies 15 ECTS, writing of the thesis 9 ECTS; final dissertation 2 ECTS.
The final exam consists of the discussion of a written report related to an original mono or multidisciplinary experimental activity carried out in a research laboratory where a Course instructor or Department faculty member operates, or in other Departments of the University of Sassari or other national or international universities, or other public or private structures with which appropriate agreements have been established.
The Master's degree CTF belongs to class LM-13, which has become enabling (Law 8 November 2022, n.163, Interministerial Decree n.651 of 5 July 2022).
As a Master's degree in class LM-13, the final exam for the CTF degree includes the performance of a practical test evaluating professional skills acquired through the Practical-Evaluative Internship (TPV) within the study course, which precedes the thesis discussion and aims to verify the candidate's technical preparation for professional qualification.
Information regarding thesis preparation, score, supervisor, etc., is contained in the specific guidelines prepared by the Study Course.
Required Knowledge for Admission.
To be admitted to the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Technology, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
The required curricular requirements for students intending to enroll in the Study Course are: elements of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and General Culture, and a basic knowledge of a foreign language (English) at least at B1 level. Following the initial preparation verification, a training debt may be assigned to be recovered during the first year. This debt may be recovered by passing the final exam of the official course.
The Study Course Council may, before the start of each Academic Year, decide on the procedures for verifying the minimum requirements for enrollment.
Expected Employment and Professional Opportunities for Graduates.
Master's Degree in Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Technology (CTF)

Their preparation is primarily directed towards the industrial sector. Additionally, since class LM-13 is enabling, and includes a highly qualified professional internship path (TPV), they can also practice the profession of pharmacist.
Specifically, and as examples, the CTF degree prepares for multiple professional activities, for example in the fields of:
• preparation of pharmaceutical forms of medicinal products;
• production and quality control of medicinal products, medical devices, and medical-surgical devices;
• analysis and control of medicinal products;
• preformulation studies;
• bio pharmaceutical studies of the pharmaceutical form of medicinal products;
• dissemination of information and advice on medicinal products, including their correct use;
• formulation, production, packaging, quality control, stability, and toxicological evaluation of cosmetic products;
• production of phytopharmaceuticals, antiparasitics, and health devices;

• analysis and quality control of products destined for food, including those for special diets and dietary products;

Communication Skills.
Master's degree graduates in CTF must be able to clearly and unambiguously communicate their thoughts and knowledge to all users of their professional activity, including specialist and non-specialist interlocutors in the field as well as members of research groups.
This outcome also requires a good knowledge of spoken and written English.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The student's CTF autonomy of judgment is developed progressively throughout the studies, both through theoretical and practical teachings (classroom exercises and laboratory activities). At the end of their path, graduates must possess the ability to autonomously manage issues related to their professional fields, such as the design and synthesis of drugs, the technological development of pharmaceutical or cosmetic formulations, preformulation studies, drug analysis, and bio-pharmaceutical studies.
The autonomy of judgment is verified throughout the training process in every exam of every course and reaches its completion through the independent preparation, during the internship, of the experimental thesis, which therefore assumes fundamental importance in the CTF training process. The experimental thesis indeed constitutes a strongly characterizing and qualifying element of the CTF training path.

Learning Ability.
The master's graduate in CTF must have developed learning abilities useful for acquiring and consolidating their own cultural foundations and professional competencies, also through the continuous updating of their knowledge, to undertake advanced studies with a high degree of autonomy aimed at further professional development, for example, through research doctorates and the School of Specialization in Hospital Pharmacy. The training path achieved through the CTF study course provides the graduate with the ability to independently handle aspects related to the type of work to be addressed. Indeed, through interdisciplinary knowledge of pharmaceutical chemistry, biochemistry, pharmacology, and pharmaceutical technology, they will be able to learn the methodologies and principles most commonly used in both the industrial sector and academic research, as well as in the healthcare sector. The expected results are verified through written and/or oral exams, scheduled tests during the internship period for the completion of the mandatory experimental thesis.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Knowledge and Understanding and Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding: SYNTHESIS Graduates of the Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology Degree Course must have demonstrated:
a) knowledge and understanding of the aspects of mathematics with elements of statistics, physics, medical statistics, and chemistry useful for solving problems related to the qualitative-quantitative scientific approach,
b) knowledge and understanding of chemical and instrumental analytical techniques of pharmaceutical and toxicological analysis and their application,
c) knowledge and understanding of organic and biological chemistry, biology, microbiology, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and pharmaceutical chemistry that enable the study of the design of molecules with potential biological activity,
d) in-depth knowledge and understanding of drugs and their mechanisms of action, dietary products, and medical-surgical devices,
e) knowledge and understanding of pharmaceutical chemistry and technology useful for addressing research, both in universities and in public and private laboratories,
f) knowledge and understanding of the legislative aspects in which pharmacies and pharmaceutical industries operate,
g) knowledge and understanding of methodologies to apply to the recognition and dosage of drugs, purity tests, and the preparation of galenic medicines;
h) knowledge and understanding useful for the production, quality control, packaging, stability, and evaluation of products of interest in pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and health fields;
i) knowledge and understanding of the English language to use specialized scientific literature, to integrate into the international scientific community, and to elaborate the results of one's own research, production, and control activities of products of interest in pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and health fields. A minimum English level of B2 is required, in compliance with DM n.1154.

The knowledge and competencies acquired constitute a fundamental basis: for personal growth; for undertaking further studies, particularly within research doctorates, in the pharmaceutical industry, in teaching, and in the professional work context.
The teaching tools for developing knowledge are frontal lectures and practical laboratory exercises, conducted by the course instructors, supported by tutoring activities, and completed by standard oral and/or written assessments.

Basic Disciplines Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF) must have demonstrated:
- in the so-called hard subjects and basic chemical subjects (mathematics with elements of statistics, physics, general and inorganic chemistry, stoichiometry, analytical chemistry, and organic chemistry), knowledge and understanding of the aspects of mathematics, the foundations of statistics, physics, and chemistry useful for applying the qualitative and numerical/quantitative scientific approach to problem-solving;
- in the basic chemical-biological subjects (human anatomy with elements of animal biology, microbiology with elements of medical terminology and physiology), knowledge and understanding:
of animal biology, human anatomy, physiology, microbiology, and medical terminology, as a support for studying the design of molecules with biological activity.
The knowledge and critical understanding of the basic disciplines connected with the synthesis, development, use, and control of drugs constitute the first objective of the training plan.

Bio-pharmacological Disciplines Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF) must have demonstrated:
- in the bio-pharmacological subjects (Cellular and Molecular Biochemistry, Biochemical Methods, Basic Principles of Pharmacology - Toxicology, Pharmacotherapy, Pharmaceutical Biology), knowledge and understanding:
of the general aspects underlying vital processes through the study of the structure and activity of major biomolecules, useful for understanding the mechanism of action of drugs, pharmacokinetics, clinical uses, toxic effects, and doses of drugs used in major diseases.

Chemical, Pharmaceutical-Chemical, and Technological Disciplines Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF) must have demonstrated:
- in the pharmaceutical-chemical and pharmaceutical-technological subjects (Pharmaceutical Chemical Analysis Laboratory, General Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Systematic Pharmaceutical Chemistry 1, Drug Design and Synthesis Laboratory, Pharmaceutical Qualitative-Quantitative Analysis, Systematic Pharmaceutical Chemistry 2, Pharmaceutical Technology and Legislation, Pharmaceutical Technology Laboratory, Advanced Pharmaceutical Forms for Drug Release with Bio-pharmaceutical Elements, Industrial Production of Medicines and Fundamentals of Business Management), knowledge and understanding:
of the most important techniques in qualitative-quantitative analysis applicable to drug dosage and recognition, and purity tests;
of the general principles of pharmaceutical chemistry, structure-activity relationships, mechanism of action, chemical-toxicological aspects, synthesis, and metabolism of drugs in relation to their therapeutic use;
of pharmaceutical technology regarding the design, preparation, and control of solid, semi-solid, and liquid pharmaceutical forms, controlled-release pharmaceutical forms, nanocarriers (nanoparticles, solid lipid particles, liposomes) for nanomedicine, and some legislative aspects concerning professional practice in Pharmacy and the production and marketing of medicines by the pharmaceutical industry.
- in the chemical subjects (advanced organic chemistry, physical chemistry, physical methods in organic chemistry):
in this context, the CTF study course offers students the opportunity to complete their training by deepening specific aspects in the characteristic areas of the course offering.

OTHER TRAINING ACTIVITIES ENGLISH LANGUAGE
- Knowledge of grammar and text composition, as well as their comprehension (European Level B2).
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Knowledge and Understanding and Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding: SYNTHESIS Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology are capable of:
a) applying knowledge of organic chemistry, physical chemistry, and pharmaceutical chemistry to the synthesis of new molecules with potential biological activity;
b) applying knowledge of analytical chemistry and pharmaceutical chemistry to perform and describe quantitative (drug dosage) and qualitative (drug recognition and purity tests) analyses of drugs;
c) applying knowledge of pharmaceutical technology to the preparation of pharmaceutical forms, technological control of pharmaceutical forms according to current standards, preformulation studies, and bio-pharmaceutical studies;
d) applying and adhering to pharmaceutical legislation in the performance of the profession;
e) applying biochemical knowledge to analyze reaction mechanisms and molecular interactions in biological systems, even in response to molecules foreign to the organism such as drugs.
Students must also have acquired: linguistic competence and mastery of the specific language of the disciplines; ability to utilize the tools and methods of pharmaceutical chemical and technological analysis; ability to apply general and specific knowledge to issues related to drugs and health products.
The achievement of results will be verified based on behavior in laboratories and assessments of progress exams, both during the course and in final written and/or oral exams.

Basic Disciplines Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology are capable of:
(mathematics with elements of statistics and physics) correctly applying mathematical, physical, and statistical models and theorems to the qualitative-quantitative representation of real cases, even in interdisciplinary contexts of interest to the course;
(general and inorganic chemistry, stoichiometry, analytical chemistry, and organic chemistry) applying and developing various stages of a chemical procedure and related equilibria, especially regarding data evaluation and reliability; applying stoichiometry knowledge to solve problems related to weight relationships; using acquired knowledge in chemical equilibrium, chemical transformation kinetic laws, and molecular structure and interactions; recognizing and identifying the main functional groups characterizing organic compounds, predicting their chemical-physical properties and reactivity, developing the mechanisms through which the main classes of organic reactions occur, and using the symbolism to describe them;
(human anatomy with elements of animal biology, microbiology with elements of medical terminology and physiology), knowing the structural organization of human eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells and knowing their structure and function in plant and animal tissues; possessing adequate knowledge of the morphological organization of the human body; applying knowledge of cell structure; applying acquired physiology knowledge to analyze correlations between structure and function of molecules and cells in tissues and organs of living organisms; applying knowledge acquired in studying molecular processes of virulence of pathogenic bacteria and fungi and human parasites to contain and limit the development of infectious diseases; appropriately using medical terminology.
To achieve these objectives, teaching tools will include frontal lectures, laboratory activities, laboratory exercises, and individual laboratory activities under instructor guidance. Learning assessment will occur through periodic verifications of analysis reports and various exercise protocols during the course, and final assessment through an appropriate final exam.

Bio-pharmacological Disciplines Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology are capable of:
-(Cellular and Molecular Biochemistry, Biochemical Methods) analyzing biological processes at the molecular level, with particular attention to the structural organization and functions of biological macromolecules and the ways in which living organisms use energy contained in nutrients; analyzing interactions of biological systems with molecules foreign to the organism such as drugs;
-(Basic Principles of Pharmacology - Toxicology, Pharmacotherapy, Pharmaceutical Biology) applying acquired knowledge of drugs for the therapy of human diseases and evaluation of adverse events and interactions; applying acquired knowledge to recognize plant species and utilize commercial preparations of herbs and their derivatives present in the herbal and pharmaceutical market; evaluating the appropriateness of using a herb rather than a drug in relation to the expected biological effect, considering the content of bioactive constituents.
To achieve these objectives, teaching tools will include frontal lectures, laboratory activities, laboratory exercises, and individual laboratory activities under instructor guidance. Learning assessment will occur through periodic verifications of analysis reports and various exercise protocols during the course, and final assessment through an appropriate final exam.

Chemical, Pharmaceutical-Chemical, and Technological Disciplines Master's graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology are capable of:
-(Pharmaceutical Chemical Analysis Laboratory, Pharmaceutical Qualitative-Quantitative Analysis) applying extraction, separation, and purification techniques, with particular reference to chromatographic methods and interpretation of a chromatogram; applying chemical and instrumental analysis methods to pharmaceutical qualitative-quantitative analysis; acquiring manual skills and experience useful for solving various qualitative-quantitative analytical problems as reported in the monographs of the European Pharmacopoeia, justifying the choice of the most appropriate technique to achieve a specific goal; acquiring, interpreting, and analyzing experimental data;
-(General Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Systematic Pharmaceutical Chemistry 1, Drug Design and Synthesis Laboratory, Systematic Pharmaceutical Chemistry 2) studying and understanding the principles of structure-activity relationships for application to chemical synthesis; knowing the rules for defining nomenclature, knowing the mechanism of action and therapeutic use of different drug classes; analyzing the chemical-physical and stereo-electronic properties of drugs in relation to their therapeutic use, acquiring the essential elements for rational drug design; applying extraction techniques to drug synthesis;
-(food chemistry and quality control) applying protocols for determining the composition and chemical-physical properties of food, evaluating data related to food quality, interpreting and applying methods for food safety control, determining sensory and health value components, and selecting sensory and instrumental analytical techniques for evaluation;
-(Pharmaceutical Technology and Legislation, Pharmaceutical Technology Laboratory, Advanced Pharmaceutical Forms for Drug Release with Bio-pharmaceutical Elements, Industrial Production of Medicines and Fundamentals of Business Management) applying theoretical and practical principles of pharmaceutical technology to the design, preparation, and control of solid, semi-solid, and liquid pharmaceutical forms, controlled-release pharmaceutical forms; applying legislative aspects concerning professional practice in Pharmacy and the production and marketing of medicines by the pharmaceutical industry; consulting the national pricing of medicines; using experimental or theoretical procedures for improving and resolving problems related to drug formulations, both in academic and industrial research, deepening knowledge in bio-pharmaceutical and innovative controlled-release form fields.
-(advanced organic chemistry, physical methods in organic chemistry, physical chemistry): acquiring in-depth knowledge of reactions and formation of enols and enolates; pericyclic reactions such as cycloadditions, sigmatropic, and electrocyclic; use of major protecting groups; applying principles of organic chemistry to sugar chemistry and heterocyclic compounds; applying the most important spectroscopic and spectrometric instrumental techniques to identify and characterize functional groups and structures of simple organic and biological molecules of potential pharmaceutical interest; solving problems related to the properties of gases, liquids, solids, and solutions, and the basic elements of kinetics, equilibrium, and thermodynamics.
To achieve these objectives, teaching tools will include frontal lectures, laboratory activities, laboratory exercises, and individual laboratory activities under instructor guidance. Learning assessment will occur through periodic verifications of analysis reports and various exercise protocols during the course, and final assessment through an appropriate final exam.

OTHER TRAINING ACTIVITIES
- Ability to apply linguistic and grammatical knowledge and experience to understand reading of written texts in English, particularly in professional and scientific contexts.
