Competencies Associated with the Role.
Master's Graduate in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF)
The CTF graduate has a multi-disciplinary preparation (see Ministerial Decree No. 1147 of October 10, 2022) primarily directed toward the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food industries; additionally, as a degree belonging to class LM-13, the CTF possesses the preparation to perform the pharmacist profession.
The CTF preparation enables the graduate to possess a solid multi-disciplinary cultural foundation and important competencies in all areas of drugs: synthetic, analytical, preformulation and formulation, bio-pharmaceutical, pharmacological, and regulatory. The CTF can use their knowledge of inorganic, organic, pharmaceutical chemistry, and pharmacology for research and development of new drugs; they can use their knowledge in pharmaceutical technological-applicative fields to prepare galenic medicines, develop industrial formulations, perform technological controls of pharmaceutical forms according to standards codified by pharmacopoeias and the EMA, design and develop preformulation and formulation studies, and participate in bio-pharmaceutical studies of a formulation. Additionally, the CTF graduate's competencies in health products are essential for the linking function and information transfer between the producing industry of medicines and doctors and healthcare professionals (drug scientific information).

Role in the Work Context.
Master's Graduate in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF)
The master's graduate in CTF is a professional figure prepared to carry out development and production activities in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food industries, as well as research. Additionally, belonging to class LM-13, the CTF degree qualifies for the pharmacist profession (Law of November 8, 2021, No. 163, Interministerial Decree No. 651 of July 5, 2022).
The theoretical and practical preparation of the master's graduate CTF makes them a fundamentally important professional figure, particularly in the fields of drug synthesis, formulation development, and quality and safety control of pharmaceutical products intended for human and animal consumption.

Description of Specific Training Objectives.
The five-year single-cycle Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF) degree course aims to prepare graduates capable of operating primarily in the pharmaceutical and health products industrial sector. The course therefore provides the most advanced scientific foundations and theoretical and practical preparation in every sector of a multidisciplinary process characterized by aspects ranging from drug and biologically active substance design and synthesis, to formulation (including preformulation and bio-pharmaceutical studies), production, registration, and control of medicines and their market placement according to codified standards.
Being the LM-13 class a professionalizing class, the CTF degree course also, thanks to the Practical Assessment Internship (TPV), provides preparation to perform the pharmacist profession in territorial and hospital settings and more generally in consulting, dissemination, and distribution of drugs (Law of November 8, 2021, No. 163, Interministerial Decree No. 651 of July 5, 2022).
To achieve all these objectives, the degree course intends to provide its graduates with a multi-disciplinary cultural foundation in the drug field (Ministerial Decree No. 1147 of October 10, 2022) through:
1- a solid preparation in basic mathematical sciences (including statistics and medical statistics), physical, computer (Office packages, statistics, data analysis), chemical, biological, and medical disciplines, capable of ensuring a scientific approach to problem-solving;
2- knowledge for the design and synthesis of new biologically active molecules for human or veterinary therapeutic use and for the identification of therapeutically active molecules of animal and plant origin;
3- knowledge for designing, preparing, developing, and controlling pharmaceutical or cosmetic formulations, including preformulation and bio-pharmaceutical studies;
4- the ability to develop and apply protocols for chemical and microbiological quality control of drugs and health products, particularly nutraceutical products;
5- knowledge of national and supranational legislative contexts useful for the market placement of raw materials, medicines, and health products;
6- knowledge and learning abilities necessary to address Doctoral Schools related to the reference professions and the School of Specialization in Hospital Pharmacy;
7- knowledge of the English language (at the end of the training path, the graduate must possess at least level B2). In compliance with Ministerial Decree No. 1147, special attention will be paid to the acquisition by the graduate of the use of English in their professional field. In addition to a 6-CFU course, an active approach in teaching will be adopted to familiarize students with technical-scientific terminology, organizing in the context of each course some lectures with English materials and/or English seminars.
The CTF training path begins with the acquisition of basic mathematical (with elements of statistics), physical, chemical (in inorganic, organic, analytical, chemical-physical aspects), and microbiological knowledge, preparatory for the subsequent understanding and learning of pharmaceutical-chemical, pharmacological, and pharmaceutical-technological disciplines. The CTF training path also includes courses aimed at integrating linguistic and computer knowledge, with particular attention to professionalizing aspects.

Program, Texts and Objectives
Professional status conferred by the degree. The graduate in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology, upon obtaining the degree, carries out research, development, and production activities of drugs, both synthetic and biotechnological, and with professional accreditation, practices the profession of pharmacist.
- Chemist (accreditation for Section A of the Professional Register of Chemists),
• chemical analyses using any method for any purpose,
• management of chemical laboratories whose activities also include chemical analyses,
• study and development of chemical processes,
• design and construction of chemical laboratories and industrial chemical plants,
• verification of the hazard or non-hazard of chemical substances
- Pharmacist (accreditation for the Pharmacist profession),
- Hospital Pharmacist (specialization in Hospital Pharmacy),
- Scientific Drug Information Specialist,
- Research Chemist (pharmaceutical, cosmetic, food industry),
- Pharmacologist,
- Researcher and graduate technician in biological sciences.
Final Exam Characteristics. The final exam consists of the discussion of a written report related to an original mono or multidisciplinary experimental activity carried out at a research laboratory where a faculty member of the Department or the Course of Study operates, or at other public or private structures with which appropriate agreements have been established (experimental thesis).
Information regarding thesis preparation, score, supervisor, etc., is contained in the specific guidelines prepared by the course of study.
Required Knowledge for Admission. To be admitted to the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
The requirements for students intending to enroll in the Course of Study are: elements of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and General Culture. Following the initial preparation check, a study debt may be assigned to be recovered during the first year. This debt can be recovered by passing the final exam of the official course. The Course Council may, before the start of each academic year, decide on the procedures for verifying the minimum requirements for enrollment.
Specific Educational Objectives. The five-year single-cycle degree course in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology aims primarily to prepare graduates capable of operating in the pharmaceutical industry and health products sector.
The course therefore provides the scientific foundations to ensure the most advanced theoretical and practical preparation in every sector of a multidisciplinary process characterized by aspects ranging from drug and biologically active substances design, to their synthesis, experimentation, production, registration, control, and market introduction according to the standards codified in the Italian and European Pharmacopoeias.
The Master's degree course in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology also provides the essential preparation to practice the profession of pharmacist in territorial and hospital settings and, more generally, to provide consultation, dissemination, and distribution of drugs.
The Master's degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology offers, in addition to the possibility of taking the accreditation exam for the pharmacist profession according to Directive 85/432/EEC, also the accreditation for the profession of chemist in Section A of the Register according to D.P.R. No. 328 of June 5, 2001.
To achieve these objectives, the degree course, based on proven multi-year experience, specifically aims to provide its graduates with:
1- a solid foundation in basic science disciplines (mathematical, physical, chemical, biological, medical) capable of ensuring a scientific approach to problem-solving;
2- an in-depth knowledge of chemical and biological characteristics necessary for designing new biologically active molecules and identifying those of animal and plant origin;
3- the ability to apply interdisciplinary scientific knowledge to the synthesis of new active principles for human therapeutic use, veterinary use, or for plants.
4- the ability to develop and apply protocols for chemical and microbiological quality control of drugs and health products, particularly nutraceutical products;
5- the ability to apply scientific and technological knowledge to the preparation and control of pharmaceutical formulations;
6- knowledge of national and supranational legislative contexts useful for the market introduction of raw materials, medicines, and health products;
7- the knowledge and learning abilities necessary to address doctoral schools related to the reference professions;
8- knowledge of the English language.
Degree Awarded. Master's Degree in PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY AND TECHNOLOGY
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Generic Area
Graduates of the Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology Degree Course must have demonstrated knowledge and understanding: of aspects of mathematics, physics, computer science, and chemistry; of biology, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, and pharmaceutical chemistry useful for gaining in-depth knowledge of drugs and their mechanisms of action; of dietary products and medical-surgical devices; and of pharmaceutical technology.
The acquired knowledge and skills constitute a fundamental basis: for personal growth; for pursuing further studies, particularly within research doctorates, in the pharmaceutical industry, teaching, and professional work contexts.
The course structure will be developed into annual and semester courses with the possibility of interim assessments for each discipline, accompanied by a final profit exam. This methodology allows for periodic checks on the learning status of the taught concepts and, if necessary, to schedule recovery courses for students lagging in preparation.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Generic Area
Graduates of the Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology Degree Course must have demonstrated the ability to apply knowledge: of analytical chemistry and pharmaceutical chemistry to perform and describe quantitative (drug dosage) and qualitative analyses of drugs (drug recognition and purity tests); of technical-practical nature for preparing galenic formulations and conducting technological controls of pharmaceutical forms according to the Italian Official Pharmacopoeia and the European Pharmacopoeia; of pharmaceutical legislation in the practice of the profession.
In conclusion, graduates of this course must be capable of applying their knowledge and understanding in multidisciplinary work and professional contexts related to pharmaceutical sciences.
The achievement of results will be verified based on behavior in laboratories and profit exam assessments, both interim and final written and/or oral exams.
III - Judgment Autonomy
Graduates of this course must possess the ability to retrieve and use data to formulate answers to practical or theoretical problems, even based on limited or incomplete information, primarily in the field of drug design, synthesis, analysis, and experimentation of pharmaceutical technologies.
These abilities are verified through preparation assessment using tools such as interim tests during the course of teaching, and/or passing written and/or oral exams at the end of courses.
It is important to verify with appropriate tests mastery of the scientific research method through evaluation of practical course exercises and thesis internship, respectively by the instructors and the thesis supervisor and co-supervisors.
The acquisition of judgment autonomy will primarily derive from the graduate's choice to apply themselves to sectors that complete their preparation in chemical, technological, and food biological fields.
IV - Communication Skills
Graduates in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology must be able to communicate their thoughts and knowledge clearly and unambiguously to colleagues, superiors, and all users of their activities.
Additionally, they must be able to provide healthcare consultation, acting as a connection between patient, doctor, and healthcare facilities; they must have relational and organizational skills in pharmacy management; and must be able to communicate, in both written and oral form, in English as well as Italian.
This result is significantly achieved through practical professional internship in pharmacy and pharmaceutical services.
The achievement of these objectives is verified through methods such as written and/or oral exams, group exercises, and seminar activities.
Regarding the curriculum internship, verification tools include interim meetings with both the professional tutor and the academic tutor, and a final judgment written by both figures.
Official Teaching and Preparation Assessment Languages. ITALIAN
V - Learning Ability
Graduates of this course must have developed learning abilities useful for: continuous updating of their knowledge; independently pursuing advanced studies oriented towards further professional development within research doctorates and conducting activities of design, synthesis, analysis, and experimentation of new drugs in the pharmaceutical industry.
The training path achieved with the CTF course provides the graduate with the ability to independently handle aspects related to the type of work to be addressed.
Indeed, through knowledge of pharmaceutical chemistry, biochemistry, and pharmacology, along with applied pharmaceutical chemistry, they will be able to learn the methodologies and principles most commonly used in both academic research, industrial sectors, and healthcare.
Expected results are verified through written and/or oral exams, scheduled tests during the internship period for the experimental thesis (mandatory), and periodic meetings regarding the achievement of results at different stages of the research work related to the thesis.
Competencies Associated with the Function.
The graduate in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology, upon obtaining the degree, carries out research, development, and production activities of drugs, both synthetic and biotechnological, and with professional accreditation, practices the profession of pharmacist.
According to Directive 85/432/EEC, the graduate in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology is authorized at least to carry out the following professional activities:
- synthesis of active principles for the manufacturing and control of medicines in the pharmaceutical industry;
- quality control of medicines in public or private laboratories;
- production and control of health devices, medical devices, and medical-surgical devices;
- production and quality control of dietary and food products;
- production, analysis, and quality control of cosmetic products;
- analysis and control of physical-chemical and hygienic characteristics of mineral waters;
- storage, preservation, and distribution of medicines during wholesale trade;
- preparation, control, storage, and distribution of medicines in public pharmacies or hospital pharmacies;
- dissemination of information and advice in the health products sector.
The above activities are only some of those coordinated by the directive; the training path may also consider other professional activities carried out by the European Union in the field of drugs, to allow equal employment opportunities in the European context.
Function in Work Context.
The graduate in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology, upon obtaining the degree, carries out research, development, and production activities of drugs, both synthetic and biotechnological, and with professional accreditation, practices the profession of pharmacist.
Among the main functions of the CTF graduate's professional figure is the characteristic role of coordination in chemical-technological-pharmaceutical research within public and private structures.
Additionally, with the acquisition of accreditation for the Pharmacist profession, this figure is able to serve as a fundamental connection between patient, doctor, and public healthcare structures, collaborating in drug monitoring on the territory, implementing therapy in both territorial and hospital settings, and providing patients and doctors with essential instructions for the correct use of drugs.

Program, texts and objectives
Professional status conferred by the title.
Food technologist and researcher in the field of food production technologies and biotechnology.
Expected career and professional opportunities for graduates.
Food technologist and researcher in the field of food production technologies and biotechnology.
Expected career opportunities in food industries and all companies related to the production, transformation, storage, and distribution of food products, in large retail companies, in public and private entities conducting research and development in the agro-food sector. Study offices and self-employment (the training of the graduate in Food Science and Technology qualifies them to take the licensing exams for the profession of Food Technologist and Agronomist).
Production and production line manager Food industries and all companies related to the production, transformation, storage, and distribution of food products, as well as in large retail companies.
Production control manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products)
Food industries and all companies related to the production, transformation, storage, and distribution of food products, in large retail companies, in public and private entities conducting planning, analysis, control activities, as well as those conducting scientific investigations for the protection and enhancement of food production, in training entities.
Expert in managing food safety and quality systems and “Lead-auditor”
Expected career opportunities in food industries and all companies related to the production, transformation, storage, and distribution of food products, in large retail companies, in public and private entities conducting planning, analysis, control, certification activities, as well as those conducting scientific investigations for the protection and enhancement of food production, in training entities, study offices, and self-employment. It will also be possible to access training courses for second-party audits (second level, external audits) and subsequently for third-party audits (third level, certification body).
Final exam characteristics.
The final exam consists of drafting and subsequent discussion of a thesis/project, with an applied-experimental character. In particular, the Master's degree in Quality and Safety of Food Products is obtained by passing a final exam, consisting of the discussion of a written thesis, prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor, before a committee of professors. The thesis, of an experimental and/or applied nature, will be related to the activities carried out by the student during the internship or will relate to the in-depth study of other topics covered during the course of study. These activities, starting from a concise but comprehensive study and in-depth analysis of the current state of the art, may concern the following points, possibly integrated:
- Monitoring and critical evaluation of one or more processes or activities in the agro-food sector, including control systems and related management software;
- Technical-economic design of agro-food production activities or part of them and/or specific innovative process and/or product interventions;
- Evaluation of the physical-sensory and food aspects of traditional and/or innovative agro-food products, related or not to specific market analyses and studies aimed at implementing and/or developing new evaluation methodologies;
- Microbiological and biotechnological evaluations and innovations applied and/or to be applied along the agro-food production chain, including specific microbiological analyses and evaluations;
- Analysis, critical evaluation, and possible implementation or design interventions for systems ensuring and managing the safety and quality of agro-food products and their production processes.
The evaluation of the final exam will follow the criteria established by the Department of Agraria's teaching regulations, with any specific integrations of the Course's teaching regulations.
Required knowledge for admission.
The first-level and master's degrees admitted for enrollment in the present Master's Degree are those belonging to the classes: L-27 (Chemical Sciences and Technologies), L-26 (Food and Agricultural Sciences), L-25 (Agricultural and Forestry Sciences), L-2 (Biotechnology), L13 Biological Sciences, L29 Pharmaceutical Sciences and Technologies, L38 Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Production Technologies, LM-86 (Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Technologies), LM-71 (Industrial Chemistry Sciences and Technologies), LM-69 (Agricultural Sciences and Technologies), LM-8 (Industrial Biotechnology), LM-7 (Agricultural Biotechnology), LM9 Medical, Veterinary, and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, LM13 Pharmacy and Industrial Pharmacy, LM54 Chemical Sciences, LM61 Human Nutrition Sciences.
The initial knowledge of candidates will be verified by a special commission and will cover:
- Principles of Mathematics and Physics.
- General and Organic Chemistry.
- Fundamentals of Primary Production (vegetable and animal).
- Unit Operations of Food Technologies.
- Main agro-food industries and Food Microbiology.
- Fundamentals of Chemistry and Food Analysis;
- English.
At the start of the Master's degree course, the student must have already acquired at least 10 CFU in English (L-LIN/12) or have a language certification at B1 level or higher.
By June of each year, the admission procedures and verification methods for the required knowledge will be published.

CURRICULUM: Communication Skills
SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10797

Communication Skills.
The graduate is able to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with peers and those with lower educational and functional levels, also using a European Union language other than their own, typically English, within the specific disciplinary context. They are also capable of communicating effectively, both orally and in writing, with higher professional functions, presenting results obtained, innovative ideas, and the current state of ongoing projects. They are able to interact with people outside productive realities, collaborate, and adapt to different work environments and topics. The acquisition of communication skills, both written and oral, will be verified through the evaluation of laboratory activities, in-course assessments for individual disciplines, and the reports prepared for the end of the practical internship and the final examination, which will be presented orally to the graduation committee.
Specific communication skills will be stimulated and verified through the organization of specific multidisciplinary group works of a technical-scientific, economic, and ethical nature, as well as through support provided for the drafting and subsequent evaluation of the internship report and the final examination (thesis).
Learning Ability.
The main professional competence areas that students will acquire are primarily related to the following areas: food technology and biotechnology processes; mastery of the scientific method and capacity to transfer knowledge to practical implementation in enterprises; optimization and management of production processes in food industries; design and management of quality and safety systems using innovative methodologies; execution of complex coordination and direction activities related to the sector; design and management of machinery and equipment used in food production processes; evaluation of physical and sensory aspects of food; management of enterprises and agri-food supply chains; communication, multidisciplinary group work, and judgment capabilities both on technical-economic and human-ethical levels; fluent use of English (at least B2 level). The aforementioned knowledge, interacting synergistically and with the stimulation of teachers involved over time, provide advanced cognitive tools essential for the continuous updating of sector knowledge, also using new communication and information technologies, to finalize the training path towards solving the multiple practical problems of the entire agri-food production chain. Graduates will have developed learning abilities that allow them to continue studies in specific sector specializations, in second-level master's programs, in research doctorate courses, and/or to directly enter the workforce with a proactive approach. Learning ability will be assessed through analysis of the individual student's academic record regarding exam grades and the time elapsed between attending a course and passing the exam, as well as through evaluation of self-learning capabilities developed during the practical internship and final examination activities.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A103] FOOD PRODUCT QUALITY AND SAFETY
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Judgment autonomy
SECTION: Judgment autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10797

Judgment autonomy.
Upon completion of studies, the graduate will have the ability to compare and discuss experimental results and prepare appropriate checkpoint and final reports, presenting them in concise and/or detailed working documents, as well as orally presenting the aforementioned results. They will have the ability to locate and evaluate sources of general information and in-depth technical-scientific information, data, and scientific literature useful for improving the safety, quality, effectiveness, and efficiency of food production, including environmental sustainability, circular economy, and bio-based economy. The acquisition of judgment autonomy will be verified through the evaluation of outcomes achieved in core disciplines and optional subjects chosen by the student, as well as through the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work individually and in groups during practical activities carried out in each course and the practical internship, as well as in the preparation of the final exam assignment.
The teaching organization encourages students to adopt a proactive approach characterized by a high degree of autonomy (in choices, critical learning, and study organization).
Knowledge and understanding.
process controls Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of food technology production processes and process/product controls through the following expected learning outcomes: basic modeling tools and analysis of automation systems for automatic controls in food industries, including analysis of specifications, management of system projects, and in-depth study of main management software.
The training activities achieving these learning outcomes are attributable to the courses "Food Industry Control Systems" (training path A) or "Principles of Food Technologies: Unit Operations and Processes" (training path B) and "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies"; as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).
food merchandising and marketing of food products Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of basic food merchandising tools and more in-depth knowledge of food merchandising, knowledge of different sectors of the agro-food industries, and various marketing strategies for products, as well as the evaluation of product placement in national, European, and international markets. Particular attention will be given to marketing analysis: consumer behavior, market and competitor analysis, innovation, and launch of new products.
The training activities achieving these learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course "Food Merchandising and Marketing of Food Products" as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).
food sciences Students will acquire a general overview of main concepts, methods, and basic tools used for evaluating foods and their nutritional principles to be included in a diet, with particular reference to different physiological conditions.
The training activities achieving these learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course "Food Sciences" as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).
applied biotechnologies for food production Students will acquire the necessary knowledge for designing and managing bioprocesses as a fundamental aspect of food quality; innovations to promote a solid economic activity; tools for managing food safety and improving food quality from a microbiological perspective, with particular reference to controlling factors regulating microbial growth, metabolic activity, and selection in food ecosystems.
The training activities achieving these learning outcomes are attributable to the courses "Advanced Microbial Biotechnologies for Food Production" and "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies"; as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).
food evaluation Students will acquire theoretical, practical knowledge, and the most suitable tools to characterize a food product; knowledge of main physical analyses and different sensory methodologies will provide students with the necessary tools to evaluate foods both for company quality control and for product identity; by the end of the course, students will have acquired basic and advanced knowledge on the role of physical and sensory analyses in evaluating the quality characteristics of food products.
The training activities achieving these learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course "Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods" and partially to the practical course "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies" as well as during the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).
food safety and quality Students will achieve appropriate knowledge regarding the application of mandatory and voluntary standards for certification of safety and quality in food industries, including implementation of official food controls; process and product certification, analytical and documentary traceability, HACCP and related analytical methodologies applicable to quality and safety control of foods; the general framework of the European system for controlling food products. Students will also have the opportunity to be qualified, upon completion of a 40-hour module, as "lead auditor" for self-control systems (HACCP) and quality management.
The training activities achieving these learning outcomes are attributable to the courses "Food Safety and Quality 1," "Food Safety and Quality 2," "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies"; as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
process controls Students will acquire skills in using, throughout the entire agro-food production chain, the practical aspects of the knowledge learned, summarized in the following expected learning outcomes: familiarity with using production process control systems; mastery of principles for applying online, in-line, and off-line control systems; application of the aforementioned knowledge and skills as an integral part of a global evaluation of agro-food sector production processes.
food merchandising and marketing of food products Students will acquire skills in utilizing knowledge regarding regulations related to food product merchandising, control bodies, and food product labeling; marketing strategies, also through evaluation of consumer opinions; identification of target groups for traditional and innovative food products; application of the aforementioned knowledge and skills as an integral part of a global evaluation of agro-food sector production processes and related products.
food sciences Students will acquire the necessary abilities for evaluating food and nutritional aspects of foods, aimed at correct food labeling and a correct communication strategy towards consumers. They will also be able to identify strategies for product innovation targeting specific consumer groups (e.g., celiac, vegetarian, etc.) and/or specific dietary needs (e.g., high-fiber foods, probiotic foods, vitaminized foods, etc.). Students will also be able to use the aforementioned knowledge and skills as an integral part of a global evaluation of agro-food sector production processes and related products.
applied biotechnologies for food production Students will acquire a critical view of the potential of microbial biotechnologies and predictive microbiology in the food sector and will be able to interpret data, develop ideas, and design innovation both in the production of fermented foods and in the microbiological control of foods. They will also be able to design and propose the application of specific innovative biotechnological techniques in production processes and evaluate their relative practical effectiveness. Students will also be able to use the aforementioned knowledge and skills as an integral part of a global evaluation of agro-food sector production processes and related products.
food evaluation Students will acquire an advanced understanding of the potential offered by using appropriate techniques for sensory evaluation of foods. They will also be able to design and manage specific panel tests aimed at discriminant and descriptive evaluations, and critically and appropriately evaluate the results obtained, also using specific software for data management and evaluation. Students will also be able to use the aforementioned knowledge and skills as an integral part of a global evaluation of agro-food sector production processes and related products.
food safety and quality Students will acquire specific skills for designing and implementing the main systems for quality management (ISO 9000, BRC, IFS, etc.) and food safety (GMP, GHP, HACCP); designing, conducting audits, and evaluating results; using acquired knowledge for a global evaluation of agro-food sector production processes and related products, which, aimed at safety and quality logic, considers multiple aspects of production controls, nutritional and sensory evaluations, biotechnological innovations, marketing strategies, etc.
Official language(s) of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN Associated competencies.
Food technologist and researcher in the field of food technologies and biotechnologies.
Ability to design and intervene, both at operational and training levels, in the management of resources, materials, and professionals in food production and transformation processes, from raw materials to semi-finished products to finished products. Ability to develop product innovations, new food products, and innovations in existing production processes. Production and line manager Ability to manage, control, and operate plants and food processing and related product processes. Management, administration, and operation of companies operating in the production, transformation, preservation, distribution, and commercialization of food.
Production control manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products)
Ability to evaluate and control production processes and product analyses. In particular, for the verification and control of requirements and specifications of: food raw materials, finished products, additives, technological aids, semi-finished products, packaging, and anything related to the production and transformation of food products, as well as defining standards and specifications for the aforementioned products.
Expert in managing food safety and quality systems and "Lead-auditor"
Ability to evaluate the level achieved by safety and quality systems in pre-inspection verification and audit, as well as to directly interact during external audit and inspection visits with the specific team of expert evaluators assigned to carry out the aforementioned controls at the company.
Work context role.
Food technologist and researcher in the field of food technologies and biotechnologies.
Programming, management, control, coordination, and training regarding food and beverage production, preservation, transformation, distribution, and service. Management of resources, materials, and professionals, aimed at the constant improvement of food products in economic terms, food safety, and quality, with particular attention to sustainability, circular economy, and bio-based economy. Research and development of processes and products.
Production and line manager Management, control, and operation of plants, even complex ones, and food processing and related product processes. Direction and management of companies operating in the production, transformation, preservation, distribution, and commercialization of food.
Production control manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products)
Responsibility for verifying safety, quality, and quantity parameters of food raw materials, semi-finished products, finished products, additives, technological aids, packaging materials, and anything related to the production and transformation of food products, as well as defining standards and specifications for the aforementioned products.
Expert in managing food safety and quality systems and "Lead-auditor"
Design, management, and continuous improvement of systems for managing food production safety (GMP, GHP, HACCP) and quality management systems. Management of internal audits aimed at pre-certification evaluation within the production reality.
Specific training objectives description.
In the first year, within front-facing training activities, at least 30% will be practical activities; additionally, the course will include visits to food industries. The second year will be entirely dedicated to practical and highly professionalizing training activities carried out within the cooperating food industries. These activities will develop through a Practical Application Internship (specialized) and an additional research and experimentation activity for the preparation of the thesis. Second-year training activities will be programmed, managed, and carried out in close collaboration with food industries.
The training objectives of the Master's Degree program primarily focus on training an expert in food technologies, with particular reference to professional competencies related to food safety and quality.
The training objectives of the Master's Degree program primarily include eleven areas of professional competencies that students must acquire:
1. Possess a solid knowledge of processes and technologies and food biotechnologies (reference: entrance test and first-level degree);
2. Possess a solid basic cultural preparation and good mastery of the scientific method, with particular reference to the ability to transfer knowledge to practical implementation in companies (reference: Practical Application Internship and final thesis activities);
3. Possess a high ability to optimize food industry production processes and manage specific organizational and control aspects (reference: Food Industry Control Systems, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
4. Be an expert in managing and promoting food safety and quality, also in compliance with regulations on operator safety and environmental protection (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
5. Possess high technical and practical skills for quality and food safety control, also using innovative methodologies (reference: Food Safety and Quality, management of starters and predictive microbiology, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Food Sciences, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
6. Have adequate knowledge and professional abilities to carry out complex coordination and direction activities related to the agro-food sector (reference: Food Safety and Quality, management of starters and predictive microbiology, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Food Sciences, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
7. Possess knowledge and professional abilities in designing and managing machines and plants used in food processing and transformation processes (reference: entrance test and first-level degree, Food Industry Control Systems, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
8. Possess advanced knowledge on the sensory and food aspects evaluation of main foods, as well as main methodologies and application strategies, also to evaluate consumer opinions (reference: Food Sciences, Food Merchandising and Marketing of Food Products, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods);
9. Have advanced skills in managing companies, agro-food supply chains, and consulting and service companies connected to them (reference: Food Merchandising and Marketing of Food Products, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
10. Have developed personal abilities in communication, multidisciplinary group work, and judgment both on technical-economic and human-ethical levels (reference: specific workshops and group works, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
11. Be able to fluently use at least one European Union language in written and oral form, beyond Italian, with reference to disciplinary lexicons (reference: entrance test and first-level degree).

Program, Texts, and Objectives
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Generic Profile - Territorial Planner The competencies and skills described above enable Master's graduates to work as consultants and self-employed professionals, as well as experts in local authorities or institutions, companies, and agencies. Their employment opportunities lie in the field of territorial, urban, and environmental planning, particularly in the development of projects, plans, programs, and policies. Specific professional activities involve the definition and management of territorial governance tools, with particular reference to:
- design, planning, and policies for the transformation and requalification of the city, territory, and environment (projects, programs, plans, and policies at various territorial scales, sector planning and policies, regulations, and norms);
- coordination and management of evaluation activities for urban, territorial, and environmental projects, programs, plans, and policies;
- management of processes for the construction of governance actions and their communication forms.
Graduates may practice self-employment (after passing the State exam) for activities specified in section A "Planners" of the Register of Architects, Planners, and Landscape Architects, or for unregulated consulting services in the field of planning and, more generally, in research related to territorial and environmental transformations.
In particular, DPR 328/2001 "Amendment to the Regulation of Professions" states that "the professional activities of registered members in section A - "territorial planning" sector include:
a) territorial, landscape, environmental, and city planning;
b) conducting and coordinating complex and specialized analyses of urban, territorial, landscape, and environmental structures, coordinating and managing environmental evaluation and feasibility activities for urban and territorial plans and projects;
c) strategies, policies, and projects for urban and territorial transformation."
These functions and professional opportunities are further specified and expanded through international training offers with various partner countries.
Final exam characteristics.
The final exam for obtaining the Master's degree consists of a discussion, held before a committee appointed by the course, of an original thesis developed by the student under the guidance of a supervisor and consistent with the interdisciplinary training objectives of the Master's program. To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in training activities must be earned in Italy or at one of the partner university locations specified in the study plan.
For dual-degree international pathways, co-supervision by a faculty member from the partner university is possible.
Required knowledge for admission.
Admission to the Master's program, following verification of personal preparation, is granted to candidates who have obtained a Bachelor's degree in one of the following classes:
L 6 – Geography (formerly class 30, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L17 – Architecture Sciences (formerly class 4, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 21 – Territorial, Urban, Landscape, and Environmental Planning Sciences (formerly class 7, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 25 – Agricultural and Forestry Sciences and Technologies (formerly class 20, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 32 – Environmental and Natural Sciences and Technologies (formerly class 27, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 7 Civil and Environmental Engineering (formerly class 8, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 9 Industrial Engineering (formerly class 10, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 1 Cultural Heritage (formerly class 13, and previous denominations before 270/04)
L 15 Tourism Sciences (formerly class 15 and previous denominations before 270/04)
Personal preparation verification will be conducted according to the procedures outlined in the teaching regulation.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in Planning and Policies for the City, Environment, and Landscape

SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10150

Communication Skills.
Graduates are able to clearly communicate the conclusions and proposed intervention hypotheses, as well as the knowledge, structure and motivations that make them possible, to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Graduates develop cooperative and interdisciplinary work skills, particularly through:
- interactive methods used to organize the educational offer (laboratory and internship activities);
- opportunities to study with peers from different degree classes and contexts;
- opportunities to enrich and integrate methodological approaches and languages in different study settings, thanks to the possibilities offered by workshops, Erasmus Projects and consortium sites.
Moreover, they develop the ability to communicate analysis content, proposals, conclusions, evaluations and projects in Italian, English, and possibly another foreign language, in writing, graphically and orally, with the support of advanced communication techniques and tools, also in relation to technologies and with reference to different contexts and actors.
Laboratory experiences particularly contribute to the development of communication skills required by professional activities oriented towards building participatory planning processes, where negotiation, decision-making and construction of public agendas play a primary role. In particular, graduates develop the ability to:
- clearly and simply present complex analytical paths and detailed project proposals;
- work in groups, engaging with different disciplinary cultures and knowledge in a cooperative and solution-oriented manner;
- communicate publicly while paying attention to the language used in relation to the understanding capabilities of the audience;
- facilitate communication and dialogue in multi-actor contexts;
- bring to light shared values and principles emerging from the dialogue between knowledge and subjects;
- communicate using appropriate representation techniques.
Learning Abilities.
Graduates develop learning abilities that enable them to continue studying and updating themselves in an autonomous and self-directed manner, identifying opportunities for continuous training and experiences most suitable to their professional profile. Graduates particularly develop abilities to:
- transform participation in concrete experiences into learning opportunities, using case studies, comparative methods and inquiry;
- identify suitable opportunities for continuous training according to their profile, taking into account the evolution of disciplines, culture and intervention practices on the territory.
The teaching methods and tools through which the expected outcomes are achieved and verified are as follows:
- integrated teaching modules where teacher comparison forces students to continuous work of translation and comparison between personal and disciplinary viewpoints;
- project laboratories inspired by complexity and interdisciplinarity;
- constant didactic reference to adopting new theoretical perspectives and the need to provide reasoned justifications for actual and possible choices;
- interpersonal comparison, achieved through group work and critical classroom discussions;
- cultivation of independent judgment.
In addition to these tools, the following will be implemented:
- periodic verifications, structured and coordinated by tutors, on themes and issues both theoretical and project-oriented chosen autonomously by students and interpreted by them using the methods and techniques they consider appropriate;
- constant verification of communication skills, both verbal, written, and representation skills in exams and in-course assessments.
In addition to the mentioned tools, and in particular, the individual interpretation and analysis tests of laboratory and course materials, it is the 'learning by doing' process itself, with numerous verifications and constant interaction with teachers, experts and tutors, that constitutes the decisive moment for evaluating learning abilities.
Graduates develop learning abilities that enable them to continue studying and updating themselves in an autonomous and self-directed manner, identifying opportunities for continuous training and experiences most suitable to their professional profile. Graduates particularly develop abilities to:
- transform participation in concrete experiences into learning opportunities, using case studies, comparative methods and inquiry;
- identify suitable opportunities for continuous training according to their profile, taking into account the evolution of disciplines, culture and intervention practices on the territory.

SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10150

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates are able to formulate judgments and define choices within a framework of awareness of the approaches and ethical matrices to which they can be related, as well as the impacts they may determine. In particular, they possess the capacity to:
- address complex issues with attention to the different dimensions and repercussions of collective decisions;
- understand (and make others understand) the stakes involved with respect to collective interests, with particular reference to non-reversible choices, and propose appropriate precautionary actions;
- select and construct, with respect to generally limited cognitive contexts, the essential information to address specific issues;
- propose projects, scenarios, and policies contextualized to the different dynamics of the territory;
- prepare evaluation designs consistent with the problems addressed and useful for deepening the relationships between actions and context.

The interdisciplinary training path focuses on building competencies related to: the interpretation of the ecological dynamics of 'sensitive' landscapes, the dynamics and strategies of urban and territorial organization of the city; the planning at territorial and urban scale of actions for transforming landscapes that represent significant places of contemporary cities; the economic, social, institutional, management, and technical feasibility of the proposed planning actions; the development of public policies that allow the landscape and environment to be at the center of urban organization and the cultural future of the city.

Graduates are also able to integrate knowledge and manage the complexity of environmental planning processes, as well as formulate judgments based on limited or incomplete information, including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities related to the application of knowledge and judgments.

The above results will be achieved through frontal courses, workshops, seminars, and laboratory activities in which different approaches and methods are proposed (also from a comparative perspective). In particular, in laboratory paths and workshops, students are required to demonstrate abilities in coordinated work, self-organization, and argumentation and evaluation of project actions based on plausible grounds.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Urban Planning and Planning The master's graduate will acquire and deepen knowledge in the field of planning and urban planning supported by interdisciplinary curricula. These knowledge will be reinforced within the disciplines of environmental science, economics, politics, and sociology, but also within integrative teaching activities.

Some disciplines, in continuity with the three-year degree, are deepened in relation to applied methods in real contexts that allow the planning student to address the complexity of urban and territorial projects. Understanding occurs mainly through the interdisciplinary experience of project laboratories that address problems and outline perspectives for transforming the city, territory, and landscape.

Area of Engineering and Territorial Sciences The master's graduate will refine interpretative abilities and technical-practical tools useful for addressing, according to an integrated approach, issues such as the organization of the transportation system within the more complex and broad process of territorial planning and regeneration. Particular emphasis is placed on the ability to recognize the reciprocal influence relationships between mobility and other components of the settlement organization, and to increase awareness of the importance of building coherent systems between interventions contributing to the functioning of the city.

Area of Economics, Politics, and Sociology Within urban management, the master's graduate will have knowledge related to the evaluation of plans and projects in line with environmental dynamics. Methods and techniques for decision support will be deepened through the use of decision support tools and software applied to territorial and environmental planning. Sociology also contributes to building methods for managing urban processes that often involve mediation between actors in a decision-making process where city transformations encompass interests between parties (e.g., in reference to public administrations, social groups, citizens).

Area of Environment The course in urban ecology will be oriented to provide the practical elements of planning, land use, and urban environment. For each frontal lesson on a specific topic, there is a critical discussion within each specific project that the student or group of students must prepare, so that the ecosystem concept of use threshold is a primary objective of every action or project hypothesis.

Area of Related or Integrative Training Activities The training path of the graduate is supported by some related or integrative disciplines that deepen the specialized knowledge of the planner in relation to emerging themes and on which the demand for skills in the job market will strengthen in the coming years. In particular, the study of methods and techniques to deepen ecosystem resilience in relation to water dynamics and environmental risks; the construction of urban space and its composition in line with environmental dynamics; the deepening of dynamic relationships between historical-cultural public goods in relation to processes of valorization and territorial development; the relationship between the urban environment and public health issues.

These disciplines allow understanding the environmental requirements of the city and territory project in relation to the possibility of generating new landscapes by innovating the tools of the Plan at urban and territorial scale.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Urban Planning and Planning The master's graduate will be able to address complex problems of city, territory, and landscape planning by applying knowledge, methods, techniques, and tools acquired in disciplines related to urban planning and planning. The training path also allows identifying the most appropriate intervention strategies to realize urban, urban, and territorial plans, projects, and action programs in relation to different scales of intervention. "Immersion" in real contexts, often promoted by teachers in agreement with Local Authorities, creates opportunities to understand urban issues, apply knowledge to specific problems through the realization of laboratories, summer schools, and workshops, in which the student is actively involved and can measure their learning ability.

Area of Engineering and Territorial Sciences Through the continuous alternation of analysis and design activities in relation to study contexts, the graduate expands their knowledge, develops an open and non-sectoral view of urban and territorial mobility, and learns a dynamic work method open to cross-disciplinary contamination.

Area of Economics, Politics, and Sociology Within urban management, the master's graduate will be able to apply what has been learned through the re-elaboration and presentation of concrete cases of territorial and urban planning using the methods of environmental assessment and sociology.

Within sociology and the processes and systems of decision support, interactive exercises, often developed in line with the topics treated in planning and urbanism, allow applying the acquired knowledge.

Area of Environment The didactic approach provides that lectures and exercises in urban ecology allow making the environmental requirements of the project hypotheses carried out in urban planning, territorial planning, or landscape architecture laboratories coherent. The application of knowledge is facilitated by field exercises and interdisciplinarity.

Area of Related or Integrative Training Activities The master's graduate will develop a critical and rigorous approach to issues of interest. Will be aware of a management process for environmental resources: from the choice of applying the principle of prevention or precaution; to the forms of absolute protection of environmental matrices. Interdisciplinary knowledge enables the student to develop urban and territorial strategies that address complex and problematic processes of urban reality and refine research abilities, interaction with experts from different disciplines, and the application of knowledge with active operationality.

Official Languages of Teaching and Assessment.
ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Function.
Generic Profile - Territorial Planner For all functions, it is necessary to:
- knowledge of the relevant Italian and European normative, administrative, and institutional frameworks, in particular those of the non-Italian partner institutions of the CdS;
- ability to dialogue with experts from other disciplines;
- ability to work within interdisciplinary and non-interdisciplinary groups;
- ability to coordinate work groups;
- ability to communicate and dialogue with non-experts;
- ability to relate fields of problems and different aspects;
- ability to choose and apply critically methods, techniques, and tools for the analysis and structuring of planning problems;
- knowledge in the field of local development;
- ability to conduct analyses of local, social, and environmental systems;
- critical knowledge of the concepts and principles of sustainability;
- ability to conduct complex and specialized analyses in the field of landscape and environment;
- ability to coordinate and manage environmental assessment activities;
In addition, the knowledge and skills acquired during the master's degree are prerequisites for accessing post-graduate university courses, including international Master's programs and Research Doctorates.

Function in the Workplace.
Generic Profile - Territorial Planner The master's graduate in planning can perform functions typical of free profession (after passing the state exam and registering with the Order of Architects, Planners, Landscape Architects, and Conservators).

In detail, the master's graduate A. coordinates work groups in the field of urban, territorial, and landscape planning at various scales B. drafts, coordinates, and manages plans, policies, urban and territorial transformation projects, programs, strategies, and policies for city and territory governance at different scales.
C. conducts and coordinates complex and specialized analyses of urban, territorial, landscape, and environmental structures, designs and coordinates environmental assessment and feasibility processes for urban and territorial plans and projects;
D. designs, manages, and coordinates participation processes for drafting, implementing, and managing plans and programs for the city and territory E. is responsible for technical-administrative procedures in public administration and can access managerial functions.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The master's degree course in Planning and Policies for the City, Environment, and Landscape is quota-limited.
The teaching of the training path is delivered in a mixed mode. It primarily uses distance learning for theoretical lessons of the core courses and related disciplines.

For the core disciplines of urban planning, in-person teaching is predominant over distance learning and includes all design laboratories and practical exercises. For the other core disciplines (Environment, Economics, Politics and Sociology, Engineering and Territorial Sciences) and for related disciplines, the number of credits for distance and in-person teaching is balanced.

The course provides mixed-mode teaching because:
- involves a wider target of students and expands the student base from other regions;
- responds to proposals from social partners (ANCI, local authorities, professional world) regarding new indications for continuous training;
- responds to the needs outlined in the recently signed agreement between the University of Sassari and the Ministry of Public Administration to expand the knowledge and skills of public employees (a target already present in the course of study).

It offers students the possibility to follow a completely local training path or an international path.

The CdS focuses on the project of territory, landscape, and city, as well as its ability to weave relationships with ecological dynamics, socio-economic and cultural trends of a context, and the processes of management and governance of the territory.

The CdS directs students towards interdisciplinary work methods that allow them to operate in multi-scalar, complex, and uncertain contexts, even at an international level.

The training path measures the possibility of innovating territories starting from a deep knowledge of the matrices of history and environment and the ability to establish strategic connections with the reality of different settlement situations, even in extra-European contexts, in relation to crucial issues of contemporaneity (climate change, processes of planetary economy, urban changes induced by dismission, abandonment, and reuse, forms of inequality, movement of people and cultures, etc.).

The planning graduate develops during the training path capacities and skills aimed at governing transformations, acting on strategic urban issues that identify, for example, alternative models of local development, applying methods of strategic and innovative planning of environmental resources, approaches of urban and territorial planning in relation to the theme of reuse, approaches to the governance of complex processes, methods of conflict mediation, etc.

The study path provides the competencies to build a figure able to:
- interpret the dynamics of the environment and different forms of the city, be able to foster dialogue with its different populations and cultures, and open future scenarios for urban and territorial development;
- design urban and territorial development scenarios that address the problems traversing contemporary landscapes and in particular the crisis of environmental ecosystems and contemporary society, also in relation to climate change and the depletion of non-renewable resources.

Master's graduates are able to:
- analyze, represent, and interpret urban and environmental problems in the processes of territorial and landscape transformation;
- interpret trends and outcomes of city and territory transformations, also in relation to socio-economic dynamics and morphologies;
- build environmental scenarios and policies aimed at protecting, valorizing, and urban regeneration of territory and landscape;
- apply theories, methods, and techniques to design plans and programs with particular attention to environmental resources;
- configure implementation processes anchored to policies and strategies for environmental education, citizen participation, and spatial practices that center the right to the city;
- monitor and evaluate transformation actions of settlement, cultural, and socio-economic processes of a territory, with tools capable of 'measuring' processes and results;
- lead environmental management and auditing activities, coordinating specialists with different cultural backgrounds and competencies.
- define strategies for administrations, institutions, and companies regarding the recovery, valorization, and transformation of the city, territory, landscape, and environment.

Description of the Training Path and Teaching Methods The different disciplines contribute to achieving the educational objectives in coordination with each other regarding the themes of the urban and territorial project to which the interdisciplinary design laboratory belongs.

The training path is organized into four semesters in which teaching units and modules are structured with a distinctive 'title'. Teaching units focus on a core project theme around which different disciplines are integrated; each laboratory involves the production of an individual or group report.

During the first year, two project themes are deepened:
- territorial scale project that experiments with the relationship between settlement projects and landscape policies, where environmental themes related to land and water management in relation to different landscapes of a study context and the objectives of the design laboratory prevail; the foundational matrices of the history of places are also investigated, and a comparison with local populations is experimented.
- urban scale project that measures the relationship between city, environment, and architecture, where sustainability approaches in line with the systemic approach of urban ecology and environmental hygiene are applied; models and tools for evaluation and decision support in urban, territorial, and environmental fields are also explored.

In the second year, the path focuses on interpreting the landscape through the architecture of transformations, including infrastructural types, investigates the existing heritage of a context and the possibilities of re-signification and reuse. The year concludes with an internship and final exam, which can be carried out at the DADU partner sites or at the partner sites.

The study plan and the didactic regulations of the degree program highlight the training activities that students can choose autonomously, in the perspective of deepening their path.

Design activities involve the presence of tutors who follow laboratory and project activities, and in some cases the frontal teaching activities. Some courses develop independently from design activities (although in many cases they can deepen interdisciplinary aspects and specific investigations related to the design work).

Intermediate verification activities of learning (written and oral tests, intermediate critiques of laboratory projects) are provided.

The training offer meets the diverse needs of students who, in addition to learning a work method and having greater job placement opportunities, have the opportunity to project themselves into an international learning and exchange environment.

The international dimension of the Study Course offers the opportunity to measure on different project contexts and approaches that can provide innovative work methods, greater employability of the issued titles, and broader occupational perspectives in an increasingly competitive global context.

Perspectives towards broader contexts, even extra-European ones such as China and the southern shore of the Mediterranean (and in particular Tunisia), strengthen the training path and the prospects of planners in relation to their life projects, thanks to the possibility of deepening work methods that will allow them to face the challenges of different contexts in which they may operate, not only at the local level or within the exclusively European dimension, but also in extra-continental contexts.

Generic profile - Architect The Master's graduate in Architecture can obtain authorization to practice the following regulated professions: Architect, Agricultural Engineer and Forestry Engineer, Civil and Environmental Engineer, Landscape Architect, Territorial Planner.
After passing the professional examination, the graduate naturally finds placement in the job market in technical offices of public bodies and private companies, in architecture and engineering firms operating in the field of architectural design or production of building processes and products.
In detail, the graduate may find employment in:

-public bodies of various nature in roles not immediately related to the degree profile but to the level of the academic qualification as an access requirement.
Final exam characteristics.
The final exam consists of submitting a portfolio of activities carried out during the degree program and discussing a final thesis in a public session, prepared under the guidance of a supervising professor, in the form of a graphic-design elaboration and/or monographic essay, which may also be written in English. Video presentations and explanatory models may be used to accompany the graphic elaborations.
The CFU allocated for the final exam are 9.
The total points awarded for the final exam are 9, including
- 6 for the discussion of the final thesis
- 3 for international mobility.
Required knowledge for access.
Candidates applying for admission to the Master's Degree Course must possess the following requirements:
a) passing the national programmed closed-number admission test;
b) holding a degree in class L17 or having acquired the minimum credits indicated in class L17 for each disciplinary area.
According to the modalities indicated in the Course Didactic Regulation, a verification of the candidate's personal preparation based on previous academic curriculum, portfolio, and an interview or test is also required.
This verification will result in an admission ranking.
The evaluation of academic curricula completed abroad will be carried out based on correspondences between course contents and Scientific-disciplinary sectors. Any curricular integrations in terms of CFU must be acquired before the individual preparation verification.

Communication Skills.
Master's degree holders are able to communicate their design choices to diverse audiences, tailoring communication according to different recipients and objectives; maximum sensitivity is required in evaluating and orchestrating visual and verbal discourse in support of or in opposition to various theses involved; in particular, a secure ability to identify weaknesses and strengths in any design choice corresponds to adequate expertise in identifying the best reasons to justify, defend, and account for one's actions.
In laboratories and courses, the set of described skills is explicitly cultivated; in practical experiences and contexts of intense internationalization, these same abilities are refined in languages other than Italian, so that linguistic barriers can be overcome through the translingual permeability of acquired communication skills.
Particular attention will be paid by instructors and tutors in assessing students' ability to rationally argue in support (but also, when necessary, against, anticipating possible criticisms) of their design choices. In class discussions, the ability to dissociate one's opinion from one's willingness to identify arguments supporting other positions will be positively evaluated. Clarity of exposition and conceptual adequacy will be highly valued in completing various examination tasks and in presenting the dissertation.
Learning Capacity.
Master's degree holders possess broad and rapid learning capabilities, enabling them to autonomously direct themselves toward specific fields of study and research not previously addressed. They have research capabilities that allow them to tackle any issue with intensity and quality, readily applying their design experiences to continuous cultural growth.
In addition to the tools indicated in relation to the previous descriptors, the primary tool for assessing learning capacity will be the project laboratory, where tutors and instructors will monitor whether students can interactively combine theoretical knowledge and design capabilities in a rich and complex manner, and whether these capabilities develop alongside greater research capacity, learning from one's mistakes and hesitations, and the ability to address complexity using the resources of relevance research.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
