SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10427

Judgment Autonomy.
Master's degree holders use architectural design not merely as a tool for problem-solving, but also as a tool for knowledge and exploration of reality; they know how to apply their critical abilities, and generally the entire cultural depth of their university education, in service of their approach to architectural design. In this way, Master's degree holders are equipped with a mature and open judgment capacity, and through empirical analysis, knowledge management, and design synthesis, they are able to formulate autonomous evaluations and choices. Such autonomy should be understood both as a responsible ability in the recruitment of concepts and reasoning in service of an objective, and as the capacity to structure logically comprehensible paths and methodologically anchored to shared practices. These results are achieved through:
- project workshops where the autonomy of choice and judgment, although set within group work and sharing responsibility, is encouraged;
- critical discussions where students are invited to confront difficult and typical professional reality situations individually;
- constant didactic invitation to formulate judgments and support them logically.
Beyond the tools indicated in the previous descriptors, the students' ability to support their preferences and choices with rational argumentation and premises derived from various disciplines will be carefully evaluated – in written and oral exams, discussions, and the progression of project activities. Judgment autonomy will also be observed in the individual capacity to create an optimal dialectic between the individual and the work group, where specialization does not yield to the global vision and where the group's inertial tendency is hindered and directed by well-motivated project intentionality. The judgment of tutors and experts who will lead workshops and specific didactic activities will be as important as that of the professors in this regard.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Area of Urban Architectural Design The teachings of this Area impart knowledge and the ability to understand as the acquisition of appropriate knowledge to interpret complex themes related to the design transformation of the built environment. In particular, the teachings of this Area, through organized work in Workshops, aim to provide tools and methods for design to interpret the various aspects of design in the existing, sustainability, and architectural and urban design at various scales.

Area of Structural Analysis and Design in Architecture The architectural student must know the most important construction systems for single- and multi-story buildings, with particular reference to resistance against vertical and horizontal actions. Additionally, they must know the limit state calculation method, and verify simple steel and reinforced concrete structures. Finally, they must be able to calculate permanent and operational loads, snow, and wind, and their effects on structures.

Area of Estimative Disciplines for Architecture and Urban Planning Students will appropriate the theory of Valuation of Plans, Programs, and Projects both from a formal perspective of deepening approaches and methods, and from an operational perspective for the application of valuation in the construction of the project.

Area of Urban Design and Territorial Planning Regarding the field of planning and urbanism, the Master's graduate will acquire knowledge that extends and/or strengthens those typically associated with the first cycle, enabling the elaboration and/or application of original ideas, often in a research context.
This is primarily achieved through interdisciplinary project workshops that address problems and outline perspectives for transforming the city, territory, and landscape, respecting the system of constraints that condition every design and planning experience, and developing a deep understanding and critical awareness of the most advanced themes and concepts within the field.

Area of Theories and Techniques for Architectural Restoration Students must possess a deep and analytical knowledge of all disciplines contributing to the structuring of an architectural restoration project, meaning they must be able to:
- critically define the historical context that generated architecture and highlight styles, materials, techniques, needs, characters, craftsmen, and elements of the construction vocabulary;
- recognize the main structural elements of historical architecture and their traditional materials;
- organize the geometric and dimensional survey of a building and its graphical restitution;
- understand the nature of issues related to the structural functioning of a building;
- view the architectural object as connected to its environment, territory, history, and the complexity of the context;
- extract logical schemes of approach and interaction with problems from styles and design experiences.

Area of Physical-Technical and Engineering Disciplines for Architecture Fundamental knowledge enabling students to link design choices with energy control techniques and environmental comfort. Understanding of the fundamentals of heat transfer, principles of environmental conditioning, and essential concepts of acoustics and lighting technology applied to construction.

Area of Technological Disciplines for Architecture and Building Production The student is trained through knowledge of the characteristics of construction materials and functional coupling criteria; as well as through knowledge of the different articulations and scales of the design process. The student must also know the environmental constraints acting on the building, which lead to material degradation phenomena; at the same time, they must manage the complex technical control of the design underlying the requirement-oriented-prestational approach.

Area of Architecture and Environment Representation Students must demonstrate understanding and full knowledge, also operational:
- of the tools, methods, and techniques of representation for design communication with the public, their engagement, awareness, and participation;
- of graphic-visual techniques for presenting and interpreting tangible and intangible cultural heritage;
- of accessibility strategies for physical, cultural, and cognitive access to cultural heritage, intended as a tool for protection;
- of digital communication strategies useful to support the design, communication, and dissemination processes of built works, spaces, territories, and all relevant aspects in the design and transformation of spaces.

Area of Economic, Social, and Legal Disciplines for Architecture and Urban Planning Students must possess a good knowledge of the role of public institutions, sources of law, mechanisms for controlling construction and planning activities at all levels.

Area of Historical Disciplines for Architecture Students, having acquired comprehensive knowledge of the most representative monuments of European architecture from the 14th to the 18th century, must develop an understanding of individual architectural monuments within the historical-cultural context of the city, applying the methodological basis of iconology.

Area of Related or Integrative Training Activities The Master's student must acquire fundamental knowledge enabling them to frame the characteristics of a complex design environment in which the territory must be read through its environmental and geological configuration, but also through the cultural signs of its anthropization over time. This will allow the student to specify not so much the answers, but the questions that the Project should pose to History and Geology, to clarify whether they can be limited to individual objects (monuments/documents) and specific locations, or whether they must investigate the environmental and historical processes that have affected, over time, territories, cities, landscapes, and even more so their intersections, vertical and horizontal.

They must also demonstrate a deep and analytical knowledge of the main methodological-philosophical issues. In particular, a living and dynamic competence regarding fundamental questions of epistemology and ethics will be important, along with a developed awareness regarding their ability to organize and differentiate concepts, control truth claims, and argue choices and theoretical positions.

Moreover, the student must know the principles of ecology and environmental hygiene and be able to apply them in the field of environmental sustainability of design interventions.

Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
Area of Urban Architectural Design Application of knowledge occurs through Project Workshops, which become the tool to reconcile within the design process the architectural, typological, morphological, structural, and environmental aspects.
Project workshops may coordinate with other disciplines among the core or related and integrative subjects, thereby enabling both the application of acquired knowledge in those subjects and the application of interdisciplinary reasoning.

Area of Structural Analysis and Design in Architecture The architectural student must be able to preliminary dimension the load-bearing framework of a single- and multi-story building. Additionally, they must be able to design and verify a simple steel structure including bracing elements, and a simple reinforced concrete structure (slab, beam, column) subject to predominantly vertical actions.

Area of Estimative Disciplines for Architecture and Urban Planning Students will be able to apply in practice approaches, methods, and techniques for multi-criteria valuation of regional, national, and community-level architectural plans, programs, and projects.

Area of Urban Design and Territorial Planning The Master's graduate, regarding the field of planning and urbanism, will be able to address complex problems of city, territory, and landscape planning, even when defined incompletely with conflicting specifications, applying acquired knowledge, methods, techniques, and tools. They will also have the ability to design and conduct experiments and interpret their results within interdisciplinary project workshops.
Furthermore, the Master's graduate must be able to identify the most appropriate intervention strategies in relation to distinct planning and design themes and distinguish the required definition scales for different design occasions.

Area of Theories and Techniques for Architectural Restoration Students must be adept at applying their knowledge to new and unprecedented situations—knowledge responding to a rigorous design methodology that forms the basis of architectural restoration.
They must know how to adapt this method to the surrounding historical built environment, developing a process that connects all their knowledge from the geometric and structural reality of the asset, to its material, condition of preservation, up to restoration hypotheses.
In this, they must integrate and enrich each application through awareness of the cultural dimensions of the intervention developed in terms of analysis, and duly integrated in terms of construction and management of complexity arising from new and diverse uses. They will thus be able to develop their technical-scientific and historical-critical competencies in new or innovative contexts, in situations never before encountered, under conditions of partial or vague knowledge of relevant information.
Finally, they will be able to relate the awareness of the need for preservation and conservation of the past with current and historical cultural trends, also in light of the regulatory and professional framework.

Area of Physical-Technical and Engineering Disciplines for Architecture Ability to apply acquired knowledge and quantify studied phenomena through practical exercises in energy, climate control, acoustics, and lighting technology. Verification of understanding and acquired competencies, primarily the ability to elaborate and apply them in a design context.

Area of Technological Disciplines for Architecture and Building Production Starting from the characteristics of known materials, the student must be able to analyze catalogued technical elements and then design new ones. They must also be able to, through performance evaluation, verify the environmental impact of adopted construction choices and reconstruct, through the technological design of the building, the synthesis between ideation and realization.

Area of Architecture and Environment Representation Students must be capable of applying their knowledge and understanding to demonstrate a professional approach to their work, possessing adequate competencies for a comprehensive experience in constructing territorial analyses based on cartographic foundations; they must be able to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors in urban planning and territorial planning.
They must acquire the ability to use drawing as an expressive and visual communication act of the design idea from the formation of the idea to its executive definition. Acquire the ability to choose, use, and combine methods, techniques, and tools of representation and communication within all phases of the design process, while also being capable of using and applying norms and technical knowledge regarding representation and projects and graphical languages in different application fields and possible different expressions.

Area of Economic, Social, and Legal Disciplines for Architecture and Urban Planning Students must apply their knowledge by framing specific legal issues related to a given operational context, particularly regarding:
- public administration; procedures and administrative acts; agreements; private law activities; public administration liability; judicial protection.
- territorial governance regulations and protected interests; territorial planning; different types of plans: content, procedures, and legal nature.
- control over construction activities; authorization titles; abuses and sanctions.

Area of Historical Disciplines for Architecture Application of acquired competencies will enable students to design buildings not only functional but also representative of architecture integrated into the historical-cultural context of the location.

Area of Related or Integrative Training Activities Through acquired knowledge, the student must be able to overcome the entrenched opinion that a historical context is a container of particularly evident historical objects, possibly well-preserved physically. This will also apply to the other Project, the historical one par excellence, the only one that elevates cultural memory and its fetishes to absolute protagonists: the Restoration, Recovery, and Valorization Project.
They must also demonstrate the ability to apply disciplinary content in the analysis and cognitive organization of any issue. The conceptual tools must serve a non-improvised problematization capacity, based on conceptual distinction, hypothesis formulation, propensity for critical control, imagination of alternatives and logically supervised possibilities, and the centrality of rational argumentation.

Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN
Associated competencies for the role.
Generic Profile - Architect The Master's graduate in Architecture will be able to design, through the tools of architecture and civil engineering, construction, transformation, and modification operations of the physical environment, with full knowledge of aesthetic, distributional, functional, structural, technical-constructive, managerial, economic aspects, with critical attention to environmental sustainability issues and cultural changes and the needs expressed by contemporary society.

Role in the workplace context.
Generic Profile - Architect The graduate will be able to design, through the tools of architecture and civil engineering, construction, transformation, and modification operations of the physical environment, with full knowledge of aesthetic, distributional, functional, structural, technical-constructive, managerial, economic, and environmental aspects, with critical attention to cultural changes and the needs expressed by contemporary society. They may prepare project works and direct their implementation, coordinating other specialists and operators in the fields of architecture, civil engineering, urban planning, and architectural restoration.
In particular, the graduate will possess the following competencies:
- knowledge of methodological-operational aspects related to the disciplinary fields characterizing the study course and the ability to identify and solve architecture and construction problems using updated methods, techniques, and tools;
- adequate knowledge of aspects concerning technical and economic feasibility, cost calculation, and the production and realization process of architectural and construction works, as well as aspects related to their safety;
- ability to use the techniques and tools of architectural and construction works design.
These competencies may enable autonomous design:
- in applied research in the fields of architecture and civil engineering;
- in the design of buildings and civil works and the related ideational and procedural processes;
- in the design of restoration interventions on architectural assets, even of complex nature;
- in processes useful for surveying, representing, designing, overseeing construction, and maintaining works, installations, and systems related to safety;
- in the analysis of prices of architectural processes and economic aspects of construction works.

Description of specific training objectives.
Students enrolled in the Course may choose to obtain only the Master's Degree in Architecture or may join one of the international pathways, one of which allows obtaining, in addition to the Architecture degree, the 'Joint master degree European master in integrated sustainable design in the Mediterranean world'. This title can be obtained by enrolling in the international pathway and attending at least one semester of the courses provided at partner universities, as well as participating in the workshops provided in the agreement. Students who do not join the international program, or who decide to leave it, follow only the courses offered by the Master's Degree Course and obtain the Master's Degree in Architecture. The Course Council has provided for the possibility of offering some courses and/or semesters in English.

The specific training objective of the Master's Degree Course in Architecture is the formation in the field of architectural and urban design at all scales, understood as an integrated activity based on an interdisciplinary and holistic theoretical background, materializing through attention to themes of materiality, open space, public space, sustainable construction, and attention to historical urban and territorial contexts.

The Course Council has authorized the modification of the Curriculum necessary for the potential activation of two additional curricula beyond the traditional one in Architecture, one on the theme of Architectural Restoration and Historical Contexts and one on Design; these tracks respond to specific needs of contemporary design practice linked to an increasingly recurring demand for competencies related to the preservation of ancient built heritage and the rapid change of markets and production, and thus of design and its communication.
All three curricula share the same main training objectives and maintain the didactic structure of the degree course as a recognizable element; they differ only in the courses contributing to defining for the Master's graduate opportunities for deepening in the thematic areas of the specific tracks according to the intervals established by regulations.
The courses specifying the curricula are, however, delivered not only through lectures but also through workshops maintaining a strong project component.

The overall structure of the degree course is organized with an innovative conception based substantially on the following aspects:
- 'learning by doing': not only are all acquired theoretical notions systematically verified against reality, but the confrontation itself with real conditions becomes an additional topic for developing critical reasoning;
- structuring of study plans oriented toward the project, enabling direct application of what is learned in the theoretical sections of courses; thus, the ability to transform learned concepts into deliverables is acquired, and students become accustomed to the rhythms and deadlines imposed by professional activity;
- pluralistic training achieved both through the cooperation of different disciplines on each individual project and through the teaching of professors from different schools, Italian and foreign;
- the scheduling of thematic workshops, generally two per academic year, follows changed learning rhythms;
- language learning during work, also through didactic blocks where teaching is conducted in English, to develop not only language knowledge but also the specific disciplinary vocabulary;
- strong openness to the European dimension, given both by the organization of teaching and by the extensive use of Erasmus programs, as well as inclusion in international agreements for the formation of a European learning space that provide for the award of double or joint degrees;
- an optimal ratio between the number of teachers and students, allowing students to be consistently followed during lectures and workshops;
- extensive and creative use of new technologies as both a study and work environment, as well as for learning and using new professional tools.
This organization of degree courses arises from a careful analysis and in-depth evaluation of major international experiences in relation to the evolution of disciplines, learning methods, and professional activities.
Each year is divided into semesters, in which the University Credit Units (CFU) are distributed.
The training activity, according to the regulations of the University Didactic Regulation and the Department Regulation of Architecture, Design, and Urban Planning, is structured as:
- project and in-depth didactic blocks
- single-discipline courses
- student-selected activities and internships
- computer and telecommunication skills
- final exam
The semester blocks are coordinated and didactically linked to each other; they are characterized by a complex design theme requiring students to use all possessed disciplinary knowledge and converge it toward the objective of solving problems, conducting analyses, and justifying choices.
In each block and for each discipline, frontal lectures, exercises, and integrated project workshops with teachers and tutors are carried out. Throughout the academic year, prolonged development courses and single-discipline courses are also held.
The widespread use of new technologies characterizes the study plan programs, creating a creative study and work environment and enabling the learning and use of new professional tools.
The exam schedule is structured in three sessions: February, July, and September (for design workshops, the exam is scheduled at the end of the block).
The first year for all possible tracks is structured into two semester blocks focused on architectural design and enriched with courses of disciplines converging on the themes raised by design reflection, while the second year presents a first semester coinciding with the final project block and a second part dedicated to acquiring free credits, further computer and telecommunication knowledge.

Foreign Degree Fees and contributions Regulation Careers - Fees Roles Responsible for approving study plans CARLA BASSU Student mobility responsibility DAVID FINBAR BRETT Chair LOREDANA SALIS Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION are able to exercise their activity both as language instructors and as foreign language correspondents, with a high level of competence. They can, in fact, leverage their interdisciplinary preparation to personally use (or teach others) the linguistic structures they have mastered through their studies in the Course, directing such structures towards institutional-business-cultural relations with foreign countries (for example, they are capable of drafting letters in foreign language, preparing documents using sector-specific languages, conducting telephone conversations in foreign language, taking notes in foreign language, etc.) in the various multi-ethnic and multicultural contexts where they may operate, both in Italy and abroad.
The expected employment opportunities also include consulting activities for local authorities and businesses (for example cooperatives or tourism sector companies), for local authorities and government institutions for the planning of complex multi-level tourist-cultural events (municipal, regional, national and international), and professional activities in public relations, image, and similar professions. Additionally, graduates in this Degree Class will become experts in sustainable tourism promotion and local development; experts in regional and local development programs and plans, consultants in planning and participation, also as trainers, for events falling under conference tourism; authors of advertising texts; technical text writers; experts in travel agency programming; consultants in natural parks and reserves; researchers, graduate technicians and similar.
Characteristics of final exam.
The final exam is public and consists of the discussion of a written thesis (written under the guidance of a supervisor and co-supervisor). The thesis may be written, in part or entirely, in the candidate's biennialized foreign language. In the latter case, an integral translation into Italian must also be produced.
Knowledge required for admission.
To access the Course, it is necessary to hold a Bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
Admission is conditional on verifying personal preparation through passing an entrance exam and possessing specific curricular requirements, listed below:
18 CFU in the SSD of the first curricular language;
18 CFU in the SSD of the second curricular language;
6 CFU in the SSD L-LIN/01;
6 CFU in the SSD INF/01;
6 CFU in the SSDs M-GGR/01 or M-GGR/02.
The methods for verifying personal preparation and the required curricular requirements are detailed in the Course Didactic Regulations.
Degree title awarded.
Link to Study Plan Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.

They can, in fact, leverage their interdisciplinary preparation to personally use (or teach others) the linguistic structures they have mastered through their studies in the Course, directing such structures towards institutional-business-cultural relations with foreign countries (for example, they are capable of drafting letters in foreign language, preparing documents using sector-specific languages, conducting telephone conversations in foreign language, taking notes in foreign language, etc.) in the various multi-ethnic and multicultural contexts where they may operate, both in Italy and abroad.
The expected employment opportunities also include consulting activities for local authorities and businesses (for example cooperatives or tourism sector companies), for local authorities and government institutions for the planning of complex multi-level tourist-cultural events (municipal, regional, national and international), and professional activities in public relations, image, and similar professions. CURRICULUM: Communication Skills
SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10721

Communication Skills.
The graduate, thanks to solid and specific linguistic, literary, and cultural knowledge acquired through attendance and individual study and verified by passing the relevant exams, is able to communicate the acquired knowledge and skills in various disciplinary fields (public and private entities, national and international institutions and organizations of a social, political, humanitarian nature, etc.) and to interact with both specialist and non-specialist operators, offering project-oriented hypotheses and solutions aimed at resolving the themes and issues of interest to the target.
It is expected that graduates achieve the following skills:
to be able to interact orally, presenting independent ideas, receiving and giving instructions, initiating and developing dialectical exchanges with specialists and non-specialists; to be able to speak in public; to be able to write clearly and well-organized various text genres; to be able to summarize and evaluate information from multiple written sources, even of scientific nature and level; to be able to carry out written activities such as describing and arguing with audiences of any level.
These abilities must be complemented by: the ability to manage relations between foreign languages and cultures and to communicate, based on solid linguistic acquisitions (in at least two languages, in addition to Italian), the competence in using information and multimedia technologies, the knowledge acquired and the project elaborations connected, addressing both specialists and non-specialists in the field. Regarding linguistic aspects, both in Italian and in the foreign languages of study, they will focus, besides the communicative and socializing aspect, on the specialized lexicons of activities related to tourism, territory, and local development with updating of management knowledge, which form the basis of cultural tourism.
The development of such skills will be pursued by granting ample space, alongside frontal teaching of courses, to teaching methods that actively involve the communicative skills of students within lectures, seminars, and laboratories, both on the side of traditional verbal and written communication, as well as through the use of multimedia means. The acquisition of such skills will be assessed through written and oral evaluations within individual courses and in the context of the final thesis discussion.
These results will be achieved through teaching methods that vary partly depending on the disciplinary sector.

CURRICULUM: Judgment Autonomy
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10721

Judgment Autonomy.
The graduate in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION, applying the methodological and theoretical knowledge acquired and deepened in various study disciplines, has the ability to manage complex situations and is capable of developing project-based solutions even based on partial or incomplete data.
The graduate, in addition to having developed learning and processing abilities based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge, is able to autonomously formulate a critical judgment and reflect on professional ethics and deontology as an operator and cultural mediator at an international level.
It is expected that, through continuous and in-depth reflection on various scientific issues experienced during lectures and exercises in the disciplines comprising their course of study, graduates will acquire the ability to formulate autonomous judgments on complex issues. In particular, with reference to their field of study, it is expected that they will become:
a) capable of collecting, using, and interpreting data in the field of foreign languages and cultural and textual traditions, from both theoretical and applied perspectives, to solve even complex linguistic, textual, and interpretative problems, developing personal perspectives and reading keys.
b) capable of theoretically assessing the problematic nature of concrete situations (for example, in the fields of teaching, cooperation, integration, tourism, programming and territorial governance and local development processes), developing effective solutions and even complex problem-solving strategies.
Graduates of the class must possess:
- the ability to integrate acquired knowledge and new realities on which to formulate conscious judgments regarding ethical responsibilities, and to express reflective processes and related conclusions.
Oral and/or written assessment methods, linguistic competencies aimed at acquiring specialized terminology, may use concrete case simulations to better evaluate the desired increasing judgment autonomy.

Learning Ability.
The graduate in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION, after assimilating knowledge in diverse but closely related disciplinary fields to the objectives of the Course of Study, having passed the examinations, is capable of developing a self-learning ability enabling them to continue studying in an autonomous and original manner.
Additionally, they can access higher levels of specialization by participating with a high degree of research autonomy in Research Doctorates and/or National and International Master's Programs of I and II level.
It is expected that, thanks to the declarative and procedural knowledge acquired, especially during lectures and exercises in the disciplines under study and generally throughout all stages of their educational activities, graduates will enhance their learning abilities, particularly developing: metacognitive strategies (reflection on language and its learning process); cognitive strategies (exploration of different learning styles and strategies, and recognition of individual needs related to the disciplines studied); communicative and social-affective strategies (through practice of the highest competencies achieved in L2).
These abilities and strategies will enable graduates to fully autonomously approach subsequent studies, both in these specific fields and in other neighboring disciplinary areas.
The achievement of these results will be supported through the use of teaching methodologies that complement traditional lectures with guided research and application activities in didactic laboratories and internships, established in agreement with public and private entities, also foreign, operating in the tourism sector. In addition to assessments related to individual training activities through written and oral exams, the acquisition of solid linguistic competencies and the ability to autonomously apply and solve complex problems using the various disciplinary contributions within the fields of tourism sciences and linguistic communication will be evaluated through the final thesis, which will consist of an original work prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor.

Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC-LITERARY AREA The student must acquire adequate linguistic knowledge and possess a high level of competence in at least one European or extra-European language. They must deepen their knowledge of the chosen foreign languages, achieving a high level of competence in the first language and refining the level in the second language.
The student must also acquire in-depth knowledge in literary and philological studies; in particular, they must master the methodological tools offered by literary theory and philology through the study and analysis of primary sources; the relationship between text and context, and between language and literature, will be fundamental for the student's formation.
Oral and/or written assessment methods, possibly ongoing during course delivery, language exercises (reading sessions) for support and deepening that accompany the teaching of foreign languages, seminars with possible request for written and/or oral reports, are considered the planned teaching tools for verifying the acquired level of knowledge. Regarding literature and philology, students are encouraged to develop research tools, critical thinking, and text and context reading skills, also through participation in in-depth seminars and related didactic activities.

MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATICS AREA The objective of this area is to develop knowledge and methodological skills specific to management and informatics disciplines. In particular, the main computer and telecommunication tools, competencies related to new communication and information languages, appropriate tools for text and image computer processing, theoretical, methodological, and technical tools for the treatment of texts and images within practical activities will be provided. This objective is complemented by transmitting knowledge of the main theories of business strategy and policy. The ultimate goal is to impart the principles underlying strategic management of companies, the techniques and tools used by economic subjects to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. Educational objectives will be pursued through activities that, in addition to frontal lectures, also include exercises, internships, and assisted study activities to facilitate the acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge in these disciplinary areas.

LEGAL AND ECONOMIC AREA The objective of this area is to provide solid knowledge in economic and legal disciplines. In particular, this area aims to analyze in a comparative perspective the constitutional models of contemporary democracies, provide fundamental theoretical knowledge of administrative law, form a critical evaluation and interpretation of treaty provisions, and experiment with the interpretation of acts in the field of navigation and land transport law.
This area also aims to equip students with basic economic-statistical knowledge, particularly regarding an introduction to statistical methods and relationships, quantitative methods, position indices, and variability measures. This knowledge will enable graduates to enter the workforce with awareness.
Educational objectives will be pursued through activities that, in addition to frontal lectures, also include exercises, internships, and assisted study activities to facilitate the acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge in these disciplinary areas.
Expected results will be verified through oral and/or written assessments, ongoing or final, aimed at verifying acquired knowledge and the ability to present it in an organized manner. Internship activities will be subject to specific evaluation by the hosting organization.

GEOGRAPHICAL, ANTHROPOLOGICAL AND SOCIAL AREA Graduates must demonstrate secure acquisition of methodological tools and linguistic-cultural, social, environmental, and anthropological knowledge capable of reinforcing and completing those acquired in the first cycle; important is also the acquisition of personal autonomy in proposing and advancing critical observations and original ideas within their study and research context, characteristic of geographical and anthropological disciplines, in order to use the studied languages with awareness in the perspective of national and international communication. The objective of this area is to provide concepts and tools for understanding the dynamics of space use in relation to socioeconomic, environmental, and cultural change processes.
Particular attention will also be given to acquiring specific competencies related to the promotion of territorial resources and local development.
Oral and/or written assessment methods, possibly ongoing, participation in guided visits, seminars with possible request for written and/or oral reports, are considered the planned teaching tools for verifying the acquired level of knowledge.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC-LITERARY AREA The acquired knowledge must be the fundamental tool to navigate the job market; graduates must be able to transfer and use it on a practical level, integrating and applying it to research and/or professional contexts in which they are involved, with intellectual curiosity and individual skills in solving new or less common themes and problems within interdisciplinary contexts. Therefore, graduates will be able to apply what they have learned, at the level expected by the educational path, in performing the tasks assigned to them.
Oral and/or written assessment methods (as well as language exercises accompanying the teaching of foreign languages) will gradually assess the ability to apply acquired knowledge for solving non-routine problems. Particular emphasis will be placed on learning activities conducted at the University Language Center.
Graduates will be able to apply the linguistic and philological-literary knowledge acquired to the extent required in the workplace. In particular, students will be trained in critical thinking, sharing it in written and oral form, and will demonstrate having acquired critical reading skills for texts and contexts, with particular attention to the literary field. They will also develop autonomous study, research, and analysis capabilities in preparation for the final thesis and potential application of literary disciplines in work experiences, internships, and training paths in Italy and abroad.

MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATICS AREA The objective of this disciplinary area is to develop the ability to use and apply knowledge in management and informatics fields as required in the workplace, to form a flexible and competent Master's graduate. In particular, abilities to use and apply knowledge related to business economics and management, strategic and business policy concepts, strategic planning, the evolution of strategic paradigms, and the theoretical and practical aspects of technological tools for content and document management will be developed. Students will have the opportunity to engage in internships aimed at acquiring direct knowledge in sectors particularly useful for entering the workforce and acquiring specific professional skills. These activities can be carried out in line with the chosen curriculum.

LEGAL AND ECONOMIC AREA The objective of this disciplinary area is to develop the ability to use and apply knowledge in legal and economic fields to form a Master's graduate capable of meeting the demands of contemporary work. Specifically, themes related to the examination of state and government forms from a comparative perspective, fundamental rights and tools for recognition and protection at national and supranational levels, navigation and transportation regulation, security, public administration activities and their functioning will be developed. Particular attention will be given to the fundamental concepts of descriptive statistics, enabling recognition of different types of statistical data and their specificities, and correct application of simple synthesis, analysis, and description methods for phenomena. These are essential topics for professional practice, which will primarily interact with Public Administration directly or indirectly.
During the educational path, graduates will begin to apply acquired competencies through an internship that allows them to experience the concrete issues of the functioning of companies, organizations, and other institutions.

GEOGRAPHICAL, ANTHROPOLOGICAL AND SOCIAL AREA The acquired knowledge in geographical, anthropological, and social fields must be the fundamental tool to navigate the job market. Graduates must be able to transfer and use it on a practical level, integrating and applying it to research and/or professional contexts in which they are involved, with intellectual curiosity and individual skills in solving new or less common themes and problems within interdisciplinary contexts connected to their study area. Oral and/or written assessment methods will gradually assess the ability to solve non-routine problems.
Graduates will be able to apply the acquired knowledge in the geographical-anthropological-social area to the extent required in the workplace.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Function.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, particularly with reference to local development. The curriculum in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION has a primarily communicative function, particularly on an international level. This function will enable graduates to navigate with competence and confidence in all work contexts where interpersonal, verbal, and non-verbal communication is central, with at least two foreign languages.
The competencies associated with the function of the curriculum FOREIGN LANGUAGES, TOURISM, TERRITORY AND LOCAL DEVELOPMENT specifically concern: territorial transformation and governance processes, particularly with reference to local development, considered in its physical, legal-economic, social, cultural aspects and their interrelationships, within a sustainability perspective. In particular, competencies for managing tourism resources will be acquired.
The expected professional opportunities for the Degree Class are as follows:
- cultural mediator, also in migration contexts; - operator in cultural services, journalism, publishing, and cultural institutions; - operator responsible for international relations in Italian and foreign companies and societies; - operator in the tourism field, with particular reference to cultural tourism; - language assistant in business, organizations, or public and private institutions, also through translation activities; - language and cultural assistant in the field of language training and education; - translator and interpreter, upon completion of the educational path, in accordance with current regulations; - teacher of foreign language and literature in primary and secondary schools, or Italian for foreigners, upon completion of the educational path, in accordance with current regulations; - specialists in public relations and image, particularly regarding the sustainable tourism sector; - scholars and researchers, referring to scientific fields related to tourism's role in spatial organization, promotion, and territorial valorization; - experts in regional development programs and plans; - experts in promoting sustainable tourism and local development; - responsible for travel agency programming and responsible for social and cultural tourism; - consultant in natural parks and reserves; - professional with high-level professional tasks as a tourism consultant and orientation specialist.

Function in the Workplace Context.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, particularly with reference to local development. Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION will be able to perform a primarily communicative function, and in particular on an international and national level. This function will enable graduates to navigate with competence and confidence in all work contexts where interpersonal, verbal, and non-verbal communication is central, with at least two foreign languages.
In particular, those in the CURRICULUM in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION must achieve adequate knowledge and skills in the chosen foreign languages and their respective cultural and literary context. They must also demonstrate high theoretical-practical knowledge in sociological, geoeconomic, and legal fields, and the ability to understand cultural and communication processes to develop original and innovative ideas and convey them in multicultural and multiethnic contexts.
The Master's Degree curriculum named FOREIGN LANGUAGES, TOURISM, TERRITORY AND LOCAL DEVELOPMENT aims to promote the ability to operate within different territorial realities to promote responsible local development even within the framework of international cooperation.
Basic theoretical knowledge will be developed and applied in specific research contexts (academic, professional, or technological) or broader interdisciplinary contexts connected to the study sectors.
The two curricula will develop:
- the ability to formulate autonomous critical judgments based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge;
- the ability to communicate (in different contexts, addressing both specialist and non-specialist, Italian and foreign interlocutors) acquired knowledge and competencies, clearly and unambiguously, based on solid linguistic preparation in both Italian and the studied foreign languages; a learning ability in the various provided study areas (linguistic-communicative, sociological-economic-legal, territorial, literary, informatics) enabling them to continue studying in an autonomous and original manner and to access higher and further specialized study levels (University Master's Programs of I and II level and Research Doctorates).

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION will be able to perform a primarily communicative function, and in particular on an international and national level. This function will enable graduates to navigate with competence and confidence in all work contexts where interpersonal, verbal, and non-verbal communication is central, with at least two foreign languages.
In particular, students must achieve adequate knowledge and skills in the chosen foreign languages and their respective cultural and literary context. They must also demonstrate high theoretical-practical knowledge in sociological-geoeconomic-legal fields, and the ability to understand cultural and communication processes to develop original and innovative ideas and convey them in multicultural and multiethnic contexts.
The Degree Class aims to train specialists in knowledge regarding linguistic, cultural, and management aspects required by the regional and international tourism system. Strongly supported by solid linguistic acquisitions, they will be able to design initiatives within the framework of sustainable tourism and territorial transformation and governance processes and local development, tourism initiatives in collaboration with foreign, national, or local entities, cultural events requiring broad and relevant coordination capabilities, as well as indispensable management knowledge.
Students' basic theoretical knowledge will be developed and applied in specific academic, professional, or technological contexts or broader interdisciplinary contexts connected to the linguistic study sectors. They will also develop the ability to formulate autonomous critical judgments based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge; communicate in different contexts, acquired knowledge and competencies, clearly and unambiguously, based on solid linguistic preparation in both Italian and the studied foreign languages; demonstrate learning ability in the various provided study areas (linguistic-communicative, sociological-economic-legal, territorial, literary, informatics) enabling them to continue studying in an autonomous and original manner and to access higher and further specialized study levels (University Master's Programs of I and II level and Research Doctorates).
The educational path offers a continuation of studies for those who have a degree in linguistic-communicative disciplines and have already acquired mastery of linguistic and computer tools for international use, as well as for those who possess adequate theoretical and practical preparation in economic and socio-legal fields underlying tourism entrepreneurship and have acquired necessary operational skills for managing, promoting, and valorizing territorial resources.
The aim is to strengthen the necessary theoretical-practical tools to navigate various contexts of linguistic communication, consolidating the theoretical and practical knowledge and skills acquired during the undergraduate program, thus facilitating greater entry into the workforce or a potential continuation of studies within Second-Level Master's programs. The interdisciplinary preparation (geographical, literary, economic, socio-cultural, and legal disciplines) aims to form a flexible Master's graduate in modern languages capable of positioning themselves as mediators between different social and productive realities, not only due to linguistic competencies but also due to sensitivity to issues related to social and cultural development and integration processes. It prepares for employment in public and private companies in the commercial sector and human resources, as well as in management staff, especially in the logistics sector, and in national and international companies more involved in the globalization of the economy or active in the production and dissemination of culture, in the growing tourism sector in general, with particular reference to planning, management, and marketing sectors.
Finally, the structure of the path allows access to teaching in secondary schools, upon obtaining the qualification through TFA.

Final Exam Characteristics. The final exam consists of the dissertation and discussion of an original thesis prepared under the guidance of a supervisor, according to the methodological requirements and formal standards of the discipline. The thesis, prepared in the form of a written report, must be consistent with the educational path and relevant to one of the subjects specified in the student's curriculum. The supervisor may establish the use of the English language for the preparation and/or presentation of the work.
Required Knowledge for Access. The required knowledge for access to the Master's degree course in Political and Legal Sciences for Administration consists of adequate mastery of the most relevant notions, methodologies, and issues in the fields of legal and political sciences, with particular regard to the role and operational methods of public administrations.

- possession of a three-year degree (with a grade not lower than 90/110) or an equivalent title obtained abroad;

- Private Law Disciplines (IUS/01, IUS/04, IUS/07): 6 CFU;

- Political Science Disciplines (SPS/01, SPS/02, SPS/03, SPS/04): 6 CFU.

Judgment Autonomy Students acquire the necessary skills to analyze, also comparatively, the data and sources required for formulating hypotheses and solutions to complex problems related to the actions of public administrative bodies, private organizations, and the third sector. These skills are acquired through various educational activities. Judgment autonomy is verified and assessed through exercises, seminars, assignments (also multimedia) and the final exam.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Legal Area Graduates will acquire advanced skills in strategic areas where public administrations operate (from public procurement law to public economic law), and skills to rationalize and guide decision-making processes, as well as to experiment and define more effective and efficient practices of administrative action. The legal knowledge and methodologies learned contribute to forming a profile capable of managing and integrating new technologies in the decision-making, management, and communication aspects of public organizations.
Social Sciences Area Graduates must achieve high-level knowledge of the specialized conceptual frameworks of social sciences, master the relevant methodological tools, and develop critical understanding of the main themes and issues connected to public administration activities.
These objectives will be pursued through teaching paths that emphasize active student participation in the learning process: seminar activities, individually or group-developed research, internships, etc.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Legal Area Thanks to acquired knowledge, graduates must be able to carry out activities focused on caring for and protecting the legal interests of the entity in which they operate, supporting its actions in all sectors where its institutional activities take place.
In particular, they must have acquired skills: drafting and verifying administrative documents, preparing agreements, contracts, resolutions; drafting and controlling contractual texts, agreements, public tenders, reports and documents; managing administrative procedures; supporting political and administrative bodies through research and documentation activities.
Social Sciences Area Graduates must be able to apply theoretical and methodological tools in multiple areas of public administration action:
a) develop and/or apply original ideas even in a research context;
b) form judgments including reflection on social and ethical responsibilities and consequences;
c) communicate conclusions derived from the analysis of individual problems, as well as the knowledge and rationale underlying them, clearly and unambiguously to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
In particular, they must be able to:
a) analyze and evaluate public policies;
b) organize and manage complex structures;
c) manage and integrate new technologies in the decision-making and management aspects of public organizations;
d) implement communication needs of public administrations.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIANO Associated competencies for the role.
Specialist in Public Administration Management
1) legal knowledge in civil, public, and administrative law, intended to ensure adequate knowledge of legal sources and mechanisms regulating relations between various institutions.
2) skills for personnel selection and recruitment activities and analysis of needs and personnel training; knowledge of public relations and promotion of the entity's image; skills to conduct analyses and identify solutions to problems of an economic, social, and political nature.
Role in work context.
Specialist in Public Administration Management The course prepares two distinct professional profiles:
1) the public administration legal officer;
2) the specialist in innovative management and organization of complex structures.
The first profile carries out activities focused on caring for and protecting the legal interests of the entity in which it operates, supporting its actions in all sectors where its institutional activities take place. In particular, this professional profile handles: drafting and verification of administrative documents, preparation of agreements, contracts, resolutions; drafting and control of contractual texts, agreements, public tenders, reports and documents; management of administrative procedures; support to political and administrative bodies through research and documentation activities.
The second profile coordinates activities of administrative offices such as local authorities, universities, ASL, etc.; possesses skills for personnel selection and recruitment activities and analysis of needs and personnel training; handles public relations and promotion of the entity's image. More generally, possesses skills to analyze and identify solutions to problems of an economic, social, and political nature.
Description of specific learning objectives.
Specific Learning Objectives The specific learning objectives of the interclass course in Political and Legal Sciences for Administration harmoniously combine those specific to class LM-62 and class LM SC-GIUR.
The course aims to train graduates with advanced and in-depth knowledge and skills in the disciplines of legal and social sciences, with particular attention to the analysis and development of innovative strategies in the organizations of the public sector (understood broadly, including both public administrations in the strict sense and the set of entities, even private in organizational structure, controlled by public administrations in various ways and for various reasons).
Study Path Structure:
The educational path includes a common first year, during which themes related to citizen-public administration relations, public policy analysis, regulations concerning territorial entities and community institutions, and legal issues of the labor world will be deepened.
In the second year, the 'Innovation and Public Administration' track aims to train students capable of managing and integrating new technologies in the decision-making, management, and communication aspects of public organizations.
To this end, the track is characterized by acquiring skills in digital administration and public and institutional communication.
The 'Legal Services for Administrations' track, in addition to providing advanced skills in strategic areas where public administrations operate (from public procurement law to public economic law), ensures advanced skills to rationalize and guide decision-making processes, as well as to experiment and define more effective and efficient practices of administrative action.

TECHNICIAN FOR FOREST AND ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCTIONS The professional profile of the Master's graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems (LM73) falls within the profile provided for the forestry engineer under D.P.R. 328 of 05.06.2001 and subsequent amendments. The Master's graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems may therefore carry out their activities not only in the field of forest production but also in the protection and management of non-urban environments, both as a self-employed professional and within public administrations and research institutions Characteristics of final examination.
The Master's degree in Forest and Environmental Systems is obtained by passing a final examination, consisting of the presentation and discussion of the thesis, written by the student under the guidance of a supervisor, before a committee of professors. The Master's thesis is a written document structured according to the lines of a scientific publication, prepared by the student under the supervision of a supervisor and concerning an original scientific experience related to the Forest and Environmental Systems degree course and addressing a topic characteristic of the study program.
The evaluation of the final examination will follow the criteria established by the Department's teaching regulations.
Required knowledge for admission.
Admission to the Master's degree in Forest and Environmental Systems is open to graduates in the class of degree L 25 Agricultural and Forest Sciences and Technologies and in the class of degree L-21 Sciences of Territorial Planning, Urbanism, Landscape and Environment (or the previous classes 20 Agricultural, Food and Forest Sciences and Technologies and class 7 Urban Planning and Territorial and Environmental Sciences, as provided for by D.M. n. 509/99), and to graduates in other degree classes possessing the curricular requirements of class L 25, following evaluation of preparation.
The Course Council has also set as requirements for enrollment in the Master's degree in Forest and Environmental Systems, for students not coming from class L-25 Agricultural and Forest Sciences and Technologies, to have earned at least 35 CFU in the following SSD: AGR01, AGR05, AGR08, AGR11, AGR12, AGR16.
In any case, adequate initial preparation must be assessed in accordance with Article 6, paragraph 2 of D.M. 270/04, using methods established in the course's teaching regulations.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in FOREST AND ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS Employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
TECHNICIAN FOR FOREST AND ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCTIONS The professional profile of the Master's graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems (LM73) falls within the profile provided for the forestry engineer under D.P.R. 328 of 05.06.2001 and subsequent amendments. The Master's graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems may therefore carry out their activities not only in the field of forest production but also in the protection and management of non-urban environments, both as a self-employed professional and within public administrations and research institutions Communication skills.
At the end of their studies, the graduate will have developed aptitudes for communication, teamwork and multidisciplinary work, and the ability to make judgments both technically and economically, as well as humanely and ethically; they will be able to use at least one European Union language in addition to Italian, preferably English, with specific reference to disciplinary terminology. The acquisition of communication skills, both written and oral, will be verified through the evaluation of the written works related to the examination tests and the final oral presentation before the committees, also using computer and cartographic tools.
Learning abilities.
