Autonomy of Judgment.
The Master's graduate will have high analytical and critical evaluation skills regarding the state of forest and environmental systems:
to implement interventions aimed at improving and conserving environmental quality and planning sustainable development of forest environmental resources;
to manage natural biodiversity;
to carry out landscape planning and environmental impact economic assessment;
to correctly implement and certify forest and environmental systems.
The acquisition of autonomy of judgment will be verified through various exam assessments, and the degree of autonomy acquired will be evaluated based on the ability to work individually or in groups during assigned activities in preparation for the final exam.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area: At the end of the training path, the graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems will have knowledge of the investigation methods specific to Forest and Environmental Sciences and will be able to address with an integrated approach the analysis and design of forest and environmental systems, evaluating their complexity and biodiversity, applying the fundamental methods of scientific investigation for problem-solving in the forest and environmental sector.
Possesses theoretical, operational, and laboratory knowledge to carry out appropriate interventions in various sectors of forest and environmental activities, with particular reference to:
- sustainable planning and management of forest environmental resources;
- improvement of forest and environmental systems;
- environmental monitoring, connected to chemical and biological risks in forest and mountain environments;
- conservation of animal and plant biodiversity;
- prevention and care of forest species using environmentally respectful phytosanitary defense strategies and techniques;
- protection and conservation of soil and mountain environments;
- environmental impact assessment;
- prevention of major environmental risks and management of initial interventions for the safety of territory and populations in local, national, and international contexts;
- design and sustainable management of environmental risk prevention interventions in national and international contexts related to climate change;
- design and management of secondary productions in forest areas, whether in natural or semi-natural conditions compatible with their potential;
- design and management of interventions for population safety in extrurban areas within the framework of international cooperation.

CURRICULUM CIVIL PROTECTION. The objective of the curriculum is to prepare a graduate capable of preventing disaster risk events and organizing initial interventions in the presence of environmental disasters in agricultural and forest contexts, as well as collaborating in interventions in the field of international cooperation in agricultural and forest contexts.
The course in Agrometeorology and Climate Change Monitoring and Analysis allows students to acquire information on the climatic characteristics of a territory, its possible variations in the short and medium term, for monitoring the main environmental components with particular reference to forest and mountain environment management.
In the course on Forest Fire Prevention and Control, techniques for reducing fire risk in agricultural and forest areas are illustrated, along with the construction of structures for initial control and management of fires in forest areas in coordination with regional and national intervention structures.
The course in Civil Protection Techniques provides students with information on initial interventions for mitigating environmental disasters in extrurban areas and first aid to affected populations in collaboration with regional and national civil protection structures.
The two modules on Chemical and Biological Risk Management and Hydrogeological Risk Assessment in the integrated course on Hydrogeological Risk Management and Monitoring aim to provide guidelines for the implementation, control, and management of monitoring networks, both biological and chemical, in waters and soils, with particular reference to possible pathogenic microorganisms and pollution.
Hydrogeological Risk Management aims to identify, according to current national and regional regulations, possible risk areas for flooding or landslides, and to prepare, for forest and mountain areas, control and prevention tools.
Finally, the two courses in Safety Techniques and First Aid and Civil Protection Logistics, which are recommended for students, aim to provide the necessary knowledge for preparing safety plans and initial interventions in business contexts and organizing an intervention network for population safety, also through the implementation of a data transmission network.
In both curricula, an English language course is provided to familiarize students with the technical terminology of the forestry engineer profession.

CURRICULUM SUSTAINABLE AGRO-FORESTAL PRODUCTIONS. The objective of the curriculum is to prepare a graduate capable of designing and managing all productive aspects of secondary forest products. Products that can represent an important source of income for the territory in the short and medium term.
The course in Wood and Biomass Arboriculture, in conjunction with the Forest Management course, allows students to acquire specific knowledge for managing forests for the production of high-quality timber or for the production of energy or eco-friendly materials.
The course in Nursery Techniques, given recent phytosanitary emergencies due to the introduction of entomofauna or foreign species of interest to the territory, requires knowledge for the implementation of nurseries capable of ensuring the health of productions and the breeding of tree species or varieties suitable for different ecosystems.
In the two modules of Zootechnical Systems and Fauna Management and Agro-silvo-pastoral Systems in the integrated course on Agro-silvo-pastoral and Zootechnical Systems, students gain knowledge of the particular complexity of issues related to the presence of zootechnically interesting animal species in forest contexts, with reference to their different grazing behavior and nutritional needs.
In the integrated course on Minor Forest Productions, the two modules on Edible Mushrooms and Truffles and Apiculture aim to provide students with productive and analytical knowledge on two secondary forest products that hold significant economic importance due to their high biological activity.
The two modules on Medicinal Plants and Mountain Fruit Cultivation in the integrated course on Medicinal Plants and Mountain Fruit Cultivation allow students to acquire the necessary knowledge for the harvesting, management, and conservation of secondary forest products that are increasingly important within the forest and woodland environment.
In both curricula, an English language course is provided to familiarize students with the technical terminology of the forestry engineer profession.

Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area: The graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems will have knowledge of the eco-physiology of forest species and methods of monitoring, inventory, silvicultural treatment, and planning forest management to improve their ecological and productive functions, including secondary ones; will acquire knowledge and methods of microbiological and biochemical soil and water monitoring essential for the protection, conservation, health, and productivity of the agroforestry system; will master techniques and methodologies for territorial assessment, correct use of physical, chemical, and biological indicators, general principles of governance for adequate management and certification of forest and environmental systems, prevention of major risks, and procedures for initial civil protection interventions in extrurban areas.
The master's graduate's abilities also allow for interpreting the natural history in the characteristics of the landscape and improving the quality of life of humans, which is inseparably linked to that of the environment.
Teaching Methods and Tools:
Knowledge of methods and cultural, scientific, and professional content will be acquired through structured courses in teaching units that will progressively achieve the training objectives for the student; frontal teaching is complemented for each course with laboratory and field exercises.
Verification of the acquisition of knowledge and understanding will occur through the successful completion of intermediate assessments and final exams of the characteristic curricular courses and optional courses chosen by students.
The graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems is able to apply the knowledge acquired during the degree course for monitoring, control, design, and management of forest and environmental systems. The acquired abilities allow the use of appropriate techniques and methods for solving complex problems related to forest and environmental management.
These competencies translate into:
- ability to understand the relationships between the structure-function of biological systems and their interactions with environmental and anthropic factors;
- mastery of analytical and monitoring techniques for forest and environmental systems;
- assessment and control of land degradation processes and planning of restoration interventions for degraded and eroded soils;
- ability to design sustainable management projects for forest environmental resources;
- control of plant health and application of integrated biological pest control;
- maintenance of natural biodiversity;
- design and management of urban and peri-urban green spaces;
- landscape planning and environmental impact economic assessment;
- design and management of interventions for prevention and fire fighting, and governance for correct implementation and certification of forest and environmental systems;
- management of initial mitigation interventions for the effects of catastrophic events in rural and mountain areas.

Teaching Methods and Tools include courses structured in frontal teaching units and laboratory and field exercises with ongoing assessments of the level of knowledge and understanding achieved.
Learning verification will be carried out through the evaluation of active student participation in exercises and laboratory sessions, while theoretical acquisitions will be verified through written (multiple-choice or open-ended) or oral intermediate assessments and final exams.
Internships at public bodies or private structures are also planned for the acquisition of additional professional knowledge.
The acquired knowledge is further verified through the preparation of the final thesis.

CURRICULUM CIVIL PROTECTION. Within the theoretical lessons and practical exercises provided by the individual disciplines, students will be encouraged to actively participate, both by proposing discussion topics related to the themes addressed in thesis research, and within the design activities planned in some disciplines.
Students will acquire the fundamental methods of scientific investigation and the ability to design, manage, and disseminate interventions and processes for protecting territory from catastrophic events in extrurban areas, managing initial mitigation interventions for populations, even within the framework of international cooperation.

CURRICULUM SUSTAINABLE AGRO-FORESTAL PRODUCTIONS. Within the theoretical lessons and practical exercises, students will be encouraged to actively participate, also by proposing discussion topics related to the themes addressed in thesis research.
Students will be able to acquire, in addition to the fundamental methods of scientific investigation, the ability to design, manage, and disseminate interventions and processes for the production, harvesting, and transformation of primary and secondary products of forest and mountain environments.

Learning Verification. In all curricula, learning verification will be carried out through the evaluation of active student participation in practical exercises and laboratory sessions, while theoretical acquisitions will be verified through written (multiple-choice or open-ended) or oral intermediate assessments and final exams.
Internships at public bodies or private structures at regional, national, or international levels are also planned for the acquisition of additional professional knowledge, especially in project and management fields.
The acquired knowledge is further verified through the preparation of the final thesis.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN. Associated Competencies.

FOREST AND ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCTION TECHNICIAN. The Master's graduate in Forest and Environmental Sciences acquires, during the study course, knowledge and competencies related to the compatible management of forest and mountain territory in its biotic and abiotic components. Therefore, their professional function is to actively participate in the management and coordination of forest enterprises' activities, collaborating and coordinating in the design and management of interventions in the territory at a large scale.

Work Context Function.
FOREST AND ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCTION TECHNICIAN. The following professional profiles fall under the Master's graduate in Forest and Environmental Systems:
- surveying, classifying, analyzing, restoring, and conserving abiotic and biotic components of natural ecosystems;
- programming and managing rural territory, with particular reference to the analysis and monitoring of mountain environments and forest ecosystems;
- designing and managing parks and gardens and ecological and territorial planning;
- designing and managing works for improvement, reconstitution, and ecological restoration of degraded environments;
- designing and managing interventions for prevention and fire fighting;
- environmental impact assessment in forest and mountain areas;
- analysis, monitoring, and certification of forest and environmental system processes for the improvement of quality of life;
- designing and managing silvicultural and reforestation works;
- designing and managing facilities for wood production and transformation;
- designing and managing integrated agro-silvo-pastoral production systems;
- consulting, technical assistance, and dissemination in the forest and environmental field;
- programming and managing facilities and structures for the harvesting, transformation, and commercialization of secondary or minor forest products and marginal areas for intensive agricultural use;
- designing and managing initial interventions for rescue and mitigation of catastrophic events in rural areas.

Specific Training Objectives Description.
The Master's degree course in Forest and Environmental Systems aims to provide advanced knowledge and professional skills useful for carrying out the multiple and complex activities related to the efficient and sustainable use of natural resources, as well as monitoring, planning, design, and management of forest and environmental systems.
The Master's degree course is structured into activities aimed at developing competencies aligned with the qualifying objectives of class LM-73 Forest and Environmental Sciences and Technologies. In particular, training activities will be carried out to:
- acquire specialized knowledge of forest and environmental systems and rural and mountain territories;
- use advanced computer tools for reading and interpreting data related to mountain and rural territories;
- perform coordination functions, assume responsibility for projects and structures;
- approach the analysis of forest and environmental systems in an integrated manner, to enhance their complexity and biodiversity, within the framework of sustainable management, both in the negative effects of anthropic action possibly connected to ongoing climate change;
- perform coordination functions, assume responsibility for projects and structures for the production, transformation, and management of forest and mountain marginal areas;
- acquire the fundamental methods of scientific investigation to collaborate in experimental activities and apply knowledge to solve technical problems in the forest and environmental sector.
The Master's degree course typically lasts two years and corresponds to the acquisition of 120 CFU, including those related to the successful completion of the final exam.
The training path for each student is guided by a Tutoring Commission operating within the study course.
Teaching activities are organized on a semester basis. Possible teaching types, frontal lessons, exercises, practical and laboratory activities, seminar activities, depend on the cultural and training characteristics of the different disciplines.
The distribution of the time commitment reserved for CFU is regulated by the University's Didactic Regulations. Courses may, according to the provisions of the aforementioned Didactic Regulations, be either single-discipline or integrated.
Students can acquire freely chosen CFU by opting for any discipline offered by the University of Sassari, provided it is deemed consistent with the study course.
In the first year common to both curricula activated in this Master's degree, the planned disciplines will allow students to complete the knowledge acquired during the three-year degree. In particular:
- Forest Management (SSD AGR/05), which allows the acquisition of knowledge related to the correct management of forests, completing those of Silviculture, Dendrometry, and Forest Inventories, all of SSD AGR/05;
- Forest Mechanization (SSD AGR/09) aims to provide the necessary knowledge for the correct use of main machinery in the forest sector, as well as safety regulations for work execution;
- The three disciplines Rural Territory Planning (SSD AGR/10), Pedology and Territory Assessment (SSD AGR/14), and Environmental Impact Economic Assessment (SSD AGR/01) allow the acquisition of knowledge related to the correct planning, protection, and management of forest areas as well as marginal areas for intensive agricultural use or environmental value.
- The two modules provided in the integrated course Monitoring and Safeguarding of Forest Systems Health, Forest Entomology (SSD AGR/11), and Plant Pathology Analysis (SSD AGR/12) offer information necessary for studying, planning, and implementing phytosanitary interventions and control of entomofauna attacks in forest and environmental contexts.
In the Civil Protection curriculum, students acquire the necessary knowledge for the prevention, control, mitigation, and initial intervention in case of catastrophic events in extrurban areas, whether of natural origin or due to anthropic action.
In particular:
- The discipline Agrometeorology, Climate Change Analysis and Monitoring (SSD AGR/03) allows the acquisition of knowledge to evaluate, prevent, and mitigate the effects of climate change in the agroforestry and environmental sector;
- Fire Prevention and Control (SSD AGR/05) is aimed at knowledge of direct control and management interventions for forest fires, as well as the preparation of preventive works and regional and national regulations related to the design and management of preventive works.
- The two disciplines, Civil Protection Techniques (SSD AGR/03) and Telecommunication Systems for Civil Protection (SSD ING-INF/03) allow the acquisition of information related to initial interventions for mitigating and controlling catastrophic events in extrurban areas, as well as the preparation of effective telecommunication and information networks for population rescue.
- The integrated course Management and Assessment of Environmental Risk, in the three modules of Chemical and Environmental Management Part I (SSD AGR/13) and Part II (SSD AGR/16), allows the preparation of monitoring and control interventions for chemical and biological pollution of waters and soils, and with the module Hydrogeological Risk Assessment (SSD AGR/08), those related to the design and management of hydraulic-forest works in hilly territories.
In the Sustainable Agro-forestry Productions curriculum, the graduate acquires the necessary knowledge for the correct management, production, harvesting, and transformation of primary secondary products of forests and marginal areas for intensive agricultural use of environmental interest. In particular:
- The two disciplines Zootechnical Systems and Fauna Management (SSD AGR/19) and Forage Systems and Fauna Management (SSD AGR/02) of the integrated course Forage Systems and Zootechnical Systems allow the acquisition of information related to the agro-silvo-pastoral use of forest and marginal areas in the Mediterranean context.
- Wood and Biomass Arboriculture and Nursery Techniques, both SSD AGR/03, respectively allow the acquisition of techniques for planting and managing forest plantations primarily for high-quality timber production and the design and management of specific nurseries for the forest sector with particular reference to phytosanitary quality.
- Secondary forest products and marginal areas are increasingly assuming an important economic role in the conservation and management of forest areas.
The two disciplines Apiculture (SSD AGR/11) and Edible Mushrooms and Truffles (SSD AGR/12) of the integrated course Minor Forest Productions are aimed at knowledge of the techniques for breeding, cultivation, and transformation of these products.
In the two modules of Medicinal Plants (SSD AGR/04) and Mountain Fruit Cultivation (SSD AGR/03) of the integrated course on Medicinal Plants and Mountain Fruit Cultivation, the techniques for planting, breeding, and harvesting of herbaceous and shrub species used for the production of essences and for the planting, breeding, and management of fruit-bearing plants in hilly and mountain environments are illustrated.

Communication skills.
The master's graduate develops the ability to express concepts, interpretations, and ideas both orally and in writing by adopting deductive logic processes during the training path. They also possess fluent knowledge of at least one European language (English) in addition to Italian, enabling them to understand and transfer technical, scientific, and specialized information within the disciplinary fields characteristic of the degree. They are capable of interacting with other professionals and integrating technical-scientific knowledge with local knowledge, adapting their role to diverse work environments and themes in the rural context.
The master's graduate in Agricultural Systems, through interaction with teachers, students, and representatives of organizations and companies when voluntary internship activities are carried out—either for additional knowledge useful for entering the workforce or for preparatory activities for the final thesis—develops during the study path the ability to express and interpret ideas critically, both orally and in writing.
The verification of the acquisition of communication skills, both in written and oral form, occurs through the evaluation of reports related to laboratory activities, any intermediate tests for individual disciplines, and the preparation of the final thesis, presented orally to the graduation committee, also utilizing computer tools.
Learning abilities.
The master's graduate acquires various forms of learning organization during their study path through:
- reports in synthesized form,
- oral and written reports,
- bibliographic and informative research,
- research and laboratory techniques,
- computer processing and automated representation,
- field activities,
- etc.
This enables autonomy in the continuous learning process useful for entering the workforce and higher education.
They will have the opportunity to develop learning abilities that allow them to deepen post-graduate studies for continuous technical-professional updating, or to successfully undertake specialized courses and second-level master's programs.
The learning ability is assessed based on the individual student's academic record, particularly the grades achieved in passing exams and the time elapsed between attending the required disciplines and passing the exam, as well as through the evaluation of self-learning capabilities developed during the final project activity.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The Master's graduate in Agricultural Systems possesses methodological and interpretative knowledge that enables them to make autonomous evaluations for most of the design and management in the rural sector as specified by the declaration of competencies attributed to the agronomist by the regulations of the Order of Agronomists and Foresters.
In particular, during their educational path, the graduate acquires the necessary tools to address specific themes on topics that may vary in relevance depending on the times and environments in which they operate, thanks to both the learning of methodologies and the innovative techniques and tools useful in managing the broader agricultural environment, which will have a specificity dictated by the curriculum chosen from those proposed by the Course Council (CdS).
The verification of the acquisition of Autonomy of Judgment is carried out through the evaluation of the results achieved in both the core disciplines and the optional subjects chosen by the student, as well as through the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work individually and in groups during practical activities, as well as in the execution of the tasks assigned for the preparation of the Master's thesis.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Curriculum PRECISION AGRICULTURE The study course aims to guide the student through a path that ensures advanced-level knowledge through the study of production processes occurring in agricultural systems, providing the tools and methods for appropriate application in the management and development of innovative technologies in the operation of these systems.
The study course provides for a common first year and the division into two curricula (PRECISION AGRICULTURE, and ECO-SUSTAINABLE DEFENSE OF CROPPED PLANTS) in the second year.
The courses of the first year aim to provide students with knowledge on: the main processes of soil genesis and their classification for the evaluation of agricultural and forestry land uses; the morpho-physiological aspects, technical information, and advanced knowledge tools for understanding the response of the main herbaceous and Mediterranean fruit crops to the environment and cultivation techniques; general aspects of plant diseases and insects, damages, symptoms, epidemiology, diagnostic techniques, plant resistance mechanisms, prevention and control strategies; raw materials for the agri-food industries, the main transformation processes, and the evaluation of the qualitative characteristics of finished food products, by-products, and semi-finished goods; the fundamental principles of energy production and management in the rural sector; the main themes of agricultural policy in light of the principles underlying public choices regarding business strategies.
PRECISION AGRICULTURE - Students following the PRECISION AGRICULTURE curriculum will have the opportunity to deepen topics related to modern techniques of data collection, representation, and analysis of territorial and business data using computer tools.
Specifically, knowledge will be provided on:
- agronomic diagnostic tools for analyzing spatial and temporal variability, for site-specific agronomic management, mapping the hydrological and nutritional status of the soil, the crop status, and yields;
- optimal management of the agricultural environment, with particular reference to the use of organic and inorganic fertilizers and pesticides, and minimizing their environmental impact through the adoption of precision farming technologies;
- the most advanced techniques for automatic monitoring of the main hydrological variables of agricultural soil, analysis and modeling of hydrological dynamics regulating water availability in the soil;
- the levels of incidence of diseases and/or plant pests, determined by applying monitoring techniques or predictive mathematical models, and the main applications of information and communication technologies (ICT) to support the phytosanitary defense of agricultural crops and the protection of food products;
- the principles of territorial, landscape, and environmental planning, with particular attention to rural areas, using computer-based planning support systems (planning support systems, PSS);
- manipulation of Big Data and their analysis and modeling related to precision agri-livestock systems.
Five of the eight CFU dedicated to other training activities are used for improving the English language to a level that allows the graduate to fully understand a technical scientific text and communicate effectively orally and in writing.
Courses are structured into frontal teaching units and laboratory and field exercises, which account for approximately 30% of the teaching load of each course, with possible interim assessments on the level of knowledge and understanding achieved.
Learning verification is carried out through the evaluation of students' active participation in practical and laboratory exercises, while theoretical and practical acquisitions are verified through possible written or oral intermediate tests and final exams.

Curriculum INTEGRATED DEFENSE INTRODUCTION The study course aims to guide the student through a path that ensures advanced-level knowledge through the study of production processes occurring in agricultural systems, providing the tools and methods for appropriate application in the management and development of innovative technologies in the operation of these systems.
The study course provides for a common first year and the division into two curricula (PRECISION AGRICULTURE, INTEGRATED DEFENSE) in the second year.
The courses of the first year aim to provide students with knowledge on: the main processes of soil genesis and their classification for the evaluation of agricultural and forestry land uses; the morpho-physiological aspects, technical information, and advanced knowledge tools for understanding the response of the main herbaceous and Mediterranean fruit crops to the environment and cultivation techniques; general aspects of plant diseases and insects, damages, symptoms, epidemiology, diagnostic techniques, plant resistance mechanisms, prevention and control strategies; raw materials for the agri-food industries, the main transformation processes, and the evaluation of the qualitative characteristics of finished food products, by-products, and semi-finished goods; the fundamental principles of energy production and management in the rural sector; the main themes of agricultural policy in light of the principles underlying public choices regarding business strategies.
Students following the ECO-SUSTAINABLE DEFENSE OF CROPPED PLANTS curriculum will have the opportunity to further deepen the themes of integrated defense against plant pests and parasites in the management of herbaceous and vegetable-fruit crop systems.
Specifically, knowledge will be provided on:
- methods for sampling insect populations, the characteristics, potential, and limitations of different tools and methods for insect control, and how different control methods can be combined within modern Integrated Pest Management (IPM) concepts;
- traditional methods and strategies, and modern biotechnologies applied to the genetic improvement of cultivated plants, exploitation of genetic variability for qualitative and quantitative production improvement, and strategies for conservation and utilization of genetic resources;
- agrometeorological and micrometeorological bases as tools for system analysis and monitoring, with particular reference to tree ecosystems;
- crop cycles and techniques for cultivating vegetable-floral species in open field and protected cultivation;
- the damaging effects and control of the main animal plant parasites other than insects, defense against cryptogamic diseases in integrated and organic agriculture, control methods for the most common afflictions in nurseries and open fields, and strategies for improvement, health selection, and sanitation for certification.
Five of the eight CFU dedicated to other training activities are used for improving the English language to a level that allows the graduate to fully understand a technical scientific text and communicate effectively orally and in writing.
Courses are structured into frontal teaching units and laboratory and field exercises, which account for approximately 30% of the teaching load of each course, with possible interim assessments on the level of knowledge and understanding achieved.
Learning verification is carried out through the evaluation of students' active participation in practical and laboratory exercises, while theoretical and practical acquisitions are verified through possible written or oral intermediate tests and final exams. The educational experience offers students the opportunity to address agricultural systems' issues in a systematic and holistic manner.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Curriculum PRECISION AGRICULTURE The educational objective is to develop in the student the ability to absorb and transfer, in autonomous or group mode, innovative processes and the application of acquired project and management competencies.
The acquired critical analysis ability will enable the graduate to actively participate in multidisciplinary and even international work groups oriented towards the production, transformation, and commercialization of agricultural products. Indeed, the core, related, and integrated disciplines provided in the study plan are all characterized by high applicability in the professional field.
The graduate in Agricultural Systems will be able to apply the acquired knowledge and operate in the following areas:
- territorial planning in non-urban areas;
- design and economic and sustainable management of crops and adaptation of agricultural systems to climate change using information technologies;
- management of precision agri-livestock systems;
- food safety, their quality, wholesomeness, and specificity;
- rational use of renewable sources and the convenience of conversion technologies;
- microeconomic and institutional aspects of agricultural policy.
The graduate can also apply their knowledge and competencies by joining national and international research groups, both public and private.

The acquired critical analysis ability will enable the graduate to actively participate in multidisciplinary and even international work groups oriented towards the production, transformation, and commercialization of agricultural products. - conservation of biodiversity;
- evaluation of the importance of plant diseases and their impact on society, human and animal health, and the environment;
- food safety, their quality, wholesomeness, and specificity;
- rational use of renewable sources and the convenience of conversion technologies;
- microeconomic and institutional aspects of agricultural policy.
The graduate can also apply their knowledge and competencies by joining national and international research groups, both public and private.

Competencies Associated with the Role.
Agronomist
The typical competence areas of the Master's graduate in Agricultural Systems relate to the ability to address complex issues related to agro-ecosystems using scientific methods and technical tools. The Master's graduate possesses multidisciplinary methodological competencies in the technical-scientific field oriented towards agricultural systems, which typically follow the path of the graduate in Agricultural Sciences and Technologies.
In particular, the Master's graduate possesses knowledge and tools for programming, management, control, coordination, and training on agricultural and livestock production processes, to respond to market and consumer needs regarding product quality and safety, and sustainable management of natural resources in rural areas.
Competencies may relate to the following disciplinary areas:
- Food and non-food agricultural productions
- Sustainable management of soil fertility
- Phytosanitary defense and food products
- Agricultural engineering
- Political-economic guidelines in the agricultural sector
- Food technologies.
Additionally, the graduate will have acquired the following transversal competencies: communication, working in groups, problem solving, work organization, and flexibility.

Role in the Workplace Context.
Agronomist
The Master's graduate possesses the necessary competencies to access the following professional roles:
- free practice of agronomist and forester, to which the Master's graduate can access after passing the qualification exam;
- public or private services for rural development and environmental and territorial protection;
- professional studies, consulting, service companies, and laboratories operating in the design and management of agricultural production systems, agri-food industry, environmental and territorial management and protection, environmental monitoring and recovery;
- technician at professional studies and companies operating in the management and disposal of effluents, environmental remediation, realization and maintenance of green areas, and soil defense works and interventions;
- training and education activities for public and private educational institutions, for technical assistance bodies in agriculture;
- consultancy, assistance, and dissemination to agricultural and agro-industrial enterprises in the sectors of vegetable productions, plant defense, and quality control of agricultural products;
- direction and management of single and associated agricultural enterprises;
- environmental protection and biodiversity conservation;
- technical consultancy on sustainable rural development in national and international contexts.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's degree course in Agricultural Systems (SA) aims to train professionals with advanced-level preparation capable of designing, managing, evaluating, and certifying systems and processes of agricultural production. In the indicated specialization areas, particular attention is given to the ability to address and manage complex problems of agricultural systems, also related to specific territorial and environmental contexts, using methodologies and equipment that involve the use of innovative technologies through the employment of computer tools.
The basic preparation is preparatory to the acquisition of advanced knowledge to form professionals capable of using a wide range of tools and knowledge to address all aspects and relationships that interact in determining the issues associated with sustainable development in the rural sector.
The Master's degree course aims to complete the basic preparation acquired in the three-year degree, with specialized teaching courses that offer the student a systemic perspective of the agroecosystem, agri-food and agro-industrial supply chains, and the tools to effectively contextualize projects and sustainable development policies in the rural sector.

Description of the Educational Path.
The Master's degree course in Agricultural Systems provides for the acquisition of 120 university credit units (CFU) and a duration of two years. It is structured into 11 passing exams and concludes with a final exam, which can be held even before the end of the final year of the course. The Study Course, through the Teaching Committee and the Tutoring Committee, provides assistance and guidance to help students complete the educational path appropriately.
The Master's degree course includes single-discipline and integrated courses. Training activities will be organized on a semester basis and will include various types (frontal lessons, exercises, practical activities, laboratories, seminar activities, internship), depending on the cultural and educational characteristics of each course.
The distribution of the time commitment reserved for each CFU is regulated by the Department's Teaching Regulations, as are the minimum required attendance hours to take the passing exams of the courses.
For the evaluation of the achievement of the expected learning objectives, interim tests may be provided in addition to the final exam; the tests may be written, oral, and/or practical.
For training activities related to language knowledge and other activities useful for entering the workforce, a maximum of 12 CFU must be acquired, of which at least 5 CFU are reserved for the English language. The possession of knowledge related to other training activities useful for entering the workforce is verified - without a grade - by a specific committee appointed by the CCS or the CCS itself.
The student can acquire the 14 CFU of their choice by selecting any course offered by the University of Sassari, provided it is consistent with the study path.
The courses of the first year aim to provide students with knowledge on: the evaluation of soil uses; cultivation techniques and response to the environment of the main herbaceous and Mediterranean fruit crops; prevention and control strategies against biotic agents; the main transformation processes of agri-food products; production and management of energy in the rural sector; the main themes of agricultural policy.
For the second year, the course provides for the activation of two curricula oriented towards:
- knowledge of topics related to modern techniques of data collection, representation, and analysis of territorial and business data using computer tools;
- management of crop systems, herbaceous and vegetable-fruit, with particular attention to the themes of protection from parasites and plant pests through the principles of integrated defense.
The Master's degree course in Agricultural Systems provides a sufficient number of CFU (25) for the final exam, which involves the execution of an experimental research that serves as a prerequisite for the final thesis. The objective of this path is the development of specific competencies in the design, management, and completion of an experimental research project, which also provides the graduate with the opportunity to gain work experience in a research group.
The educational path has therefore been designed with the objective of offering the Master's graduate the opportunity to integrate technical knowledge, scientific method, systemic vision of problems in the rural and environmental field, and concrete field experiences, drawing on the basic and methodological knowledge acquired in the three-year degree.

Final Exam Characteristics. The Master's Degree in Animal Production Sciences is obtained by passing a final exam, consisting of the presentation and discussion of the thesis, written by the student under the guidance of a supervisor professor, before a committee of professors. The Master's thesis is a written document, structured according to the lines of a scientific publication, prepared by the student under the supervision of a supervisor and concerning an original scientific experience, related to the topics of the degree course in Animal Production Sciences and regarding a characteristic topic of the study course.

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences possesses high analytical and critical evaluation skills within various agro-animal systems, programming, management, and control of production processes aimed at improving the quality of animal productions, economic management of the animal production enterprise, including energy issues and eco-compatibility.
Acquisition of judgment autonomy is verified through evaluation of the student's study plan courses and assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work in groups during activities assigned for the final exam preparation.

Learning Ability.
The Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences possesses adequate preparation for deepening and updating knowledge within the professional sector, innovative technologies, and scientific research.
Learning ability is verified through analysis of the individual student's career regarding exam grades and the time elapsed between attending a course and passing the exam, as well as assessment of self-learning capabilities developed during the final exam-related activities.

Knowledge and Understanding.
DISCIPLINES OF THE TECHNOLOGICAL MACROAREA The disciplines taught in this macroarea provide the Master's graduate with knowledge and tools for understanding:
1. Use, management, and development of innovative technologies in the animal production sector, with particular reference to animal nutrition, genetic improvement, management, quality, and sustainability of productions;
2. Production, quality, and transformation of animal-origin products, energy management, and eco-compatibility of the animal production enterprise;
3. Production and conservation of animal feeds using advanced agronomic, entomological, and pathological techniques. Expected learning outcomes are achieved through attendance of theoretical courses, combined with practical exercises and internship activities, integrated with individual study and possible tutoring activities.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through final exams for individual courses and possible in-course assessments.
Assessments may be written, oral, and/or practical.

DISCIPLINES OF THE ECONOMIC-PROJECT MACROAREA INTRODUCTION The training path for the Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences is characterized by disciplines that promote an integrated approach to understanding production processes in the animal production sector. These disciplines can be grouped into two macroareas: Technological and Economic-Project.

- DISCIPLINES OF THE ECONOMIC-PROJECT MACROAREA -
The disciplines taught in this macroarea provide the Master's graduate with knowledge and tools for understanding:
1. Design, technological control, and improvement of production processes in the feed and supplement industry;
2. Design, technological control, and improvement of production processes for obtaining mass-market products, traditional and/or typical foods, and functional foods;
3. Quality process and product certification in animal and fish supply chains, respecting animal welfare and environmental sustainability;
4. Economics, market dynamics, marketing, and planning of the animal production sector;
5. Design and sizing of animal production facilities. Expected learning outcomes are achieved through attendance of theoretical courses with practical purposes and internship activities, supported by individual study and possible tutoring activities.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through final exams for individual courses and possible in-course assessments.
Assessments may be written, oral, and/or practical.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
DISCIPLINES OF THE TECHNOLOGICAL MACROAREA The knowledge and understanding of processes acquired through disciplines organized in the two macroareas will provide the Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences with the ability to apply:
1. Critical evaluation of fundamental relationships between structure, physiology, genetic improvement, nutrition, and breeding technologies and production processes in various animal production sectors, including aquaculture;
2. Identification of necessary methodologies for developing innovative, sustainable production processes for obtaining mass-market, traditional, typical, and functional foods;
3. Management and control of breeding technologies for species of interest in animal production;
4. Development of methodologies for achieving quality and process certification in various animal production supply chains;
5. Economic management and organizational strategies of the animal production enterprise, as well as marketing of animal feeds and animal-origin products;
6. Design of facilities for production and transformation of animal-origin products;
7. Evaluation and management of the eco-compatibility of the animal production enterprise.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding is verified through final exams for individual courses and possible in-course assessments. Assessments may be written, oral, and/or practical.

DISCIPLINES OF THE ECONOMIC-PROJECT MACROAREA The knowledge and understanding of processes acquired through disciplines organized in the two macroareas will provide the Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences with the ability to apply:
1. Critical evaluation of fundamental relationships between structure, physiology, genetic improvement, nutrition, and breeding technologies and production processes in various animal production sectors, including aquaculture;
2. Identification of necessary methodologies for developing innovative production processes for obtaining mass-market, traditional, typical, and functional foods;
3. Management and control of breeding technologies for species of interest in animal production;
4. Development of methodologies for achieving quality and process certification in various animal production supply chains;
5. Economic management and organizational strategies of the animal production enterprise, as well as marketing of animal feeds and animal-origin products;
6. Design of facilities for production and transformation of animal-origin products;
7. Evaluation and management of the eco-compatibility of the animal production enterprise.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding is verified through final exams for individual courses and possible in-course assessments. Assessments may be written, oral, and/or practical.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Associated Competencies.
Generic Profile The competencies of the Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences will enable them in the workplace to integrate various tools for improving the quantitative and qualitative aspects of productions of major terrestrial and aquatic animal species of interest in animal production, such as genetic improvement, nutrition, and breeding technologies; to develop innovative production processes, manage and control breeding technologies for species of interest in wildlife and hunting; to develop and apply methodologies for quality and process certification in various animal production supply chains; to implement economic planning and management of the animal production enterprise, as well as marketing of its products; to design facilities for production and transformation of animal-origin products; to evaluate and manage the eco-compatibility of the animal production enterprise.

Work Context Function.
Generic Profile The professional activity of the Master's graduate in Animal Production Sciences primarily takes place in agro-animal enterprises, feed industries, transformation industries of animal products, public and private bodies conducting planning, analysis, control, and certification activities, as well as those conducting scientific research for the protection and valorization of agro-animal productions, research bodies, training and technical assistance bodies, studies offices, and in free profession. In these work contexts, the graduate in Animal Production Sciences may perform tasks of group coordination, management of production structures, and interact with other professional figures such as veterinarians, chemists, economists, and engineers.

Specific Training Objectives Description.
The study course in Animal Production Sciences aims to provide specialized knowledge and skills for managing, designing, and technologically controlling production and quality processes in the supply chain of various animal productions, including aquaculture.
The study course is oriented towards training a versatile professional figure with broad employment opportunities, possessing advanced competencies in various animal production sectors (genetic improvement, animal nutrition and feeding, feed industry, breeding techniques, modeling of animal production processes and systems), agricultural engineering (design and sizing of animal production facilities), agronomy (herbaceous and forage crops), agricultural economics (economic policies and market dynamics of animal productions), food transformation and safety, environmental impact of livestock, and veterinary prophylaxis.
The graduate's activity is oriented: towards continuous quantitative and qualitative improvement of production processes for obtaining high-quality, safe animal feeds and animal-origin products, as well as functional foods and products; towards quality process and product certification in animal and fish supply chains; towards optimization of production and transformation of animal feeds and animal-origin products; towards eco-compatible energy management of the animal and agro-animal enterprise; towards economics, economic policies, and marketing of the animal production sector; towards economic, social, and environmental sustainability of animal production activities. Professional activity takes place in various agro-animal systems and enterprises connected to animal and fish production supply chains, in quality and/or typicality production consortia, in protected areas, and in public and private bodies.

Training Path Description.
The Master's Degree in Animal Production Sciences requires the acquisition of 120 university credit points (CFU) over a two-year duration. It is structured into 11 exams and concludes with a final exam, which may be taken before the end of the second year of study. Each student's training path will be guided by a tutoring committee operating within the study course.
The Master's Degree includes single-discipline courses and integrated courses. Training activities will be organized on a semester basis and will include various types (frontal lessons, exercises, practical activities, laboratories, seminar activities, internship), depending on the cultural and training characteristics of individual courses.
The allocation of weekly hours for each CFU is regulated by the Department's Teaching Regulations, as well as the minimum required attendance hours to take profit exams.
For the assessment of achieved learning objectives, in addition to the final exam, one or more in-course assessments may be scheduled; assessments may be written, oral, and/or practical.
For training activities related to language knowledge, telematic skills, internship experiences, or other activities useful for entering the workforce, 10 CFU (total) are required. Possession of knowledge related to these training activities is verified—without a merit grade—by a dedicated committee appointed by the CCS or the CCS itself.
Students may acquire the 12 CFU of free choice by selecting, with the assistance of a tutor, any course offered by the University of Sassari.

Final exam characteristics.
The final exam consists of writing and subsequent discussion of a written thesis, with an applied-experimental character. In particular, the degree in Quality and Safety of Food Products is obtained by passing a final exam, consisting of the discussion of a written thesis, prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor, before a committee of professors. The thesis, of an experimental and/or applied nature, will be related to the activities carried out by the student during the internship or will relate to the in-depth study of other topics covered during the course of study. These activities, starting from a concise but comprehensive study and in-depth analysis of the current state of the art, may concern the following points, possibly integrated:
- monitoring and critical evaluation of one or more processes or activities in the agro-food sector, including control systems and related management software;
- technical-economic design of agro-food production activities or part of them and/or specific innovative interventions in processes and/or products;
- evaluation of the physical-sensory and food aspects of traditional and/or innovative agro-food products, related or not to specific market analyses and studies aimed at implementing and/or developing new evaluation methodologies;
- microbiological and biotechnological evaluations and innovations applied and/or to be applied along the agro-food production chain, including specific microbiological analyses and evaluations;
- analysis, critical evaluation, and possible implementation or design interventions for the assurance and management of food safety and quality systems and related production processes.
The evaluation of the final exam will follow the criteria established by the Department of Agraria's teaching regulations, with any specific integrations of the Course's teaching regulations.
Required knowledge for admission.
The first-level and master's degrees admitted for enrollment in this Master's Degree are those belonging to the classes: L-27 (Chemical and Technology Sciences), L-26 (Agro-Food Sciences and Technologies), L-25 (Agricultural and Forestry Sciences and Technologies), L-2 (Biotechnology), L13 Biological Sciences, L29 Pharmaceutical Sciences and Technologies, L38 Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Production Technologies, LM-86 (Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Technologies), LM-71 (Industrial Chemistry Sciences and Technologies), LM-69 (Agricultural Sciences and Technologies), LM-8 (Industrial Biotechnology), LM-7 (Agrarian Biotechnology), LM9 Medical, Veterinary, and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, LM13 Pharmacy and Industrial Pharmacy, LM54 Chemical Sciences, LM61 Human Nutrition Sciences.
The initial knowledge of candidates will be verified by a special committee and will concern:
- Principles of Mathematics and Physics.
- General and Organic Chemistry.
- Fundamental Principles of Primary Production (vegetable and animal).
- Unit Operations of Food Technologies.
- Main Agro-Food Industries and Food Microbiology.
- Fundamental Principles of Chemistry and Food Analysis;
- English.
At the time of enrollment in the Master's Degree, the student must have already acquired at least 10 ECTS in English (L-LIN/12) or have a language certification at B1 level or higher.
By June of each year, the admission and knowledge verification procedures will be published.

Communication skills.
The graduate is able to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with peers and those with lower educational or functional levels, also using a European Union language other than their own, typically English, within the specific disciplinary context. They are also capable of communicating effectively, both orally and in writing, with higher professional functions, presenting results obtained, innovative ideas, and the current state of ongoing projects. They are able to interact with people outside productive realities, collaborate, and adapt to different work environments and topics. The acquisition of communication skills, both written and oral, will be verified through the evaluation of laboratory activities, in-course assessments for individual disciplines, and the written reports prepared for the end of the practical internship and the final exam, which will be presented orally to the graduation committee.
Specific communication skills will be stimulated and verified through the organization of specific multidisciplinary technical-scientific, economic, and ethical group work, as well as through support provided for drafting and subsequent evaluation of the internship report and final exam (thesis).
Learning abilities.
The main professional competence areas that students will acquire are primarily related to the following areas: food technology and biotechnology processes; mastery of the scientific method and capacity to transfer knowledge to practical implementation in enterprises; optimization and management of production processes in food industries; design and management of quality and safety systems using innovative methodologies; execution of complex coordination and direction activities related to the sector; design and management of machinery and plants used in food production processes; evaluation of physical and sensory aspects of food; management of enterprises and agri-food supply chains; communication, multidisciplinary group work, and judgment capabilities both on technical-economic and human-ethical levels; fluent use of English (at least B2 level). These knowledge areas, interacting synergistically with each other and with the guidance of teachers involved over time, provide advanced cognitive tools essential for continuous updating of sector knowledge, also using new communication and information technology tools, to finalize the training path towards solving the multiple practical problems of the entire agri-food production chain. Graduates will have developed learning abilities that enable them to continue studies in specific sector specializations, in second-level master's programs, in research doctorate courses, and/or to directly enter the workforce with a proactive approach. Learning abilities will be assessed through analysis of the individual student's academic record regarding exam grades and the time elapsed between attending a course and passing the exam, as well as through evaluation of self-learning capabilities developed during the practical internship and final exam activities.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari

TYPE: Master's Degree
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment

Autonomy of Judgment.
At the end of the studies, the graduate will have the ability to compare and discuss experimental results and to draft appropriate checkpoint and final reports, presenting them in concise and/or detailed work documents, as well as orally presenting the aforementioned results. They will have the ability to retrieve and evaluate sources of general and in-depth technical-scientific information, data, and scientific literature, useful for improving the safety, quality, effectiveness, and efficiency of food production, also in terms of environmental sustainability, circular economy, and bio-based economy. The verification of the acquisition of autonomy of judgment will occur through the evaluation of the outcomes achieved in the core disciplines and in the optional subjects chosen by the student, as well as through the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work individually and in groups during the practical activities carried out in each course and the practical application internship, as well as in the execution of the assigned activity in preparation for the final thesis.
The teaching organization stimulates students to adopt a proactive approach, characterized by a high degree of autonomy (in choices, critical learning, and study organization).
Knowledge and Understanding.
Process Controls: Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of food technology production processes and process and product controls through the following expected learning outcomes: basic tools for modeling and analysis of automation systems for automatic controls in food industries, including specification analysis, system project management, and in-depth study of major management software.
The teaching activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are attributable to the courses “Food Industry Control Systems” (Training Path A) or “Principles of Food Technologies: Unit Operations and Processes” (Training Path B) and “Technologies and Applied Biotechnology”; as well as to the “Practical Application Internship” and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the “Final Thesis” (Master’s Thesis).
Food Product Merchandising and Marketing: Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the basic tools of merchandising and a deeper understanding of food merchandising, knowledge of the different sectors of the agri-food industries, and various product marketing strategies, as well as the evaluation of product placement on national, European, and international markets. Particular attention will be given to marketing analysis: consumer behavior, market and competitor analysis, innovation, and the launch of new products.
The teaching activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course “Food Product Merchandising and Marketing” as well as to the “Practical Application Internship” and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the “Final Thesis” (Master’s Thesis).
Food Sciences: Students will acquire a general overview of the main concepts, methods, and basic tools used for evaluating foods and their nutritional principles to be included in a diet, with particular reference to different physiological conditions.
The teaching activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course “Food Sciences” as well as to the “Practical Application Internship” and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the “Final Thesis” (Master’s Thesis).
Applied Biotechnology in Food Production: Students will acquire the necessary knowledge for designing and managing bioprocesses as a fundamental aspect of food quality; innovations aimed at promoting a solid economic activity; tools for managing food safety and improving food quality from a microbiological perspective, with particular reference to controlling factors regulating microbial growth, metabolic activity, and selection in food ecosystems.
The teaching activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are attributable to the courses “Advanced Microbial Biotechnology for Food Production” and “Technologies and Applied Biotechnology”; as well as to the “Practical Application Internship” and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the “Final Thesis” (Master’s Thesis).
Food Evaluation: Students will acquire theoretical, practical knowledge, and the most suitable tools to characterize a food product; knowledge of the main physical analyses and different sensory methodologies will provide students with the necessary tools to evaluate foods both for company quality control and for the identity of the products themselves; by the end of the course, students will have acquired basic and advanced knowledge on the role of physical and sensory analyses in evaluating the quality characteristics of food products.
The teaching activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course “Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods” and partially further explored in the practical course “Technologies and Applied Biotechnology” as well as during the “Practical Application Internship” and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the “Final Thesis” (Master’s Thesis).
Food Safety and Quality: Students will achieve an appropriate knowledge regarding the application of mandatory and voluntary standards for the certification of safety and quality in food industries, including the implementation of official food controls; process and product certification, analytical and documentary traceability, HACCP and the relevant analytical methods applicable to quality and safety control of foods; the general framework of the European system for controlling food products. Students will also have the opportunity to be qualified, upon completion of a 40-hour module, as a “Lead Auditor” for self-control systems (HACCP) and quality management.
The teaching activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are attributable to the courses “Food Safety and Quality 1,” “Food Safety and Quality 2,” “Technologies and Applied Biotechnology”; as well as to the “Practical Application Internship” and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the “Final Thesis” (Master’s Thesis).
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Process Controls: Students will acquire the skills to apply, throughout the entire agri-food production chain, the practical aspects of the learned knowledge, summarized in the following expected learning outcomes: familiarity with the use of production process control systems; mastery of principles for the online, in-line, and off-line application of control systems; application of the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of the agri-food sector's production processes.
Food Product Merchandising and Marketing: Students will acquire the skills to utilize knowledge regarding food product merchandising regulations, control bodies, and product labeling; marketing strategies, also through the evaluation of consumer opinions; identification of target audiences for traditional and innovative food products; application of the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of the agri-food sector's production processes and related products.
Food Sciences: Students will acquire the necessary capabilities for evaluating food and nutritional aspects, aimed at correct product labeling and effective communication strategies to consumers. They will also be able to identify product innovation strategies targeting specific consumer groups (e.g., celiac, vegetarian, etc.) and/or specific dietary needs (e.g., high-fiber foods, probiotic foods, vitaminized foods, etc.). Students will also be able to apply the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of the agri-food sector's production processes and related products.
Applied Biotechnology in Food Production: Students will acquire a critical perspective on the potential of microbial biotechnology and predictive microbiology in the food sector and will be able to interpret data, develop ideas, and design innovations both in the production of fermented foods and in the microbiological control of foods. They will also be able to design and propose the application of specific innovative biotechnological techniques in production processes and evaluate their practical effectiveness. Students will also be able to apply the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of the agri-food sector's production processes and related products.
Food Evaluation: Students will acquire an advanced understanding of the potential offered by the use of appropriate techniques for sensory evaluation of foods. They will also be able to design and manage specific panel tests aimed at discriminative and descriptive evaluations, and critically and appropriately assess the results obtained, thanks to specialized software for data management and evaluation. Students will also be able to apply the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of the agri-food sector's production processes and related products.
Food Safety and Quality: Students will acquire specific capabilities for designing and implementing the main quality management systems (ISO 9000, BRC, IFS, etc.) and food safety (GMP, GHP, HACCP); designing, conducting, and evaluating audits; using acquired knowledge for a comprehensive evaluation of the agri-food sector's production processes and related products, considering multiple aspects of production controls, nutritional and sensory evaluations, biotechnological innovations, marketing strategies, etc.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages: ITALIANO
Associated Competencies for the Role.
Food Technologist and Researcher in the field of food production technologies and biotechnology.
Ability to design and intervene, both at the operational and training levels, in the management of resources, materials, and personnel for production processes and the transformation of food products, from raw materials to semi-finished products to finished products. Ability to develop product innovations, new food products, and innovations in existing production processes.
Production and Line Manager
Management, control, and operation capabilities of equipment and food processing and related product processes. Direct, manage, and administer companies operating in the production, transformation, preservation, distribution, and marketing of food.
Production Control Manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products)
Ability to evaluate and control production processes and food product analyses. In particular, regarding the verification and control of requirements and specifications for: food raw materials, finished products, additives, technological aids, semi-finished products, packaging, and anything related to the production and transformation of food products, as well as the definition of standards and specifications for the aforementioned products.
Expert in Managing Food Safety and Quality Systems and “Lead Auditor”
Ability to assess the level achieved by safety and quality systems in pre-inspection verification and audit, as well as to directly interact during external audit visits and inspection visits with the specific team of expert evaluators entrusted with conducting the aforementioned controls at the company.
Role in Work Context.
Food Technologist and Researcher in the field of food production technologies and biotechnology.
Programming, management, control, coordination, and training regarding the production, preservation, transformation, distribution, and serving of food and beverages. Management of resources, materials, and personnel, aimed at the continuous improvement of food products in economic terms, food safety, and quality, with particular attention to ensuring sustainability, circular economy, and bio-based economy. Research and development of processes and products.
Production and Line Manager
Management, control, and operation of equipment, even complex, and food processing and related product processes. Direct and manage companies operating in the production, transformation, preservation, distribution, and marketing of food.
Production Control Manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products)
Responsibility for verifying safety, quality, and quantity parameters of food raw materials, semi-finished products, finished products, additives, technological aids, packaging materials, and anything related to the production and transformation of food products, as well as defining standards and specifications for the aforementioned products.
Expert in Managing Food Safety and Quality Systems and “Lead Auditor”
Design, management, and continuous improvement of food safety production systems (GMP, GHP, HACCP) and quality management systems. Management of internal audits aimed at pre-evaluating certified assessments within the production environment.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
In the first year, within the front-facing teaching activities, at least 30% of practical activities will be included; additionally, the course will include a series of activities conducted through educational visits to food industries. The second year will be entirely dedicated to practical and highly professionalizing activities carried out within the cooperating food industries. These activities will be developed through a Practical Application Internship (specialized) and an additional research and experimentation activity for the preparation of the thesis. The second-year teaching activities will be planned, managed, and carried out in close collaboration with food industries.
The educational objectives of the Master’s program primarily focus on training an expert in food technologies, with particular reference to professional competencies related to food safety and quality.
The educational objectives of the Master’s program primarily include eleven areas of professional competencies that students must acquire:
1. Possess a solid knowledge of food processes, technologies, and biotechnology (reference: entrance test and first-level degree);
2. Possess a solid basic cultural preparation and a good mastery of the scientific method, with particular reference to the ability to transfer knowledge to practical implementation in enterprises (reference: Practical Application Internship activities and final thesis);
3. Possess a high capacity to optimize food industry production processes and manage specific organizational and control aspects (reference: Food Industry Control Systems, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
4. Be an expert in managing and promoting food safety and quality, even in compliance with regulations on operator safety and environmental protection (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
5. Possess high technical and practical skills for quality and food safety control, also using innovative methodologies (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Starter Management and Predictive Microbiology, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Food Sciences, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
6. Have adequate professional knowledge and skills for complex coordination and direction activities in the agri-food sector (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Starter Management and Predictive Microbiology, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Food Sciences, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
7. Possess knowledge and professional skills in designing and managing machinery and equipment used in food processing and transformation processes (reference: entrance test and first-level degree, Food Industry Control Systems, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
8. Possess advanced knowledge on the sensory and nutritional evaluation of main foods, as well as the main applicable methodologies and strategies, also to assess consumer opinions (reference: Food Sciences, Food Product Merchandising and Marketing, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods);
9. Possess advanced skills in managing companies, agri-food supply chains, and consulting and service companies connected to them (reference: Food Product Merchandising and Marketing, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
10. Have developed personal abilities in communication, multidisciplinary group work, and judgment both on technical-economic and human-ethical levels (reference: specific workshops and group work, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
11. Be able to fluently use at least one European Union language in addition to Italian, both in written and oral form, with reference to disciplinary terminology (reference: entrance test and first-level degree).
