These activities, starting from a concise but comprehensive study and in-depth analysis of the current state of the art, may concern the following points, possibly integrated:
- Monitoring and critical evaluation of one or more processes or production activities in the agro-food sector, including control systems and related management software;
- Technical-economic design of agro-food production activities or part of them and/or specific innovative process and/or product interventions;
- Evaluation of physical-sensory and food aspects of traditional and/or innovative agro-food products, related or not to specific market analysis and studies aimed at implementing and/or developing new evaluation methodologies;
- Microbiological and biotechnological evaluations and innovations applied and/or to be applied along the agro-food production chain, including specific microbiological analyses and evaluations;
- Analysis, critical evaluation, and possible implementation or design interventions for systems ensuring and managing the safety and quality of agro-food products and their production processes.
The evaluation of the final exam will follow the criteria established by the Didactic Regulations of the Department of Agraria, with possible specific integrations of the Didactic Regulations of the Study Program.
Required knowledge for admission.
The first-level and Master's degrees admitted for enrollment in this Master's Degree are those belonging to the classes: L-27 (Chemical Sciences and Technologies), L-26 (Agro-Food Sciences and Technologies), L-25 (Agricultural and Forestry Sciences and Technologies), L-2 (Biotechnology), L13 Biological Sciences, L29 Pharmaceutical Sciences and Technologies, L38 Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Production Technologies, LM-86 (Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Technologies), LM-71 (Industrial Chemistry Sciences and Technologies), LM-69 (Agricultural Sciences and Technologies), LM-8 (Industrial Biotechnology), LM-7 (Agrarian Biotechnology), LM9 Medical, Veterinary and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, LM13 Pharmacy and Industrial Pharmacy, LM54 Chemical Sciences, LM61 Human Nutrition Sciences.
The initial knowledge of candidates will be verified by a dedicated committee and will concern:
- Principles of Mathematics and Physics.
- General and Organic Chemistry.
- Fundamental Principles of Primary Production (plants and animals).
- Unit Operations of Food Technologies.
- Main Agro-Food Industries and Food Microbiology.
- Fundamental Principles of Chemistry and Food Analysis;
- English.
For admission to the Master's Degree program, students must have already acquired at least 10 CFU in English (L-LIN/12) or hold a language certification at B1 level or higher.
By the end of June each year, the admission procedures and verification methods for the required knowledge will be published.
Expected career opportunities and professional roles for graduates.
Food Technologist and researcher in the field of food production technologies and biotechnologies.
Career opportunities are available in food industries and all companies connected to the production, transformation, preservation, and distribution of food products, in Large Scale Distribution companies, in public and private bodies conducting research and development activities in the agro-food sector. Study offices and self-employment (the training of a graduate in Food Science and Technology qualifies them to take the exams for professional certification as Food Technologist and Agronomist).
Production and line manager in food industries and all companies connected to the production, transformation, preservation, and distribution of food products, as well as in Large Scale Distribution companies.
Production control manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products)
Food industries and all companies connected to the production, transformation, preservation, and distribution of food products, in Large Scale Distribution companies, in public and private bodies conducting planning, analysis, control activities, as well as those conducting scientific investigations for the protection and enhancement of food production, in training bodies.
Expert in managing food safety and quality systems and "Lead-auditor"
Career opportunities are available in food industries and all companies connected to the production, transformation, preservation, and distribution of food products, in Large Scale Distribution companies, in public and private bodies conducting planning, analysis, control, certification activities, as well as those conducting scientific investigations for the protection and enhancement of food production, in training bodies, study offices, and self-employment. It will also be possible to access training courses for second-party audits (second level, external audits) and subsequently for third-party audits (third level, certification body).

Communication Skills.
The graduate is able to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with peers and those with lower educational or functional levels, also using a European Union language other than their own, typically English, within the specific disciplinary context. They are also capable of communicating effectively, both orally and in writing, with higher professional functions, presenting results obtained, innovative ideas, and the current state of ongoing projects. They are able to interact with people outside productive realities, collaborate, and adapt to different work environments and topics. The acquisition of communication skills, both written and oral, will be verified through the evaluation of laboratory activities, in-course assessments for individual disciplines, and the written reports prepared for the end of the practical internship and the final examination, which will be presented orally to the graduation committee.
Specific communication skills will be stimulated and verified through the organization of specific multidisciplinary technical-scientific, economic, and ethical group works, as well as through support provided for drafting and subsequent evaluation of the internship report and final examination (thesis).
Learning Ability.
The main professional competence areas that students will acquire are primarily related to the following areas: food technology and biotechnology processes; mastery of the scientific method and capacity to transfer knowledge to practical implementation in companies; optimization and management of production processes in food industries; design and management of quality and safety systems using innovative methodologies; execution of complex coordination and direction activities related to the sector; design and management of machinery and plants used in food production processes; evaluation of physical and sensory aspects of food; management of businesses and agri-food supply chains; communication, multidisciplinary group work, and ability to judge both on technical-economic and human-ethical levels; fluent use of English (at least B2 level). These knowledge areas, interacting synergistically with each other and thanks to the stimulation provided by teachers involved at each stage, provide advanced cognitive tools essential for continuous updating of sector knowledge, also using new communication and information technologies, to finalize the training path towards solving the multiple practical problems of the entire agri-food production chain. Graduates will have developed learning abilities that allow them to continue studies in specific sector specializations, in second-level master's programs, in research doctorates, or to directly enter the workforce with a proactive approach. Learning ability will be assessed through analysis of the individual student's academic record regarding exam grades and the time elapsed between attending a course and passing the exam, as well as through evaluation of self-learning capabilities developed during practical internship activities and the final examination.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A103] QUALITY AND SAFETY OF FOOD PRODUCTS
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Judgment Autonomy
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10797?annoOrdinamento=2019

Judgment Autonomy.
Upon completion of studies, the graduate will have the ability to compare and discuss experimental results and draft appropriate checkpoint and final reports, presenting them in concise and/or detailed work documents, as well as orally presenting the aforementioned results. They will have the ability to retrieve and evaluate sources of general information and in-depth technical-scientific data, scientific literature, useful for improving the safety, quality, effectiveness, and efficiency of food production, also in terms of environmental sustainability, circular economy, and bio-based economy. The verification of the acquisition of judgment autonomy will occur through the evaluation of the outcomes achieved in the core disciplines and in the optional subjects chosen by the student, as well as through the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work individually and in groups during practical activities carried out during each course and the practical internship, as well as in the execution of the assigned activity in preparation for the final exam. The teaching organization encourages students to adopt a proactive approach, characterized by a high degree of autonomy (in decision-making, critical learning, and study organization).

Knowledge and Understanding.
Process Controls
Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of food technology production processes and process and product controls through the following expected learning outcomes: basic tools for modeling and analysis of automation systems for automatic controls in food industries, including specification analysis, system project management, and in-depth study of major management software. The training activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are attributable to the courses "Control Systems in Food Industries" (Training Path A) or "Principles of Food Technologies: Unit Operations and Processes" (Training Path B) and "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies"; as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).

Food Merchandising and Marketing
Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the basic tools of merchandising and more in-depth knowledge of food merchandising, knowledge of different sectors of the agri-food industries and various product marketing strategies, as well as the evaluation of product placement on national, European, and international markets. Particular attention will be given to marketing analysis: consumer behavior, market and competitor analysis, innovation, and launching new products. The training activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course "Food Merchandising and Marketing" as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).

Food Sciences
Students will acquire a general overview of the main concepts, methods, and basic tools used for evaluating foods and their nutritional principles to be included in a diet, with particular reference to different physiological conditions. The training activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course "Food Sciences" as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).

Applied Biotechnology in Food Production
Students will acquire the necessary knowledge for designing and managing bioprocesses as a fundamental aspect of food quality; innovations aimed at promoting a solid economic activity; tools for managing food safety and improving food quality from a microbiological perspective, with particular reference to controlling factors regulating microbial growth, metabolic activity, and selection in food ecosystems. The training activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are attributable to the courses "Advanced Microbial Biotechnology for Food Production" and "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies"; as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).

Food Evaluation
Students will acquire theoretical, practical knowledge, and the most suitable tools for characterizing a food product; knowledge of the main physical analyses and different sensory methodologies will provide students with the necessary tools to evaluate foods both for company quality control and for product identity; by the end of the course, students will have acquired basic and advanced knowledge on the role of physical and sensory analyses in evaluating the quality characteristics of food products. The training activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are primarily attributable to the course "Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods" and partially further explored in the practical course "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies" as well as during the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).

Food Safety and Quality
Students will achieve appropriate knowledge regarding the application of mandatory and voluntary standards for certifying safety and quality in food industries, including the implementation of official food controls; process and product certification, analytical and documentary traceability, HACCP and applicable analytical methods for quality and safety control of foods; the general framework of the European system for controlling food products. Students will also have the opportunity to be qualified, upon completion of a 40-hour module, as "lead auditor" for self-control systems (HACCP) and quality management. The training activities that achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes are attributable to the courses "Food Safety and Quality 1," "Food Safety and Quality 2," "Applied Technologies and Biotechnologies"; as well as to the "Practical Application Internship" and, if chosen as an area of in-depth study, during the "Final Exam" (thesis).

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Process Controls
Students will acquire the skills to apply, throughout the entire agri-food production chain, the practical aspects of the knowledge gained, summarized in the following expected learning outcomes: familiarity with using production process control systems; mastery of principles for applying online, in-line, and off-line control systems; application of the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of agri-food sector production processes.

Food Merchandising and Marketing
Students will acquire the skills to utilize knowledge regarding the regulation of food product merchandising, control bodies, and food product labeling; marketing strategies, also through the evaluation of consumer opinions; identification of target audiences for traditional and innovative food products; application of the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of agri-food sector production processes and the related food products.

Food Sciences
Students will acquire the necessary capabilities for evaluating the nutritional and food aspects of foods, aimed at correct food labeling and effective communication strategies toward consumers. They will also be able to identify strategies for product innovation targeting specific consumer groups (e.g., celiac, vegetarian, etc.) and/or specific dietary needs (e.g., high-fiber foods, probiotic foods, vitamin-fortified foods, etc.). Students will also be able to apply the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of agri-food sector production processes and the related food products.

Applied Biotechnology in Food Production
Students will acquire a critical view of the potential of microbial biotechnology and predictive microbiology in the food sector and will be able to interpret data, develop ideas, and design innovations both in the production of fermented foods and in the microbiological control of foods. They will also be able to design and propose the application of specific innovative biotechnological techniques in production processes and evaluate their practical effectiveness. Students will also be able to apply the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of agri-food sector production processes and the related food products.

Food Evaluation
Students will acquire an advanced understanding of the potential offered by using appropriate techniques for sensory evaluation of foods. They will also be able to design and manage specific panel tests aimed at discriminant and descriptive evaluations, critically and appropriately assessing the results obtained, thanks to specialized software for data management and evaluation. Students will also be able to apply the acquired knowledge and skills as an integral part of a comprehensive evaluation of agri-food sector production processes and the related food products.

Food Safety and Quality
Students will acquire specific skills for designing and implementing the main systems for quality management (ISO 9000, BRC, IFS, etc.) and food safety (GMP, GHP, HACCP); designing, conducting audits, and evaluating results; using acquired knowledge for a comprehensive evaluation of agri-food sector production processes and related food products, considering multiple aspects of production controls, nutritional and sensory evaluations, biotechnological innovations, marketing strategies, etc.

ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Role.
Food Technologist and Researcher in the Field of Food Technologies and Biotechnologies.

Ability to develop product innovations, new food products, and innovations in existing production processes. Production and Line Manager. Management, control, and operation of equipment and food processing and related product processes. Management, administration, and operation of companies operating in the production, transformation, preservation, distribution, and commercialization of food.

Ability to assess the level achieved by safety and quality systems during pre-inspection verification and audits, as well as to interact directly during external audit and inspection visits with the specific team of evaluators responsible for conducting the aforementioned controls within the company.

Role in Work Context.
Food Technologist and Researcher in the Field of Food Technologies and Biotechnologies.
Programming, management, control, coordination, and training related to food and beverage production, preservation, transformation, distribution, and service. Management of resources, materials, and professionals, aimed at continuously improving food products in economic terms, food safety, and quality, with particular attention to sustainability, circular economy, and bio-based economy. Research and development of processes and products.

Production and Line Manager
Management, control, and operation of equipment, even complex, and food processing and related product processes. Direction and management of companies operating in the production, transformation, preservation, distribution, and commercialization of food.

Production Control Manager (raw materials, semi-finished products, finished products)
Responsibility for verifying safety, quality, and quantity parameters of raw food materials, semi-finished products, finished products, additives, technological aids, packaging materials, and all aspects related to food production and transformation, as well as defining standards and specifications for the aforementioned products.

Expert in Managing Food Safety and Quality Systems and "Lead-Auditor"
Design, management, and continuous improvement of systems for managing food production safety (GMP, GHP, HACCP) and quality. Management of internal audits aimed at pre-evaluating certification within the production environment.

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
In the first year, within front-facing training activities, at least 30% of practical activities will be included; additionally, the course will include visits to food industries. The second year will be entirely dedicated to practical and highly professionalizing training activities carried out within the cooperating food industries. These activities will be developed through a Practical Application Internship (specialized) and an additional research and experimentation activity for the preparation of the thesis. Second-year training activities will be programmed, managed, and carried out in close collaboration with food industries.

The educational objectives of the Master's program primarily focus on training an expert in food technologies, with particular reference to professional competencies related to food safety and quality.

The educational objectives of the Master's program primarily include eleven areas of professional competencies that students must acquire:
1. Possess a solid knowledge of processes and food technologies and biotechnologies (reference: entrance test and first-level degree);
2. Possess a solid foundational cultural preparation and good mastery of the scientific method, particularly regarding the technological transfer of knowledge to practical implementation in companies (reference: Practical Application Internship and final thesis);
3. Possess a high capacity to optimize food industry production processes and manage specific organizational and control aspects (reference: Control Systems in Food Industries, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
4. Be experts in managing and promoting food safety and quality, even in compliance with regulations on operator safety and environmental protection (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
5. Possess high technical and practical skills for quality and safety control of foods, also using innovative methodologies (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Starter Management and Predictive Microbiology, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Food Sciences, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
6. Possess adequate knowledge and professional skills for complex coordination and direction activities related to the agri-food sector (reference: Food Safety and Quality, Starter Management and Predictive Microbiology, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Food Sciences, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
7. Possess knowledge and professional skills in designing and managing machines and equipment used in food processing and transformation (reference: entrance test and first-level degree, Control Systems in Food Industries, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
8. Possess advanced knowledge on evaluating sensory and food aspects of main foods, as well as main methodologies and strategies for application, also to assess consumer opinions (reference: Food Sciences, Food Merchandising and Marketing, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods);
9. Possess advanced skills in managing companies, agri-food supply chains, and consulting and service companies connected to them (reference: Food Merchandising and Marketing, Physical and Sensory Analysis of Foods, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
10. Have developed personal skills in communication, multidisciplinary group work, and judgment abilities both on technical-economic and human-ethical levels (reference: specific workshops and group work, Practical Application Internship, and final thesis);
11. Be able to fluently use at least one European Union language in addition to Italian, both in written and oral form, with reference to disciplinary terminology (reference: entrance test and first-level degree).

Critical Judgment.
The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to manage the acquired knowledge and skills to make appropriate evaluations and decisions that respect the principles of sustainability in an increasingly innovative international context such as tourism. In particular, the graduate will be able to define and implement sustainable strategies and respond to the challenges that the continuous pursuit of innovation imposes on all tourism organizations (public and private). From an operational perspective, the student will be able to use the acquired skills to manage companies operating in the tourism sector from a multidimensional perspective, shaped by economic, environmental, and social needs, and to leverage digital knowledge at the foundation of innovation.
The student will acquire critical judgment skills for understanding, interpreting, and resolving the various issues encountered in the innovative and sustainable management of tourism companies. This ability is ensured by the interdisciplinary nature of the educational path, as well as specific training activities, whose content is developed through the analysis of business cases and the completion of group work requiring a strong participatory approach from the student.
More specifically, participation in various training activities (classroom and laboratory teaching, business testimonials, internships), during which students can engage in critical reflection on problems, simulated or drawn from reality, allows students to independently identify the most critical aspects and evaluate possible decision-making and management alternatives.
Critical analysis skills are also developed through systematic and continuous analyses over time (according to the principles of smartness and big/open data), with the aim of effectively designing the service-experience in physical, digital, or phigital contexts.
This judgment autonomy is also acquired through the activities carried out for the preparation of the final thesis, represented by the writing and discussion of a thesis that must be characterized by originality, comprehensiveness, and clarity in both the framing and in-depth analysis of the topic under study.

Knowledge and Understanding.
ECONOMIC AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to know and understand innovative dynamics and their interrelationships among the companies that form the economic fabric of the tourism sector. The graduate will be able to evaluate the development and management of destination ecosystems (smart tourism destinations) capable of optimally utilizing resources and providing integrated services (accessibility, digitalization, sustainable mobility, smart destinations, secure and inclusive communities, etc.), acquiring the ability to assess sustainability and the potential contribution of innovation to the development of the economic system and the quality of life of the local community.
BUSINESS AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to know and understand:
- innovative dynamics within individual tourism organizations and the resulting change processes;
- the use of new technologies for implementing marketing strategies (for the company and destination), as well as advanced destination management models;
- analysis and monitoring models to support the business decision-making process.
LEGAL AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to know and understand all legal tools that are essential for successfully operating in the tourism sector. In particular, the graduate must know the legal models for sustainable tourism and mobility, for tourism entrepreneurship, destination management, and digital marketing, quality management.
STATISTICAL-MATHEMATICAL AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to know and understand the use of quantitative analysis tools to support the decision-making process, with particular reference to market analysis and the effects of innovative strategies. The graduate will be able to know quantitative models useful for measuring equitable and sustainable well-being.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
ECONOMIC AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to apply the acquired knowledge and analytical tools to:
- conduct scenario studies that allow companies to orient their investment decisions;
- evaluate, through the use of appropriate models, the impacts of new technologies on the entire economic system and their sustainability, with particular reference to the well-being of the community.
BUSINESS AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to apply the acquired knowledge and analytical tools to:
- set up the analysis of managerial and financial variables to support business decisions;
- initiate entrepreneurial paths and innovative start-ups oriented towards the principles of economic, social, and environmental sustainability;
- facilitate the integration and collaboration between different business functions and between companies and entities;
- implement innovation management principles in the tourism sector to support innovative strategies such as digital marketing or to create networking among various tourism sector operators.
LEGAL AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to apply the acquired knowledge and analytical tools to set up the analysis of the regulatory framework within the context of scenario studies that allow companies to orient their decisions concerning innovation management, with particular reference to intellectual property and competition rights.
STATISTICAL-MATHEMATICAL AREA The Master's graduate in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism will be able to apply the acquired knowledge and analytical tools to develop interpretive and decision-making models to support choices concerning innovation and sustainability in the tourism sector. The graduate will be able to use some quantitative analysis and business intelligence tools to activate customer relationship management systems, brand reputation management, and BES measurement.

Innovation Management Expert in Tourism Sector Companies

- Evaluate, propose, and implement new technologies useful for the conservation, utilization, and valorization of environmental, cultural, and social heritage, as well as for creating territorial networks oriented towards innovation and continuous improvement of tourism services and experiences;
- Design and implement control systems for evaluating and monitoring performance from various perspectives and for activating customer relationship management and customer satisfaction to support market-oriented management.

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The Master's Degree Course in Innovation Management for Sustainable Tourism (IMaST) aims to provide advanced, solid preparation in the fields of economics and business management, enabling students to acquire evolved, methodological, and analytical tools necessary to understand, anticipate, and manage innovation pathways of an economic system and a company, with particular attention to the sustainability and competitiveness of growth processes in the tourism sector.
For this purpose, the study path integrates new knowledge in the business, quantitative, economic, and legal areas with a set of training activities useful for characterizing different professional profiles, thereby enabling students to acquire specific skills necessary for studying new models of business and territorial development.
In particular, the first year of the two-year program focuses on the core of economic-quantitative and legal knowledge indispensable for acquiring tools to understand the specific market, relevant regulatory profiles, and predictive analysis (with particular reference to sustainable development economics from the perspective of the environment, nature, and territory, data analysis, predictive methods for sustainable tourism, the legal and regulatory framework) as well as managerial knowledge related to innovation management (specifically referring to governance models, strategic analysis, and international marketing in the tourism sector). It is further complemented by the choice of elective courses that help students enrich their knowledge base according to their personal inclinations.
The second year involves acquiring advanced knowledge in economic (with particular reference to natural capital, ecosystem services, and, more generally, cultural capital), quantitative (related to measuring equitable-sustainable well-being), and managerial areas (referring to innovation management in the tourism sector and advanced business finance tools) capable of characterizing the superior abilities of future graduates from the perspective of operational autonomy functional to the strategic and competitive growth of companies and tourism destinations.
Consistent with the proposed cultural and professional profiles, and to respond to the challenges that digitalization imposes on all tourism organizations (public and private), the study program aims to provide, in addition to the disciplines necessary for managerial training in an international operational context, more practical laboratory training activities (related to sustainable entrepreneurship in the tourism sector, quality management, destination management, digital marketing, business organization, human resource management, ethical tourism, geo-economic analysis models, European law, and the use of the European indicator system ETIS for sustainable tourism management), which also focus on building soft skills and are aimed at developing:
- the ability for systematic and continuous analysis over time (according to the principles of smartness and big/open data);
- the ability to analyze tourist behaviors with the aim of effectively designing the service-experience in physical, digital, or phigital contexts through the implementation of innovation management principles;
- the ability to use new technologies for implementing marketing strategies (for the company and destination);
- the ability to master digital marketing strategies and activities (at the company and destination level);
- the ability to develop effective destination management models (governance & branding);
- the ability to facilitate integration and collaboration between different business functions;
- the ability to facilitate the integration and activation of horizontal (between competing companies), vertical (between companies at successive levels of the tourism supply chain), and oblique (between companies in different sectors, which, although not necessarily tourism-related, play a role in constructing a territory's tourism offering) collaboration relationships.
Additionally, the educational objectives aim to develop students' international and multicultural experience, also through opportunities to obtain double degrees. The development of international programs and the creation of laboratories aimed at fostering constant interaction with managers, professors, and students from innovative and multidisciplinary contexts form the basis for developing specific professional competencies for the tourism sector.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The Master's graduate in Business Economics is able to:
- properly set up the decision-making process to support business management, integrating general economic, business economic, legal, and quantitative knowledge to select and propose the most appropriate decision options;
- select the necessary approaches and tools to manage the problems that companies must face to define their own strategies and policies aimed at successfully competing in the global market;
- manage complex and articulated decision-making processes, which involve collective participation where it is necessary to demonstrate relational skills and the ability to work in a team in order to actively participate in the formation of shared and conscious decisions.
The Autonomy of Judgment is developed particularly through participation in various educational activities (classroom teaching activities and sometimes laboratory and internship activities), where it is possible to conduct case studies and participate in moments of critical reflection on problems, simulated or drawn from reality, with respect to which students identify the most critical aspects and evaluate possible decisional and managerial alternatives. This Autonomy of Judgment is also acquired through the activities carried out for the preparation of the final exam.

Ability to Learn.
The Master's graduate in Business Economics is able to:
- follow the evolution of various doctrinal positions and existing techniques regarding management problems related to specific businesses;
- frame situations and problems from a legal perspective, through the use of regulatory sources and their interpretations, and consequently be able to pursue their constant updating;
- set up analysis for strategic and operational purposes in different internal and external contexts of companies;
- access information sources of various types (publications, data banks, online information, regulatory sources, practices) to deepen topics of various nature related to both existing organizations and the development of new enterprises and/or activities.
The learning abilities are acquired throughout the entire course of study, with particular regard to the required individual study, the preparation of individual and group projects, and the activities carried out for the preparation of the thesis. The achievement of these abilities is verified within the final evaluation of the various educational activities and the final exam.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The Master's graduate in Business Economics:
- possesses in depth all the fundamental knowledge for the direction of companies and for the understanding of the processes that enable their governance;
- knows the conceptual and operational elements, related to the different business functions (production, marketing, R&D, planning and control, finance) necessary to start an entrepreneurial activity or to develop new projects within already consolidated companies, which operate in all sectors of the modern economy;
- possesses a solid knowledge of advanced planning and control tools to support strategic and operational business management;
- masters the knowledge in the field of business administration, both in the economic-management and legal fields, with particular reference to the themes of economic-financial trend recording and reporting and economic-financial planning;
- has the basic knowledge of business organization that support the control and management of human resources;
- has the basic knowledge of information systems and their relationships with business organization and administration;
- possesses a computer and statistical background useful for the quantitative analysis of important business phenomena (market demand analysis, quality control, etc.);
- possesses an in-depth legal background in relation to knowledge in the fields of commercial, tax, market regulation, and property and the relationships that follow;
- possesses a solid background in general and quantitative economics, with particular reference to national and international economic systems, market structures and competition, sector analysis, and the analysis and processing of data and information to support decision-making processes.
The above-mentioned knowledge and understanding abilities are acquired through participation in frontal lessons, exercises, and seminars that also include moments of critical discussion on various topics, the use and discussion of cases provided by many activated educational activities, as well as through continuous guided personal study by the teachers. Knowledge and technical and operational skills are also acquired through participation in business workshops, where there is the possibility of interacting with subjects operating in the business system and which often allow for the execution, both individually and in groups, of simulations of management and administrative issues that may arise in specific business realities operating in various sectors.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The Master's graduate in Business Economics is able to:
- develop interdisciplinary analyses of the main management issues in the different sectors of the economy;
- use qualitative/quantitative models useful for framing business problems from a systemic perspective and facilitating their solution;
- formulate decision alternatives, integrating general economic, business economic, legal, and quantitative knowledge;
- design the structure and operational systems of organizations and coordinate the activities of organizational systems, even complex ones;
- oversee business administration systems, in the accounting, financial, and legal aspects (contractual, administrative, commercial, tax, labor, regulatory);
- design and coordinate management systems in the different areas of functional management specializations, mastering the knowledge of management models and techniques;
- approach management problems according to an integrated and interdisciplinary approach, integrating knowledge and methods;
- conduct in-depth research on predetermined topics, work in groups, and provide a critical and original reading of complex phenomena.
The achievement of the above-mentioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding occurs through critical reflection on the texts proposed for individual study prompted by classroom activities, the study of business cases, participation in seminars where there are many prompts on operational topics, as well as during the preparation of the final exam. The assessments (written and/or oral exams, reports, exercises) involve the completion of specific tasks in which the student demonstrates mastery of tools, methodologies, and critical autonomy. The methods of carrying out these tasks are detailed in the syllabi of the individual courses.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.

Competencies Associated with the Role.
Business Manager Expert in management and control in private enterprises Expert in management and control of public administrations Expert in strategic analysis Expert in strategic marketing Expert in operational marketing Expert in market studies Expert in consumer behavior Expert in economic-financial accounting (or financial accounting)
Expert in tax and fiscal aspects Expert in management accounting (or managerial accounting)
Expert in administrative direction of healthcare structures Expert in public service management Expert in local authority administration

Role in Work Context.
Business Manager The graduate in the Business Economics course can find placement in enterprises of various economic sectors, with particular attention to those most developed in the territory, but also in public administrations and other private and public entities. The functions that the graduate will be destined to perform are adaptable to specific contexts and business functions in relation to the chosen curriculum and are as follows:
- Directorial responsibility roles in all business processes;
- Senior management roles in monobusiness or diversified companies;
- Direction roles in the individual functional areas of the company; in particular, strategic direction, administrative direction, marketing and sales, finance, process quality control and certifications;
- Senior management and directorial responsibility roles in central, regional public administrations, local authorities, and healthcare companies;
- Senior management and directorial responsibility roles in companies operating in the financial sector;
- Entrepreneurial and managerial roles in companies operating in the tourism sector;
- External consulting activities for enterprises and other entities, public or private, with particular reference to the administrative management and business law fields;
- Control activities both in internal company bodies and in audit firms;
- The profession of Chartered Accountant, which requires registration with Section A of the Register of Chartered Accountants and Accounting Experts, following a traineeship and passing the state exam (d. leg. 139/2005).

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The Master's degree course in Business Economics aims to train highly qualified graduates capable of performing directorial, administrative, and consulting functions within private and public companies operating in various sectors, with particular attention to those most developed in the Sardinian territory. The main objective of the Master's degree is to train professionals with particular expertise in the management and administration of companies and in the system of regulations that influence their activities. The course also aims to train graduates specialized in managing certain crucial business functions for business success, such as marketing and organization and control. The Master's graduate in Business Economics, through the acquired competencies, is able to perform roles in the general management of private and public companies operating in industrial and service sectors and to manage the main business functions, in various reference contexts, both through full mastery of strategic analysis, analysis techniques, and decision-making process support, and by coordinating and organizing operational units. With the acquired competencies, they can support company management and administration also as a business consultant and a qualified professional for the Chartered Accountant profession. The training path is structured to initially offer advanced training in the disciplinary areas of law, economics, and business, then focus on theoretical knowledge, operational competencies, and practical skills necessary to allow specialization that can be used in specific sector contexts and, in any case, in a wide range of roles in the field of management and professional consulting.

Judgment autonomy.
The Master's graduate in Economics exercises their judgment autonomy by utilizing the logical-formal apparatus and technical knowledge acquired throughout the entire study path and formulates recommendations and evaluations inspired by:
- the distinction between normative and positive propositions;
- the use of reliable empirical evidence where possible;
- integration and comparison with other disciplines concerned with the same phenomena;
- scrutiny of the results of choices from both the equity and efficiency perspectives;
- weighing the relevant effects in the short and long term.
Judgment autonomy is developed particularly through explicit reference, in lectures and in the supervision of thesis work, to methodological and epistemological aspects, critical analysis of the literature, and the role of value judgments, as well as through targeted activities (such as seminars and workshops) where students have the opportunity to observe the presentation/defense of scientific work by other scholars or to present the results of their own individual or group work.
The writing of the thesis and preparation for the final exam occurs under the supervision of the thesis advisor and co-advisor, who work together to provide the student both verification and stimulus for improving the work.
Learning capacity.
The Master's graduate in Economics is able to:
- follow the evolution of methods, models, and techniques acquired during the study course;
- critically examine relevant information sources (scientific publications, databases, online archives, regulatory sources, etc.) to develop specific projects for study, analysis, and professional consultancy;
- access third-cycle education levels (research doctorates, scientific specialization courses, University Master's programs at the second level), also internationally, thanks to mastery of the fundamentals and operational tools of the professional economist.
Learning capacities are achieved throughout the study path, with particular attention to individual study, preparation of individual and group projects, and activities carried out for thesis preparation.
The achievement of these capacities is verified within the final assessment of various training activities and the final exam.
Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area To obtain the Master's Degree in Economics, the student must have achieved:
- secure mastery of the methods and analytical tools used by economic science to study the functioning of markets, consumer and firm behavior, and the properties of systems resulting from the combined actions of individuals, firms, and institutions;
- significant familiarity with mathematical procedures essential for solving static and dynamic optimization problems, financial and actuarial analysis, game theory, and probabilistic calculus;
- operational knowledge of statistical and econometric methods for studying collective phenomena, hypothesis testing, survey design, estimation and forecasting, and decision support;
- precise knowledge of the legal framework, tools, and institutions characterizing monetary and financial markets, also with reference to antitrust regulation;
- familiarity with the fundamentals of computer science for managing data archives, coupled with knowledge of major software packages for economic research and operational analysis;
- good knowledge of major research findings, theoretical developments, and current debates in one or more disciplinary sub-areas and specialized research fields.
The aforementioned knowledge and understanding capacities are achieved through participation in lectures, exercises, seminars, workshops, and other activities related to the courses in the study plan.
Verification of achieving learning outcomes occurs primarily through written tests and/or individual or group reports. The Master's thesis provides an additional opportunity to evaluate the expected learning outcomes.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The Master's graduate in Economics:
- Is able to use analytical tools and techniques to:
a) describe and predict the functioning of individual markets (financial and non-financial) and the economy as a whole;
b) evaluate optimal investment and financing strategies;
c) design rational and sustainable economic and business policies;
d) measure and explain the performance of a plurality of decision units;
e) outline and estimate the costs and benefits (including non-market) of projects by public bodies and private enterprises;
f) evaluate corporate competitive strategies;
g) prepare interventions for international or local cooperation.
- Is able to address novel and complex issues with a systematic approach, navigating international economic literature and applying advanced information processing tools where necessary;
- Is able to extract useful indications from computer archives and balance sheets for business strategy planning, customer portfolio management, rating assignment, and understanding phenomena at various territorial scales;
- Is able to assist public administrations in designing investments in public-private partnerships (or vice versa), both in the evaluation of market spaces and optimal contractual form selection, and in the mathematical-financial analysis of structured finance operations;
- Is able to analyze economic contexts and production sectors, identifying needs, strengths, and weaknesses for preparing intervention and economic-business policy projects;
- Is able to prepare intervention and economic-business policy projects by defining objectives and actions consistent with identified needs;
- Is able to conduct administrative control and reporting of projects;
- Is able to independently pursue post-graduate research paths and access higher-level training opportunities in an international context.
The achievement of the aforementioned competencies occurs through critical reading of texts proposed in various courses, completion of exercises and laboratory activities, use of specialized software for empirical analysis, participation in seminars, bibliographic research, and case studies.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Associated competencies for the role.
Economist Specialist controllers in Public Administration Financial specialists Market analysts Economic systems specialists Business economics specialists
Work context role.
Economist The Master's course looks at the new profession of economist implicitly defined by globalization processes and the international political-economic framework (supranational monetary policy, macroeconomic coordination, bank capital agreements, capital markets harmonization, rules for protecting savers and shareholders, etc.): a professional who systematically studies the market and its rules to define optimal strategies for enterprise governance, investment financing, and savings management. The training path also stems from recognizing ongoing changes in the public sector, particularly the need to rationalize spending through systematic evaluation of policies both over time (ex-ante, in-itinere, ex-post) and across the classic sustainability dimensions (environmental, economic, and social). An activity that requires specialized skills typically spread across multiple paths, looking at a series of professional profiles highly sought after by public administrations, management bodies, local tourism systems, promotion and development agencies.
A solid mastery of analytical and quantitative tools combined with specialized competencies in monetary and financial fields or in the design and evaluation of public policies opens up a wide range of job opportunities for the Master's graduate in Economics.
In addition to classical opportunities in the banking and financial sector (as operator, financial services technician, analyst, etc., at credit institutions, intermediary and insurance companies, rating agencies, pension funds, private enterprises, and credit unions) and in extra-academic economic research (at public and private research centers, sector associations, functional and territorial bodies), graduates of this class can perform functions with high professional content at national and international bodies responsible for economic policy and market regulation, or compete as consultants, consortium technicians, or public officials in the elaboration and implementation of economic development programs at international, national, and local levels.
Finally, the Master's degree in Economics allows access to the qualification exams for the profession of Chartered Accountant, which requires registration with section A of the Chartered Accountants and Accounting Experts Register, following an internship and passing the state exam (d. leg. 139/2005).
Description of specific training objectives.
The Master's degree in Economics aims to provide advanced preparation to graduates of the three-year degree who are interested in positions with high professional content within enterprises, banks, supervisory and regulatory authorities, research centers, sector associations, development agencies, territorial bodies, etc., or who wish to further deepen their knowledge of economic subjects through second-level Master's programs and/or doctoral programs.
The acquired competencies will enable entry into activities of analysis and forecasting, evaluation of real and financial investments, design and implementation of public policies, market supervision and regulation, support for strategic decisions, and performance measurement within a broad spectrum of decision units.
The characteristic training background concerns knowledge of economic phenomena, markets, institutions, and the regulatory framework of the national and international economic system, the ability to relate microeconomic and macroeconomic levels, analyze situations characterized by uncertainty and imperfect information, and develop econometric investigations to support decisions.
The training path is structured to initially provide advanced training in legal, economic, mathematical, econometric, and business disciplines, then focus on the theoretical knowledge, operational skills, and practical abilities necessary to acquire specialization that can be used by a professional dealing with economics who studies the market and its rules to define optimal strategies for enterprise governance, investment financing, and savings management.
The Master's degree in Economics enables the acquisition of fundamental competencies to act in responsible positions both in organizations operating on the demand and supply side of financial services (banks, enterprises, insurance companies, investment firms, issuing companies, etc.).

Final exam characteristics.
The final exam is accessed after acquiring the CFU related to all training activities specified in the study plan.
The final exam consists of preparing a thesis report, presenting the objectives, methodologies used and results obtained during the experimental thesis, carried out within an Italian or foreign research structure under the supervision of a course instructor. The thesis must consist of laboratory or field work, involve an experimental approach, and focus on issues related to scientific research. It must also include the acquisition and processing of original data, as well as a critical discussion and presentation of results in the context of relevant international scientific literature.

- Anatomy and Physiology

Students must possess the above-mentioned curricular requirements at the time of submitting the application for enrollment in the course.
The assessment of personal preparation adequacy upon entry will be conducted through an interview with a committee composed of teachers from different disciplines, according to the procedures specified in the Course Study Teaching Regulations.

CURRICULUM: Communication Skills
SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10799

Communication Skills.
The Master's graduate in WMCC is able to:
- communicate clearly and comprehensively, also in English, using appropriate scientific terminology, results, information, data and comments to both specialist and non-specialist audiences;
- work in groups, interacting with different professional figures such as veterinarians, naturalists, biologists, agronomists, and technologists, and with people of different nationalities;
- express and synthesize, both in written and oral form, in Italian and/or English, reports, projects, plans, guidelines and anything else that may be useful in management practice.
Written and oral communication skills are particularly developed during seminars, exercises, and training activities that involve preparing written reports and documents and presenting them orally.
The verification of the achievement of the above-mentioned communication skills occurs during the preparation and discussion of the final exam, as well as during oral examinations, and in particular during the presentation of case studies required for specific training activities.

Learning Ability.
The Master's graduate in WMCC possesses a developed predisposition for in-depth study and continuous updating of knowledge within the fields of innovative technologies, wildlife and hunting regulations, and scientific research. They are accustomed to comparing with other territorial and environmental contexts. They are able to use the main tools for updating, including access to computer databases and scientific literature.
These competencies will be acquired during exam preparation, classroom exercises, and particularly during internship and thesis periods. The learning ability is verified through analysis of the individual student's academic record regarding exam results, the time elapsed between attending a course and passing the exam, and finally during the execution of the experimental thesis and the preparation of the final exam report.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A104] WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION, AND CONTROL
TYPE: Master's Degree
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10799

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's graduate in WMCC acquires high-level analytical and critical evaluation skills regarding issues related to wildlife management and conservation, is able to plan, coordinate, and carry out the different phases of wildlife monitoring, draft plans and projects within the scope of conservation management, demographic control, damage prevention, and health prophylaxis concerning animal populations in nature and captivity. They are also able to independently implement protocols, techniques, and methodologies derived from scientific literature.
Judgment autonomy is particularly developed during internship and thesis periods and final exam preparation. Additionally, some disciplines involve individual or group analysis of specific case studies, requiring students to analyze complex situations and independently propose possible initiatives to address them.
Acquisition of judgment autonomy is verified through evaluation of the final exam and assessments during individual exams specified in the study plan, as well as through evaluation of the degree of autonomy achieved during experimental thesis and internship activities and project tests.

Knowledge and Understanding.
ZOOLOGY
- Knowledge of major natural dynamics related to the origin and transformation of animal biodiversity;
- Understanding of dynamics through which ecological processes operating at global, regional, and local scales, including those related to human activities, impact terrestrial and aquatic biocenoses;
- Theoretical and practical knowledge of major monitoring techniques for estimating population size;
- Knowledge of major international protocols for habitat and species conservation;
- Knowledge of a range of computer tools used in processing population and genetic data;
- Knowledge of major wildlife control techniques and damage prevention methods;
- Understanding of genetic mechanisms that may determine reduced vitality in populations, in nature and captivity.

VETERINARY SCIENCE
- Knowledge of major diagnostic, preventive, and control techniques for infectious and parasitic diseases;
- Knowledge of animal management techniques in captivity and major ethological, physiological, genetic, and health issues related to this condition;
- Knowledge of major international protocols for species conservation, reduction of health risks, and animal welfare;
- Knowledge of a range of computer tools used in processing epidemiological data;
- Knowledge of methods for evaluating animal welfare;
- Knowledge of veterinary aspects for capturing, restraining, handling, and transporting wild animals;
- Knowledge of physiological and pathophysiological mechanisms activated by wild animals in stressful situations;
- Knowledge of major aspects related to animal nutrition in nature and controlled conditions;
- Knowledge of gamete biology and application of major assisted reproduction techniques in vivo and in vitro for wild species.

ECONOMICS
- Knowledge of theoretical approaches related to economics and management of natural resources;
- Knowledge of interpretative models of sustainability of economic processes on natural resources;
- Knowledge of approaches related to circular economy, green economy, and blue economy;
- Knowledge of approaches used to estimate the economic value of natural heritage.

LANGUAGE COMPETENCIES
- Knowledge of specific terminology in the field;
- Understanding of scientific texts in English;
- Understanding of seminars, dialogues, and audiovisual materials in English related to course topics.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
ZOOLOGY
1. Ability to recognize major vertebrate wildlife species and their presence signs in nature;
2. Ability to propose and coordinate interventions for wildlife population management and control;
3. Ability to conduct monitoring activities for abundance, distribution, and genetic status of wildlife;
4. Ability to carry out wildlife planning at different spatial levels.

VETERINARY SCIENCE
1. Management capabilities related to control of infectious diseases and parasitosis in wildlife, including formulation of prophylactic measures;
2. Ability to manage capture, transport, and reintroduction of wild species respecting animal welfare;
3. Ability to determine nutritional needs and food types for wild species in natural and controlled conditions;
4. Ability to manage captive breeding programs.

ECONOMICS
- Ability to quantify the economic value of different elements of natural and wildlife heritage in relation to ecosystem services provided and their conservation use.

LANGUAGE COMPETENCIES
- Ability to correctly express scientific content in written and oral form using specific terminology;
- Ability to update on course topics through consultation of literature, technical documents, web resources, or participation in courses, seminars, and conferences.

Official teaching and assessment languages.
ENGLISH Competencies Associated with the Role.
Wildlife Manager - expert in wildlife management
- Able to design and coordinate, respecting animal welfare and current regulations, interventions for wildlife population management and control, including hunting management, eradication, capture, transport, and reintroduction;
- Able to design and manage plans for controlling infectious diseases and parasitosis in wildlife, including formulation of prophylactic measures;
- Able to plan and conduct monitoring activities for abundance, distribution, genetic diversity, and health status of wildlife;
- Able to quantify the economic value of wildlife heritage in relation to different ecosystem services provided;
- Able to design and manage captive breeding programs;
- Able to determine nutritional needs and food types for wild species in natural and controlled conditions.

Role in Work Context.
Wildlife Manager - expert in wildlife management
Conservation and productive management of wild animal populations
Control and prevention of health emergencies in free-living and captive wildlife
Design, development, and management of ex-situ and in-situ conservation programs for wild animal populations
Design, development, and management of relocation, reintroduction, and restocking interventions for wild animal populations.

Specific Training Objectives Description.
The training objectives of the WMCC course include acquiring skills in wildlife management and conservation, encompassing acquisition of techniques and management capabilities related to general issues and specifically concerning terrestrial and aquatic wildlife, genetic knowledge related to management and conservation of animal populations, and methods for analyzing population data. This is complemented by a block of physiological-veterinary competencies including knowledge of physiological adaptations to environmental changes and reproduction and nutrition physiology, acquisition of methodologies and management capabilities related to epidemiology and control of infectious diseases and parasitosis in wildlife, and elements of first aid and animal welfare. Elements of environmental legislation and environmental capital assessment further complete the acquired training.

All these activities are integrated with study stays at European universities participating in the course project and possessing specific expertise in the aforementioned subjects.

Master's degree graduates must:
- Have a solid scientific, technical, and operational preparation in the disciplinary fields characterizing and related to the course;
- Have good mastery of the scientific method of investigation;
- Be able to competently and autonomously address major management issues related to wildlife management, including: formulation of management and control plans for animal populations in terrestrial and freshwater contexts, application of monitoring techniques, planning and execution of reintroduction operations, formulation of management guidelines for animal populations, prevention and resolution of epidemiological and health issues related to animal populations, evaluation of animal welfare in different contexts related to wildlife (in nature and captivity), management of captive breeding projects regarding demographic, health, and ethological aspects, evaluation of genetic implications arising from species management in nature and captivity;
- Be able to fluently use English, both written and oral, with specific reference to technical-scientific terminology.

Training Path.
The student's training path includes a group of characterizing disciplines of class LM-86, divided into zootechnical and animal production disciplines and management and sustainability disciplines, together with a group of integrative disciplines necessary to direct the curriculum toward management and conservation of wild animals. An English language exam is added, aimed at refining and standardizing students' language skills.

Individual preparation for each training activity is assessed through a final exam and, where applicable, intermediate knowledge tests and through the presentation and discussion of reports.

The training path aimed at achieving the aforementioned objectives, in addition to classroom activities, includes the following:
- Laboratory activities dedicated to practicing experimental methods in genetics, physiology, parasitology, and microbiology;
- Practical data acquisition and processing activities, aimed at deepening knowledge of computer and computational tools for applying to various types of data (demographic, ecological, genetic) from real or simulated sources;
- Seminar activities, aimed at integrating knowledge acquired from attending core courses with content proposed by invited professors or visiting scientists;
- External activities such as training internships at companies, professional offices, public administration structures, and laboratories, based on specific training projects;
- Study stays at foreign universities and research centers, within specific international agreements;
- A experimental thesis consisting of conducting an experimental work under the supervision of a course professor, processing the obtained data, writing a scientific report, and finally discussing the results.

Foreign Title Fees and contributions Regulation Career - Fees Roles Responsible for approving study plans MASSIMO CARRARO Chair LIDIA VERA GIOVANNA DE LUCA Program, textbooks and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Chemist The Master's graduate in Chemical Sciences may register, after passing the State Exam as provided by DPR of June 5, 2001, No. 328, in the professional register of Chemist, and thus access the practice of the Chemist profession (section A). In addition to the practice of free professional activity, the Master's graduate in Chemical Sciences may find employment in sectors such as:
• Industry (in sectors such as agri-food, environmental, green chemistry, materials chemistry, petrochemical and pharmaceutical chemistry)
• Control agencies and laboratories (e.g., ARPA, Zooprophylactic Institutes, ATS, Fraud Inspection Office, Customs)
• Public and private analysis laboratories (e.g., in environmental control, merchandise analysis and/or chemical-clinical analysis)
• Research centers
• Scientific information
• Scientific dissemination agencies
• Certification companies
• Quality control.
The graduate may also further their education by attending Research Doctorate Courses, Specialization Courses, teaching training courses, or second-level Master's programs.
Graduates who have sufficient credits in appropriate subject groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths.
Final exam characteristics.
The final exam consists of preparing and discussing an experimental thesis carried out under the supervision of one or more teachers belonging to the Department of Chemistry and Pharmacy.
The thesis must consist of an original work developed independently by the student based on laboratory experimental activity focused on issues related to scientific research. The thesis aims to achieve skills in autonomous experimental work, acquisition and processing of data, critical discussion and presentation of results and international bibliographic sources.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences, one must hold a first-level Degree (class 21 or class L-27) or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent. Admission is also permitted to students holding other Degrees characterized by a good basic scientific knowledge in mathematical and physical disciplines and adequate preparation in various chemical disciplines: general and inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, and materials chemistry. For all students, admission is conditional on meeting the requirements defined in the study course didactic regulation; specifically: at least 80 CFU in the overall SSD FIS/01-08, MAT/01-08, INF/01, BIO/10-12, ING-IND/21-22 and CHIM/01-12 (with a minimum of 40 CFU in SSD CHIM/01-12). English language knowledge at B1 level (or higher) is required, certified or recognized with equivalent linguistic competence in a university course or verified through an interview.
The verification of the adequacy of personal preparation, which is a necessary condition for enrollment in the Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences, will be carried out through an interview, exempting graduates in Chemistry (class 21 or class L-27), provided they meet the specified English language knowledge requirements.
Degree awarded.

Communication Skills.
The graduate in Chemical Sciences must be able to communicate, clearly and unambiguously, information, scientific data and conclusions to specialist and non-specialist audiences, also through the preparation of written reports, presenting experimental data in the form of diagrams, tables and graphs, using English and the necessary computer tools for presentation. They must be capable of working in a group, operating with high degrees of autonomy and quickly integrating into work environments. The acquisition of the aforementioned skills is assessed at various levels within the training activities, primarily during evaluations, mainly consisting of oral exams, written tests and laboratory reports, as well as through participation in group work activities. These abilities are further refined in the preparation of the thesis project and final dissertation, also through the use of multimedia systems.
