Autonomy of Judgment.
Graduates must have acquired high-level critical reasoning skills and be able to independently conduct scientific research in their chosen field, identifying the most appropriate methods to address issues within chemistry and materials science. They must be capable of designing and conducting experiments, interpreting results, and devising the logical progression of experimentation to acquire knowledge and/or optimize methodologies or processes in a scientific and applied research context. They must also be able to appropriately utilize bibliographic sources and electronic archives available on the Web.
The acquisition of autonomy of judgment is ensured within specific training activities where the role of the discipline and its evolution are emphasized. Practical exercises and laboratory activities provide opportunities to develop decision-making and judgment skills, while the preferred teaching tool is the substantial thesis work on a research topic.
The verification of the acquisition of autonomy of judgment will occur through the evaluation of the courses in the student's individual study plan and the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work in a group during the research activities conducted during the thesis period.

Learning Ability.
Graduates must have developed the learning ability that enables them to effectively update their knowledge across all areas of chemistry, materials science, and their applications. They must therefore be able to effectively integrate acquired knowledge by identifying textbooks, reference scientific literature, and other materials useful for in-depth study. They must finally have the ability to read and learn in English. The achievement of the aforementioned abilities is particularly supported by the work carried out during the thesis period.
Learning ability is monitored throughout the study course through achievement checks and exam tests. The final evaluation emerges from the analysis of the student's academic record (exam grades and the time elapsed between attending the course and passing the exam) and from the abilities in deepening and self-learning expressed during the thesis activity and its preparation.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The master's graduate must have acquired in-depth knowledge in the fields of inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry, and macromolecular chemistry. The graduate must be proficient with the main analytical and synthetic instrumental methodologies, structural characterization, definition of structure-property relationships, and understanding of phenomena at the molecular level. They must also be familiar with fundamental computational approaches to problems related to chemistry and materials science.
Affine and Integrative Activities and Student's Free Choice The curriculum plan provides that the study path be personalized through an appropriate selection of both affine and integrative activities and those of the student's free choice. These activities contribute 14 and 8 CFU respectively towards the total 120 CFU required. The scientific-disciplinary sectors involved in these activities may be those specified in the characteristic activities, while also allowing space for more applied, specific, or frontier topics in chemical sciences, or other sectors.
Depending on the chosen path, the student will acquire knowledge and skills in the areas of Materials Chemistry (analytical chemistry sensors; synthesis and application of macromolecules; metals in medicine; physics of ionizing radiation), Green Chemistry (sustainable organic chemistry, legislation and environmental analysis, multistep synthesis and organic materials), and Applied Chemistry for Cultural Heritage (materials, technologies, and conservation of cultural heritage; physical methodologies applied to cultural heritage).

Inorganic Chemistry Area The graduate in Chemical Sciences must know the main aspects of coordination and organometallic chemistry of transition metals, homogeneous and asymmetric catalysis, synthesis methods of coordination compounds, their main reaction mechanisms, and their spectroscopic characterization (IR, NMR).
Analytical Chemistry Area The graduate must know the main electroanalytical techniques, their underlying principles, and their application in the study of materials and sensorics. They must also know the principles of mass spectrometry and interfaced techniques, as well as the methods for validating an analytical method. The graduate will also have skills in environmental chemistry, including from a legislative perspective.
Organic Chemistry Area The graduate must know the principles of designing organic synthesis, from more traditional approaches to more current ones, including green chemistry and its applications in organic synthesis, supramolecular chemistry, and the main spectroscopic characterizations.
Macromolecular Chemistry Area The graduate must know the recent aspects of macromolecular chemistry, including those related to green chemistry, synthetic approaches, and the functional and structural characterization of polymeric materials, as well as their use.
Physical Chemistry Area The graduate must know the principles of statistical mechanics, solid-state theory, and the main numerical simulation methods. The graduate must know the historical development of spectroscopic observations and the formulation of basic problems addressed to resolve modern issues (spectroscopy), as well as the methods for combining spatial filling modes based on maintaining 3-D periodicity compatible with possible geometries and symmetries (space groups). They must also be able to connect the modes from the original direct space to the reciprocal space of spatial frequencies and apply the connections based on Fourier theory (diffraction and spectroscopy). They must know the main physical methodologies used for studying materials with applications in the field of diagnostics and conservation of Cultural Heritage.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The graduate must be able to apply their knowledge across various fields of chemistry, demonstrating mastery of the scientific investigation method and possessing skills to devise and support arguments as well as solve chemical problems even in interdisciplinary contexts. They must be able to work correctly in the laboratory with autonomy and decision-making ability, addressing and solving problems in various areas of chemical sciences, making informed decisions and drawing conclusions based on available data and information.
Inorganic Chemistry Area The graduate will be able to apply the knowledge acquired during the course to develop strategies for synthesizing new coordination and organometallic compounds. The graduate will also be able to design new species containing transition metal centers with potential applications in various fields, such as materials, biomedicine, and homogeneous catalysis. They must also be able to identify and use appropriate instrumental techniques, primarily spectroscopic, for characterizing coordination and organometallic compounds.
Analytical Chemistry Area The master's graduate in Chemical Sciences is able to autonomously and critically use the main controlled potential analytical techniques and various instrumental types of mass spectrometry, both in basic applications and in more specific and current applications. Their training potentially enables them to devise and use even non-elementary analytical methods, and to plan and implement the most suitable validation procedures for an analytical method. They also have skills in specific aspects of analytical chemistry related to environmental analysis, including legislative aspects.
Organic Chemistry Area The graduate must be able to plan appropriate organic synthesis strategies using innovative methods, such as retrosynthesis, multistep synthesis, and approaches related to green chemistry, critically evaluating potential alternatives. They must also be able to assess and use the most appropriate characterization techniques, as well as the possible applications at academic and industrial levels.
Macromolecular Chemistry Area The graduate will be able to develop synthesis strategies for innovative polymeric materials and use appropriate functional and structural characterization techniques.
Physical Chemistry Area The graduate will be able to apply the principles of statistical mechanics, computational study, and solid-state theory to solve specific problems in the chemical field, with particular reference to materials science. They will also be able to develop the design of complex systems. The graduate will be able to know the sample preparation procedure for the spectrometer in use (spectroscopic and diffractometric), collect spectra or traces, and provide a coherent interpretation based on diagnostic bands and/or identified crystalline phases, using expert systems and updated databases. The graduate will know the main physical methodologies used for studying materials in the field of cultural heritage.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH Associated Competencies.
Chemist Excellent understanding of chemical aspects associated with industrial, research, and analytical laboratories, environmental protection, conservation of cultural heritage, health, energy, and materials science.
Full ability to use chemical instrumentation of varying complexity and interpret data derived from it.
Ability to devise and develop original analytical and chemical methodological procedures meeting the requirements of the client.
High level of interaction in multidisciplinary contexts.
Full autonomy in their work, potential ability to coordinate the activities of subordinates. Potentially able to perform freelance activities as a Chemist, Category A.

Work Function.
Chemist The master's graduate in Chemical Sciences finds placement in high-level industrial contexts, in responsible positions in research and analytical laboratories, in the fields of environmental protection, conservation of cultural heritage, health, energy, and materials science, as well as in freelance activities as a Category A Chemist. They are able to apply the experimental method broadly and thoroughly, use complex scientific instruments with total autonomy, are capable of devising and developing analytical procedures and fully interpreting the results derived from them, are able to plan the activities of subordinates with broad autonomy, and interact comprehensively and with extensive autonomous propositional-decisional ability in multidisciplinary scientific contexts.

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The Master's Degree Course in Chemical Sciences aims to integrate and consolidate the basic competencies acquired in the first cycle across various fields of chemistry, and seeks to provide students with specialized skills in a specific area of chemistry. The course aims to prepare professional figures capable of operating, even at a managerial level, in laboratories and public and private companies, offering a qualified and original contribution in the following areas: (i) innovation in the synthesis of old and new products, responding to efficiency and environmental sustainability criteria imposed by social awareness and rigorous European regulations entering into force in 2007; (ii) use of the most modern technologies for the structural determination of new molecules; (iii) design and use of the most suitable technologies for analysis in industrial, quality, and process control contexts, as well as in clinical, toxicological, forensic, and environmental fields; (iv) application of computational techniques.
The reformed Master's thesis project provides a wide range of training options within which the student must choose a defined number of CFU distributed across the SSDs belonging to the characteristic disciplinary areas of class LM-54. A significant space is dedicated to activities related to the thesis, during which the student addresses a specific scientific research topic and learns to apply the acquired theoretical knowledge. The teaching resources, research facilities, and teaching services available to the Degree Course allow for a proposal that includes multiple training paths in relation to the teachers' expertise in specific research areas.

Program, Texts, and Objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Natural Environment and Territory Manager The Master's graduate in Environmental and Territory Management has employment prospects in the public sector, private sector, and self-employment.
In the public sector, they may find employment in Ministries and other entities such as the Istituto Superiore di Sanità, ISPRA, Experimental Stations, Parks, and Natural Reserves. They may also find employment in Research Entities such as Universities or CNR, Regional, Provincial, Municipal Administrations, or other Public Entities requiring advanced environmental and territorial expertise.
Regarding employment opportunities in the private sector, an increasing number of companies and consortia require highly qualified professionals who, after collecting and processing environmental data, can develop descriptive and functional models of the environmental and territorial state to formalize, design, and implement environmental territorial planning and environmental remediation plans at various spatial and temporal scales in complex and detailed terms. There is also growing demand for Master's graduates in Environmental and Territory Management capable of managing, in terms of management, all impact assessments, eco-balance, environmental certification, and permissible development operations within specific ecosystems.
The Master's graduate in Environmental and Territory Management, like all Master's graduates in Class LM-75 Environmental and Territorial Sciences and Technologies, can take the state exam for professional orders of Landscape Architect, Biologist, Geologist, and Agronomist to carry out self-employment activities.
Final Exam Characteristics.
The final exam consists of preparing and discussing an experimental thesis conducted under the supervision of one or more faculty members affiliated with the Course Council within a period of at least one year. The thesis must consist of an original work developed independently by the student based on laboratory or field experimental activities focused on issues related to scientific research in the fields of environmental and territorial sciences and technologies and natural sciences. The thesis aims to develop skills in independent experimental work, data acquisition and processing, critical discussion and presentation of results and international bibliographic sources.
Required Knowledge for Admission.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree Course in Environmental and Territory Management, one must hold a first-level degree (class 27 or class L-32) or another foreign degree recognized as suitable. Admission is also permitted to students holding other degrees, subject to a comprehensive assessment of the previous educational path. The Course Council will assess the specific scientific and cultural level of candidates, which must be sufficient to achieve the Master's degree within the specified timeframe. In particular, the submission of the application for admission to the Master's degree course is conditional on possessing at least one of the following requirements.
- three-year degree in class 27 or L-32;
- three-year degree in class 12 or L-13;
- three-year degree in class L-25;
- five-year degree in Environmental Sciences under the previous framework;
- degree in Natural Sciences under the previous framework;
- degree in Biological Sciences under the previous framework;
- other degrees provided that the following credits have been previously acquired in the required scientific-disciplinary sectors: CHIM/02, CHIM/03 and/or CHIM/06: 12 CFU; BIO/01 and/or BIO/02 and/or BIO/03 and/or BIO/05 and/or BIO/07: 12 CFU; GEO/03 and/or GEO/02 and/or GEO/04 and/or GEO/07: 12 CFU.
In the case of an educational path not meeting the above criteria, the missing credits related to the training activities in the above-mentioned SSDs must be acquired before enrollment. Indeed, those who have not previously acquired the required CFU must acquire the relevant CFU before enrolling in the Master's Degree. To achieve this goal, it is possible to enroll in single courses of the relevant SSDs of the first-level Degree Course in Natural Sciences at the University of Sassari.
Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level B1 is required, certified or recognized with equivalent linguistic proficiency in a university course or verified through an interview.
Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in ENVIRONMENT AND TERRITORY MANAGEMENT

Communication skills.

They are capable of effectively communicating their knowledge and skills within groups and in work contexts, both during planning and management phases.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: frontal courses and exercises will require the student to continuously participate and interact with others, also through the resolution of case studies and field-based data collection and study activities. Examination assessments require the written and/or oral presentation of a theoretical model, a scientific paradigm or a concept with relevance, mastery and linguistic propriety.
Assessment: presentation and discussion of reports, intermediate tests (where applicable) and final tests.
Learning ability.
Master's graduates, thanks to their training, possess the ability to continuously develop and deepen their competencies throughout their professional career. In particular, they are able to consult and process data, adopt methodologies and investigation techniques derived from international scientific publications. They are also able to consult specialized databases, adopt innovative technologies, and use advanced knowledge tools for updating their knowledge.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: the set of methods and teaching tools already described for other descriptors will enable the student to easily acquire the ability to learn the various topics of study and achieve the specified qualifying and specific training objectives.
Assessment: evaluation of reports, intermediate tests (where applicable), final exams and final test at the conclusion of the training path.

Judgment autonomy.
Master's graduates acquire high-level critical reasoning skills and are able to independently carry out technical-scientific activities, identifying the most appropriate methods to address issues within the fields of natural, environmental, and territorial sciences and the management of biotic and abiotic resources.
Their judgment autonomy stems from an interdisciplinary education that ensures understanding and the ability to act in broad and complex contexts, also evaluating the contributions of individual specialized disciplines. This autonomy is expressed in the evaluation of projects and decision-making processes related to their management, as well as in the responsibility for structures and personnel and in identifying innovative development perspectives/strategies. Furthermore, Master's graduates are able to manage, with personal responsibility, the evaluation and interpretation of experimental data in applied research.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: lectures and practical exercises will require continuous student participation and interaction with others, also through case study resolution.
Examination requirements: written and/or oral presentation of a theoretical model, scientific paradigm, or concept with relevance, mastery, and linguistic propriety.
Verification: presentation and discussion of assignments, intermediate tests (where applicable), and final tests.
Knowledge and understanding.
Learning Area: Terrestrial Ecosystems The graduate knows and understands:
-biological diversity and its evolution;
-methods for analyzing and monitoring populations of terrestrial macrofauna and vascular plants;
-natural dynamics and those induced by anthropogenic processes following the exploitation of georesources, which affect the physical elements of the Earth's surface;
-diversity of natural and rural landscapes;
-main international and national protocols for habitat and species conservation;
-legislation related to environmental issues;
-problems related to soil pollution and methods of remediation.
They are able to work in groups and interact with other professional figures, also in coordination roles, in environmental and territorial management.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: methodological and scientific/professional knowledge is acquired through lectures, integrated with practical exercises and/or field or laboratory experiences.
Verification: students are assessed, also based on active participation in exercises and practical experiences, through a final exam and, where applicable, intermediate knowledge tests and presentation and discussion of assignments.
Learning Area: Marine Ecosystems The graduate knows and understands:
-dynamics affecting the coastline and relationships between hydrodynamics and sediment movement, also in relation to georesource exploitation;
-economic and legal dimensions of natural resources in the coastal zone and methods for estimating the economic value of environmental goods;
-marine biological diversity at different levels (genetic, species, community, and ecosystem);
-evolutionary forces shaping biological diversity;
-methods for analyzing and monitoring the structure and functioning of coastal marine habitats and the main interactions between species and anthropogenic activities, assessing impacts and restoration strategies;
-main international and national protocols for the conservation of marine and coastal habitats and vulnerable species;
-fundamental principles for identifying areas of significant interest for biodiversity conservation and recovery.
For this purpose, the Master's Course includes intensive field activities so that students, through direct experience, acquire broad knowledge and mastery of the main modern conceptual and instrumental methodologies for assessing resources.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: methodological and scientific/professional knowledge is acquired through lectures, integrated with practical exercises and/or field or laboratory experiences.
Verification: students are assessed, also based on active participation in exercises and practical experiences, through a final exam and, where applicable, intermediate knowledge tests and presentation and discussion of assignments.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Learning Area: Terrestrial Ecosystems The graduate is able to:
-Apply geological survey techniques, prospecting, and characterization of georesources;
-Evaluate and quantify terrestrial ecosystem services to contribute to defining sustainable development lines, also in relation to the ability to analyze local stakeholders' needs;
-Design experimental protocols for monitoring animal and plant populations;
-Apply methodologies for monitoring biological diversity and functional, biotic, and abiotic relationships in terrestrial ecosystems;
-Identify the main threats to animal and plant populations and possible management solutions for habitat and species conservation;
-Work in groups and interact with other professional figures, also in coordination roles, in environmental and territorial management;
-Choose and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to survey structural and functional diversity;
-Prepare faunal, geological, and vegetation maps.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: methodological and scientific/professional knowledge is acquired through lectures, integrated with practical exercises and/or field or laboratory experiences.
Verification: students are assessed, also based on active participation in exercises and practical experiences, through a final exam and, where applicable, intermediate knowledge tests and presentation and discussion of assignments.
Learning Area: Marine Ecosystems The graduate is able to:
-Conduct marine geological surveys and sampling in marine environments;
-Apply cost/benefit analysis techniques and their evolution from impact assessment;
-Evaluate and quantify marine ecosystem services to contribute to defining sustainable development lines, also in relation to the ability to analyze local stakeholders' needs;
-Design experimental protocols for monitoring marine species and habitats;
-Identify the main threats to animal and plant populations and possible management solutions for habitat and species conservation;
-Apply methodologies for monitoring biological diversity and functional, biotic, and abiotic relationships in coastal marine ecosystems;
-Survey and process marine habitat maps.
Acquisition methods and teaching tools: methodological and scientific/professional knowledge is acquired through lectures, integrated with practical exercises and/or field or laboratory experiences.
Verification: students are assessed, also based on active participation in exercises and practical experiences, through a final exam and, where applicable, intermediate knowledge tests and presentation and discussion of assignments.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Natural environment and territory manager For performing their functions, the Master's graduate in Environment and Territory Management relies on acquired competencies that enable them to rigorously apply the scientific method, apply appropriate data analysis methods, address environmental issues with a multidisciplinary approach, use suitable tools for environmental management, evaluate resources and impacts due to anthropogenic activities, and disseminate information rigorously.
Work context role.
Natural environment and territory manager The Master's graduate in Environment and Territory Management is able to work autonomously, interact with different scientific backgrounds, and coordinate multidisciplinary work groups. They can therefore find employment in public or private work contexts for performing responsible and organizational functions related to territorial management; monitoring the conservation status of habitats and animal and plant species; monitoring environmental health; valorizing and restoring compromised environmental resources; conducting basic and applied research in naturalist and environmental fields; analyzing and evaluating the impacts of anthropogenic activities on biotic and abiotic ecosystem components and ecosystem services; and providing teaching, scientific dissemination, and environmental education.
Specific training objectives description.
The graduate in Environment and Territory Management is a professional and intellectual figure possessing knowledge of scientific language, its foundations, and a solid systemic culture of the environment, derived from the integration of basic knowledge related to mathematical, physical, chemical, geological, and biological sciences with those related to describing and quantifying natural processes and ecological systems. The specialized training acquired in different sectors enables the Environment and Territory Management graduate to operate autonomously in the fields of environmental and territorial resource management and protection. The training activities are organized so that graduates of the Master's Degree in Environment and Territory Management acquire knowledge and competencies to:
-analyze, control, and manage complex environmental and territorial realities from a systemic perspective, having clear knowledge of structures, functions, related processes, and regulating factors;
-know and be able to develop appropriate techniques for territorial investigation and data analysis, supported by specific methodologies, allowing the integration of multidisciplinary knowledge and competencies at different systemic, temporal, and spatial scales;
-address problems related to territorial control and management, evaluated according to sustainability and permissibility criteria;
-be able to evaluate resources (renewable and non-renewable) and environmental impacts through the formulation and use of models, employing conceptual and methodological tools;
-design and independently manage the restoration and conservation of the quality of complex environmental realities.
Specifically, the Master's Course will provide adequate preparation for:
-identifying and evaluating biotic and abiotic resources at the ecosystem level;
-analyzing and managing terrestrial, inland aquatic, and marine systems according to an holistic approach;
-evaluating environmental quality, impacts related to anthropogenic interventions, and pollutant control in the complex system;
-managing specific ecosystems within permissible limits;
-managing populations of endangered species both in situ and ex situ;
-designing the most suitable solutions to recover compromised ecosystems.
The training path is structured to develop specific competencies in the various fields related to environmental and territorial management.
During the first year, most lectures are held to leave ample space in the second year, particularly in the second semester, for internship and thesis work.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1214] HEALTH, MEDICAL, AND VETERINARY BIOTECHNOLOGY
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM:
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10405

Autonomy of Judgment.
The acquisition of competencies through a training path rich in laboratory activities and ongoing assessments will be crucial for developing the ability to autonomously formulate evaluations on the quality and accuracy of experimental designs, biotechnological processes used to achieve research and medical-veterinary application goals, as well as for interpreting experimental data.
Master's graduates will be able to propose and manage the various alternatives of biotechnological approaches applied to different medical-veterinary reference topics.

Capacity for Learning.
Master's graduates are capable of learning autonomously and self-directedly, also thanks to consulting databases and other online information on relevant topics and understanding scientific articles in English. Graduates effectively utilize appropriate information sources for solving health problems through biotechnological applications. The learning capacity is verified through analysis of the student's academic record. The evaluation of self-learning abilities occurs during the conduct of monographic seminars and the activity related to the final exam.

Knowledge and Understanding.
CORE SUBJECTS During the training path, the student must deepen the scientific foundations useful for understanding complex biological systems and preparatory for developing specific competencies applied to biotechnology, with particular regard to disciplines for the morphological and functional characterization of human and animal tissues and organs, and for understanding cellular and molecular pathogenic mechanisms of diseases.
At the end of the training activity, the student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of:
- the macroscopic and microscopic anatomy of the different organ systems of veterinary interest animals, with particular attention to the main species differences.
- the morpho-structural organization at the anatomical, tissue, and cellular level and the embryogenetic and organogenetic processes.
- the functions of different cell types of the organs and systems of veterinary interest animals and humans, the dynamic integration between different functions, and the mechanisms that control and regulate their activity.
- the cellular, molecular, and functional mechanisms underlying the general etiology of human diseases, cellular adaptations, mechanisms of cellular damage and death, genetic pathology, inflammation, oncology, and immune response processes.

BIOCHEMICAL/MOLECULAR DISCIPLINES AND DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC METHODOLOGIES The student must acquire advanced knowledge regarding genetic, biochemical, and molecular parameters in biological samples at different levels of structural organization, from individual molecules to cells to the entire organism, for studying the indicators of alterations underlying hereditary and acquired genetic diseases, neoplastic pathologies, autoimmune diseases, and major infections of interest to humans and veterinary medicine. Additionally, the student will gain in-depth knowledge of advanced analytical technologies at the omic scale and their utilization in prevention and diagnosis, as well as methodological approaches for the repair/regeneration of various organs/tissues, both in animal models and in humans.
At the end of the training activity, the student must demonstrate in-depth knowledge and understanding of:
- genetic, biochemical, and metabolic aspects of human and animal cells and tissues in relation to the main proliferative, differentiative, morphogenetic, and functional processes.
- the molecular structure and function of biological macromolecules.
- the molecular bases of the main veterinary and zoonotic parasitoses.
- the general background of infections and host response (innate and adaptive immunity) and the main autoimmune diseases, also in relation to previous infections.
- neoplastic pathologies focusing on the mechanisms of transformation, invasion, and metastasis.
- biochemical and molecular indicators of pathological alterations and quality control.
- biological characteristics of mesenchymal stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and the principles underlying their application potential.
- molecular processes underlying the isolation, maintenance, and differentiation of stem cells.
- biochemical and molecular methodological approaches necessary for studying molecular mechanisms related to pathologies, considering both research aspects and clinical-diagnostic applications and prognostic and therapeutic implications.

APPLIED BIOTECHNOLOGY The student must acquire specific competencies to translate the understanding of biotechnological processes and knowledge of complex biological systems into biomedical contexts of specific interest to medicine and veterinary medicine.
At the end of the training activity, the student must demonstrate advanced knowledge of:
- the regulations governing animal experimentation both in Italy and abroad.
- the methodologies and experimental models that can be used for the study and treatment of pathologies affecting both humans and animals.
- the functioning of biosensors, their geometry, and the different signal transduction modalities.
- the principles of biocompatibility, integration, biological degradation, and the application possibilities of biomaterials in various medical-surgical specialties, with particular emphasis on those of interest to molecular and regenerative medicine.
- the theoretical foundations and methodologies related to the application of assisted reproduction techniques in veterinary and human fields.
- molecular biology techniques applied to the analysis of gametes and pre-implantation embryos and implantation diagnosis techniques.
- systems for the production of transgenic animals.
- biotechnology applications in food microbiology and animal production.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
CORE SUBJECTS The student must be able to apply the acquired knowledge and understanding to:
- the recognition of anatomical, tissue, and cellular structures with particular reference to differences between animal species and the human organism, and to identify major lesions and alterations.
- the application and interpretation of information in physiological and pathophysiological contexts for identifying potential biotechnological applications.
- the development and application of diagnostic systems.
- the use of scientific terminology and language.

BIOCHEMICAL/MOLECULAR DISCIPLINES AND DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC METHODOLOGIES The acquired knowledge will enable graduates to develop adequate capacity and competence to:
- develop strategies for analyzing and interpreting biochemical and molecular parameters for personalized diagnosis and therapy.
- appropriately use methodologies specific to cellular, molecular, and gene transfer biotechnology to identify and validate therapeutic targets and innovative diagnostic approaches for molecular and regenerative medicine.
- identify new biomarkers for the prevention and early diagnosis of pathological states.
- develop innovative methodological approaches for diagnosing medical-veterinary pathologies.
- contribute to research in the field of vaccinology.
- apply the main methodologies for identifying, selecting, and differentiating stem cells, aimed at their application in repair/regeneration techniques of various organs/tissues, both in animal models and in humans.

APPLIED BIOTECHNOLOGY The acquired knowledge will enable graduates to develop advanced capacity and competence to:
- apply experimental protocols while safeguarding the welfare of experimental animals.
- develop cellular and molecular biotechnological methodologies for diagnosing medical-veterinary pathologies.
- apply innovative therapies based on the implantation of biomaterials, scaffolds, and nanotechnology.
- prepare experimental designs and independently conduct research in the field of biotechnology applied to human and veterinary medicine.
- develop targeted assisted reproduction protocols for treating infertility in humans, genetic improvement, and biodiversity conservation in veterinary contexts.
- implement drug-toxicological studies.
- apply biotechnological competencies to various medical-veterinary sectors, with particular reference to infectious diseases, obstetrics and gynecology, endocrinology, tissue engineering, and the use of biocompatible prosthetic materials.
- apply biotechnology in food microbiology in animal production and food transformation phases for human and animal consumption, with aspects related to food safety and hygienic safety.
- prepare experimental designs and independently conduct research in the field of biotechnology applied to human and veterinary medicine.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Biotechnologist
Integration into research programs as a Junior figure. Execution of diagnostic and research phases in specialized laboratories in the biomedical and veterinary sectors, both public and private. Creation of mini-enterprises (academic spin-offs and/or start-ups) for the application of biotechnological technologies in industrial fields.

Function in the Workplace.
Biotechnologist
Employment and development of complex instruments and processes in healthcare laboratories due to expertise in biomolecular, biosensor, reproductive technologies, infectious and infestive pathologies, and food production and transformation processes. Design and conduct of research and innovation projects in the healthcare sector.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's degree course aims to train professional skills to operate in the main fields of biotechnological applications in biomedical contexts. Additionally, it provides knowledge to ensure deep biomedical preparation and culture, with particular reference to aspects of human and animal pathophysiology susceptible to diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive intervention through a biotechnological approach. Advanced competencies will also be acquired for biotechnological applications in gene therapy, human and animal reproduction, animal production, food transformation, and technologically advanced diagnostic systems, based on solid practical laboratory experience.
In particular, Master's graduates must:
- deeply understand the genetic and biochemical aspects of human and animal cells and tissues in relation to the main proliferative, differentiative, morphogenetic, and functional processes;
- possess in-depth knowledge of the structure and function of biological macromolecules and solid competencies necessary for their characterization, analysis, and design, with particular emphasis on genomics and proteomics approaches;
- understand medical and veterinary pathologies, congenital or acquired, where biotechnological intervention is possible, with particular focus on those where innovative molecular technologies are expected to develop;
- know and apply the main methodologies for identifying, selecting, and differentiating stem cells, aimed at their application in repair/regeneration techniques of various organs/tissues, both in animal models and in humans;
- know the principles of biocompatibility, integration, biological degradation, and the application possibilities of biomaterials in various medical-surgical specialties, with particular emphasis on those of interest to molecular and regenerative medicine;
- know and be able to use methodologies specific to cellular, molecular, and gene transfer biotechnology to identify and validate therapeutic targets and innovative diagnostic approaches for molecular and regenerative medicine;
- know the methodologies in cellular and molecular biotechnology for reproduction, both in experimental and clinical fields.
- know the application of biotechnology in animal production and food transformation phases for human and animal consumption, with aspects related to food safety and hygienic safety.

Subject to the qualifying educational objectives set by class LM-9, the Master's Degree course aims to train biotechnologists capable of:
- organizing and coordinating laboratory activities for research or diagnostic investigations requiring the use of biotechnological methodologies on individuals and populations;
- using post-genomic approaches for engineering/manipulating bacteria, viruses, or eukaryotic cells;
- proposing systems and algorithms for personalized diagnosis and therapy;
- assisting physicians or veterinarians in diagnostic and therapeutic activities involving biotechnological applications (e.g., genetic diagnosis and therapy; assisted reproduction; therapy with engineered cells; development of biosensors; development of advanced nano-biotechnological diagnostic tools; molecular imaging; drug delivery; vaccinology and modulation of immune response);
- preparing experimental designs and independently conducting research in the field of biotechnology applied to human and veterinary medicine;
- applying biotechnological competencies to various medical-veterinary sectors, with particular reference to infectious diseases, obstetrics and gynecology, endocrinology, tissue engineering, and the use of biocompatible prosthetic materials;
- operating consciously regarding technology transfer, business management, and communication;
- working in research, experimentation, and/or production sectors with a highly interdisciplinary character, integrating their knowledge into broader application contexts;
- developing learning abilities that enable them to perform highly professional activities in an autonomous or self-directed manner.

Description of the Training Path.
The Master's degree in Medical, Health, and Veterinary Biotechnology requires the acquisition of 120 University Credit Units (CFU) over a two-year duration. The degree program includes integrated courses and concludes with a final exam. Each student's training path will be guided by a tutoring committee operating within the study program.
Training activities will normally be organized for each academic year into two coordinated cycles of less than one year, conventionally called 'semesters', each lasting at least 12 weeks on a semester basis. Various types of activities (lectures, exercises, practical activities, laboratories, seminars, internships) will be provided depending on the cultural and training characteristics of each course. A specific training activity in the form of an internship at qualified research laboratories is also provided. The distribution of weekly workload per CFU is regulated by the Course's Didactic Regulations, as well as the minimum required attendance hours to take profit exams.
For the assessment of achieved learning objectives, in addition to the final exam, one or more ongoing assessments may be provided; these may be written, oral, and/or practical.
Additional CFUs will be acquired through internship and orientation experiences. The possession of knowledge related to these training activities is verified—without a grade—by a committee appointed by the Academic Board or the Board itself.
Students may acquire the 8 optional CFUs by selecting any course offered by the University of Sassari, with the assistance of a tutor.

Judgment Autonomy.
The master's graduate must demonstrate judgment autonomy through the following abilities: - Develop complex analyses and formulate autonomous reflections and evaluations of a scientific, legal, ethical, and deontological nature to support decisions necessary to address complex problems in the management of assistive, organizational, educational, and research processes connected to the exercise of nursing and midwifery functions; - anticipate and evaluate the effects resulting from their decisions and activities, assuming the consequent social responsibility; - integrate high ethical standards and values into daily work activities and projects. - The teaching tools aimed at achieving the following abilities include the dissertation of student projects presented by students, which contain the phases of constructing an intervention project in the healthcare setting and demonstrate the ability to analyze, manage, and interpret data with judgment autonomy using available literature material and producing original and innovative data in a multidisciplinary and multidimensional perspective (also in preparation for the final exam).
Learning Ability.
The master's graduate must develop the following self-learning abilities: - Evaluate their own performance based on professional practice standards and organizational criteria, continuously identifying their own educational needs in relation to the nature and complexity of problems to be addressed and the project and operational strategies to be managed, in order to implement their professional improvement plan; - autonomously adopt effective strategies to continue learning, both formally and informally, throughout their professional life, also through further training paths; - use comprehensive information systems, software, and databases to collect, organize, and catalog information; identify a problem, conduct a literature review on the topic, critically analyze the problem and current knowledge, develop a strategy to apply research in practice, and facilitate the dissemination of research results. - Learning abilities are achieved through the overall study process, particularly through individual study, preparation of individual projects, and activities carried out in preparation for the thesis. The verification of these abilities occurs within specific laboratories through the evaluation of the ability to query databases, access international bibliographies on topics proposed within the teaching, and illustrate the innovative aspects introduced by scientific research; identify which issues, in different areas of competence, pose further questions for the development of research and in which directions.
Knowledge and Understanding.
1) Organizational, Management, and Healthcare Area (legal, economic, and organizational context, planning and organizational processes of healthcare activities and management of relevant personnel).
- Knowledge and Understanding. Master's graduates must be able to:
- interpret the principles of health and administrative law to understand their application in managing healthcare services, work processes, and professional relationships;
- analyze models and organization of healthcare systems, particularly European ones, the methods of health planning and financing of healthcare facilities;
- critically identify and evaluate the evolution of healthcare needs relevant to the specific professional role, also in gender-related aspects where required;
- design and intervene operationally in complex healthcare and organizational problems;
- plan, manage, and evaluate healthcare services with a focus on quality improvement (planning, organization, direction, control);
- supervise healthcare relevant to the specific professional role and carry out professional consulting actions;
- apply and evaluate the impact of different theoretical models in healthcare operations.
2) Training Area (university training, planning and management of educational processes).
- Knowledge and Understanding. Master's graduates must be able to: design, implement, and evaluate training interventions; develop teaching abilities for the specific professional role within tutorial activities and coordination of internships in basic, complementary, and continuous training.
3) Research and Socio-Psychological Area (scientific research and socio-psychological sciences).
- Knowledge and Understanding. Master's graduates must be able to:
- interpret epidemiological data to analyze complex phenomena and problems in healthcare and in the fields of nursing and midwifery;
- use statistical methodologies and research tools relevant to the professional role in clinical-assistive, organizational, and training areas;
- critically analyze ethical aspects related to healthcare and multi-professional and multicultural problems.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
1) Organizational, Management, and Healthcare Area (legal, economic, and organizational context, planning and organizational processes of healthcare activities and management of relevant personnel).
- Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding: Master's graduates must be able to evaluate performance based on professional practice standards and organizational criteria, continuously identifying educational needs in relation to the nature and complexity of problems to be addressed and the project and operational strategies to be managed, in order to implement a professional improvement plan, also using appropriate information systems to collect, catalog, and manage information.
2) Training Area (university training, planning and management of educational processes).
- Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding: Master's graduates must be able to autonomously adopt effective strategies to continue learning, both formally and informally, throughout their professional life, also through further training paths.
3) Research and Socio-Psychological Area (scientific research and socio-psychological sciences).
- Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding: Master's graduates must be able to identify a problem, conduct a literature review on the topic, critically analyze the problem and current knowledge, develop a strategy to apply research in practice, and facilitate the dissemination of research results.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
Master's graduates in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences, pursuant to Article 6, paragraph 3 of Legislative Decree No. 502 of December 30, 1992, and subsequent amendments, and in accordance with Law No. 251 of August 10, 2000, Article 1, paragraph 1, possess advanced cultural and professional training to intervene with high-level competencies in assistive, managerial, educational, and research processes within the areas relevant to the various healthcare professions included in the class (nurse, midwife, pediatric nurse).
Master's graduates who have acquired the necessary scientific knowledge, ethical values, and professional competencies relevant to the nursing, pediatric nursing, and midwifery professions, and have further deepened the study of the discipline and specific research, at the end of the training path are able to demonstrate advanced educational, preventive, assistive, rehabilitative, palliative, and complementary competencies in response to priority health issues of the population and quality service problems. Based on acquired knowledge, they are able to consider, in the planning and management of healthcare personnel, both the needs of the community, the development of new work organization methods, the planning and organization of pedagogical and educational interventions, as well as the harmonization of operational standards with those of the European Union.
Master's graduates develop, following adequate professional experience, an integrated approach to organizational and managerial problems of healthcare professions, qualified by mastery of healthcare management techniques and procedures, respecting their own and others' competencies. The acquired methodological knowledge also enables them to intervene in the training and research processes specific to the aforementioned areas.

• critically analyze ethical aspects related to healthcare and multi-professional and multicultural problems.

CURRICULUM: Communication Skills
SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10781

Communication Skills.
At the end of the preparatory course, students in the Master's Degree in Food Science, Health and Human Well-Being must demonstrate documented ability to communicate (communication skills) clearly and concisely the various knowledge acquired in the food field, highlighting the strengths of the topics and using the most appropriate terminology. The student must be able to communicate in writing and orally with interlocutors of equal standing or with lower or higher expertise.
a) Knowledge regarding the most appropriate terminology and its current meaning will primarily be imparted by teachers during frontal lessons with appropriate and repeated feedback.
b) Simulation sessions for learning techniques of collecting demographic and anamnestic data, administering questionnaires (food diaries, 7‒days recalls, physical activity diaries) and collecting data relevant for preparing the diet report.
c) Use of telecommunication means (video conferencing, instant messaging, chat, virtual classroom, etc.), to be implemented especially in the internship context.
d) Assessment of the student's achieved autonomy will also include their ability to interact synchronously with other collaborators and work in teams.
Learning Skills.
Students in the Master's Degree in Food Science, Health and Human Well-Being, upon completion of the training path, must demonstrate acquisition of an independent (learning skills) and constant learning method that enables the graduate to continuously update and deepen through systematic consultation of online databases of national and international literature, indispensable in the food sector, whose scientific paradigms are constantly evolving. This aspect is of crucial importance especially during the delicate phase of entering the job market, whose increased competitiveness requires constant effort in self-learning and acquisition of new knowledge.
Learning will be facilitated by the availability of reference texts for various curricular disciplines and foreign language texts recommended for in-depth study. Additional teaching support tools will include slides and lectures, as well as participation in seminars featuring recognized national and international experts. The official course website will also provide guidance for non-attending students.
To foster and consolidate in the student a deductive reasoning ability, small study groups will be organized with the teacher/tutor using the problem-oriented learning (POL) technique. The student will be taught how to apply theoretical knowledge to practical situations concerning the nutritional and health properties of foods, particularly those typical of the territory, recognize their characteristics and identify any harmful adulterations for human health. The teacher will present students with problems of increasing difficulty. Theoretical POL sessions will alternate with short practical stages.
The stages will take place at companies operating in the food sector in the territory with which specific agreements will be established. The POL training activities, alongside the professionalizing stages, will enable the future graduate to acquire the competencies required to independently address complex and articulated situations.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A086] FOOD SCIENCE, HEALTH AND HUMAN WELL-BEING
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Autonomy of judgment
SECTION: Autonomy of judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10781

Autonomy of judgment.
Students in the Master's Degree Course in Food Science, Health and Human Well-being, upon completion of their educational path, must demonstrate sufficiently consolidated autonomy of judgment (making judgments) enabling them to develop logically structured and compelling reasoning, and to act accordingly in a consistent and unambiguous manner. The acquisition of autonomy of judgment will also be pursued by students during the internship period in the final semester through exposure to operational contexts requiring specific personal skills and the didactic experience acquired.

Knowledge and understanding.
Food processing technology, food safety, and agro-industrial economy and marketing. Students must demonstrate knowledge of aspects related to technological processes, quality control, and microbiological aspects of food production, from the presence of microorganisms in food (as contaminants or probiotics) to microbiological, chemical, and physical alterations in preserved and industrially produced foods, and to regulations concerning food safety and preservation. Students must learn the fundamentals of agro-industrial economy and marketing at global, national, and local levels.

Food chemistry and biochemistry and human nutrition physiology. At the end of the educational path, students must know aspects related to food chemistry and their composition in terms of macronutrients and micronutrients. Students must also demonstrate full knowledge of the physiological and biochemical foundations of human nutrition.

Interactions between human organism, intestinal microbiota, foods, and drugs. At the end of the studies, students must demonstrate knowledge of aspects related to the impact of human genetics (nutrigenomics and nutrigenetics) and epigenetics on human nutrition, and the role of intestinal microbiota in modulating the functionality of various systems and organs, as well as its importance in determining pathological states. Special attention will be given to acquiring competencies regarding the role of foods as "drugs," according to the modern concept of "nutritional medical therapy," without neglecting topics related to "functional" and nutraceutical foods and interactions between diet and pharmacological therapies.

Human nutrition clinical practice and hygiene-sanitary aspects. Students must demonstrate knowledge of aspects concerning dietary characteristics in specific clinical conditions, both physiological (pregnancy, developmental age, aging, sports activity) and pathological, with particular reference to gastrointestinal pathologies causing malabsorption and endocrine/metabolic disorders. This learning area also includes topics related to food hygiene for human nutrition, nutritional education, and dietary education.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Food processing technology, food safety, and agro-industrial economy and marketing. Graduates, upon completion of the educational path, will have acquired the following abilities:
a) Ability to assess risks related to the biosafety of plant or animal origin food and related issues in a specific production chain;
b) Ability to assess the use of specific technologies (for a specific plant or animal origin food) related to food processing, preservation, and transportation that reduce biosafety risks and improve food characteristics for human nutrition.
c) Ability to understand the main mechanisms of the agro-food market, both globally and locally, within which the production, distribution, and commercialization of a specific food can be placed.
Typically, the knowledge and understanding mentioned above will be acquired through attendance at lectures, seminars, internships; guided and independent personal study. Assessment of learning outcomes will primarily occur through oral and/or written exams, in-course or final, case studies, project work, reports.

Food chemistry and biochemistry and human nutrition physiology. Graduates, upon completion of the educational path, will have acquired the following abilities:
a) Ability to assess the chemical composition of food, processes related to its interaction with the human body under physiological conditions (digestion, absorption, and biochemical processes), and determine body composition. Ability to estimate energy expenditure;
b) Ability to assess the nutritional characteristics of food and calculate nutritional needs under physiological conditions in terms of macronutrients and micronutrients;
c) Ability to understand the impact of processed, functional, fortified foods, and food supplements on the biochemistry and physiology of human nutrition;
Typically, the knowledge and understanding mentioned above will be acquired through attendance at lectures, seminars, internships; guided and independent personal study. Assessment of learning outcomes will primarily occur through oral and/or written exams, in-course or final, case studies, project work, reports.

Interactions between human organism, intestinal microbiota, foods, and drugs. Graduates, upon completion of the educational path, will have acquired the following abilities:
a) Ability to assess the role of intestinal microbiota in maintaining health status and its interaction with the immune system, and knowledge of the main technologies for characterizing intestinal microbiota/microbiome.
b) Ability to assess the role of the human genome and its interaction with the environment and diet (epigenetics), and knowledge of the main technologies for genomic and epigenetic characterization.
c) Ability to know the most important and representative nutraceuticals present in foods and their pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties. Ability to predict the impact of diet on pharmacological therapy and the impact of pharmacological therapy (e.g., use of antibiotics and chemotherapeutics) on intestinal microbiota.
Typically, the knowledge and understanding mentioned above will be acquired through attendance at lectures, seminars, internships; guided and independent personal study. Assessment of learning outcomes will primarily occur through oral and/or written exams, in-course or final, case studies, project work, reports.

Human nutrition clinical practice and hygiene-sanitary aspects. Graduates, upon completion of the educational path, will have acquired the following abilities:
a) Ability to calculate the energy and micronutrient needs of a patient based on age and sex, under physiological and pathological conditions; formulation of appropriate diets guided by tutors in relation to specific pathologies (obesity, dyslipidemias, diabetes, diverticulosis, chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, gastroesophageal reflux disease, obstinate constipation, etc.).
b) Ability to simulate and decompose food diaries under the different conditions indicated in point a);
c) Ability to know and apply food legislation concerning hygiene-sanitary aspects related to food for human nutrition in the phases of: production, processing, packaging, distribution, storage, sale, and service.
Typically, the knowledge and understanding mentioned above will be acquired through attendance at lectures, seminars, internships; guided and independent personal study. Assessment of learning outcomes will primarily occur through oral and/or written exams, in-course or final, case studies, project work, reports.

Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIANO Associated competencies for the role.
Specialist of Health/Nutrition Biologist, Food Biotechnologist, Researcher in Food Science. The professional opportunities that specialist graduates in this class can undertake in the early years of employment in the labor market are primarily related to the figure of the nutrition biologist, food biotechnologist, and researcher in the field of human nutrition. In particular, the Master's graduate can register with the National Order of Biologists (after passing the State Exam) and independently carry out the above-mentioned activities.

The training activities of the Master's Degree Course are aimed at learning the correct application of nutrition, diet, and relevant current regulations, using new technologies applied to food and human nutrition and interpreting their data to evaluate nutritional quality, safety, suitability of foods for human consumption, and overnutrition or undernutrition in individuals and populations.

In particular, the competencies associated with the roles in the work context described above are:
1) Ability to assess the nutritional characteristics of foods and their modifications induced by technological and biotechnological processes;
2) Ability to conduct surveys on food consumption aimed at monitoring nutritional trends in the population;
3) Ability to analyze the bioavailability of nutrients in foods and food supplements and their effects;
4) Ability to apply methods to assess food safety and suitability for human consumption;
5) Ability to assess the nutritional status at population level and specific groups;
6) Ability to provide information, training, and education to institutional operators and the general population on principles of food quality and safety;
7) Ability to develop and prescribe individual diets, diets for company canteens, for communities, for sports groups, etc., diets for specific pathological conditions, following a health status evaluation by a physician;
8) Ability to use and employ devices for measuring parameters useful for evaluating nutritional and energy needs, provided they are non-invasive;
9) Ability to prescribe food supplements;
10) Ability to carry out research activities within studies on the relationship between food intake and health status;
11) Ability to support/collaborate in international programs for training and assistance regarding food availability in depressed areas and emergency situations;
12) Ability to contribute to the management of enterprises in the human food sector;
13) Ability to provide consultancy to enterprises in the human food sector;
14) Ability to collaborate in accreditation and surveillance procedures for laboratories and health structures regarding food preparation, preservation, and distribution.

Role in work context.
Specialist of Health/Nutrition Biologist, Food Biotechnologist, Researcher in Food Science. The training activities are aimed at learning the correct application of nutrition, diet, and relevant current regulations, using new technologies applied to food and human nutrition and interpreting their data to evaluate nutritional quality, safety, suitability of foods for human consumption, and overnutrition or undernutrition in individuals and populations.

In particular, the activities that specialist graduates in this class can carry out are:
1) Assessment of nutritional characteristics of foods and their modifications induced by technological and biotechnological processes;
2) Collaboration in surveys on food consumption aimed at monitoring nutritional trends in the population;
3) Analysis of bioavailability of nutrients in foods and food supplements and their effects;
4) Application of methods to assess food safety and suitability for human consumption;
5) Assessment of nutritional status at population level and specific groups;
6) Information and education directed to institutional operators and the general population on principles of food quality and safety;
7) Prescribing individual diets, diets for company canteens, for communities, for sports groups, etc., diets for specific pathological conditions, following a health status evaluation by a physician;
8) Use of devices for measuring parameters useful for evaluating nutritional and energy needs, provided they are non-invasive.

Specific educational objectives description.
The educational objectives of the Master's Degree Course primarily include nine areas of professional competencies that students must acquire during the two years of training:
1. Knowledge of foods (properties and associated technological processes) and agro-food biosafety. As a result of this first educational objective, the graduate must possess solid knowledge of the properties of nutrients and non-nutrients present in foods and the modifications occurring during technological processes. The graduate must also know the main industrial technologies applied to the preparation of food supplements and foods for special diets. Special attention will be devoted to the biosafety of agro-veterinary origin foods.
2. Knowledge of agro-food economy and marketing. As a result of this educational objective, the graduate must possess knowledge of the food market at international, national, and local levels.
3. Knowledge of issues related to national and international food policies. Knowledge of national and community food and health legislation regarding the marketing and safety of foods, ingredients, additives, and food supplements.
4. Knowledge of biochemical and physiological mechanisms of digestion, absorption, and metabolic processes related to nutrients.
5. Knowledge of nutritional quality, nutraceutical aspects, and energy contribution of different food classes, and ability to assess factors regulating the bioavailability of macronutrients and micronutrients.
6. Knowledge of the influence of foods on well-being and prevention and treatment of diseases, as well as safety levels, acceptable daily intakes, and assessable risks in the intake of substances contained in or conveyed by the diet.
7. Knowledge of food needs and ability to use techniques for monitoring food consumption and nutritional surveillance strategies in populations with specific physiological conditions, such as pregnancy, lactation, growth, senescence, and sports activity, and in pathological conditions.
8. Knowledge of the effects of overnutrition and undernutrition; ability to use techniques and methods for measuring body composition and energy expenditure; knowledge and application of techniques for assessing nutritional status and interpreting results.
9. Ability to fluently use (beyond Italian) the English language, in written and oral form, including disciplinary terminology.

STUDY PROGRAM ORGANIZATION The teaching activity is structured into lectures, seminars, laboratory exercises, company internships, specialized seminars, research activities, to acquire knowledge, skills, and abilities that facilitate entry into the labor market.
Attendance for classroom lectures is free and not mandatory.
The course, distributed over four semesters, includes frontal teaching, internship activities, and thesis preparation. Students may carry out the internship period within research structures provided by the University or at external research institutions or local, national, or international companies, subject to appropriate agreements.
The first year will be mainly oriented towards acquiring competencies in food processing technologies, agricultural microbiology, food safety, and agro-industrial economy and marketing. In this phase of the Master's Degree, the characteristic educational offer will be completed with an in-depth study of human nutrition physiology. Special attention has been given to preparing students in English language and ensuring the availability of other training activities to complete the educational offer.
The first-year educational offer will also gradually shift the focus from the study of foods to human health and well-being, with the educational offer progressing from food chemistry and biochemistry and nutrition to the treatment of nutrigenomics, nutrigenetics, and epigenetics, passing through the study of relationships between nutrition and intestinal microbiota.
The second-year educational offer will be mainly oriented towards the study of human nutrition in pediatric, adult, and geriatric age, under physiological and pathological conditions, with or without concurrent pharmacological therapies. The nutraceutical role of nutrients present in foods will also be deepened, and on the biosafety side, the quality and safety of animal origin foods.
The Course Council and individual teachers will work to promote internationalization, activating agreements with foreign research institutes and companies where students can carry out training periods aimed at acquiring new professional competencies.

Foreign qualification Fees and contributions Regulation Careers - Fees Roles President MARILENA FORMATO Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Biologist
- as a laboratory biologist, career opportunities include employment in microbiological and clinical chemistry analysis laboratories in hospital structures; in Immunotransfusion Centers, private laboratories, veterinary prophylactic institutes, biotoxicology sections of Regional Environmental Prevention Agencies (ARPA); in private companies and organizations managing wastewater treatment and disposal plants and quality control of liquid and solid waste;
- as a research biologist in public and private research centers, regional and national natural parks; in the pharmaceutical industry, both in human and veterinary fields; in the food and cosmetic industry;
- as a forensic biologist, i.e., biologists with "special technical skills" who can perform the delicate work of a forensic biologist with quality, as provided for in the recent memorandum of understanding signed between the National Order of Biologists, the Superior Council of the Judiciary and the National Forensic Council (March 12, 2019).
Registered professionals may also practice as a biologist officer and/or consultant in public and private research centers and in the public health sector of ASLs; in regional health departments; in the ecological and environmental protection sectors of regional and provincial administrations.
To practice as a free-lance biologist, it is necessary to pass the state exam and register with the Register of the Order of Biologists - Section A. Graduates registered in Section A are entitled to the professional title of Biologist.
Final exam characteristics.
For the completion of the Master's Degree, the candidate must submit a written dissertation on a topic defined with the supervisor, which must be consistent with the educational objectives of the course and aimed at deepening specific scientific themes. For experimental theses, a substantial portion of the data must be obtained by the student, and the committee must be able to determine the candidate's actual contribution.
The internship can be carried out at a university or non-university laboratory, national or international.
Required knowledge for access.
The two-year Master's Degree program has open access and is open to graduates who during their Bachelor's Degree acquired a good basic preparation in biological disciplines. Admission to the Master's Degree program requires a Bachelor's Degree in Biological Sciences (class 12 or L-13) or another foreign degree recognized as suitable. Admission is permitted to graduates holding other degrees provided their curriculum includes specific required courses, which will be listed in the course regulations.
For admission to the Master's Degree program, a Commission appointed by the Master's Degree Council will verify the possession of the required curriculum and the suitability of the preparation through a mandatory interview to which all intending to enroll must participate, including students enrolled conditionally.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Biologist
- as a laboratory biologist, career opportunities include employment in microbiological and clinical chemistry analysis laboratories in hospital structures; in Immunotransfusion Centers, private laboratories, veterinary prophylactic institutes, biotoxicology sections of Regional Environmental Prevention Agencies (ARPA); in private companies and organizations managing wastewater treatment and disposal plants and quality control of liquid and solid waste;
- as a research biologist in public and private research centers, regional and national natural parks; in the pharmaceutical industry, both in human and veterinary fields; in the food and cosmetic industry;
- as a forensic biologist, i.e., biologists with "special technical skills" who can perform the delicate work of a forensic biologist with quality, as provided for in the recent memorandum of understanding signed between the National Order of Biologists, the Superior Council of the Judiciary and the National Forensic Council (March 12, 2019).
Registered professionals may also practice as a biologist officer and/or consultant in public and private research centers and in the public health sector of ASLs; in regional health departments; in the ecological and environmental protection sectors of regional and provincial administrations.
To practice as a free-lance biologist, it is necessary to pass the state exam and register with the Register of the Order of Biologists - Section A. Graduates registered in Section A are entitled to the professional title of Biologist.

Communication Skills.
The student acquires appropriate skills and tools for communication in written and oral form and through the use of graphical and formal languages; computer skills related to data processing and presentation; the ability to work in a group; the ability to organize and present information on current biological topics. A significant moment for verifying communication skills is represented by the final exam. During this phase, the student uses suitable computer tools for technical-scientific communication, demonstrating an adequate level of knowledge of the English language in written and oral form.
Learning Ability.
The student acquires abilities that promote the development and deepening of competencies, with particular reference to learning innovative technologies, consulting bibliographic material, consulting specialized databases and retrieving other information available online.
Learning abilities are acquired throughout the study path, particularly during the internship period when the student is integrated into the research team of the scientific supervisor and must demonstrate the ability to independently address new study topics and new issues related to experimental activity.
Learning ability is verified through continuous assessment during the development of training activities, through the presentation of autonomously retrieved data and through the evaluation of the self-learning ability developed during the final exam activity.
