Foreign Degree Tuition and fees Regulation for Careers - Fees Roles Responsible for approving study plans CARLA BASSU Student mobility responsibility DAVID FINBAR BRETT President LOREDANA SALIS Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION are able to exercise their activity both as language instructors and as foreign language correspondents, with a high level of competence. They can, in fact, leverage their interdisciplinary preparation to personally use (or teach others) the linguistic structures they have mastered through their studies in the Course, directing these structures towards institutional-business-cultural relations with foreign countries (for example, they are capable of drafting letters in foreign language, preparing documents using sector-specific languages, conducting telephone conversations in foreign language, taking notes in foreign language, etc.) in the various multietnic and multicultural contexts where they may operate, both in Italy and abroad.
The expected employment opportunities also include providing consultancy services to local authorities and businesses (for example cooperatives or tourism sector companies), to local authorities and government institutions for the planning of complex multi-level tourist-cultural events (municipal, regional, national and international), and professional activities in public relations, image, and similar professions. Additionally, graduates in this Master's Degree Class will become experts in sustainable tourism promotion and local development; experts in regional and local development programs and plans, consultants in planning and participation, also as trainers, for events falling under conference tourism; authors of advertising texts; technical text writers; experts in travel agency programming; consultants in natural parks and reserves; researchers, graduate technicians and similar.
Final exam characteristics.
The final exam is public and consists of the discussion of a written thesis, prepared under the guidance of a supervisor and co-supervisor. The thesis may be written, in part or entirely, in the candidate's biennial foreign language. In the latter case, an integral translation into Italian must also be produced.
Required knowledge for admission.
To access the Course, it is necessary to hold a Bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
Admission is conditional on verifying personal preparation through passing an entrance exam and possessing specific curricular requirements, listed below:
18 CFU in the SSD of the first curricular language;
18 CFU in the SSD of the second curricular language;
6 CFU in the SSD L-LIN/01;
6 CFU in the SSD INF/01;
6 CFU in the SSDs M-GGR/01 or M-GGR/02.
The methods for verifying personal preparation and the required curricular requirements are detailed in the Course's Didactic Regulations.
Degree title awarded.

Communication Skills.
The graduate, thanks to solid and specific linguistic, literary, and cultural knowledge acquired through attendance and individual study and verified by passing the relevant exams, is able to communicate the acquired knowledge and skills in various disciplinary fields (public and private entities, national and international institutions and organizations of a social, political, humanitarian nature, etc.) and to interact with both specialist and non-specialist operators, offering project-oriented hypotheses and solutions aimed at resolving the themes and issues of interest to the target.
It is expected that graduates will achieve the following skills:
to interact orally, presenting independent ideas, receiving and giving instructions, initiating and developing dialectical exchanges with specialists and non-specialists; to speak in public; to write clearly and well-organized various text genres; to summarize and evaluate information from multiple written sources, even of scientific nature and level; to carry out written activities such as describing and arguing with audiences of any level.
These abilities must be complemented by: the ability to manage relations between foreign languages and cultures and to communicate, based on solid linguistic acquisitions (in at least two languages, in addition to Italian), the competence in using information and multimedia technologies, the knowledge acquired and the project elaborations connected, addressing both specialists and non-specialists in the field. Regarding linguistic aspects, both in Italian and in the foreign languages of study, they will focus, beyond the communicative and socializing aspect, on the specialized lexicons of activities related to tourism, territory, and local development with current management knowledge, which form the basis of cultural tourism.
The development of these skills will be pursued by granting ample space, alongside frontal teaching of courses, to teaching methods that actively involve the communicative competencies of students within lectures, seminars, and laboratories, both on the traditional verbal and written communication front and through the use of multimedia means. The acquisition of these competencies will be assessed through written and oral evaluations within individual courses and during the final thesis discussion.
These results will be achieved through teaching methods that vary partly depending on the disciplinary sector.

Autonomy of judgment.
The graduate in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION, applying the methodological and theoretical knowledge acquired and deepened in various disciplines, has the ability to manage complex situations and is capable of developing valid project solutions even based on partial or incomplete data.
The graduate, in addition to having developed learning and processing abilities based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge, is able to autonomously formulate critical judgment and reflect on professional deontology and ethics as an operator and cultural mediator at an international level.
It is expected that, through continuous and in-depth reflection on various scientific issues experienced during lectures and exercises in the disciplines comprising their course, graduates will acquire the ability to formulate autonomous judgments on complex issues. In particular, with reference to their field of study, it is expected that they will become:
a) capable of collecting, using, and interpreting data in the field of foreign languages and cultural and textual traditions, from both theoretical and applied perspectives, to solve complex linguistic, textual, and interpretative problems, developing personal perspectives and reading keys.
b) capable of theoretically assessing the problematic nature of concrete situations (e.g., in the fields of teaching, cooperation, integration, tourism, programming and governance processes of territory and local development), developing effective and complex problem-solving strategies and solutions.
Graduates of the class must possess:
- the ability to integrate acquired knowledge with new realities, formulating conscious judgments regarding ethical responsibilities, and expressing reflective processes and related conclusions.
Oral and/or written assessments, linguistic skills aimed at acquiring specialized lexicons, and the use of case simulations will be employed to better evaluate the desired increasing autonomy of judgment.
Learning ability.
The graduate in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION, after assimilating knowledge in different but closely related disciplinary fields to the objectives of the study program, having passed the examinations, is able to develop a self-learning ability enabling continued independent and original study.
Furthermore, they can access higher levels of specialization by participating with a high degree of research autonomy in Research Doctorates and/or National and International Master's Programs of I and II level.
It is expected that, thanks to the declarative and procedural knowledge acquired, especially during lectures and exercises in the disciplines studied and generally throughout all phases of their training, graduates will enhance their learning abilities, particularly developing: metacognitive strategies (reflection on language and the learning process); cognitive strategies (exploration of different learning styles and strategies, and recognition of individual needs related to the disciplines studied); communicative and social-affective strategies (through practice of the highest competencies achieved in L2).
These abilities and strategies will enable graduates to independently address subsequent studies, both in these specific fields and in related disciplinary areas.
The achievement of these results will be supported through the use of teaching methodologies that complement traditional instruction with guided research and application activities in teaching laboratories and internships, established in agreement with public and private entities, also foreign, operating in the tourism sector. In addition to verifications related to individual training activities through written and oral exams, the acquisition of solid linguistic skills and the ability to autonomously elaborate and apply diverse disciplinary contributions to complex problems in the fields of tourism sciences and linguistic communication will be assessed through the final thesis, which will consist of an original work prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor.
Knowledge and understanding.
LINGUISTIC-LITERARY AREA The student must acquire adequate linguistic knowledge and possess a high level of competence in at least one European or extra-European language. They must deepen the knowledge of the chosen foreign language(s), reaching a high level of competence in the first language and refining the level in the second language.
The student must also acquire in-depth knowledge in literary and philological studies; in particular, they must master the methodological tools offered by literary theory and philology through the study and analysis of primary sources; the relationship between text and context, and between language and literature, will be fundamental for the student's formation.
Oral and/or written assessments, possibly during the course, linguistic exercises (readings) to support and deepen the teaching of foreign languages, seminars with possible written and/or oral reports are considered teaching tools for verifying the acquired level of knowledge. Regarding literature and philology, students are encouraged to develop research tools, critical thinking, and text and context reading skills, also through participation in in-depth seminars and related teaching activities.
MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATICS AREA The objective of this area is to develop knowledge and methodological skills specific to management and informatics disciplines. In particular, the main computer and telecommunication tools, competencies related to new communication and information languages, appropriate computer tools for analysis, theoretical, methodological, and technical tools for the computer processing of texts and images within practical activities will be provided. This objective is complemented by transmitting knowledge regarding the main theories of business strategy and policy. The ultimate goal is to impart the principles underlying strategic management of companies, the techniques and tools used by economic subjects to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. Educational objectives will be pursued through activities that, beyond frontal lectures, include exercises, internships, and assisted study activities to facilitate the acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge in these disciplinary areas.
LEGAL AND ECONOMIC AREA The objective of this area is to provide solid knowledge in economic and legal disciplines. In particular, this area of knowledge aims to analyze in a comparative perspective the constitutional models of contemporary democracies, provide fundamental theoretical knowledge of administrative law, form a critical and interpretative evaluation of treaty norms, and experiment with the interpretation of acts in the field of navigation and land transport law.
This area also aims to equip students with basic knowledge in economic-statistical fields, particularly regarding the introduction to methods and statistical relationships, quantitative methods, position indices, and measures of variability. This knowledge will enable graduates to enter the workforce with awareness.
Educational objectives will be pursued through activities that, beyond frontal lectures, include exercises, internships, and assisted study activities to facilitate the acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge in these disciplinary areas.
Expected results will be verified through oral and/or written assessments, ongoing or final, aimed at verifying acquired knowledge and the ability to present it in an organized manner. The internship activity will be subject to specific evaluation by the hosting organization.
GEOGRAPHICAL, ANTHROPOLOGICAL AND SOCIAL AREA Graduates must demonstrate secure acquisition of methodological tools and linguistic-cultural, social, environmental, and anthropological knowledge capable of reinforcing and completing those acquired in the first cycle; important is also the achievement of personal autonomy in proposing and carrying out critical observations and original ideas in their study and research context, characteristic of geographical and anthropological disciplines, in order to use the studied languages consciously in the perspective of national and international communication. The objective of this area is to provide concepts and tools for understanding the dynamics of space use in relation to socioeconomic, environmental, and cultural change processes.
Particular attention will also be given to acquiring specific competencies related to the promotion of territorial resources and local development.
Oral and/or written assessments, possibly ongoing, participation in guided visits, seminars with possible written and/or oral reports are considered teaching tools for verifying the level of acquired knowledge.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
LINGUISTIC-LITERARY AREA The acquired knowledge must be the fundamental tool for navigating the professional world; graduates must be able to transfer and apply them practically, integrating and applying them to research and/or professional contexts in which they are inserted, with intellectual curiosity and individual ability to solve new or less common themes and problems within interdisciplinary contexts. Therefore, the graduate will be able to apply what has been learned, at the level expected by the training path, in performing assigned tasks.
Oral and/or written assessments (as well as linguistic exercises accompanying the teaching of foreign languages) will gradually evaluate the ability to apply acquired knowledge for solving non-routine problems. Particular emphasis will be placed on learning activities conducted at the University Language Center.
The graduate will be able to apply the linguistic and philological-literary knowledge acquired to the extent required in the professional context. In particular, students will be trained in critical thinking, sharing it in written and oral form, and will demonstrate having acquired the ability to critically read texts and contexts, with particular attention to the literary field. They will also develop autonomous study, research, and analysis skills in preparation for the final thesis and the potential application of literary disciplines in work experiences, internships, and training paths in Italy and abroad.
MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATICS AREA The objective of this disciplinary area is to develop the ability to use and apply knowledge in management and informatics contexts to the extent required in the professional world, to form a flexible and competent Master's graduate. In particular, abilities to use and apply knowledge related to business economics and management, concepts of strategy and business policy, strategic planning, evolution of strategic paradigms, basic theoretical and practical aspects of technological tools for content and document management, and the ability to effectively use tools for multimedia content production and computer-assisted translation will be developed. Students will have the opportunity to carry out internship activities, aimed at acquiring direct knowledge in sectors particularly useful for entering the workforce and acquiring specific professional skills. These activities can be carried out in line with the chosen curriculum.
LEGAL AND ECONOMIC AREA The objective of this disciplinary area is to develop the ability to use and apply knowledge in legal and economic contexts to form a Master's graduate capable of responding to the needs of contemporary work. Specifically, themes related to the examination of state and government forms in a comparative perspective, fundamental rights and instruments for recognition and protection at national and supranational levels, navigation and transport law, security, public administration activities and functioning will be developed. Particular care will be given to the foundational concepts of descriptive statistics, which will enable recognizing different types of statistical data and their specificities, correctly applying simple synthesis, analysis, and description methods for phenomena. These are essential topics for professional practice, which will have, as the primary interlocutor, direct or indirect relationships with public administration.
During the training path, graduates will begin to apply the acquired skills through an internship that will allow them to experience the concrete issues of the functioning of companies, entities, and other institutions.
GEOGRAPHICAL, ANTHROPOLOGICAL AND SOCIAL AREA The acquired knowledge in geographical, anthropological, and social fields must be the fundamental tool for navigating the professional world. Graduates must be able to transfer and apply them practically, integrating and applying them to research and/or professional contexts in which they are inserted, with intellectual curiosity and individual ability to solve new or less common themes and problems within interdisciplinary contexts connected to their field of study. Oral and/or written assessments will gradually evaluate the ability to solve non-routine problems.
The graduate will be able to apply the acquired knowledge in the geographical-anthropological-social area to the extent required in the professional context.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated functions.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development. The curriculum in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION has a primarily communicative function, particularly on an international level. This function will enable graduates to navigate with competence and confidence in all work contexts where interpersonal, verbal, and non-verbal relationships are central. Regarding the first, graduates will be able to manage verbal communication, both oral and written, not only in Italian but also and particularly in at least two foreign languages.
The competencies associated with the function of the curriculum FOREIGN LANGUAGES, TOURISM, TERRITORY AND LOCAL DEVELOPMENT specifically concern: territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development, considered in its physical, juridico-economic, social, cultural aspects and their interrelationships, in a sustainability perspective. In particular, competencies for managing tourist resources will be acquired.
The expected professional opportunities for the Degree Class are the following:
- cultural mediator, also in migration contexts; - operator in cultural services, journalism, publishing, and cultural institutions; - operator in international relations in Italian and foreign companies and societies; - operator in the tourism field, particularly cultural tourism; - linguistic assistant in company, entity, or public and private institution contexts, also through translation activities; - linguistic and cultural assistant in the context of language training and education; - translator and interpreter, after completing the training path, in accordance with current regulations; - teacher of foreign language and literature in primary and secondary schools, or Italian for foreigners, after completing the training path, in accordance with current regulations; - specialists in public relations and image, particularly regarding the sustainable tourism sector; - scholars and researchers, referring to scientific fields related to tourism's role in spatial organization, promotion, and territorial valorization; - experts in regional development programs and plans; - experts in sustainable tourism promotion and local development; - managers of travel agency programming and managers of social and cultural tourism; - consultant in natural parks and reserves; - professional with high-level consultancy tasks in tourism and orientation.
Function in work context.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development. Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION will be able to perform a primarily communicative function, particularly on an international and national level. This function will enable graduates to navigate with competence and confidence in all work contexts where interpersonal, verbal, and non-verbal relationships are central, with at least two foreign languages.
In particular, those in the CURRICULUM in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION must achieve adequate knowledge and skills in the chosen foreign languages and their respective cultural and literary context. They must also demonstrate possessing high theoretical-practical knowledge in sociological, geoeconomic, and legal fields, and the ability to understand cultural and communication processes that allow them to develop original and innovative ideas and convey them in multicultural and multiethnic contexts.
The Master's Degree Course curriculum named FOREIGN LANGUAGES, TOURISM, TERRITORY AND LOCAL DEVELOPMENT aims to promote the ability to operate in different territorial realities to promote responsible local development within the framework of international cooperation.
Basic theoretical knowledge will be developed and applied in specific research contexts (academic, professional, or technological) or in broader interdisciplinary contexts connected to the study fields.
The two curricula will develop:
- the ability to formulate autonomous critical judgments based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge;
- the ability to communicate (in different contexts, addressing specialists and non-specialists, Italians and foreigners) acquired knowledge and competencies, also based on solid linguistic preparation, both in Italian and in the studied foreign languages, clearly and without ambiguity; a learning ability in the various study areas (linguistic-communicative, sociological-economic-legal, territorial, literary, informatic) that enables them to continue studying independently and originally, and to access higher and further specialized study levels (University Master's Programs of I and II level and Research Doctorates).
Specific educational objectives description.
Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION will be able to perform a primarily communicative function, particularly on an international and national level. This function will enable graduates to navigate with competence and confidence in all work contexts where interpersonal, verbal, and non-verbal relationships are central, with at least two foreign languages.
In particular, students must achieve adequate knowledge and skills in the chosen foreign languages and their respective cultural and literary context. They must also demonstrate possessing high theoretical-practical knowledge in sociological-geoeconomic-legal fields, and the ability to understand cultural and communication processes that allow them to develop original and innovative ideas and convey them in multicultural and multiethnic contexts.
The Degree Class aims to train specialists in knowledge regarding linguistic, cultural, and managerial aspects required by the regional and international tourism system. Strongly supported by solid linguistic acquisitions, they will be able to design initiatives within the framework of sustainable tourism and territorial transformation and governance processes and local development, tourism initiatives in collaboration with foreign, national, or local entities, cultural events requiring broad and relevant coordination skills, as well as indispensable managerial knowledge.
Students' basic theoretical knowledge will be developed and applied in specific academic, professional, or technological contexts, or in broader interdisciplinary contexts connected to the linguistic study fields. They will also develop the ability to formulate autonomous critical judgments based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge; communicate in different contexts, knowledge and competencies acquired also based on solid linguistic preparation, both in Italian and in the studied foreign languages, demonstrating learning ability in the various study areas (linguistic-communicative, sociological-economic-legal, territorial, literary, informatic) sufficient to enable continued independent and original study and access to higher and further specialized study levels (University Master's Programs of I and II level and Research Doctorates).
The training path offers students a continuation of studies for those who have a degree in linguistic-communicative disciplines and have already acquired mastery of linguistic and computer tools for international use, but also for those who possess adequate theoretical and practical preparation in economic and socio-legal fields underlying tourism entrepreneurship and have acquired necessary operational skills for managing, promoting, and valorizing territorial resources.
The aim is to strengthen the necessary theoretical-practical tools for navigating the most varied contexts of linguistic communication, Italian and foreign, consolidating the theoretical and practical knowledge and skills students have acquired in the undergraduate training path, thus facilitating greater entry into the workforce or a possible continuation of studies in the field of second-level Master's programs. The interdisciplinary preparation (geographical, literary, economic, socio-cultural, and legal disciplines) aims to form a flexible Master's graduate in modern languages capable of positioning themselves as a mediator between different social and productive realities, not only due to linguistic competencies but also due to sensitivity to issues related to social and cultural development and integration processes. It prepares for employment in public and private companies in the commercial sector and human resources, and in management staff, especially in logistics sectors and national and international companies more involved in the globalization of the economy or active in the production and dissemination of culture, in the growing tourism sector in general, with particular reference to planning, management, and marketing sectors.
Finally, the structure of the path allows access to teaching in secondary schools, after obtaining the qualification through TFA.

Professional title conferred by the degree.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in processes of transformation and governance of the territory with particular reference to local development. The graduates of the Master's Degree in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION are able to exercise their activity both as a linguistic instructor and as a foreign language correspondent, with a high degree of competence. They can, in fact, leverage their interdisciplinary preparation to use (or teach to others) the linguistic structures they have mastered through their studies in the Course, directing such structures towards institutional, business, and cultural relations with foreign countries (for example, they are able to write letters in a foreign language, prepare documents using sector-specific languages, communicate by phone in a foreign language, take notes in a foreign language, etc.) in the various multietnic and multicultural contexts in which they may operate, both in Italy and abroad.
The expected career opportunities also include providing consultancy services to local authorities and businesses (for example, cooperatives or companies in the tourism sector), to local authorities and government institutions for the planning of complex tourist-cultural events at multiple levels (municipal, regional, national, and international), and professional activities in public relations, image, and similar professions. Additionally, graduates in this degree class will become experts in sustainable tourism promotion and local development; experts in regional and local development programs and plans, consultants in planning and participation, also as trainers, for events falling under conference tourism; writers of advertising texts; writers of technical texts; experts in travel agency programming; consultants in natural parks and reserves; researchers, graduate technicians, and similar.
Final exam characteristics.
The final exam is public and consists of the discussion of a written thesis (thesis), prepared under the guidance of a supervisor and co-supervisor. The thesis may be written, in part or in full, in the foreign language chosen by the candidate. In the latter case, an integral translation into Italian must also be provided.
Knowledge required for access.
To access the Course, it is necessary to hold a Bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma, or another title acquired abroad and recognized as suitable.
Admission is conditional on verifying personal preparation through the successful completion of an entrance exam and possession of specific curricular requirements, listed below:
18 CFU in the SSD of the first curricular language;
18 CFU in the SSD of the second curricular language;
6 CFU in the SSD L-LIN/01;
6 CFU in the SSD INF/01;
6 CFU in the SSDs M-GGR/01 or M-GGR/02.
The methods for verifying personal preparation and the required curricular requirements are detailed in the Course's Didactic Regulation.
Degree title awarded.

CURRICULUM: Communication Skills
SECTION: Communication Skills

Communication Skills.
The graduate, thanks to solid and specific linguistic, literary, and cultural knowledge acquired through attendance and individual study and verified by passing the relevant exams, is able to communicate the acquired knowledge and skills in various disciplinary fields (public and private bodies, national and international institutions and organizations of a social, political, humanitarian nature, etc.) and to interact with both specialists and non-specialists, offering project-oriented hypotheses and solutions aimed at addressing the themes and issues of interest to the target audience.
It is expected that graduates will achieve the following skills:
be able to interact orally, presenting independent ideas, receiving and giving instructions, initiating and developing dialectical exchanges with both specialists and non-specialists; be able to speak in public; be able to write clearly and well-organized various text genres; be able to summarize and evaluate information from multiple written sources, even of scientific nature and level; be able to carry out written activities such as describing and arguing for audiences of all levels.
These abilities must be complemented by: the ability to manage relations between foreign languages and cultures and to communicate, based on solid linguistic acquisitions (in at least two languages, besides Italian), the competence in using information and multimedia technologies, the knowledge acquired and the project elaborations connected, addressing both specialists and non-specialists in the field. Regarding linguistic aspects, both in Italian and in the foreign languages of study, they will focus, besides the communicative and socializing aspect, on the specialized lexicons of activities related to tourism, territory, and local development with updating of management knowledge, which form the basis of cultural tourism.
The development of such skills will be pursued by granting ample space, alongside frontal teaching of courses, to teaching methods that actively involve the communicative skills of students within readerships, seminars, and laboratories, both on the side of more traditional verbal and written communication, as well as through the use of multimedia means. The acquisition of such skills will be assessed through written and oral evaluations within individual courses and in the context of the final thesis discussion.
These results will be achieved through teaching methods that vary partly depending on the disciplinary field.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari

CURRICULUM: Curriculum
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10721?annoOrdinamento=2016

Autonomy of Judgment.
The graduate in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION, applying the methodological and theoretical knowledge acquired and deepened in various study disciplines, has the ability to manage complex situations and is capable of developing project-based solutions even based on partial or incomplete data.
The graduate, in addition to having developed learning and processing abilities based on acquired theoretical and professional knowledge, is able to autonomously formulate a critical judgment and reflect on professional ethics and deontology as an operator and cultural mediator at an international level.
It is expected that, through continuous and in-depth reflection on various scientific issues, which they experience during lectures and exercises in the disciplines that compose their course of study, graduates will acquire the ability to formulate autonomous judgments on complex issues. In particular, with reference to their field of study, graduates are expected to become:
a) capable of collecting, using, and interpreting data in the field of foreign languages and cultural and textual traditions, from both theoretical and applied perspectives, to solve complex linguistic, textual, and interpretative problems, developing personal perspectives and reading keys.
b) capable of theoretically assessing the problematic nature of concrete situations (e.g., in the fields of teaching, cooperation, integration, tourism, programming and governance processes of territory and local development), developing effective and complex problem-solving strategies and solutions.
Graduates of the class must possess:
- the ability to integrate acquired knowledge with new realities, formulating conscious judgments regarding ethical responsibilities, and expressing reflective processes and related conclusions.
Oral and/or written assessment tests, linguistic competencies aimed at acquiring specialized terminology, and the use of case simulations will be employed to better evaluate the increasingly autonomous judgment expected.
Learning Ability.
The graduate in FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES FOR CULTURAL MEDIATION AND TERRITORIAL VALORIZATION, after assimilating knowledge in different but closely related disciplinary fields to the objectives of the Course of Study (CdS), having passed the exams, is able to develop a self-learning ability capable of enabling them to continue studying in an autonomous and original manner.
Additionally, they can access higher levels of specialization by participating with a high degree of research autonomy in Research Doctorates and/or National and International Master's Programs of I and II level.
It is expected that, thanks to the declarative and procedural knowledge acquired primarily during lectures and exercises in the disciplines of study, and generally throughout all phases of their educational activities, graduates will enhance their learning abilities, particularly by developing:
- metacognitive strategies (reflection on language and the learning process);
- cognitive strategies (exploration of different learning styles and strategies, and identification of individual needs related to the disciplines studied);
- communicative and social-affective strategies (through practice of the highest competencies achieved in second languages).
These abilities and strategies will enable graduates to independently address subsequent studies, both in these specific fields and in related disciplinary areas.
The achievement of these results will be supported through teaching methodologies that complement traditional instruction with guided research and application activities in didactic laboratories and internships, established in collaboration with public and private entities, including foreign ones, operating in the tourism sector. In addition to assessments related to individual educational activities through written and oral exams, the acquisition of solid linguistic competencies and the ability to autonomously apply and solve complex problems using the various disciplinary contributions within tourism sciences and linguistic communication will be evaluated through the final thesis, which will consist of an original work prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor.
Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC-LITERARY AREA The student must acquire adequate linguistic knowledge and possess a high level of competence in at least one European or extra-European language. They must deepen their knowledge of the chosen foreign language(s), reaching a high level of competence in the first language and refining the level in the second language.
The student must also acquire in-depth knowledge in literary and philological studies; in particular, they must master the methodological tools offered by literary theory and philology through the study and analysis of primary sources; the relationship between text and context, and between language and literature, will be fundamental for the student's formation.
Oral and/or written assessment tests, possibly conducted during the course, linguistic exercises (readings) to support and deepen the teaching of foreign languages, seminars with possible written and/or oral reports are considered teaching tools for verifying the acquired level of knowledge. Regarding literature and philology, students are encouraged to develop research tools, critical thinking, and text and context reading skills, also through participation in in-depth seminars and related didactic activities.
MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATICS AREA The objective of this area is to develop knowledge and methodological skills specific to management and informatics disciplines. In particular, students will be provided with the main information and telecommunication tools, competencies related to new communication and information languages, appropriate information tools for analysis, theoretical, methodological, and technical tools for the computer processing of texts and images within the activities practiced. This objective is complemented by transmitting knowledge of the main theories of business strategy and policy. The ultimate goal is to impart the principles underlying strategic management of companies, the techniques and tools used by economic subjects to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. Educational objectives will be pursued through activities that, in addition to frontal lectures, include exercises, internships, and assisted study activities to facilitate the acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge in these disciplinary areas.
LEGAL AND ECONOMIC AREA The objective of this area is to provide solid knowledge in economic and legal disciplines. In particular, this area aims to analyze in a comparative perspective the constitutional models of contemporary democracies, provide fundamental theoretical knowledge of administrative law, form a critical and interpretative evaluation of treaty norms, and experiment with the interpretation of acts in the field of navigation and land transport law.
This area also aims to equip students with basic knowledge in economic-statistical fields, particularly regarding the introduction to methods and statistical relationships, quantitative methods, position indices, and measures of variability. This knowledge will enable graduates to enter the workforce with awareness.
Educational objectives will be pursued through activities that, in addition to frontal lectures, include exercises, internships, and assisted study activities to facilitate the acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge in these disciplinary areas.
Expected results will be verified through oral and/or written tests, conducted during the course or at the end, aimed at assessing acquired knowledge and the ability to present it in an organized manner. Internship activities will be subject to specific evaluation by the hosting organization.
GEOGRAPHICAL, ANTHROPOLOGICAL, AND SOCIAL AREA Graduates must demonstrate the secure acquisition of methodological tools and linguistic-cultural, social, environmental, and anthropological knowledge capable of reinforcing and completing those acquired in the first cycle; it is also important to achieve personal autonomy in proposing and carrying out critical observations and original ideas within their study and research context, characteristic of geographical and anthropological disciplines, in order to use the studied languages with awareness in the perspective of national and international communication. The objective of this area is to provide concepts and tools for understanding the dynamics of space use in relation to socioeconomic, environmental, and cultural change processes.
Particular attention will also be given to acquiring specific competencies related to the promotion of territorial resources and local development.
Oral and/or written assessment tests, possibly conducted during the course, participation in guided visits, seminars with possible written and/or oral reports are considered teaching tools for verifying the level of acquired knowledge.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC-LITERARY AREA The acquired knowledge must be the fundamental tool for navigating the professional world; graduates must be able to transfer and apply it practically, integrating and applying it to research and/or professional contexts in which they are involved, with intellectual curiosity and individual skills in solving new or less common themes and problems within interdisciplinary contexts. Therefore, the graduate will be able to apply what has been learned, at the level expected by the educational path, in the performance of assigned tasks.
Oral and/or written assessment tests (as well as linguistic exercises accompanying the teaching of foreign languages) will gradually assess the ability to apply acquired knowledge for solving non-routine problems. Particular emphasis will be placed on learning activities conducted at the University Language Center.
The graduate will be able to apply the linguistic and philological-literary knowledge acquired to the extent required in the professional context. In particular, students will be trained in critical thinking, sharing it in written and oral form, and will demonstrate the acquisition of critical reading skills for texts and contexts, with particular attention to the literary field. They will also develop autonomous study, research, and analysis skills in preparation for the final thesis and the potential application of literary disciplines in work experiences, internships, and training paths in Italy and abroad.
MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATICS AREA The objective of this disciplinary area is to develop the ability to use and apply knowledge in management and informatics contexts to the extent required in the professional world, aiming to form a flexible and competent Master's graduate. In particular, abilities to use and apply knowledge related to business economics and management, strategic and business policy concepts, strategic planning, the evolution of strategic paradigms, and the theoretical and practical aspects of technological tools for content and document management will be developed. Students will have the opportunity to engage in internships aimed at acquiring direct knowledge in sectors particularly useful for entering the workforce and acquiring specific professional skills. These activities can be carried out in line with the chosen curriculum.
LEGAL AND ECONOMIC AREA The objective of this disciplinary area is to develop the ability to use and apply knowledge in legal and economic contexts to form a Master's graduate capable of meeting the demands of contemporary work. Specifically, topics related to the examination of state and governance forms in a comparative perspective, fundamental rights and tools for recognition and protection at national and supranational levels, navigation and transport law, security, public administration activities and functioning will be developed. Particular attention will be given to the foundational concepts of descriptive statistics, enabling the recognition of different types of statistical data and their specificities, and the correct application of simple synthesis, analysis, and description methods for phenomena. These are essential topics for professional practice, which will primarily interact directly or indirectly with public administration.
During the educational path, graduates will begin to apply acquired competencies through an internship that will allow them to experience the concrete issues of the functioning of companies, entities, and other institutions.
GEOGRAPHICAL, ANTHROPOLOGICAL, AND SOCIAL AREA The acquired knowledge in geographical, anthropological, and social fields must be the fundamental tool for navigating the professional world. Graduates must be able to transfer and apply it practically, integrating and applying it to research and/or professional contexts in which they are involved, with intellectual curiosity and individual skills in solving new or less common themes and problems within interdisciplinary contexts related to their field of study. Oral and/or written assessment tests will gradually assess the ability to solve non-routine problems.
The graduate will be able to apply the acquired knowledge in the geographical-anthropological-social area to the extent required in the professional context.
Official Languages of Teaching and Assessment of Preparedness.
ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Function.
Expert in verbal and non-verbal communication in multicultural contexts, with specific attention to intercultural aspects; Expert in territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development. The competencies associated with the function of the curriculum FOREIGN LANGUAGES, TOURISM, TERRITORY, AND LOCAL DEVELOPMENT specifically concern: territorial transformation and governance processes, with particular reference to local development, considered in its physical, juridico-economic, social, cultural aspects, and their interrelationships, within a sustainability perspective. In particular, competencies for managing tourism resources will be acquired.
The expected professional opportunities for the Degree Class are as follows:
- cultural mediator, also in migration contexts; - operator in cultural services, journalism, publishing, and cultural institutions; - operator in international relations in Italian and foreign companies and societies; - operator in the tourism field, particularly cultural tourism; - linguistic assistant in company, public or private entity contexts, also through translation activities; - linguistic and cultural assistant in the field of language training and education; - translator and interpreter, following completion of the educational path, in accordance with current regulations; - teacher of foreign language and literature in primary and secondary schools, or Italian for foreigners, following completion of the educational path, in accordance with current regulations; - specialists in public relations and image, particularly in the field of sustainable tourism; - scholars and researchers, referring to scientific fields related to tourism's role in spatial organization, promotion, and territorial valorization; - experts in regional development programs and plans; - experts in sustainable tourism promotion and local development; - managers of travel agency programming and managers of social and cultural tourism; - consultant in natural parks and reserves; - professional with high-level consultancy tasks in tourism and orientation.

Program, Texts, and Objectives Professional status conferred by the title.
Expert in humanities disciplines and creator and producer in various sectors of culture and communication The Master's degree in Modern Philology is characterized by its vocation for excellence training that prepares for scientific research activities in various fields of the humanities, from linguistics to philology, arts, geo-history, and performance, in national and international research centers, and within the academic context (appointment as a specialist, project assignments, etc.). The degree obtained is a privileged requirement for participation in doctoral programs in research areas related to modern and contemporary humanities. The Master's graduate may also apply acquired linguistic knowledge for the critical revision of texts to be published, audiovisual, and multimedia. Alongside attention to the traditional publishing world, the possession of relational skills to propose in the socio-cultural market: as a specialist in various text types, the Master's graduate may be entrusted with promoting the image of a company, organization, or theater or film production company, writing texts, selecting and disseminating favorable publicity material, organizing and sponsoring events of particular importance and visibility, beneficial activities for the population, and similar activities not directly related to advertising promotion. Educated in a critical sense to exercise creativity, the LM-14 graduate possesses the skills to engage with the cultural industry market, in the field of literary writing, professional writing, and art criticism and history. The LM-14 graduate can interact fruitfully with public administration sectors operating on the territory for the valorization of cultural assets and, in the private sector, can leverage their cross-disciplinary skills by proposing themselves as teachers and experts in training and curriculum design. Finally, the degree obtained, supported by CFU acquired in the SSD required by regulation, and adequate credits for specific groups of sectors in psycho-social-pedagogical subjects, as provided by current regulations, constitutes the key to access competitive exams that enable teaching in literary and linguistic subjects in secondary schools of I and II degree (classes A-11 – Literary disciplines and Latin; A-12 – Literary disciplines in secondary schools of II degree; A-21 - Geography; A-22 – Italian, history, geography in secondary schools of I degree; A-23 – Italian language for foreign language students [Alloglotti]).
Final exam characteristics.
The Master's thesis consists of an original, well-structured, and in-depth dissertation prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor.
Required knowledge for admission.
To enroll in the Course, it is necessary to possess a Bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
For all students, admission is conditional on passing the verification test of the candidate's knowledge adequacy and possessing curricular requirements, which consist of holding a three-year Bachelor's degree in class L-10 or, for graduates in other classes, holding credits in specific scientific-disciplinary sectors detailed in the course's didactic regulation. During the admission interview, the possession of adequate B1 level competence in a chosen foreign language (English, French, Spanish, German) will also be verified. For details, refer to the Course's Didactic Regulation.
Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Expert in humanities disciplines and creator and producer in various sectors of culture and communication The Master's degree in Modern Philology is characterized by its vocation for excellence training that prepares for scientific research activities in various fields of the humanities, from linguistics to philology, arts, geo-history, and performance, in national and international research centers, and within the academic context (appointment as a specialist, project assignments, etc.). The degree obtained is a privileged requirement for participation in doctoral programs in research areas related to modern and contemporary humanities. The Master's graduate may also apply acquired linguistic knowledge for the critical revision of texts to be published, audiovisual, and multimedia. Alongside attention to the traditional publishing world, the possession of relational skills to propose in the socio-cultural market: as a specialist in various text types, the Master's graduate may be entrusted with promoting the image of a company, organization, or theater or film production company, writing texts, selecting and disseminating favorable publicity material, organizing and sponsoring events of particular importance and visibility, beneficial activities for the population, and similar activities not directly related to advertising promotion. Educated in a critical sense to exercise creativity, the LM-14 graduate possesses the skills to engage with the cultural industry market, in the field of literary writing, professional writing, and art criticism and history. The LM-14 graduate can interact fruitfully with public administration sectors operating on the territory for the valorization of cultural assets and, in the private sector, can leverage their cross-disciplinary skills by proposing themselves as teachers and experts in training and curriculum design. Finally, the degree obtained, supported by CFU acquired in the SSD required by regulation, and adequate credits for specific groups of sectors in psycho-social-pedagogical subjects, as provided by current regulations, constitutes the key to access competitive exams that enable teaching in literary and linguistic subjects in secondary schools of I and II degree (classes A-11 – Literary disciplines and Latin; A-12 – Literary disciplines in secondary schools of II degree; A-21 - Geography; A-22 – Italian, history, geography in secondary schools of I degree; A-23 – Italian language for foreign language students [Alloglotti]).

Communication Skills.
Graduates must be able to communicate, both orally and in writing, the acquired knowledge and skills through in-depth study of the specific disciplinary fields within human sciences, adapting the presentation to different audiences and situational specifics; they must demonstrate expressive and compositional abilities in creating scientific communications and written essays, taking into account the target audience, and thus develop linguistic capabilities in educational, popularizing, and scientific contexts. They must also be able to articulate reports utilizing computer support and audiovisual technologies. The graduate will be able to present the complexity of interpreting a textual or contextual system at conferences and seminars. Additionally, they will be able to offer forms of popularization for the general public through exhibitions and virtual media. This will be achieved through lectures and seminar and laboratory activities, with ongoing assessments. In particular, laboratory activities across various disciplinary fields (teaching of Italian literature, art criticism, musicology, creative writing, musicology) will serve as the medium through which technical communication skills are tested in simulated situations requiring the application of peer-to-peer argumentative strategies.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A041] LETTERS, MODERN PHILOLOGY AND CULTURAL INDUSTRY
TYPE: Master's Degree
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10722

Autonomy of Judgment.
Master's graduates in class LM-14 must be able to, with critical mastery and independence of judgment, compare acquired knowledge and skills with emerging events, problems, and phenomena in various life situations, using literary competencies related to the humanities as a productive tool for communication and interaction between different areas of knowledge. By the end of the Course, graduates will have developed the ability to address historical-interpretive themes and problems, even of an interdisciplinary nature, in an autonomous manner, demonstrating independence of judgment regarding the acquired informational, critical, and methodological background, which allows for the maturation of new hermeneutic perspectives. In this sense, autonomy of judgment will be exercised even in the presence of an incomplete information framework, through pedagogical training aimed at placing students before interpretative alternatives, of both philological and historical nature. Autonomy of judgment will be tested and verified by stimulating opportunities for synchronous (real-time) and asynchronous (via email, forums, etc.) interaction among peers and between students and the instructor; the privileged moment for verifying the acquired autonomy of judgment as a habitus will be the final exam, in which the graduate can appropriately express the acquired mastery of their own evaluation system and the ability to reflect and elaborate within specific cultural domains.

Learning Ability.
The Master's degree class LM-14 will be aimed at providing students with the ability to navigate the complex universe of literary sciences, with the possibility of deepening knowledge and skills related to individual humanities sectors, using conceptual and technical tools (in the fields of bibliographic, cartographic, documentary research, and didactic-educational) that enable them to quickly achieve secure competence even in areas not directly addressed during the course of study. The internalized habit of continuous updating (lifelong learning) in technical and cultural terms will facilitate graduates' relationship with further study experiences, such as second-level Master's programs and PhDs, as well as other work contexts related to tertiary and advanced tertiary activities, both nationally and locally. In this context, it will be of fundamental importance to evaluate the results achieved by students in internship activities, carried out abroad preferably within the international mobility programs initiated by the University, or alternatively in the laboratory activities that have been successfully conducted for several years within the Master's Degree Course.

Knowledge and Understanding.
I) AREA OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY HISTORY
The area of diachronic linguistics and literary history is characterized by its historical and philological vocation in conveying the traditional disciplinary content of humanism, especially within Italian literature, but also within Latin literature (ancient, medieval, and humanistic). Therefore, the history of the formation of Italian unfolds from the historical-linguistic study of epigraphic documents, which is embedded within the framework of Romance origins, in an evolutionary process rooted in Latin, viewed in the fluid transition that leads it to establish itself as the grammaticalized language of the cultivated koiné during the medieval and modern eras. The historical dimension is further expressed in the attention paid to diachronic processes that, in the modern era, mark continuities and fractures with the classical pedagogical concept of paideia.

II) AREA OF COMMUNICATION, ARTS, AND MULTIMEDIA
The area of communication, arts, and multimedia expresses its educational content within an interdisciplinary horizon oriented towards contemporaneity, in the vibrant dialectic between innovation and tradition in various arts (plastic arts, music, cinema) and literature. The relationship between media and cultural industry is critically, theoretically, and methodologically examined, in the practice of genre writing and in the dissemination and consumption within contexts not necessarily highbrow.

III) AREA OF LINGUISTIC DIDACTICS AND GEOHISTORY
The area of linguistic didactics and geohistory directs its educational offer towards the synchronic horizon where interference and integration between semiotic and linguistic codes of foreign origin mature. Linguistic acclimatization processes leading to the use of Italian as a vehicle language are studied, despite the disparity in approaches that favor assimilationist, transitional, or bilingual teaching. Knowledge of the territory, in its physical-anthropological dimension, using cartographic analysis, forms the basis for assessing the consistency and processuality of contemporary migration dynamics. Knowledge and linguistic didactic practice will abandon the 'intercultural dimension', understood as a process that focuses on the idea of knowing the culture of the language under study (static approach), instead characterizing itself as a comparison with the discursive practices of a community (the language-culture nexus), with educational feedback effects on the experience of the teacher-scholar (dynamic approach).

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
I) AREA OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY HISTORY
The student, with solid mastery of the methods and content of historical linguistics, will be able to read linguistic variation phenomena and apply advanced procedures for the restitution of literary textuality, using digital technologies in theoretical and laboratory settings. This will be implemented, especially through pedagogical disciplines, the ability to present acquired knowledge content didactically, also in view of potential entry into the teaching field.

II) AREA OF COMMUNICATION, ARTS, AND MULTIMEDIA
Supported by adequate competence in the international language of communication and its most recent literary developments, the student will be able to interpret the semiotic codes regulating expressiveness across various multimedia channels, in the tension between advanced and experimental developments in the artistic field and redundant reuse in the iconic and linguistic sphere of the advertising message. The semiotic aspect is applied in the practical context of presenting and consuming the artistic phenomenon, both in the curation of exhibitions and in the analysis of editorial mechanisms directing the fortunes of writing in various genres, especially narrative.

III) AREA OF LINGUISTIC DIDACTICS AND GEOHISTORY
Through the study of dynamics, also from a translation perspective, that lead Italian to be assimilated as a secondary socialization or schooling language, and thanks to the simulation of typical didactic situations, the student will be able to reflect humanistically on the complexity of a pedagogy that shifts attention from purely cognitive aspects of the learner to the person in their entirety, including emotional, motivational, psychological aspects, and the "physical" dimension of learning; they will have acquired the theoretical and curricular tools that, in conjunction with other qualifications required by regulations, will allow them to participate in the entrance exams for qualification in class A-23.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Expert in Humanities Disciplines and Creator and Producer in Various Sectors of Culture and Communication
- autonomous critical approach to the principles of textual production and reception, in literary, artistic, historical, and geographical contexts. The ability to penetrate the principles of textual codification, studied diachronically, allows the Master's graduate, as a communication specialist, to draw maps and connect nodes between various types of structured communication that fluctuate within the fluid universe of modern liquid society;
- full mastery of the philological methodology leading to the retrieval, critical study, and use of sources, which the Master's graduate applies to the systems of conservation and valorization of cultural heritage;
- full awareness of the socio-economic mechanisms governing the dissemination and promotion of publishing products;
- specific and targeted glottological and linguistic competence regarding the formation, change, and transmission of the Italian language, used as a vehicle language for educational purposes, even with non-native speakers;
- appropriate use of the main computer tools and telecommunication tools in specific areas of competence.

Master's degree graduates will be able to, based on the described competencies, perform high-responsibility functions in the following areas:
- organizing exhibitions and events linked to the territory, highlighting the archaeological, linguistic, and cultural specificities of individual realities, without neglecting aspects of broader social impact, such as theater and cinema, and managing press offices for festivals and similar initiatives;
- organizing and participating in literary, artistic, visual, and multimedia awards, involving other educational realities such as schools and interacting with them;
- collaborating and supporting cultural activities promoted by public and private foundations requiring specific competencies in literary, editorial, and historical-artistic fields;
- Master's degree graduates will be able to exercise high-responsibility functions in various sectors of the cultural industry and cultural institutions, both domestic and foreign, as well as in all areas requiring specific disciplinary competencies, even in the digital field, combined with critical ability and skill in representing knowledge.

Function in the Workplace.
Expert in Humanities Disciplines and Creator and Producer in Various Sectors of Culture and Communication
The function of the LM-14 graduate will be to direct offices, sectors, and structures; coordinate services; ideate and design advertising campaigns, products, solutions; plan initiatives, shows, and events; collect, preserve, and valorize documents and materials; conduct complex research independently; select, teach, and train.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's degree course in LM-14 bases its educational offer within the field of humanities studies. The humanism that serves as the foundation for its educational plan aims at the contemporary world, but is also aware of the continuities and persistences of past traditions, including classical and Christian ones, which are at the roots of European identity. The course name was chosen referring to that sanctioned by the ministerial declaration, amplified and specified to make visible a continuity with the immediately congruent three-year degree (in L10), and to explicitly state its dynamic and communicative vocation, in the local/global dialectic affecting the production and consumption of cultural goods. The course's detailed project spectrum, on one hand, directs towards research in all areas connected with literary studies (with perspectives towards master's programs, specialization schools, and PhDs); on the other hand, constitutes an institutional access channel to the relevant teaching competition classes. Alongside preparation for advanced scientific education and teaching, the Master's course also opens a channel for further educational development, linked to the mass media, editorial, theatrical, and communicative dimensions, with practical experiences of acquired disciplinary competencies through laboratory exercises and internship conventions, and offers the possibility to refine linguistic competence in the main languages of the European Union, as per QCER. The Master's degree course thus prepares Master's graduates capable of meeting the demands of the territory and regional labor market, but also of proposing and valorizing acquired competencies on a supraregional scale, forming cultural operators able to relate with full awareness of their social significance and relevance, and their impact in the business and territorial context, with the procedures for implementing events, exhibitions, initiatives in the fields of cultural promotion, arts, publishing, and public relations, in collaboration with local authorities, foundations, philological centers, cultural institutions not only regional but also national and foreign, and more generally regarding the various dimensions of publishing enterprises, both traditional and electronic. Specifically within the educational path, Master's graduates, depending on the chosen path, will be able to acquire in-depth preparation, aimed at developing autonomous critical abilities in the fields of modern philology (L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/13 Italian Literary Philology, and L-FIL-LET/09 Romance Philology) and ancient, medieval, and humanistic philology (L-FIL-LET/04 Latin Philology and L-FIL-LET/08 Medieval and Humanistic Latin Literature); they will acquire theoretical and methodological tools, articulated according to different approaches, necessary for acquiring versatile and critical communication abilities related to the arts (L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Literature and Experimentation, L-ART/03 Contemporary Art History, L-ART/06 Film History and Criticism, L-ART/07 Music History); they will be able to fully utilize the main critical analysis tools in the sphere of cultural goods production and consumption linked to the territory (M-DEA/01 Media Anthropology, M-PED/02 Literature and Writing for Children, L-FIL-LET/14 Literary Criticism and Publishing; M-GGR/01 Geography); they will know how to apply, with full awareness of their significance, linguistic and glottological tools to Italian language teaching in the context of training and integration of non-native speakers (L-FIL-LET/12 Italian Linguistics, L-LIN/01 General Linguistics, L-LIN/02 Teaching of Modern Languages). In order to specialize in humanities knowledge linked to the territory, some disciplines are also presented in their more specific variant (L-FIL-LET/12 History of the Italian Language in Sardinia, L-LIN/01 Sardinian Linguistics and Dialectology, L-ANT/03 Roman Sardinian History, L-FIL-LET/09 Sardinian Medieval Text Philology, L-FIL-LET/13 Sardinian Literature and Philology, L-ART/03 Sardinian Art History, L-ART/07 Sardinian Music History, M-GGR/01 Sardinian Geography). The LM-14 course will also use specific laboratories for students' practical training, including the Creative Writing Laboratory, the Curatorial Practices Laboratory, the Musicology Laboratory, the Cartography Laboratory, the Author Philology Laboratory, and the Latin Translation Laboratory. The Language Laboratories for Sardinian, Algherese, Sassarese, and Gallurese are directed at students in the Sardinian Languages and Cultures curriculum. The Master's course will use frontal lectures and practical exercises, carried out using advanced telecommunication and electronic tools, with teaching activities that will also have a seminar-like character.

Program, texts and objectives
Professional status conferred by the title.
Archaeologist
Archaeologists will be able to work with fixed-term and permanent employment contracts at public bodies (Universities, Research Institutes, Archaeological Superintendencies, Museum Complexes, Unions of Municipalities, etc.) and some private entities (Construction Companies, Cooperatives, Scientific Societies, Professional Studios, etc.) that operate directly or indirectly in the field of archaeological research. Master's degree graduates in Archaeology will therefore be able to operate with coordination functions in archaeological excavation sites, both in relation to study, valorization, recovery and restoration projects of archaeological heritage, and in the case of emergency interventions or scheduled excavations within public and private tenders.
Researcher
In the research sector, employment opportunities lead towards the figure of the archaeologist and/or the graduate technician at public and private research bodies and institutes. The Master's degree allows one to work as archaeologists in excavation sites and to participate in the selection of professionals within specific research projects activated by Universities and other public bodies (Municipalities, Superintendencies).
Museum activities coordinator
Various technical-scientific roles may be held within various public and private bodies such as: Archaeological, artistic, ethnographic museums, Picture galleries, Antiquities, Foundations and other cultural places and institutions. Graduates will be able to work on projects for the cataloging, classification and publication of tangible and intangible cultural heritage supported and funded by public and private bodies; on interventions for updating information material and rearranging public and private museum collections; on public reception services and educational initiatives; and in the preparation of scientific-popular content.
Final exam characteristics.
The graduation exam consists of the writing of an original written work (on a topic agreed with a Supervisor) that is well-structured and in-depth, and the subsequent discussion of the same; the topic must be consistent with the educational path followed by the student, and, through the work, the candidate must demonstrate having acquired adequate knowledge on the chosen specific topic and the necessary methodological, critical and communication skills.
Required knowledge for access.
Three-year degree in Cultural Heritage Sciences (L-1) or equivalent of the old regulations, for those who have acquired at least 48 CFU of which 30 CFU in archaeological disciplines and 18 CFU in historical disciplines (curricular requirement) as detailed below:
- 6 CFU in SSD L-ANT/10 (Archaeological research methodologies);
- 24 CFU in the following SSD: L-ANT/01 (Prehistory and Protohistory), L-ANT/06 (Etruscology and Italian antiquities), L-ANT/07 (Classical Archaeology), L-ANT/08 (Christian and Medieval Archaeology), L-ANT/09 (Ancient Topography), L-OR/05 (Archaeology and art history of the Ancient Near East), L-OR/06 (Phoenician-Punic Archaeology);
- 18 CFU in the following SSD: M-STO/01 (Medieval History), M-STO/02 (Modern History), M-STO/04 (Contemporary History), M-STO/09 (Paleography), L-ANT/02 (Greek History), L-ANT/03 (Roman History).
The Master's Degree Course can also be accessed by:
- students in possession of the degree in Cultural Heritage Sciences (L-1) who have not earned the 48 CFU required for direct access,
- or graduates in other classes,
- or students who graduated abroad.
In these cases, the individual curriculum (above-mentioned curricular requirements) and personal preparation will be evaluated by a special commission, which may establish any necessary alignment training paths.
It will also be necessary to demonstrate mastery, written and oral, of at least one European Union language (level B1 - referring to the CEFR classification - Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) in addition to Italian.
The possession of the curricular requirements and the student's preparation for access to the Master's Degree Course is verified through an interview with a special commission.
Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in ARCHAEOLOGY
