Critical Judgment.
The title of Doctor in Tourism Planning, Management, and Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Itineraries will be awarded to students who have achieved the ability to collect and interpret data and information useful for determining autonomous and scientific judgments, with particular reference to territorial transformation processes, protection and valorization of cultural assets in the broadest possible sense, risk assessment, social and environmental emergencies, at local, national, and international levels. The acquisition of such abilities will be achieved through guided practical exercises linked to some courses, and will find further development and deepening in the activities for the preparation of the final exam.
Verification of the achieved ability to formulate autonomous and scientifically grounded judgments will occur during the examination moments of the core courses and, especially, those specifically oriented.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Cultural, Territorial, and Landscape Area The graduate must possess a body of knowledge in areas related to the study of the territory, geographical, geo-cartographic, literary, musical, artistic, archaeological, historical, and anthropological emergencies that characterize the cultural and social landscape and allow for understanding and applying strategies useful for the valorization of tourism resources. The study of Geography, Regional Geography, Economic Geography, Territorial Systems and geo-economic models, Territorial Development and Tourism, Cultural, Landscape, and Environmental Resource Planning and Management, as well as Tourism Sociology, will provide the graduate with a good awareness of complex phenomena related to contemporary reality, both in relation to the peculiarities of the local territory and in an increasingly indispensable globalized perspective. To these competencies are added knowledge related to natural and urban landscapes and their changes (Architecture, Culture, and Environment), which are studied both from a cultural perspective (Tourism Anthropology and Audiovisual Landscapes) and from a scientific-health perspective (Environmental and Territorial Hygiene, Nutraceuticals and Pharmacology). Thanks to the study of literature, the graduate has a good preparation in the field of narratives and their potential in the context of cultural tourism and its valorization. Additionally, the graduate will have a good preparation in the historical, literary, artistic, and archaeological fields, both in the ancient context (Archaeology and Analysis of Territorial Systems of the Nuragic Age, Economic and Social History of Roman Sardinia) and in the modern and contemporary context (History of Music in Sardinia, Curatorial Practices and Museum Management); such knowledge allows them to understand the richness of territories and the potential for development and valorization of cultural assets present therein.

Economic and Statistical Area The graduate in L 6 will have good knowledge of the economic geography field as well as useful statistical notions that will allow them to navigate the complex territory of tourism planning. The graduate is indeed a hybrid figure, trained in interdisciplinarity, since they must necessarily combine traditional humanistic knowledge relevant to the Cultural and Territorial Area described above with a more technical body of knowledge. Thanks to the study of Economics and Business Management and of Territory Measurement and Analysis, they will possess good capabilities for reading and interpreting data and economic flows related to tourism and its spin-offs, and will also be capable of applying innovative implementation and sustainable development strategies.

Linguistic and Communication Area The graduate, in addition to a good knowledge of the Italian language, general linguistics, and Sardinian linguistics, will master the chosen linguistic disciplines for exchanging information in the specific tourism field, having had the opportunity to choose at least two foreign languages from English, Spanish, and German. The acquisition of such competencies is ensured not only by institutional Language and Linguistics courses, but also by opportunities for study abroad through student mobility (Erasmus and Erasmus Placement Programs). The study of languages will ensure the acquisition of a good general and sector-specific preparation, and the ability to use the chosen languages fluently in the exchange of current information, as well as through the use of new communication techniques in the specific tourism sector. Within the framework of communication skills, the graduate will also have good preparation in the field of computer science and new technologies adopted in the GIS Laboratory, since social communication, careful use of network resources, and the ability to handle basic computer tools will be indispensable skills for a training path aimed at the valorization of cultural and sustainable tourism.

Legal Area The graduate in this Course of Study possesses good knowledge of the legal field that allows them to navigate the regulatory framework governing tourism offerings, programming, and promotion (Tourism Public Law and Comparative Public Law). The graduate, thanks to the study of legal disciplines, will indeed have the necessary competencies to navigate the opportunities offered by European measures and national and regional policies within the field of cultural and sustainable tourism.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Cultural, Territorial, and Landscape Area The graduate in L 6 will be able to apply the acquired cultural and territorial knowledge in the concrete scenario of cultural and sustainable tourism. Indeed, they are capable of imagining alternative geographical, historical, artistic, musical, cultural, and natural itineraries that valorize the territory's cultural heritage, particularly but not exclusively local, in order to expand and enrich the tourism offer in the cultural and regional environmental sustainability aspect.

Economic and Statistical Area The graduate in L 6 will have the ability to apply the acquired geo-economic knowledge within the vast and complex field of tourism planning and will be able to identify useful tools for businesses and for planning initiatives to enhance the tourism offer. Additionally, they will be able to analyze data and information related to the territory and apply appropriate management strategies for the valorization, promotion, and development of cultural and sustainable tourism.

Linguistic and Communication Area The graduate in L 6 will be able to apply the acquired linguistic and communication knowledge within the broad panorama of tourism communication. Therefore, they are able to produce texts related to the territory and tourism valorization in both Italian and the chosen foreign languages; and are also able to communicate tourism-related content appropriately, effectively, and fluently in Italian and the chosen foreign languages during conversation. The acquired computer skills finally allow them to navigate the web and produce content useful for promoting and valorizing sustainable and cultural tourism on the internet, social networks, and the main information dissemination channels.

Legal Area The graduate in L 6 will be able to employ the acquired legal competencies to navigate and move within the regional and community legislative landscape. They will also be able to interpret fundamental public law norms and institutions, analyze and identify the main forms of legal organization of businesses, and analyze the legal relationships between parties involved in business-labor.

Graduates are able to effectively use, in written and oral form, at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian. They possess specific competencies regarding local development strategies, territorial marketing, wellbeing, and the legislation of cultural, landscape, and environmental assets.

Function in the Work Context.
Tourism, Cultural, and Environmental Consultant
- Consultant in territorial and environmental fields
- Expert in multimedia products and audiovisual documentation
- Expert in landscape analysis and GIS representations
- Expert in environmental, historical-cultural, and tourism context analyses
- Coordinator of interdisciplinary work groups
- Consultant for organizing cultural events and exhibitions
- Consultant for regional and municipal urban plans
- Consultant for regional and municipal strategic plans
- Consultant for landscape-ambiental plans
- Operator in the field of cultural and environmental promotion of the territory
- Operator in the field of managing advanced cultural tourism systems for territory valorization
- Operator in the field of scientific dissemination and specialized publishing on cultural aspects of the territory
- Operator at public and private entities involved in the management of cultural and environmental assets.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The dual and connected relationship between physical and anthropic components and between environmental and population health currently holds great significance for the implications that may arise at various levels. The interdisciplinary perspective becomes pivotal for a varied series of aspects and phenomena, such as: the interpretation of existing components and current trends, aspects related to quality of life, demographic, economic spheres, etc.; the prospects for recovery and development within the capacity of ecosystems to respond and bear load; the reduction of inequalities and territorial disparities; the active valorization of historical-cultural and environmental assets in a patrimonialization perspective. Therefore, it becomes appropriate to train figures with integrated competencies, capable of providing a careful interpretative reading of the processes and phenomena developing and a detailed and relational analysis of the elements characterizing different contexts, at local and global scales. In this perspective, the course in Tourism Planning, Management, and Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Itineraries aims to train figures who can combine interdisciplinary knowledge and content and systematize various abilities and application competencies for synthesis analysis and territorial screening.

The first block of courses is designed and structured to provide foundational knowledge preparatory for the knowledge of the two subsequent blocks, at the geographical level (M-GGR/01), historical, social, archaeological (L-ANT/03, L-ANT/01, and SPS/10), and economic (SECS-P/08) levels, which are constantly linked to the understanding of the relationships between culture, environment, and landscape (ICAR/20). Additionally, an optional group of linguistic courses is provided.

The second block aims to provide more specific competencies at the environmental, territorial, and management of landscape and local resources level (M-GGR/02) with in-depth studies in the field of literature (L-FIL-LET/14 and L-FIL-LET/11). A specific focus is dedicated to economic functionality and management of public and private enterprises with in-depth studies in the statistical field (SECS-S/01) and the analysis of public law institutions from a comparative perspective (IUS/21), with particular reference to the attribution of normative and administrative competencies on the territory, with an aim to provide tools for knowledge and application of relevant legal institutions in national, regional, local, and comparative contexts. Concurrently, the deepening of linguistic competencies is also planned.

In the third block, the course focuses on territorial and tourism development from an anthropological and legal perspective (M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, M-DEA/01, and IUS/09) with a view also to the field of hygiene and environment (MED/42). The study of the representation and dissemination of the landscape and local cultural heritage in the linguistic and artistic field in general (L-LIN/01, L-ART/06) will be deepened, thus moving towards delicate and highly relevant directions at national and international levels, and combining the qualitative-perceptual-emotional component with the more purely technical-planning component. In the third block, in addition to further elective disciplines and a group of practical-laboratory activities, internship or stage activities are also provided for students at public or private sector enterprises.

Certain relevance, within the training path, is also attributed to other knowledge useful for entering the workforce, with often laboratory-type training activities, focusing on geotechnology or aimed at addressing current theme-problems, and internships. By combining direct and indirect observation, teamwork experiences, and activities with a high participatory component, the course aims to train figures that can serve as a bridge between specialists from different sectors and bring added value and original elements to interdisciplinary research.

Junior Computer Engineer The main expected employment opportunities refer to the following sectors:
- Computer industries, operating in hardware and software development,

Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, students must have regularly attended the training activities and earned the credits specified in the curriculum.
The final exam consists of developing a technical-practical project under the guidance of a supervising lecturer. This project must synthesize as much as possible the basic and specific skills acquired over the three years of training. The outcome of this activity (which may or may not include a demonstrator) must be summarized in a written report explaining the activities carried out and the results achieved. The report must also demonstrate correct use of sources and bibliography, systematic and argumentative skills, and clarity in presentation. The project is discussed before a specially appointed committee. On the student's request, the final report may be written in English.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the degree course, one must hold a high school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent. An adequate initial preparation is also required. In particular, the following are required: knowledge of spoken and written Italian, logical reasoning ability, knowledge and ability to use the main results of elementary mathematics and experimental sciences.
Since the course is delivered in Italian and English, students must possess an adequate level of English. If not present, a level not lower than B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages must be acquired and verified during the first year of studies, through initiatives agreed with the University Language Center and/or accredited external bodies; for this purpose, students are awarded 3 ECTS without a grade.
The Course Regulations detail the procedures for awarding these ECTS. The Course Regulations also provide for additional training obligations to be fulfilled in the first year of the course, in case the verification of the required knowledge for admission is not successful.
Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Junior Computer Engineer The main expected employment opportunities refer to the following sectors:
- Computer industries, operating in hardware and software development,
- Automation industries,
- Industries operating in the telecommunications sector.
- Electronic, electromechanical companies, design and production of components and systems.
- Agri-food industries, manufacturing industries.
- Public administration.

Communication skills.
The graduate will be able to effectively communicate data, information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors.
To prepare students for these outcomes, the course will include training activities requiring the presentation of individual or group project work, publicly presented through oral communications and demonstrations. Students' communication skills will also be stimulated during seminars and in assessment tests based on written reports and oral presentations of the same. Finally, the final exam will require the preparation of a report and a concise presentation to be publicly delivered during the graduation session.
Learning abilities.
The graduate will have developed the necessary learning abilities to pursue, with a high degree of autonomy, advanced studies, as well as to continuously update and improve their own skills.
The achievement of the aforementioned abilities is supported by training activities in the disciplinary areas identified in the current curriculum, particularly those carried out with partial autonomy.
The specific teaching methodologies used include, among others, tutoring activities.
The assessment of the achievement of learning abilities is subject to the various exam tests provided for in the course.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A106] COMPUTER ENGINEERING English Italian
SECTION: Independent Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10796

Independent Judgment.
The graduate will be able to collect, filter, and interpret data in the field of Information Engineering, and develop an independent judgment on the technical-scientific relevance of such data. They will be able to correctly identify and interpret the concrete terms of typical professional problems for a junior Information Engineer. The graduate will know how to select, process, and evaluate the necessary knowledge for solving such problems and will have the ability to draw appropriate conclusions.
Independent judgment will be developed primarily through exercises, organized seminars, projects, preparation of reports, and tasks assigned by the supervisor for the final thesis preparation.
Where possible, project activities will be organized in groups to allow students to engage in a productive and dynamic exchange of their judgment capabilities with peers.
The acquisition of independent judgment will be verified through the evaluation of maturity demonstrated during exams and during the preparation activity for the final thesis.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Mathematics, Computer Science, and Statistics The examined training path will, upon completion, allow the student to know and understand the methodological-operational aspects of computer science, mathematics, and statistics related to Information Engineering. In particular, for the learning area in question, these knowledge areas, achieved through the following training activities, will include: structured procedural programming (C language) and object-oriented programming (C++, Java); data structures, problem analysis, and algorithmic problem solving; differential and integral calculus for functions of one or more variables; linear algebra and analytical geometry; differential equations and systems; probability spaces and random variables; basic methods for solving linear systems and calculating integrals; solving ordinary differential equations.
Physics and Chemistry Regarding the area "Physics and Chemistry," always related to Information Engineering, in the present training path, the student, through the successful completion of the related disciplinary activities, will achieve the following learning objectives: knowledge and understanding of the basic aspects of physics and general chemistry; knowledge and understanding of the structure of matter, classification of elements, electrochemistry, and elements of organic chemistry; knowledge and understanding of the mechanics of a point and a system of points, as well as rigid body mechanics, deformable bodies, and fluids, and elements of quantum mechanics; knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of thermodynamics and electromagnetism; knowledge and understanding of the wave equation for electric and magnetic fields and electromagnetic waves; knowledge and understanding of general methodologies for designing measurements of physical quantities.
Engineering Upon completion of the course, with reference to the Engineering learning area, students will acquire the necessary knowledge to achieve the educational objectives, as identified for the following macro areas:
1) Computer Engineering;
2) Automation Engineering;
3) Electronic Engineering;
4) Telecommunications Engineering.
1) Within the field of Computer Engineering, the following foundational knowledge will be acquired: Boolean Algebra and logic circuits; knowledge of digital design modules: combinatorial and sequential circuits; methods for designing finite state machines; VHDL language; Assembler language; internal organization and operating principles of a processing system; processing system architectures; database design; Relational Model; SQL language; Entity-Relationship Model; web application development; principles of Software Engineering; principles and methods of concurrent programming; operating system architecture; telecommunication and computer networks; protocols and programming underlying modern computer networks.
2) Within the field of Automation Engineering, the following foundational knowledge will be acquired: modeling, classification of systems and models; analysis of dynamics and stability; the control problem: frequency response and design in the frequency domain.
3) Within the field of Electronic Engineering, the following foundational knowledge will be acquired: physics and technology of semiconductors; small and large signal models of transistors; semiconductor memory technology and structures; difference between analog and digital signals; characteristics and models of operational amplifiers; use of negative and positive feedback in electronic circuits; interconnection of electronic devices and systems; main characteristics of amplifiers; energy management in electronic systems; principles of operation of electronic measurement instrumentation.
4) Within the field of Telecommunications Engineering:
- Detailed knowledge of the Fourier transform domain; methodologies for analyzing continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems, both deterministic and random; design of digital filters; numerical signal processing methodologies; knowledge of telecommunications and computer networks; detailed knowledge of the techniques and protocols underlying modern Internet networks; main network layer protocols.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Mathematics, Computer Science, and Statistics With reference to the above-disciplined knowledge, the graduate will acquire the ability to use the acquired methodological tools for studying and solving problems.
In particular, upon completion of the training path, the graduate will be able to: use structured programming for data representation and algorithm implementation; study single-variable functions (limits, derivatives, integrals); solve analytical geometry problems in the plane and space (lines, planes, spheres, circles, conic sections, and quadrics); solve calculus and differential systems problems; solve probability problems; use computer tools for solving linear systems, approximating numerical data and functions, calculating integrals, and solving ordinary differential equations with initial values; recognize and correctly use the main components of a computer.
Physics and Chemistry At the end of the study cycle, through the provided tools, the graduate will be able to apply the acquired disciplinary competencies, achieving the following results: ability to calculate chemical equilibria, electrochemical systems, and solutions; ability to apply models or abstract mathematical concepts to real and concrete scientific problems in the fields of mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, and optics; ability to design and implement the measurement of a physical quantity and analyze the results; ability to determine the electrical properties of matter (semiconductors: electrical resistance, mobility, and carrier concentration); ability to solve elementary electromagnetism problems.
Engineering With reference to the above-specified knowledge for the area in question, the graduate will be able to put into practice the specific disciplinary competencies acquired.
Regarding the macro areas already identified, the graduate will be able to:
1) within the field of Computer Engineering: apply programming paradigms to real cases (problem solving); develop a software project using object-oriented programming paradigms; analyze and design databases through the application of the relational model; create a database query in SQL language; manage the resources of a processing system through system programming; use Linux operating system administration commands and system calls; design an information system (application program, computer architecture, computer network) and verify its correctness in the laboratory or through simulations; use software to assist in the design of digital circuits; evaluate an information system in terms of hardware module cost and processing time required for a process; use the correct level of programming language abstraction based on the problem specifications.
2) within the field of Automation Engineering: build a model (for electrical, mechanical, thermal systems); design control loops on real stable, weakly damped, and unstable systems.
3) within the field of Electronic Engineering: numerically evaluate the most relevant quantities of semiconductor materials at equilibrium and out of equilibrium; use operational amplifiers to create amplifiers; use an electronic oscilloscope in measurements of complex waveforms; design macroblocks capable of realizing basic functions such as amplifiers, filters, interconnections, conversions, and power supplies.
4) within the field of Telecommunications Engineering: use methodologies for analyzing continuous-time signals and systems, both deterministic and random; use computer tools for numerical signal processing; use techniques and tools for designing telecommunications systems at both the physical and network levels, such as software for mathematical simulation of telecommunications systems.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Junior Computer Engineer Software Design and Development
- development of tools and applications in the fields of medicine, environment, and territory;
- development of tools and applications in the food industry;
- development of intelligent autonomous systems with particular reference to agricultural robotics and crop monitoring;
- development of integrated devices (embedded) in the field of componentry and process automation.
Information System Design and Implementation
- design of hardware architectures and embedded systems;
- analysis and re-engineering of enterprise information systems;
- management of information systems;
- automation of services for businesses and public administration;
- process automation for industry.
Function in Work Context.
Junior Computer Engineer Design Support (e.g., development, testing, and debugging) and implementation of web tools and information services. Network System Analysis and Design. Junior graduates will be able to join work teams that include technical team leaders or sector leaders and/or coordination or management roles. Additionally, in some cases, they will have the opportunity to interface directly with clients, acquiring further cross-functional competencies.
To achieve higher levels of responsibility, the junior graduate must instead complete an additional period of training and/or sector activities.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The graduate in Computer Engineering must adequately know the methodological aspects of mathematics, physics, and other basic sciences and be able to use such knowledge to interpret and describe engineering problems. The objective of the examined training path is to provide graduates with solid engineering foundations that, among other things, allow an easy transition to most related master's degree courses.
The distinctive characteristic of the examined path will be the acquisition of specific competencies aimed at developing systems and applications of interest in some of the areas identified by the Sardinia Region's Smart Specialization Strategy, with particular reference to agroindustry and the development of distributed systems.
This specificity will enable effective team collaboration with professionals from different backgrounds, contributing to the graduate's positioning according to the principles of cross-functionality and mutualism repeatedly mentioned in the region's strategic documents.
The methodological and operational aspects of engineering sciences will constitute the core of the study course; the graduate must particularly be able to identify, formulate, and solve engineering, and specifically computer engineering, problems using updated methods, techniques, and tools.
The graduate must also know the main issues related to local industry and business sectors and understand their solutions through advanced devices and tools, as well as applications designed to adequately exploit network potential, new computing architectures, and the best interactive technologies.
Finally, the ability to conduct experiments and analyze and interpret the data, as well as understand and evaluate the impact of engineering solutions in the considered context, will be of fundamental importance for the study path.
The planned training path details the principles of operation of modern information processing and transmission systems. Training activities are grouped into four disciplinary macro areas as follows.
- Core Subjects Basic training activities in mathematical, physical, and computer science disciplines, concentrated mainly in the first year and in a small part at the beginning of the second year.
- Characteristic Subjects Characteristic training activities in the field of Information Engineering, concentrated mainly in the second and third years. These activities mainly concern computer architectures, data processing and management, operating systems, telecommunication systems, and automation. They represent the core of the study path in Information Engineering, covering all issues of modern processing systems, from hardware to software aspects, including the increasingly stringent needs for connectivity and interaction with the outside. These activities are also essential for achieving the specific goal of training technicians with adequate competencies in the development of distributed systems and their applications.
- Related and Integrative Subjects Related and integrative activities, with particular reference to technologies in industrial, chemical, and biomedical fields. This group of activities is aimed at characterizing the proposed study path towards themes relevant to the territory, developing essential competencies to interact profitably in various application areas of medicine and environmental monitoring.
- Elective Subjects These are additional student-selected activities, aimed at acquiring diverse knowledge and competencies of specific interest to the student.
The training activity will be structured into a limited number of teaching modules. Each teaching module will generally include classroom lectures, classroom and/or laboratory exercises, individual study or exercises, leading to credit points (following pass exams). To facilitate the circulation of international students, some courses in the second and third years will be delivered exclusively in English.
From a methodological perspective, particular attention will be paid to the interdisciplinary approach, also through the conduct of joint exercises within multiple modules. Operational tasks will also be proposed, configured as individual and group work (projects), using advanced tools.
It is emphasized that project activities will be carried out under the constant or periodic supervision of the instructor. The operational skills acquired (design, development, experimental validation) will then be applied during the thesis activities.
Both projects and thesis activities may be carried out in an academic (laboratory) or company setting, under the joint supervision of an industry tutor and a reference instructor. This mode is particularly important for those aiming for a quick integration into the local production network.

Secondary School Diploma Fees and Contributions Career Regulations - Fees Roles President PASQUALE BANDIERA Program, Texts and Objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Nurse: health professional who, holding the university degree enabling registration and being registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
Graduates in Nursing can find employment in public or private healthcare and social assistance facilities, either as employees or as self-employed professionals.
In particular, career opportunities include:
- in hospitals in all inpatient units and outpatient services;
- in territorial and hospital emergency services;
- in post-acute, long-term care facilities, assisted health residences, rehabilitation centers, disability care centers, hospices;
- in territorial, home care and outpatient health services;
- in prevention and public health services.
Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities specified in the study plan must be earned. The final exam, which has the value of a State Exam enabling the profession, consists of a theoretical, applied and experimental dissertation and the demonstration of practical skills in managing a situation related to the specific professional profile.
To regulate more precisely the scoring attribution in line with the guidelines of the Conference of Health Professions, a specific regulation has been established, effective from the academic year 2014/2015.
In particular, the final grade (expressed in hundredths, with possible honors) is determined by the following parameters:
- weighted average of grades obtained in the exams converted to hundredths;
- points assigned by the Graduation Committee during the thesis discussion based on the following parameters: practical test, thesis paper, graduation in progress, honors obtained in profit exams, participation in international exchange programs (Internships or Erasmus Programs).
The Final Exam Committee, appointed by the competent Academic Authority in accordance with the law, consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector and including at least 2 members designated by the Professional College or by the most representative professional associations as per current regulations.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the Nursing Bachelor's Degree, as provided by Article 6, paragraph 3, of D.M. n. 270/2004, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another equivalent foreign qualification.
The recognition of foreign qualifications for admission to the degree course is decided in compliance with current international agreements.
Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics at secondary school level is required.
The number of students admitted to the degree course is determined annually by a decree of the Ministry of Health in consultation with the Ministry of Education, University and Research, based on the regional training plan, taking into account national health needs and the didactic project and training potential.
Admission to the degree course is quota-based and requires an admission exam consisting of a multiple-choice test; the exam will cover topics in: general culture, biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics.
The call for quota-based courses at national level is available at the following link:
https://www.uniss.it/didattica/offerta-formativa/prove-di-accesso-ai-corsi-di-studio/corsi-numero-programmato The modalities and content of the admission exams for quota-based bachelor's courses at national level are defined in D.M. n. 85 of 05/02/14.
Student initial preparation will be assessed through the analysis of errors in the logic, chemistry, biology, physics-mathematics quizzes (multiple-choice questions) administered in the admission test, common to all health area bachelor's programs of the Faculty, and the assignment of any deficiencies according to the modalities specified in the course didactic regulation.
Awarded degree.
Bachelor's Degree in NURSING (Eligible for the Health Profession of Nurse)

SECTION: Communication skills

Communication skills.
Nursing graduates must develop the following communication skills:
- Use appropriate communication skills (verbal, non-verbal, and written) with users of all ages and their families within the care process and/or with other healthcare professionals in an appropriate verbal, non-verbal, and written manner;
- Use appropriate communication methods in the multi-professional team;
- Use principles of teaching and learning for specific information or educational interventions directed at individual users, families, and groups, and other professionals (support staff, nursing students, nurses);
- Support and encourage users towards health choices, reinforcing coping skills, self-esteem, and enhancing available resources;
- Manage conflicts arising from different positions;
- Facilitate coordination of care to achieve agreed health care outcomes;
- Collaborate with the care team to agree on operational methods and implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- Lectures;
- Videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives, testimonies;
- Case discussions and analysis of paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- Internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Observation of film or written frames, dialogues with structured grids;
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports);
- Structured objective examination with stations featuring simulations of relational skills.
Learning abilities.
Nursing graduates must develop the following self-learning abilities:
- Develop skills for independent study;
- Demonstrate the ability to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activity;
- Develop the ability to pose questions relevant to the timing, location, and interlocutors of one's professional practice;
- Demonstrate the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning;
- Demonstrate the ability for self-assessment of one's competencies and outline personal development and learning needs;
- Demonstrate the ability for collaborative learning and sharing knowledge within work teams;
- Demonstrate the ability and autonomy to seek necessary information to solve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, critically selecting secondary and primary sources of research evidence.
Didactic tools, methods, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Problem-based learning;
- Use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- Research methodology workshops for printed and online bibliographic research;
- Guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Project work, reports on specific research assignments;
- Tutor supervision of the internship path;
- Active participation in work sessions;
- Punctuality and quality in the presentation of assignments.
The teaching methods provided to achieve this specific training objective (ability to apply knowledge) include frontal lectures, conferences, seminars, work groups, and discussions. The teaching process will utilize modern didactic tools. The ability to apply acquired knowledge is developed through internship activities in various care settings in medical and surgical fields, both general and specialized, especially with interdisciplinary approaches.
Verification of this learning is assessed through examination tests, which, in addition to traditional oral or written exams, include a sequence of in-course assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews) to verify acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, the tools may be: (1) multiple-choice or short written questions organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; (2) written reports on assigned topics, analyzing activities and reports related to the final exam, as well as comments on practical exercises performed, and evaluation of the overall profile based on predefined criteria.
The course organization includes monitoring the achievement of the aforementioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding in terms of expected learning outcomes, through an articulated coordination, also prepared for this purpose.

Autonomy of Judgment.
Nursing graduates must demonstrate autonomy of judgment through the following skills:
- make clinical decisions;
- determine priorities for patient groups;
- decide interventions to be assigned to support staff;
- implement personalized nursing care by making choices based on similarities and differences among patients in terms of values, ethnicity, and socio-cultural practices;
- decide appropriate nursing interventions considering legal, political, geographical, economic, ethical, and social influences;
- critically evaluate the outcomes of nursing decisions based on patient outcomes and nursing standards;
- take responsibility and account for one's professional practice in accordance with the professional profile, code of ethics, and ethical and legal standards;
- make decisions using a scientific problem-solving approach for patients;
- analyze organizational problems and propose solutions;
- make decisions in situations of differing positions (conflicts or dilemmas).
Methodologies and training activities, teaching tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- guided reading and application exercises;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and graphs;
- case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility;
- debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, staged case tests;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.

- lectures to introduce the topic;
- guided reading and application;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and graphs;
- construction of cognitive maps.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, staged case tests.

Clinical Nursing Area Nursing graduates must know and understand the:
- general and clinical nursing sciences for understanding the fields of nursing intervention, the clinical method guiding effective care, operational techniques, and evidence guiding decision-making;
- psycho-social and humanistic sciences for understanding normal and pathological relational dynamics and defense or adaptation reactions of individuals facing psychological, social, and physical distress.
Methodologies and training activities, teaching tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic;
- guided reading and application;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and graphs;
- construction of cognitive maps.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, staged case tests.

- learning and change theories for understanding educational processes directed at citizens or patients.
Methodologies and training activities, teaching tools to develop expected outcomes:

Clinical Nursing Area Nursing graduates must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- integrate knowledge, skills, and attitudes of care to provide safe, effective, evidence-based nursing care;
- provide safe, evidence-based nursing care to improve health outcomes or stabilize the patient's condition;
- conduct a comprehensive and systematic assessment of the care needs of individual patients;
- use assessment techniques to accurately collect data on major health issues of patients;
- accurately analyze and interpret collected data through patient assessment;
- plan nursing care delivery in collaboration with users and the interdisciplinary care team;
- evaluate care progress in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team;
- manage a variety of activities required to deliver nursing care to patients in various care settings, both hospital and community-based.

Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:

- structured objective station exam.

Prevention and Management Area Nursing graduates must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- use theoretical knowledge derived from nursing sciences, behavioral and social biology, and other disciplines to recognize needs of patients across different ages and developmental stages throughout life;
- use theoretical models and role models within the care process to facilitate growth, development, and adaptation in promoting, maintaining, and recovering health of citizens;
- facilitate the development of a safe environment for patients by ensuring constant nursing vigilance.
Methodologies and training activities, teaching tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- application exercises;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and graphs;
- construction of cognitive maps;
- case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, staged case tests, project work, reports;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Function.
Nurse: a healthcare professional who, holding the university degree entitling them to practice and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
The educational path of the Nursing degree course has specific educational objectives that contribute to competence through knowledge (knowing), attitude, and practical skills (knowing how to do).
In particular, in the training of nurses, the objectives are aimed at ensuring that the nursing graduate is able to:
- manage preventive and care interventions for patients, families, and communities with autonomy and responsibility;
- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, and elderly) with acute and chronic respiratory problems, cardiovascular issues, metabolic and rheumatic problems, acute and chronic renal problems, acute and chronic gastrointestinal problems, liver problems, neurological problems, oncological problems, infectious problems, orthopedic and traumatic problems, obstetric-gynecological problems, hematological conditions, behavioral and cognitive alterations, psychological discomfort/disturbance;
- assess and manage nursing care for patients with chronic conditions and disabilities;
- manage perioperative nursing care;
- ensure safe administration of therapy and monitor its effectiveness;
- perform nursing techniques defined by the degree course standards;
- activate decision-making processes based on patient conditions, altered parameter values, reports, and laboratory tests;
- manage diagnostic pathways ensuring adequate patient preparation and follow-up after procedures;
- integrate nursing care into multidisciplinary care projects;
- assess patient problems using structured and systematic techniques through identification of alterations in functional models (activity and exercise, perception and maintenance of health, nutrition and metabolism, elimination model, rest and sleep, cognition and perception, self-concept, role and relationships, coping and stress management, sexuality and reproduction, values and beliefs);
- activate and support residual capacities of individuals to promote adaptation to limitations and alterations caused by illness and changes in lifestyle;
- identify nursing care needs of individuals and their reactions related to illness, ongoing treatments, institutionalization, changes in daily activities, and perceived quality of life;
- define intervention priorities based on care needs, organizational requirements, and optimal use of available resources;
- design and implement, collaborating with other professionals, information and educational interventions for risk factor control targeting individuals and groups;
- evaluate the results of delivered care and adjust nursing planning based on patient problem evolution;
- manage and organize nursing care for a group of patients (including night shifts);
- distinguish care needs from nursing care needs, differentiating the contribution of support staff from that of nurses;
- assign and supervise care activities to support staff;
- manage paper and electronic information systems supporting care;
- document nursing care delivered in accordance with legal and ethical principles;
- ensure patients and significant persons receive relevant and up-to-date information about their health status;
- prepare conditions for patient discharge, collaborating with team members;
- guarantee continuity of care between different shifts and between different services/structures;
- use professional integration tools (meetings, team meetings, case discussions);
- work integratively within the team respecting competence boundaries;
- ensure an effective physical and psychosocial environment for patient safety;
- use practices for protection against physical, chemical, and biological risks in the workplace;
- adopt precautions for manual handling of loads;
- adopt strategies for infection risk prevention (standard precautions) in hospital and community settings;
- monitor clinical and psychosocial patient conditions, identifying early signs of deterioration;
- activate necessary interventions to manage acute and/or critical situations;
- identify triggering factors for exacerbation in chronic patients;
- activate and manage a therapeutic and supportive relationship with the user, their family, and significant persons;
- manage care processes respecting cultural, ethnic, generational, and gender differences;
- support, in collaboration with the team, the patient and family during terminal phases and grief;
- activate informal care networks to support the user and family in long-term care projects.

Function in the Work Context.
Nurse: a healthcare professional who, holding the university degree entitling them to practice and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
The main functions are: disease prevention, care for sick and disabled individuals of all ages, and health education.
In particular, the nurse:
a) participates in identifying health needs of individuals and the community;
b) identifies nursing care needs of individuals and the community and formulates related objectives;
c) plans, manages, and evaluates nursing care interventions;
d) ensures correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions;
e) acts both individually and in collaboration with other healthcare and social professionals;
f) utilizes support staff as necessary to fulfill functions;
g) performs professional activities in public or private healthcare facilities, in the territory, and in home care, in dependent or freelance capacity.

In relation to these specific educational objectives, the educational activity ensures a unified and, at the same time, interdisciplinary vision of the educational goals, with in-depth exploration of knowledge derived from characteristic disciplinary areas, including those more specifically professionalizing, and from related and integrative disciplinary areas. According to Ministerial Decree of February 19, 2009, each activated course includes an integer number of credit units to avoid fragmentation of information transmitted to students. The teaching methods include frontal lectures, seminars, working groups, and discussions on relevant topics and simulations aimed at achieving the educational path objectives. The teaching process will utilize modern teaching tools. Traditional teaching activities are complemented by supervised internship activities at specialized public healthcare services and other scientifically relevant and educationally valuable institutions in Italy or abroad, linked by specific agreements. This training allows for progressive assumption of responsibility and professional autonomy, enabling nursing students to acquire the ability to assess various issues related to nursing care, plan appropriate nursing care, and integrate into cooperative group work with different figures involved in nursing care across various public and social healthcare contexts. Laboratory and internship activities are conducted under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors specifically designated based on communication skills, adequately trained for this role. Laboratory and internship activities are coordinated by a faculty member belonging to the highest educational level for the specific profile.

The study plan includes exams and/or final assessments organized as integrated exam sessions for multiple courses or coordinated modules. The assessment of this learning is verified through exam procedures, which, beyond traditional oral or written exams, include intermediate assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate discussions) to verify acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, the tools used are: (1) multiple-choice or short written responses, organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; (2) written reports on assigned topics and analysis of activities related to the final exam, as well as comments on exercises performed, through evaluation of the overall profile developed based on predefined criteria. The degree course regulations define, within legal limits, that the student's total weekly study time for personal study or other individual training activities shall not be less than at least 50% of the thirty hours provided for each CFU.

The educational path is structured, monitored, validated, and optimized in a continuum to acquire the competencies, knowledge, and skills specified in the curriculum profile established by current regulations and the specific objectives of the course. These specific educational objectives are supported by a faculty aware of the need to use all institutional tools activated by competent bodies (NVF and NVA) for the accreditation of teaching quality. Through these tools, it is possible to measure improvements in teaching performance at all different stages contributing to the attainment of the first-level degree, in terms of educational path, exams, perceived quality assessment by students, and acquisition of professional competencies aligned with the specific objectives of the educational path.
