Secondary School Diploma Fees and contributions Regulation Careers - Fees Roles President LUCIANA GOISIS Program, texts and objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Professional profile oriented towards environmental, food and health security This is an innovative professional figure with strong characteristics in terms of interface between different professionals and decision-makers in the areas of competence of the course (Human rights, security and cooperation). It is emphasized that it is difficult to assign it to professional registers regulated by state laws. However, clear pertinences with the professional profiles codified by ISTAT can be highlighted in the relevant field.
The graduate can pursue a career as a staff officer/manager in international non-governmental organizations and volunteer networks oriented towards solving environmental, food and socio-health problems; career as a staff officer/technical manager in state and local administrations and non-governmental organizations operating in civil protection and cooperation in the fields of natural resource and biodiversity protection, rural development and socio-health assistance; technician in specialized companies operating, for example, in environmental monitoring and sampling, remediation of contaminated sites.
Professional profile oriented towards human security and peace support activities This is an innovative professional figure with strong characteristics in terms of interface between different professionals and decision-makers in the areas of competence of the course (Human rights, security and cooperation). It is emphasized that it is difficult to assign it to professional registers regulated by state laws. However, clear pertinences with the professional profiles codified by ISTAT can be highlighted in the relevant field.
The graduate can pursue a career as a staff officer/manager in international non-governmental organizations and volunteer networks oriented towards international cooperation, safeguarding of human rights, peaceful resolution of conflicts and protection of historical-artistic-cultural assets; career as a staff officer/manager in state administrations, both central and peripheral, oriented towards civil protection; career as a technical-analyst in public and private organizations, with particular regard to monitoring emergencies.
Characteristics of final exam.
The student's training path concludes with a final exam, which consists of verifying the graduate's ability to clearly and competently present and discuss, before a Degree Committee, a document related to the individual experience gained in the context of further training activities (Art 10, paragraph 5 letter d).
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities provided for in the study plan must be obtained.
Knowledge required for access.
For enrollment in the Study Course, a secondary school diploma or another degree obtained abroad, recognized as suitable according to current regulations, is required.
To conveniently undertake the studies, the student must possess adequate knowledge of basic notions of Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology, as well as basic competencies in geographical, historical, legal, economic and socio-political disciplines, as well as adequate logical, reading and comprehension skills. The possession of the requirements will be verified through an entrance test, which will be conducted with methods defined in the course's didactic regulation, also in view of possible access programming.
If the verification of initial knowledge does not yield a positive outcome, additional training obligations will be assigned to be fulfilled during the first year, according to the didactic regulation.
Specific training objectives.
The three-year Bachelor's degree course in "Security and International Cooperation" aims to train an expert capable of exercising operational coordination, management, training and control functions in national and international contexts, in the following sectors:
1. environmental, food and health security;
2. human rights, security and peace support activities.
The training path is structured to develop, also in relation to the chosen learning profile, specific competencies in the field of security, including the thematic areas concerning environmental, food and health security or those of human rights and peace support.
Graduates in the three-year Bachelor's degree course in "Security and International Cooperation" must organically acquire the essential theoretical knowledge related to the following disciplinary fields:
- Basic sciences (mathematical, physical, chemical and computer sciences), in the perspective of their subsequent professional application;
- Legal, political-institutional and economic disciplines, in the perspective of organizing and managing civilian units engaged in security in international cooperation contexts, in specific public administration fields or in volunteer associations and non-governmental organizations;
- Historical and geographical-territorial disciplines, for in-depth study of operational contexts in which coordination and management activities of civil organizational-functional systems are exercised, such as those typical of international development cooperation projects, peace support operations and interventions for the protection of populations affected by disasters.
- Linguistic and anthropological-psychosocial disciplines relevant for effective communication in international contexts and for adequate understanding of the socio-cultural characteristics of different operational contexts.
- Technical-scientific disciplines related to environmental, food and health security, hydro-geological and demographic emergencies, and more generally to crisis situations.
Graduates in the class must also acquire:
- Critical awareness of the professional deontological implications in the different operational fields of internal and external security, also for humanitarian purposes and protection of civilian populations in case of natural disasters;
- Integrated competencies developed through coordinated forms of training and internship, for the application of theoretical knowledge to the aforementioned coordination and management functions;
- Adequate knowledge for further personal qualification and for cooperating in the implementation of selective and training activities for specific public administration personnel;
- Technical knowledge for the treatment and management of information and communication problems, for the use of diagnostic tools and computer systems, also networked, and for accessing and managing databases;
- Technical competencies for the identification and evaluation of risks connected to the performance of their functions.
The course, with its evident interdisciplinary approach, aims to intercept, through a targeted professional training path, the multiple and complex needs of intervention that current complex problems of environmental, food, health and human security impose on public decision-makers and national and international organizations operating in civilian contexts. It is a highly innovative cultural project in the landscape of Italian higher education. By declining the concept of security in its different connotations and subsequent operational fields, the course integrates disciplines belonging to the socio-political-economic-legal area with disciplines of the technical-scientific area, with particular reference to the fields of environmental, food and health security.
Potential beneficiaries of the course are students from secondary schools and motivated by a strong sensitivity towards issues such as respect for human rights, international development cooperation, security in its various dimensions. The course may also welcome students who have served in the Armed Forces and wish to deepen, within the specific themes of class L-DS, the interdisciplinary competencies necessary to perform functions in the context of civil organizational-functional systems, such as those typical of international development cooperation projects, peace support operations and interventions for the protection of populations affected by disasters. Furthermore, the designed training paths may be of interest to personnel operating in Civil Protection who wish to acquire specialization in the field of civil protection.
During the training path, which will have a theoretical and practical character, graduates will have acquired the appropriate cultural, scientific and technological resources to competently address and manage the implementation of operational projects in the contexts already indicated above. From a cultural and methodological point of view, the course offers ample space and opportunities for innovative teaching methods, through the interdisciplinary analysis of case studies, the conduct of internships and other activities in different operational contexts, also within development cooperation projects, volunteer networks, etc. Among the training objectives is therefore the acquisition of effective methodologies to competently address the choices that must be made in dealing with the complex issues concerning security in the various declinations mentioned above.
From the didactic organization perspective, the course's ordering allows for the articulation of training paths oriented towards the different cultural fields of security, such as the thematic areas concerning environmental, food and health security or those of human rights and peace support.
After a shared first year, the course divides into two curricula, which provide for some common teachings in the second year, before completely differentiating in the third year.
The course normally takes place in conventional mode and provides for the physical presence of the teacher and students in the classroom. All lessons can be transmitted via videoconference in partner locations present in the territory that request it. This solution allows those who, for work reasons or due to difficulties in moving within the regional territory, cannot always guarantee their physical presence at the Sassari location, to follow theoretical lessons at the partner location, while maintaining the possibility to interact with the teacher and actively participate in lessons and seminar activities.
In addition to the conventional in-person mode, the delivery of only theoretical lessons and seminars can also be carried out in e-learning mode on the Moodle platform.
While the absence of mandatory attendance for this degree course is maintained, all practical activities (laboratories, exercises, internships) are delivered exclusively in person.
The study plan, in addition to aiming at the professional insertion of graduates, provides the basic preparation propaedeutic to continuing studies for the attainment of the Master's degree in class LM-DS or in other Master's degrees coherent with the L/DS training path.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Articulation of the knowledge framework The knowledge framework provided by the Bachelor's degree course in Security and International Cooperation is structured into a common training path and two alternative profiles.
The teachings provided in the common training path aim to provide a broad base of basic knowledge regarding human rights, comparative political science, international relations, conflict mediation, management and organization of work groups even in multi-ethnic and multi-cultural contexts, technical-administrative management of intervention projects requiring sufficient technical-scientific competencies related to cartography, ecology, public health hygiene, information security and physical activities. The Course, in this common training part, also aims to provide sufficient specific linguistic competencies to operate autonomously in multicultural contexts. The educational project on which the Study Course is based then allows for the refinement and qualification of graduates' knowledge, directing them along two different educational paths, corresponding to two different cultural and professional profiles.
A first profile directs the student's knowledge towards the deepening of themes, analysis perspectives and intervention modalities concerning human rights, security and peace support activities. The knowledge characterizing this training path aims to provide the graduate with a cultural basis to manage interactive dynamics in interdisciplinary groups of specialists who must effectively address the complex problems of various security and cooperation fields, with functions of coordination, dialogue facilitation, reporting, auditing, etc., also in international and multicultural contexts. To develop these knowledge objectives to the maximum extent, the study path of this first curriculum profile is mainly based on disciplines of the areas of applied legal sciences, sociological, psychological and communication sciences, and geopolitical, economic and territorial sciences. In this profile, the knowledge base in legal and social sciences (economic, socio-political and psychological) assumes a predominant weight, while also providing for the acquisition of knowledge that encompasses aspects of environmental, food and health security and the protection of historical-artistic-cultural assets.
The knowledge framework of the second profile, oriented towards environmental, food and health security, encompasses a robust technical-scientific cultural base aimed at consolidating competencies related to various types of intervention, such as, for example, the setting up of refugee camps and reception centers; organization of food and health humanitarian aid; official control activities (inspection, sampling, audit, monitoring and surveillance) for the correct implementation of health promotion and environmental protection programs; management of emergencies in disadvantaged rural areas in the field of food security; management of first aid related to environmental and hygiene-health emergencies; remediation interventions, hydro-geological emergencies and public health.
In order to acquire such competencies, the curriculum path is based on the acquisition of specific knowledge in the disciplinary fields of agricultural sciences and food production (agricultural systems, sustainable management of water resources in agriculture, plant protection, food security, epidemiology and agro-terrorism), earth and environmental sciences (geology and hydrogeology, environmental protection and remediation, disaster prevention, climatology), health sciences (public health hygiene, biosafety, epidemic prevention, first aid), combined with a sufficiently broad cultural base of knowledge related to legal and socio-political sciences.
For each profile, variations and personalizations of the study path are possible in relation to the optional teachings available to the student, which are able to orient knowledge more clearly towards specific technical-scientific disciplinary sectors (sectors AGR*; BIO/03 – 07; MED/07 – 45; VET*; L-ANT/10).
Development and verification of understanding capabilities In relation to the overall knowledge framework outlined above, the graduate must develop a level of understanding that allows for the effective use of methodological tools typical of different disciplinary groups, theoretical-conceptual tools for critical analysis of the main themes and problems recurring therein and their developments, and the practical principles of consolidated knowledge. The expected learning outcomes are achieved through the application of teaching methodologies based on frontal lessons, theoretical, empirical and experimental exercises, seminar activities. The verification of learning outcomes provides for the use of a varied and appropriately balanced set of assessment methods: final exams in individual courses, in written and/or oral form, possibly preceded by intermediate tests; written or oral reports at the end (or during) seminar activities. The Bachelor's degree course is structured to integrate these conventional teaching tools with tools and methods that allow the graduate to practically test the theoretical knowledge acquired. This will occur through facilitating learning through various methods such as case study analysis, open laboratory teaching, "brainstorming" sessions, tele-teaching and videoconferencing, guided visits, participation in projects and design groups, internships at Public and Private Entities and organizations in Italy or abroad, etc. For these activities, verification tools will concern the evaluation of written reports or oral presentations or in the form of posters or other media (e.g., video clips), whose production will be an integral part of the training path of various disciplines, with particular regard to communication methodologies and sociological methods.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The graduate in the three-year interdepartmental Bachelor's degree in "Security and International Cooperation", based on the methodological, theoretical-conceptual tools and practical principles learned during studies, must be able to apply acquired knowledge to operate with adequate levels of responsibility and demonstrate a professional approach to designing proposals and solving problems, also in the role of consultant, particularly in those sectors of the labor market that include, among others, environmental, food and health security, human security and management of migration flows, conflict resolution and peace-keeping, international development cooperation, preventive and coordinating interventions in areas affected by natural disasters.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding develops through a gradual process of socialization, learning and concrete use of different methodologies, apparatuses and disciplinary tools. It is first stimulated and developed in the initial phase of socialization and learning, through collective classroom activities such as frontal lessons and seminar activities. In a second phase of learning, which has limited specific weight in the Bachelor's degree but should not be underestimated for the practical application of acquired knowledge, this applicative ability is further developed through interactions and individual meetings between the final project supervisor and the candidate, in order to produce a final dissertation that meets the minimum requirements of originality and critical application of acquired knowledge. In the third and decisive phase, the student can concretely apply the knowledge learned through the internship path and related case studies.
To these different phases and activities correspond different verification methods regarding the actual acquisition of such applicative abilities: for the first phase, verifications will be carried out through exams and, in particular, through individual or group elaboration of reports on seminar topics; for the second phase, the application of knowledge and understanding is a criterion that guides the quality assessment of the final project of the study path; for the third phase, the outcome of internships certified by the hosting entity constitutes a relevant element of judgment regarding the development and maturation of effective applicative abilities.
III - Judgment autonomy The graduate in the three-year Bachelor's degree in "Security and International Cooperation" will acquire practical and operational tools and competencies to develop their own judgment autonomy, enabling them to:
- acquire and interpret data related to legal-social, political, institutional and technical-scientific phenomena that fall within the sphere of their disciplinary and professional competencies in the field of security and international cooperation;
- interpret the diachronic and comparative development of security and international cooperation problems, in light of appropriate theoretical-conceptual orientation schemes;
- formulate autonomous judgments and evaluate their possible implications, with specific reference to the complex problems of a social, scientific and regulatory nature that characterize, on the one hand, human security and peace support activities, and on the other hand, environmental, food and health security.
Judgment autonomy and the critical abilities derived from it are developed within individual courses through an interaction process between teacher and student, within different teaching methods (frontal lessons, seminar activities, independent text elaboration and discussion, preparation of the final internship report), which stimulate the abilities to: interdisciplinary framing of theoretical and practical problems; selection and analysis of data subject to empirical verification and therefore objective validation; formulation of hypotheses and alternative scenarios; evaluation of explanatory theories and models and their applicability to concrete cases.
IV - Communication skills The three-year interdepartmental Bachelor's degree course in "Security and International Cooperation" allows the acquisition of competencies and tools for the development of communication and relational skills. In particular, the graduate must acquire the ability to:
- communicate information (ideas, problems, solutions, perspectives) related to the different disciplinary fields in which the study course is structured, also using one or more foreign languages, both to specific and qualified interlocutors and to an undifferentiated and non-specialist public;
- express concepts and arguments relevant, drawing from the knowledge acquired during the degree course, using appropriately the specialized languages of the different disciplines of security and international cooperation, both with experts and non-experts of the subjects.
- communicate within negotiations and negotiation activities, with particular regard to human security and peace-keeping activities and within management interactions of complex security environmental, food and health interventions.
- draft written reports on the various security and international cooperation issues, presenting them orally and through multimedia interaction tools.
To this end, the Bachelor's degree course provides, through individual teachings, the learning of an appropriate and rigorous language related to a wide range of disciplinary competencies, which is associated with the ability to produce written texts using the same language. These abilities will be developed in the didactic learning path of the various teaching courses, whose typical verification tool (the final or intermediate exam) provides for the assessment of the student's communication skills in written or oral form. The final exam provides for a document aimed at also verifying the necessary communication maturity of the candidate for obtaining the degree. The course also offers the possibility to refine communication skills "in the field" through other training activities, including the internship and related documents.
To develop and consolidate knowledge of the English language, specific training activities with relative verification test are provided.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
ITALIAN V - Learning ability The graduate in "Security and International Cooperation" must have developed the methodological abilities and learning capacities necessary to undertake Master's studies and post-graduate training, professional updating and continuous training, with a high degree of autonomy.
Also for the development of learning ability, as already for the development of communication skills, the Bachelor's degree course relies on teaching tools such as frontal lessons, seminar activities, exercises, group work and written, oral or other media-based documents, aimed at deepening interpretative, in-depth analysis, comprehension, representation and evaluation abilities of the problems and critical nodes underlying the development of the various disciplines in which the study course is structured. These activities will test the abilities of comprehension, deepening and critical analysis of complex themes such as those related to the various declinations proposed by the Bachelor's degree course in security and international cooperation.
Associated competencies for the role.
Professional profile oriented towards environmental, food and health security The common training path is oriented to provide basic competencies regarding human rights, geopolitics, international relations, conflict mediation, management and organization of work groups even in multi-ethnic contexts, technical-administrative management of intervention projects requiring sufficient technical-scientific competencies related to cartography, ecology, public health hygiene, information security. The graduate will acquire specific linguistic competencies sufficient to operate autonomously in multicultural contexts. Moreover, the common training path provides ample space for carrying out practical application internships in Italy and/or abroad in operational contexts related to the training objectives.
The graduate who chooses a training path in the field of environmental, food and health security will acquire additional technical-scientific competencies related to the following disciplines: geology, chemistry and biochemistry, agro-ecology, renewable energies, protection of agricultural and forest crops, biodiversity protection, food safety (safety and security), merchandising, remediation of contaminated sites, health security (microbiology, parasitology and zoonoses, first aid, epidemiology), sampling and diagnostic methodologies.
Professional profile oriented towards human security and peace support activities The common training path is oriented to provide basic competencies regarding human rights, geopolitics, international relations, conflict mediation, management and organization of work groups even in multi-ethnic contexts, technical-administrative management of intervention projects requiring sufficient technical-scientific competencies related to cartography, ecology, public health hygiene, information security. The graduate will acquire specific linguistic competencies sufficient to operate autonomously in multicultural contexts. Moreover, the common training path provides ample space for carrying out practical application internships in Italy and/or abroad in operational contexts related to the training objectives.
The graduate who chooses a training path in the field of human security and peace support activities will acquire additional competencies in legal, administrative and economic-social sciences, such as for example transport and trade policies, international criminal law, analysis of migration flows and demographic dynamics, management and accounting of development cooperation projects, conflict mediation, micro-credit policies, reporting and communication strategies.
Function in work context.
Professional profile oriented towards environmental, food and health security The graduate can perform coordination, management of work groups and experts, technical and logistical organization, preliminary diagnosis and sampling activities useful for planning interventions, consultancy and support actions in types of interventions and situations such as those listed below as examples:
- setting up of refugee camps and reception centers;
- food and health humanitarian aid;
- projects in implementation of public programs for prevention of environmental disasters;
- projects in implementation of public health promotion, food security and environmental protection policies;
- official control activities (inspection, sampling, audit, monitoring and surveillance) for the correct implementation of health promotion and environmental protection programs;
- emergencies in disadvantaged rural areas (e.g., nomadic and agro-pastoral systems), with particular reference to Developing Countries;
- first aid related to environmental emergencies (e.g., droughts, floods, fires) and hygiene-health emergencies (e.g., epidemics, zoonoses, parasitosis);
- first aid in conflict zones;
- emergencies in the field of food security, declined in the dual meaning of food safety (e.g., food quality and hygiene, microbial contaminants, nutritional value) and food security (e.g., food emergencies and famines, protection of crops from pathogens and parasites, agro-terrorism, dynamics of the food market);
- remediation interventions, hydro-geological emergencies (hydraulic emergencies in agricultural and forest contexts, prevention of erosive phenomena);
- demographic emergencies (migration flows following conflicts or environmental disasters);
- management of patients hosted in damaged hospital structures or in field health structures, provision of medicines and medical-surgical equipment for the affected population, basic health assistance;
- public health interventions such as hygiene-health surveillance, water quality controls until the restoration of the water supply network, disinfection and pest control.
Professional profile oriented towards human security and peace support activities perform coordination, management of communication strategies both within security operational units and towards the external environment; coordination and technical-administrative management, consultancy and support actions in types of interventions and situations such as those listed below as examples:
- resolution of internal and international crises;
- coordination of domestic and international administrative units in the provision of security services;
- selection of personnel and economic and administrative management of crisis units;
- conduct of operational groups for determining resources and configuring the impact scenarios of emergency intervention policies;
- conduct of systems for reporting international crises;
- monitoring of security interventions and peace support operations in terms of efficiency and effectiveness;
- analysis of the impact of security policies, peace support and development cooperation;
- analysis of the needs of populations receiving humanitarian aid;
- analysis of violations of the rights of populations benefiting from humanitarian aid;
- protection of historical-artistic-cultural assets;
- technical-administrative management of intervention projects in the fields described above.

Curriculum Legal Services for Administration The various professional qualifications (for which a three-year degree is sufficient) in the public administration sector (state, regional, and local and territorial bodies), private entities, and third-sector organizations. The aim is thus to train a professional figure with basic skills and (although limited to a three-year degree) specialized skills for various public administrations and for entities that, in the course of their activities, interact with public administrations. A professional figure that, although classified under ISTAT codes within professions designated for a second level, acquires basic skills applicable in these sectors. Indeed, considering the different levels of complexity characterizing the professional figures in question and their multidisciplinary nature, such skills can be acquired, at least in part, through the three-year degree program.
Curriculum in Legal Services for Business Legal operators in private companies and in the banking, insurance, and financial sectors, also employed in public companies (autonomous companies, economic entities, or joint-stock companies). The aim is thus to train a professional figure with basic skills and (although limited to a three-year degree) specialized skills for legal operators in companies, insurance, and banks or public companies. A professional figure that, although classified under ISTAT codes within professions designated for a second level, acquires basic skills applicable in these sectors. Indeed, considering the different levels of complexity characterizing the professional figures in question and their multidisciplinary nature, such skills can be acquired - at least regarding the non-exclusively specialized level - through the three-year degree program.
Consider, for example, operators in the financial sector, such as credit agents and mediators Final Exam Characteristics.
The final exam consists of the candidate preparing a written compilation and the subsequent oral discussion, under the guidance of a supervisor. The final grade is expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors, taking into account the student's overall academic record.
Required Knowledge for Admission
To enroll in the Bachelor's Degree in Sciences of Juridical Services, one must possess: - basic knowledge obtainable in secondary school, certified by a secondary school diploma or another title, even obtained abroad, recognized as equivalent; - general cultural knowledge, basic knowledge of history with particular reference to the legal phenomenon, basic knowledge of civic education with particular reference to constitutional principles.
The adequacy of such knowledge will be verified through a non-selective entrance exam (Article 6, D.M. 270/2004) that all enrolled students must take at the beginning of the academic year. The entrance exam is preceded by an introductory course to legal studies.
It is specified that the Course's Teaching Regulations will also indicate any additional educational requirements in case the verification is not positive.

- final dissertation, specifically designed to assess the student's synthesis ability and acquired autonomy.
Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The student in Legal Services Sciences must demonstrate:
- complete knowledge and understanding of fundamental legal sectors;
- basic knowledge of economic disciplines, with particular regard to the functioning of public administration and enterprises;
- ability to understand the purposes and contexts of community and national policies regarding public and private enterprise.

These knowledge will be verified during the course through intermediate assessments, also in the form of tests, during the teaching activities, and at the end of the lecture courses, through final written and/or oral exams.

Generic Area The graduate in Legal Services Sciences has:
- the ability to retrieve, also through the consultation of databases, national and community regulatory sources;
- the ability to understand and use case law;
- the ability to apply and interpret legal and commercial regulations related to business and labor;
- the ability to solve legal and organizational problems related to business management.

Finally, particular emphasis is placed on internships carried out by the student as particularly effective tools for applying the knowledge in question.

ITALIAN
Competencies associated with the function.
Curriculum Legal Services for Administration The competencies acquired during the studies, which will enable the graduate to perform the aforementioned functions, will be basic legal training and mastery of specific regulatory application sectors (State accounting and public bodies, tax law, public contracting) necessary for performing one's work activities under public entities or private entities operating in the public sector or sectors presided over by public entities.
Upon completion of the study course, specifically, the graduate acquires the competencies suitable for performing the following functions: organizational-management in public and private administrations and enterprises, in the third sector, and in activities requiring specific legal preparation, judicial operator, legal operator of administration and enterprise, labor consultant.
Curriculum in Legal Services for Business The competencies acquired during the studies, which will enable the graduate to perform the aforementioned functions, will be basic legal training and mastery of specific regulatory application sectors, different in the three curricula (in this third dedicated to business, the banking, insurance, consumer, and financing sectors, examples being State accounting, cultural property law, and banking and insurance law), sufficient for performing organizational-management functions (in non-managerial roles) in public and private enterprises and the third sector.
It is precisely the needs of the territory, highlighted also in meetings with social partners, that have made it necessary to enhance the figure of the business legal operator through a dedicated curriculum: the training in the disciplinary areas characterizing the same aims to lay the foundation for insertion within the corporate staff of private and public enterprises, with a collaborative function in drafting national and international contracts, and providing support for formulating opinions on the compliance with the law of management choices, also with the perspective of preventing risks and administrative and criminal sanctions.
Moreover, the in-depth study of subjects concerning navigation law, transport law, and international and European law enables the graduate to find employment placement in service and infrastructure management enterprises, in the transport and logistics sector, which carry out activities in Italy and/or abroad.
Function in the workplace context.
Curriculum Legal Services for Administration The functions that the graduate will perform will concern the execution of public organizational and decision-making processes. This both from the perspective within public administrations (competencies/tasks in the various stages of administrative procedures aimed at adopting decisions; implementation and execution of organizational modules; exercise of support tasks for measuring organizational performance and public decision-making processes, etc.) and from the perspective within private entities that interact with public administrations (participation in administrative procedures; support and management tasks in tendering procedures and, in general, in competitive and selection procedures initiated by public administrations), also employing the knowledge and competencies acquired in the tax, State accounting, and public bodies sectors.
Graduates of the course class may perform activities, up to the qualification compatible with a three-year degree, as staff members and officials in institutions, public administrations, private enterprises, and entities operating in the social, socio-economic, and political sectors.
Curriculum in Legal Services for Business The functions that the graduate will perform will be those of support and orientation in administrative choices, providing evaluation elements based on their regulatory competencies, which will therefore help in making formally legitimate decisions (e.g., compliance with tax regulations and business crisis) and appropriate in terms of expected results (e.g., regarding regulations on internal and European funding, also in the cultural field). In short, not only a protective function against risks related to regulatory violations (even towards consumers), but also positively recognizing the opportunities offered by sector regulations.
The competencies will then be enriched practically through attendance at a corporate strategy and finance laboratory or through the completion of an internship.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The objectives of the Bachelor's degree course in Legal Services Sciences are as follows:
a) equip graduates with a framework of competencies in the fundamental sectors for legal preparation, with specific reference to the subjects of historical-philosophical, private, public, commercial, administrative, economic, business, procedural, criminal, and internationalist fields, in order to ensure an adequate knowledge base for the work they will perform and the possibility to deepen and improve these competencies through attendance at Master's and specialization courses; among the competencies to be acquired, graduates must be able to retrieve national and international regulatory sources, interpret them, and apply them in their respective operational fields.
b) provide technical competencies to improve the professional qualification of graduates, making it more suitable to the dynamism of the labor market. Graduates must acquire knowledge and competencies necessary for legal management and consultancy for enterprises, for public and private organization of work, for resolving business management and conflict management problems in the workplace, civil, and commercial sectors.
To achieve the stated objectives, the training path is structured as follows:
In the first year, the Bachelor's degree course includes the study of private law institutions and constitutional law, political and business economics, foreign language, and the acquisition of logical and critical competencies provided by the history and philosophy of law.
In the second year, the study of subjects related to the legal life of public administration and private enterprise is provided, allowing the student to acquire knowledge in the field of labor, administrative, and commercial law. The navigation sector assumes particular relevance due to specific interest in the regional reality. To complete the training in the legal field, criminal and internationalist disciplines are studied, to which the analysis of procedural subjects is added.
In the third year, the study of tax law, present in both curricula, administrative sector disciplines, in-depth of the constitutional sector, specifically regarding territorial autonomy, is provided. The banking and insurance law sector, bankruptcy law, consumer protection, and European funding regulations play a significant role, which are functional to the performance of consultancy activities, making the offer more responsive to the class profile.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The graduate of the three-year degree program in 'Strategic and Legal Sciences of Defense and Security' will acquire practical and operational tools and competencies to develop their own autonomy of judgment, enabling them to:
- Acquire and interpret data related to juridical-social, political, institutional, and technical-scientific phenomena within the scope of their disciplinary and professional competencies in the field of internal and international security;
- Interpret the diachronic and comparative development of internal and international security issues, in light of appropriate theoretical-conceptual frameworks;
- Formulate autonomous judgments and evaluate their possible implications, with specific reference to the complex issues of a social, scientific, and regulatory nature that characterize, on one hand, internal civil security and, on the other, international security.
The autonomy of judgment and the critical abilities derived from it are developed within individual courses through a process of interaction between instructor and student, within various teaching methods (lectures, seminar activities, independent text analysis and discussion, preparation of the final report on internship activities), designed to stimulate the ability to: interdisciplinarily frame theoretical and practical problems; select and analyze data subject to empirical verification and thus objective validation; formulate hypotheses and alternative scenarios; evaluate explanatory theories and models and their applicability to concrete cases.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Human and Social Sciences Area Graduates in Strategic and Legal Sciences of Defense and Security will have acquired specific knowledge and understanding in the disciplinary fields of basic and applied legal sciences; sociological, political, geopolitical, economic, historical, exact, and psychological sciences. Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Human and Social Sciences Area Graduates in Strategic and Legal Sciences of Defense and Security must be able to manage interactive dynamics within interdisciplinary groups of specialists addressing complex issues in the fields of internal and international civil security, with functions including:
- Coordination and liaison between operational units, also engaged in peacekeeping and peace enforcement actions;
- Facilitation of dialogue and mediation between: a) institutional and non-institutional actors; b) public and private subjects; c) cooperation actors and local populations;
- Design and implementation of reporting, auditing, and performance evaluation tools for international organizations;
- Analysts of political, economic, and social conditions and operational scenarios in which actors and international organizations operate;
- Professionals capable of understanding and interpreting the legal constraints and opportunities within the context in which actors and international organizations operate.

- Analysis of the needs of populations receiving humanitarian aid;
- Analysis of violations of the rights of populations benefiting from humanitarian aid;
- Analysis of the legal aspects of environmental protection;
- Technical and administrative management of intervention projects in the aforementioned areas.

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The three-year degree program in "Strategic and Legal Sciences of Defense and Security" aims to train experts capable of exercising operational, coordination, direction, training, and control functions in domestic and international contexts, in the following fields:
- Internal Security;
- International Security.
The course, with an evident interdisciplinary approach, seeks to address, through a targeted professional training path, the multiple and complex intervention needs imposed by current, complex civil security issues, alongside military security, on public decision-makers and international organizations. By interpreting the concept of security in its various connotations and corresponding operational fields, the course integrates disciplines from scientific, legal, economic, historical-political-institutional, socio-political, psychological, geographical-territorial, and military areas into the training program. The educational objective is to form a figure with adequate interdisciplinary preparation, particularly including legal disciplines interpreted through a modern perspective, capable of meeting the requirements of international organizations and military forces.
The proposed training is therefore directed towards various categories: in addition to students interested in international and internal security issues, the course may welcome military personnel wishing to deepen, within the specific themes of class L-DS, disciplines related to the coordination, management, and direction of military organizational-functional systems, as well as peace support operations. Additionally, the course may be of interest to personnel operating within the PP.AA., as well as those aspiring to work in international organizations and in the field of international security.
The innovative training proposed pays particular attention to emerging defense and security issues in the digital dimension, deepening competencies related to cybersecurity, public law of digital ecosystems, and digital globalization and finance.
The training path is structured as follows:
1. The first two years of the course provide a common path for all students, aimed at providing foundational knowledge in various disciplines, particularly scientific (physics, chemistry, computer science), legal (Italian and Comparative Constitutional Law, Institutions of European Private Law, Administrative Law of Defense and Security, Globalization and Digital Finance, International and European Law, International Criminal Law and Military Criminal Law, Maritime and Aerospace Law), socio-political (Political Science and International Relations, Criminological Sciences and Security Policies), historical (The Contemporary World from 1945 to the Present), economic (Fundamentals of Business Economics), psychological (General Psychology), and geographical-territorial (Geopolitics), as well as the mandatory English language.
2. The third year, of a specific and professionalizing nature, allows the choice between two distinct training paths regarding internal and international security, respectively.
Professionalizing training activities include the 60 CFU of coordinated training and internship forms required by the degree class, acquired through practical thematic workshops and professional training internships coordinated with various military forces, as well as international organizations and/or interested public or private entities.
The organization of such internships and activities will be conducted in agreement with the military forces and major international organizations engaged in the fields of international security and human rights protection.
In particular, within the two paths, the following themes will be deepened in a laboratory format:
- For the Internal Security path, themes concerning the principles of environmental law, law and investigation techniques, conflict mediation and negotiation, as well as public law of digital ecosystems;
- For the International Security path, themes concerning human rights, conflict mediation and negotiation, international organization, cybersecurity, as well as judicial protection of fundamental rights.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1176] Viticultural, Enological, and Food Technologies
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10152

Autonomy of Judgment.
Upon completion of the studies, the graduate will have the ability to compare and discuss the topics addressed during the study path and to draft appropriate concluding reports and present them orally. They will have the ability to retrieve and evaluate information sources, data, and scientific literature useful for improving the quality and efficiency of food production, also in terms of environmental sustainability and eco-compatibility.
Verification of the acquisition of autonomy of judgment will occur through the evaluation of the results achieved in the core disciplines as well as in the optional subjects chosen by the student, and through the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work individually and in groups during practical activities and in the execution of the assigned activity in preparation for the final exam.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The bachelor's degree course in Viticultural, Enological, and Food Technologies provides knowledge that, in light of the Dublin descriptors, can be considered adequate in the various disciplinary fields. The expected learning outcomes can be summarized as follows:
1) Mathematical, physical, computer science, and statistical disciplines: full understanding of the concept of function and the basic principles governing differential and integral calculus, with particular reference to the concepts of limit and continuity;
2) Chemical disciplines: knowledge of the atomic-molecular constitution of materials according to weight ratios described by stoichiometry; understanding of the role of chemical bonds and structure on the properties of materials, and the main chemical and biochemical reactions occurring during the production, transformation, and preservation of food products;
3) Biological disciplines: understanding of the fundamental aspects of the biology of prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms; management of technological, altering, and/or pathogenic microorganisms for nutritional improvement and ensuring food safety;
4) Food technology disciplines: understanding of the relationships between biological, agricultural, and breeding issues and the quality of transformed products; possession of logical and knowledge tools to understand the main operations and processes of the food industry and the "production process - product quality" binomial; awareness of the complementarity of knowledge acquired in other disciplinary areas for managing a food process and optimizing the quality of finished products; knowledge of analytical techniques, even non-instrumental, for characterizing typicity, quality, and safety of food products; knowledge of cultivars of various herbaceous and arboreal species for human food use;
5) Food safety and analysis techniques disciplines: knowledge of techniques for the prevention and treatment of various plant species from phytophagous insects or fungi; knowledge of analytical techniques, even non-instrumental, for characterizing typicity, quality, and safety of vitivinicultural products; knowledge of applied thermodynamics, applied thermofluid dynamics, and heat transfer; knowledge of the functional role of nutrients and the nutritional characteristics of animal and plant food products;
6) Economic and legal disciplines: knowledge of the main economic theories of supply, demand, production, and trade; understanding of the fundamental characteristics of the food industry, distribution, and the issues of agro-food markets even at the international level; basic knowledge of food and vitivinicultural legislation.

The teaching program has aimed to pursue the specific educational objectives of the Course through a division into two curricula (Food Technologies and Viticulture and Enology) which both feature a first year characterized by common basic training activities. These activities provide a number of CFUs higher than the minimum ministerial requirements for mathematical, physical, computer science, and chemical disciplines. The necessary basic preparation to perform functions in a work context is verified, ex ante, through a prerequisite entrance test for knowledge integration. For these disciplines, knowledge refinement is provided through enhancement courses, preliminary to the official ones, which are planned and initiated by the CDS before the start of the academic year. Verification of these basic knowledge, pre and post preliminary course, allows for better efficiency of the official courses. With the aim of improving the level of knowledge and understanding achieved by students and reaching the final objectives of the course, an increase in the number of credits compared to those minimally required by the DM has been planned, even regarding the core activities. Both in the teaching structure and in the annual manifestos' arrangement, from the course's start date to the present, it has been chosen to enhance food technology disciplines and food safety disciplines.

Consequently, in the Viticulture and Enology curriculum, knowledge and skills related to vine cultivation and protection and the enological sector play a prominent role, while in the Food Technologies curriculum, disciplinary areas related to knowledge and management of food processes; optimization of finished product quality; and product innovation prevail. The choice of disciplines in the related fields, provided in the AGR area, as well as the role of other activities, including the appropriate number of CFUs required for knowledge of a foreign language and the completion of a training internship, complete the effort to increase in the student the degree of mastery of such knowledge and skills. Their verification is continuous both within individual disciplines, through in-course assessments and final exams of the core curricular and optional subjects chosen by students, as well as through feedback from parallel activities to the courses (such as internships, stages, wine-making competitions).

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The course has adopted the documents elaborated in the period 2016-17 by the National Coordinating Bodies of Food Technology (COSTAL) and Viticulture and Enology (CUVE) courses after discussing them in various CdS Councils.
The bachelor's graduate in TVEA has the ability to use, along the entire food production chain, the practical aspects of the acquired knowledge as summarized in the following learning outcomes:
- uses computer tools with mathematical and statistical applications for solving problems of interest in food and vitivinicultural sectors with particular attention to product quality;
- can describe the biochemical, chemical, physical, and biological factors important for the qualitative assessment of raw materials, production, and transformation of food; identifies dangers due to chemical and biological contaminants; and applies appropriate procedures for prevention and risk reduction;
- is able to conduct chemical, microbiological, and sensory analysis of plant products and transformed animal and plant food products;
- is able to evaluate the nutritional correctness of a food and assess the quality of animal and plant products based on their intended use;
- has specific competencies to understand and solve various problems related to the management and governance of companies;
- is able to know and manage the main quality and certification systems for food production;
- is able to understand the operation of the main machines and basic equipment in the vitivinicultural sector and in food industries, as well as manage the main unit operations;
- is able to prepare protocols for the testing and verification of food suitability of packaging, those related to the conscious and effective use of analytical techniques, even non-instrumental, for characterizing typicity, quality, and safety of food products;
- is able to develop monitoring and pest control plans against harmful insects and pathogens according to the principles of integrated pest management;
- has mastery of basic economic concepts, the ability to define needs and goods, and to interpret the financial statements of an agro-food enterprise.
Additionally, possesses the basic knowledge of business organization and strategy and the ability to analyze and interpret consumer and business behavior in the exchange of goods and services.

Teaching Methods and Tools: courses structured in frontal teaching units and laboratory and field exercises with in-course assessments on the level of knowledge and understanding achieved. Learning verification will be carried out through the evaluation of students' active participation in practical and laboratory exercises, while theoretical acquisitions will be verified with written intermediate tests (multiple-choice or open-ended) or oral exams and final exams.

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The bachelor's degree course in Viticultural, Enological, and Food Technologies aims to train a professional figure in the most characteristic areas of agro-food production. The course aims to provide knowledge and form professional skills adequate to operate in all stages of the chain, from production to consumption. The course is structured into two curricula with the first year common, represented by basic subjects, and the following two years structured into specific core disciplines. The training of the graduate in the food technologies sector includes the necessary competencies to ensure hygienic-sanitary safety and quality of food, reduce waste, and reconcile economy and ethics in production. Additionally, the training path aims to provide mastery of chemical, physical, sensory, and microbiological methods and current legislation for the control and evaluation of food, raw materials, and semi-finished products (fresh and processed fruit, dairy, meat, and fish products). In the Viticulture and Enology curriculum, the course will train technical figures capable of operating in the production and consumption chain of grapes and wine, from the design and planting of vineyards, to their sustainable management, to the transformation of grapes and the marketing of wines.

The acquired competencies of the graduate can be utilized in business management or technical assistance in the production and transformation phases carried out in public or private contexts. Their communication skills will be enhanced by knowledge of the English language, primarily used in scientific and commercial fields, and therefore made mandatory with a high number of CFUs.

The bachelor's degree course has a duration of three years and corresponds to the acquisition of 180 university credit units (CFUs). It concludes with the acquisition of CFUs corresponding to the successful completion of the final exam. Teaching is organized for each academic year into two semesters of at least 12 weeks each. The bachelor's degree course includes both theoretical teaching, with a prevalence of frontal lessons, and teaching with a predominantly practical purpose held in the field and in the laboratory. The distribution of the time commitment reserved for each CFU is regulated in the University and Department Teaching Regulations. Each student's training path is guided by a Tutoring Committee operating within the study course. In the bachelor's degree course, monodisciplinary and/or integrated teaching is provided, in accordance with the current Teaching Regulations. For the evaluation of the achievement of the expected learning objectives, in-course assessments are mandatory, in addition to the final exam; the assessments may be written, oral, and/or practical.

The course includes an internship to be carried out at one of over 200 public or private companies contracted with the Department of Agriculture. The internship activity is regulated by a specific regulation that provides a training path followed by an enterprise tutor and a teaching tutor. Only a small part of the internship can be carried out in university facilities.

Verification of foreign language knowledge requires a written and/or oral exam or the validation of a diploma issued by an institute recognized by the University Language Center. Verification of computer skills requires the validation of a diploma issued by the University or a recognized institute attesting the skills required by the ECDL (European Computer Driving License).

The student can acquire elective CFUs by taking one or more courses indicated in the SUA (Student Unit of Assessment) in addition to the mandatory ones or other courses offered by the University of Sassari. CFUs for other activities may be recognized if consistent with the training path of the bachelor's degree course. These activities include the numerous seminars and conferences organized by the Department and the bachelor's degree course, also in collaboration with the association of enologists, a wine-making competition, and other documented training activities carried out by student associations are also evaluated.

Attendance is strongly recommended for all teaching activities; the study manifesto annually establishes the mandatory attendance percentage, distinguishing between full-time students and working students, and the prerequisites between disciplines.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The graduate in the Political Science course must be able to acquire, interpret, and process, according to the methods of the social sciences and using a multidisciplinary approach, the data related to historical, social, political, economic, and legal phenomena pertaining to their professional competence sphere, in order to formulate autonomous judgments, critically evaluate the implications of the issues examined, assess possible solutions, and plan and organize the necessary activities for their implementation, in relation to time, objectives, resources, and results. The acquisition of such skills will be promoted through frontal lectures, exercises, and seminar activities aimed at stimulating the in-depth study of specific topics in an autonomous and group manner. Verification will occur through the evaluation of students' active participation in lectures, exercises, and seminar activities; the completion of intermediate tests and final exams, in written and/or oral form.
Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area The graduate in the Political Science course must acquire adequate knowledge of the specialized conceptual frameworks of historical, political, legal, sociological, economic, and linguistic disciplines, master the relevant methodological tools, and develop critical understanding of the main themes and issues recurring in these disciplines and their developments.
Economic Area Graduates must acquire knowledge and understanding of the principles and methodologies of statistics, as well as the basic concepts of political economy and economic policy.
Sociological Area Graduates must learn the fundamental methods of social research, both quantitative and qualitative, and develop the ability to understand and interpret social phenomena, with particular attention to cultural processes and political communication.
Historical Area Graduates must acquire knowledge and understanding of historical events, main themes, and interpretative methods of historical disciplines through the study of modern and contemporary history. Particular attention will be given to the evolution of political thought through the study of the history of political doctrines, and to the evolution of local and national political institutions.
Political Science Area Graduates must acquire the ability to understand and interpret political and administrative phenomena at both national and international levels through the study of political science, political philosophy, public administration science, and international relations.
Legal Area Graduates will acquire the basic notions and methods of legal disciplines, both public and private. In particular, they must understand the fundamental principles of the legal systems studied, the hierarchy of sources, the division of competences between State and Regions, the functioning mechanisms of international and European Union legal systems, and the relationships between different legal systems.
Linguistic Area Written and oral mastery of two foreign languages, including English and a second language.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area The graduate in the Political Science course must be able to apply acquired knowledge to operate at appropriate levels of responsibility and demonstrate a professional approach to designing proposals and solving problems, even in the role of consultant, within those sectors of the labor market where graduates of class L-36 traditionally find employment, with particular reference to public administrations, businesses, complex organizations, and the third sector, both national and international.
Economic Area Graduates must acquire the fundamental methods of economic research, both quantitative and qualitative, and develop the ability to analyze simple economic problems and statistical data related to the national and international market, in order to apply the acquired knowledge and methodologies to real-world economic phenomena.
Sociological Area Graduates must be able to apply the methods and competencies acquired to contemporary social phenomena, with particular attention to the analysis and evaluation of forms and approaches of political communication.
Historical Area Thanks to the methods and knowledge acquired, graduates will be able to understand the roots of contemporary political phenomena at both local and international levels.
Political Science Area Thanks to the methods specific to each discipline learned, the graduate will be able to apply acquired theories to contemporary political dynamics at local, national, and international levels.
Legal Area Thanks to the acquired knowledge, graduates must be able to conduct legal research, understand the content of internal and international norms, and argue a judgment rendered by a domestic or international judicial body.
Linguistic Area Graduates must be able to communicate in written and oral form in English and the chosen second language, through reading and understanding texts of medium difficulty, drafting simple texts, and conducting conversations on topics related to the studied disciplines.
Official Languages of Teaching and Assessment of Preparedness.
ITALIAN Competencies Associated with the Function.
Experts in Political and Social Sciences The Political Science degree provides a solid and versatile preparation applicable in various work contexts at local, national, or international levels, thanks to the acquisition of methodological competencies and basic knowledge in economic, legal, political, sociological, and historical disciplines, as well as the learning of at least two foreign languages, including English.
In relation to personal interests, individual aptitudes, and occupational expectations, each student may further develop their foundational knowledge by choosing between two recommended pathways: one aimed at acquiring greater mastery of administrative and organizational processes within public and private institutions, through the study of administrative law, labor law, public administration science, human resource management, work psychology, the history of political institutions, and public economics.
The other pathway is intended for those with a strong interest in the international dimension, whether aiming for a traditional diplomatic career or seeking to join public or private organizations operating abroad, or even local organizations maintaining international relations: essential to this is knowledge of international institutions and legal norms, the peculiarities of foreign legal systems from a comparative perspective, and the dynamics underlying international relations from political, geographical, and economic viewpoints.
The multidisciplinary nature of the course, which constitutes a fundamental resource, exposes students to a plurality of perspectives, fosters the development of general competencies, adaptability to multiple contexts and functions, and a flexible approach capable of addressing diverse situations and issues, equipping graduates with a heightened predisposition to adapt to the evolving dynamics of the contemporary labor market.
Function in Workplace Context.
Experts in Political and Social Sciences In today's labor market, Political Science graduates can perform a wide variety of functions. Beyond providing the essential foundational preparation for access to traditional occupations closely linked to politics, political-labor relations, diplomatic-consular careers, and media professions (journalism and related communication management), the degree offers the opportunity to undertake a plurality of job roles corresponding to different occupational profiles, including, for illustrative purposes:
- Staff responsible for management and control in public and private administration;
- Experts in personnel management and organization of work;
- Staff handling secretarial services, archiving, accounting, and similar activities;
- Staff managing public services for issuing certifications and documentation;
- Experts in collecting and processing information;
- Analysts of economic, political, and social processes;
- Evaluators of public policies;
- Curators of communications and relations with internal and external stakeholders (press offices, public relations, event organization);
- Operators in social services and development cooperation;
- State police, urban firefighters, forest rangers;
- Commercial, financial, and insurance agents;
- Administrative staff at diplomatic and consular representations and international organizations;
- Staff handling international business relations in public and private enterprises;
- International relations staff in public and private offices and non-governmental organizations.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
With the aim of training graduates capable of operating in very different professional contexts and addressing a wide range of master's degree courses or similar advanced training paths, the three-year Political Science degree program primarily pursues the following specific objectives:
a) To provide a preparation centered on multi- and interdisciplinary approaches, offering methodological competencies and basic knowledge in historical, political, legal, economic, and social fields;
b) To offer flexible training capable of leveraging different disciplinary sensitivities to read and interpret the complexity of contemporary political, economic, and social phenomena at national and international levels;
c) To develop the flexibility and adaptability necessary to integrate into and adapt to a rapidly evolving labor market;
d) To provide adequate knowledge of English and at least one other foreign language, as indispensable tools for occupying most professional roles sought by Political Science graduates, thereby enhancing the attractiveness of the curriculum vitae.
To achieve the stated objectives, the training path is structured as follows: the first year focuses on acquiring foundational methodological knowledge and preliminary essential knowledge in each disciplinary area contributing to the formation of a Political Science graduate, through the study of:
- Modern History and History of Political Doctrines (historical-political area),
- Public Law Institutions (legal area),
- Political Economy (economic area),
- Statistics, which is appropriately placed in the first year as it is functional to a better understanding and mastery of methods and content not only of economic disciplines but also of sociological and Political Science disciplines, which can be more effectively approached in the following year.
Basic sociological knowledge is provided through a General Sociology course, complemented by Sociology of Cultural and Communication Processes, which provides the fundamentals of political communication necessary to understand the dynamics between media, political systems, and citizens.
In the second year, further deepening occurs in:
- Historical disciplines through the study of Contemporary History, essential for appreciating with due awareness the events of recent history that most influence the present reality;
- Political science through Political Philosophy and Political Science, each offering appropriate evaluation parameters for public policies according to their respective analytical methods;
- Legal disciplines through Private Law Institutions and European Union Law, a discipline that introduces an international dimension into the proposed training path, focusing particularly on European institutions and their competencies, which significantly influence the conduct of national and local public administrations, as well as the activities of private actors across all productive sectors.
In the third year, students complete their path by consolidating foundational preparation in areas of greater interest and more precisely defining their professional profile, considering individual occupational expectations. In particular, students are advised to choose between two pathways: political-administrative and political-international. The first is recommended for those prioritizing in-depth knowledge of the management and control of administrative and organizational processes within public and private institutions, through the study of Administrative Law, Labor Law, Public Administration Science, Human Resource Management, Work Psychology, History of Political Institutions, and Public Economics. The second pathway is intended for those with greater interest in the international dimension and who wish to investigate the functioning of international institutions and the dynamics underlying relations between multiple actors, public and private, operating on the global stage, through the study of International Economics, International Relations, Geopolitics, Comparative Public Law, International Law, and additional legal disciplines offering broader knowledge of the rules governing international relations in specific sectors, such as Maritime Law, International Criminal Law, and International Organizations. Regardless of the chosen pathway, preparation is completed with the acquisition of 12 CFU through one or two exams selected from available options, provided they are consistent with the training project. Additionally, all students must compulsorily take an English language exam and one in a foreign language.
To promote mastery of foreign languages and stimulate willingness to engage with different social and cultural realities—skills that strengthen flexibility, autonomy, and adaptability—the Political Science program strongly encourages all enrolled students to undertake international mobility experiences through Erasmus Plus for study or internship purposes, and the University's Ulisse program for research and internship periods in non-European countries.
Furthermore, the acquisition of training credits is expected through the completion of integrative activities, even outside the university setting, attesting to additional scientific competencies, linguistic abilities, and IT skills, as well as the performance of tasks consistent with the training project through work experiences and internships at public bodies, private companies, associations, and third-sector organizations.

Characteristics of final exam.
The degree in Agro-Zootecnic Sciences is obtained by passing a final exam, consisting of the preparation of a written report, drafted by the student under the guidance of a supervisor teacher, and/or the discussion of a report before a committee of teachers.
The final exam is related to the activities carried out by the student during the internship or is related to the in-depth study of topics addressed during the study course. These activities may concern the following points, possibly integrated:
- Monitoring and critical evaluation of an agro-zootecnic production process or activity;
- Technical-economic design of an agro-zootecnic production activity or part of it;
- Critical analysis and evaluation of certification methods for agro-zootecnic products;
- In-depth bibliographic and documentary research on a specific topic related to internship activities.
The evaluation of the final exam will follow the criteria established by the Didactic Regulations of the Department of Agraria.

The graduate is able to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with agricultural and animal science researchers and specialists, as well as with managers and operators of agricultural and animal production companies, also using a European Union language other than their own, typically English. Learning Ability.
The degree program provides the essential cognitive tools necessary for the continuous updating of knowledge in the specific field, also using new communication and information technology tools, in order to apply knowledge to solving multiple practical problems throughout the entire agricultural and animal production chain. Graduates will have developed learning abilities that allow them to continue studies in a master's degree, a level I master's program, or to enter the workforce directly.
