Autonomy of Judgment.
Graduates must have acquired the ability to compare the thematic nodes emerging in psycho-pedagogical thought with events, problems, and phenomena originating from other fields of knowledge, their applications, and the various life situations, demonstrating critical mastery and independence of judgment.
After the training path, consisting of theoretical study, exercises, group work, internship activities, and in-depth studies, the graduate must be able to critically, consciously, and creatively address educational and psycho-pedagogical issues, hypothesizing and implementing targeted actions for the promotion of the person and support for individuals in difficulty.
The achievement of such expected outcomes will be promoted within specific disciplines and, transversally, through the various teaching and learning activities proposed in the degree course (lectures, workshops, seminars and conferences, internship, and final thesis). Their evaluation will be conducted both in the intermediate and final exams of individual courses and the curricular internship activity, as well as overall at the end of the path, through the student's elaboration and discussion of a final thesis.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Pedagogical Disciplines: Knowledge of the main theoretical models, themes, and issues in the pedagogical-educational-didactic sector, also in their historical evolution.
Knowledge of the main methodologies and operational strategies in the educational field for different intervention sectors.
Psychological Disciplines: Mastery of the main psychological theories and themes, both general and social, as well as developmental psychology, also in relation to educational psychology.
Didactic and Disability Integration Disciplines: Knowledge of the main issues concerning cognitive, affective, and psychosocial aspects from an evolutionary perspective.
Sociological and Anthropological Disciplines: Basic knowledge of the main approaches, methods, and themes in the sociological field and the main theoretical orientations and themes in the anthropological field.
Historical Disciplines: Basic knowledge of the main historical phenomena and historiographical aspects in various eras, with particular attention to the modern and contemporary periods.
Geographical Disciplines: Basic knowledge of the connections between environments and economies using the theoretical tools of economic and political geography as a reading key.
Philosophical Disciplines: Knowledge of themes in contemporary philosophy, the history of philosophical thought, and philosophical historiography.
Language Skills: Good written and oral knowledge of at least one European language, and preferably other foreign languages.
Computer Skills: Knowledge of the main computer tools relevant to the processing of cultural content: electronic text processing, electronic communication, mastery of techniques for consulting electronic databases, etc.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Pedagogical Disciplines: Ability to argue the main themes and issues of the pedagogical-didactic sector.
Ability to apply theoretical assumptions acquired in the pedagogical field to practical educational interventions, as well as to their planning and evaluation.
Ability to interpret and respond to educational questions of the territory in order to realize personalized educational projects.
Psychological Disciplines: Ability to apply theoretical knowledge and skills acquired in the educational field, with particular reference to motivational, emotional, cognitive, and social processes.
Didactic and Disability Integration Disciplines: Ability to integrate and apply theoretical knowledge within specific rehabilitation and educational intervention contexts.
Sociological and Anthropological Disciplines: Ability to read and interpret major social phenomena.
Ability to read and interpret individual and collective human behavior from an anthropological perspective.
Historical Disciplines: Analytical and argumentative skills regarding major historical phenomena and events, also in relation to pedagogical thought.
Geographical Disciplines: Application of acquired skills in planning educational interventions within territorial policies.
Philosophical Disciplines: Ability to critically analyze and argue, with particular attention to developing the capacity to identify interdisciplinary connections for understanding the complexity of reality.
Language Skills: Regarding the languages studied during the degree program, students must have acquired the following competencies:
(a) understanding of scientific literature in the original language, especially concerning content related to the disciplines of the course;
(b) use of at least one foreign language for effective communication of content related to the disciplines of the course;
(c) ability to conduct written exchanges in a foreign language;
(d) ability to engage in oral conversations in a foreign language.
Computer Skills: Ability to process humanistic content (including multimedia) using electronic computers and communicate them via the Internet through appropriate use of specific application programs.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN
Competencies Associated with the Role.
Professional Sociopedagogical Educator (3.4.5.2.0)
Pedagogical competencies and theoretical and operational knowledge of analyzing the main educational and training issues in their various dimensions; knowledge of the principles and methods of planning, management, and evaluation of educational interventions; relational skills and knowledge of group dynamics and the principles of team and network work; ability to analyze and evaluate the personal, family, and social situation of the individual.
Social Reintegration and Integration Technicians (3.4.5.2.0)
Knowledge of the main educational and training issues; knowledge of the main social influences and trends, migration phenomena, and intercultural aspects; applied skills regarding needs analysis, intervention planning and prevention of difficulty, group work techniques, and group management.
Active Elderly Care Expert (3.4.5.2.0)
Knowledge of the main educational and training issues related to andragogy and elderly management; applied skills regarding needs analysis, intervention planning, group work techniques, and group management.
Early Childhood Educators (3.4.5.2.0)
Understanding and knowledge of the childhood condition in contemporary society and the different developmental stages of growth; knowledge of the main pedagogical and didactic intervention models; operational skills for the concrete implementation of educational action within services for early childhood.
Role in the Work Context.
Professional Sociopedagogical Educator (3.4.5.2.0)
Design, develop, and manage networked interventions in the area of personal and educational services, aiming to promote the development of individual growth potential and social inclusion of people (minors and adults) in a state of difficulty, marginalization, and/or deviance.
Social Reintegration and Integration Technicians (3.4.5.2.0)
Work in synergy with the local service network to develop intervention strategies that promote new social and occupational opportunities for the reintegration and development of autonomous pathways for disadvantaged individuals (youth and adults) with particular personal and socio-family difficulties and/or in a state of difficulty or deviance.
Active Elderly Care Expert (3.4.5.2.0)
Work in synergy with the local service network to develop intervention strategies that promote new social, cultural, and animation opportunities for active elderly individuals and the reintegration of pensioners to develop autonomous pathways within a lifelong learning perspective.
Early Childhood Educators (3.4.5.2.0)
Analysis of individual and group educational needs of children. Planning and programming of educational activities aimed at developing children's developmental potential, also through involving their family backgrounds, exercising direct and indirect functions to support parenting.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The specific educational objective for graduates of the Course is the acquisition of a solid cultural preparation in the field of education sciences through in-depth study of pedagogical, psychological, philosophical, and socio-anthropological disciplines. These multidisciplinary competencies and knowledge are essential both for entering the workforce and for continuing studies (enrollment in master's degrees). They are indispensable for the educator's activity in response to the diverse needs of the territory regarding educational needs in various contexts. Therefore, additional specific educational objectives are:
- Acquisition of theoretical and operational competencies for understanding and analyzing socio-cultural contexts, achieved through the teaching of anthropological-social, historical, and economic-social geography disciplines, foreign languages, and contemporary multimedia languages;
- Acquisition of competencies related to the educator's field of activity, developed through specialized education sciences courses and the mandatory curricular internships at educational and training institutions, companies, and public administration bodies, and possibly including stays at other Italian and foreign universities, also within international agreements. The final thesis is also related to fieldwork.
The teaching methodology used in the three-year degree will primarily be classroom-based (also with the support of multimedia, interactive, and online tools), which may take the form of frontal communication, deepening of problematic nodes (group activities, exercises, and workshops), reading and comparing sources, documents, original texts, tables, directories, case studies, etc., also using new online multimedia technologies. Study and thematic deepening seminars will also be held, possibly with the support of external experts, as well as internship activities aimed at acquiring and refining professional competencies.
Regarding the training path, theoretical competencies are acquired predominantly in the first and second years, while specialized courses are entrusted to the second and third years. Theoretical reflection on professional opportunities occurs at various times throughout the three years, while field experience is gained through internships assigned to the second and/or third year. The thesis concludes the L-19 path, but is preceded by bibliographic research and research techniques, treated as integrative aspects of various disciplines and also within the teaching aimed at acquiring the research methodology in the educational field.

a) mastery of the Italian language;
b) basic knowledge of a European Union language;
c) a good basic cultural preparation of a humanistic nature.

Communication Skills.
Graduates must be able to communicate, in both written and oral form, knowledge, theories, and practices related to Cultural Heritage to a wide variety of audiences, including those within the same field of knowledge, in related intercultural fields, or in different fields, adapting the communication style to the diverse needs of the audience. They must possess knowledge of at least one EU language for scientific communication, dissemination, and bibliographic consultation.
They must possess good oral communication skills for conveying information (verified first in individual exam assessments) and good written composition skills for drafting texts on specific topics, starting with the final thesis.
Communication skills are first verified during lectures, in teacher-student interactions (office hours and tutoring), and in seminar and laboratory activities.
Fundamental assessments also occur during passing exams and especially during the graduation exam: this final assessment serves to demonstrate the acquired skills and the ability to express, in an articulated manner, the results of the individual training path through a written text and an oral presentation.
Learning Abilities.
Graduates will be encouraged to develop critical thinking, to reflect on problems, and to cultivate personal knowledge initiative, which will enable future researchers to deepen doubts and thus foster a virtuous process of acquiring further knowledge. For this reason, students will be provided with conceptual tools that, during various teaching phases (lectures, seminars, bibliographic research, archival research, archaeological excavations, field ethnographic research), will be prioritized over mere factual knowledge. Graduates will thus be able to independently pursue further specialized studies, having acquired a precise learning method.
Learning abilities are assessed on multiple occasions: during lectures, in student-teacher meetings (office hours, tutoring activities), in practical and internship activities, in in-course assessments if applicable, in seminar activities, and during passing exams. An additional global assessment occurs in the preparation and discussion of the final thesis.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1171] SCIENCES OF CULTURAL HERITAGE
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10171

Autonomy of Judgment.
Graduates must have acquired the ability to critically analyze the thematic and methodological issues specific to Cultural Heritage, recontextualizing themes and problems related to the ancient world. After completing the training path, which includes theoretical knowledge, exercises, group work, and internship activities, graduates must be able to approach the new uses and recontextualization of archaeological, demo-ethno-anthropological, and environmental heritage in an analytical, conscious, and creative manner. They will also be able to assess the needs for research and valorization activities at both local and national levels, collaborating and supporting various projects promoted by public and private entities. Graduates will thus develop the ability to collect and interpret data for the development of autonomous judgments.

Autonomy of Judgment, a competence that is gradually acquired, is continuously verified throughout the lessons, encouraging students to engage with the topics discussed and connect events; reception and tutoring services, field activities, internships, and especially final exams are fundamental.

Knowledge and Understanding.
HISTORICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge and understanding of historical processes in different eras, in relation to the origins and development of events and the chronological frameworks of reference. Additionally, considering the specific characteristics, knowledge of the political-institutional history of Sardinia from the medieval to the contemporary era is included.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge and understanding of archaeological testimonies relevant to a broad, articulated, and uninterrupted temporal span, from Prehistory to the post-medieval period, and of the fundamental methodological tools for archaeological research, understood from a multidisciplinary perspective.

DEMO-ETHNO-ANTHROPOLOGICAL AND SOCIOLOGICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge and understanding of the approaches and fundamental themes of anthropological research, with particular attention to issues related to identity and multiculturalism in historical and contemporary contexts; knowledge of current theoretical and epistemological frameworks of the disciplines within the demo-ethno-anthropological field.

Knowledge and understanding of the fundamental methodological tools for studying social, political, and environmental processes in urban contexts.

PHILOLOGICAL AND ANCIENT AND MEDIEVAL LITERATURE FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge of the Latin language and its evolution into the Romance languages; knowledge and understanding of texts relevant to ancient, medieval, and humanistic Latin literature and the literary and cultural contexts of reference. Knowledge and understanding of specific themes of ancient literary culture and their connections with aspects of current reality.

ITALIAN LITERATURE FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge of Italian literature in its diachronic development and of linguistic, rhetorical, and stylistic tools.

FOREIGN LANGUAGE FIELD DISCIPLINES: Satisfactory written and oral knowledge of a European Union foreign language.

GEOGRAPHIC FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge of the geographical characteristics of a territory and the methods for analyzing and interpreting related information and graphical representations on cartographic documents; knowledge and understanding of the physical evolution of the landscape, with particular attention to the relationship between geomorphology and cultural heritage.

Knowledge of tools to identify the attractive factors of a territory in relation to cultural heritage and to develop effective marketing strategies.

LEGAL AND ECONOMIC FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge and understanding of Italian and European legislative provisions regarding Cultural Heritage, both material and immaterial, and their implications for the reference territorial contexts, closely linked to policies and systems for the management, use, and valorization of cultural and environmental heritage.

SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge and understanding of scientific methods useful for characterizing artifacts of archaeological, architectural, and historical-artistic interest in relation to various aspects (components, origin, chronology) and for conducting diagnostics to assess their condition and causes of deterioration.

Knowledge and understanding of the fundamental elements regarding the structure, function, and processes of ecosystems, also in relation to cultural heritage.

HISTORICAL-ARTISTIC FIELD DISCIPLINES: Knowledge and understanding of artistic currents and expressions from antiquity to the contemporary era in relation to their historical, social, and cultural contexts. Knowledge of the characteristics and functions of a museum structure in relation to the historical period and cultural and territorial reference context.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
HISTORICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to analyze historical phenomena in close relation to the cultural, social, and economic frameworks of reference, over the long term, and to examine the features and changes in the political, institutional, and economic landscape of medieval, modern, and contemporary Sardinia.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to analyze the main aspects and issues related to different periods and cultural contexts through the examination and study of material documents, contextualized using various types of sources, including written ones. Ability to integrate and apply, according to an interdisciplinary approach, theoretical knowledge in various field research activities (excavation, survey) and artifact analysis (classification and cataloging).

DEMO-ETHNO-ANTHROPOLOGICAL AND SOCIOLOGICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to analyze and interpret human behavior in relation to individual and social dimensions. Ability to analyze theoretical and epistemological frameworks related to contemporaneity, also in relation to issues of identity and multiculturalism.

Ability to address the study of urban phenomena in their transformations and development prospects in relation to social, political, and environmental dynamics.

PHILOLOGICAL AND ANCIENT AND MEDIEVAL LITERATURE FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to approach the reading and analysis of texts from ancient literatures, including hagiographic works, and from medieval and humanistic contexts within their literary and cultural contexts. Ability to relate aspects of ancient culture to current phenomena and situations.

ITALIAN LITERATURE FIELD DISCIPLINES: Critical analysis and commentary of Italian literature texts in relation to the historical-cultural contexts of reference.

FOREIGN LANGUAGE FIELD DISCIPLINES: Satisfactory ability in understanding texts and oral communication of content in a European Union foreign language.

GEOGRAPHIC FIELD DISCIPLINES: Competence in processing and interpreting geographical information using Geographic Information Systems, also in relation to interventions on the territory and environment. Ability to analyze and interpret the evolution of processes determining the physical forms of the landscape.

Ability to examine a territory in relation to cultural sites to promote its development and identify effective management tools.

LEGAL AND ECONOMIC FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to relate Italian and European legislative provisions on Cultural Heritage to the application areas related to research, promotion, management, and valorization activities of the aforementioned heritage, with particular attention to the reference territorial context.

SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNICAL FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to conduct diagnostic analysis of cultural heritage through the most appropriate investigation techniques to determine useful data (material composition, technology, dating) for a coherent historical reconstruction of the heritage - in relation to technological and material characteristics and the context of discovery - and to the needs related to conservation and restoration interventions.

Ability to analyze the structure and functionality of environmental heritage in close connection with cultural heritage, also from the perspective of related management systems.

HISTORICAL-ARTISTIC FIELD DISCIPLINES: Ability to use critical tools for analyzing artistic phenomena, placing them within their historical, social, and cultural context. The application of competencies is further articulated through the ability to evaluate the structure and management of a museum reality that effectively presents works of art and culturally significant artifacts.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Competencies associated with the function.
Museum Operator: Graduates will apply acquired knowledge and competencies to provide valid support for all scientific, dissemination, and management activities of Museums and cultural sites, having the opportunity to express their professional potential through the experience gained during the training path. Through numerous integrative teaching activities and training internships, graduates will be able to: experiment with continuous collaboration in differentiated work groups, apply knowledge for writing synthetic texts, conduct bibliographic research, create catalog sheets, digitize various types of documentation, use main digital devices and internet platforms.

Instructor in Professional Training: Graduates will be able to apply acquired competencies in the retrieval, study, organization, systematization, and presentation of scientific content, tailored to ensure the transfer of specific knowledge and concepts of disciplines with a historical, archaeological, geographical, ethno-anthropological, and historical-artistic character.

Tourist Guide: The functions of guide and tourist companion will allow graduates to express their acquired knowledge and effectively adapt communication to different types of users and visitors of Cultural Heritage. The broad spectrum of acquired knowledge will be a determining factor in the ability to navigate different areas of Cultural Heritage, and the competencies developed in group work dynamics will enable professional operation with local authorities and various public and private entities responsible for the management, promotion, and valorization of cultural sites.

Administrative and Technical Secretaries of General Affairs: The functions of secretaries and technical officers of general affairs allow graduates in Cultural Heritage Sciences to apply argumentative competencies and linguistic-discursive abilities developed during the training path. They will also be able to apply integration and interaction skills with external work groups and colleagues.

Function in the Work Context.
Museum Operator: Graduates will be able to perform educational and organizational support functions at museums of various types, collaborating in the arrangement of museum displays, the realization of exhibitions, the writing of scientific-dissemination texts and panels, promotional campaigns on social media, and assistance in educational activities and other public-oriented initiatives. Support functions within the management of Museums, Pinacothecas, Antiquities, Foundations, and other cultural institutions may also be concretized through computerized cataloging and document reorganization, as well as support for all project activities requiring adequate knowledge in the specific intervention context.

Instructor in Professional Training: Graduates will be able to collaborate in professional training paths that rely on qualified figures for teaching and teaching assistance within courses for the Cultural Heritage sector.

Tourist Guide: Graduates in Cultural Heritage Sciences will perform the functions of guides and tourist companions within diversified work contexts in the cultural tourism sector, enhancing the staff of various public and private entities, such as Cooperatives and other entities managing Museums, Archaeological Areas and Parks, Naturalistic, Literary, and Historical-Artistic Trails, etc. Functions may also be performed through freelance professional activities.

Administrative and Technical Secretaries of General Affairs: Graduates will perform work activities with responsibilities in general services and secretarial roles at public and private administrations. Activities primarily, but not exclusively, involve drafting informational reports, preparing specific dossiers, writing minutes, archiving sensitive information, organizing meetings and conferences, supporting the drafting and presentation of content, and managing relations with users.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The training path of the Cultural Heritage Sciences degree program is structured into multiple curricula to offer a wide range of choices that respond to differentiated demand.

For all paths, a solid historical and philological-literary foundation is provided, with the main disciplines imparted in the first years of the course to provide a historical framework (Greek History, Roman History, Medieval History, Modern History, Contemporary History) and those aimed at providing a historical-literary overview and enabling knowledge of the main sources of different eras (Greek Culture, Latin Literature, Early Christian Literature and Hagiography, Medieval and Humanistic Latin Literature, History of Culture and Classical Tradition, Italian Literature). Of course, the choice of specific disciplines within this broad offer is determined by the specific path chosen and/or personal interests. Essential for all is knowledge of the regulations governing Cultural Heritage Legislation, as well as geographical disciplines, especially for their practical applications (Fundamentals of Thematic Cartography and Geographic Information Systems) or specific in-depth studies (Landscape Geography).

Among the related and integrative disciplines, with options available, there are in-depth studies in the technical-scientific field (Applied Sciences for Cultural Heritage) and historical field (History of Juridical and Economic Institutions of Sardinia).

For all paths, written and oral knowledge of at least one European Union language (B1 level - referring to the CEFR - Common European Framework of Reference for Languages), in addition to Italian, is required.

Fundamental is also the Internship activity, guided by course professors (excavations, surveys, GIS laboratory, etc.) or carried out at external institutions (such as museums, Superintendencies, Restoration Centers, etc.), which allows students to integrate and deepen, through specific paths, the knowledge acquired at the theoretical level.

In particular, the internship at external institutions, verified by the appropriate commission, is aimed at acquiring professional skills in disciplines closely related to the CDSS path.

In the first curriculum, Archaeological, in addition to archaeological research methodologies, disciplines are offered that are differentiated by chronological and cultural areas, starting from those related to the oldest periods, such as Prehistory and Protohistory; followed by Phoenician-Punic Archaeology, Etruscology, and Italian Antiquities, Greek and Roman Archaeology and Art History, Christian Archaeology and Art History, up to Medieval Archaeology.

The second curriculum focuses on themes related to the use and valorization of Cultural Heritage, such as Territorial Marketing and Environmental Policies, along with Cultural Heritage Management; this path also includes disciplines of the demo-ethno-anthropological field (Methodology of Anthropological Research, Cultural Anthropology and Ethnology), which are closely linked to Urban Sociology and Ecology.

A further curriculum provides a Historical-Artistic training, for which all disciplines of this field are offered: History of Medieval, Modern, and Contemporary Art, complemented by Greek and Roman Archaeology and Art History, and Christian Archaeology and Art History. Additionally, with a transversal approach, Museology is included.

Final exam characteristics.
The final exam represents an important moment to apply theoretical, methodological and practical skills acquired during the course. The written work will focus on a historical-geographical-anthropological theme-problem, while simultaneously emphasizing interdisciplinary analysis approaches.
The final work may also consist of an original audiovisual product (in the form of a reportage, documentary, interview, etc.), related to the course subjects, always accompanied by a brief written text.
The final exam is worth 6 CFU and is intended as a first step in conducting research activities.
Required knowledge for access.
To enroll in the Course, a secondary school diploma or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad and recognized as suitable is required.
Students must possess the necessary knowledge for understanding and reading a first-year university text, have developed adequate synthesis skills across different disciplinary contents, be familiar with the spatial and temporal dimensions of anthropic and environmental phenomena, and manage the synchronous and diachronic organization of events with sufficient skill. Regarding the chosen first foreign language, entry-level competencies at A2 level will be required. The verification will be conducted in written form. The methods for verifying the possession of required knowledge and any additional mandatory training obligations to be completed within the first year of the course will be defined in the course's didactic regulations.

Communication skills.
The Master's degree in Planning, Management and Promotion of Culture and Environmental Itineraries will be awarded to students who demonstrate they have acquired the necessary knowledge to effectively communicate scientific, methodological and evaluative content, as well as the problems, hypotheses and solutions for an appropriate relationship between territory, environment and health to both sector experts and non-experts, through the appropriate use of linguistically and technologically suitable tools and systems. Verification will occur through exam tests and in-course assessments and the evaluation of the final exam.
Learning capabilities.
The Master's degree in Planning, Management and Promotion of Culture and Environmental Itineraries will be awarded to students who demonstrate they have developed the necessary learning capabilities to undertake subsequent studies requiring a high degree of applied knowledge, understanding, autonomy and essential communication skills for initiating higher-level analyses.
Verification of the achievement of these capabilities will occur through exam tests and in-course assessments and the evaluation of the final exam.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A116] Design, Management, and Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Tourism Itineraries
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10829?annoOrdinamento=2023

Autonomy of Judgment.
The title of Doctor in Design, Management, and Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Tourism Itineraries will be awarded to students who have achieved the ability to collect and interpret data and information useful for determining autonomous and scientific judgments, with particular reference to territorial transformation processes, protection and valorization of cultural assets in the broadest possible sense, risk assessment, and social and environmental emergencies, at local, national, and international levels. The acquisition of such abilities will be achieved through guided practical sessions linked to certain courses, and will find further development and deepening in the activities for the preparation of the final exam. The verification of the achieved ability to formulate autonomous and scientifically grounded judgments will take place during the examination moments of the core courses and, especially, of those specifically oriented.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Cultural, Territorial, and Landscape Area. The graduate must possess a body of knowledge in areas related to the study of territory, geographical, geo-cartographic, literary, musical, artistic, archaeological, historical, and anthropological phenomena that characterize the cultural and social landscape and allow for understanding and applying strategies useful for the valorization of tourism resources. The study of Geography, Regional Geography, Economic Geography, Territorial Systems and geo-economic models, Territorial Development and Tourism, Cultural, Landscape, and Environmental Resource Planning and Management, as well as Tourism Sociology, will provide the graduate with a good awareness of complex phenomena related to contemporary reality, both in relation to the peculiarities of the local territory and in an increasingly indispensable globalized perspective. To these competencies are added knowledge related to natural and urban landscapes and their changes (Architecture, Culture, and Environment), which are studied both from a cultural perspective (Tourism Anthropology and Audiovisual Landscapes) and from a scientific-health perspective (Environmental and Territorial Hygiene, Nutraceuticals and Pharmacology). Thanks to the study of literature, the graduate has a good preparation in the field of narratives and the potential they offer within the context of cultural tourism and its valorization. Moreover, the graduate will have a good preparation in the historical, literary, artistic, and archaeological fields, both in the ancient context (Archaeology and Analysis of Territorial Systems of the Nuragic Age, Economic and Social History of Roman Sardinia) and in the modern and contemporary context (History of Music in Sardinia, Curatorial Practices and Museum Management); such knowledge allows them to understand the richness of territories and the potential for development and valorization of cultural assets present therein.

Economic and Statistical Area. The graduate in L 6 will possess good knowledge in the economic geography field as well as useful statistical notions that will enable them to navigate the complex territory of tourism planning. The graduate is indeed a hybrid figure, trained in interdisciplinarity, as they must necessarily combine traditional humanistic knowledge relevant to the Cultural, Territorial, and Landscape Area described above with a more technical body of knowledge. Thanks to the study of Economics and Management of Enterprises and Measurement and Analysis of Territory, they will possess good capabilities for reading and interpreting data and flows related to tourism and its spin-offs, and will also be able to apply innovative strategies for implementation and sustainable development.

Linguistic and Communication Area. The graduate, in addition to a good knowledge of the Italian language, general linguistics, and Sardinian linguistics, will master the chosen linguistic disciplines for information exchange within the specific tourism context, having had the opportunity to choose at least two foreign languages among English, Spanish, and German. The acquisition of such competencies is ensured not only by institutional courses in Languages and Linguistics but also by opportunities for study abroad through student mobility (Erasmus and Erasmus Placement programs). The study of languages will ensure the acquisition of a good general and sector-specific preparation, and the ability to use the chosen languages fluently in the exchange of current information, as well as through the use of new communication techniques specific to the tourism sector. Within the scope of communication capabilities, the graduate will also have good preparation in the field of informatics and new technologies adopted in the GIS Laboratory, since social communication, careful use of network resources, and the ability to engage with basic informatics tools will be indispensable skills for a training path aimed at the valorization of cultural and sustainable tourism.

Legal Area. The graduate in this program possesses good knowledge of the legal field that enables them to navigate the regulatory frameworks governing tourism offerings, programming, and promotion (Public Tourism Law and Comparative Public Law). Thanks to the study of legal disciplines, the graduate will have the necessary competencies to navigate opportunities offered by European measures and national and regional policies within the context of cultural and sustainable tourism.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Cultural, Territorial, and Landscape Area. The graduate in L 6 will be able to apply the acquired cultural and territorial knowledge in the concrete scenario of cultural and sustainable tourism. Indeed, they are capable of imagining alternative geographical, historical, artistic, musical, cultural, and natural itineraries that valorize the cultural heritage of the territory, particularly but not exclusively local, in order to expand and enrich the tourism offer in terms of culture and regional environmental sustainability.

Economic and Statistical Area. The graduate in L 6 will have the ability to apply the acquired geo-economic knowledge within the vast and complex field of tourism planning and will be able to identify useful tools for enterprises and for the planning of initiatives to enhance the tourism offer. Furthermore, they will be able to analyze data and information related to the territory and apply appropriate management strategies for the valorization, promotion, and development of cultural and sustainable tourism.

Linguistic and Communication Area. The graduate in L 6 will be able to apply the acquired linguistic and communication knowledge within the broad panorama of tourism communication. Therefore, they are able to produce texts related to the territory and tourism valorization in both Italian and the chosen foreign languages; they are also able to communicate content related to the tourism sector appropriately, effectively, and fluently in Italian and the chosen foreign languages. The acquired informatics skills will finally enable them to navigate the web and produce content useful for promoting and valorizing sustainable and cultural tourism on the network, social networks, and major information dissemination channels.

Legal Area. The graduate in L 6 will be able to employ the acquired legal competencies to navigate and operate within the regional and community legislative landscape. They will also be capable of interpreting fundamental public law norms and institutions, analyzing and identifying the main forms of legal organization of enterprises, and analyzing legal relationships between parties involved in the enterprise-labor context.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

- Definition of proposals for the valorization of local and tourism components

- Classification of landscapes in GIS

- Identification of development strategies and execution of cost-benefit analyses
- Definition of proposals for the valorization of local and tourism components
- Production and acquisition of knowledge data on cultural and environmental assets of the territory
- Collaboration in organizing educational activities of museums, areas, and archaeological parks.

Graduates are able to effectively use, in written and oral form, at least one European Union language in addition to Italian. They possess specific competencies regarding local development strategies, territorial marketing, wellbeing, and legislation concerning cultural, landscape, and environmental assets.

Work Context Function.
Tourism, Cultural, and Environmental Consultant
- Territorial and Environmental Consultant
- Expert in multimedia products and audiovisual documentation
- Expert in landscape analysis and GIS representations
- Expert in environmental, historical-cultural, and tourism context analyses
- Coordinator of interdisciplinary work groups
- Consultant for organizing cultural events and exhibitions
- Consultant for urban planning: regional and municipal
- Consultant for regional and municipal strategic plans
- Consultant for landscape-environmental plans
- Operator in the field of cultural and environmental territory promotion
- Operator in the field of managing advanced cultural tourism systems for territory valorization
- Operator in the field of scientific dissemination and specialized publishing on territorial cultural aspects
- Operator at public and private bodies involved in the management of cultural and environmental assets.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The dual and connected relationship between physical and anthropic components and between environmental and population health has, at present, great relevance due to the implications that may arise at various levels. The interdisciplinary perspective becomes central for a varied series of aspects and phenomena, such as: interpreting existing components and current trends, aspects related to quality of life, demographic, economic, etc.; perspectives for recovery and development within the capacity of ecosystems to respond and bear loads; reduction of territorial inequalities; active valorization of historical-cultural and environmental assets in a patrimonialization perspective. Therefore, it is appropriate to train figures with integrated competencies, capable of providing a careful interpretative reading of processes and phenomena developing and a detailed and relational analysis of elements characterizing different contexts, at local and global scales. In this perspective, the course in Design, Management, and Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Tourism Itineraries aims to train figures that can combine interdisciplinary knowledge and content and systematize various abilities and practical competencies for territorial synthesis and screening analyses.

The first block of courses is designed and structured to provide foundational knowledge preparatory for the subsequent two blocks, at the geographical level (M-GGR/01), historical, social, archaeological (L-ANT/03, L-ANT/01, and SPS/10), and economic (SECS-P/08) levels, which are constantly linked to the understanding of the relationships between culture, environment, and landscape (ICAR/20). Additionally, an optional group of linguistic courses is provided.

The second block aims to provide more specific competencies at the environmental, territorial, and landscape resource management level (M-GGR/02) with in-depth studies in literature (L-FIL-LET/14 and L-FIL-LET/11). A specific focus is dedicated to the economic functionality and management of public and private enterprises with statistical in-depth studies (SECS-S/01) and the analysis of public law institutions from a comparative perspective (IUS/21), with particular reference to the attribution of normative and administrative competencies on the territory, with an aim to provide tools for knowledge and application of relevant legal institutions in national, regional, local, and comparative contexts. Concurrently, the deepening of linguistic competencies is continued.

In the third block, the course focuses on territorial and tourism development from an anthropological and legal perspective (M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, M-DEA/01, and IUS/09) with a view also to the field of hygiene and environment (MED/42). The study of the representation and dissemination of the landscape and local cultural heritage in linguistic and artistic fields in general (L-LIN/01, L-ART/06) will be deepened, thus moving towards delicate and highly relevant directions at the national and international level, and combining the qualitative-perceptual-emotional component with the more purely technical-planning one. In the third block, in addition to further elective disciplines and a group of practical-laboratory activities, internship or stage activities are also provided for students at public or private sector enterprises.

Certain relevance, within the educational path, is also attributed to other knowledge useful for entering the workforce, with training activities often of a laboratory type, focusing on geotechnologies or aimed at addressing current thematic issues, and to internships. By combining direct and indirect observation, teamwork experiences, and activities with a high participatory component, the course aims to train figures that can act as a bridge between specialists from different sectors and bring added value and original elements to interdisciplinary research.

They will also be capable of interpreting fundamental public law norms and institutions, analyzing and identifying the main forms of legal organization of enterprises, and analyzing the legal relationships between parties involved in the enterprise-labor context.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The dual and connected relationship between physical and anthropic components and between environmental and population health acquires, at present, great relevance for the implications that may arise at various levels. The interdisciplinary perspective becomes pivotal for a varied series of aspects and phenomena, such as: interpretation of current components and trends, aspects related to quality of life, demographic and economic spheres, etc.; prospects for recovery and development within the capacity of ecosystems to respond and bear load; reduction of inequalities and territorial disparities; active valorization of historical-cultural and environmental assets in a patrimonialization perspective. Therefore, it is appropriate to train figures with integrated competencies, capable of providing a careful interpretative reading of the processes and phenomena developing and a detailed and relational analysis of the elements characterizing different contexts, at local and global scales. In this perspective, the course in Design, Management, and Promotion of Cultural and Environmental Itineraries aims to train figures that can combine interdisciplinary knowledge and content and systematize various abilities and practical competencies for synthesis analysis and territorial screening.

The first block of course disciplines is designed and structured to provide foundational knowledge preparatory for the next two blocks, at the geographical level (M-GGR/01), historical, social, archaeological (L-ANT/03, L-ANT/01, and SPS/10), and economic (SECS-P/08) levels, which are constantly linked to understanding the relationships between culture, environment, and landscape (ICAR/20). Additionally, an optional group of linguistic courses is provided.

The second block is aimed at providing more specific competencies at the environmental, territorial, and landscape resource management level (M-GGR/02) with in-depth studies in literature (L-FIL-LET/14 and L-FIL-LET/11). A specific focus is dedicated to economic functionality and management of public and private enterprises with statistical (SECS-S/01) and comparative public law institutions analysis (IUS/21), with particular reference to the attribution of normative and administrative competencies on the territory, with a view to providing tools for knowledge and application of relevant legal institutions at national, regional, local, and comparative levels. Concurrently, the deepening of linguistic competencies is continued.

In the third block, the course focuses on territorial and tourism development from an anthropological and legal perspective (M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, M-DEA/01, and IUS/09), also looking at the field of hygiene and environment (MED/42). The study of the representation and dissemination of the landscape and local cultural heritage in linguistic and artistic fields in general (L-LIN/01, L-ART/06) will be deepened, moving towards delicate and highly relevant directions at national and international levels, and combining the qualitative-perceptual-emotional component with the more purely technical-planning one. In the third block, in addition to further elective disciplines and a group of practical-laboratory activities, internship or placement opportunities are also provided for students at public or private sector enterprises.

A certain relevance is also attributed within the training path to other useful knowledge for entering the workforce, with often laboratory-type training activities, focusing on geotechnology or addressing current problem themes, and internships-placements. By combining direct and indirect observation, teamwork experiences, and activities with a high participatory component, the course aims to train figures that can act as a bridge between specialists from different sectors and bring added value and original elements to interdisciplinary research.

Communication Skills.
The entire range of courses within the fields of Study Languages and Cultures of the Respective Countries, as well as Sectoral Languages, advanced linguistic skills, and linguistic mediation from/to the study languages work together to ensure the highest possible development of communication skills achievable over the three years of the Course. Thanks to the knowledge and abilities thus acquired, and in light of the critical judgment developed in the ways previously described, graduates in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation are able to constructively engage with their Italian and foreign interlocutors: taking into account the diversity of cultural and linguistic contexts and knowing how to value them, while modulating their intervention and adapting it to the specific needs that arise in each case.
Through the successful completion of assessments and examinations, and then the graduation examination, the actual acquisition of the ability to express thoughts, projects, and study results in a detailed and complex manner, both orally and in writing, is verified. Graduates are thus capable of effectively and independently conveying what they have learned during their studies, adapting to diverse work contexts. Other moments for verifying communication skills occur during lectures, student office hours, and tutoring sessions.
Learning Skills.
Given that learning ability implies the development of sensitivity, critical and methodological skills necessary for identifying suitable educational paths and means to achieve a given knowledge goal, all courses comprising the Course's educational offer serve as valid experiential fields for this purpose. In particular, graduates in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation draw upon courses in the fields of Language, Italian Literature, Comparative Literature, as well as Sectoral Languages, advanced linguistic skills, and linguistic mediation from/to the study languages. Following the competencies acquired over the three years, graduates in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation are able to interact in multiple languages with diverse interlocutors in different professional and cultural contexts, interpreting, understanding, and autonomously utilizing the modes of expression and communication of these contexts. They are able to critically navigate an increasingly complex multimedia world, distinguishing reliable information sources from unreliable ones, and identifying places from which to gain genuine knowledge. The high degree of learning autonomy and the advanced linguistic level, verified through the successful completion of in-course assessments and final examinations, then provide an effective pathway to access two-year master's degree courses or first-level master's programs. Other moments for verifying learning skills occur during lectures, student office hours, and tutoring sessions.

SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10071

Autonomy of Judgment.
The ability to formulate autonomously constructed and deeply elaborated judgments, which is refined through engagement with theoretical and practical situations stimulating the adoption of a personal perspective, is evidently matured through the contribution of each discipline constituting the Study Plan of Linguistic and Cultural Mediation. However, its development particularly depends on the pivotal teachings of the Italian Language and Literature and Comparative Literature fields. The in-depth reading of a literary text, Italian and foreign, indeed requires the gradual development of a critical and exegetical spirit, which, once acquired, can be applied to any field, remaining a lasting heritage of the student.
The teachings related to the field of Philology and General and Applied Linguistics therefore offer the opportunity to test and strengthen the autonomy of judgment thus matured. Therefore, through debates, exercises, and interactions with teachers and other students (experiences continuously encouraged during the three-year program within lectures, seminars, study days, conferences, symposiums, cineforums), graduates in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation have acquired a method and sensitivity enabling them to effectively translate and interpret the expressions of other cultures and civilizations. They also demonstrate the ability to overcome, through their critical autonomy, prejudices and obstacles that constantly arise in intercultural encounters.
The autonomy of judgment, gradually acquired, is the result of meticulous and constant verification, carried out not only through the aforementioned activities but also through weekly student meetings, tutoring, and especially exams, which constitute crucial feedback for improving the teaching body's educational intervention.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Area of Communication, Linguistics, and Literature The Bachelor's Degree Course in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation strongly bases its teaching and educational action on linguistic, literary, and broadly cultural texts, Italian and foreign, particularly emphasizing a variety of interactive modalities between teacher and student. This is particularly addressed by the teaching activities related to the Area of Communication, Linguistics, and Literature. This allows students to gradually acquire, over the three years of the course, a significant ability to understand, express, and interact orally and in writing in Italian and at least two foreign languages, along with an ability to understand the possible range of theoretical-practical problems and identify problem-solving methods, supported by an expanding knowledge base and a continuously refined research methodology. The reference to the acquired knowledge, at written and oral levels, related to at least two foreign languages must be understood differently depending on the educational path the student intends to pursue. It is clear, for example, that a professional figure with a linguistic-cultural connotation requires knowledge related to the field "Languages of Study and Cultures of the Respective Countries" higher than those required for a figure with a literary-philological character, and therefore must acquire a greater number of CFU (60 vs 48) within its field. Therefore, graduates in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation, thanks to frontal lectures, seminars, exercises, and multimedia laboratory activities (including self-learning) organized by the teaching staff of the Course, acquire a high level of knowledge of at least two foreign languages, combined with a pronounced ability to understand the cultural context within which they develop. The competencies thus acquired, verified through in-course assessments and final exams, are nourished by the ability to connect and compare elements of one's own language and culture with those of the languages and cultures of the world. It is for all this that, as mentioned, graduates, thanks to the critical-methodological readings provided within individual courses, possess a deep level of critical analysis ability regarding linguistic, literary, and broadly cultural texts, Italian and foreign, even complex ones, and other forms of expression and interaction.

Area of Philosophy, History, Art, and Cinema The Area of Philosophy, History, Art, and Cinema is intended to strengthen and expand the knowledge and abilities of understanding, expression, and interaction provided to the student by the teachings of the Communication, Linguistics, and Literature Area. It expresses its educational content within an interdisciplinary horizon composed of courses that enable students to deeply penetrate the theoretical and practical mechanisms that animate a culture in its philosophical, historical, pedagogical, artistic, and critical-cinematic aspects. The intense teacher-student interaction during lectures, seminars, and cineforums allows for the simultaneous acquisition of competence and critical sensitivity.

Area of Sociology, Anthropology, Economics, and Geopolitics The Area of Sociology, Anthropology, Economics, and Geopolitics is also aimed at integrating the knowledge and understanding abilities provided to the student by the teachings of the Communication, Linguistics, and Literature Area. The educational content it expresses is primarily aimed at creating practical competence, not just theoretical, in reference to the social, economic, and political dimension (in its various layers) within which the student will operate after graduation. This Area presents itself as an important point of connection between the Course and the reference economic-workforce fabric.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Area of Communication, Linguistics, and Literature Graduates in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation, thanks to the knowledge and abilities of understanding, expression, and interaction acquired through the teaching activities related to the Communication, Linguistics, and Literature Area (frontal lectures, exercises, guided readings, individual assignments, multimedia laboratory activities, which deeply introduce them into foreign cultures and Italian culture), are able to interact with texts, people, or organizations of other cultures and civilizations in various contexts of daily and professional life, with flexibility and critical spirit. Through the linguistic and cultural tools they have mastered (and whose acquisition has been verified through the successful completion of written and/or oral exams), they can address the most diverse problematic situations arising from cultural exchange. They have indeed acquired the ability to combine knowledge and competencies in the interdisciplinary dimension, and to interpret, by relating them to each other, different linguistic and cultural fields. They also know how to apply these abilities thanks to the acquisition of computer elements obtained through computer lab exercises and related assessments.

Area of Philosophy, History, Art, and Cinema The abilities to apply knowledge and understanding are especially expanded and strengthened by the seminar, symposium, and cineforum activities specific to the Area of Philosophy, History, Pedagogy, Art, and Cineforum. The debates to which students are constantly prompted following the viewing of films or readings of essays, contemporary art works, visits to museums and galleries allow them to grasp the philosophical, historical, pedagogical, and broadly cultural aspects characterizing the knowledge acquired during the course of study.

Area of Sociology, Anthropology, Economics, and Geopolitics The Area of Sociology, Anthropology, Economics, and Geopolitics is also intended to expand and strengthen the abilities to apply knowledge and understanding acquired through the activities of the Communication, Linguistics, and Literature Area. Since its educational content is primarily aimed at creating the aforementioned practical competence, not just theoretical, in relation to the social, economic, and political dimension (in its various layers) within which the student will operate after graduation, this Area presents itself as an important point of connection between the Course and the reference economic-workforce fabric.

Official Languages of Teaching and Assessment of Preparedness.
ITALIAN

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Linguistic Mediator in Multicultural Contexts The graduate is able to manage interpersonal communication contexts that include, among other things, the preparation of documents using specialized languages, the ability to write letters in a foreign language, take notes in a foreign language, and navigate the use of digital tools. He can also leverage his interdisciplinary preparation to personally use (or teach others) the linguistic structures he has mastered through the studies conducted in the Course, directing these structures towards institutional, business, and cultural relations with foreign countries in various multietnic and multicultural contexts where he may operate, both in Italy and abroad.

Function in the Workplace Context.
Linguistic Mediator in Multicultural Contexts The tasks the graduate is able to routinely perform are those related to communication and linguistic and interlinguistic mediation, oral and written, in at least two foreign languages in addition to Italian. This makes the graduate particularly suitable for collaborating with figures who, in their respective work areas, hold managerial and organizational roles.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Course in Linguistic and Cultural Mediation aims to combine the qualifying educational objectives of the class (as established at the ministerial level) with the specific needs of the territory (that of the Sassari area and, more generally, of Northern Sardinia), offering a rich educational path divided into three curricula.

Specific Educational Objectives Two are the fundamental educational objectives of the Course. One is to ensure that graduating students have a solid knowledge and versatile competence in at least two foreign languages, along with an enhanced oral and written mastery of the Italian language; the other is to develop a strong competence regarding the cultures that animate the studied foreign languages and the Italian language. These fundamental objectives are functional to creating a specific professional profile that allows the graduate to leverage the acquired competencies to enter the job market, seizing not only the economic potential inherent in the territory but also those present on the international level.

Description of the Educational Pathway Regarding the more strictly linguistic part of the educational offering proposed to students by the Course, in addition to the main foreign languages spoken in Europe and the Americas, the Course offers a training path in Chinese language and Chinese culture, enabling interaction and communication not only at the international level (due to China's growing importance in global markets) but also at the local level (due to the presence of a continuously expanding Chinese community in the Northern Sardinia territory). Always with the aim of best satisfying the territory's needs, the Course also offers a training path in Catalan language, highly important for valuing and revitalizing the typical linguistic-cultural heritage of the Alghero area. Regarding this, it is also worth noting, on one hand, that the competencies acquired through the study of French language and culture enable interaction and communication with the increasing number of immigrants in Northern Sardinia from African nations where French is a common medium of linguistic mediation (the growing needs of the Sassari City Council's immigration office are just one example among many), and, on the other hand, that the competencies acquired through the study of the Russian language enable graduates to intercept the tourist flow from Russia, leveraging this mediation for work and economic purposes. Regarding the more strictly cultural part of the educational offering, in addition to providing training paths centered on the cultures that animate the studied foreign languages, the Course has placed particular emphasis on valuing the historical, social, and cultural dynamics that have shaped Northern Sardinia over the centuries: hence the introduction of courses that take into account Greek civilization, Roman history, sociology of interethnic relations, social anthropology, and the study of Sardinian minority languages. The aforementioned objective of enabling the graduating student to enter the job market with appropriate competencies regarding both the local and international situation is achieved through courses related to business economics, geopolitics, computer science, the geographical-economic composition of the world, etc. Finally, aware that making all this possible requires the development of significant human and intellectual sensitivity, the Course provides training paths related to Italian literature, foreign literatures, comparative literature, literary criticism, philosophical reflection, contemporary arts, and cinema. As can be inferred from a look at the table of educational activities, the aforementioned objectives are achieved, starting from the first year of the course, through the in-depth study, both practical and theoretical, of two foreign languages in addition to Italian. In subsequent years, in addition to enhancing linguistic structures and theoretical-cultural reflection, the objectives are achieved through frontal lectures, exercises, seminars, and various contextual activities (participation in symposiums, cultural cineforums in foreign language, plenary conferences, interactive study days), which allow for the acquisition of in-depth theoretical-practical knowledge regarding the contextualization of the studied languages and their cultures.

The learning capability is continuously measured and verified through tutoring and career monitoring actions implemented by the CdS: the constant interaction between teachers and students ensures the effectiveness of learning processes, providing students with essential methodological support.
