Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
1) Foundational Sciences The graduate is able to apply the knowledge and understanding acquired in theoretical training, laboratory experience, and internship in a manner that demonstrates a professional approach to work and possesses adequate skills to develop and support arguments and solve problems. In particular, they are able to:
- Relate correctly and professionally with patient companions, general and specialist doctors, technical colleagues, and other healthcare staff;
- Correctly use patient protection devices and technical-methodological strategies to minimize patient dose as much as possible;
- Monitor the correct functioning of equipment and devices entrusted to them, addressing minor issues, and implementing verification and control programs to ensure quality, according to predefined indicators and standards, in collaboration with the medical physicist;
- Maximize image quality and minimize artifacts, based on knowledge of available options regarding image formation parameters, knowledge of various components of instrumentation/hardware, and understanding of their operation, as a result of training in basic and core subjects, computer science, as well as laboratory attendance and internship completion;
- Implement procedures for treatment, processing, evaluation, storage of data, transmission, and archiving of acquired images.

The achievement of the ability to apply the aforementioned knowledge and understanding occurs through frontal lectures, critical reflection activities on proposed texts, simulation activities in courses related to specific professional competencies, professional laboratory activities, and internship completion.

Knowledge and skills are acquired and verified in the following educational activities:
Clinical and Radiological Sciences The graduate is able to apply the knowledge and understanding acquired in theoretical training, laboratory experience, and internship in a manner that demonstrates a professional approach to work and possesses adequate skills to develop and support arguments and solve problems. In particular, they are able to:
- Identify the radiological request, determining a work plan consistent with the clinical question and realistic in relation to the patient's characteristics;
- Verify patient identity and, in the case of fertile women, inquire about pregnancy status; inform the patient, using language appropriate for non-experts, about preparation and execution of the examination, justifying any invasive or merely uncomfortable maneuvers; inform the patient about the method of report retrieval; identify and eliminate any privacy-related issues;
- Perform multi-competency procedures within their scope in collaboration with the medical physicist, radiologist, nuclear medicine physician, and radiation therapist, according to previously defined diagnostic and therapeutic protocols by the facility manager;
- Operate safely and correctly perform conventional radiology, computed tomography, nuclear magnetic resonance, mammography, interventional radiology, angiography, neuroradiology, nuclear medicine, etc., using contrast media when specified by diagnostic protocols;
- Interpret and evaluate, from an operational perspective, a radiotherapy treatment plan and medical prescription;
- Provide consultation on technological products and identify areas requiring further consultation.

The achievement of the ability to apply the aforementioned knowledge and understanding occurs through frontal lectures, critical reflection activities on proposed texts, simulation activities in courses related to specific professional competencies, professional laboratory activities, and internship completion.

Knowledge and skills are acquired and verified in the following educational activities:
Prevention and Management The graduate is able to apply the knowledge and understanding acquired in theoretical training, laboratory experience, and internship in a manner that demonstrates a professional approach to work and possesses adequate skills to develop and support arguments and solve problems. In particular, they are able to:
- Understand the organizational context of the Operational Unit where work is performed, identify involved professional figures, and the type of radiological equipment and devices available; identify personal protective devices and verify their completeness, communicating any deficiencies to the Manager;
- Use personal dosimeters according to the procedures set by the protection manager in all activities involving exposure to ionizing radiation;
- Verify personal hygiene and workplace conditions, communicating any deficiencies to the Manager;
- Participate in the planning and organization of work within the structure in collaboration with other healthcare figures;
- Operate safely with radiotherapy equipment, including the accuracy and precision of daily setup;
- Design, deliver, and monitor technical training programs;
- Identify critical issues and promote proposals for their resolution;
- Collaborate on research projects and apply results to improve health quality.

The achievement of the ability to apply the aforementioned knowledge and understanding occurs through frontal lectures, critical reflection activities on proposed texts, simulation activities in courses related to specific professional competencies, professional laboratory activities, and internship completion.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Associated Competencies.
Medical Radiology Technician The competencies associated with the role of Medical Radiology Technician include: knowledge of diagnostic imaging procedures and techniques; skills in using advanced radiological and radiotherapy equipment; knowledge of healthcare procedures and radiation protection standards; knowledge of the functionality of the RIS (Radiology Information System); good communication skills; ability to work in a team; stress management skills; empathy and sensitivity; precision and attention to detail.

Work Context Function.
Medical Radiology Technician The medical radiology technician is the healthcare professional who, holding a university diploma enabling the profession and registered with the Professional Register, is responsible for their actions and authorized to perform radiological examinations and procedures.

The medical radiology technician is an authorized healthcare professional to perform, in accordance with Law of January 31, 1983, No. 25, independently or in collaboration with other healthcare figures, on medical prescription, all interventions requiring the use of ionizing radiation sources, both artificial and natural, thermal energy, ultrasonic, nuclear magnetic resonance, as well as interventions for physical or dosimetric protection.

Additionally, the medical radiology technician participates in the planning and organization of work within the structure they operate, respecting their competencies; plans and manages the delivery of multi-competency services in direct collaboration with the radiologist, nuclear medicine physician, radiation therapist, and medical physicist, according to previously defined diagnostic and therapeutic protocols by the facility manager; is responsible for their actions, particularly by monitoring the correct functioning of equipment entrusted to them, addressing minor issues, and implementing verification and control programs to ensure quality according to predefined indicators and standards; performs their activities in public or private healthcare structures, either as an employee or as a self-employed professional.

Finally, the medical radiology technician contributes to the training of support staff and directly participates in updating their professional profile and research.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Bachelor's Degree Course in Medical Radiology Techniques, Imaging, and Radiotherapy aims to train graduates who possess:
a) Adequate mastery of general scientific methods and content in the areas of Diagnostic Imaging and Radiotherapy, Neuroradiology, Applied Physics in Medicine, and Medical Sciences and Techniques, acquiring methodological, theoretical, and experimental competencies suitable for further development in subsequent cycles;
b) Professional competencies for the exercise of the profession of Medical Radiology Technician.

A sufficient preparation in basic disciplines, enabling the best understanding of the most relevant elements underlying pathological processes developing in childhood, adulthood, and old age, which are the focus of the diagnostic intervention of the Radiology Technician, is guaranteed by the study, concentrated especially in the first year of the course, of Anatomy, Histology, Applied Biology, Medical Chemistry and Biochemistry, Human Physiology, Computer Science, and Medical Statistics, Fundamentals of Physics, Physical Foundations of Radiological Equipment, Radiobiology, and Radiation Protection.

Basic knowledge is completed in the second and third years with the study of Pathology and Elements of First Aid.

Elements of medical-surgical sciences and interdisciplinary clinical sciences, chosen from fields of particular interest, are provided mainly in the second and third years of the course.

Over the three years of the course, specific competencies in Diagnostic Imaging, Radiology Sciences and Techniques for Imaging and Radiotherapy, Neuroradiology, and Image Processing Systems are acquired, immediately applicable in the workplace, through theoretical lectures, laboratory activities, and professional internship conducted in the specific work context of the radiology technician. In particular, laboratories and internships are assigned 60 CFU distributed across conventional radiography, computed tomography, nuclear magnetic resonance, mammography, interventional radiology, angiography, neuroradiology, nuclear medicine, radiotherapy, radiation protection, and quality control.

The graduate's formation is completed by achieving B1 level in English and knowledge of elements of hygiene, occupational medicine, legal medicine, psychology, and health management.

Program, texts and objectives Professional status conferred by the title. Biomedical Laboratory Technician

The Biomedical Laboratory Technician carries out their activities in a dependent or freelance capacity in public and private laboratory structures, authorized according to current regulations, such as:
- Universities and public and private research institutions
- Healthcare facilities
- Biotecnological, chemical-pharmaceutical, food, and agro-chemical industries
- Analysis and quality control laboratories, public and private
- Zooprophylactic Institutes

Final exam characteristics.
The final exam, which has the value of a state exam enabling the exercise of the profession of Biomedical Laboratory Health Technician, consists of:
1) A practical test during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the profile of Biomedical Laboratory Technician;
2) The preparation and presentation of a thesis paper, whose content must be related to themes or disciplines relevant to the professional profile.

To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities specified in the study plan must be earned, including those related to the internship activity. Six ECTS credits are assigned to the preparation of the thesis paper.
For the thesis work, the student will have the supervision of a faculty member of the Bachelor's Program, called the supervisor, and of any co-supervisors, even external to the Bachelor's Program.
The final degree score is expressed on a scale of 110 and will take into account the student's university career, the weighted average of grades obtained in exams, the practical test, and the quality of the final thesis work and its presentation.
Students may have the option to prepare the thesis in English.

The final exam commission consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector on the proposal of the Bachelor's Program Council, and includes at least 2 members designated by the professional order, if it exists, or by professional associations identified by a specific decree of the Minister of Health based on national representation.

Required knowledge for admission.
According to Article 6 of D.M. 270/2004, candidates who possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable may be admitted to the Bachelor's Program in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques.
Admission to the Bachelor's Program is quota-based and requires an admission exam consisting of a multiple-choice test.
To be admitted to the Bachelor's Program in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques, candidates must have adequate initial preparation and specific preparation in the fields of Physics, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, General Culture, and Logical Reasoning.
The methods and content of the admission exams for quota-based Bachelor's Programs are available annually on the MIUR links.
The number of students admitted to the Bachelor's Program is determined annually based on the guidelines in the regional training plan, considering national healthcare needs and based on the teaching project and training potential.
Students admitted to the program who score below the annual threshold set by the Bachelor's Program Council in the admission exam are assigned additional mandatory training obligations in Chemistry, Biology, and Physics. To allow the cancellation of any verified training debt, personalized recovery plans will be activated under the responsibility of the discipline instructors or specially selected teaching tutors. Training debts are considered fulfilled with a specific verification on the integrated part at the same time as the regular exam for the relevant courses.

Degree awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES (Enabling the Health Profession of Biomedical Laboratory Technician)

Occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Biomedical Laboratory Technician The Biomedical Laboratory Technician carries out their activities in a dependent or freelance capacity in public and private laboratory structures, authorized according to current regulations, such as:
- Universities and public and private research institutions
- Healthcare facilities
- Biotecnological, chemical-pharmaceutical, food, and agro-chemical industries
- Analysis and quality control laboratories, public and private
- Zooprophylactic Institutes

Communication skills.
Graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques, through interaction with various teaching methodologies, including practical and highly interactive ones, will have developed the ability to interact regarding issues of different origins, both with other professional figures and with the public. They will also be able to support debates and report on topics related to their work in various settings and according to different needs, including those that involve training equal or similar professional figures.
This ability will be developed through interaction during teaching hours and practical activities, as well as during seminar activities carried out by students.
Written and oral communication skills are developed during laboratory internship assessments, which include written reports and discussion of protocol results in group work. The internship, which is mandatory, also contributes to this goal using similar methodologies. The internship can be carried out in foreign accredited institutions or in Italian research institutes or laboratories of the University of Sassari, which operate in international contexts, allowing students to develop their relational skills in such environments. For English, which is required at B1 level, it is learned and verified through e-learning, and both acquisition of the four linguistic skills (reading, writing, listening, speaking) and mandatory attendance may be required, according to criteria specified during the course, in line with the requirements of the Academic Bodies.
Acquisition of communication skills will be verified through meetings with professors and tutors, encouraging active student participation in multidisciplinary team activities, as well as during seminar activities carried out by students. Verification will also occur through exams, including internship exams, and during the final exam.

Learning abilities.
The graduate in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques is capable of:
- working independently and continuing their professional training;
- learning additional laboratory techniques to constantly update their technical and scientific professional preparation, also in preparation for further specialized studies;
- working towards goals;
- seeking necessary information to solve professional practice problems, critically selecting secondary sources.
Learning abilities are developed throughout the entire study path, both through individual study, through interaction with professors during oral assessments or review of written assignments, and through organizing experimental protocols during laboratory exercises under the supervision of professors and tutors.
Key opportunities to expand learning abilities are the internship and the activities carried out for the preparation of the final exam. Learning ability is assessed through the verification methods provided for each training activity, giving significant weight to adherence to deadlines in different academic years, considering individual data obtained during the setting of internship goals in both clinical and experimental laboratory settings, evaluating the self-learning ability developed during the internship or final exam activities, and the ability to critically discuss scientific topics covered.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1224] BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES (ENABLING THE PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATION AS A BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNICIAN)
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10251

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques will possess the knowledge and skills enabling them to exercise operational and professional autonomy, including in organizational, managerial, and planning phases.
Graduates will be able to critically interpret results derived from both diagnostic protocols and procedures as well as research projects, formulating judgments aimed at implementing corrective measures to achieve optimal technical and overall quality, and making a significant contribution to scientific innovation.
Graduates will be able to address and evaluate, in the various aspects of their work, the ethical, deontological, and medical-legal implications, placing the well-being and dignity of the person at the center, and respecting the new GDPR regulations.
The development of the student's judgment autonomy will occur through continuous interaction with the various responsible figures in their training, in a series of activities characterized by a high degree of interactivity.
Judgment autonomy will be developed through laboratory internship, conducted independently and individually, as well as through individual reports or discussions at the end of the internship and for the final exam.
The acquisition of these competencies will be verified through continuous interaction with the various responsible figures in training, in a series of activities characterized by a high degree of interactivity, and through individual and small-group problem-solving activities.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Sciences Area: The courses in this learning area enable students to acquire the foundations for understanding major biological phenomena, aimed at their application to comprehending the subjects characterizing the profession. Students will acquire knowledge regarding cellular biology of animal organisms and microorganisms, with particular reference to morphological/functional, chemical/biochemical, physiological, and molecular aspects, using appropriate statistical tools.
This includes knowledge of the risks associated with laboratory activities and prevention strategies, the fundamentals of physics, and occupational psychology. Students will also acquire computer skills aimed at managing information systems for services, and English language skills aimed at communication and scientific updating.
Learning occurs through frontal lectures, seminars, laboratory exercises, and technical-practical internships, along with appropriate time for independent study. Objective achievement is verified through written and/or oral exams, and in some cases, laboratory tests.

Human Biology Area: The courses in this area are aimed at understanding the structural and functional principles governing metabolic and functional activities of living organisms, particularly humans, and the fundamental pathogenic processes and biological defense mechanisms, as well as interpreting the main mechanisms by which disease alters the functions of tissues, organs, systems, and apparatuses.
These knowledge areas will be specifically applied to clinical contexts such as infectious, oncological-hematological, rheumatological, dermatological, and endocrinological diseases, laying the foundation for subsequent learning of related diagnostic pathways.
Specific laboratory methodologies used in the context of diagnosing these pathological conditions will be progressively introduced.
Learning occurs through frontal lectures, laboratory exercises, seminars, and technical-practical internships, and is assessed through written and/or oral exams, with laboratory tests also being required in some cases.

Laboratory Diagnostics Area: The courses in this area enable students to acquire knowledge and understanding of the methodologies employed in various sectors of biomedical laboratories, knowledge of procedures for analyzing various biological materials for diagnostic purposes, and the clinical significance of the results obtained.
In particular, emphasis will be placed on methodological aspects related to molecular biology, microbiology, clinical biochemistry, radioimmunology, cytology, and histology, with reference to the specific placement of these methodologies within the laboratory diagnostic pathway and in the context of experimental procedures.
Learning occurs through frontal lectures, laboratory exercises, and technical-practical internships, and is assessed through written and/or oral exams, with laboratory tests also being required in some cases.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Sciences Area: Students, thanks to the knowledge acquired across various disciplinary fields in this area, will be able to understand the educational content of other learning areas. Students will develop competencies related to laboratory safety and will be able to apply morphological/functional, chemical/biochemical, physiological, and molecular knowledge to the field of human biology.
Propaedeutic competencies for understanding various laboratory methodologies will be acquired. The ability to apply knowledge and understanding will be assessed through oral and/or written exams, laboratory practical tests, and the practical qualifying test for the profession, conducted concurrently with the thesis discussion.

Human Biology Area: Students, through the knowledge acquired across various disciplinary fields in this area, will acquire knowledge related to human physiology and pathology.
They will be able to apply this knowledge to the patient's diagnostic pathway in infectious, pathophysiological, oncological-hematological, rheumatological, dermatological, and endocrinological contexts.
Particular attention will be given to the appropriate integration and harmonization of various available methodologies (morphological, serological, molecular, and cytofluorimetric tests) for the correct delineation of different pathological conditions.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding will be assessed through oral and/or written exams, laboratory practical tests, and the practical qualifying test for the profession, conducted concurrently with the thesis discussion.

Laboratory Diagnostics Area: Students will acquire methodological and technical-diagnostic skills for managing the analytical process in various laboratory settings.
They will develop multidisciplinary, methodological, technological, and instrumental competencies for conducting biological, biochemical, biomedical, microbiological, and toxicological analyses; for analyzing and controlling quality and hygiene in the environment and food; for adopting biochemical, biomolecular, biotechnological, statistical, and bioinformatics methodologies; and for using broad-spectrum methodological and instrumental procedures for biomedical research.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding will be assessed through oral and/or written exams, laboratory practical tests, and the practical qualifying test for the profession, conducted concurrently with the thesis discussion.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Biomedical Laboratory Technician
- Laboratories for biochemical-clinical, microbiological, hematological, immunohematological, immunological, genetic-molecular, toxicopharmacological, anatomopathological, and medical-legal analyses operating in hospital and non-hospital structures of the National Health Service (SSN) and in analogous private structures and scientific research hospitals;
- Laboratories for analysis and research in veterinary public health, hygiene, and food inspection;
- Quality control laboratories in the biomedical field;
- University and non-university research laboratories in the biomedical field, both human and veterinary;
- Research and production laboratories in pharmaceutical industries;
- Laboratories for research and production in pharmaceutical industries and sales agencies operating in the laboratory diagnostics sector.

Function in the Workplace Context.
Biomedical Laboratory Technician: Graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques are responsible for their areas of competence, perform laboratory analysis and research activities related to biomedical and biotechnological analyses, particularly in biochemistry, microbiology, parasitology, virology, pharmacotoxicology, immunology, clinical pathology, hematology, and histopathology. Graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques independently carry out their professional activities with technical-professional autonomy in direct collaboration with qualified personnel responsible for various operational roles; they are accountable for the correct execution of analytical procedures and their work within their functions, in accordance with protocols defined by responsible managers; they verify that delivered services meet predefined indicators and standards set by the facility manager; they monitor and verify the correct functioning of equipment, perform routine maintenance, and address minor issues; they participate in planning and organizing work within their facility; they carry out their activities in public and private, authorized laboratories operating under current regulations, either as employees or self-employed professionals; they contribute to the training of support staff and directly participate in updating their professional profile and research. Graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques must also acquire knowledge and skills in the activities of veterinary prophylaxis institutes and in the field of biotechnology.

Specific Training Objectives Description.
At the end of the training path, students must have acquired knowledge, skills, and attitudes sufficient to meet the expectations of laboratory diagnostic services.
To achieve this goal, students must demonstrate the ability to:
- Manage biological sample collection and verification, check request conformity, and prepare samples for the next stage;
- Plan and implement the analytical phase using appropriate methods and technologies in compliance with laboratory quality recommendations and requirements;
- Critically evaluate and document the reliability of test results and analyses in accordance with laboratory quality systems and considering the patient's health and treatment status;
- Manage the diagnostic process in line with quality systems and actively participate in developing systems for validating laboratory tests and analyses;
- Ensure workplace safety and collaborate in risk assessment and implementing prevention and protection measures;
- Independently conduct database and search engine investigations to acquire and critically evaluate new knowledge related to various laboratory technologies, using this information to contribute to the development of methods and implementation of tests and analyses;
- Constructively contribute to the development of professional skills, structures, and healthcare organizations;
- Act responsibly and professionally, understanding ethical and deontological issues in relation to users and in collaboration with other health professionals;
- Manage their professional and personal growth in line with technological, scientific, and social progress, through awareness of their development potential.

STRUCTURE OF THE TRAINING PATH
1ST YEAR: Designed to provide fundamental molecular, biomedical, biological, and microbiological knowledge, as well as the principles of the professional discipline, as prerequisites for the first internship experience, aimed at acquiring basic competencies and orienting students within the professional fields related to Biology, Anatomy, Microbiology, and Biochemistry laboratories.

2ND YEAR: Focused on deepening knowledge in Microbiology, General and Molecular Pathology, and Hygiene, as well as professional competencies related to the fields of Clinical Physiology, Pathological Anatomy, Clinical Biochemistry, and Clinical Microbiology laboratories.
Multiple internship experiences in various contexts are provided, allowing students to apply and test the knowledge, methodologies, and techniques they have acquired and are acquiring.

3RD YEAR: Directed toward specialized deepening, particularly in Biology and Molecular Pathology, and acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice, the ability to work collaboratively with professionals, and in complex organizational contexts. In this year, students will acquire research methodologies to support the final thesis in the fields of Special Microbiology, Pathological Anatomy, Cytogenetics, Hygiene, and Health Management, Molecular Pathology, and Clinical Biochemistry.
The importance of internship experiences increases in the 3rd year, allowing students to gradually assume autonomy and responsibility under expert supervision. This curricular logic is also reflected in the selection of internship content, which progressively increases from the 1st to the 3rd year of the degree program.

Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities provided for in the study plan must be earned, including having passed the required training internships.
The final exam, which has the value of a State Exam qualifying for the profession of Audiometrist, consists of:
a) Practical test, in which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile.
b) Thesis dissertation. The thesis will address a topic related to one of the basic, characterizing, related or complementary scientific-disciplinary fields, or otherwise consistent with the educational objectives of the bachelor's degree course; in the work, the student reports the acquired knowledge on the topic, demonstrating the ability to critically process information derived from research conducted on bibliographic data consulted.
Students who fail the practical test cannot be admitted to the thesis dissertation.
The final grade (expressed in hundredths, with possible honors) is determined based on the following parameters:
- weighted average of the grades obtained in the exams, converted to hundredths;
- points assigned by the Graduation Committee for the final exam based on the following parameters: practical test, thesis work, graduation in progress, honors obtained in the exams, participation in international exchange programs (Internships or Erasmus Programs).
The Final Exam Committee, appointed by the Rector, consists of a minimum of seven and a maximum of eleven members, to be chosen among Professors and Researchers or instructors of teaching courses (one of whom is the Coordinator of the Class, or his substitute, who serves as Committee Chair), the General Coordinator of Internships or his substitute, and at least 2 representatives proposed by the professional college. The majority of the Committee members must be permanent teaching staff. To these names are added 2 additional representatives, respectively proposed by the Ministry of University and Research and the Ministry of Health. In case of failure to designate by the Ministries, the Rector exercises the substitutive power.
The final exam is organized in two sessions in periods defined at national level by a decree of the Ministry of University in agreement with the Competent Ministry. The first, normally, in the period October-November and the second in March-April. The dates are set by the Class Council Coordinator.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the bachelor's degree course, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable; additionally, one must possess or acquire adequate initial preparation.
The bachelor's degree course in Audiometric Techniques has targeted admission according to the regulations for access to health professions courses.
The access requirements for the course are possession of a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable, as well as possession of the knowledge and skills in general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, biology and chemistry based on the secondary school curriculum.
Admission to the course is subject to passing an admission test, the content of which, in accordance with Article 4, paragraph 1, Law No. 264/1999, and the modalities of which are regulated by the competition notice published on the University website.
Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Audiometrist Technician Regarding employment opportunities, graduates in Audiometric Techniques find placement within the SSN and regional sectors as employees or self-employed professionals, both in SSN hospital and non-hospital facilities and in similar private structures and research and care institutions with a scientific character.

Communication skills.
Graduates in Audiometric Techniques must be able to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, and in particular to patients and their families, colleagues, other healthcare professionals, and multidisciplinary team operators.
Therefore, they must be able to:
- listen, inform, and dialogue with patients, families, and caregivers in an appropriate, effective, and understandable manner;
- communicate, argue, and justify their actions and decisions with colleagues and different professional figures;
- adapt communication according to context while respecting cultural, ethnic, and value differences of the people assisted;
- implement audiologic counselling techniques to activate the user's resources and response capabilities and involve family and caregivers in the diagnostic/rehabilitation process;
- use tools for documenting clinical activity.
The aforementioned communication skills are achieved through participation in frontal lessons, critical analysis of videos, simulations, narratives, testimonies, discussions of cases and paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions, and internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.
The verification of learning outcomes is primarily carried out through observation of videos or dialogues using structured grids and evaluation feedback during the internship (through portfolios, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports), as well as in the final exam.
Learning abilities.
Graduates in Audiometric Techniques must have developed the necessary learning abilities to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Therefore, they must be able to:
- develop autonomous study skills;
- demonstrate ability and autonomy in seeking necessary information to solve professional practice problems or uncertainties, consulting current literature and promoting its application in audiologic practice;
- demonstrate ability to access and use research methods related to audiometric issues, also through computer tools, scientific literature, and related fields, critically evaluating and personalizing them;
- demonstrate continuous capacity to seek self-learning opportunities;
- demonstrate ability to self-assess their competencies and outline their development and learning needs.
The acquisition of learning ability is entrusted to the use of self-learning plans aimed at empowering students in planning their internship path and self-assessment, bibliographic research methodology workshops (both paper and online), and guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Learning ability is assessed through continuous verification forms during training activities, including project work, reports on specific research assignments, tutorial supervision of the internship path, and evaluation of active participation and critical contribution in work and debriefing sessions.

Critical Judgment.
Graduates in Audiometric Techniques must have the ability to collect and interpret data deemed useful for determining independent judgments, including reflection on social, scientific, or ethical issues related to them.
Therefore, they must be able to:
- Perform appropriate diagnostic exams and rehabilitative treatments, recognizing and respecting the dignity, culture, values, and rights of individuals;
- Utilize critical thinking skills to deliver effective interventions to users across different age groups;
- Assume responsibility and account for their professional practice in accordance with the professional profile, code of ethics, and ethical and legal standards;
- Demonstrate awareness of the influence of their emotions, values, and biases on the relationship with the patient and decision-making.

The teaching tools aimed at achieving the above Critical Judgment include lectures, guided reading, application exercises, case discussions in small groups with presentations in plenary sessions, internships with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts and with progressive autonomy and responsibility.

Verification of the acquisition of Critical Judgment occurs through written and oral exams, practical tests on clinical cases, evaluation feedback during the internship (through portfolios, structured evaluation forms, and clinical reports on professional practice), as well as in the final exam.

Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area Graduates must have demonstrated knowledge and understanding in each of the following fields:
- General anatomy of all human systems, detailed topographical anatomy of the auditory and vestibular systems;
- General principles of biology, histology, medical chemistry, and biochemistry necessary for understanding physiological and pathological processes;
- Basic knowledge of major macro/microscopic pathological conditions and anatomical-clinical correlations;
- General principles of physiology and pathology of interest;
- Foundations of specific interest equipment, conventional radiology imaging;
- Fundamentals of computer science necessary for managing the equipment in use and ensuring quality in therapeutic interventions and in the production, processing, transmission, and storage of images;
- Fundamentals of statistics for information processing;
- Fundamentals of healthcare organization and information systems;
- e-learning;
- Principles of preventive sciences and healthcare services, with regard to occupational medicine and legal medicine, for awareness of risks and responsibilities in performing interventions within their competence;
- Principles of professional ethics;
- Principles of psychology, to facilitate the establishment of correct relationships with the patient, their relatives, specialist doctors, technical colleagues, and support staff;
- Elements of medical-surgical and interdisciplinary clinical sciences chosen from the fields of particular interest.

Graduates must have demonstrated knowledge of written and spoken English up to the intermediate level (B1), to be able to study topics within their competence in English texts, ask questions to English-speaking patients, and understand their responses.

Graduates must also have demonstrated knowledge of hospital information systems and the organization of hospital services.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area Graduates in audiometric techniques must demonstrate knowledge and understanding in a post-secondary field of study and reach a level characterized by the use of advanced textbooks, including knowledge of some cutting-edge topics in their field of study.

They must therefore demonstrate advanced knowledge in the specific work and study area, which presupposes:
- Critical understanding of physiological and pathological processes related to the development and alterations of hearing, language, and balance across different life stages;
- Critical understanding of the cognitive and social aspects of communication, psychological, relational, and cultural dynamics related to hearing and/or vestibular disabilities, language, to improve understanding of educational processes directed at citizens or individual patients and related pedagogical aspects of disability;
- Critical understanding of the intervention fields of an audiometrist technician, methods for assessing auditory and vestibular functions, diagnostic and rehabilitative methodologies, and evidence guiding decision-making;
- Critical understanding of the organizational complexity of the healthcare system, the importance and utility of acting in accordance with regulations and guidelines, as well as respecting values and ethical dilemmas encountered in daily practice, as well as understanding professional autonomy, areas of integration, and interdependence with other members of the care team;
- Critical understanding of health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions aimed at promoting the safety of healthcare operators and users;
- Critical understanding of professional interest scientific literature, both printed and online, including in English;
- Critical understanding of the practical applications of information systems in clinical practice (data management and storage, use of computer aids as compensatory tools for disability, use of computer programs for rehabilitation).

The methodological choices for delivering teaching, interaction with professors during lectures, particularly during internship activities, assessment of learning through oral exams or written assignments, and personal deepening due to individual study provide students with the opportunity to enhance their knowledge and develop their understanding capacity.

The teaching tools aimed at achieving the above abilities include all front-line teaching activities (characteristic courses as well as student-selected courses), guided reading followed by application, demonstrations of images, videos, diagrams, materials, and graphics, discussion of clinical cases, as well as internships and professional activities, conducted under the guidance of clinical tutors and professors, as well as individual study.

Verification of the acquisition of these abilities is entrusted to in-progress assessments, exam tests (written and oral), and practical tests on clinical cases.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Audiometrist Graduates in the Bachelor's degree in Audiometric Techniques, in accordance with European Union guidelines, must possess the following requirements:
- Possess a sufficient foundational preparation in the fields of medicine, mathematics, physics, statistics, computer science, chemistry, and biology oriented towards practical aspects;
- Acquire disciplinary investigation methods and the ability to participate in research and experimentation in the medical field, with particular reference to aspects and issues concerning the acoustic and vestibular sensory apparatus;
- Possess basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of their knowledge;
- Be able to analyze epidemiological problems of communities and evaluate responses provided by healthcare or social assistance services;
- Possess the necessary knowledge for understanding biological phenomena and the functional mechanisms of sensory organs and apparatus.

- Learn the basics of the physiology of the auditory and labyrinthine apparatus;
- Learn the scientific foundations of alterations in auditory and vestibular function and rehabilitation methodology;
- Use instrumental methodologies to perform an otoscopic evaluation;
- Acquire methods of threshold and suprathreshold audiometry;
- Acquire methods of behavioral audiometry for children;
- Acquire impedance measurement investigation methods;
- Acquire oto-neurological investigation methods for diagnosing disorders of the balance system;
- Learn the basics of recording bioelectrical phenomena;
- Know and use electro-physiological investigation techniques of the auditory and vestibular system;
- Know the basics of acoustic measurements and audiometry;
- Be able to program and perform screening investigations in childhood and adulthood;
- Acquire examination methods for detecting and diagnosing noise-induced hearing loss in work environments;
- Acquire examination methods for detecting the electroacoustic characteristics of hearing aids and auditory aids;
- Know rehabilitation methods for hearing loss;
- Have knowledge of technological aids aimed at recovering hearing;
- Know rehabilitation methods for patients with vestibular apparatus injuries;
- Be able to design preventive and diagnostic interventions for hearing-impaired individuals based on their social, cultural, and physical conditions;
- Learn the basics of research methodology and develop programs;
- Acquire teaching skills for training internship students and teaching paramedical staff.

Function in the Workplace Context.
Audiometrist The audiometrist is a healthcare professional who performs technical procedures necessary for conducting diagnostic methods with professional ownership and autonomy. In particular, the activities of graduates in audiometric techniques are aimed at performing all non-invasive, psycho-acoustic, and electro-physiological tests for evaluating and measuring the auditory and vestibular systems, as well as rehabilitating disabilities resulting from pathology of the auditory and vestibular apparatus. They operate, upon the doctor's prescription, through professional acts that imply full responsibility and consequent autonomy; collaborate with other healthcare professionals in prevention and rehabilitation programs for hearing loss and vestibular disorders using instrumental and prosthetic techniques and methodologies; carry out their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in a dependent or self-employed capacity.

In reference to the diagnosis and the doctor's prescription, the Audiometrist, within their competence, presents a technical report aimed at identifying the user's problem; autonomously practices therapeutic/rehabilitative activities for the functional rehabilitation of vestibular and audiometric disabilities; evaluates the effectiveness of aids and trains users in their use; verifies the response of the implemented rehabilitation methodology to functional recovery goals.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
In accordance with the qualifying educational objectives of class L-SNT3, the specific mission of the Bachelor's degree in Audiometric Techniques is to train healthcare professionals who perform the duties specified by the Ministry of Health Decree of September 14, 1994, No. 667 and subsequent amendments and integrations, i.e., carry out their activities in the prevention, evaluation, and rehabilitation of pathologies of the auditory and vestibular systems, respecting the diagnostic and therapeutic competencies of the physician.

Therefore, the specific educational objectives of the Bachelor's degree in Audiometric Techniques, in accordance with European Union guidelines, will include:
- Provide a sufficient foundational preparation in the fields of medicine, mathematics, physics, statistics, computer science, chemistry, and biology oriented towards practical aspects;
- Provide knowledge of specific investigation techniques and the ability to participate in research and experimentation in the medical field, with particular reference to aspects and issues concerning the acoustic and vestibular sensory apparatus;
- Provide basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of their knowledge;
- Enable students to analyze epidemiological problems of communities and evaluate responses provided by healthcare or social assistance services;
- Provide the necessary knowledge for understanding biological phenomena and the functional mechanisms of sensory organs and apparatus.

- Provide the basics of the physiology of the auditory and labyrinthine apparatus;
- Provide the scientific foundations of alterations in auditory and vestibular function and rehabilitation methodology;
- Enable students to use instrumental methodologies to perform an otoscopic evaluation;
- Transmit methods of threshold and suprathreshold audiometry;
- Transmit methods of behavioral audiometry for children;
- Transmit impedance measurement investigation methods;
- Transmit oto-neurological investigation methods for diagnosing disorders of the balance system;
- Provide knowledge related to the basics of recording bioelectrical phenomena;
- Enable students to understand and use electro-physiological investigation techniques of the auditory and vestibular system;
- Provide the basics of acoustic measurements and audiometry;
- Enable students to program and perform screening investigations in childhood and adulthood;
- Teach examination methods for detecting and diagnosing noise-induced hearing loss in work environments;
- Teach examination methods for detecting the electroacoustic characteristics of hearing aids and auditory aids;
- Teach rehabilitation methods for hearing loss;
- Provide specific competencies on technological aids aimed at recovering hearing;
- Teach rehabilitation methods for patients with vestibular apparatus injuries;
- Enable students to design preventive and diagnostic interventions for hearing-impaired individuals based on their social, cultural, and physical conditions;
- Transmit the basics of research methodology and develop programs;
- Allow students to acquire teaching skills for training internship students and teaching paramedical staff.

These competencies will be progressively transmitted throughout the 3-year educational path, with the first year focused on acquiring basic morphological and physiological knowledge, initially more general and common with other healthcare professions, and then more specific to the field of audiometrist technician. In the second year, students will delve into clinical aspects, particularly in diagnostic and classification areas (core knowledge), alongside an increase in practical internship hours, which will further increase in the third year. In this final year, greater attention will be placed on therapeutic and rehabilitative aspects of the profession ('knowing how to be and knowing how to do').

Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Professional in physical activity and sports for human well-being The professional in physical activity and sports and human well-being will be able to work as a self-employed professional or employee in:
Sports companies at all levels Sports organizations and recreational and social associations Gyms Fitness centers, wellness centers, senior centers, tourist facilities Pools Sports associations for disabled people Sports promotion bodies and structures, also with activities in non-conventional environments Companies producing and distributing, also as consultants, products and services related to the world of sport and physical activity Communication skills.
Students in the Bachelor's Degree Course in Sports, Physical Activity and Human Well-being, upon completion of the training path, must demonstrate documented ability to communicate (communication skills) clearly and concisely the various knowledge acquired in the field of physical activity and sports, highlighting the strengths of the topics and using the most appropriate terminology. The student must be able to communicate in writing and orally with interlocutors of equal or lower or higher expertise, also through the use of the other community language (English), for appropriate international communication. The student must demonstrate the ability to explain physical activities and engage participants clearly and effectively, using appropriate technical terms, motivating them through knowledge of the benefits and risks of the motor program to achieve goals, ensuring adherence to the proposed program and communicating results effectively in relation to the proposed objectives.
Communication skills will be acquired within the training activities through various forms: preparation of written or multimedia documents, coordination activities or participation in working groups, seminar activities, and internship activities.
In particular, communication skills will be developed through courses in basic and characteristic psychological and pedagogical fields.
Expected learning outcomes related to communication skills will be primarily assessed through oral presentations in various training activities, evaluation of written or multimedia documents, organization of peer lessons and/or seminars with teacher and/or tutor assistance, and assessment of text comprehension. Communication skills will also be assessed in the final exam.
Learning abilities.
Students in the Bachelor's Degree Course in Sports, Physical Activity and Human Well-being, upon completion of the training path, must demonstrate having acquired an independent (learning skills) and continuous learning method that enables the graduate to continuously update and deepen knowledge through systematic consultation of online databases of national and international literature. This aspect is crucial, especially during the delicate phase of entering the job market, whose increased competitiveness requires constant self-learning and acquisition of new knowledge, as well as for potential continuation of studies in a Master's degree or research activities, but also for evaluating one's own professional activity in accordance with evidence-based best practices. Learning will be facilitated by reference texts for various curricular disciplines and texts in foreign language recommended for in-depth study. Additional teaching support tools will include slides, lectures, and participation in seminars featuring recognized national and international experts.
Learning abilities will be assessed continuously through in-course assessments and exams, in oral or written form (multiple-choice tests and/or open questions), essays and/or reports on internship activities, preparation and discussion of the final exam.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A119] MOTOR SCIENCES, SPORTS, AND HUMAN WELL-BEING
SECTION: AUTONOMY OF JUDGMENT
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10828

Autonomy of Judgment.
Students of the Bachelor's Degree Program in Motor Sciences, Sports, and Human Well-being, upon completion of the educational path, must demonstrate a sufficiently consolidated autonomy of judgment, enabling them to develop logically structured reasoning and to act based on it in a coherent and unambiguous manner. The student must demonstrate autonomous capabilities in evaluating the lifestyles of practitioners of motor-sport activities, verifying the adequacy of proposed programs in relation to the objectives to be achieved based on the practitioner's age, gender, and physical condition, and their actual and correct execution through objective parameters; they will demonstrate critical abilities in reading and interpreting functional assessment tests; they will be able to recognize the onset of discomfort situations that could lead to abandonment of the activity or a deviation between program assignment and implementation, taking corrective actions to achieve the objectives.
The acquisition of autonomy of judgment will be achieved by the student primarily through practical activities and exercises, internships, and placements through exposure to operational contexts requiring the use of specific personal skills and acquired pedagogical experience.
The verification of results related to the acquisition of autonomy of judgment will occur through the assessment of the ability to work both independently and in groups, through in-course assessments, oral and/or written evaluations, reports, and short papers related to practical, exercise, internship, and placement activities.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Biomedical Area In the biomedical area, knowledge will be acquired regarding:
the anatomical structure, biochemical foundations, and physiological mechanisms of human organs and systems underlying homeostasis both in resting conditions and during physical activity of varying intensity and duration;
in particular, knowledge will be deepened on the nervous system and the musculoskeletal system in relation to movement, with regard to movement analysis and anthropometric assessment;
the foundations of proper nutrition, understanding food composition and nutritional needs in relation to the type and intensity of activity performed;
the foundations of epidemiology and the main preventive measures for the risks of infectious and multifactorial diseases.
Knowledge and understanding capabilities will be achieved through frontal lectures and exercises (when present), as well as through individual study.
The verification of learning outcomes will primarily occur through in-course assessments and oral or written exams (multiple-choice tests and/or open-ended questions); additionally, practical exercises, even in small groups, will allow the student a more direct comparison with the instructor, providing an additional tool for improving understanding and knowledge.

Technical-Sports Area In the technical-sports area, graduates will acquire knowledge related to:
classification and functions of human movement and postural and dynamic motor patterns;
general theory and methodology of various individual and team sports, as well as water-based and outdoor physical activities in unstructured contexts, and their application methods in educational, recreational, and sports contexts;
evaluation of physical activities for achieving and maintaining physical efficiency, health, and psychophysical well-being;
movement techniques and pedagogy for different age groups, developmental, adult, and elderly, and in various applied contexts (educational, sports, occupational, outdoor life, etc.);
pedagogical techniques and tools for adapted, compensatory, and preventive physical and sports activities for individuals with specific conditions and disabilities.
Knowledge and understanding capabilities will be achieved through frontal lectures and primarily through practical activities conducted in small groups, as well as through individual study.
The verification of learning outcomes will primarily occur through in-course assessments and oral or written exams (multiple-choice tests and/or open-ended questions); the numerous practical exercises in this area will allow the student individualized interaction with the instructor, contributing to the development of understanding and knowledge.

Educational and Well-Being Area In the educational and well-being area, knowledge will be acquired regarding:
basic knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical aspects related to major cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, as well as fundamental knowledge for recognizing possible traumas, their causes during physical activity, and the diagnostic and treatment process for a trauma, basic first aid and BLS-D knowledge; doping knowledge;
basic pedagogical and didactic knowledge for independently designing and conducting a motor path suitable for different life stages and contexts, motor and leisure-sports;
foundations of the structure and functioning of sports organizations within the state and European community;
data collection and foundations of static and epidemiological processing and analysis.
Knowledge acquisition will be achieved through frontal lectures and practical activities for different sectors, as well as through individual study.
The verification of learning outcomes will occur through in-course assessments and oral or written exams with multiple-choice and/or open-ended questions.

Professionalizing Area In the professionalizing area, through participation in practical internship and placement activities, under the supervision and guidance of instructors and specifically identified tutors, the student will be able to acquire the necessary knowledge and tools for entering the workforce in the field of motor and sports activities, both individual and team, educational, adapted, compensatory, and preventive, with attention to the psychophysical well-being of the practitioner, which will take place at the sports facilities of the CUS of the University of Sassari, as well as at primary and secondary schools and at agreed-upon sports organizations and societies.
The verification of achieving educational objectives will be conducted through oral and written exams (multiple-choice and/or open-ended questions), as well as through final practical assessments and evaluation of internship and placement activities.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Biomedical Area The application of acquired knowledge will allow understanding the foundations of human body functioning in movement, adaptation to physical exercise, and promotion of healthy lifestyles, including nutritional aspects, as well as forming the cultural basis for applying knowledge to other capabilities in the technical-sports area.
The verification of achieving the indicated capabilities will occur through the completion of assessments (written exam, oral exam, short paper, etc.), where the student can demonstrate mastery of specific tools and methodologies and their critical autonomy, as well as through practical exercise activities, where the student, under the instructor's supervision, will autonomously apply what has been acquired.

Technical-Sports Area The application of acquired knowledge will allow graduates to plan and manage both individual and group physical activities in different environments, both codified and uncodified; to utilize pedagogical techniques and strategies, even through the use of different pedagogical aids, to safely and effectively teach the execution of physical exercises and the use of appropriate equipment; to plan and teach aquatic physical and sports activities; to be able to perform and manage functional movement assessments; to implement physical activity protocols specifically designed for individuals or groups with different physical fitness levels, aiming to promote well-being and improve lifestyle; to work with people who, due to age, deficits, or disabilities, require special attention and adaptation.
The achievement of these capabilities will primarily occur through practical and exercise activities, conducted even in small groups, under the supervision of the instructor or tutor, within sports facilities, laboratories, agreed-upon organizations, and natural environments, including internship activities. The verification of expected results will be obtained through written, oral exams, and short papers in specific sectors, in addition to the verification of internship activities.

Educational and Well-Being Area The graduate will be able to quickly identify situations requiring medical intervention and will be able to provide first aid until medical personnel arrive; they will have the ability to promote lifestyles suitable for motor activity and personal well-being at various ages, integrating the competencies acquired in the biomedical and technical-sports areas; they will be capable of managing motor and sports activities with individuals in the developmental age through pedagogically correct relationships and will have knowledge to interact effectively with practitioners of individual or group motor activities, considering age, gender, and social condition; they will also have basic legal competencies for managing sports organizations within their specific professional competencies; they will personally manage, analyze, and evaluate the parameters characterizing motor and sports activities.
The teaching of English will serve as an additional tool for more effective learning of other subjects and will also be useful in preparing the Bachelor's thesis.
The acquisition of these capabilities can occur through frontal teaching activities, exercise activities, and individual study.
The acquisition of these capabilities will be verified through in-course assessments, oral or written exams (multiple-choice and/or open-ended questions), and short papers demonstrating mastery of specific tools and methodologies.

Professionalizing Area Practical activities will give the graduate the ability to know and apply critically the necessary tools for their professional activity.

Official Languages of Teaching and Assessment.
ITALIANO Associated Competencies with the Function.
Professional in Motor and Sports Activities for Human Well-being For the performance of the functions of a professional in motor activities, specialized knowledge, skills, and abilities are required; the main competencies associated with the function are represented by:
- knowledge of the foundations of human body functioning in movement, adaptation to physical exercise for promoting healthy lifestyles, including nutritional aspects.
- skills in planning and managing both individual and group physical activities in different environments, both codified and uncodified; utilizing pedagogical techniques and strategies, even through the use of different pedagogical aids, to safely and effectively teach the execution of physical exercises and the use of appropriate equipment; ability to plan and teach aquatic physical and sports activities; ability to perform and manage functional movement assessments; implementing physical activity protocols specifically designed for individuals or groups with different physical fitness levels, aiming to promote well-being and improve lifestyle; working with people who, due to age, deficits, or disabilities, require special attention and adaptation.
- ability to quickly identify situations requiring medical intervention and to provide first aid until medical personnel arrive; ability to promote lifestyles suitable for motor activity and personal well-being at various ages, integrating competencies acquired in the biomedical and technical-sports areas; capable of managing motor and sports activities with individuals in the developmental age through pedagogically correct relationships and having knowledge to interact effectively with practitioners of individual or group motor activities, considering age, gender, and social condition; basic legal competencies for managing sports organizations within their specific professional competencies; competence in personally managing, analyzing, and evaluating the parameters characterizing motor and sports activities.

Function in the Workplace Context.
Professional in Motor and Sports Activities for Human Well-being The professional in motor and sports activities is capable of operating in public and private structures, sports organizations, and recreational and social associations, with particular reference to the management, operation, and evaluation of individual and group motor activities with compensatory, adaptive, educational, leisure-recreational, and sports characteristics, aimed at maintaining psychophysical well-being through the promotion of active lifestyles, and the management, operation, and evaluation of individual and group fitness activities.

Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The Three-year Bachelor's Degree Program in Motor Sciences, Sports, and Human Well-being aims to develop basic scientific knowledge and skills in various fields of human motor activities, acting in an integrated manner across different disciplinary areas to build a professional figure capable of quickly integrating into work environments.
The educational path includes training activities in the biomedical, technical-sports, educational, and well-being areas, as well as the professionalizing area; additional credit hours are provided for English language knowledge and the final exam, for student-selected activities; some credits are reserved for the category of other useful knowledge for entering the workforce.

In the biomedical area, knowledge is acquired regarding the anatomical structure, biochemical foundations, and physiological mechanisms of human organs and systems underlying normal functions and homeostasis both in resting conditions and during physical activity; in particular, knowledge will be deepened on the cardiovascular and neuroendocrine systems and the musculoskeletal system in relation to movement and its biomechanics; the foundations of proper nutrition and the organism's nutritional needs; all within a general context considering gender differences and referring to different life stages, with reference to the type and intensity of physical activity; additionally, knowledge will be acquired on the foundations of epidemiology and the main preventive measures for the risks of infectious and multifactorial diseases, as well as basic knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical aspects related to major cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, along with fundamental knowledge for recognizing possible traumas, their causes during physical activity, and the diagnostic and treatment process for a trauma, basic first aid and BLS-D knowledge, and doping knowledge.

In the technical-sports area, knowledge is acquired regarding the classification and functions of human movement and postural and dynamic motor patterns, as well as anthropometric assessment; general theory and methodology of various individual and team sports, as well as water-based and outdoor physical activities in unstructured contexts and uncodified environments, and their application methods in educational, recreational, and sports contexts; evaluation of physical activities for achieving and maintaining physical efficiency, health, and psychophysical well-being; movement techniques and pedagogy for different age groups, developmental, adult, and elderly, and in various applied contexts (educational, sports, occupational, outdoor life, etc.); pedagogical techniques and tools for adapted, compensatory, and preventive physical and sports activities for individuals with specific conditions and disabilities.

In the educational and well-being area, basic pedagogical and didactic knowledge is acquired to independently design and conduct a motor path suitable for different life stages and contexts, motor and leisure-sports; foundations of the structure and functioning of sports organizations within the state and European community; collection of data related to performance and foundations of processing and analysis of motor and sports activities. An English language course is provided, allowing the achievement of a B1 level, fundamental for adequately accessing the most modern scientific and technical knowledge, both for exercising one's activity in an increasingly global world.

In the professionalizing area, through participation in practical internship and placement activities, under the supervision and guidance of instructors and specifically identified tutors, the student acquires the necessary knowledge and tools for entering the workforce in the field of motor and sports activities, both individual and team, educational, open-air activities, and in the sector of adapted, compensatory, and preventive activities, with attention to the psychophysical well-being of the practitioner; these activities will take place in suitable facilities according to the number of students and the planned activity, at the sports facilities of the CUS of the University of Sassari, as well as at primary and secondary schools and at public and private organizations, Sports Promotion and Social Organizations, and sports societies, also affiliated with CONI, agreed-upon.

Additional credit hours are also provided for student-selected activities, and some credits are reserved for the category of other useful knowledge for entering the workforce through training meetings, such as workshops and seminars, with major local, national, and international realities operating in the field of motor and sports activities, even with a professional character, and with the school world.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari

SECTION: Program, texts, and objectives
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10276

Program, texts, and objectives Access to further studies.
The degree grants access to all second-cycle degree courses, including University Master's courses of the first level. Professional status conferred by the title.
Upon passing the State Exam, registration in the National Register of Biologists for the profession of biologist - Section B - with the professional title of Junior Biologist, a recognized professional figure for carrying out regulated activities.
The main employment opportunities involve technical-operational activities as well as autonomous professional and support activities, within the limits indicated by the law establishing the regulation of the biologist profession (DPR 328/2001). In particular, graduates can directly enter the workforce to perform professional and technical activities in laboratories and analysis, control, and management services in various operational contexts (university research laboratories, public and private analysis laboratories, environmental and territorial control and management structures, in industry and public bodies). These employment areas, however, do not exhaust the potential job market.
Final Exam Characteristics.
To obtain the Biological Sciences Degree, it is necessary to take the Final Exam. To prepare for the Final Exam, the student must write a report on the specific activity carried out during the internship, particularly developing the technical aspects of the experience (http://www.uniss.it/scienzebiologiche). Students are taught to use typical analytical instrumentation, learn methodologies suitable for solving biological problems, and understand and critically discuss the results.
During the Final Exam, the candidate must demonstrate to the Commission the ability to clearly and confidently present and discuss, without the aid of slides, the practical experience gained during the internship. To facilitate the presentation, the student may describe the graphs and images included in the final report or draw diagrams directly during the graduation session.
The Final Exam evaluation is expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors. For the grading, the starting point is the weighted average of the grades. For calculation purposes, each 30 with honors corresponds to a score of 31. The Commission evaluates the academic record, the duration of the course, the practical experience gained, the presentation ability during the Final Exam, the ability for autonomous learning, the skill in retrieving bibliographic information and utilizing available online databases, and any participation in mobility programs for study or internship offered by the university. The Commission also takes into account the candidate's conduct during the internship period.
The Final Exam and Internship are assigned a number of credits published annually in the Study Program.
Required Knowledge for Admission.
For admission to the degree course, a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable according to current regulations is required. To adequately undertake the studies, the student must possess basic mathematical knowledge and skills, as well as the ability to understand texts containing logical deductions and problems (Article 6 of D.M. 270/2004). A syllabus of the required mathematical and logical knowledge that is considered necessary for students intending to enroll in the degree course is available at: www.uniss.it/scienzebiologiche. The possession of these requirements will be verified through mandatory participation in a multiple-choice quiz test. The methods for verifying knowledge and the assignment of any additional educational requirements to be fulfilled during the first year of the course in case of negative verification will be defined in the course's academic regulations and made available in the Study Program.
Degree Awarded.
Biological Sciences Degree. Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Upon passing the State Exam, registration in the National Register of Biologists for the profession of biologist - Section B - with the professional title of Junior Biologist, a recognized professional figure for carrying out regulated activities.
The main employment opportunities involve technical-operational activities as well as autonomous professional and support activities, within the limits indicated by the law establishing the regulation of the biologist profession (DPR 328/2001). In particular, graduates can directly enter the workforce to perform professional and technical activities in laboratories and analysis, control, and management services in various operational contexts (university research laboratories, public and private analysis laboratories, environmental and territorial control and management structures, in industry and public bodies). These employment areas, however, do not exhaust the potential job market.
