Communication Skills.
The student acquires appropriate tools for written and oral communication through the use of graphical and formal languages, necessary for presenting reports and/or specific data on biological topics.
A significant moment for verifying communication skills is the period of internship. During this phase, the student demonstrates the ability to work in a group, to interact with scientific supervisors with whom they must engage, including from different departments or research centers than the one they are interning at.
It is during the internship that the student is required to prepare the final report and use appropriate computer tools for technical-scientific communication (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) or for online bibliographic research and consultation of online databases. For these activities, the student must also demonstrate an adequate level of English proficiency.

Judgment Autonomy.
The educational path aims to train graduates who develop judgment autonomy focused on interpreting and evaluating experimental procedures. Gradually, the student acquires increasingly complex skills requiring good observation, representation, and comparison abilities, culminating in the ability to apply acquired theoretical knowledge to address specific problems.
The achievement of the expected objectives will be verified through responses to precise questions posed during oral or written exams for each course.

Learning Ability.
Acquisition of abilities that promote the continuous development and deepening of skills, with particular reference to consulting bibliographic material, database consultation, and other online information, as well as utilizing basic knowledge tools for continuous knowledge updating.
A significant moment to verify the learning level is the Internship, during which the student uses theoretical knowledge and practical aspects learned during the course to analyze problems. This enables the graduate to choose subsequent study paths consciously based on their own abilities and inclinations.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Knowledge and Understanding All disciplines and training activities within the course's educational framework contribute to acquiring integrated theoretical and operational competencies in various fields. The fundamentals of mathematics, statistics, and physics are preparatory for the theoretical-experimental study of biological phenomena. Various courses (syllabi available in the Guide accessible at https://sdr.medicinachirurgia.uniss.it/it/didattica/scienze-biologiche) address various aspects of microbiological and animal and plant biology, morphological/functional, chemical/biochemical, cellular/molecular, evolutionary, and ecological/environmental aspects (see Tuning Matrix: https://sdr.medicinachirurgia.uniss.it/sites/st03/files/rev_tabella_tuning_l13_uniss_2021-22.pdf).
The student acquires these competencies by attending lectures and exercises and participating in laboratory activities, during which, under the responsibility of a teacher, they are involved in implementing experimental methods and evaluating the results. It is particularly the activity carried out during the Internship that allows the student to acquire and/or refine competencies in using information and communication technologies, database use for bibliographic research and other information, as well as software applications for managing, processing, and presenting results.

Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area All basic, characteristic, related, and integrated disciplines, along with the Internship experience conducted at the University's facilities or at external public or private laboratories and/or at Italian and foreign universities, contribute to acquiring multidisciplinary, methodological, technological, and instrumental competencies for conducting biological, biomedical, microbiological, biomolecular analyses, and for analyzing and controlling environmental and hygiene quality and statistical result processing. To train the student to acquire such abilities, the study plan includes integrated exercises and laboratories alongside theoretical courses and a substantial number of hours dedicated to the Internship, where levels of autonomy achieved can emerge more easily, also useful for pursuing subsequent higher-level studies.
The verification of learning level, maturity, and critical ability to address and connect various topics is carried out through oral and/or written exam sessions. For the specific indicator (application of knowledge and understanding), the training acquired during the Internship period is particularly significant, an experience on which the student is questioned by the graduation committee during the Final Exam.

Knowledge and abilities are acquired and verified in the following training activities:
Mathematics, Physics, Biostatistics:
Knowledge and Understanding Know and understand:
1. logical reasoning
2. fundamental concepts in mathematics and physics
3. principles of classical physics, especially those applied in biological methodologies
4. tools of descriptive statistics and statistical inference, and fundamental concepts of probability calculation
Application of Knowledge and Understanding:
Acquisition of practical competencies:
1. processing and presenting data
2. being able to model a problem and translate it into mathematical language
3. being able to perform a function study of a single variable, solve problems of analytical geometry in the plane
4. acquiring tools of the scientific method
5. being able to apply principles of classical physics to solve questions
6. being able to use statistical methods in various phases of biomedical research

General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry
Knowledge and Understanding Know and understand:
1. fundamentals of general chemistry and organic chemistry
2. nomenclature, structure, and properties of main inorganic and organic compounds
3. fundamental laws of chemistry, structure of matter, and its transformations
Application of Knowledge and Understanding:
Acquisition of practical competencies:
1. performing stoichiometric calculations
2. applying chemical knowledge in biological contexts

Animal Biology, Plant Biology, Botany, Ecology
Knowledge and Understanding Know and understand:
1. mechanisms responsible for biological diversity and complexity in general, and animal and plant diversity and complexity in particular
2. specificity of animal and plant organisms through their cytological, morphological, anatomical, and physiological study
3. fundamentals of plant physiology aimed at understanding the development and growth of higher plants
4. knowing the fundamental elements of ecosystem functioning, structure, and governing processes, understanding the delicate balances connecting different components
Application of Knowledge and Understanding:
Acquisition of practical competencies:
1. techniques and methodologies for biodiversity analysis
2. analysis of organization, structure, and morpho-functional systems of major animal and plant phyla
3. analysis and evaluation of concrete examples of ecosystem functioning and the different balances that can be determined

Genetics, Biochemistry, Clinical Biochemical Analysis, Molecular Biology
Knowledge and Understanding Know and understand:
1. mechanisms of inheritance and biological bases of evolution
2. principles and fundamentals of main metabolic pathways and biochemistry-clinical analysis procedures and their applicability to laboratory diagnostics
3. molecular mechanisms underlying genetic information flow
4. principles of cellular metabolism and gene expression regulation
Application of Knowledge and Understanding:
Acquisition of practical competencies:
1. Biochemical and biomolecular investigation methodologies
2. Main molecular cloning techniques and gene expression analysis
3. Critical analysis of laboratory quality control procedures

C.I. Cytology and Histology, C.I. Anatomy, General Physiology
Knowledge and Understanding Know and understand:
1. structural aspects and morphological-functional diversities characterizing animal eukaryotic cells
2. elements and criteria for defining interaction modes between cells and between them and extracellular components, aimed at highlighting organizational peculiarities of different tissues
3. mechanisms underlying development and fundamentals of vertebrate anatomy from an embryological-evolutionary perspective. Acquire, through a comparative approach, the relationships between phylogeny and morphogenesis with the aim of highlighting the interconnection between structure, function, and adaptation
4. organization of the human body, its divisions into systems and organs, macroscopic and microscopic description of various organs, appropriate terminology for effectively communicating anatomical information
5. basic notions of general physiology in studying fundamental properties of main organs and systems constituting the animal organism
Application of Knowledge and Understanding:
Acquisition of practical competencies:
1. setting up cultures of different cell types and examining structures and organelles in relation to specific functional activities
2. preparing histological specimens and applying criteria for morphological identification of different animal tissues
3. describing and interpreting maps and diagrams related to main models of organ and system development in vertebrates
4. demonstrating the ability to describe, using appropriate anatomical terminology, computerized images of the human body, human organs, and related microscopic preparations. Being able to reconstruct 3D anatomical models.
5. applying acquired knowledge and understanding abilities, demonstrating adequate competencies for discussing and solving problems related to human physiology, both cellular and organ level

Hygiene, General Microbiology, General Microbiology
Knowledge and Understanding Know and understand:
1. the concept of health and determinants of health and disease
2. fundamentals of epidemiology and disease prevention
3. general epidemiology of infectious diseases and main prevention measures
4. structure and genetics of microorganisms with understanding of pathogenicity mechanisms and host response
5. mechanisms of antibiotic action and microbial resistance
Application of Knowledge and Understanding:
Acquisition of practical competencies:
1. methodological skills for studying health/disease determinants and understanding scientific works
2. in biological, biomedical, and microbiological analysis procedures
3. in prevention measures for infectious diseases
4. in diagnostic techniques and molecular epidemiology applied to microorganisms

Official languages of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN

Competencies associated with the function.
After passing the State Exam, registration in the National Register of Biologists for the profession of biologist - section B - with the professional title of Junior Biologist, a recognized professional figure for performing regulated activities.
The acquired competencies imply the use of standardized methodologies, such as independently executing: a) analytical-instrumental procedures related to biological investigations; b) technical-analytical procedures in biotechnology, biomolecular, and biomedical fields, also aimed at research activities; c) technical-analytical procedures and controls in environmental and water, air, soil, and food hygiene; d) technical-analytical procedures in chemical-physical, biochemical, microbiological, toxicological, pharmacological, and genetic fields; e) quality control procedures.

Function in work context.
After passing the State Exam, registration in the National Register of Biologists for the profession of biologist - section B - with the professional title of Junior Biologist, a recognized professional figure for performing regulated activities.
The three-year graduate can perform work activities in a technical-executive role in laboratories of the agri-food, environmental, research, and pharmaceutical industry sectors, etc.

Description of specific educational objectives.
The objective of the degree course is to train graduates with updated theoretical and practical basic knowledge of the fundamental sectors of biology, also for continuing studies in second-level degree courses or first-level master's programs. The educational path prioritizes access to the Master's degree courses of Class LM-6 (Biology) and Class LM-9 (Medical, Veterinary, and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology), activated at the Sassari University.
Students must acquire the ability to apply the scientific method in biological investigation and be able to independently analyze experimental data using statistical methods. Among the objectives are also the achievement of communication skills for exchanging general information within the various aspects of biology and knowledge of the English language. In accordance with the principles of European harmonization, the competencies acquired by graduates in Biological Sciences meet the specific requirements identified by the national Tuning Matrix table for Class L-13, prepared by the College of Biologists of Italian Universities (CBUI).
The educational path, described in the Study Plan published on the website www.uniss.it/scienzebiologiche, includes basic mathematical, physical, chemical, and biological training activities and characteristic training activities aimed at acquiring theoretical foundations and appropriate operational elements related to microbiological, animal and plant, and human biology (including humans) at morphological, functional, cellular, molecular, and evolutionary levels. Credit points are also provided for student-selected activities, English language knowledge, training Internship, final exam, and to offer students the possibility of earning credits by attending non-curricular courses also taught by representatives of the working world, some credits are reserved for the entry "other useful knowledge for entering the working world."

Final exam characteristics.
The final exam, which has the value of a state exam enabling the practice of the Midwifery profession, consists of:
1) A practical test during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the Midwife profile;
2) The writing and presentation of a thesis, whose content must be related to themes or disciplines relevant to the professional profile.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities provided for in the study plan must be earned, including those related to the internship activity.
Six CFU are assigned to the thesis preparation.
For the thesis work, the student will have the supervision of a lecturer from the Degree Course, called the supervisor, and of any co-supervisors, also external to the Degree Course.
The final degree score is expressed in hundredths and will take into account the student's university career, the weighted average of marks obtained in exams, the practical test, and the quality of the final thesis and its presentation.
Students may prepare the thesis in English.
The final exam committee consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector on proposal from the Degree Course Council, and includes at least 2 members designated by the professional college.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the Midwifery Degree Course, candidates must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable. Admission to the Degree Course is programmatic and requires an admission exam consisting of a multiple-choice test.
An adequate initial preparation in Physics, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, General Culture and Logical Reasoning is required for admission.
Admission to the Degree Course is programmatic and requires an admission exam consisting of a multiple-choice test; the test will cover topics in General Culture, Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics. The modalities and content of the admission tests for programmatic access degree courses at national level for the 2013/2014 academic year are defined in DM No. 334 of April 24, 2013, available at the following link:
http://hubmiur.pubblica.istruzione.it/web/universita/accesso-corsi-a-numero-programmato In case the preparation verification is not positive, specific additional training obligations may be assigned to the student to be fulfilled during the first year of the course, according to the modalities and criteria established in the course's didactic regulations.

SECTION: Communication skills

Communication skills.
Graduates in Midwifery must develop the following communication skills:
- Use appropriate communication skills (verbal, non-verbal, and written) with users of all ages and their families within the care process and/or with other healthcare professionals in an appropriate manner.
- Use appropriate communication methods in the multi-professional team.
- Apply teaching and learning principles for specific information or educational interventions directed at individual users, families, groups, other professionals (support staff), midwifery students, nursing students;
- Support and encourage users towards health choices, reinforcing coping skills, self-esteem, and enhancing available resources;
- Manage conflicts arising from different positions;
- Facilitate coordination of care to achieve agreed care outcomes;
- Collaborate with the care team to agree on operational methods and implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- Lectures
- Videos and critical analysis of film clips, simulations, narratives, testimonies;
- Case discussions and analysis of paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- Internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts and debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team. Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Observation of film clips or written materials, dialogues with structured grids;
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports)
- Structured objective exam with simulations on relational skills.
Learning abilities.
Graduates in Midwifery must develop the following learning abilities:
- Develop skills for independent study
- Demonstrate the ability to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activity;
- Develop the ability to pose questions about the exercise of one's own activity, relevant in time, place, and to interlocutors;
- Demonstrate the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning;
- Demonstrate self-assessment abilities regarding one's own competencies and outline personal development and learning needs;
- Demonstrate collaborative learning abilities and sharing of knowledge within work teams;
- Demonstrate ability and autonomy in seeking necessary information to solve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, critically selecting secondary and primary sources of research evidence. Didactic tools, methods, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Problem-based learning
- Use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- Research methodology workshops for printed and online bibliographic research
- Guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Project work, reports on scientific research assignments
- Tutor supervision of the internship path
- Active participation in work sessions
- Punctuality and quality in the presentation of assignments. The teaching methods provided to achieve this specific training objective (ability to apply knowledge) include frontal lectures, conferences, seminars, work groups, and discussions. The teaching process will utilize all modern didactic tools. The ability to apply acquired knowledge will also be acquired through internship activities in various care settings, especially with interdisciplinary approaches.
Verification of this learning is assessed through examination methods, which, in addition to traditional oral or written exams, include a sequence of in-course assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews), useful for verifying acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, tools may include: multiple-choice tests or short written answers, organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; preparation of written reports on assigned topics, analyzing activities, and also commenting on practical exercises performed.
The course organization includes monitoring of the achievement of the aforementioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding in terms of expected learning outcomes, through a coordinated approach, also prepared for this purpose.

Judgment autonomy.
Graduates in Midwifery must demonstrate judgment autonomy through the following skills:
- Making clinical decisions
- Prioritizing patient groups
- Deciding on interventions to assign to support staff
- Implementing personalized midwifery care by adapting choices based on similarities and differences of the individuals assisted regarding values, ethnicity, and socio-cultural practices;
- Deciding on appropriate clinical interventions considering legal, political, geographical, economic, ethical, and social influences;
- Critically evaluating the outcomes of clinical decisions based on patient outcomes and care standards;
- Taking responsibility and being accountable for their professional practice in accordance with the professional profile, code of ethics, and ethical and legal standards;
- Making decisions through a scientific problem-solving approach for the patient;
- Analyzing organizational problems and proposing solutions
- Deciding in situations of diverse positions (conflicts or dilemmas).
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- Lectures
- Guided reading and application exercises
- Videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts
- Case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions
- Internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility
- Debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Written and oral exams, case tests
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms, and clinical reports on professional practice)
- Objective structured clinical examination at stations Knowledge and understanding.
Biomedical - Biological Area Graduates acquire adequate knowledge for understanding the fundamental principles of human anatomy, particularly the pelvic floor, the structure and function of major biological molecules and their transformations, with particular reference to major metabolic pathways; the main physiological and pathological processes of pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum, neonatal adaptation phase, puberty, and menopause, with the aim of acquiring progressive judgment autonomy in managing and implementing diagnostic-therapeutic procedures for the health of women, newborns, and couples at different life cycle stages; understanding the macroscopic and microscopic structure of the human body, particularly the male and female genital apparatus (including embryological aspects); and knowledge of principles and methodologies of bio-physical and bio-chemical applications for prenatal and postnatal diagnostics, as well as clinical-diagnostic aspects related to medical genetics.
Preventive Hygiene Sciences Graduates acquire adequate knowledge for understanding health determinants, risk factors, and prevention strategies applied to promoting and supporting the health of women, pregnant women, parturients, postpartum women, newborns, couples, and the community, as well as interventions aimed at promoting and ensuring safety in work environments for healthcare workers and users.
Human Sciences and Psychopedagogy Graduates acquire adequate knowledge for understanding historical-evolutionary processes of the profession and midwifery care; identifying psycho-emotional aspects related to endogestation and exogestation states, adolescence, and menopause; educating towards biological and social processes of birth, motherhood, and parenthood; training and updating professionals belonging to their own professional profile and support staff; acquiring judgment autonomy towards discomforts, fragilities, and psychological alterations related to the gravid-puerperal state, adolescence, and menopause; conducting counseling activities and establishing good relationship processes with women and couples throughout the birth journey, including foreign-origin users.
Ethical, Legal, and Organizational Sciences Graduates acquire adequate knowledge for understanding principles of programming and organization of healthcare services in the maternal-infant area and the maternal-infant department and women's health, with progressive assumption of judgment autonomy regarding the midwife's competence. The graduate must understand and apply principles of risk management and current regulations related to professional practice and socio-health matters, specifically concerning protection of working mothers, assistance to foreign women, family law, and recognition of the newborn at birth. The graduate must also know and apply techniques, tools, and methodologies of epidemiological research in obstetric-gynecological areas for evaluating healthcare interventions, measuring outcomes, and assessing levels of effectiveness and efficiency of specific obstetric-gynecological-neonatal care activities.
Informatics and Linguistic Disciplines Graduates acquire adequate knowledge for deepening English language and informatics knowledge for interpreting scientific literature and communication processes with foreign users and comparison at European and international levels with professionals of their profile and related fields.
Obstetric-Gynecological and Neonatal Sciences Graduates acquire adequate knowledge for understanding and acquiring principles, values, theories, and models of Midwifery, obstetric semeiotics for assessing the health status of the assisted person and planning, managing, and evaluating midwifery, neonatal, and gynecological care; collecting data and processing research in disciplinary fields.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Biomedical - Biological Area Apply biological knowledge for surveillance and evaluation of normal pregnancy evolution, for planning appropriate care at different need levels based on scientific evidence. Evaluate the health status of the newborn and monitor postnatal adaptation processes in term and healthy newborns.
Preventive Hygiene Sciences Apply and interpret clinical-care data useful for research and evaluation of care outcomes.
Define screening and effective techniques for early oncological diagnosis in gynecological context (e.g., Pap test; breast palpation and self-palpation, etc.). Implement interventions for prevention and detection of genital female tumors, including breast, and participate in organizing educational and health promotion activities with particular attention to sexually transmitted diseases, also through adoption of appropriate lifestyles. Define and apply techniques for prevention of pelvic floor disorders. Apply techniques for promotion, support, and protection of breastfeeding as a tool for prevention of chronic and oncological diseases of the female sexual sphere.
Human Sciences and Psychopedagogy Apply theoretical and practical obstetric-gynecological and neonatal knowledge integrated with biological, psychological, social, and anthropological sciences to identify needs of Italian and foreign women/couples, ensuring appropriate counseling and support interventions for situations of discomfort and socio-cultural fragility.
Ethical, Legal, and Organizational Sciences Use knowledge to read the organizational model, resources, and care processes of healthcare services dedicated to gender health promotion, birth journey, and developmental age. Be accountable for professional practice in accordance with the profile and code of ethics.
Informatics and Linguistic Disciplines Apply acquired informatics and linguistic knowledge to interact with subjects of various ages and different social and ethnic backgrounds in performing midwifery/gynecological care functions, management, research, training, and consultation.
Obstetric-Gynecological and Neonatal Sciences Use the corpus of theoretical knowledge of Midwifery care-educator, behavioral and social biological sciences, and other disciplines to recognize health needs of women in various reproductive life stages, couples within their social context, and newborns up to one year of age.
- Know models of birth assistance facilitating women/couple self-determination and normal physiological evolution of pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum, newborn adaptation, and breastfeeding.
- Apply knowledge regarding the use of family planning methods and techniques necessary to identify strategies for promoting conscious and responsible procreation, considering women's or couples' values and preferences.
- Interpret and apply research results to obstetric, gynecological, and neonatal practice, linking research processes to theoretical development of obstetrics (midwifery).
- Connect general principles of human reproductive physiopathology and couple infertility/sterility to main assisted medical reproduction techniques and the collaborative role of the midwife within the care team.
- Use clinical, instrumental, and laboratory diagnostic tools to identify early risk factors, anomalies, pathological situations in pregnancy, labor/childbirth, and postpartum, and fetal and neonatal well-being.
- Apply hygiene norms for newborn care and prevention of neonatal risk factors and diseases.
- Collaborate in care of newborns requiring sub-intensive care.
- Assist in eutocic births with personal responsibility and provide care to the newborn.
- Use care models promoting women/couple self-determination and normal physiological evolution of pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum, and breastfeeding.
- Plan, participate in obstetric and gynecological surgical interventions.
- Plan and implement support and breastfeeding promotion interventions.
- Plan and participate in creating birth and parenthood support pathways, health education including sexual health in various life stages of women, and directed to families and communities.
- Provide midwifery care to pregnant women, parturients, and postpartum women at different care intensity levels.
- Indicate main contraceptive methods for conscious and responsible procreation, considering women's health needs and status.
- Collect, analyze, and interpret clinical-care data according to scientific methodology for research and evaluation of provided care outcomes.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Midwife The occupational opportunities are identifiable within the areas of competence within the maternal-infant sector and on the territory:
obstetric-gynecological emergency department, midwifery, pregnancy pathology, gynecology, physiological nursery, delivery rooms, specialized operating rooms, outpatient diagnostic services for prenatal care at university or hospital clinics, public and private socio-health services.
Work context role.
Midwife The graduate in Midwifery is a specialist in care for women, newborns, and couples connected to the female biological-sexual cycle.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The educational path of the Midwifery degree course aims specifically at acquiring comprehensive competencies involving knowledge (knowing), as well as attitudes and practical skills (knowing how to do).
In particular, in the training of the midwife, the objectives are aimed at ensuring that the graduate in midwifery is able to:
1. Identify physical, psychological, and social needs and diagnose assistance needs of women, couples, and communities in various socio-health contexts, integrating theoretical and practical knowledge to respond with technical-scientific competence.
2. Identify needs for obstetric-gynecological care requiring preventive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative competencies in specific areas of gynecology and ultra-specialized obstetrics such as breast pathology, pelvic static alterations, sterility, infertility, metabolic diseases, and infectious diseases, etc.
3. Provide good information and advice regarding family planning according to the principle of responsible motherhood and fatherhood.
4. Provide women/couples with good information and advice regarding the birth journey.
5. Implement health education interventions for women/couples and communities, specifically regarding sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
6. Implement health education interventions for prevention of neoplastic pathologies of the female genital apparatus and associated glands through information processes and methodologies within their competence (e.g., breast self-palpation, Pap test, etc.).
7. Identify socio-health needs of pregnant women, providing appropriate information-educational support to remove conflicting situations in cases of drug addiction, poverty, disability, etc.
8. Evaluate clinical manifestations connected to the female biological-sexual cycle.
9. Evaluate clinical manifestations specifically related to pregnancy, having conducted at least 100 prenatal examinations on pregnant women.
10. Plan, provide, and evaluate gynecological and obstetric-neonatal care for healthy and sick individuals within a complex and integrated socio-care system, promoting positive health lifestyles and adopting care systems oriented towards self-management and self-care.
11. Monitor maternal-fetal well-being during physiological pregnancy and spontaneous childbirth, and (in collaboration with the specialist) in pathological situations, having practical experience in surveillance and care of at least 40 parturients.
12. Perform normal childbirth in vertex presentation having practical experience in at least 40 births or at least 30 births with additional participation in 20 other births.
13. Have actively participated in at least two breech births, or, in absence of cases, have completed appropriate simulated exercises.
14. Practice episiotomy and initiate suturing (including simple perineal lacerations); practice can be simulated in absence of cases.
15. Prevent, identify, monitor, and manage potentially pathological situations requiring medical intervention, and perform necessary emergency measures using available means and within their competence, having actively participated in surveillance and care of at least 40 pregnant women, parturients, or postpartum women in pathological pregnancies or difficult births.
16. Evaluate clinical manifestations connected to gynecological and obstetric-neonatal pathologies, reactions to illness, interventions in inpatient, day-hospital, and day-surgery settings, as well as home care, having actively participated during internship in gynecological-obstetric care and neonatal and infant care.
17. Evaluate clinical manifestations connected to immediate, intermediate, and late physiological postpartum in inpatient settings and home care, including evaluation of newborns without significant pathologies, having actively participated in examination of at least 100 postpartum women and newborns without significant pathologies.
18. Have participated in care and treatment of newborns requiring special care, including pre- and post-term, low-weight, or with various pathologies.
19. Implement planned care interventions according to verified and verifiable evidence-based guidelines (EBM/EBC).
20. Examine and care for the newborn, take necessary initiatives in case of need, and perform immediate resuscitation when required, having participated in surveillance and care of at least 25 newborns in Neonatal Intensive Care (NICU) in Level III facilities.
21. Ensure correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions, adapting them to the assisted person according to scientific principles, in relation to different priority health issues of women and couples, both reproductive and non-reproductive.
22. Contribute to identifying, defining, and organizing gynecological and obstetric care in regular and emergency/urgent settings according to priority criteria, ensuring continuity of care through optimization of human and material resources.
23. Define, implement, and evaluate research projects aimed at applying results in the gynecological-obstetric-neonatal care process and improving quality in terms of efficiency and effectiveness of care.
24. Implement performance evaluation interventions for preventive, curative, palliative, and rehabilitative gynecological, obstetric, and neonatal care according to specific process and outcome indicators.
25. Demonstrate professional and decision-making ability in planning and implementing health and sexual education interventions for women, couples, and communities.
26. Demonstrate ability to plan, implement, and evaluate training interventions for support staff, as well as directly contribute to training and updating related to their professional profile, also in reference to clinical internship of university students in obstetric-gynecological and neonatal fields.
27. Demonstrate possession of knowledge, skills, and abilities in practicing innovative and traditional surgical procedures in collaboration with specialist doctors and other healthcare personnel, having actively collaborated in at least 30 cesarean sections, 30 traditional gynecological interventions, and 20 laparoscopic and hysteroscopic procedures.
28. Demonstrate knowledge of ethical-deontological and medical-legal principles and ability to implement and evaluate their application in gynecological-obstetric and neonatal contexts.
29. Demonstrate recognition and respect for their own role and competencies and those of other members of the care team, in accordance with current regulations on responsibility and fields of action of the midwife, independently and in collaboration with other healthcare professionals.
30. Demonstrate knowledge of and ability to propose different birth technologies respecting different ethnicities and according to the principle of personalization and appropriateness of care.
31. Demonstrate knowledge of and ability to use at least one European Union language, besides Italian, within their specific area of competence and for general information exchange.
In relation to these specific educational objectives, the educational activity, predominantly organized in "Specific Teaching Units," ensures a unified and at the same time interdisciplinary vision of the educational objectives, with in-depth knowledge from the disciplinary areas characterizing the course, including those more specifically professionalizing and from related and integrative disciplinary areas. The teaching methods include frontal lectures, seminars, working groups, and discussions on relevant topics and simulations aimed at achieving the educational path objectives. The teaching process will utilize modern didactic tools. Traditional teaching activity is complemented by guided internship activity at healthcare services: University Clinics, Hospital Departments and Services, Territorial Services (District/Consultory, etc.), accredited private institutions, and other scientifically significant structures for achieving educational objectives, located in Italy or abroad based on specific agreements.
This teaching allows progressive assumption of responsibility and professional autonomy, within which midwifery students acquire the ability to evaluate various issues related to midwifery care, plan correct care in midwifery, gynecological, and neonatal contexts, integrate into cooperative group work with different figures involved in care in various healthcare contexts.
Laboratory and internship activities are carried out under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors specifically designated and adequately trained for this function. Laboratory and internship activities are coordinated by a teacher belonging to the highest educational level provided for the specific profile.
Learning assessment is carried out through exam tests, including traditional oral or written exams, as well as a sequence of in-course assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews) useful for verifying acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, the tools used are multiple-choice tests or short written answers, organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; preparation of written reports on assigned topics with analysis of activities, including comments on exercises performed.
The educational path is structured, monitored, validated, and optimized in a continuum to enable acquisition of competencies, knowledge, and skills specified in the curriculum profile established by current regulations and the specific objectives of the Course. These specific educational objectives are supported by a faculty aware of the need to use all institutional tools activated by competent bodies for the accreditation of teaching quality. Through these tools, it is possible to measure improvement in teaching performance in all different phases contributing to the degree, in terms of educational path, exams, perceived quality evaluation by students, and acquisition of professional competencies included in the specific objectives of the educational path.

High School Diploma Tuition and Fees Career Regulation - Fees Roles President FRANCESCO BUSSU Program, Texts and Objectives Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Logopedist Regarding employment opportunities, the Logopedics graduate finds placement within the National Health Service (SSN) and regional sectors as an employee or self-employed professional, both in hospital and non-hospital SSN structures and in similar private structures and scientific research and treatment institutions.

Final Exam Characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities specified in the study plan must be earned, including having completed the required training internships.
The final exam, which serves as the State Exam qualifying for the Logopedist profession, consists of:
a) a practical exam during which the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical, practical, and technical skills specific to the professional profile;
b) a final thesis whose content must relate to themes or disciplines connected to the professional profile.
The final grade (expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors) is determined by the following parameters:
- weighted average of grades obtained in the exams, converted to a scale of 110;
- points assigned by the Degree Committee based on the following: practical exam, final thesis, graduation during the course, honors obtained in the exams, participation in international exchange programs (Internships or Erasmus programs).
The Final Exam Committee, appointed by the Rector, consists of a minimum of seven and a maximum of eleven members, to be selected from Professors, Researchers, or instructors of teaching courses (one of whom is the Course Coordinator or their substitute, serving as Committee Chair), the Internship Coordinator or their substitute, and at least two representatives proposed by the Professional College. The majority of the Committee members must be permanent faculty. Two additional representatives, appointed respectively by the Ministry of University and Research and the Ministry of Health, are added as supernumeraries. In case of failure to appoint by the Ministries, the Rector exercises the substitute power.
The final exam is organized in two sessions held during nationally defined periods by a decree of the Ministry of University in coordination with the competent Ministry. The first session typically occurs in October-November, and the second in March-April. Dates are set by the Course Council.

Required Knowledge for Access.
The Logopedics degree course has national quota access (under Article 1, paragraph 1, letter a), Law No. 264/1999).
Access requirements include holding a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, as well as possessing the knowledge and skills in general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, biology, and chemistry as specified in the secondary school curriculum.
The selection test for admission to the national quota course will also verify the possession of initial knowledge; minimum thresholds for correct answers in each area of the test will be defined in the course regulations to pass the OFA (Additional Training Obligations).

Specific Educational Objectives.
In accordance with the qualifying educational objectives of class L-SNT2, the specific mission of the Logopedics degree course is to train health professionals entitled to the responsibilities specified by the Ministry of Health Decree of September 14, 1994, No. 742, and subsequent amendments and integrations, i.e., they carry out their activities in the prevention and rehabilitative treatment of language and communication disorders in childhood, adulthood, and old age. Logopedics graduates focus on educating and reeducating all conditions causing voice, speech, oral and written language, and communication disabilities.

Logopedics graduates, in reference to medical diagnosis and prescriptions, within their scope of competence:
- develop, also in a multidisciplinary team, the logopedic assessment aimed at identifying and overcoming the health needs of the disabled;
- independently perform therapeutic activities for the functional rehabilitation of communication and cognitive disabilities, using logopedic therapies for the rehabilitation and enhancement of communication and language, verbal and non-verbal;
- propose the adoption of aids, train users in their use, and verify their effectiveness;
- conduct research, teaching, and professional consultancy activities in health services and settings requiring their professional skills;
- verify the effectiveness of the rehabilitative methodology against functional recovery goals;
- carry out professional activities in public or private healthcare facilities, either as employees or self-employed professionals.

Upon completion of the training path, the Logopedics graduate will have acquired theoretical knowledge, practical skills, and relational abilities, with particular reference to the following areas:
- Prevention: The Logopedics graduate must be able to identify the health needs of the individual and the community through the use of screenings aimed at early detection of voice, speech, oral and written language disorders, communication disabilities, and swallowing issues in all age groups;
- Evaluation and Rehabilitation: The Logopedics graduate must be able to use assessment tools and procedures to conduct the logopedic assessment of the aforementioned disorders; collaborate with other team members to develop and implement the rehabilitation plan through program definition and selection of appropriate methods for disability recovery; document the rehabilitation plan in the clinical record through the setting of short-, medium-, and long-term therapeutic goals, record treatment outcomes, and adapt the program to patient-specific challenges;
- Communication and Relationship: The Logopedics graduate must possess communication and therapeutic relationship skills with the user, their family, and caregivers, applying active listening techniques and managing relational dynamics. They must also interact with other team professionals while respecting specific areas of competence.

These competencies are progressively acquired throughout the three-year training path, with the first year focused on acquiring foundational morphological and physiological knowledge, initially more general and shared with other health professions, then increasingly specific to the logopedic field. In the second year, students delve into clinical aspects, particularly diagnostic and classification (core knowledge), alongside an increase in practical internship hours, which further increase in the third year. In the final year, greater emphasis is placed on therapeutic and rehabilitative aspects specific to the profession ("knowing how to be and knowing how to do").

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Logopedics graduates must demonstrate knowledge and understanding in a post-secondary field of study, reaching a level that, characterized by the use of advanced textbooks, includes knowledge of some cutting-edge topics in their field.
They must therefore demonstrate advanced knowledge in their specific work and study area, which presupposes:
- Critical understanding of physiological and pathological processes related to the development and alterations of voice, speech, language, communication, and swallowing across different life stages;
- Critical understanding of cognitive and social aspects of communication, psychological, relational, and cultural dynamics related to speech, language, communication, and swallowing disorders, as well as learning theories to improve understanding of educational processes for citizens or individual patients and related pedagogical aspects;
- Critical understanding of the fields of intervention in logopedics, methods for assessing communication and hearing functions, rehabilitation methodologies, and evidence guiding decision-making;
- Critical understanding of the organizational complexity of the healthcare system, the importance and utility of acting in compliance with regulations and guidelines, respect for ethical values and dilemmas encountered in daily practice, and understanding of professional autonomy, areas of integration, and interdependence with other care team members;
- Critical understanding of health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions aimed at promoting safety for healthcare workers and users;
- Critical understanding of professional scientific literature, both printed and online, including in English;
- Critical understanding of the applicability of information systems in clinical practice (data management and archiving, use of assistive technologies for disabilities, use of software for rehabilitation).

Methodological choices for teaching delivery, discussion with professors during lectures, particularly during internship activities, assessment of learning through oral or written exams, and personal study deepen the student's knowledge and enhance their understanding.

Teaching tools aimed at achieving these competencies include all frontal teaching activities (characteristic courses and student-selected courses), guided reading followed by application, demonstrations of images, videos, schemes, materials, and graphics, discussion of clinical cases, internships, and professional activities conducted under the guidance of clinical tutors and professors, as well as individual study.

Verification of acquired competencies is carried out through ongoing assessments, written and oral exams, practical exams on clinical cases.

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Logopedics graduates must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to demonstrate a professional approach to their work and possess adequate skills to design and support arguments and solve complex problems in their specific work and study area with mastery and innovation.

In particular, upon completion of the training path, graduates will be able to:
- Use clinical knowledge and linguistic theories to assess alterations in voice, speech, language, communication, and swallowing;
- Understand physiological and pathological processes—across pediatric, adult, and geriatric ages—that may require logopedic intervention;
- Understand and manage voice, speech, oral and written language, communication disabilities, and swallowing disorders across childhood, adulthood, and old age;
- Select and use appropriate assessment procedures, also utilizing validated and psychometric tools;
- Accurately analyze and interpret data collected through assessment, integrating with patient history information;
- Integrate knowledge and skills to implement safe, effective, evidence-based rehabilitation interventions;
- Develop appropriate therapeutic and rehabilitation plans with measurable and achievable goals, adapted to different ages while considering cultural and linguistic differences;
- Measure and evaluate patient performance in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team;
- Modify the therapeutic plan based on patient needs;
- Assume responsibility for providing logopedic interventions in line with professional quality standards, considering legal, ethical implications, and the rights of the assisted person;
- Interpret and apply research results to logopedic practice;
- Use pedagogical and psychological knowledge to motivate patients to treatment and propose effective educational strategies;
- Understand health determinants, risk factors, and prevention strategies for both the community and healthcare workers;
- Use information systems appropriately;
- Possess good proficiency in understanding and producing the English language.

Teaching tools aimed at achieving these competencies include lectures, application exercises, demonstrations of videos, images, mental schemes, materials, and graphics, discussions of cases in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions, internship activities with supervised experiences in diverse contexts and progressive autonomy and responsibility. Acquisition of these competencies is verified throughout the training path through ongoing assessments, written and oral exams, staged case studies, project work, reports, and evaluation feedback during internships (through portfolios, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice).

III - Judgment Autonomy Logopedics graduates must have the ability to collect and interpret data deemed useful for forming independent judgments, including reflection on social, scientific, or ethical issues related to them.

Therefore, they must be able to:
- Practice logopedic rehabilitation treatments while recognizing and respecting the dignity, culture, values, and rights of individuals;
- Use critical thinking skills to deliver effective interventions to users across different age groups;
- Assume responsibility and accountability for their professional practice in accordance with the professional profile, code of ethics, and ethical and legal standards;
- Demonstrate awareness of the influence of their emotions, values, and biases on the relationship with the patient and decision-making.

Teaching tools aimed at achieving judgment autonomy include lectures, guided reading, application exercises, discussions of cases in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions, internships with supervised experiences in diverse contexts and progressive autonomy and responsibility.

Verification of judgment autonomy acquisition occurs through written and oral exams, practical exams on clinical cases, evaluation feedback during internships (through portfolios, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports), as well as in the final exam.

IV - Communication Skills Logopedics graduates must be able to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, particularly to patients, their families, colleagues, other healthcare professionals, and multidisciplinary team members.

Therefore, they must be able to:
- Listen, inform, and dialogue with patients, families, and caregivers in an appropriate, effective, and understandable manner;
- Communicate, argue, and motivate their actions and decisions with colleagues and different professional figures;
- Adapt communication according to context while respecting cultural, ethnic, and value differences of the assisted individuals;
- Implement logopedic counseling techniques to activate the user's resources and abilities and involve families and caregivers in the rehabilitation process;
- Use tools for documenting clinical-rehabilitative activities.

Communication skills are achieved through participation in lectures, critical analysis of videos, simulations, narratives, testimonies, discussions of cases and relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions, internships with supervised experiences in diverse contexts and debriefing sessions to reflect on and reinterpret relational experiences with users and the team.

Verification of learning outcomes is primarily conducted through observation of videos or dialogues using structured grids and evaluation feedback during internships (through portfolios, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports), as well as in the final exam.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN V - Learning Ability Logopedics graduates must have developed the learning abilities necessary to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Therefore, they must be able to:
- Develop autonomous study skills;
- Demonstrate ability and autonomy in seeking necessary information to resolve professional practice problems or uncertainties, consulting current literature and promoting its application in logopedic practice;
- Demonstrate ability to access and use research methods related to logopedic issues, including through information tools, scientific literature, and related fields, critically evaluating and personalizing them;
- Demonstrate continuous ability to seek self-learning opportunities;
- Demonstrate ability to self-assess their competencies and outline their development and learning needs.

Acquisition of learning ability is entrusted to the use of self-learning plans aimed at empowering students in planning their internship path and self-assessment, bibliographic research methodology workshops (both printed and online), and guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.

Learning ability is assessed through continuous verification methods during training activities, including project work, specific research assignments, tutorial supervision of the internship path, and evaluation of active participation and critical contribution in work and debriefing sessions.

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Logopedist Upon completion of the training path, the Logopedics graduate will have acquired theoretical knowledge, practical skills, and relational abilities, with particular reference to the following areas:
- Prevention: The Logopedics graduate must be able to identify the health needs of the individual and the community through the use of screenings aimed at early detection of voice, speech, oral and written language disorders, communication disabilities, and swallowing issues in all age groups;
- Evaluation and Rehabilitation: The Logopedics graduate must be able to use assessment tools and procedures to conduct the logopedic assessment of the aforementioned disorders; collaborate with other team members to develop and implement the rehabilitation plan through program definition and selection of appropriate methods for disability recovery; document the rehabilitation plan in the clinical record through the setting of short-, medium-, and long-term therapeutic goals, record treatment outcomes, and adapt the program to patient-specific challenges;
- Communication and Relationship: The Logopedics graduate must possess communication and therapeutic relationship skills with the user, their family, and caregivers, applying active listening techniques and managing relational dynamics. They must also interact with other team professionals while respecting specific areas of competence.

Function in Work Context.
Logopedist Logopedists carry out their activities in the prevention and rehabilitative treatment of language and communication disorders in childhood, adulthood, and old age. The activities of Logopedics graduates focus on educating and reeducating all conditions causing voice, speech, oral and written language, and communication disabilities.

Logopedics graduates, in reference to medical diagnosis and prescriptions, within their scope of competence:
- develop, also in a multidisciplinary team, the logopedic assessment aimed at identifying and overcoming the health needs of the disabled;
- independently perform therapeutic activities for the functional rehabilitation of communication and cognitive disabilities, using logopedic therapies for the rehabilitation and enhancement of communication and language, verbal and non-verbal;
- propose the adoption of aids, train users in their use, and verify their effectiveness;
- conduct research, teaching, and professional consultancy activities in health services and settings requiring their professional skills;
- verify the effectiveness of the rehabilitative methodology against functional recovery goals;
- carry out professional activities in public or private healthcare facilities, either as employees or self-employed professionals.

Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, students must have regularly attended the training activities and earned the credits required by the regulation.
The final exam consists of developing a technical-practical project under the guidance of a supervising professor. This project must synthesize as much as possible the basic and specific skills acquired over the three years of training. The result of this activity (which may or may not include a demonstrator) must be summarized in a written report explaining the activities carried out and the results achieved. The report must also demonstrate correct use of sources and bibliography, systematic and argumentative skills, and clarity in presentation. The project is discussed before a specially appointed committee. On the student's request, the final report may be written in English.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the degree course, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent. An adequate initial preparation is also required. In particular, the following are required: knowledge of spoken and written Italian, logical reasoning ability, knowledge and ability to use the main results of elementary mathematics and experimental sciences.
Since the course is taught in Italian and English, students must possess an adequate level of English. If not present, a level not lower than B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages must be acquired and verified during the first year of studies, through initiatives agreed with the University Language Center and/or accredited external bodies; for this purpose, 3 CFU without a grade are granted to the student.
The Course Regulations detail the procedures for awarding these CFU. The Course Regulations also provide for additional training obligations to be fulfilled in the first year of the course, in case the verification of the required knowledge for admission is not positive.
Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Junior Information Engineer The main employment opportunities refer to the following sectors:
- Information technology industries, operating in hardware and software development,
- Automation industries,
- Industries operating in the telecommunications sector.
- Electronic, electromechanical companies, design and production of components and systems.
- Agri-food industries, manufacturing industries.
- Public administration.
