UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [A106] INFORMATION ENGINEERING English and Italian
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10796?annoOrdinamento=2022

Autonomy of Judgment.
The graduate will be able to collect, filter, and interpret data in the field of Information Engineering, and develop an autonomous judgment on the technical-scientific relevance of such data. They will be able to identify and correctly interpret the concrete terms of typical professional problems for a junior information engineer. The graduate will know how to select, process, and evaluate the necessary knowledge for solving such problems and will have the ability to draw appropriate conclusions.
Autonomy of Judgment will be developed particularly through exercises, organized seminars, projects, preparation of reports, and through the activities assigned by the supervisor for the preparation of the final exam.
Where possible, project activities will be organized in groups to allow students to engage in a productive and dynamic comparison of their judgment capabilities with those of their peers.
The acquisition of Autonomy of Judgment will be verified through the evaluation of maturity demonstrated during the exam and during the preparation of the final exam.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Mathematics, Computer Science, and Statistics The training path will, upon completion, enable the graduate to know and understand the methodological-operational aspects of computer science, mathematics, and statistics related to Information Engineering. In particular, for the area of learning in question, these knowledge, which will be achieved through the training activities indicated below, will include: structured procedural programming (C language) and object-oriented programming (C++, Java); data structures, problem analysis, and algorithmic problem solving; differential and integral calculus for functions of one or more variables; linear algebra and analytic geometry; differential equations and systems; probability spaces and random variables; basic methods for solving linear systems and calculating integrals; solving ordinary differential equations.

Physics and Chemistry Regarding the "Physics and Chemistry" area, also related to Information Engineering, in the present training path, the student, through the successful completion of the related disciplinary activities, will achieve the following learning objectives: knowledge and understanding of the basic aspects of physics and general chemistry; knowledge and understanding of the structure of matter, classification of elements, electrochemistry, and elements of organic chemistry; knowledge and understanding of the mechanics of a point and a system of points, as well as the mechanics of rigid bodies, deformable bodies, and fluids, and elements of quantum mechanics; knowledge and understanding of the elements of thermodynamics and electromagnetism; knowledge and understanding of the wave equation for electric and magnetic fields and electromagnetic waves; knowledge and understanding of general methodologies for designing measurements of physical quantities.

Engineering Upon completion of the course, with reference to the Engineering learning area, students will acquire the necessary knowledge to achieve the following educational objectives, categorized by macro areas:
1) Information Engineering;
2) Automation Engineering;
3) Electronic Engineering;
4) Telecommunications Engineering.

1) In the Information Engineering field, the following foundational knowledge will be acquired:
Boolean algebra and logic circuits; knowledge of digital design modules: combinational and sequential circuits; finite state machine design methods; VHDL language; Assembler language; internal organization and operating principles of a processing system; processing system architectures; Database design; Relational Model; SQL language; Entity-Relationship Model; web application development; software engineering principles; principles and methods of concurrent programming; operating systems architecture; telecommunications and computer networks; protocols and programming underlying modern computer networks.

2) In the Automation Engineering field, the following foundational knowledge will be acquired: modeling, classification of systems and models; analysis of dynamics and stability; the control problem: frequency response and design in the frequency domain.

3) In the Electronic Engineering field, the following foundational knowledge will be acquired: semiconductor physics and technology; large and small signal transistor models; semiconductor memory technology and structures; difference between analog and digital signals; characteristics and models of operational amplifiers; use of negative and positive feedback in electronic circuits; interconnection of electronic devices and systems; main characteristics of amplifiers; energy management in electronic systems; principles of operation of electronic measurement instrumentation.

4) In the Telecommunications Engineering field:
- Detailed knowledge of the Fourier transform domain; methodologies for analyzing continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems, both deterministic and random; digital filter design; numerical signal processing methodologies; knowledge of telecommunications and computer networks; detailed knowledge of the techniques and protocols underlying modern Internet networks; main network layer protocols.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Mathematics, Computer Science, and Statistics Referring to the above disciplinary knowledge, the graduate will acquire the ability to use the acquired methodological tools for studying and solving problems.
In particular, upon completion of the training path, the graduate will be able to: use structured programming for data representation and algorithm implementation; perform the study of functions of a single variable (limits, derivatives, integrals); solve problems of analytic geometry in the plane and space (lines, planes, spheres, circles, conics, quadrics); solve problems of calculus and differential systems; solve probability problems; use computer tools for solving linear systems, approximating numerical data and functions, calculating integrals, and solving ordinary differential equations with initial values; recognize and correctly use the main components of a computer.

Physics and Chemistry Upon completion of the study cycle, using the provided tools, the graduate will be able to apply the acquired disciplinary competencies to achieve the following results: ability to calculate chemical equilibria, electrochemical systems, and solutions; ability to apply abstract mathematical models and concepts to real and concrete scientific problems in mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, and optics; ability to design and carry out the measurement of a physical quantity and analyze the results; ability to determine the electrical properties of matter (semiconductors: electrical resistance, carrier mobility, and concentration); ability to solve elementary electromagnetism problems.

Engineering With respect to the above knowledge, also for the area in question, the graduate will be able to put into practice the specific disciplinary competencies acquired.
Regarding the previously identified macro areas, the graduate will be able to:
1) In the Information Engineering field: apply programming paradigms to real cases (problem solving); implement software development using object-oriented programming paradigms; analyze and design databases using the Relational Model; create database queries in SQL language; manage processing system resources through system programming; use Linux operating system administration commands and system calls; design an information system (application software, computer architecture, computer network) and verify its correctness in the lab or through simulations; use software for aiding the design of digital circuits; evaluate an information system in terms of hardware module cost and processing time required for a process; use the appropriate level of programming language abstraction based on problem specifications.
2) In the Automation Engineering field: construct a model (for electrical, mechanical, thermal systems); design control loops for real, stable, weakly damped, and unstable systems.
3) In the Electronic Engineering field: numerically evaluate the most relevant quantities of semiconductors in equilibrium and out of equilibrium; use operational amplifiers to realize amplifiers; use an electronic oscilloscope in measurements of complex waveforms; design macroblocks capable of realizing basic functions such as amplifiers, filters, interconnections, conversions, and power supplies.
4) In the Telecommunications Engineering field: use methodologies for analyzing continuous-time signals and systems, both deterministic and random; use computer tools for numerical signal processing; use techniques and tools for designing telecommunications systems at both physical and network levels, such as software for simulating telecommunications systems.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Junior Information Engineer Software Design and Development
- development of tools and applications in the fields of medicine, environment, and territory;
- development of tools and applications in the agri-food industry;
- development of intelligent autonomous systems with particular reference to agricultural robotics and crop monitoring;
- development of integrated devices (embedded) in the field of componentry and process automation.

Information System Design and Implementation
- design of hardware architectures and embedded systems;
- analysis and reengineering of enterprise information systems;
- management of information systems;
- automation of services for enterprises and public administration;
- automation of processes for industry.

Function in the Work Context.
Junior Information Engineer Design Support (e.g., development, testing, and debugging) and implementation of web tools and information services. Analysis and design of network systems. The junior graduate will be able to join work teams that may include technical or sector team leaders and/or coordination or management roles. Additionally, in some cases, they will have the opportunity to interface directly with clients, acquiring further cross-functional competencies.
To reach higher levels of responsibility, the junior graduate will need to complete an additional training period and/or sector activities.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The graduate in Information Engineering must adequately know the methodological aspects of mathematics, physics, and other basic sciences and be able to use such knowledge to interpret and describe engineering problems. The objective of the training path is to provide graduates with solid engineering foundations that, among other things, allow for an easy transition to most related master's degree courses.
A distinctive characteristic of the training path will be the acquisition of specific competencies aimed at developing systems and applications of interest in some of the areas identified by the intelligent specialization strategy of the Sardinia Region, with particular reference to the agri-industry and the development of distributed systems.
This specificity will enable effective teamwork with professionals from diverse backgrounds, contributing to the graduate's positioning according to the transversality and mutualism principles repeatedly emphasized in regional strategic documents.
The methodological and operational aspects of engineering sciences will form the core of the study program; the graduate must particularly be able to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems, specifically information engineering problems, using updated methods, techniques, and tools.
The graduate must also know the main issues related to local industries and companies and understand their solutions through advanced devices and tools, as well as applications designed to adequately exploit the potential of the network, new computing architectures, and the best interactive technologies.
Finally, of fundamental importance for the study path will be the ability to conduct experiments and analyze and interpret their data, as well as understand and evaluate the impact of engineering solutions in the considered context.
The planned training path details the operating principles of modern information processing and transmission systems. Training activities are grouped into four disciplinary macro areas as follows.
- Basic Subjects: Fundamental training activities in mathematical, physical, and computer science disciplines, concentrated mainly in the first year and partially in the beginning of the second year.
- Characterizing Subjects: Characterizing training activities in the field of Information Engineering, concentrated mainly in the second and third years. These activities primarily cover computer architectures, data processing and management, operating systems, telecommunications systems, and automation. They represent the core of the study path in Information Engineering, covering all aspects of modern processing systems, from hardware to software, including the increasingly stringent connectivity and interaction requirements with the outside world. These activities are also essential for achieving the specific goal of training technicians with adequate competencies in the development of distributed systems and their applications.
- Affine and Integrative Subjects: Affine and integrative activities, with particular reference to industrial, chemical, and biomedical technologies. This group of activities aims to characterize the proposed study path towards themes relevant to the territory, developing essential competencies to interact profitably in various application areas of medicine and environmental monitoring.
- Elective Subjects: Additional student-selected activities aimed at acquiring diverse knowledge and competencies of specific interest to the student.
The training activity will be structured into a limited number of teaching modules. Each teaching module will generally include classroom lectures, classroom and/or laboratory exercises, individual study or exercises, resulting in credit points (following successful exams). To facilitate the circulation of international students, some second and third-year courses will be offered exclusively in English.
Methodologically, particular attention will be given to the interdisciplinary approach, also through joint exercises within multiple modules. Operational tasks will also be proposed, configured as individual and group work (projects), using advanced tools.
It is emphasized that project activities will be carried out under the constant or periodic supervision of the instructor. The operational skills acquired (design, development, experimental validation) will then be applied during thesis activities.
Both projects and thesis activities may be carried out in an academic setting (laboratories) or in a company, under the joint supervision of an industry tutor and a reference instructor. This mode is particularly important for those aiming for a rapid integration into the local production fabric.

1) In the Computer Engineering area: apply programming paradigms to real cases (problem solving); implement software development projects using object-oriented programming paradigms; analyze and design databases using the Relational Model; create database queries in SQL language; manage processing system resources through system programming; use Linux operating system administration commands and system calls; design an information system (application software, computer architecture, computer network), verifying its correctness in the lab or through simulations; use software tools for digital circuit design; evaluate an information system in terms of hardware module costs and processing time required for a process; use the appropriate level of programming language abstraction based on problem specifications.

2) In the Automation Engineering area: Construct a model (for electrical, mechanical, thermal systems); Design control loops for real, stable, weakly damped, and unstable systems.

3) In the Electronic Engineering area: Numerically evaluate the most relevant quantities of semiconductors in equilibrium and out of equilibrium; use operational amplifiers to create amplifiers; use an electronic oscilloscope in measurements of complex waveforms; design macroblocks capable of implementing basic functions such as amplifiers, filters, interconnections, conversions, and power supplies.

4) In the Telecommunications Engineering area: Use methodologies for analyzing continuous-time signals and systems, both deterministic and random; use computer tools for numerical signal processing; use techniques and tools for designing telecommunications systems at both physical and network levels, such as mathematical simulation software for telecommunications systems.

Official Languages of Teaching and Assessment of Preparedness.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Junior Computer Engineer Software Design and Development
- Development of tools and applications in the fields of medicine, environment, and territory;
- Development of tools and applications in the agri-food industry;
- Development of intelligent autonomous systems with particular reference to agricultural robotics and crop monitoring;
- Development of integrated devices (embedded) in the field of components and process automation.

Information System Design and Implementation
- Design of hardware architectures and embedded systems;
- Analysis and re-engineering of enterprise information systems;
- Management of information systems;
- Automation of services for businesses and public administration;
- Automation of processes for industry.

Function in Work Context.
Junior Computer Engineer Support for design (e.g., development, testing, and debugging) and implementation of web tools and information services. Analysis and design of network systems. Junior graduates can join work teams that may include technical team leaders or sector coordinators and/or management. Additionally, in some cases, they will have the opportunity to interface directly with clients, acquiring further transversal competencies.
To reach higher levels of responsibility, the junior graduate must instead complete an additional period of training and/or sector activities.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The graduate in Computer Engineering must adequately know the methodological aspects of mathematics, physics, and other basic sciences and be able to use such knowledge to interpret and describe engineering problems. The objective of the training path is to provide graduates with solid engineering foundations that, among other things, allow easy entry into most related master's degree courses.
A distinctive feature of the course will be the acquisition of specific competencies aimed at developing systems and applications of interest in some of the areas identified by the Sardinia Region's Smart Specialization Strategy, with particular reference to agroindustry and the development of distributed systems.
This specificity will enable effective teamwork with professionals from diverse backgrounds, contributing to the graduate's positioning according to the transversality and mutualism principles repeatedly emphasized in regional strategic documents.
The methodological and operational aspects of engineering sciences will form the core of the study program; the graduate must particularly be able to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems, specifically computer engineering problems, using updated methods, techniques, and tools.
The graduate must also know the main issues related to local industries and companies and understand their solutions through advanced devices and tools, as well as applications designed to effectively leverage network potential, new computing architectures, and the best interactive technologies.
Finally, of fundamental importance for the study program will be the ability to conduct experiments and analyze and interpret their data, as well as understand and evaluate the impact of engineering solutions in the considered context.
The planned training path details the operating principles of modern information processing and transmission systems. Training activities are grouped into four disciplinary macro areas as follows.
- Basic Subjects: Fundamental training activities in mathematical, physical, and computer science disciplines, concentrated mainly in the first year and partially in the beginning of the second year.
- Characterizing Subjects: Characterizing training activities in the field of Information Engineering, concentrated mainly in the second and third years. These activities primarily cover computer architectures, data processing and management, operating systems, telecommunication systems, and automation. They represent the core of the study path in Information Engineering, covering all issues of modern processing systems, from hardware to software aspects, including increasingly stringent connectivity and external interaction needs. These activities are also essential for achieving the specific goal of training technicians with adequate competencies in the development of distributed systems and related applications.
- Related and Integrative Subjects: Related and integrative activities, with particular reference to industrial, chemical, and biomedical technologies. This group of activities aims to characterize the proposed study path towards themes relevant to the territory, developing essential competencies to interact profitably in various application areas of medicine and environmental monitoring.
- Elective Subjects: Additional student-selected activities aimed at acquiring diversified knowledge and competencies of specific interest to the student.

The training activity will be structured into a limited number of teaching modules. Each teaching module will generally include classroom lectures, classroom and/or laboratory exercises, individual study or exercises, resulting in credit points (following pass exams). To facilitate the circulation of international students, some second and third-year courses will be offered exclusively in English.

Methodologically, particular attention will be given to the interdisciplinary approach, also through joint exercises within multiple modules. Operational tasks will also be proposed, configured as individual and group work (projects), using advanced tools.

It is emphasized that project activities will be carried out under constant or periodic supervision by the instructor. The operational skills acquired (design, development, experimental validation) will then be applied during thesis activities.

Both projects and thesis activities may be carried out in an academic setting (laboratories) or in a company, under the joint supervision of a company tutor and a reference instructor. This mode is particularly important for those aiming for quick integration into the local production sector.

Generic profile Graduates in Industrial Engineering can carry out professional activities in the fields of computer-aided design, production, technical management, energy analysis of plants and processes, verification and testing, assistance to technical-commercial structures, both in free practice and in manufacturing or service companies and public administrations.
Main employment opportunities are:
• Manufacturing companies and processing industries (chemical, metallurgical, food, pharmaceutical and electronic);
• Advanced mechanical, electromechanical and biomedical industries;
• Companies and entities operating in the energy production and conversion sector;
• Companies operating in the services sector for the management of equipment and plants;
• Public and private entities operating in the certification and quality control of products and processes;
• Industrial laboratories and testing laboratories for material characterization for civil and industrial use;
• Professional studios and consulting companies.
After passing the state exam, the graduate in Industrial Engineering can register with the Engineers' Register Section B, Industrial Sector (Junior Engineer).
The training path of the Industrial Engineering bachelor's degree course is designed to provide graduates with the appropriate training for performing the professional activities of a junior engineer, as well as to allow the possible continuation of studies in first-level master's degrees or in master's degree (LM) courses in industrial engineering, which are the natural continuation of the Industrial Engineering bachelor's degree with particular reference to the disciplinary areas identified within it (Materials Engineering, Energy Engineering, Management Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or equivalent).

Final exam characteristics.
The final exam, corresponding to 3 CFU, will consist of the discussion of a report related to the experiences and skills acquired during the internship. To be admitted to the final exam, the student must have earned all the required training credits as specified in the course's didactic regulations, except for those reserved for the final exam. The oral presentation will take place in one of the graduation sessions established by the Course Council.
The graduation committee consists of at least 5 members. The committee verifies the graduate's ability to clearly and competently present and discuss the activities and knowledge developed during the internship period. The final exam grade will be expressed in hundredths, according to the procedures outlined in the University's regulations for awarding the graduation grade.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the three-year bachelor's degree course, it is necessary to hold a five-year high school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
Successful participation in the training path requires possession of certain fundamental skills and abilities:
Essential abilities:
- Ability to communicate effectively, in written and oral form, in Italian.
- Ability to correctly interpret the meaning of a text, to summarize it in writing, and to answer questions based on its content.
- Basic knowledge of English, both spoken and written.
- Aptitude for a methodological approach.
Basic scientific knowledge:
- Knowledge of mathematical and arithmetic topics and tools.
- Knowledge of geometric and analytical geometry topics and tools.
- Basic knowledge of physics and chemistry.
- Basic computer skills in line with the standard identified in the European Computer Driving Licence (ECDL) basic level.
Verification of entry knowledge is carried out through an entry test according to the procedures outlined in the Course's Didactic Regulation. All students enrolling in the course must compulsorily take this test. If the entry test is not passed, additional compulsory training obligations must be fulfilled in the first year of the course according to the procedures specified in the Course's Didactic Regulation.

Communication Skills.
At the end of the training path, the graduate in Industrial Engineering is able to:
• draft technical reports and specifications, in Italian and English, and interpret technical reports written by third parties;
• understand, interpret and draft standards, documentation and technical manuals;
• effectively integrate into a work group, also of a multidisciplinary nature, and possibly coordinate it;
• adequately present technical issues, solutions and results of their activities both in a synthetic form, as well as through the drafting of reports and technical notes;
• communicate clearly and substantively to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors;
• master the English language at an appropriate level of knowledge (at least B2) in comprehension, writing and presentation.
Written and oral communication skills are particularly developed during seminars, exercises, training activities that also involve preparing reports and their oral presentation, also with multimedia support. Participation in internships, traineeships and study stays in Italy and abroad (for example within Erasmus initiatives) proves to be a valuable tool for developing communication and relational skills.
Learning Abilities.
At the end of the training path, the graduate will have acquired:
• awareness of the progressive and rapid evolution of technological and scientific knowledge and the consequent need to adapt their skills through continuous learning, to be undertaken autonomously throughout their working career;
• the ability to autonomously acquire new technical-scientific knowledge starting from scientific and technical literature in the fields characteristic of industrial engineering and in culturally and operationally adjacent areas.
The training path of the three-year degree in Industrial Engineering includes teaching methodologies that stimulate learning autonomy and at the same time the ability to work in groups. For this purpose, many courses require the preparation of individual and group assignments. The final course project will represent a final assessment of the graduate's abilities and autonomy.

Judgment autonomy.
The graduate in Industrial Engineering must be fully autonomous in understanding project solutions in the sector. They must also possess a constant propensity for updating technical knowledge through attendance at appropriate seminars. In particular, the graduate will have acquired:
• ability to evaluate, interpret and reprocess data and information;
• ability to operate autonomously in applied roles and responsibilities;
• ability to select and use the most appropriate methods and tools to solve engineering problems without supervision;
• ability to understand and interpret technical documentation of products and processes;
• ability to identify, consult and interpret laws and regulations applicable to industrial engineering problems;
• ability for autonomous analysis of the impact of engineering solutions on the social, economic and environmental context;
• full awareness of ethical-legal aspects in the exercise of the engineering profession and respect for the norms of engineering practice.
The ability of judgment autonomy is verified during the delivery of courses, following lessons and exercises, and on the occasion of the final assessment. Some courses include a project component and/or laboratory activities, thus allowing verification and assessment of the student's judgment ability when facing project choices or selection of instrumentation in the execution of experimental tests. The training internship, carried out in research laboratories of the University or external companies and organizations, contributes to the development of transversal professional skills. The final exam ultimately aims to develop judgment autonomy and critical evaluation of a specific topic assigned to the student.
Knowledge and understanding.
Mathematical, physical, chemical and computer sciences The subjects in this area aim to place graduates in Industrial Engineering in a position to understand and solve mathematical, physical, chemical and computer science problems. The graduate of the Program:
- knows the basic mathematical tools for representation and study of engineering systems of medium complexity.
- acquires a basic knowledge of fundamental laws and main concepts of general physics divided into the fields of mechanics, electromagnetism, optics and thermodynamics, and applies them to specific fields in different areas of engineering, also in English.
- knows the principles, design methodologies and fundamental tools for developing computer applications.
The acquisition of such knowledge and skills will be preparatory to the study of engineering and design subjects.
Verification of acquired knowledge and the resulting judgment will primarily be based on the completion of intermediate written tests and final written and/or oral exams.
Engineering sciences The subjects in this area aim to train industrial engineering students through the acquisition of technical fundamentals, tools and application methodologies typical of industrial engineering, with particular reference to the disciplines constituting the study course. The graduate of the Program:
- understands the principles of applied thermodynamics, heat transfer, hygrometry and hydraulics.
- knows the structure, chemical-physical and mechanical properties of materials, applications, processes and industrial and biomedical/bioengineering processing technologies.
- knows the methodologies for measuring mechanical, thermal and electrical quantities and signal processing.
- possesses the fundamental knowledge of industrial automation for the design and supervision of industrial automatic systems of medium/low complexity.
- is able to understand problems, even of high complexity, related to the design, realization and management of industrial systems and the transfer and utilization of energy.
- knows the typical economic-organizational issues of industrial reality.
Verification of acquired knowledge and the resulting judgment will primarily be based on the completion of intermediate written tests, reports and individual and/or group projects, final written and/or oral exams.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Mathematical, physical, chemical and computer sciences Graduates in Industrial Engineering are:
- able to understand and elaborate problems, specifically those in the engineering field, using appropriate terminology and formulations under the mathematical, physical, chemical and computer science aspects, also in English.
- possessing the ability to apply acquired knowledge and tools in the fields of mathematics, physics, chemistry and computer science to solve engineering design problems.
The application abilities of the basic areas are developed through exercises, also of a multidisciplinary nature, carried out during lessons and through individual and group study activities.
Verification of acquired knowledge and the resulting judgment will primarily be based on the completion of written tests and oral interviews.
Engineering sciences Graduates in Industrial Engineering are able to:
- select and design, and finally verify simple and complex components;
- select and appropriately use analytical methods for solving engineering problems;
- carry out the basic design of plants and industrial systems, thermal and electrical plants in civil and industrial contexts, energy conversion and transport systems.
- implement the management of industrial plants and supervise industrial processes, even automatic ones.
- evaluate the operation and performance of industrial systems and plants.
- identify, formulate and solve medium-difficulty problems related to the design or production of standardized company products;
- update themselves on methods, techniques, technologies and tools in the field of industrial engineering in general;
- consult the main technical-scientific journals and national, European and international regulations of the sector.
- identify and clearly articulate aspects of a problem referring to different disciplines and identify the external competencies required to address them.
The common didactic approach for all courses involves theoretical training accompanied by examples, applications, individual and group work, and verifications that encourage active participation, propositional attitude, ability for autonomous processing, and communication of work results. Additionally, the training internship scheduled in the third year at University laboratories or local organizations/companies allows for the enhancement of application abilities acquired during the course.
Verification of acquired knowledge and the resulting judgment will primarily be based on the completion of written tests, individual and/or group reports with oral presentation, and oral interviews with instructors.
Official language(s) of instruction and assessment.
ITALIAN Competencies associated with the role.
Junior Industrial Engineer To be able to operate effectively in various contexts, both national and international, the industrial engineer:
• possesses a solid foundation of basic knowledge that allows effective application of the methodological-operational aspects of engineering sciences;
• knows the fundamental principles of disciplines necessary for operating in the design, innovation, management and control of production processes;
• knows business contexts and the principles of business culture in its economic, management and organizational aspects, and possesses excellent relational and decision-making skills with a propensity for teamwork;
• possesses the basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of their own knowledge;
• has excellent command of the Italian language and effectively masters at least one additional community language, both orally and in writing.
Professional role in work context.
Junior Industrial Engineer The industrial engineer graduate from the University of Sassari is characterized by versatility of employment derived from a multidisciplinary training that includes both specific direction courses, such as mechanics, energy, automation, materials science, and industrial bioengineering, as well as courses with complementary technical-scientific content such as electronics, telecommunications, business organization, economics and markets, and environmental sustainability.
The Industrial Engineer professional operates in the field of technological plants within residential, industrial, commercial and tertiary sectors. The activities inherent to this professional role include:
• Operational functions in design, production process, verification and commissioning of technological plants, linked to an adequate knowledge of the tools of mathematics and other basic sciences, used to interpret and describe physical phenomena and typical problems of Industrial Engineering, and a solid cultural training in some characteristic areas of Industrial Engineering such as materials science and technology, applied thermodynamics and heat transfer, electrical engineering, industrial automation and industrial bioengineering.
• Complementary functions and ability to operate in responsible roles - such as work direction, coordination of business activities, evaluation of environmental impacts and costs, and technical-administrative compliance related to industrial reality - thanks to the acquired technical-organizational knowledge in the context of industrial processes and business management.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The objective of the study course is to train industrial engineers with a broad spectrum of technical-scientific competencies typical of engineering, with particular reference to the energy and electrical fields, the fields of management engineering, materials science and industrial bioengineering.
The path aims to provide a solid scientific and technical-applicative preparation, with general knowledge regarding the productive, design, energy and environmental aspects of industrial systems. The specific educational objectives of the Industrial Engineering degree course are as follows:
• adequately know the methodological-operational aspects of mathematical analysis, geometry, chemistry and physics and be able to use such knowledge to interpret and describe industrial engineering problems;
• effectively use techniques and tools for the design and management of components, systems and processes in the energy and electrical, biomedical, productive and management fields;
• develop knowledge on different types of materials, both traditional and innovative, their production processes, processing technologies and environmental impact;
• operate in the production, distribution and utilization of energy in its various forms (mechanical, electrical, thermal, chemical), evaluating their interactions with environmental and economic/business aspects;
• acquire the fundamentals of industrial bioengineering in order to develop adequate knowledge to support the study of biomedical applications, interface with biomedical professional figures, and understand the origin of phenomena on which intervention must be made, as well as the related issues;
• know and be able to manage fundamental organizational, management and economic issues that arise in various business contexts, and be able to estimate the impact of engineering decisions and solutions adopted in the business, social and environmental context.
• know contemporary contexts, develop relational and decision-making skills, and possess the cognitive tools for continuous updating of their knowledge and competencies;
• communicate effectively, in written and oral form, regarding topics related to the professional profile in at least one language of the European Union, in addition to Italian.
The educational path develops over three academic years, divided into semesters, and is structured to develop basic disciplines in the first three semesters and reserve the remaining three semesters for disciplines more specifically engineering. In particular, the first year prioritizes basic preparation in mathematics, algebra, geometry, physics, chemistry and computer science, to provide students with the necessary methodological-operational foundations for industrial engineering. Starting from the second year, the acquisition of competencies focuses on the fields of electrical engineering, materials science, management engineering and energy engineering. In the third year, which also includes elective courses and the final exam, the training is completed in the characteristic areas of the study course and in the related and complementary fields of interest. Also in the third year, a training and orientation internship is scheduled to be carried out at companies, professional offices and research organizations of the territory or in national and international contexts (with particular attention to the Erasmus+ Traineeship program). The Study Course has established a corporate partnership that participates in organizing these specific activities and carries out consultancy for some modules of the Course and seminar activities.
The educational objectives and expected learning outcomes are designed to provide the graduate with the tools both for direct entry into the workforce as a junior industrial engineer, and for continuing studies in a Master's degree course in engineering.

Nurse: health operator who, possessing the enabling university degree and registration with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
Graduates in Nursing can find employment in public or private health and social care facilities, either as employees or in independent practice.
In particular, employment opportunities are identifiable in:
- hospitals in all inpatient units and outpatient services;
- territorial and hospital emergency services;
- post-acute, long-term care facilities, assisted health residences, rehabilitation centers, disability care centers, hospices;
- territorial, home-based and outpatient health services;
- prevention and public health services.
Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities provided for in the study plan must be earned. The final exam, which has the value of a State exam enabling for the profession, consists of a theoretical, applied and experimental dissertation and the demonstration of practical skills in managing a situation related to the specific professional profile.
To regulate more precisely the assignment of the score in line with the guidelines of the Conference of Health Professions, a specific regulation has been drawn up, effective from the academic year 2014/2015.
In particular, the determination of the graduation grade (expressed in hundredths, with possible honors) involves the following parameters:
- weighted average of the grades obtained in the exams transformed into hundredths;
- points assigned by the Graduation Committee during the thesis discussion based on the following parameters: practical test, thesis paper, graduation in progress, honors obtained in the exams, participation in international exchange programs (Internships or Erasmus Programs).
The Final Exam Committee, appointed by the competent Academic Authority in accordance with the law, consists of not less than 7 and not more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector and includes at least 2 members designated by the Professional College or by the most representative professional associations identified in accordance with current regulations.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the Nursing Degree Course, in accordance with Article 6, paragraph three, of D.M. n. 270/2004, it is necessary to possess a secondary school diploma or another equivalent foreign degree.
The recognition of foreign degrees for admission to the degree course is decided in compliance with existing international agreements.
Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics at secondary school level is required.
The number of students admitted to the degree course is determined annually by a decree of the Ministry of Health in consultation with the Ministry of Education, University and Research, based on the regional training plan, taking into account national health needs and based on the teaching project and training potential.
Admission to the Degree Course is subject to a limited number and requires an admission exam consisting of a multiple-choice test; the exam will cover topics in: general culture, biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics.
The call for admission to nationally limited number courses is available at the following link:
https://www.uniss.it/didattica/offerta-formativa/prove-di-accesso-ai-corsi-di-studio/corsi-numero-programmato The modalities and content of the admission exams for nationally limited number degree courses are defined in D.M. n. 85 of 05/02/14.
The initial preparation of the student will be assessed through the analysis of errors found in the logic, chemistry, biology, physics-mathematics quizzes (multiple-choice questions) administered in the admission test, common to all health area degree courses of the Faculty, and the assignment of any deficiencies according to the modalities specified in the course didactic regulation.

Communication Skills.
Nursing graduates must develop the following communication skills:
- use appropriate communication skills (verbal, non-verbal, and written) with patients of all ages and their families within the care process and/or with other healthcare professionals in an appropriate verbal, non-verbal, and written manner;
- use appropriate communication methods in multi-professional teams;
- use principles of teaching and learning for specific information or educational interventions directed at individual patients, families, and groups, and other professionals (support staff, nursing students, nurses);
- support and encourage patients towards health choices, reinforcing coping skills, self-esteem, and enhancing available resources;
- manage conflicts arising from different positions;
- facilitate coordination of care to achieve agreed health care outcomes;
- collaborate with the care team to agree on operational methods and implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives, testimonies;
- discussion of cases and paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with patients and the team.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- observation of film frames or written dialogues using structured grids;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolios, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports);
- structured objective examination with stations featuring simulations of relational skills.
Learning Abilities.
Nursing graduates must develop the following self-learning abilities:
- develop skills for independent study;
- demonstrate the ability to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activity;
- develop the ability to pose questions relevant to the timing, location, and interlocutors of their professional practice;
- demonstrate the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning;
- demonstrate the ability for self-assessment of their competencies and outline their development and learning needs;
- demonstrate the ability for collaborative learning and sharing knowledge within work teams;
- demonstrate the ability and autonomy in seeking necessary information to solve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, critically selecting primary and secondary research evidence sources.
Didactic tools, methods, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- problem-based learning;
- use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- research methodology workshops for printed and online bibliographic research;
- guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- project work, reports on specific research assignments;
- tutorial supervision of the internship path;
- active participation in work sessions;
- punctuality and quality in presenting assignments.
The teaching methods provided to achieve this specific training objective (ability to apply knowledge) include frontal lessons, lectures, seminars, work groups, and discussions. The teaching process will utilize modern didactic tools. The ability to apply acquired knowledge is developed through internship activities in various healthcare settings in medical and surgical fields, both general and specialized, especially with interdisciplinary approaches.
Verification of this learning is assessed through examination tests, which, in addition to traditional oral or written exams, include a sequence of in-course assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews) to verify acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, the tools may be: (1) multiple-choice or short written questions organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; (2) written reports on assigned topics, analyzing activities and reports related to the final exam, as well as comments on practical exercises performed, and evaluation of the overall profile based on predefined criteria.
The course organization includes monitoring the achievement of the aforementioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding in terms of expected learning outcomes, through a coordinated approach specifically designed for this purpose.

UNIVERSITY: University of Sassari
COURSE: [1219] NURSING (ENTITLED TO THE HEALTH PROFESSION OF NURSE)
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10035?annoOrdinamento=2022

Autonomy of Judgment.
Nursing graduates must demonstrate autonomy of judgment through the following skills:
- make clinical decisions;
- determine priorities for patient groups;
- decide interventions to be assigned to support staff;
- implement personalized nursing care by making choices based on similarities and differences among patients in terms of values, ethnicity, and socio-cultural practices;
- decide appropriate care interventions that take into account legal, political, geographical, economic, ethical, and social influences;
- critically evaluate the outcomes of care decisions based on patient outcomes and care standards;
- assume responsibility and account for one's professional practice in accordance with the professional profile, code of ethics, and ethical and legal standards;
- make decisions through a scientific problem-solving approach for patients;
- analyze organizational problems and propose solutions;
- make decisions in situations of differing positions (conflicts or dilemmas).
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- guided reading and application exercises;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings, with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility;
- debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Prerequisite Area Nursing graduates must know and understand the:
- biomedical sciences for understanding physiological and pathological processes related to health and illness across different life stages;
- informatics and linguistic disciplines, with particular emphasis on the English language for understanding nursing scientific literature, both printed and online.
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic;
- guided reading and application;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- construction of cognitive maps.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests.
Clinical Nursing Area Nursing graduates must know and understand the:
- general and clinical nursing sciences for understanding the fields of nursing intervention, the clinical method guiding an effective approach to care, operational techniques, and evidence guiding decision-making;
- psychosocial and humanistic sciences for understanding normal and pathological relational dynamics and the defense or adaptation reactions of individuals to situations of psychological, social, and physical distress.
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic;
- guided reading and application;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- construction of cognitive maps.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests.
Prevention and Management Area Nursing graduates must know and understand the:
- hygienic-preventive sciences for understanding health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions aimed at promoting safety for healthcare workers and users;
- ethical, legal, and sociological sciences for understanding the organizational complexity of the Healthcare System, the importance and utility of acting in accordance with regulations and guidelines, as well as respecting values and ethical dilemmas encountered in daily practice; these are also aimed at fostering understanding of professional autonomy, areas of integration and interdependence with other members of the care team;
- learning and change theories for understanding educational processes directed at citizens or patients.
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic;
- guided reading and application;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- construction of cognitive maps.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Prerequisite Area Nursing graduates must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- interpret and apply research findings to nursing practice and link research processes to the theoretical development of nursing science;
- integrate theoretical and practical nursing knowledge with biological, psychological, socio-cultural, and humanistic sciences to understand individuals of all ages, groups, and communities.
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- application exercises;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- construction of cognitive maps;
- case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings, with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests, project work, reports;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.
Clinical Nursing Area Nursing graduates must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- integrate knowledge, skills, and attitudes of care to provide safe, effective, and evidence-based nursing care;
- provide safe and evidence-based nursing care to improve health outcomes or achieve a state of well-being for the patient;
- conduct a comprehensive and systematic assessment of the individual's care needs;
- use assessment techniques to accurately collect data on the main health issues of patients;
- accurately analyze and interpret collected data through patient assessment;
- plan the delivery of nursing care in collaboration with users and the interdisciplinary care team;
- evaluate care progress in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team;
- manage a variety of activities required to deliver nursing care to patients in various care settings, including hospital, community, and residential environments.
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- application exercises;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- construction of cognitive maps;
- case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings, with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests, project work, reports;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.
Prevention and Management Area Nursing graduates must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- use a body of theoretical knowledge derived from nursing sciences, behavioral and social biological sciences, and other disciplines to recognize the needs of patients across different ages and developmental stages throughout life;
- use theoretical models and role models within the care process to facilitate growth, development, and adaptation in promoting, maintaining, and recovering health for citizens;
- facilitate the development of a safe environment for the patient by ensuring constant nursing vigilance.
Teaching methods and tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- application exercises;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- construction of cognitive maps;
- case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings, with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, stepwise case tests, project work, reports;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Nurse: a healthcare professional who, holding the university degree entitling them to practice and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
The educational path of the Nursing degree course has specific educational objectives, contributing to competence through knowledge (knowing), attitude, and practical skills/applications (knowing how to do).
In particular, in the training of nurses, the objectives are aimed at ensuring that the nursing graduate is able to:
- manage preventive and care interventions for patients, families, and communities with autonomy and responsibility;
- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, and elderly) with acute and chronic respiratory problems, cardiovascular issues, metabolic and rheumatic problems, acute and chronic renal problems, acute and chronic gastrointestinal problems, liver problems, neurological problems, oncological problems, infectious problems, orthopedic and traumatic problems, obstetric-gynecological problems, hematological conditions, behavioral and cognitive alterations, psychological discomfort/disturbance);
- assess and manage nursing care for patients with chronic conditions and disabilities;
- manage perioperative nursing care;
- ensure the safe administration of therapy and monitor its effectiveness;
- perform nursing techniques defined by the degree course standards;
- activate decision-making processes based on patient conditions, altered parameter values, reports, and laboratory tests;
- manage diagnostic pathways, ensuring adequate patient preparation and subsequent monitoring;
- integrate nursing care into the multidisciplinary care project;
- assess the patient's problems using structured and systematic techniques, identifying alterations in functional models (activity and exercise, perception and maintenance of health, nutrition and metabolism, elimination model, rest and sleep, cognition and perception, self-concept, role and relationships, coping and stress management, sexuality and reproduction, values and beliefs);
- activate and support residual capacities of the person to promote adaptation to limitations and alterations caused by illness and changes in lifestyle;
- identify the nursing care needs of the person and their reactions related to illness, ongoing treatments, institutionalization, changes in daily activities, and perceived quality of life;
- define intervention priorities based on care needs, organizational requirements, and optimal use of available resources;
- design and implement, collaborating with other professionals, informational and educational interventions for risk factor control directed at individuals and groups;
- evaluate the results of delivered care and adjust nursing planning based on the evolution of the patient's problems;
- manage and organize nursing care for a group of patients (including night shifts);
- distinguish between care needs and nursing care needs, differentiating the contribution of support staff from that of nurses;
- assign and supervise care activities to support staff;
- manage paper and computerized information systems supporting care;
- document nursing care delivered in accordance with legal and ethical principles;
- ensure patients and significant persons receive relevant and up-to-date information about their health status;
- prepare conditions for the patient's discharge, in collaboration with team members;
- guarantee continuity of care between different shifts and between different services/structures;
- use professional integration tools (meetings, team meetings, case discussions);
- work integratively within the team, respecting competence areas;
- ensure an effective physical and psychosocial environment for patient safety;
- use practices for protection against physical, chemical, and biological risks in the workplace;
- adopt precautions for manual handling of loads;
- adopt strategies for preventing infectious risk (standard precautions) in hospital and community settings;
- monitor the clinical and psychosocial situation of patients, identifying early signs of patient deterioration;
- activate necessary interventions to manage acute and/or critical situations;
- identify triggering factors for re-exacerbation in chronic patients;
- activate and manage a helping and therapeutic relationship with the user, their family, and significant persons;
- manage care processes respecting cultural, ethnic, generational, and gender differences;
- support, in collaboration with the team, the patient and family during the terminal phase and grief;
- activate informal care networks to support the user and family in long-term care projects.
Function in the Work Context.
Nurse: a healthcare professional who, holding the university degree entitling them to practice and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
The main functions are: disease prevention, care for patients and disabled individuals of all ages, and health education.
In particular, the nurse:
a) participates in identifying health needs of individuals and the community;
b) identifies nursing care needs of individuals and the community and formulates related objectives;
c) plans, manages, and evaluates nursing care interventions;
d) ensures the correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions;
e) acts both individually and in collaboration with other healthcare and social professionals;
f) utilizes support staff as necessary to perform functions;
g) carries out professional activities in public or private healthcare facilities, in the territory, and in home care, in dependent or self-employed regime.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The educational path of the Nursing degree course has specific educational objectives, defined for each professional profile, contributing to competence through knowledge (knowing), attitude, and practical skills/applications (knowing how to do).
In particular, in the training of nurses, the objectives are aimed at ensuring that the nursing graduate is able to:

- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, and elderly) with acute and chronic respiratory problems, cardiovascular issues, metabolic and rheumatic problems, acute and chronic renal problems, acute and chronic gastrointestinal problems, liver problems, neurological problems, oncological problems, infectious problems, orthopedic and traumatic problems, obstetric-gynecological problems, hematological conditions, behavioral and cognitive alterations, psychological discomfort/disturbance);

In relation to these specific educational objectives, the educational activity ensures a unified and, at the same time, interdisciplinary vision of the educational objectives, with in-depth knowledge from the characteristic disciplinary areas, including those more specifically professionalizing, and from related and integrative disciplinary areas. According to DM 19 February 2009, each activated course includes an integer number of credit points to avoid information fragmentation for students. The teaching methods include frontal lectures, seminars, work groups, and discussions on relevant topics and simulations aimed at achieving the educational path's objectives. The teaching process will utilize modern teaching tools. Traditional teaching activity is complemented by guided internship activity at specialized public healthcare services and other scientifically relevant and valuable structures for achieving educational objectives, located in Italy or abroad and linked by specific agreements. This training allows for progressive assumption of responsibility and professional autonomy, within which nursing students acquire the ability to assess various issues related to nursing care, plan correct nursing care, and integrate into a cooperative group work with different figures involved in nursing care in various public and social healthcare contexts. Laboratory and internship activities are carried out under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors specifically designated based on communication skills, adequately trained for this function. Laboratory and internship activities are coordinated by a faculty member belonging to the highest educational level for the specific profile.
The study plan includes exams and/or final assessments organized as integrated exams for multiple courses or coordinated modules. The verification of this learning is assessed through exams, which, in addition to traditional oral or written exams, include a sequence of in-course assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews) to verify acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, the tools used are: (1) multiple-choice or short written answers, organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; (2) written essays on assigned topics and analysis of activities related to the final exam and comments on exercises performed, through evaluation of the overall profile based on predefined criteria. The degree course's teaching regulations define, within the limits of legal constraints, that the student's total weekly study time for personal study or other individual training activities will not be less than at least 50% of the thirty hours provided for each CFU.
The educational path is structured, monitored, validated, and optimized in a continuum to acquire the competencies, knowledge, and skills specified in the curriculum profile established by current regulations and the specific objectives of the course. These specific educational objectives are supported by a faculty aware of the need to use all institutional tools activated by competent bodies (NVF and NVA) for the accreditation of teaching quality. Through these tools, it is possible to measure the improvement of teaching performance in all different phases contributing to the achievement of the first-level degree, in terms of educational path, exams, perceived quality assessment by students, and acquisition of professional competencies included in the specific objectives of the educational path itself.

High school diploma Tuition and fees Regulations for careers - Fees Roles President PASQUALE BANDIERA Program, textbooks and objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Nurse: health professional who, holding the enabling university degree and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.
Graduates in Nursing can find employment in public or private health and social care facilities, either as employees or in independent practice.
In particular, employment opportunities are identifiable in:
- hospitals in all inpatient units and outpatient services;
- territorial and hospital emergency services;
- post-acute, long-term care facilities, assisted health residences, rehabilitation centers, disability care centers, hospices;
- territorial, home-based and outpatient health services;
- prevention and public health services.
Final exam characteristics.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities specified in the study plan must be earned. The final exam, which has the value of a State Exam enabling for the profession, consists of a theoretical, applied and experimental dissertation and the demonstration of practical skills in managing a situation related to the specific professional profile.
To regulate more precisely the scoring attribution in line with the guidelines of the Conference of Health Professions, a specific regulation has been established, effective from the academic year 2014/2015.
In particular, the final grade (expressed in hundredths, with possible honors) is determined by the following parameters:
- weighted average of grades obtained in exams converted to hundredths;
- points assigned by the Degree Committee during the thesis discussion based on the following parameters: practical test, thesis paper, graduation during the course, honors obtained in profit exams, participation in international exchange programs (Internships or Erasmus Programs).
The Final Exam Committee, appointed by the competent Academic Authority in accordance with the law, consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector and including at least 2 members designated by the professional college or by the most representative professional associations as per current regulations.
Required knowledge for access.
To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Nursing, as provided for in Article 6, paragraph 3, of DM n. 270/2004, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another equivalent foreign degree.
Recognition of foreign degrees for admission to the degree program is decided in compliance with current international agreements.
Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics at secondary school level is required.
The number of students admitted to the degree program is determined annually by a decree of the Ministry of Health in consultation with the Ministry of Education, University and Research, based on the regional training plan, taking into account national health needs and the didactic project and training potential.
Admission to the Bachelor's Degree program is quota-based and requires an admission exam consisting of a multiple-choice test; the exam will cover topics in: general culture, biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics.
The admission notice for quota-based courses at national level is available at the following link:
https://www.uniss.it/didattica/offerta-formativa/prove-di-accesso-ai-corsi-di-studio/corsi-numero-programmato The modalities and content of admission exams for quota-based degree courses at national level are defined in DM n. 85 of 05/02/14.
Student initial preparation will be assessed through analysis of errors in logic, chemistry, biology, physics-mathematics quizzes (multiple-choice questions) administered in the admission test, common to all health area degree programs of the Faculty, and the assignment of any deficiencies according to the procedures specified in the course didactic regulation.
Degree awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in NURSING (Enabling for the Health Profession of Nurse)

Communication Skills.
Nursing graduates must develop the following communication skills:
- use appropriate communication skills (verbal, non-verbal, and written) with users of all ages and their families within the care process and/or with other healthcare professionals in an appropriate verbal, non-verbal, and written manner;
- use appropriate communication methods in the multidisciplinary team;
- use principles of teaching and learning for specific information or educational interventions directed at individual users, families, and groups, and other professionals (support staff, nursing students, nurses);
- support and encourage users towards health choices, reinforcing coping skills, self-esteem, and enhancing available resources;
- manage conflicts arising from different positions;
- facilitate coordination of care to achieve agreed health care outcomes;
- collaborate with the care team to agree on operational methods and implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives, testimonies;
- case discussion and discussion of paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- observation of film or written frames, dialogues with structured grids;
- evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports);
- structured objective examination with stations with simulations on relational skills.
Learning Abilities.
Nursing graduates must develop the following self-learning abilities:
- develop skills for independent study;
- demonstrate the ability to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activity;
- develop the ability to pose questions relevant to the timing, location, and interlocutors of one's professional practice;
- demonstrate the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning;
- demonstrate self-assessment abilities of one's own competencies and outline personal development and learning needs;
- demonstrate collaborative learning abilities and sharing of knowledge within work teams;
- demonstrate ability and autonomy in seeking necessary information to solve professional practice problems or uncertainties, critically selecting primary and secondary research evidence sources.
Didactic tools, teaching methods, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- problem-based learning;
- use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- research methodology workshops for printed and online literature;
- guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- project work, reports on specific research assignments;
- tutorial supervision of the internship path;
- active participation in work sessions;
- punctuality and quality in presenting deliverables.
The teaching methods provided to achieve this specific training objective (ability to apply knowledge) include frontal lessons, lectures, seminars, work groups, and discussions. The teaching process will utilize modern didactic tools. The ability to apply acquired knowledge is developed through internship activities in various care settings in medical and surgical fields, both general and specialized, especially with interdisciplinary approaches.
Verification of this learning is assessed through examination tests, which, in addition to traditional oral or written exams, include a sequence of in-course assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews) to verify acquired knowledge. Regarding written tests, tools may include: (1) multiple-choice or short written answers organized around interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; (2) written reports on assigned topics, analyzing activities and reports related to the final exam, as well as commenting on practical exercises performed, and through evaluation of the overall profile developed based on predefined criteria.
The course organization includes monitoring of the achievement of the aforementioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding in terms of expected learning outcomes, through an articulated coordination, also prepared for this purpose.
