- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various settings and with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.

Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, staged case studies, project-work, reports;
- assessment feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice);
- structured objective station exam.

Prevention and Management Area Nursing graduates must demonstrate the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- use a body of theoretical knowledge derived from nursing sciences, behavioral and social biology, and other disciplines to recognize the needs of individuals across various ages and developmental stages throughout life;
- use theoretical models and role models within the care process to facilitate growth, development, and adaptation in promoting, maintaining, and recovering health in citizens;
- facilitate the development of a safe environment for the patient by ensuring constant nursing vigilance.

Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Nurse: A healthcare professional who, holding the qualifying university degree and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.

The educational path of the Nursing Bachelor's Degree Program has specific educational objectives, contributing to competence through knowledge (knowing), attitude, and practical skills (knowing how to do).

In particular, in the training of the nurse, the objectives are aimed at ensuring that the nursing graduate is able to:
- manage preventive and care interventions for the assisted person, family, and community with autonomy and responsibility;
- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, and elderly) with acute and chronic respiratory problems, cardiovascular issues, metabolic and rheumatic problems, acute and chronic renal problems, acute and chronic gastrointestinal problems, liver problems, neurological problems, oncological problems, infectious problems, orthopedic and traumatic problems, obstetric-gynecological problems, hematological conditions, behavioral and cognitive alterations, psychological discomfort/disturbance;
- assess and manage nursing care for patients with chronic conditions and disabilities;
- manage perioperative nursing care;
- ensure safe administration of therapy and monitor its effectiveness;
- perform nursing techniques defined by the Bachelor's Degree Program standards;
- activate decision-making processes based on patient conditions, altered parameter values, reports, and laboratory tests;
- manage diagnostic pathways by ensuring adequate patient preparation and subsequent monitoring;
- integrate nursing care into multidisciplinary care projects;
- assess problems of the patient using structured and systematic techniques through the identification of alterations in functional models (activities and exercise, perception and maintenance of health, nutrition and metabolism, elimination model, rest and sleep, cognition and perception, self-concept, role and relationships, coping and stress management, sexuality and reproduction, values and beliefs);
- activate and support residual capacities of the person to promote adaptation to limitations and alterations caused by illness and changes in lifestyle;
- identify the nursing care needs of the person and their reactions related to illness, ongoing treatments, institutionalization, changes in daily activities, and perceived quality of life;
- define the priorities of interventions based on care needs, organizational requirements, and optimal use of available resources;
- design and implement, collaborating with other professionals, informational and educational interventions for risk factor control directed at individuals and groups;
- evaluate the results of delivered care and adjust nursing planning based on the evolution of the patient's problems;
- manage and organize nursing care for a group of patients (including night shifts);
- distinguish between care needs and nursing care needs, differentiating the contribution of support staff from that of nurses;
- assign and supervise care activities to support staff;
- manage paper and computer-based information systems supporting care;
- document nursing care delivered in accordance with legal and ethical principles;
- ensure patients and significant persons receive relevant and up-to-date information about their health status;
- prepare conditions for the discharge of the assisted person, in collaboration with team members;
- ensure continuity of care between different shifts and services;
- use professional integration tools (meetings, team meetings, case discussions);
- work integratively within the team respecting competence areas;
- ensure an effective physical and psychosocial environment for patient safety;
- use practices for protection against physical, chemical, and biological risks in the workplace;
- adopt precautions for manual handling of loads;
- adopt infection risk prevention strategies (standard precautions) in hospital and community settings;
- monitor the clinical and psychosocial situation of patients, identifying early signs of deterioration;
- activate necessary interventions to manage acute and/or critical situations;
- identify triggering factors for reactivation in chronic patients;
- activate and manage a therapeutic and supportive relationship with the user, their family, and significant persons;
- manage care processes respecting cultural, ethnic, generational, and gender differences;
- support, in collaboration with the team, the patient and family during the terminal phase and grief;
- activate informal care networks to support the user and family in long-term care projects.

Function in the Work Context.
Nurse: A healthcare professional who, holding the qualifying university degree and registered with the professional register, is responsible for general nursing care.

The main functions are: disease prevention, care for patients and disabled individuals of all ages, and health education.

In particular, the nurse:
a) participates in identifying health needs of the person and the community;
b) identifies nursing care needs of the person and the community and formulates related objectives;
c) plans, manages, and evaluates nursing care interventions;
d) ensures correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions;
e) acts both individually and in collaboration with other healthcare and social professionals;
f) utilizes support staff as necessary to perform functions;
g) carries out professional activities in public or private healthcare facilities, in the territory, and in home care, in dependent or freelance practice.

Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The educational path of the Nursing Bachelor's Degree Program has specific educational objectives, defined for each professional profile, contributing to competence through knowledge (knowing), attitude, and practical skills (knowing how to do).

In particular, in the training of the nurse, the objectives are aimed at ensuring that the nursing graduate is able to:
- manage preventive and care interventions for the assisted person, family, and community with autonomy and responsibility;
- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, and elderly) with acute and chronic respiratory problems, cardiovascular issues, metabolic and rheumatic problems, acute and chronic renal problems, acute and chronic gastrointestinal problems, liver problems, neurological problems, oncological problems, infectious problems, orthopedic and traumatic problems, obstetric-gynecological problems, hematological conditions, behavioral and cognitive alterations, psychological discomfort/disturbance;

- integrate nursing care into multidisciplinary care projects;
- assess problems of the patient using structured and systematic techniques through the identification of alterations in functional models (activities and exercise, perception and maintenance of health, nutrition and metabolism, elimination model, rest and sleep, cognition and perception, self-concept, role and relationships, coping and stress management, sexuality and reproduction, values and beliefs);
- activate and support residual capacities of the person to promote adaptation to limitations and alterations caused by illness and changes in lifestyle;
- identify the nursing care needs of the person and their reactions related to illness, ongoing treatments, institutionalization, changes in daily activities, and perceived quality of life;
- define the priorities of interventions based on care needs, organizational requirements, and optimal use of available resources;
- design and implement, collaborating with other professionals, informational and educational interventions for risk factor control directed at individuals and groups;
- evaluate the results of delivered care and adjust nursing planning based on the evolution of the patient's problems;
- manage and organize nursing care for a group of patients (including night shifts);
- distinguish between care needs and nursing care needs, differentiating the contribution of support staff from that of nurses;
- assign and supervise care activities to support staff;
- manage paper and computer-based information systems supporting care;
- document nursing care delivered in accordance with legal and ethical principles;
- ensure patients and significant persons receive relevant and up-to-date information about their health status;
- prepare conditions for the discharge of the assisted person, in collaboration with team members;
- ensure continuity of care between different shifts and services;
- use professional integration tools (meetings, team meetings, case discussions);

- identify triggering factors for reactivation in chronic patients;
- activate and manage a therapeutic and supportive relationship with the user, their family, and significant persons;

- activate informal care networks to support the user and family in long-term care projects.

In relation to these specific educational objectives, the educational activity ensures a unified and, at the same time, interdisciplinary vision of the educational objectives themselves, with in-depth knowledge from the characteristic disciplinary areas, including those more specifically professionalizing, and from related and integrative disciplinary areas. According to Ministerial Decree No. 19 February 2009, each activated course provides an integer number of credit points to avoid information fragmentation for students. The teaching methods include frontal lectures, seminars, work groups, and discussions on relevant topics and simulations aimed at achieving the educational path objectives. The teaching process will utilize modern teaching tools. Traditional teaching activities are complemented by guided internship activities at specialized public healthcare services and other scientifically relevant and valuable structures for achieving educational objectives, located in Italy or abroad and linked by specific agreements. This training allows for progressive assumption of responsibility and professional autonomy, within which Nursing students acquire the ability to assess various issues related to nursing care, plan correct nursing care, and integrate into a cooperative group work with different figures involved in nursing care in various public and social healthcare contexts. Laboratory and internship activities are carried out under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors specifically designated based on communication skills, adequately trained for this function. Laboratory and internship activities are coordinated by a faculty member belonging to the highest educational level provided for the specific profile.

The study plan includes exams and/or final assessments organized as integrated exams for multiple courses or coordinated modules. The verification of this learning is assessed through exams, which, in addition to traditional oral or written exams, include a sequence of in-progress assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews) to verify acquired knowledge. Regarding written exams, the tools used are: (1) multiple-choice or short written answers on interdisciplinary issues, followed by exams to verify acquired competencies; (2) written reports on assigned topics and analysis of activities related to the final exam, as well as comments on exercises performed, through evaluation of the overall profile based on predefined criteria. The teaching regulations of the Bachelor's Degree Program define, within the limits of legal constraints, that the student's total weekly study time for personal study or other individual training activities will not be less than at least 50% of the thirty hours provided for each CFU.

The educational path is structured, monitored, validated, and optimized in a continuum to acquire the competencies, knowledge, and skills specified in the curriculum profile established by current regulations and the specific objectives of the Course. These specific educational objectives are supported by a faculty aware of the need to use all institutional tools activated by competent bodies (NVF and NVA) for the accreditation of teaching quality. Through these tools, it is possible to measure the improvement of teaching performance in all different phases contributing to the acquisition of the first-level degree, in terms of educational path, exams, perceived quality assessment by students, and acquisition of professional competencies included in the specific objectives of the educational path itself.

Physiotherapist The Physiotherapist is a health professional who provides services in infant, adult and geriatric areas within physiotherapy and rehabilitation services under the National and Regional Health Service (National Health Service contract), in private accredited and contracted structures with the National Health Service, clinics, rehabilitation structures and centers, Nursing Homes, at the patient's home, in thermal resorts and wellness centers, medical offices and/or multi-specialty clinics. Current regulations allow the performance of self-employed activities in individual or associated professional offices, sports associations and societies of various types, service cooperatives, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), public or private prevention services.
Characteristics of the final exam.
The final exam, which has the value of a state exam enabling the practice of the profession of Physiotherapist, consists of:
1) A practical test during which the student must demonstrate to have acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the Physiotherapist profile;
2) The writing and presentation of a thesis, whose content must be related to themes or disciplines relevant to the professional profile.
To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities provided for in the study plan must be obtained, including those related to the internship activity.
For the thesis work, the student will be supervised by a university lecturer, called the supervisor, and by any co-supervisors.
Required knowledge for admission.
Candidates who possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable may be admitted to the Physiotherapy Degree Course.
Additionally, it is necessary to possess the knowledge and skills defined annually by the ministerial decree regarding the admission tests for nationally targeted degree courses.
The modalities and content of the admission tests for nationally targeted degree courses are defined by specific ministerial decrees. The test serves a selective function and also verifies the possession of adequate initial preparation.
Students admitted to the Degree Course who obtain a score below the annual threshold set by the Course Council in the admission test are assigned additional training obligations in Chemistry, Biology and Physics. To allow the cancellation of any verified training debt, personalized recovery plans will be activated under the responsibility of the lecturers of the disciplines or of specially selected teaching tutors. Training debts are considered fulfilled with a verbalized verification on the integrated part at the same time as the regular examination of the relevant courses.
Degree awarded.
Degree in PHYSIOTHERAPY (Enabling to the Health Profession of Physiotherapist)
Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.

Communication Skills.
The graduate, at the end of the study program, must be able to:
• Utilize effective therapeutic communication and relationship skills, including non-verbal communication, with people of all ages and their families, and establish effective relationships with other healthcare professionals
• Listen, inform, and dialogue effectively and understandably with patients and their families, communicate, justify, and present arguments regarding one's work and decisions with colleagues and different professional figures
• Adapt communication according to the context while respecting cultural, ethnic, and value differences of the patients
• Use communication tools in the healthcare setting, demonstrating the ability to complete the physiotherapy record and draft a therapeutic report
• Communicate clearly, concisely, and professionally in both verbal and written form, technically and grammatically accurate, and able to translate technical language into understandable terms for patients and the team
• Communicate appropriately in national and international scientific contexts to convey ideas, problems, and their solutions
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
• Frontal lectures and seminars to introduce the topic
• Videos and critical analysis of film clips, simulations, narratives, and testimonies
• Discussion of cases and paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions
• Internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts, followed by debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with patients and the team
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
• Observation of film clips or written materials, dialogues using structured grids
• Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms, and clinical reports)
• Structured objective station-based assessment with simulations of relational skills
• Written or oral report
Learning Ability.
The graduate, at the end of the study program, must be able to:
• Develop competent and independent problem-solving skills, demonstrating the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning
• Take responsibility for one's professional development and respond to ongoing changes in knowledge and health and social needs
• Use self-assessment of one's educational level to maintain knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice
• Design self-training paths to enhance one's competencies, with particular reference to Evidence-Based Practice in physiotherapy/rehabilitation
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
• Problem-Based Learning (PBL)
• Use of cognitive maps
• Use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment
• Research methodology workshops for online and printed literature
• Guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English
Critical Judgment.
The graduate, at the end of the study program, will be able to independently:
• Know and apply, independently, the physiotherapy process using clinical reasoning as a decision-making criterion within the possible options composing the various phases of the process, with a critical thinking approach to deliver personalized treatment according to international guidelines and evidence-based practice
• Carry out professional activities by effectively responding to individual and/or collective health needs, either as an individual practitioner or within a team
• Evaluate the effectiveness of one's work, identifying critical issues and participating in their resolution
• Integrate knowledge of cultural diversity, values, and rights of the individual and community within ethical frameworks, respecting relevant regulations, professional, legal, health, and ethical guidelines
• Fully realize through habitual and judicious use of communication, emotions, values, a creative attitude oriented toward research and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual and the community
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
• Frontal lectures and seminar activities
• Videos, demonstrations of images, schemes, materials, and graphs
• Activation of cognitive maps
• Case discussions
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
• Written and oral formative assessments, written and oral exams, staged case tests, project work, reports
• Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms, and clinical reports on professional practice)
• Structured objective station-based assessment
• Debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences
Knowledge and Understanding.
Prevention and Care Graduates in Physiotherapy must acquire a broad and extensive range of knowledge in basic sciences, prevention, and related characteristic disciplines.
In particular, they must acquire solid cultural and scientific foundations in the fields of:
- Physical, biological, morphological, and functional preparatory sciences useful for understanding biological phenomena, organ and apparatus functioning mechanisms, motor and psychomotor development, physiological phenomena; for acquiring the functional scientific basis for rehabilitation methodology in various areas of interest.
- Hygienic-preventive sciences of healthcare services for understanding and analyzing health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions aimed at promoting safety for healthcare workers and users.
- Statistical, computer, and linguistic sciences for developing knowledge of statistical tools useful for understanding scientific data and analytical methods to be used in professional practice.
Rehabilitation and Management Graduates must acquire knowledge and understanding of the fundamental principles underlying their professional activity, as well as in communication/relationship and management and professional management. In particular, they must acquire solid cultural and scientific foundations in the fields of:
- Physiotherapy sciences to identify rehabilitation needs through clinical data evaluation in motor, psychomotor, cognitive, and functional areas, considering symptom severity and significance; understand the components underlying pathological processes targeted by rehabilitation/therapeutic interventions, in pediatric, adult, or geriatric age; develop the best therapeutic, technical, and methodological approaches for resolving health problems of the patient; acquire the scientific basis for functional alterations and general and specific rehabilitation methodology in various specialized fields (neurology, orthopedics and trauma, cardiovascular, critical care, oncology, pulmonology, maternal-infant area, etc.); plan and verify physiotherapy interventions using objective and effective evaluation and therapeutic methods and all appropriate tools for resolving different issues (instrumental therapies, manual therapies, psychomotor and occupational therapies, proposing the possible use of orthoses, prostheses, and aids), also in relation to medical indications and prescriptions;
- Interdisciplinary and surgical sciences for understanding pathophysiological elements applicable to various clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters;
- Management, ethical, legal, and sociological sciences aimed at organizing rehabilitation activities through defining priorities, appropriateness, and utilization of available resources, both by delegating tasks to collaborators and working in teams, ensuring continuity and quality of care; necessity to act in compliance with regulations and guidelines while respecting ethical values in clinical practice; also aimed at fostering understanding of professional autonomy, areas of integration and interdependence with other members of the care team;
- Human sciences for understanding normal and pathological relational dynamics and defense or adaptation reactions of people in psychophysical discomfort situations, also in correlation with psychological, social, and environmental dimensions related to processes determining priority health issues and disabilities, in acute phases, chronicity, in relation to different life stages and their impact on lifestyle and personal autonomy; improving understanding of processes
Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
Prevention and Care Graduates at the end of the training program must:
- Develop and contribute to diagnostic reasoning within an interdisciplinary team
- Identify health needs of the individual
- Integrate theoretical and practical knowledge with biological, psychological, socio-cultural, and human sciences to understand individuals of all ages, groups, and communities
- Apply and develop knowledge considering fundamental aspects such as interaction with the real-life context of people, interpersonal and inter-professional relationships, and organizational management of aspects directly related to the type of work performed.
Rehabilitation and Management Application of Knowledge and Understanding Graduates in Physiotherapy must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to demonstrate a professional approach to their work and possess adequate competencies to design and support arguments and solve problems in their field of study. In particular, they must:
- Critically apply knowledge, strategies, and tools underlying the physiotherapy process
- Use the body of theoretical knowledge and skills derived from physiotherapy sciences and recognize the needs of patients across different ages and developmental stages
- Correlate procedures enabling effective and safe interventions based on evidence in rehabilitation areas of motor, cortical, and visceral functions following pathological events of various congenital or acquired etiology
- Apply the physiotherapy process within the rehabilitation setting, both in simulated and patient scenarios, adopting problem-solving and clinical reasoning methodologies
- Be responsible for providing and evaluating treatment in line with professional quality standards in relation to ethical, bioethical, legal standards, and patient rights
- Interpret and apply research results to clinical practice and link research processes to the theoretical development of physiotherapy discipline
- Deliver direct physiotherapy treatment safely to individuals and groups of patients through evidence-based practice, using the physiotherapy process to evaluate and diagnose health status, plan goals, implement, and evaluate care provided, considering physical, psychological, and socio-cultural dimensions of the person
- Manage a variety of activities required to deliver physiotherapy/rehabilitation interventions to patients in the wide range of care settings: hospital, territorial, residential, outpatient, home-based
- Formulate training programs after conducting self-assessment, taking responsibility for one's own training, reflecting on professional practice to learn
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN
Competencies associated with the role.
Physiotherapist The training path of the Physiotherapy degree course aims to achieve the competence that combines knowledge (knowing), aptitude, and practical skills (knowing how to do). The graduate, at the end of the three-year program, must be able to:
Formulate physiotherapy diagnosis and prognosis.
- Collect data related to anamnesis, functions, activities, participation, and personal and environmental factors.
- Perform evaluations of different functional systems using validated tools, measures, guidelines, according to the principles of Evidence-Based Practice (EBP).
- Critically analyze and interpret relevant data to identify a physiotherapy functional diagnosis and prognostic hypotheses, considering recovery indices.
- Identify the level of disability in reference to ICF (impairment, disability, social participation) (ICF).
- Define possible alternative interpretations of the data.
- Explicitly state the clinical reasoning used in relation to the physiotherapy functional diagnosis.
- Compare data emerging from the evaluation with potential bibliographic deepening for the protection of the patient's health.
Define and plan the physiotherapy intervention.
- Involve the patient by requesting active participation and informing them of the sequence of the physiotherapy path.
- Define physiotherapy problems and the related goals to be achieved progressively during treatment.
- Identify possible preventive, educational, therapeutic, and palliative interventions.
- Choose resources usable within the rehabilitation path.
- Justify planning choices in relation to theoretical knowledge, built on evaluation data and based on the best available evidence and patient choices/preferences.
- Formulate one's physiotherapy proposal to the team for defining the rehabilitation project goals for the patient.
- Participate in planning educational-informational interventions and suggest activities for managing the person and self-care for patients and families.
Manage one's work within the Service.
- Plan one's work considering the service's goals and priorities in line with organizational needs and optimal use of available resources.
- Evaluate in the planning of physiotherapy treatment the duration and frequency of the intervention in relation to potential side effects of medications that may influence physiotherapy treatment.
- Plan each rehabilitation session according to the priority of interventions, in relation to problems and needs of each individual patient.
Perform physiotherapy treatment.
- Pursue physiotherapy goals according to the path established in the intervention planning.
- Choose physiotherapy proposals in relation to the presence of possible comorbidities.
- Prepare the setting to implement the physiotherapy intervention.
- Implement preventive interventions.
- Propose activities consistent with the planned program to the person being assisted, ensuring patient safety and respecting current regulations.
- Propose and suggest creative alternative solutions in relation to the results obtained by the patient.
- Use aids/orthoses to facilitate functional abilities.
- Maintain a growing and continuous collaboration process in the care of the patient and/or family and/or caregivers.
Verify and evaluate achieved results.
- Critically analyze the treatment plan and rehabilitation proposals in a constructive manner.
- Verify interim results of the physiotherapy proposal in collaboration with other professionals.
- Evaluate the achievement of goals and measure the outcomes of the physiotherapy intervention using validated methodologies and tools.
- Evaluate the entire physiotherapy process in relation to the effectiveness and efficiency of the results obtained.
Document professional acts.
- Document activities performed on the clinical case, respecting the sequence of the physiotherapy path methodology, using the didactic physiotherapy record inspired by ICF principles for the required competencies.
- Draft reports relevant to the internship area using the methodology for writing scientific articles.
Assume professional attitudes respecting the code of ethics.
- Ensure confidentiality of information related to the person.
- Respect the individuality, ideas, and expectations of the patient.
- Operate with methodological rigor, applying continuous scientific acquisitions to the field of competence.
- Demonstrate awareness of one's own limitations regarding professional attitude, abilities, and competencies through critical self-assessment.
Establish an effective relationship with the person assisted, family, and team.
- Establish effective communication within the helping relationship through understanding non-verbal communication, body expressiveness, and adopting behavior consistent with the person's characteristics.
- Explain to the person how physiotherapy proposals may influence and/or modify functional activity.
- Share the physiotherapy project with the person and their family.
Role in the work context.
Physiotherapist The main functions are: disease prevention, rehabilitation of patients and disabled individuals of all ages, and health education in reference to ICF.
In particular, the Physiotherapist:
a) Formulates functional diagnosis and physiotherapy prognosis;
b) Defines and plans the physiotherapy intervention;
c) Manages one's work within the Service;
d) Performs the physiotherapy intervention;
e) Verifies and evaluates the results obtained;
f) Documents professional acts;
g) Assumes professional attitudes respecting the code of ethics;
h) Establishes an effective relationship with the person assisted, family, and team;
i) Acts within the scope of one's professional competencies, integrating into the interdisciplinary team.

- Explain to the person how physiotherapy proposals may influence and/or modify functional activity.
- Share the physiotherapy project with the person and their family.
Training program structure:
1st year Focused on providing essential biological, biomedical, anatomical-physiological, cognitive, and communication knowledge as foundations of the discipline and professional methodology, fundamental requirements for undertaking the first internship experience aimed at orienting the student to professional fields and acquiring basic competencies.
2nd year Focused on providing knowledge related to motor, cognitive, and functional changes in kinesiology/biomechanics within the context of orthopedic and neurological pathology in adults, and specialized in pediatric age, acquiring, through internship experiences, related professional competencies in clinical contexts where students can experiment with intellectual, relational, and motor skills; identifying theoretical aspects emerging in clinical practice, researching the best available evidence in literature to engage with a reference professional community for acquiring the 'best possible practice'.
3rd year Focused on deepening cardiovascular and respiratory pathologies, pelvic floor pathologies, and sports trauma, as well as acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice, ability to work in teams and complex organizational contexts, and basic hygienic-preventive pathways. The relevance of internship experiences increases, allowing students to gradually assume autonomy and responsibility under expert supervision (in various specialized fields: neurology, orthopedics and trauma, cardiovascular, critical care, oncology, infectious diseases, pulmonology, maternal-infant area, etc.); scientific research methodology skills to support thesis development; and management and leadership elements useful for professional development in work contexts.
This curricular logic has been concretized in the choice of credits assigned to internship experiences, which gradually increase from the 1st to the 3rd year.

Biotechnologist The three-year Bachelor's degree in Biotechnology and Bioinformatics Analysis qualifies graduates to work in professional roles supporting diagnostic-therapeutic activities, within medical-veterinary structures, and in biotechnology companies operating in the agri-food and chemical-pharmaceutical sectors. The pre-graduation activity, carried out at university departments or healthcare facilities (AOU, ASL) or other settings, including entities such as IZS (Sardinian Experimental Zooprophylaxis Institute), AGRIS Sardegna (Sardinian Agency for Agricultural Research), or Porto Conte Ricerche (Sardinian Scientific and Technological Park), provides opportunities for involvement in the specific research and development activities characteristic of the Sardinian Region. National and international prospects are not neglected through an adequate information network, also related to international mobility opportunities.

Final exam characteristics.
The Final Exam consists of an oral examination in public session before the Degree Committee regarding the experience gained during the Internship period. If the student completes the Internship at other public or private national or foreign entities, the Degree Course appoints a faculty member affiliated with the Degree Course as scientific tutor, who will also serve as the examiner during the Final Exam.
To be admitted to the Final Exam, the student must have earned all credits required in the study plan's training activities.
The Degree Committee consists of at least 5 members. The Committee assesses the graduate's ability to clearly and competently present and discuss the experience gained during the Internship period.
The grade is calculated by summing the points from the weighted average of the university career with those assigned by the Degree Committee during the Final Exam according to criteria defined by the Degree Course.
Procedures for applying for Graduation and completing the AlmaLaurea Questionnaire are performed exclusively online. The student accesses this through the "Self Studenti Uniss" Private Area.

Required knowledge for admission.
For enrollment in the Bachelor's Degree Course (CdL) in Biotechnology and Bioinformatics Analysis, a high school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable under current regulations is required.
To effectively pursue studies, students must possess a good knowledge of basic Mathematics, Chemistry, and Biology, as well as adequate logical, reading, and comprehension skills.
The possession of these requirements will be verified using methods defined in the course's didactic regulations, also depending on quota-managed access.
The assessment of initial knowledge (Article 6, paragraph 1, D.M. 270/2004) to verify adequate knowledge of the fundamental concepts of the above subjects, any OFA, and the methods to fulfill any educational debt will be defined using methods published in the course's didactic regulations.

Communication Skills.
Participation in laboratory activities carried out individually or as a member of a group stimulates the student to effectively manage communication. This skill is enhanced through the experience gained during assessments related to courses that require the presentation of a summary report or the critical reading of scientific articles.
One of the decisive moments for the development of communication skills is the final thesis defense. This, in addition to the judgment prepared by the supervisor, is subject to the judgment of the graduation committee and represents the synthesis of the work completed during the internship. During this phase, the student uses appropriate materials for communicating technical-scientific information and demonstrates a level of English knowledge adequate for understanding and critically reading scientific articles on topics related to experimental disciplines, particularly of a biological and biotechnological nature.

UNIVERSITÀ: Università degli studi di Sassari
CORSO: [A147] BIOTECNOLOGIE E ANALISI BIOINFORMATICHE
SEZIONE: Autonomia di giudizio
URL: https://uniss.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10903

Autonomia di giudizio.
Lo studio di discipline che si fondano su principi teorici e sull'applicazione di metodologie multidisciplinari facilita il raggiungimento di un atteggiamento critico mirato alla scelta dell'approccio più adatto per affrontare e risolvere problemi specifici. Il raggiungimento di questi obiettivi deriva dalla esperienza acquisita in laboratorio e dalla sua integrazione con gli aspetti teorici, nonché dall'autonomia nell'interpretazione dei risultati e dall'acquisizione della capacità di saperli presentare in forma scritta e orale.
Elemento importante, affinché il laureato sia in grado di esercitare una riflessione critica sulle tematiche oggetto di studio, è il suo inserimento nel gruppo di ricerca e/o di sperimentazione applicata, coordinato dal proprio responsabile scientifico, durante il periodo del Tirocinio.
Il conseguimento dei risultati attesi viene verificato in apposite prove orali o scritte, per ciascun insegnamento, anche con il supporto dato dall'interpretazione di grafici o dall'utilizzazione di strumenti informatici.
Ad integrazione del percorso formativo, il CdS prevede eventi periodici di tipo seminariale e/o workshop con la presentazione di linee di ricerca finalizzate alla soluzione di problematiche di interesse sia per la scienza di base che per la ricerca industriale. Nel corso di tali eventi, gli studenti sono sollecitati a partecipare alla discussione ed è programmata la distribuzione di questionari e successiva valutazione della capacità di comprensione e di esprimere giudizi, riflessioni e proposte in merito agli argomenti trattati.
Capacità di apprendimento.
Lo studente matura la capacità di apprendimento e di studio autonomo divenendo indipendente ed autosufficiente nell'affrontare nuovi argomenti, impostare il metodo di studio e imparare ulteriori tecniche di laboratorio. Acquisisce padronanza e capacità nel reperire informazioni bibliografiche ed avvalersi delle banche dati disponibili in rete. Momento decisivo per verificare il grado di apprendimento è il Tirocinio, durante il quale lo studente combina teoria e pratica nell'analisi dei problemi, lavora in gruppo ed apprezza anche il valore dell'apprendimento autonomo. Tutto ciò si concretizza nella capacità del laureato di intraprendere percorsi di studio successivi avendo una solida consapevolezza delle proprie inclinazioni ed attitudini.
Elementi di monitoraggio, in progressione, e di verifica finale della capacità di apprendimento sono dati da prove in itinere (per specifici insegnamenti) e da esami finali in forma scritta e/o orale.
Particolare rilievo assume la prova finale in cui è possibile ottenere elementi complessivi di verifica.
Conoscenza e comprensione.
PREMESSA Le conoscenze acquisite dallo studente ricalcano l'attuale diversificazione delle applicazioni biotecnologiche e derivano dal contributo fornito da attività formative degli ambiti chimico-farmaceutico, bio-sanitario e agro-alimentare.
Il percorso formativo assicura l'integrazione di competenze disciplinari diverse e la formazione all'interno delle diverse aree disciplinari per il laureato è garanzia di flessibilità applicativa.
Nei primi tre semestri, sono impartiti i fondamenti e i principi delle discipline che caratterizzano le aree matematica, fisica, chimica, informatica, statistica, genetica e biochimica. A partire dal 4° semestre, è prevista l'acquisizione di ulteriori conoscenze specifiche in campo chimico farmacologico, biologico-molecolare e nell'area biotecnologica, con particolare riguardo all'integrazione delle conoscenze dei sistemi biologici con gli aspetti tecnologici più avanzati e innovativi quali le applicazioni bioinformatiche, le applicazioni tecnologiche in biotecnologie microbiche, sistemi diagnostici innovativi, tecnologie di genomica funzionale e proteomica.
Il laureato avrà capacità di integrare i dati sperimentali in una prospettiva nuova del metodo scientifico in quanto gli insegnamenti saranno focalizzati sull'impiego dei principi informatici per gestire e analizzare grandi quantità di dati sia nell’ambito della ricerca che in quello diagnostico.
Rilevante ai fini della conoscenza e della capacità di comprensione è la funzione svolta dal Tirocinio pratico che lo studente svolge sotto la guida di un responsabile scientifico, presso le strutture dipartimentali dell'Ateneo oppure presso aziende ed enti nazionali o esteri.
Segue descrizione dettagliata della Conoscenza e Comprensione e della Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione nelle tre aree disciplinari.
MATEMATICA, FISICA, INFORMATICA E BIOSTATISTICA Lo studente, anche con il supporto di attività pratiche, apprende:
- gli strumenti di base per sviluppare capacità logico e capacità operative relative ai principi della matematica, della fisica e della statistica per la comprensione e l’analisi di sistemi e fenomeni biologici;
- i principi di un linguaggio di programmazione open source, specifico per risolvere problemi matematici-statistici e per l'analisi statistica dei dati;
- strumenti di calcolo, programmazione e gestione di dataset.
CHIMICA Lo studente acquisisce concetti alla base della conoscenza e comprensione delle trasformazioni chimiche, con particolare riguardo a struttura atomica della materia, tavola periodica degli elementi, legame chimico, proprietà e geometrie molecolari, reattività chimica, stati di aggregazione della materia. Tali conoscenze sono prerequisito e propedeutiche all’apprendimento della chimica organica. La conoscenza della nomenclatura IUPAC, della struttura e della reattività dei principali gruppi funzionali, e della stereochimica molecolare contribuiscono alla comprensione della struttura tridimensionale delle molecole organiche. In una visione mirata alla comprensione del metabolismo cellulare, lo studente acquisisce la conoscenza di struttura, reattività e principali funzioni biologiche delle macromolecole organiche. Le conoscenze di chimica generale e organica acquisite risultano propedeutiche all’acquisizione dei fondamenti della chimica farmaceutica generale, relativamente ai meccanismi di azione dei farmaci, agli aspetti farmacocinetici e ai processi di drug discovery.
BIOLOGIA E BIOTECNOLOGIE Lo studente apprende i fondamenti delle scienze della vita, con particolare attenzione per gli ambiti cellulare, biochimico-molecolare, genetico e microbiologico, ed acquisisce conoscenze specifiche relative alle principali applicazioni biotecnologiche sviluppate nei suddetti ambiti.
Per quanto concerne l'ambito cellulare e biochimico-molecolare, lo studente conosce in modo approfondito la struttura molecolare e la funzione dei componenti della cellula ed è in grado di comprendere il loro ruolo nel mantenimento della diversità dei compartimenti e degli organuli e le implicazioni nei processi metabolici. Apprende inoltre gli aspetti fondamentali della comunicazione cellulare, dei principi che governano l'espressione genica in procarioti ed eucarioti. Dal punto di vista istologico è dato rilievo al differenziamento ed al ricambio dei tessuti basato sulle componenti staminali e sui processi di morte cellulare programmata. Dal punto di vista molecolare apprendono le principali tecniche d’analisi delle molecole biologiche e le possibili applicazioni biotecnologiche di proteine ed acidi nucleici.
Per quanto concerne l'ambito genetico, lo studente acquisisce dapprima i fondamenti della genetica di base, della citogenetica e della genetica molecolare che gli consentono di comprendere i meccanismi di trasmissione dei caratteri ereditari in organismi animali e vegetali. Successivamente lo studente apprende i meccanismi evolutivi e demografici che stanno alla base dell’origine e della diversificazione delle popolazioni naturali e gli strumenti per predire gli effetti delle principali forze evolutive. Studia, inoltre, i principi alla base del miglioramento genetico e della selezione di specie di interesse agrario, come anche l’utilizzo di metodi molecolari per l’analisi del miglioramento genetico delle piante e della costituzione di piante geneticamente modificate.
Per quanto concerne l'ambito microbiologico, lo studente apprende concetti fondamentali riguardanti morfologia, classificazione, genetica e fisiologia delle varie tipologie di microrganismi (batteri, virus, miceti, protozoi, comunità microbiche) e studia i meccanismi della loro interazione con l’ambiente e gli ospiti animali. Esamina, inoltre, le principali tecniche per l'analisi colturale e molecolare dei microrganismi e acquisisce le competenze di base necessarie per valutare e sfruttare le potenzialità biotecnologiche dei microrganismi (anche geneticamente modificati) nella produzione di beni e servizi. Lo studente approfondisce anche le implicazioni negli ambiti della patologia vegetale e animale, inclusi gli aspetti relativi alla risposta immunitaria dell'ospite.
Le nozioni biologiche di base acquisite dallo studente sono completate da elementi di anatomia macroscopica, di fisiologia della riproduzione negli animali domestici (con specifico riferimento alle biotecnologie riproduttive in campo animale) e di biologia vegetale (con richiami all’utilizzo di metaboliti primari e secondari).
Completano l’articolato quadro di conoscenze e comprensione i principi base del diritto dei brevetti, comprendenti i requisiti necessari per la brevettabilità di un'invenzione industriale e la sua tutela giuridica, con riferimento ai diritti morali e patrimoniali dell'inventore.
Per ciò che attiene all’attività pratica di laboratorio, lo studente ha una buona conoscenza delle principali metodologie sperimentali e dei relativi strumenti analitici, con particolare riferimento alle tecniche di analisi molecolare del DNA e delle proteine, di clonaggio molecolare e di analisi dell'espressione genica, nonché ai principi di base dell'analisi dei dati molecolari in contesti applicativi differenti (dalla salute dell’uomo agli organismi d’interesse agrario e veterinario). Integrano la preparazione scientifico molecolare la conoscenza di competenze informatiche di base e dei fondamenti dei metodi computazionali e bioinformatici finalizzati all'utilizzo di dati molecolari e alla loro presentazione in una visione attuale del metodo scientifico.
Infine, lo studente ha la capacità di utilizzare la letteratura scientifica (libri e riviste), partendo dallo studio razionale dei testi universitari consigliati e sfruttando la possibilità di accesso a piattaforme e banche dati informatiche.
Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione.
PREMESSA L'organizzazione didattica del CdL in Biotecnologie e Analisi Bioinformatiche consente al laureato di acquisire competenze teoriche finalizzate all’applicazione di metodologie di base con riferimento a differenti procedure analitiche. L'approccio multidisciplinare caratteristico del CdL permette l'intervento su diversi sistemi biologici (anche eventualmente modificati) e loro componenti, per applicazioni biotecnologiche in campo sanitario (medico e veterinario), microbiologico, agro-alimentare e chimico-farmaceutico.
Diversi insegnamenti orientano gli studenti all'impiego dei principi informatici per gestire e analizzare grandi quantità di dati sia nell’ambito della ricerca che in quello diagnostico. In particolare le competenze in ambito informatico sono introdotte con l'acquisizione di alcuni concetti fondamentali come basi di hardware e software, di principi di programmazione fino alla conoscenza e applicazione di metodi computazionali per l'analisi di fenomeni biologici.
Particolare attenzione è rivolta agli elementi di innovazione che vedono il settore biotecnologico in rapido progresso e che impongono un continuo ed efficiente aggiornamento delle conoscenze dei fondamenti teorici e delle loro applicazioni tecnologiche quali le tecnologie genomiche, post-genomiche e l'applicazione di risorse bioinformatiche per la loro analisi.
Durante le attività di laboratorio e il periodo di Tirocinio gli studenti sono stimolati ad affrontare i problemi pratici e la loro risoluzione, inizialmente in forma guidata e successivamente, ed in modo progressivo, con modalità che richiedono un maggiore contributo personale ed un livello consistente di autonomia lavorativa.
MATEMATICA, FISICA, INFORMATICA E BIOSTATISTICA Lo studente sarà in grado di applicare le conoscenze acquisite nello studio e nella comprensione dei sistemi e dei processi biotecnologici. In particolare gli strumenti logico-matematici, statistici, informatici e della fisica per l'analisi e l'elaborazione delle informazioni e dei dati sperimentali;
Inoltre, la conoscenza della lingua inglese permetterà allo studente di comprendere e e sviluppare capacità critica nello studio di specifici articoli scientifici.
CHIMICA Lo studente è in grado di comprendere e bilanciare una reazione chimica, trattare gli equilibri chimici così come la stereochimica, la cinetica e la termodinamica delle reazioni inorganiche e organiche. E’ in grado di applicare le conoscenze sulla struttura tridimensionale delle molecole organiche e delle macromolecole biologiche, con riferimento alle proprietà stereochimiche, nonché i formalismi per rappresentare le molecole organiche in forma bidimensionale. Ha inoltre conoscenze propedeutiche, relative ai concetti di legame covalente e interazione noncovalente e alla funzione svolta nel definire e sostenere la struttura della materia, che utilizzerà nei corsi di biochimica e chimica farmaceutica. Completano questo ambito, conoscenza delle superfici di potenziale elettrostatico, come moderno strumento computazionale per lo studio e la comprensione delle molecole organiche.
Attraverso tale percorso formativo, lo studente giunge ad un livello di preparazione appropriato relativamente alle conoscenze chimiche e biochimiche, sviluppando, in particolare, la capacità di interpretare i processi biologici e l’attività farmacologica in chiave "molecolare".
BIOLOGIA E BIOTECNOLOGIE L'organizzazione del percorso formativo assicura l'integrazione di competenze disciplinari diverse e la formazione, curata all'interno delle diverse aree disciplinari, è garanzia di flessibilità applicativa. I laureati acquisiscono competenze teoriche finalizzate all’applicazione di metodologie di base con riferimento a differenti procedure analitiche. L'approccio multidisciplinare caratteristico del CdL permette l'intervento pratico su diversi sistemi biologici (anche geneticamente modificati) e loro componenti, per applicazioni biotecnologiche nei campi biomedico, microbiologico, agro-alimentare e chimico-farmaceutico. In particolare, il percorso di studi è organizzato in modo da consentire di apprendere progressivamente ed applicare le principali tecniche relative all’ambito biochimico, alla tecnologia del DNA ricombinante ed alla coltura ed ingegnerizzazione di procarioti ed eucarioti animali e vegetali, nonché agli approcci analitici relativi alle moderne scienze "omiche". Tematiche quali la diagnostica molecolare e l'immunoprofilassi sono acquisite dal laureato al terzo anno di corso, dopo aver acquistato familiarità con argomenti propedeutici al settore delle biotecnologie microbiche.
Ai fini della capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione hanno una funzione rilevante le attività di laboratorio ed il periodo di Tirocinio, durante i quali gli studenti sono spinti ad affrontare i problemi pratici e la loro risoluzione, inizialmente in forma guidata e, successivamente ed in modo progressivo, con modalità che richiedono un maggiore contributo personale ed un livello consistente di autonomia lavorativa.
Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione.
ITALIANO Competenze associate alla funzione.
Biotecnologo Il Cds fornisce una preparazione di base e l’autonomia tecnico professionale spendibile in attività lavorative che implicano l'uso di metodologie standardizzate per l'esecuzione delle seguenti procedure:
a) procedure analitico-strumentali connesse alle indagini biologiche;
b) procedure tecnico-analitiche in ambito biotecnologico, biomolecolare, biosanitario (medico/veterinario) anche finalizzate ad attività di ricerca;
c) procedure tecnico-analitiche in ambito chimico-fisico, biochimico, microbiologico, genetico e farmaceutico.
d) procedure tecnico-analitiche e di controllo in ambito agronomico/ambientale.
e) applicazione di metodi bioinformatici per gestire e analizzare grandi quantità di dati sia nell’ambito della ricerca che in quello diagnostico.
Funzione in contesto di lavoro.
Biotecnologo La figura professionale creata si caratterizza per la capacita di operare interventi tipo tecnico su processi biotecnologici inerenti l’utilizzazione di sistemi biologici e parti di essi al fine di ottenere prodotti innovativi in ambito sanitario (medico-veterinario) ed agroalimentare. La laurea in Biotecnologie e Analisi Biotecnologiche conferisce, inoltre, le competenze per il controllo biologico, l’esame analitico e la verifica dei processi e delle metodologie dei prodotti biotecnologici. Il laureato triennale è in grado di inserirsi nell’attività di ricerca applicata nell’ambito biologico e biotecnologico anche intervenendo sul genoma di microrganismi e organismi.
Le competenze acquisite gli permetteranno di svolgere funzione supporto alle attività scientifiche, sia presso laboratori di ricerca in ambito biologico medico per applicazioni bioinformatiche, cliniche e scientifiche, sia presso aziende informatiche operanti nel settore medico, presso industrie agroalimentari, chimiche e farmaceutiche.
Descrizione obiettivi formativi specifici.
Il Corso di Laurea in Biotecnologie e Analisi Bioinformatiche si propone di formare laureati in grado di disporre delle risorse culturali, scientifiche e tecnologiche adeguate per affrontare in modo appropriato problematiche in ambito biotecnologico, anche in settori di ricerca applicata e/o di base, nei campi biomedico, agro-industriale, veterinario e farmaceutico. La solida preparazione di base nelle scienze biotecnologiche è integrata da competenze informatiche fondamentali orientate all'utilizzo di dati di tipo molecolare e biochimico e allo sviluppo di modelli computazionali per tematiche di natura biologica (es. trattamento di grandi quantità di dati).
Per quanto attiene alle competenze in ambito biotecnologico, il laureato sarà in grado di allestire e mettere in atto procedure sperimentali per l'analisi ed il trattamento di cellule o di loro componenti, anche in forma modificata, per la produzione di prodotti utili all'uomo, per il miglioramento di piante ed animali o per lo sviluppo di microrganismi da applicare per usi specifici.
Il piano di studi, oltre a mirare all'inserimento professionale dei laureati nell'area biotecnologica, fornisce la preparazione di base propedeutica al proseguimento degli studi per il conseguimento della laurea magistrale. L'organizzazione del percorso formativo assicura l'integrazione di competenze disciplinari diverse e la formazione, curata all'interno delle diverse aree disciplinari, è garanzia, per il laureato, di flessibilità applicativa.
Nel primo anno di corso, sono impartite le nozioni essenziali dei fondamenti e dei principi delle discipline che caratterizzano gli ambiti matematico (matematica, statistica, fisica), informatico, chimico (chimica generale e chimica organica) e biologico (biologia cellulare e istologia, genetica).
Nel corso del secondo e del terzo anno, lo lo studente approfondisce alcune discipline di base e caratterizzanti (biochimica, microbiologia e immunologia, biologia molecolare, genetica molecolare) integrate da nozioni applicative in settori specifici delle biotecnologie, quali quelle relative alla microbiologia industriale ed alle applicazioni biotecnologiche in ambito vegetale ed animale. Particolare attenzione è rivolta agli elementi di innovazione che vedono il settore biotecnologico in rapido progresso e che impongono un continuo e efficiente aggiornamento delle conoscenze dei fondamenti teorici e delle loro applicazioni tecnologiche, quali quelle di genomica funzionale e proteomica.
Al fine di garantire a tutti gli studenti adeguate competenze informatiche, un congruo numero di crediti verrà attribuito a insegnamenti del settore ING-INF /05 attivato nell’ambito delle Attività Affini e Integrative. Gli studenti acquisiranno le nozioni essenziali dei fondamenti e dei principi delle discipline che caratterizzano la bioinformatica al primo anno nel corso di Fondamenti di Informatica. Al secondo anno, nel corso di Modelli Computazionali per la Biologia, acquisiranno i principi dei metodi computazionali e bioinformatici per l'analisi della complessità biologica.
La preparazione scientifico-tecnica sarà integrata con aspetti normativi relativi ai requisiti di brevettabilità con riferimento anche a brevetti speciali (farmaceutico, informatico e biotecnologico) ed a elementi di responsabilità e bioetica.
Le lezioni frontali e le esercitazioni teorico-pratiche, sono propedeutiche all'attività di laboratorio. Quest'ultima è principalmente fondata all'utilizzo di attrezzature di laboratorio e all'esecuzione di tecniche e protocolli individuali e/o di gruppo per favorire familiarità con il metodo sperimentale applicato a sistemi biologici complessi. Per questo motivo, la maggior parte degli insegnamenti è articolata in lezioni frontali ed in esercitazioni pratiche di laboratorio che sono organizzate e si svolgono sotto la guida di docenti e che fanno parte integrante dell'esame finale.
Durante l'ultimo anno, lo studente deve obbligatoriamente svolgere un periodo di almeno 250 ore di Tirocinio pratico. Questo può essere condotto presso laboratori di strutture Universitarie o di enti pubblici o privati, purché convenzionati con l'Ateneo nazionali o esteri. E' soprattutto durante il Tirocinio che lo studente acquisisce competenze sull'uso delle tecnologie dell'informazione e della comunicazione per la ricerca bibliografica e di altre informazioni e per l'utilizzo di software per la gestione, l'elaborazione e la presentazione dei risultati.
